preguntas.pregunta: May a physician decline to take on a patient or to provide a treatment that has been requested?
opciones: Yes, as when the treatment is not indicated by the history given
Yes, but only where another provider has already agreed to take over
No, once the person has been registered as a patient of the practice
No, unless an emergency elsewhere makes the schedule impossible
preguntas.explicacion: The right runs in both directions. A physician may in many circumstances decline to enter into the relationship or to offer a treatment, for instance when accepting a referral for a specific treatment seems unwarranted or the treatment is not indicated by the history provided. The privilege is old, dating to the Hippocratic era, but no law protects it as broadly as the profession states, and the laws that do protect it usually rest on freedom of religion.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Treatment Refusal (by Both Patient and Physician)
preguntas.subtema: The provider's refusal · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k212 · CMA II.E.4 · RMA I.C.4 · NCMA 4.1

preguntas.pregunta: Axillary crutches are being fitted. Where should the shoulder pad sit and how should the elbow be?
opciones: About two finger widths below the axilla, with the elbow flexed some 30 degrees
Snug against the axilla itself, with the elbow flexed to about 30 degrees
About two finger widths below the axilla, with the elbow held nearly straight
About four finger widths below the axilla, with the elbow flexed to 90 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The pad stops roughly two inches, or two fingers, short of the armpit with the shoulder relaxed, the grip is set so the elbow bends about 30 degrees, and the tips rest some six inches outside the feet. The patient is told never to rest the armpit on the pad. Patient handouts give the gap as one to one and a half inches, measured the same way.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Preparation; and MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using crutches
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14

preguntas.pregunta: In which setting may an employer decide that gloves are not routinely required for every phlebotomy?
opciones: A volunteer blood donation center, under conditions such as gloves for trainees
A clinical laboratory, if it applies Universal Precautions to all specimens
An outpatient draw station, if the phlebotomist has no cuts on the hands
Any facility, if the employee documents that gloves reduce manual dexterity
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix) requires gloves for vascular access procedures with one carve-out, (d)(3)(ix)(D): a volunteer blood donation center whose employer judges routine gloving unnecessary. Even there the employer must periodically reevaluate the policy, make gloves available to anyone who wants them, never discourage their use, and require them when the employee has cuts or breaks in the skin, when hand contamination is likely such as with an uncooperative donor, and during phlebotomy training. No other setting gets the exception.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix) and (d)(3)(ix)(D), Gloves
preguntas.subtema: Glove exception for blood donation · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: What is the medical expert witness first asked to do in a malpractice case?
opciones: Establish the standard of care that applied to that case
Establish the damages the patient's family should receive
Establish whether the defendant's license should be revoked
Establish which of the two parties told the truth in discovery
preguntas.explicacion: The expert's role has three parts, and the first is to establish the standard of care applicable to that case. Next comes an opinion on whether the care deviated from it, and only then, if there was a deviation, an opinion on whether it caused the injury alleged. Damages are for the jury, and licensure is a matter for the state board.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Function
preguntas.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: One patient's chart lists diabetes, hypertension and chronic kidney disease at once. Which term names that situation?
opciones: Comorbidity, having two or more diseases at the same time
Etiology, the set of causes behind two or more diseases
Prevalence, the count of people who have several diseases
Remission, the fading of the signs of several diseases
preguntas.explicacion: Comorbidity is the condition of having two or more diseases at once, and it changes both the risk and the plan of care. A risk factor is something else again: anything that raises the chance of developing a disease, such as age, family history, tobacco use or exposure to radiation or certain chemicals.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, comorbidity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.A.2.b · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: What hemodynamic change is expected when a patient is placed in reverse Trendelenburg?
opciones: Venous return falls, and that drop can show up as hypotension
Venous return and cardiac output rise for the first ten minutes
Intracranial and intraocular pressure climb while the head is down
Functional residual capacity falls as the abdomen presses upward
preguntas.explicacion: Tilting the bed so the head becomes the highest point of the trunk drains blood away from the heart: venous return drops and hypotension can follow, and cerebral perfusion may fall with it, so invasive arterial monitoring is considered. The rises in preload, in intracranial pressure and the loss of lung volume all belong to the head-down tilt instead.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Supine Position Variations
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.b · CCMA 3B4 k61 · RMA III.F.2.b.i

preguntas.pregunta: After a draw with an evacuated tube system, how does the WHO say the needle and holder should be disposed of?
opciones: Discard barrel and needle together as a single unit whenever possible
Unscrew the needle by hand and drop it into the sharps container, keeping the barrel
Recap the needle with both hands, then remove it from the barrel for reuse
Leave the needle on the barrel and place both in the regulated-waste bag
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says to discard the barrel and needle as a single entity where possible; if the barrel must be reused, the needle is removed with a one-hand scoop technique or with a sharps container that has a needle removal hold, always one-handed. Annex E adds that an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and OSHA prohibits two-handed recapping and removal except where no alternative is feasible.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1 and Annex E; and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient cannot raise sputum on his own and sputum induction is started. When is the procedure stopped?
opciones: When 1 to 2 mL has been obtained, after 15 minutes of nebulization, or if chest tightness begins
When 1 to 2 mL has been obtained, after 60 minutes of nebulization, or if the patient coughs hard
When 10 to 20 mL has been obtained, after 15 minutes of nebulization, or if the patient coughs hard
When 1 to 2 mL has been obtained, after 5 minutes of nebulization, or if the patient starts to gag
preguntas.explicacion: Induction has the patient breathe a nebulized 3 percent hypertonic saline mist for about five minutes to thin the secretions, then take deep breaths and cough. It is halted once 1 to 2 mL of sputum is in the container, at 15 minutes of nebulization, or if chest tightness, breathlessness or wheezing appear, because a pleural bulla can rupture and cause a pneumothorax. Saliva goes into an emesis bowl, not the container.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Sputum Induction
preguntas.subtema: Sputum induction limits · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4)

preguntas.pregunta: Which products fall outside the scope of the FDA guidance on sharps injury prevention features?
opciones: Sharps containers and needle recapping devices
Winged sets and retractable safety lancet devices
Insulin syringes and their orange needle covers
Blood collection needles fitted with a shield
preguntas.explicacion: That guidance covers medical devices carrying an active or passive component that protects the user from a sharps injury. It says plainly that it does not deal with sharps containers or with needle recapping devices, which are handled by separate guidance of their own.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Section 4, Scope
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: The beat under the fingers is irregular. How is the rate counted?
opciones: For a full minute, because a longer count is more accurate when the rhythm is irregular
For 15 seconds and multiplied by 4, which keeps the intake moving without losing accuracy
For 10 seconds and multiplied by 6, then repeated on the opposite wrist for comparison
For 30 seconds and multiplied by 2, then rounded to the nearest multiple of 10 beats
preguntas.explicacion: Short counts multiplied up are usually good enough on a regular pulse: 30 seconds doubled, or even 10 or 15 seconds multiplied by 6 or 4. An irregular rhythm breaks that assumption, because the beats are not evenly spread, so the count runs the full minute. Rounding a recorded value to the nearest ten is a documented error, not a rule.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's sinoatrial node stops firing. At what rate does the atrioventricular node take over?
opciones: 40 to 60 per minute, the inherent rate of that part of the system
20 to 30 per minute, the inherent rate of that part of the system
15 to 20 per minute, the inherent rate of that part of the system
80 to 100 per minute, the inherent rate of that part of the system
preguntas.explicacion: Every level of the conduction system can fire on its own, and the rate drops the farther down you go: the sinoatrial node on its own runs 80 to 100, the atrioventricular node 40 to 60, the bundle branches 20 to 30 and the Purkinje fibers 15 to 20. A rate of 40 to 60 is still enough to keep a person conscious.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Prepotential
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's driver takes blood samples to the hospital laboratory every afternoon. Besides a rack or padded holder for the tubes, what must the vehicle carry according to WHO?
opciones: A blood spillage kit, so that a broken sample can be cleaned up safely on the way
A portable centrifuge, so that serum can be separated if the trip is delayed
A carbon dioxide incubator, so that culture specimens keep their organisms viable
A second set of empty tubes, so that a broken sample can be recollected on arrival
preguntas.explicacion: For transporting blood samples outside a hospital, WHO asks that the vehicle be equipped with a blood spillage kit, because a sample can break during transport just as it can in the phlebotomy area; the spill is then handled with gloves and, for large spills, a gown or apron, paper towels that go into infectious waste, and a freshly prepared bleach solution. Multiple tubes travel in a rack or padded holder precisely to avoid that breakage.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Steps 10 and 11
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5D k89 · PBT III.D · CCMA 3E14 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: How does the visual analogue scale differ from the numeric rating scale?
opciones: The patient marks a line whose ends are labelled, and the distance is the score
The patient chooses among printed words, and each word carries a fixed score
The observer scores facial expression and limb movement instead of asking
The patient scores pain, enjoyment and general activity from zero to ten each
preguntas.explicacion: On the visual analogue scale the patient marks a point along a line whose ends read no pain and worst possible pain, and the score is how far the mark lies from the first end. Pictures can be added for patients who do not share the clinician's language. Its limitations are the same as those of the numeric scale.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A tray is set up an hour ahead of a procedure and left covered in an empty room. What is the problem?
opciones: Airborne microbes settle over time, and an unattended field may be contaminated unseen
The drape dries out over an hour, and a dry drape wicks microbes up from the tabletop
The chemical indicators inside the packs reverse their color once the packs cool down
The one-inch border widens as the drape relaxes, leaving less usable surface for the tray
preguntas.explicacion: Sterile fields are set up as close to the procedure as possible and are not left unattended. The longer a field sits open the more airborne microbes settle on it, and leaving it alone adds the risk that someone contaminated it without being seen. Either way the patient is exposed to a hospital-acquired infection.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.D.2.f

preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for the first step of two-step gestational screening asks what she should do about food beforehand. What do you tell her?
opciones: No fast and no diet change: the screening step needs neither one
No food or drink, apart from sips of water, for 8 to 14 hours before
Eat an unrestricted diet with 150 g of carbohydrate a day for 3 days
Eat a light breakfast exactly one hour before the appointment time
preguntas.explicacion: For the screening step the patient does not have to prepare or change her diet in any way: she drinks the glucose liquid and blood is drawn one hour later. The 8-to-14-hour fast belongs to the 3-hour follow-up test and to the one-step 75 g test; the three-day carbohydrate load is a condition of the nonpregnant diagnostic OGTT. Eating normally in the days before is the only instruction given.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), How the Test is Performed and How to Prepare for the Test
preguntas.subtema: Gestational screening preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions

preguntas.pregunta: Which signs suggest that a patient may have low health literacy?
opciones: Missed appointments, few questions, no follow-through
Frequent questions, detailed notes, early arrival
A long medication list and several specialist referrals
A preferred language other than English on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Indications include frequently missed appointments, medication nonadherence, trouble identifying medicines or recalling their purpose and dosage, asking fewer questions, and not following through on tests or referrals. Because low health literacy cannot be spotted by appearance, care is delivered as if everyone had limited literacy.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pharmacy Communication Strategies", Other Issues: Health Literacy
preguntas.subtema: Health literacy · CCMA 4F k160 · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-month-old infant weighing 5 kg needs a capillary specimen. Which site does WHO Table 7.1 indicate, and where on it is the lancet placed?
opciones: The heel, on the medial or lateral plantar surface
The heel, on the posterior curve where skin is thickest
The middle or ring finger, on the side of the ball
The thumb or index finger, on the side of the ball
preguntas.explicacion: Table 7.1 assigns the heel-prick to infants from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, with the lancet on the medial or lateral plantar surface; the finger-prick is for children over 6 months and over 10 kg. Chapter 7 says the posterior heel should be avoided because the bone lies only 2.33 mm beneath the skin, and the table itself warns against the thumb and index finger.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1; and Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: Site by age · CPT D3 k55 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient moving to another state asks whether her Medicaid will work the same way there. How are the rules set?
opciones: The federal government sets general guidelines and each state writes its own rules
The federal government writes one single set of rules that applies in every one of the states
Each state writes its rules with no federal guideline of any kind standing above
The insurance marketplace in each state writes the rules for its own state plans
preguntas.explicacion: Medicaid is government health insurance that helps many low-income people pay their medical bills. The federal government sets up general guidelines for the program, but each state has its own rules, and a state may require the person to pay part of the cost of some services. Eligibility can turn on age, pregnancy, blindness, disability, income and resources, and immigration status.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medicaid: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: What separates health care disparities from health disparities?
opciones: Health care disparities are about access and coverage
Health care disparities are about outcomes and illness
Health care disparities are about cultural preferences
Health care disparities are about staffing and workload
preguntas.explicacion: Health disparities are differences in health outcomes that grow out of entrenched economic, sociopolitical or environmental disadvantage, and they fall on groups by ethnicity, gender, age, disability, orientation, income or location. Health care disparities is the narrower term: differences in access to care and in coverage.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, III Glossary
preguntas.subtema: Health disparities · CCMA 4D k166

preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture, what form of consent does WHO step 2 describe obtaining?
opciones: Verbal consent, after discussing the test with the patient
Written consent, signed by the patient and witnessed by staff
Implied consent, shown by the patient's presence in the clinic
Consent given by the ordering physician on the laboratory form
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO step reads: discuss the test to be performed and obtain verbal consent, adding that the patient can refuse at any point before the sampling. StatPearls describes written documentation for informed consent in general, but the WHO phlebotomy step relies on a spoken yes after an explanation. Nothing in either source lets the requester's signature stand in for the patient.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E types of consent · CCMA 3E1 · CMA E.3.b (both outlines) · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: In the PQRSTU framework, what does the letter U ask the patient?
opciones: What the patient believes is causing the symptom they came in with
How long the symptom has lasted and whether it comes and then goes
Whether any activity makes the symptom better or makes it worse
Where the symptom is felt and whether it moves somewhere else
preguntas.explicacion: U stands for understanding, and it asks the patient what they think is behind the problem. Provocation and palliation cover what worsens and what relieves it, region covers where it sits and whether it radiates, and timing covers when it began and whether it is constant. The framework is used for pain and works just as well for nausea, itching or breathlessness.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.5, Table 2.5b: PQRSTU Focused Questions
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.4.b · CCMA 3A3 · NCMA 2B.4

preguntas.pregunta: How is the machine calibrated on the voltage axis?
opciones: A signal of 1 mV moves the stylus 1 cm on the paper
A signal of 1 mV moves the stylus 1 mm on the paper
A signal of 5 mV moves the stylus 1 cm on the paper
A signal of 1 mV moves the stylus 5 cm on the paper
preguntas.explicacion: The machine is set so that one millivolt deflects the stylus by one centimeter, which is ten small squares tall. That is the standardization mark printed at the edge of the tracing, and if it is not the expected height the amplitudes on that recording cannot be compared with anything.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k157 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5

preguntas.pregunta: Minutes after using a short-acting inhaler a patient reports shaky hands and a pounding heart. What explains it?
opciones: Beta-2 agonists also stir the sympathetic system, producing tremor and palpitations
Beta-2 agonists damp the sympathetic system, so the heart slows and the hands shake
Anticholinergic inhalers give tremor, dry mouth and retention within a few minutes
Paradoxical bronchospasm always opens with tremor before the airways start closing
preguntas.explicacion: The usual adverse effects of a bronchodilator come from sympathetic activation: tremor, nervousness, palpitations the patient can feel, and muscle cramps. The severe ones are paradoxical narrowing of the airway, low potassium and, rarely, myocardial infarction. Anticholinergic inhalers give a different picture, with dry mouth, urinary retention, tachycardia and constipation, and delirium in older adults.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Bronchodilators", Adverse Effects and Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse asks why a glucose flagged as a critical value is handled differently from a test ordered STAT. What distinguishes the two?
opciones: A critical value is defined only by how far the result deviates from the normal range; a STAT test is designated by the ordering clinician
A critical value is designated by the ordering clinician; a STAT test is defined by how far the result deviates from the normal range
A critical value applies only to results from laboratory analyzers; a STAT designation applies only to point-of-care devices
A critical value must be repeated on a new specimen; a STAT test is reported from the first run without any repetition
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are defined solely by the degree to which a result deviates from the established normal range, regardless of the patient's condition, whereas STAT or urgent tests are designated by the ordering clinician and usually presuppose knowledge of the patient's status. Point-of-care results that reach a critical value are addressed promptly and often change management, so both the result and the actions taken are documented.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13 k111

preguntas.pregunta: By what age does attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder usually begin?
opciones: Usually before age 12
Usually before age 6
Usually before age 18
Usually before age 3
preguntas.explicacion: Onset is usually before age 12, symptoms show up at school, at work or at home, and the disturbance causes significant impairment in social, occupational and academic functioning without being explained by another behavior disorder. Three types are described: mainly inattentive, mainly hyperactive-impulsive, and combined.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder", History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Mental health conditions · CCMA 1E k30 · CMA F.1.a / 2027 F.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse is about to insert an IV cannula and asks whether the blood tests can be drawn at the same time. What does the WHO say?
opciones: It is acceptable but not ideal, when the cannula is first inserted and before the fluids are connected
It is the preferred method, because it spares the patient a second puncture and gives identical results
It is never acceptable; specimens from any in-dwelling device carry a risk of contamination
It is acceptable only for blood cultures, which must be drawn before any fluid is connected
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 states that it is acceptable, but not ideal, to draw blood when first introducing an in-dwelling venous device, before the cannula is connected to the intravenous fluids. The same passage forbids drawing from an access that is already in use because of false results, and notes that central line specimens taken by nurses or physicians under protocol carry a contamination risk.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and IV access · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: How often does an office have to check the List of Excluded Individuals/Entities, and on what other occasion?
opciones: Every month, and again in connection with any new enrolment or new hire
Every year, and again whenever a claim comes back denied for a coding error
Every three years, the same interval an employer keeps its training records
Only when the Inspector General writes to say an employee has been excluded
preguntas.explicacion: Anyone who hires an individual or entity on the exclusion list may face civil monetary penalties, so health care entities are told to check it routinely for new hires and current employees. The list has to be checked monthly, and in connection with any new enrolment, so that an excluded person is not enrolled or kept on.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k189 · NCMA 4.6

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement describes the prone position correctly?
opciones: The patient lies on the front with head, neck and spine held in neutral alignment
The patient lies on one side with the upper leg flexed over the lower leg
The patient lies on the back with the knees flexed and the feet in supports
The patient lies halfway between the back and the front, with legs flexed
preguntas.explicacion: Prone means face down, turned from supine while head, neck and spine stay in line. Headrests with openings for the eyes, nose and chin keep pressure off those structures, since vision loss is an avoidable complication of the position. It recruits alveoli and raises oxygenation without changing cardiac output, which is why it is used in severe hypoxemia.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Structure and Function: Prone Position

preguntas.pregunta: What does it mean to use health literacy universal precautions in a practice?
opciones: Structuring information and services so that everyone can understand and use them
Structuring information so that only patients who screen as low literacy get help
Structuring information at a college level and simplifying it when a patient asks
Structuring services so that written material replaces spoken explanation entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Universal precautions here means the same posture used for infection: assume the need and apply it to everyone. Health information and services are laid out so anyone can understand and use them, communication is simplified and understanding confirmed with every patient, the system is made easier to navigate, and self-management is supported.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd ed.: Health Literacy Universal Precautions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMAA 2D · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h

preguntas.pregunta: A prevacuum steam sterilizer is loaded with wrapped supplies. What is the shortest exposure recognized for that cycle?
opciones: 4 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
4 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
30 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
3 minutes at 134 °C (273 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: A prevacuum sterilizer has a pump that pulls the air out of the chamber and the load before steam enters, so penetration is almost instantaneous even into porous loads and four minutes at 132 °C suffices for wrapped supplies. Thirty minutes at 121 °C is the gravity figure, and 134 °C for 3.5 minutes is the run used for the daily air-removal test, not for a load.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA 2027 I.C.5.b(3) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA Essential 5

preguntas.pregunta: How must controlled substances in Schedules II through V be stored in a practitioner's office?
opciones: In a securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet at the registered location
In a refrigerator held between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius with a continuous data logger
In the original shipping cartons, in a room whose door stays closed during clinic hours
In a container marked with the biohazard symbol, emptied when three-quarters full
preguntas.explicacion: Schedule I substances and those in Schedules II through V alike are stored in a securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet. Pharmacies and institutional practitioners have one alternative: dispersing the controlled stock among the non-controlled stock in a way that obstructs theft or diversion. The refrigerator range belongs to vaccine storage, and the biohazard container is the one used for sharps.
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k71 · CMA I.D.1.e · RMA III.G.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the superficial arm veins is typically the larger of the two?
opciones: The basilic vein, although the cephalic is sometimes larger
The cephalic vein, although the basilic is sometimes larger
The median cubital vein, which is larger than either of them
Both are the same calibre, since they drain equal territories
preguntas.explicacion: Size varies a great deal between patients, but the basilic is usually the larger superficial vein of the arm and sometimes the cephalic takes that place. Calibre alone does not decide the puncture: an artery and a nerve travel with the basilic, which makes it the riskier of the two.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Physiologic Variants

preguntas.pregunta: Which principle appears in the AAMA Code of Ethics?
opciones: Respecting confidential information unless disclosure is legally required
Reporting any coworker who deviates from the practice's written protocol
Refusing to assist with a procedure the assistant personally disagrees with
Referring every request for records straight to the practice's own attorney
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets out five principles that members pledge to strive toward: rendering service with full respect for human dignity; respecting confidential information gained through employment unless the law authorizes or responsible duty requires disclosure; upholding the honor and high principles of the profession and accepting its disciplines; continually improving knowledge and skills; and taking part in community health activities.
preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Ethics

preguntas.pregunta: A draw with a needle and syringe has finished. How are the two treated at the moment of disposal?
opciones: As a single unit, dropped straight into a robust sharps container
As two items, the needle in the sharps bin and the syringe in waste
As a single unit, but only after the needle has been re-sheathed
As two items, the syringe rinsed first and the needle discarded
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction treats a needle and syringe as one unit and asks for the used device to go immediately into a robust sharps container. The prohibition on the other side of the table is equally plain: an unprotected needle is never left lying outside that container.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2

preguntas.pregunta: A lavender tube arrives in the emergency laboratory with no label at all, together with a requisition for a CBC. According to the rejection criteria used by emergency laboratories, what happens to it?
opciones: It is rejected as a misidentified specimen and a new sample is requested
It is accepted if the requisition in the bag identifies the patient
It is held at 4 °C for up to 24 hours until the ward sends a label to attach to it
It is tested and the result is reported with a comment about the label
preguntas.explicacion: Unlabeled, mislabeled and mismatched samples fall under misidentification, one of the standing rejection criteria of the emergency laboratory, alongside missing barcodes, improper containers, insufficient volume, hemolysis, lipemia and clots. The requisition in the bag does not identify the tube, storing it while waiting for a label amounts to relabeling, and reporting a result from an unidentified tube is the error the criteria exist to prevent.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the blood culture bottle in the WHO order-of-draw table contain, and what is it used for?
opciones: A broth mixture that keeps microorganisms viable; aerobes, anaerobes and fungi
Sodium citrate that removes calcium; coagulation tests such as prothrombin time
Acid-citrate-dextrose that inactivates complement; HLA typing and DNA studies
A clot activator that yields serum; chemistries, serology and cross-match
preguntas.explicacion: Row 1 of Table 2.3 describes the yellow-black striped blood culture bottle: its additive is a broth mixture, its mode of action is to preserve the viability of microorganisms, and its uses are microbiology for aerobes, anaerobes and fungi. The other three descriptions are the rows for the light blue citrate tube, the pale yellow ACD tube and the red clot activator tube.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature does an effective event reporting system need?
opciones: A set way of reviewing the reports and turning them into action plans
A rule that names the reporter in the summary sent to the whole staff
A limit that lets only licensed providers file a report of an event
A yearly deadline by which all of the reports of the year are filed
preguntas.explicacion: Four attributes make the system work: an environment that supports reporting and guards the privacy of whoever reports, reports coming in from a broad range of personnel, summaries shared promptly, and a structured way of reviewing reports and building action plans. Reporting is usually confidential, with legal protection short of misconduct.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, PSNet Patient Safety Primer: Reporting Patient Safety Events
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · CMAA 3 k44 · NCMA 4.10

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives after a cigarette and a coffee. What does the technique call for?
opciones: Wait until 30 minutes have passed since the caffeine, the smoking or any exercise
Wait five minutes seated, which is enough to clear the effect of either of them
Take the reading now and add a note, since the effect of both is under 2 mm Hg
Wait 60 minutes, which is the interval given for caffeine, nicotine and exertion
preguntas.explicacion: Caffeine, nicotine and exercise inside the previous half hour all push the reading up, so the measurement is delayed until 30 minutes have gone by. Smoking within that window can raise the systolic value by as much as 20 mm Hg, far from a rounding error. The five minutes seated is a separate requirement that comes after.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Measuring Your Blood Pressure: Things that can affect a reading
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: An accessioning clerk scans a specimen barcode and the screen fills with far more than the patient's name. What kind of data does such a barcode key typically pull up?
opciones: Tube and specimen type, print and collection times, the ward, and who drew it
Only the patient's names and hospital number, kept short to avoid misreads
The analyser assigned to the tube and the position it holds in the rack
The insurance carrier, the diagnosis code and the billing account number
preguntas.explicacion: In the hospital that published its rejection audit, a nine-digit internal barcode identified name, surname, gender, age, tube type, specimen type, the time the label was printed, the collection date and time, the service where the specimen was taken, the tests requested, the ordering physician and the phlebotomist. Access to those databases is restricted to clinical and laboratory staff.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k89 k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 k112 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: When is the extent of an ocular chemical injury assessed?
opciones: After irrigation, once the surface pH has come back to neutral
Before irrigation, so that the initial appearance is documented first
Before irrigation, because the fluid washes the injured epithelium away
After irrigation, once the topical corticosteroid has taken effect
preguntas.explicacion: Irrigation comes before assessment; grading waits until the eye and its structures have been flushed and the pH is neutral. Visual acuity is checked then if it can be, and a topical anesthetic may be needed because pain and blepharospasm limit the examination. Retained particles are then removed, with the upper lid everted to clear the superior fornix.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ocular Burns", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.2.a · CCMA 3B9 k76

preguntas.pregunta: Which employers must keep a sharps injury log, and how must the log treat the injured worker?
opciones: Those that must keep injury records under 29 CFR part 1904, protecting the worker's confidentiality
Every employer with a single exposed worker, listing the worker's name for follow-up
Only hospitals accredited by CMS-approved organizations, identifying each worker by badge number
Only employers who have had an exposure incident, keeping the log for 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(ii) applies the sharps injury log requirement to any employer already required to keep a log of occupational injuries and illnesses under 29 CFR part 1904, and (h)(5)(iii) keeps it for the period required by 1904.33. The information is recorded so as to protect the confidentiality of the injured employee, which is the opposite of listing names. Accreditation is not the test, and the 30-year period belongs to the employee medical record in (h)(1)(iv).
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), (ii) and (iii), Sharps injury log

preguntas.pregunta: According to the standard, where may staff food and drink NOT be kept?
opciones: In refrigerators, cabinets or on benchtops where blood or OPIM is present
In any refrigerator inside the laboratory building, labeled or not
In a break-room refrigerator that lacks a fluorescent orange biohazard label
In any refrigerator that is not inspected and decontaminated on a set schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(x) forbids keeping food and drink in refrigerators, freezers, shelves, cabinets or on countertops and benchtops where blood or other potentially infectious materials are present. The test is the presence of blood or OPIM in that storage space, not the building or the label. Labels under (g)(1)(i)(A) go on refrigerators that contain blood, which is the reverse of the situation; a break-room refrigerator with no specimens needs no label and may hold lunches.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls

preguntas.pregunta: For an adult fingerstick glucose, which puncture site does the procedure recommend, and which fingers are avoided?
opciones: The side of the fingertip of the 2nd, 3rd or 4th finger; the thumb, index and little finger are avoided
The center of the fingertip pad of the index finger, because it has the thickest tissue over the bone
The side of the fingertip of the little finger, because it is the least sensitive and heals the fastest
The center of the thumb pad, because its larger surface yields the biggest drop with the least squeezing
preguntas.explicacion: The lateral aspect of the distal fingertip of the second, third or fourth finger gives enough tissue depth to protect the bone. The fifth finger is avoided because its tissue may be too shallow, and the thumb and index finger because they are more sensitive. Lancet depth is set to no more than 2.0 mm, and alternate sites such as forearm or palm are used only if the device's instructions approve them.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Fingerstick site · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii · NCMA 2B.19

preguntas.pregunta: Which chest electrode is positioned before V3, and why?
opciones: V4, because V3 is then placed midway between V2 and V4
V5, because V3 is then placed midway between V2 and V5
V6, because V3 is then placed midway between V2 and V6
V1, because V3 is then placed midway between V1 and V4
preguntas.explicacion: V3 has no landmark of its own: it is defined by the two electrodes on either side of it. So V4 goes on first, at the fifth intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line, and V3 is then dropped exactly halfway between V2 and V4. V5 is placed the same way, halfway between V4 and V6.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4

preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen for culture will not be processed for another hour. Where should it be kept?
opciones: At room temperature or in a carbon dioxide incubator, never in the refrigerator
In the refrigerator at 4 degrees, the same as a urine specimen that is held for culture
On ice at the bedside, so the cell count is not altered before it is read
In a freezer at −70 degrees, the way a viral culture specimen is transported
preguntas.explicacion: Cold kills the very organisms the culture is looking for: Neisseria meningitidis and Haemophilus influenzae lose viability at low temperature, so cerebrospinal fluid for microbiology is held at room temperature or in a carbon dioxide incubator until it is examined. Refrigeration is the rule for urine, and freezing at −70 degrees Celsius is how viral culture specimens travel.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples
preguntas.subtema: CSF never refrigerated · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.a.vi · NCMA 2C.15

preguntas.pregunta: Which question in the WHO Annex C script asks for the patient's consent?
opciones: 'Are you willing to be tested?'
'Have you ever had blood taken before?'
'How are you feeling at the moment?'
'Did you understand what I explained?'
preguntas.explicacion: After describing the needle, the tests and where results go, the script asks three things in a row: whether the patient has questions, whether they understood, and whether they are willing to be tested. The last is the consent question. The questions about earlier draws and current feelings belong to the second part of the script, the pre-draw interview.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A patient insists there is a fever because the forehead feels warm to the hand. How reliable is that judgement?
opciones: Unreliable: judging fever by touch is wrong in up to 40% of people, so a reading is taken
Reliable in adults but not in children, whose skin loses heat faster to the room air
Reliable when the hand is placed on the neck instead, where the skin is better perfused
Unreliable only when the room is cold, which chills the skin and hides a real fever
preguntas.explicacion: Deciding whether someone is febrile by feeling the skin is inaccurate in as many as 40% of people, in either direction. When fever is suspected, an instrument reading is obtained and documented with the route used. The patient's own baseline matters too: some people habitually run warmer or cooler than the average.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker challenges your decision, naming a risk to the patient. What is your responsibility?
opciones: Acknowledge the concern rather than ignore the person
Explain the reasoning once and then carry on as planned
Send them to the supervisor before giving an answer
Record the challenge in the patient's own medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Receiving a challenge carries its own duty: acknowledge the concern instead of ignoring the person. Any team member should be empowered to stop the line when they sense an essential safety breach, which halts the process until the issue is resolved. The exchange sets the tone for future ones.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: Two insurers sell Medigap Plan G. What differs between the two policies?
opciones: The price, since policies with the same letter carry the same basic benefits
The benefits, since each company designs the coverage its own policy will give
The waiting period, since each company sets how long pre-existing care waits
The network, since each company contracts hospitals for its lettered policies
preguntas.explicacion: Medigap policies are standardized: those sold under the same letter offer the same basic benefits wherever the buyer lives and whichever company sells them, so price is the difference between two Plan G policies. Ten types are sold in most states, lettered A through D, F, G, and K through N; Massachusetts, Minnesota and Wisconsin standardize their policies differently.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Get Medigap Basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Besides its bed limit, which operating requirement must a critical access hospital meet?
opciones: Emergency services around the clock, seven days a week, with on-site or on-call staff
A surgical suite staffed at every hour so that no patient must wait for an operating room
An intensive rehabilitation program supervised daily by a physician for every patient
A governing board whose majority is made up of patients treated at the hospital
preguntas.explicacion: Among the basic requirements, the hospital must furnish emergency services 24 hours a day, seven days a week, using staff on site or on call within set response times. It also reports an annual average acute inpatient length of stay of 96 hours or less, excluding swing bed and distinct part unit days. The patient-majority board belongs to the health center program.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006400 Information for Critical Access Hospitals: regulatory requirements
preguntas.subtema: Critical access hospital services · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between an active error and a latent error?
opciones: The active one is the act that harms; the latent one is the flaw waiting to
The active one is caught in time; the latent one reaches the patient later
The active one is reported at once; the latent one is found on later audit
The active one involves a device; the latent one involves a staff decision
preguntas.explicacion: An active error is a specific event that harms the patient and involves the professional giving the care, such as operating on the wrong eye. A latent error is a built-in failure in the process — faulty equipment, poor system design, a weak organizational structure — that can sit unnoticed for a long time. A ventilator that malfunctions is latent; not checking it before use is active.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Active and Latent Errors
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: A lipid panel reports HDL and LDL. Which statement matches those two abbreviations?
opciones: HDL is high density lipoprotein, the good cholesterol; LDL is the bad one
HDL is heavy density lipoprotein, the bad cholesterol; LDL is the good one
HDL is high dietary lipid, the good cholesterol; LDL is the low dietary lipid
HDL is hepatic density lipase, the good enzyme; LDL is the liver-derived one
preguntas.explicacion: HDL is high density lipoprotein, described as the good cholesterol, and LDL is low density lipoprotein, the bad one. Both are types of cholesterol carried in the blood, and both appear on the same panel, so mixing them up reverses the meaning of the whole result for the patient.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: What harm from unnecessary or excessive testing is named as falling directly on the patient's arm?
opciones: Repeated phlebotomies that cause phlebitis, pain or bruising
Repeated phlebotomies that cause haemolysis in every tube
Repeated phlebotomies that void the earlier results on file
Repeated phlebotomies that trigger a specimen rejection notice
preguntas.explicacion: Testing without clear clinical justification carries risk: unnecessary or excessive testing may lead to repeated phlebotomies that cause phlebitis, pain or bruising, and may delay essential diagnostic procedures. It also wastes patient and laboratory time, raises costs, and breeds confusion or anxiety through false-positive results.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k42 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k124 · RMA III.C.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which conviction triggers a mandatory exclusion from federal health care programs?
opciones: A conviction for patient abuse or neglect, excluded for at least 5 years
A conviction for patient abuse or neglect, excluded for at least 1 year
A misdemeanor conviction for health care fraud outside Medicare programs
A default on a health education loan taken out during the training years
preguntas.explicacion: Mandatory exclusions follow convictions for Medicare or Medicaid fraud and related offenses, for patient abuse or neglect, for felony health care fraud, theft or other financial misconduct, and for felony drug offenses; the minimum period is 5 years, and aggravating factors can lengthen it. Misdemeanor health care fraud outside those programs and loan defaults fall on the permissive list, where the length varies.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Mandatory Exclusions
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k189

preguntas.pregunta: Why do a health plan's funds transfer and its remittance advice carry the same trace segment?
opciones: So the payment can be matched to the remittance explaining it, called re-association
So the bank can confirm the payer's routing number before the funds are released
So the plan can prove the remittance was delivered before the payment was made
So the provider can post the payment before the remittance advice has arrived
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans are required to put the trace segment of the 835 into the addenda record of the corporate credit or deposit entry that carries the money. That segment is supposed to match the one in the remittance advice describing the payment, so the funds and the explanation of them can be brought together — the step known as re-association.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT
preguntas.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181

preguntas.pregunta: What are the sixty lifetime reserve days of Medicare Part A used for?
opciones: Days ninety-one to a hundred and fifty of an inpatient stay, at $868 a day
Days sixty-one to ninety of an inpatient stay, which are charged at $434 a day
Days twenty-one to a hundred of a skilled nursing stay, at $217 for each day
The first sixty days of every benefit period, which carry no charge at all
preguntas.explicacion: The lifetime reserve days are the sixty extra inpatient days that carry the patient from day ninety-one to day a hundred and fifty, at $868 a day in 2026, and once they are used they are gone. Days sixty-one to ninety are charged at $434, and the skilled nursing rate of $217 belongs to a different benefit altogether.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs

preguntas.pregunta: A patient collecting a stool sample for culture asks whether it matters if urine or toilet water gets into it. What is the answer?
opciones: Yes: urine, toilet water and toilet tissue must all be kept out of the sample
Only urine matters; toilet water is acceptable because the sample is cultured anyway
Only toilet tissue matters, because paper fibers block the culture medium
It matters only for occult blood cards, not for a culture or a parasite exam
preguntas.explicacion: Stool for culture or for parasites must not be mixed with urine, water or toilet tissue. The patient can catch it on plastic wrap laid loosely over the bowl and held by the seat, in a container that fits on the toilet, or with the special tissue in a kit, then transfer it to the clean container provided and return it as soon as possible. The occult blood card has the same rule about urine.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fecal culture (003758), How the Test is Performed; and Stool ova and parasites exam (003756), How the Test is Performed

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has just been given a sedative and an opioid for pain. What does that mean for the forms still waiting for a signature?
opciones: They cannot be signed by the patient after those medications are given
They may be signed as long as a family member witnesses the signature
They may be signed once the patient repeats the instructions back to you
They may be signed because the pain relief was given before the teaching
preguntas.explicacion: Pain is a physiological barrier, so relief should come before teaching. The same paragraph adds the limit that catches people out: sedatives and some pain medications impair the ability to receive and perceive a message, so health care documents cannot be signed by a patient after they are given. A witness or a repeat-back does not fix that.

preguntas.pregunta: The HIPAA Security Rule requires which three categories of safeguards for electronic PHI?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Clinical, financial and operational
Encryption, passwords and firewalls
Privacy, transactions and enforcement rules
preguntas.explicacion: While the Privacy Rule covers all PHI, the Security Rule is specific to electronic PHI and organizes protection into administrative safeguards, such as written procedures, a designated official, access authorization, training, backups and audits; physical safeguards, such as controlling access to hardware, keeping monitors out of public view and training contractors; and technical safeguards, such as access controls, protection of transmissions over open networks and integrity checks. preguntas.pregunta: Which mechanism moves a substance against its concentration gradient, and what does that require?

Simple diffusion, which needs a carrier molecule and cellular energy
Osmosis, which needs a pressure difference across the membrane
Filtration, which needs a carrier molecule and cellular energy

Diabetes, because it is 5.7 % or higher
Diabetes, because it is at or above 6.0 %

Within 30 days after discovery, matching the right-of-access deadline
Within 90 days after discovery, the period a substitute web notice stays posted

Apply an adhesive strip at once, since infants bleed longer than adults
Leave it uncovered and unpressed so that a clot forms without disturbance
Massage the site gently to disperse any haematoma that has started to form

Integrative, because the approach is limited to nutritional products only

5 percent, the share of the blood that sits in the systemic capillaries

It happens during the T wave, which hides it
It happens during the PR segment, which hides it
It happens during the ST segment, which hides it

At least 70 percent, the concentration used to disinfect the skin before venipuncture

preguntas.pregunta: A splint has just been applied. What is checked immediately afterward?

The alignment of the fracture, by repeating the imaging that was ordered
The temperature of the plaster, which must have finished setting hard
The patient's ability to bear weight on the limb that has been splinted

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with lactose intolerance asks whether she must give up milk entirely. What is accurate?

Most people tolerate about three cups at a time if spread across the day

preguntas.explicacion: Cutting back on the milk products that carry lactose usually settles the symptoms, and most people with a low lactase level handle up to about half a cup, roughly 2 to 4 ounces, at one sitting; servings above 8 ounces are what tend to cause trouble. preguntas.pregunta: A respiratory specimen in viral transport medium will not ship to the public health laboratory for five days. How should it be stored?

Refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius, the same as for a same-day shipment
Frozen at −20 degrees Celsius, because the delay runs past 3 to 4 days
At room temperature, the way cerebrospinal fluid for culture is held

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist attaches a 10 mL syringe to a butterfly for a 2-year-old. What is the rule on syringe size in children?

Use any size, since the syringe barrel does not affect the vein; only needle gauge matters
Use a 1 to 5 mL auto-disable syringe, which the WHO recommends for all paediatric draws
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe should have a barrel volume of 1 to 5 mL depending on collection needs, because the vacuum produced by drawing with a larger syringe will often collapse the vein. preguntas.pregunta: A caller asks for a patient by name and wants to know how he is doing. What does the facility directory provision allow?
opciones: Giving the general condition and location, if the patient had a chance to agree or object
Giving the full diagnosis and treatment plan, since the caller already knew the patient's name
Withholding both, because condition and location are never releasable to an outside caller
Giving the religious affiliation to any caller, since clergy need not ask for the patient by name
preguntas.explicacion: A directory may list a patient's name, general condition, religious affiliation and location on the strength of informal permission, obtained by asking outright or through circumstances that clearly give a chance to object. The provider may then release condition and location to anyone asking for the patient by name. Religious affiliation goes to clergy, and only clergy are excused from asking by name.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient on a beta blocker and digoxin has a pulse of 54 beats per minute. How is that finding weighed?
opciones: Both drugs are known to slow the pulse, so the value is read against the medication list
Neither drug affects rate, so a value of 54 always points to a conduction problem
Both drugs speed the pulse, so 54 means the patient has been missing doses lately
The value can be dismissed, because resting rate normally falls below 60 after age 65
preguntas.explicacion: Medicines are part of the reading. Digoxin, used in heart failure, and the beta blockers can both slow the pulse, so a rate in the fifties on those drugs is interpreted with the list in hand. Resting heart rate does not itself drop with age, so age alone does not explain the value.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Aging changes in vital signs

preguntas.pregunta: Rejections keep repeating in one ward, and the laboratory director asks what CLIA expects beyond simply counting them. What does the preanalytic quality assessment standard require?
opciones: Reviewing whether corrective actions worked, revising procedures and telling staff
Reporting the recurring problem to the accrediting organisation each quarter
Suspending testing for that ward until its collection practice is re-approved
Repeating the proficiency testing challenge for every affected specialty
preguntas.explicacion: The standard asks for written policies and an ongoing mechanism to monitor, assess and, where needed, correct problems in the test request and specimen handling systems. That assessment has to include a review of how effective the corrective actions were, revision of the policies so the problem does not come back, and discussion of the reviews with the relevant staff, all documented.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice appeals very few of the claims it gets denied. What does a low denial appeal rate point to?
opciones: Denials being written off or adjusted away instead of being worked
Denials being worked so promptly that few of them are ever appealed
A denial rate that has already fallen below the benchmark for claims
Claims being scrubbed so thoroughly that few of them are ever denied
preguntas.explicacion: The denial appeal rate is the number of denials appealed divided by the total number of denials, and a high ratio is the desirable one. A low ratio is read as a sign that denials are being turned into automatic write-offs or adjustments instead of pursued. It measures what the practice does after a denial, not how many denials it gets: that is the separate denial rate, benchmarked at five to ten per cent.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Denial Appeal Rate

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting chemotherapy asks whether palliative care means she is dying. What is accurate?
opciones: Palliative care treats symptoms and stress at any stage of a serious illness
Palliative care starts only after curative treatment has been stopped for good
Palliative care is another name for the hospice benefit paid under Part A
Palliative care is limited to patients with a prognosis of 6 months or less
preguntas.explicacion: Palliative care is treatment of the discomfort, symptoms and stress of a serious illness, relieving pain, shortness of breath, fatigue, nausea, poor appetite and trouble sleeping. Hospice, which is care at the end of life, always includes palliative care, but a patient may receive palliative care at any stage of an illness while other treatment continues.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Palliative Care: Summary

preguntas.pregunta: In the classic stat-laboratory series of preanalytical errors, which problem dominated the hematology samples?
opciones: Clotted samples
Hemolysed samples
Lost samples
Wrong tube samples
preguntas.explicacion: The most commonly reported preanalytical error types in that stat laboratory were hemolysed samples (46.4 % in biochemistry), clotted samples (43.2 % in hematology), lost samples (6.4 %), inadequate sample-to-anticoagulant ratio (2.9 %), patient misidentification (0.7 %), wrong collection tube (0.3 %) and missing test requests (0.1 %). The core laboratory of the same institution had reported clotted specimens as 55.8 % of its rejections, followed by inadequate volume at 29.3 %.

preguntas.pregunta: Above what income does a health center give no sliding fee discount at all?
opciones: Above 200% of the federal poverty guidelines for the family size
Above 138% of the federal poverty guidelines for the family size
Above 100% of the federal poverty guidelines for the family size
Above the income limit the state sets for its own Medicaid program
preguntas.explicacion: The schedule provides no discount to individuals and families whose annual income is greater than twice the federal poverty guidelines, that is above 200%. Full discounts go to those at or below 100%, with partial discounts in between. The 138% figure belongs to the Medicaid expansion for adults, and state Medicaid limits govern that program rather than the center's discount schedule.

preguntas.pregunta: Which tense does plain language guidance call the simplest and strongest?
opciones: The present tense, which keeps the writing direct
The future tense, which shows what will happen next
The past tense, which is clearer for events already over
The conditional, which covers what may or may not occur
preguntas.explicacion: The present tense is called the simplest and strongest form of a verb; the more conditional or future tense a text carries, the harder the reader has to work. Even when the subject is something that already happened, as much as possible should be written in the present. Other tenses are used only where accuracy demands them.
preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Plain language guides: Writing for understanding, Use the present tense

preguntas.pregunta: Besides screenings and vaccines, what else falls under Medicare's preventive services?
opciones: Counseling and education that help the patient care for their own health
Emergency transport when a screening finds an urgent abnormal result
Prescription drugs that lower the risk of the conditions being screened
Long-term nursing home care once a screening confirms a chronic disease
preguntas.explicacion: Preventive services under Part B are meant to keep patients healthy, catch problems early and steer treatment. They take in exams, vaccines, lab tests and screenings, and also health monitoring programs and the counseling and education that help patients look after their own health.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Preventive & screening services: Description

preguntas.pregunta: Which landmark is used to count down to the right intercostal space for the chest leads?
opciones: The sternal angle, known as the angle of Louis
The xiphoid process, at the lower end of the sternum
The clavicle, counting downward from the first rib
The nipple, taken as the level of the fourth space
preguntas.explicacion: Only bony landmarks give a placement that can be repeated from visit to visit. Two fingers find the sternal angle, then walk down the spaces on the right border of the sternum until the fourth one is reached. Even a small displacement of a chest electrode can change the pattern considerably.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.1 Placement of the Precordial Electrodes

preguntas.pregunta: Nine per cent of a practice's claims were denied last quarter, and the manager wants to know whether that is out of line.
opciones: It is inside the usual range, which runs from five to ten per cent of claims
It is above the usual range, which runs from two to five per cent of claims
It is below the usual range, which runs from ten to fifteen per cent of claims
It is above the usual range, which runs from one to three per cent of claims
preguntas.explicacion: The benchmark for the claim denial rate is five to ten per cent, so nine per cent sits at the top of the normal band rather than outside it. Denial rates climb with errors in demographic, coding, documentation or billing data, and with missed invoices, unclear preauthorization or services billed on medical necessity. Two to five per cent is a different figure: the share of net patient revenue providers never manage to collect.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate

preguntas.pregunta: Which request from a law enforcement official may a covered entity answer under the law enforcement purpose?
opciones: A request for information to identify or locate a suspect, fugitive, witness or missing person
A request to browse the day's schedule for names that might be worth interviewing later
A request for a patient's whole chart because the officer believes a crime may have occurred
A request for records of every patient treated for a gunshot wound in the past five years
preguntas.explicacion: The rule allows disclosures to law enforcement in six circumstances, subject to conditions: as required by law, including court orders, warrants and subpoenas; to identify or locate a suspect, fugitive, material witness or missing person; about a victim or suspected victim of crime; to alert officials to a death suspected to be criminal; when the information is evidence of a crime on the premises; and in a medical emergency away from the premises.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Law Enforcement Purposes

preguntas.pregunta: Which infections does the CDC give as examples requiring Airborne Precautions?
opciones: Tuberculosis, measles, chickenpox and disseminated herpes zoster
Influenza, pertussis and mumps, which travel in respiratory droplets
Clostridioides difficile, scabies and multidrug-resistant organisms
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV, the bloodborne pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: Tuberculosis, measles, chickenpox and disseminated herpes zoster are the infections spread by the airborne route, and smallpox joins them among those for which susceptible staff should be kept out of the room. StatPearls places influenza, pertussis and mumps under Droplet Precautions and C. difficile, scabies and multidrug-resistant organisms under Contact Precautions. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV are bloodborne and are covered by Standard Precautions and the OSHA standard rather than by isolation categories.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: A professional attends a six-hour qualified program and has already met the cycle's requirement. What happens to the extra credits?
opciones: They are lost: three credits are earned, and surplus does not carry over
They are lost: six credits are earned, and surplus does not carry over
They carry over: three credits are earned and applied to the next cycle
They carry over: six credits are earned and applied to the next cycle
preguntas.explicacion: Two hours of attendance at a qualified continuing education program equal one credit, so six hours come to three credits. Credits earned beyond what the cycle requires cannot be applied to the following cycle. Failing to meet the requirement before the expiration date nullifies the credential, and there is a one-month grace period for submitting.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Recertification Requirements; and Recertification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A toddler is tugging at one ear, is irritable and has a low-grade fever. Which finding on otoscopy would support acute otitis media?
opciones: Moderate to severe bulging of the tympanic membrane
Moderate to severe swelling of the external auditory canal
A pale tympanic membrane that moves briskly on insufflation
Tenderness over the mastoid region behind the affected ear
preguntas.explicacion: Ear pain is the most reliable indicator, but small children often show only irritability, poor feeding or disturbed sleep, and about two-thirds run a low-grade fever. The diagnosis rests on history and examination, with no laboratory test or imaging: bulging of the tympanic membrane, or new discharge, is what confirms it. Marked canal swelling points to otitis externa, and mastoid tenderness raises the question of mastoiditis.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Otitis Media", History and Physical and Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: The lymphatic system has no pump of its own. What moves lymph along its vessels?
opciones: Skeletal muscle action, respiratory movement and smooth muscle in the walls
The pumping of the heart, which pushes lymph through the same circuit
The pressure of arterial blood entering the lymph capillaries directly
Gravity alone, which is why lymph moves only when a person is upright
preguntas.explicacion: Lymphatic vessels carry fluid only away from the tissues, and their walls are thin and valved like veins to stop backflow. With no heart of their own, the pressure gradients come from skeletal muscle action, the movements of breathing and contraction of the smooth muscle in the vessel walls.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Lymphatic System: Components of the Lymphatic System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027 I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A mother of a 4-month-old asks what the Dietary Guidelines say about feeding at this stage. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Human milk alone for about the first 6 months, with vitamin D from soon after birth
Human milk alone for about the first 6 months, with iron drops from soon after birth
Human milk with complementary foods already introduced at about 4 months of age
Human milk alone for about the first 12 months, with no supplement of any kind
preguntas.explicacion: The first guideline covers every life stage. For roughly the first half year infants are fed human milk alone, with supplemental vitamin D starting soon after birth; iron-fortified formula is the substitute when human milk is not available. Nutrient-dense complementary foods come in at about 6 months, not at 4.
preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 1
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA B.21

preguntas.pregunta: Which health information falls outside the requirements of the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
opciones: De-identified information, with no code that would allow re-identification disclosed
Health information about a patient who died more than 6 years before the request
Health information kept only on paper charts and never transmitted electronically anywhere
Health information spoken aloud rather than written or stored
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(d) says information that meets the de-identification standard of 164.514 is not individually identifiable and the Privacy Rule does not apply to it, with two provisos: disclosing a code or other means of re-identification is itself a disclosure of PHI, and re-identified information is PHI again. Paper and spoken information remain protected, which is why elevator conversations and unattended charts are violations, and a deceased person's information stays protected for 50 years after death.

preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report mentions the visceral layer of a serous membrane. Which surface is that layer covering?
opciones: The organ itself, while the parietal layer lines the cavity wall
The cavity wall, while the parietal layer covers the organ itself
The joint space, while the parietal layer covers the bone ends
The airway lining, while the parietal layer covers the skin surface
preguntas.explicacion: A serous membrane has two layers with a thin fluid space between them. The parietal layer lines the wall of the cavity and the visceral layer clings to the organs, the viscera. The fluid in between lets the heart beat and the lungs inflate with little friction. Joint cavities are lined by synovial membrane instead.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Membranes of the Ventral Body Cavity

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a weight management plan asks how much activity is advised for healthy adults. What is recommended?
opciones: 150 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus strength work on 2 days
150 minutes a week of vigorous aerobic activity plus strength work on 5 days
75 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus strength work on 2 days
300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity with no strength work needed
preguntas.explicacion: Healthy adults are told to get at least 150 minutes a week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, brisk walking or dancing being the usual examples, together with muscle-strengthening work covering all the major muscle groups on two or more days. Moderate intensity speeds the heart and the breathing without overworking the person.
preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Healthy Eating & Physical Activity for Weight Management — Get regular physical activity

preguntas.pregunta: Which change to the intake forms is recommended so a practice welcomes patients from the LGBTQ community?
opciones: Add the term partner beside spouse, and include transgender as an option
Add a field for the sex assigned at birth and leave the rest unchanged
Add a note asking staff to record the patient's appearance and manner
Add a required field naming the patient's next of kin and their gender
preguntas.explicacion: Among the steps for a welcoming practice: train staff to refer to patients by their name and chosen descriptive pronouns, and on intake forms include the term partner in addition to spouse, and include transgender as an option. Forgetting gender-neutral terms such as partner is listed as a challenge, as is making assumptions about behaviour from appearance.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is scheduled for a catheterized urine culture and says he has no urge to urinate. What preparation applies?
opciones: He should not have urinated for at least 1 hour, and may be told to drink a glass of water 15 to 20 minutes before
He should not have urinated for at least 2 to 3 hours, and may be told to drink a glass of water 1 hour before
He should empty his bladder completely just before the procedure so the catheter drains only fresh urine
He should fast for 6 hours and avoid caffeine and smoking, as required before a urea breath test
preguntas.explicacion: The only preparation for a catheterized specimen is not to urinate for at least an hour beforehand; a patient without the urge to void may be asked to drink a glass of water 15 to 20 minutes before the procedure. The 2-to-3-hour bladder dwell is the ideal for a voided clean-catch, emptying the bladder first would leave nothing to collect, and fasting with no caffeine or smoking belongs to breath and metanephrine testing.
