preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has just climbed the stairs asks why the pulse is not taken immediately. What is the reason?
opciones: A resting heart rate requires the patient to have been at rest for at least 10 minutes
A resting heart rate requires the patient to have been at rest for at least 30 minutes
The pulse cannot be counted at all while the rhythm is still faster than 100 beats a minute
The pulse must be taken at the same hour each visit for the values to be comparable
preguntas.explicacion: The figure charted as the resting heart rate only means something if the patient has been resting, and 10 minutes is the interval given for that. A rate taken during or just after exercise is an exercise heart rate and says something different: it reports fitness, not baseline.

preguntas.pregunta: A health center's sliding fee schedule is being explained to a patient. Who receives a full discount?
opciones: Patients with income at or below 100% of the federal poverty guidelines
Patients with income at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines
Patients with income at or below 400% of the federal poverty guidelines
Patients who have applied for Medicaid and are waiting for a decision
preguntas.explicacion: A health center's schedule of discounts must give a full discount to individuals and families at or below 100% of the federal poverty guidelines, although a nominal charge may be collected from them, and no discount above 200% of those guidelines. Between the two figures the discounts are partial and step down by income across at least three pay classes. A pending Medicaid application is not the criterion.
preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Health Center Program Compliance Manual, Chapter 9: Sliding Fee Discount Program

preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, when must a mask with eye protection or a face shield be worn?
opciones: When blood may splash or spray and contamination of the eyes, nose or mouth can be anticipated
Whenever gloves are worn, since hand contact with blood implies facial exposure
Whenever gross contamination is anticipated, as with autopsies or orthopaedic surgery
Whenever the patient is on Droplet Precautions, but not for routine venipuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(x) ties facial protection to the task: masks combined with goggles, glasses with solid side shields, or chin-length face shields are worn whenever splashes, spray, spatter or droplets of blood or OPIM may be generated and contamination of the eyes, nose or mouth can reasonably be anticipated. Gloves have their own trigger in (d)(3)(ix). Gross contamination, as in autopsies, is the trigger for caps, hoods and shoe covers in (d)(3)(xii). Droplet Precautions are a CDC isolation category, not the test this OSHA paragraph applies.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(x), Masks, Eye Protection, and Face Shields
preguntas.subtema: Face and eye protection · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A nursery nurse asks why the laboratory keeps a separate list of critical limits for newborns. What is the reason?
opciones: Neonatal limits differ from adult ones for several analytes; a published list gives a lower glucose threshold and higher haemoglobin thresholds for newborns
Neonatal limits are the adult limits halved, since newborn blood volume is smaller and the same absolute change carries more weight
Neonatal specimens are capillary, and capillary blood has no critical limits because its values are not comparable with venous ones
Neonatal limits are the same as adult limits; the separate list exists only because newborn results are reported to the mother's chart
preguntas.explicacion: Published critical-limit tables carry a separate neonatal section: in the 2003 list, glucose becomes critical below 30 mg/dL (1.7 mmol/L) in a newborn against 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L) in adults, haemoglobin below 8.5 or above 23 g/dL against 6.6 and 19.9 g/dL, and entries such as cord blood IgM above 20 mg/dL exist only for neonates. Those figures come from one author's list, so the working numbers are the ones each laboratory agrees with its clinicians.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), Table 1 and Table 3
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13

preguntas.pregunta: A patient gives a name at check-in that does not match the one on the chart. What is the practice?
opciones: Refer to the patient by the name and pronouns they state
Refer to the patient by the legal name until it is amended
Refer to the patient by the name the insurance card carries
Refer to the patient by a title such as sir or ma'am instead
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are trained to refer to patients by their name and their chosen descriptive pronouns. Sharing your own pronouns during an introduction helps a transgender patient feel safe doing the same, and asking a patient which pronoun they use counts as part of the assessment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: Interference is still on the tracing after every electrode has been checked. Where does the search go next?
opciones: To the equipment near the room, following the guide step by step
To the calibration of the unit, using the external calibrator on it
To the age of the electrodes, changing the whole card being used
To the patient's jewelry, taking off the wristwatch and the rings
preguntas.explicacion: Alternating-current interference comes from one of two places: poor contact at an electrode or equipment near the room. With contact ruled out, the technician works through the trouble-shooting guide. Watches, glasses, rings and bracelets are not a cause.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the cell membrane described as selectively permeable?
opciones: Its hydrophobic interior lets only small nonpolar substances cross unaided
Its hydrophobic interior lets only large charged substances cross unaided
Its rigid protein lattice lets only water and salts cross without a carrier
Its double layer of cholesterol lets only proteins cross without a carrier
preguntas.explicacion: The membrane is a double layer of phospholipids with the water-fearing tails packed in the middle. That interior lets small nonpolar molecules such as oxygen and carbon dioxide slip straight through, while water-soluble things like glucose, amino acids and electrolytes need a channel or a carrier protein to get across.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.1 The Cell Membrane, Transport Across the Cell Membrane

preguntas.pregunta: What is syncope?
opciones: A transient loss of consciousness and postural tone with spontaneous recovery, from reduced cerebral perfusion
A brief seizure with loss of sphincter control and confusion on waking, from an acute neurologic event
A feeling that one is about to pass out without actually losing consciousness, caused by cerebral hypoperfusion
A prolonged loss of consciousness lasting several minutes, from a fall in blood glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Syncope is a transient loss of consciousness and postural tone followed by spontaneous recovery, resulting from decreased cerebral perfusion. The feeling of being about to pass out without doing so is what the chapter calls near syncope or presyncope, and an episode lasting more than a few minutes is not syncope but more likely a seizure. Hypoglycemia is listed among conditions that mimic fainting.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", sections Continuing Education Activity and Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: In the outpatient setting, what is the first-listed diagnosis?
opciones: The condition chiefly responsible for the services provided at that encounter
The condition that carries the highest reimbursement among those documented
The chronic condition the patient has been treated for over the longest time
The condition established after all the testing ordered that day is resulted
preguntas.explicacion: Outpatient reporting uses the term first-listed diagnosis rather than principal diagnosis, and it is the condition, problem or other reason for the encounter shown in the record to be chiefly responsible for the services given; coexisting conditions follow as additional codes. Chronic conditions may be coded repeatedly when they are treated, but that does not put them first, and reimbursement never drives the sequence.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section IV.A and IV.G

preguntas.pregunta: How often does the contingency planning guidance expect a written downtime and recovery policy to be reviewed?
opciones: At least every two years, and a paper copy is kept in the units and off site
At least every six months, and a paper copy is filed with the software vendor
At least every five years, and a paper copy is posted in the waiting area
Only after a downtime occurs, and a paper copy goes to each staff member
preguntas.explicacion: The written policy is what makes everyone act the same way during a planned or unplanned outage: when a downtime is declared, who leads it on the clinical and the technical side, how people are told, and how the information gathered on paper gets back into the system. It is reviewed at least every two years, and a printed copy lives both in the units and in a safe off-site place.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime policy · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which group of donors was fainting most often reported in?
opciones: Female donors giving for the first time
Male donors over fifty giving again
Male donors under thirty giving again
Female donors over sixty giving again
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting was reported in 5.3 per cent of cases and usually happened in first-time female blood donors, while vasovagal attacks occurred occasionally and ranged from mild to severe. It is a reminder to ask about earlier faints and to have the chair ready for a reaction.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with polycythemia has a hematocrit of 60 %. What must be considered when collecting blood for a prothrombin time?
opciones: The reduced plasma volume leaves excess citrate; the citrate amount must be adjusted or the PT reads falsely prolonged
The excess red cells consume clotting factors as they settle, so the sample should be drawn in an EDTA tube instead of citrate
The sample should be diluted with saline before testing so that the analyzer can detect the clot optically
No adjustment is needed, because plasma-based coagulation tests are independent of the patient's hematocrit
preguntas.explicacion: When the hematocrit is above 55 %, there is less plasma in the tube for the same volume of blood, so the fixed amount of sodium citrate is relatively excessive and the prothrombin time comes out artificially prolonged unless the citrate volume is readjusted. EDTA is not used for coagulation testing, and dilution with saline is itself listed as a contaminant that alters clotting times.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors (Polycythemia with a hematocrit greater than 55 %)
preguntas.subtema: High hematocrit and citrate · PBT IV.A.3 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(5) INR (2027: b.(8)) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has just received a routine vaccine. How long is the patient observed before leaving?
opciones: 15 minutes for most vaccines, and 30 minutes for some COVID-19 recipients
5 minutes for most vaccines, and 15 minutes for some COVID-19 recipients
30 minutes for every vaccine, whichever product has just been administered
No observation, provided the screening before the dose found no problem
preguntas.explicacion: A 15-minute observation period is recommended after most vaccines, and some people should be watched for 30 minutes after a COVID-19 vaccine. The patient is seated or lying down for the injection, and the staff watch for the warning signs of fainting, such as weakness, dizziness and pallor. Epinephrine and equipment for managing an airway are kept ready for immediate use.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: After the Visit
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(1)

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is most likely to put muscle tremor on the tracing?
opciones: One who is cold, tense or has a nerve or muscle disorder
One who has a slow heart rate or a first-degree block
One whose chest hair keeps the electrodes from sticking
One whose lead wires were left looped across the table
preguntas.explicacion: Tremor signals come from skeletal muscle, so the patients who produce them are the ones who are shivering, tense, or living with a muscle or nerve disorder. Hair under an electrode and looped wires cause different faults: electrodes that fall off and interference from the room current.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k149 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of natural rubber latex is linked to the type IV hypersensitivity reaction?
opciones: The chemical antioxidants added during processing
The natural rubber proteins bound by IgE antibodies
The cornstarch powder that carries particles in the air
The fruit proteins that cross-react with banana and kiwi
preguntas.explicacion: The natural proteins in rubber are associated with asymptomatic sensitisation and with type I IgE-mediated hypersensitivity. What can produce type IV reactions is the chemical antioxidants added while the latex is processed. Cornstarch in gloves and tyre dust are the usual sources of inhaled particles, and cross-reacting foods are a separate risk marker.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Introduction and section Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii

preguntas.pregunta: Which circumstances raise the chance that a needlestick from an HIV-positive patient transmits the virus?
opciones: A visibly bloody device, a needle that was in a vein or artery, and a deep injury
A solid needle, a superficial scratch, and contact limited to intact skin
A small-bore needle, a source on treatment, and a splash onto the forearm
A used lancet, a gloved hand, and a source patient with a low viral load
preguntas.explicacion: The average risk after a percutaneous injury with HIV-infected blood is about 0.3 percent, but it is not the same for every injury. A case-control study found the risk higher when the worker met a larger quantity of blood, which showed up as a visibly bloody device, a procedure that put the needle in a vein or an artery, or a deep injury. Large-bore hollow needles and a source with a high viral load point the same way; intact skin carries no meaningful risk at all.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Risk of Infection After a Needlestick Injury: HIV; StatPearls, "Needlestick", Etiology: HIV
preguntas.subtema: What makes an exposure worse · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which task does the data backup plan specification of the contingency plan standard require?
opciones: Creating and keeping copies of the information that can be retrieved exactly
Restoring the information that was lost once the systems are running again
Keeping critical processes going while the office works in emergency mode
Ranking which applications and data matter most to the rest of the planning
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan standard splits into five specifications, and the wording of each decides the answer. The data backup plan is about making and maintaining retrievable exact copies beforehand; restoring what was lost is the disaster recovery plan, and the criticality analysis is the addressable one that ranks them.
preguntas.subtema: Data backup plan · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant resigns on a Friday. Which addressable specification tells the practice what to do about her access to the system?
opciones: Termination procedures, which end access when the working arrangement finishes
Access establishment and modification, which reviews and changes a user's rights
Workforce clearance, which decides whether her access was appropriate to start
Authorization and supervision, which covers staff working where records are open
preguntas.explicacion: Workforce security carries three addressable specifications, and the one written for the end of an employment or other arrangement is termination procedures. The other three answer questions asked while the person is still working there, which is why they are easy to reach for and wrong here.
preguntas.subtema: Termination procedures · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: After installing a longer, faster pneumatic tube route, a laboratory sees more hemolysed samples. Which change in how tubes are sent is supported by the literature as reducing transport hemolysis?
opciones: Using padded inserts inside the carriers, gel tubes and properly filled tubes
Sending tubes uncapped so that pressure changes do not build up inside them
Sending each tube in its own carrier at the highest speed to shorten travel time
Chilling the carriers before use so that the red cells are less fragile in transit
preguntas.explicacion: Variables shown to increase hemolysis during transport are rapid accelerations and decelerations, greater length of travel and high speeds; variables shown to reduce it are gel tubes, properly filled tubes and padded inserts within the canisters. Higher speed works in the wrong direction, and neither uncapping nor chilling appears in the evidence the study cites.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.D.4 · CCMA 3E k144 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: The practice is retiring three computers and donating them to a school. Which Security Rule standard governs that?
opciones: Device and media controls, which require removing ePHI before media are reused
Workforce security, which requires authorization and supervision of staff who reach ePHI
Information access management, which limits access to what a person's role calls for
Security incident procedures, which require identifying and responding to known incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls are a physical safeguard covering the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media holding ePHI into and out of a facility, their movement inside it, and the final disposition of both the information and the equipment. The rule adds an explicit duty to implement procedures for removing ePHI from electronic media before those media are made available for reuse.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Media disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's right to refuse care is founded on which ethical principle?
opciones: Autonomy, the right to make informed decisions about one's own care
Beneficence, which asks that actions be taken for the patient's benefit
Non-maleficence, which requires steps be taken so no one is harmed
Justice, which spreads benefits and risks evenly and without bias
preguntas.explicacion: Refusal of care rests on autonomy: every person may make informed decisions about their health care, and staff should not impose their own beliefs or decisions on the patient. Beneficence, non-maleficence and justice sit alongside autonomy and guide the same difficult situations, but the refusal itself is not founded on them.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A lesion is to be excised just beside the eye. Which antiseptic is relatively contraindicated there, and what may be substituted?
opciones: Chlorhexidine is avoided; a 3% chloroxylenol surgical scrub may be used safely instead
Povidone-iodine is avoided; a 3% chloroxylenol surgical scrub may be used safely instead
Chlorhexidine is avoided; a hexachlorophene emulsion may be used safely on that area
Povidone-iodine is avoided; a hydrogen peroxide solution may be used safely on that area
preguntas.explicacion: Chlorhexidine can cause irreversible keratitis and, through a perforated eardrum, sensorineural deafness, so it is relatively contraindicated on skin at or beside the eye and the conchal bowl. A 3 percent chloroxylenol scrub is the named substitute, and aqueous povidone-iodine scrubs can also be used safely near those areas.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.d

preguntas.pregunta: What defeats a claim of battery?
opciones: Consent, whether it was expressed or implied by taking part
Absence of any lasting injury from the contact that occurred
Absence of an intention to hurt the person who was touched
Presence of a witness who saw the contact and thought it fine
preguntas.explicacion: Battery is intentional harmful or offensive contact without consent, so consent is the defense — express, such as agreeing, or implied, such as joining in a sport. No actual damages need be shown, because the contact itself counts as the injury. Intending the contact is enough; the defendant does not have to have meant it to be harmful.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: battery
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(6) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31

preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations is a covered entity REQUIRED, rather than merely permitted, to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual who requests access or an accounting, and to HHS investigating compliance
To law enforcement on request, and to the patient's employer for workers' compensation
To any treating provider, and to the health plan paying the claim, on request
To public health authorities, and to a coroner or medical examiner determining cause of death
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(a)(2) names only two required disclosures: to the individual when requested under the right of access or the right to an accounting of disclosures, and to the Secretary of HHS when required to investigate or determine the entity's compliance. Everything else in the rule, treatment, payment, operations, public health, law enforcement, coroners and workers' compensation, is permitted under conditions but not compelled by HIPAA itself, although other laws may require some of those reports.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(a)(1) and (a)(2), Permitted and required disclosures

preguntas.pregunta: The tape on a pack has changed color after the cycle. What has that told the staff?
opciones: Only that the pack was run through a sterilization cycle, not that sterility was achieved
That the pack is sterile, since the ink reacts only when every parameter has been met
That the resistant spores inside the pack were inactivated during the exposure period
That the air was fully removed from the chamber before the steam was admitted to it
preguntas.explicacion: A chemical indicator is cheap, convenient and limited: affixed outside each pack, it shows the package went through a cycle, and it does not prove sterilization happened. Only a biological indicator made of resistant spores measures the killing power of the process directly, and an indicator inside the pack is preferred as well, to verify the sterilant got in.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA Essential 5

preguntas.pregunta: Which six elements make up a point-of-care competency assessment under the accreditation requirements described for CLIA?
opciones: Direct observation of testing, review of result recording and reporting, review of QC records, observation of maintenance and function checks, testing of previously analyzed specimens, and problem-solving assessment
A written examination, a practical examination, a review of the operator's education, an interview with the director, an annual retraining session, and a signed attestation of competence
Observation of specimen collection, review of patient identification, review of infection control practice, observation of waste disposal, a safety quiz, and documentation of the hepatitis B vaccine
Enrollment in proficiency testing, review of PT scores, comparison with a referral laboratory, an external inspection, a peer audit of records, and a manufacturer's certificate of training
preguntas.explicacion: The six elements are: direct observation of test operation; monitoring of recording and reporting of results; review of intermediate steps such as results and QC records; direct observation of preventive maintenance and function checks; testing of specimens previously analyzed; and assessment of problem-solving skills. Waived tests are excluded from the CMS competency assessment requirement, though states and accreditors may still require it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Quality Control and Lab Safety (six competency elements)
preguntas.subtema: Six competency elements · PBT VI.C Proficiency Testing and Competency Assessment · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.vi

preguntas.pregunta: A vaccine is to be given subcutaneously to an adult. Which angle and which site are used?
opciones: 45 degrees into the fatty tissue over the upper outer triceps of the arm
90 degrees into the fatty tissue over the upper outer triceps of the arm
45 degrees into the fatty tissue of the thigh, the site used at every age
90 degrees into the deltoid muscle, the site recommended for adult doses
preguntas.explicacion: A subcutaneous vaccine is injected at a 45-degree angle into the fatty tissue below the dermis and above the muscle, after pinching up the skin and that tissue. For infants under 12 months the fatty tissue of the thigh is used; from one year onward it is the fatty tissue over the upper outer triceps. MMR, varicella, IPV, MMRV and PPSV23 are given this way, and the last two may also be given intramuscularly.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 6: Subcutaneous Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(2)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with asthma needs a beta blocker for a cardiac problem. Which choice fits current recommendations?
opciones: A beta-1 selective agent such as atenolol, bisoprolol, metoprolol or esmolol
A non-selective agent such as propranolol, which binds beta-1 and beta-2 alike
Sotalol, whose potassium channel blockade also protects the airway from spasm
Labetalol, whose alpha-1 blockade cancels the airway effect of beta-2 blockade
preguntas.explicacion: Beta blockers were once ruled out in asthma altogether. Recommendations now allow the cardio-selective ones, which bind only beta-1, while the non-selective agents remain out because beta-2 blockade can bring on bronchospasm. Sotalol's extra effect is on potassium channels and it prolongs the QT interval; the alpha-1 blockade of carvedilol and labetalol helps blood pressure, not breathing.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Beta Blockers", Contraindications and Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.d · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3

preguntas.pregunta: In the collaborative care model, where is care usually delivered?
opciones: In the primary care setting, unless the patient needs specialty services
In a separate behavioral health clinic, so that the two records stay apart
In the hospital outpatient department, where partial hospitalization runs
In a community mental health center, the only site the model recognizes
preguntas.explicacion: Medical and behavioral health clinicians work as a team on the patient's concerns, and integrated teams deliver that care in the primary care setting unless patients request or require specialty services. Behavioral health clinicians often sit right in the medical setting; where they do not, they are folded into the established procedures, team and information systems. The gain is coordination and communication.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Academy for Integrating Behavioral Health and Primary Care: How would I recognize integrated behavioral health?
preguntas.subtema: Collaborative care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: Why is calling a patient courageous for having overcome a disability discouraged?
opciones: It makes people inspirational only for the disability
It reveals protected information to the other patients
It puts an opinion where the diagnosis belongs in the chart
It suggests the person no longer needs accommodations
preguntas.explicacion: One of the tips is not portraying people with disabilities as inspirational solely because of the disability: has overcome and is courageous sit in the do-not-use column, while is successful and is productive are the wording to use. The aim is dignity and respect rather than praise.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, "Communicating With and About People with Disabilities", Tips
preguntas.subtema: Person-first language · CCMA 6B k195 · RMA I.D.1.e · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is the earliest and most sensitive warning that a patient is deteriorating?
opciones: A rising respiratory rate, which usually moves before the pressure falls
A falling blood pressure, which moves before the other measurements shift
A rising temperature, which is the first of the vital signs to change
A falling oxygen saturation, which precedes any change in the breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing changes early. Tachypnea is a more accurate and earlier marker of deterioration than hypotension, and it commonly comes before hypoxemia as well; one study found that a rate above 35 breaths a minute was the single strongest predictor of a life-threatening event. It is also the value most often left uncounted.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Patient Safety and Early Detection of Clinical Deterioration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · RMA III.E.3 Respiration b · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement must appear prominently at the top of a notice of privacy practices?
opciones: A header stating how medical information may be used and disclosed and how to access it
The names of every business associate that may receive the patient's information during care
The civil penalty amounts for HIPAA violations, from $100 up to $50,000 per violation
A list of the 18 identifiers that turn health information into protected information
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be written in plain language and open with a prominently displayed header telling the reader that it describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking them to review it carefully. It then describes uses for treatment, payment and operations with examples, the other permitted purposes, the uses that require authorization, the individual's rights, the entity's duties, how to complain without retaliation, a contact person and the effective date. Business associate names, penalty tables and identifier lists are not required elements.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1), Required elements of the notice
preguntas.subtema: Content of the notice · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: To open the pre-draw interview, which question follows the principle of open-ended questioning first?
opciones: 'How have blood draws gone for you in the past?'
'Have you ever fainted during a blood draw?'
'You're not scared of needles, are you?'
'Did you fast for twelve hours like the doctor said?'
preguntas.explicacion: The technique table says to begin with open-ended questions that allow a free-flowing account, and to move to closed-ended questions afterwards. The other three are closed or leading: the fainting question is a legitimate item from the WHO Annex C interview, but it invites a yes or no, and the leading question about needles steers the answer.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), Open-ended questioning
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k40 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 k126 · CMA I.A.3.b / 2027 A.3.b · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient aged 68 still works for a company with 40 employees and has the group plan. Who pays first?
opciones: The group health plan pays first and Medicare pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first and the group health plan pays second for that patient
The group health plan pays first only for hospital care under Part A
Medicare pays first because the patient is already past the age of 65
preguntas.explicacion: For a patient 65 or older covered by a group health plan through current employment, the group plan pays first when the employer has 20 or more employees, and Medicare pays second; with fewer than 20 employees, the order is reversed. The threshold changes to 100 or more employees when Medicare entitlement rests on disability. The rule covers the whole claim, not Part A alone.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 5B k66 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with Original Medicare asks whether she can see a doctor while she is staying in Puerto Rico.
opciones: Yes, any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare, anywhere in the United States
Yes, but only for emergency care while she is away from her own home state
No, unless she joins a Medicare Advantage plan with a nationwide network
No, unless the doctor there agrees to bill her as an out-of-network provider
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare lets a patient use any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare anywhere in the United States, and that reaches all fifty states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and American Samoa. Networks and advance approvals belong to the other route: a Medicare Advantage plan, where the patient may have to use the plan's own doctors.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A range-of-motion note says the patient moved the arm laterally away from the body at the shoulder. Which movement is that?
opciones: Abduction, the opposite of adduction
Adduction, the opposite of abduction
Flexion, the opposite of extension
Rotation, the opposite of circumduction
preguntas.explicacion: Abduction moves a limb laterally away from the midline, and adduction brings it back toward or across the midline; spreading and closing the fingers count as the same pair. Flexion and extension work in the front-to-back plane instead, and circumduction is a circular sweep that strings four of these movements together.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 9.5 Types of Body Movements, Abduction and Adduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A passenger in a burning car is not breathing. Using Maslow's hierarchy to prioritize, what comes first?
opciones: Moving the passenger away from the car, for safety
Starting rescue breaths where the passenger is sitting
Checking the airway before touching the passenger
Calling for help and waiting beside the vehicle
preguntas.explicacion: The worked example is exactly this: the passenger is removed from the car first because of safety, even though breathing has stopped. Only after safety is handled and help is called does resuscitation follow. Physiological needs and safety sit together at the base of the pyramid.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 4 Nursing Process, Prioritization
preguntas.subtema: Prioritizing needs · CCMA 1E k29

preguntas.pregunta: Every September the same clinic is swamped by school physicals and flu shots. What does the open access guidance tell it to prepare?
opciones: A contingency plan naming who can supplement or stand in for each physician those days
A block of the schedule set aside weeks ahead for the physicals and the flu shots
A waiting list of patients willing to come in whenever another patient cancels
Another six to eight weeks of longer days, as when the practice cleared its backlog
preguntas.explicacion: The model asks for a contingency plan for days, or parts of days, when demand far outstrips the physicians available, and that plan has to say who can supplement or substitute for each of them. The guidance also tells the group to be proactive about the surges it can predict, and names school physicals and flu shots as the examples.

Requesting what you want the provider to do about it
Reviewing the admitting diagnoses and the code status

preguntas.pregunta: Which muscles do most of the work of quiet breathing, and what role do the lungs themselves play?
opciones: The diaphragm and intercostals work; the lungs stay passive throughout
The diaphragm and intercostals work; the lungs pull themselves open
The lungs contract on their own; the diaphragm stays passive throughout
The abdominal wall muscles work; the diaphragm stays passive throughout
preguntas.explicacion: Contraction and relaxation of the diaphragm and of the intercostal muscles between the ribs create most of the pressure changes that pull air in and push it out. The lungs are passive: the sticky pleural fluid makes them follow the chest wall outward on inspiration, and the recoil of that wall compresses them on expiration.

preguntas.pregunta: Which skin cancer is the most fatal, and which cell does it arise from?
opciones: Melanoma, from the melanocytes that make the pigment of the skin
Melanoma, from the keratinocytes of the layer beneath the surface
Basal cell carcinoma, from the melanocytes that make the pigment
Squamous cell carcinoma, from the stem cells of the deepest layer
preguntas.explicacion: Melanoma is uncontrolled growth of melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells, and usually starts from a mole; it spreads readily and is hard to catch before it reaches other organs, which makes it the deadliest of the skin cancers. Basal cell carcinoma is the most common one, and squamous cell carcinoma arises from keratinocytes.

preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is put in the specimen refrigerator to await pick-up. Why is that the wrong choice?
opciones: Whole blood for these assays is held at room temperature, not chilled
Whole blood for these assays is held frozen, and chilling is not enough
Refrigeration bursts the red cells and haemolyses the whole specimen
Refrigeration hardens the gel barrier and traps the plasma underneath
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood drawn for clotting tests is kept at room temperature, roughly eighteen to twenty-four degrees, and refrigeration is avoided because cold can activate factor VII. Chilling whole blood also lowers factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, which can imitate a bleeding disorder.

Disclosure: the risks of the procedure were never fully listed
Capacity: the patient's understanding was never assessed
Documentation: the consent form was never signed

preguntas.pregunta: How often should the mopping solution be replaced during floor cleaning?
opciones: Every three patient rooms, and no less often than every 60 minutes
Every three patient rooms, and no less often than every 30 minutes
Every ten patient rooms, and no less often than every 60 minutes
Once per shift, unless the solution turns visibly cloudy before then
preguntas.explicacion: If the water and disinfectant mixture is not changed regularly, mopping stops cleaning and starts spreading heavy contamination through the building. The interval given is about every three patient rooms and never longer than 60 minutes. Mop heads and cleaning cloths are also decontaminated regularly, with laundering and drying at least daily.

Care continues for 30 days from the notice, then stops at the deadline
Care stops, but the practice must file the records with the state board
Care stops, provided the patient is handed a list of low-cost clinics
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency or while the patient is critically ill, termination has to be delayed until the patient is medically stable. Abandonment cases have consistently affirmed the responsibility to keep caring for a patient in a critical stage of illness regardless of ability to pay, and one court held a psychiatrist liable where a foreseeable risk of self-harm was involved.

preguntas.pregunta: How does an ultrasonic cleaner remove soil from an instrument?
opciones: Acoustic waves cause cavitation and implosion that break the bonds holding debris on surfaces
Acoustic waves heat the bath to a temperature that dissolves protein and fat residue away
Acoustic waves drive a detergent through lumens under pressure until the channels run clear
Acoustic waves inactivate the bacteria directly, which then wash off with the loosened debris
preguntas.explicacion: Ultrasonic cleaning works mechanically: waves of acoustic energy travel through the solution and the cavitation and implosion they produce break the bonds that hold particles to the surface. The sound alone does not kill bacteria to any useful degree, and used cleaning solutions can themselves carry bacterial contamination, since they make no antibacterial claim.

preguntas.pregunta: Among the oral antidiabetic agents, which one carries the highest hypoglycemia risk because of its long half-life and active metabolites?
opciones: Glyburide
Glipizide
Glimepiride
Repaglinide
preguntas.explicacion: All three sulfonylureas named here can drop the glucose, but glyburide carries the highest risk: it lasts a long time and leaves active metabolites behind, which is also why it is avoided once the eGFR falls under 30. Glipizide and glimepiride are generally preferred for that reason. Repaglinide is a meglitinide; hypoglycemia is its main adverse effect too, but it is usually milder because the drug acts briefly.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are prothrombin time results usually reported as an INR in addition to seconds?
opciones: PT in seconds varies between laboratories and methods, and the ratio makes results comparable
Seconds measure only the intrinsic pathway, and the ratio adds in the extrinsic pathway result
The ratio corrects the raw clotting time for the patient's hematocrit and platelet count
The ratio converts the prothrombin time into the equivalent partial thromboplastin time
preguntas.explicacion: A prothrombin time counts the seconds a sample takes to clot, but that number differs from one laboratory or reagent method to another. Converting it to an international normalized ratio lets providers compare and interpret results from different laboratories and methods, which matters when a warfarin dose is adjusted on the basis of serial tests. The PTT is a separate test that examines different clotting factors.

Section 6, which also covers containment and cleanup after a spill
Section 9, which also gives the flash point and the boiling range
Section 7, which also covers safe storage and incompatible products

preguntas.pregunta: A cane is being adjusted to a patient's height. Where should the handle sit?
opciones: Level with the patient's wrist, so that the elbow bends a little on the grip
Level with the patient's hip, so that the elbow stays straight on the grip
Level with the patient's waist, so that the shoulder can be raised slightly
Level with the patient's elbow, so that the forearm rests along the shaft
preguntas.explicacion: Standing straight with the arms down, the handle should reach the crease of the wrist; gripping it then leaves the elbow slightly bent. Hip level is the landmark for the handles of a walker, not a cane. The patient is taught to look ahead rather than down at the feet, and to check the rubber tips daily and replace them once they wear.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck at the end of her shift and says she will go to occupational health tomorrow. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Be seen at once, rather than waiting twelve to seventy-two hours for a visit
Be seen within seven days, the deadline that applies to hepatitis B treatment
Be seen at the end of the shift, once the incident report has been written
Be seen within ninety days, while the baseline sample is being preserved
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up with occupational health should be immediate rather than delayed by twelve to seventy-two hours, because the decisions that depend on it are time-sensitive: baseline testing, hepatitis B immune globulin within about a day, and antiretroviral prophylaxis started preferably within hours. The ninety days is how long a baseline sample is preserved when the employee does not consent to HIV testing on the spot, not a period in which to be seen.

Seated upright, with the chin lifted and eyes closed
Standing, leaning back against the corridor wall
Seated backwards, with both legs stretched out flat

A gain in lean mass, which the index reads as a fall in body fat
A measurement error, since the index moves slowly by its nature
Dehydration only, since fluid loss is the one thing that moves it fast

preguntas.pregunta: Which test is called the gold standard for diagnosing a type I hypersensitivity to latex?
opciones: The skin prick test, though it is not available in the United States
The serum assay for bound IgE, which rarely gives a false positive
A trial of exposure to latex, run as the first step by an allergist
The blood test for latex antibodies, which is the in-vivo assay
preguntas.explicacion: Skin prick testing, an in-vivo assay that applies a non-ammoniated latex extract and watches for a wheal, is considered the gold standard for type I hypersensitivity to latex, yet it is not available in the United States for want of an approved reagent. Its shape, which is rod-like
Its stain, which is negative
Its habitat, which is the soil

Have him write the dose and the times down and file the note in the chart

preguntas.pregunta: A differential on a patient with a bacterial infection shows 80 percent of one leukocyte type. Which type is normally the most common and rises with bacterial infection?
opciones: Neutrophils, normally 50 to 70 percent of leukocytes
Lymphocytes, normally 20 to 30 percent of leukocytes
Monocytes, normally 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
Eosinophils, normally 2 to 4 percent of leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Neutrophils are the most common leukocyte at 50 to 70 percent of the count; they respond fast to infection, prefer bacteria, and high counts point to bacterial infection or inflammation, as well as burns and stress. Lymphocytes are second at 20 to 30 percent and rise with viral infections; monocytes are 2 to 8 percent and eosinophils 2 to 4 percent, rising with allergies and parasitic worms.

Stop the test and report it to the provider as a failed glucose screen
Offer her a light snack to settle her stomach before the next blood draw

preguntas.pregunta: What does the P wave on a tracing represent?
opciones: Depolarization of the atria, right side first, then left
Repolarization of the atria, left side first, then right
Depolarization of the ventricles, right first, then left
Repolarization of the ventricles, from apex toward base
preguntas.explicacion: The P wave is atrial depolarization. Because the impulse is born in the sinoatrial node, which sits in the right atrium, the first half of the wave belongs to the right atrium and the second half to the left. A P wave of abnormal shape or size can point to enlargement of one of the atria.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: P-wave

preguntas.pregunta: A cognitive test is about to be done on an older patient whose son came along. Why might the son be asked to step out?
opciones: So he cannot answer for her or cover for any lapses
So he can finish her paperwork out in the waiting area
So he can be asked about her condition on his own
So the score can be worked out before she is told
preguntas.explicacion: Asking the companion to step out during part of the visit makes room for sensitive topics and gives the patient private time. During a test of cognitive abilities it has a second purpose the guidance states outright: the companion cannot answer the questions or cover for the patient's cognitive lapses.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient living alone needs home-delivered meals and help around the house. Which organization is the one to contact?
opciones: The Area Agency on Aging, which serves older adults regionally and locally
The Aging and Disability Resource Center, which only funds senior centers
The Center for Independent Living, which handles meals for older adults
The State Council on Developmental Disabilities, which arranges meals
preguntas.explicacion: Area Agencies on Aging work at the regional and local level on what older adults need to keep living independently, home-delivered meals and homemaker assistance among the examples given. Aging and Disability Resource Centers are the ones that give information and counseling about long-term services and help people reach programs.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a loud, high-pitched musical sound heard over the neck on inspiration. What is that?
opciones: Stridor, which points to obstruction of the upper airway
Wheezing, a continuous sound of 400 Hz or more from the airways
Rhonchi, a low-pitched sound from fluid or mucus in the airways
Crackles, brief popping sounds made by air passing secretions
preguntas.explicacion: Stridor is loud, high-pitched and musical, and it comes from obstruction of the upper respiratory tract; heard on inspiration it points above the thoracic inlet. Wheezes are continuous sounds at 400 Hz or above; rhonchi are continuous but around 200 Hz or less; crackles are brief, discontinuous and non-musical. A patient reporting wheeze often has stridor.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Lung Exam", Function: Auscultation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a(1) · RMA III.F.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4

preguntas.pregunta: What may the healthcare professional's written opinion after an exposure incident contain?
opciones: That the employee was informed of the results and told of any conditions needing further evaluation
The source individual's test results and the diagnosis, so that the employer can plan work restrictions
All findings and diagnoses from the evaluation, so the employer can complete the sharps injury log
The dates of hepatitis B vaccination and the employee's serologic status for the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5)(ii) limits the post-exposure opinion to two statements: that the employee has been informed of the evaluation results, and that the employee has been told about any conditions from the exposure that need further evaluation or treatment. Paragraph (f)(5)(iii) adds that every other finding or diagnosis stays confidential and is left out of the report. The employer is not entitled to diagnoses or source results through this document; vaccination dates live in the medical record of (h)(1), not in the opinion.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(5)(ii) and (f)(5)(iii), Healthcare Professional's Written Opinion

preguntas.pregunta: A label reads 0.25 g and the order is written in milligrams. Which equivalence applies?
opciones: 1 gram equals 1000 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 1000 micrograms
1 gram equals 100 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 100 micrograms
1 gram equals 1000 micrograms, and 1 milligram equals 1000 grams
1 gram equals 10 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 10 micrograms
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is built on units of ten, so converting is a matter of moving the decimal point. The equivalences to hold in the head are that a gram is 1000 milligrams and a milligram is 1000 micrograms, alongside a litre being 1000 millilitres. Confusing milligrams with micrograms is a thousand-fold error, which is exactly why the microgram symbol is written out as mcg on an order.

opciones: Access, communication, care coordination and staff
Cleanliness, quiet, food service and discharge timing
Billing accuracy, waiting time, parking and signage
Staffing ratios, credentials, office hours and equipment
preguntas.explicacion: Every version of the survey asks about the same broad areas: how easily care can be obtained, how providers communicate, how care is coordinated, and how the staff treat people. The core items work across primary and specialty practices, and may take supplemental items. The CAHPS program itself began in 1995.

preguntas.pregunta: Influenza rises every winter in the northern hemisphere. Why is it wrong to call that an epidemic each year?
opciones: The seasonal rise is expected, and an epidemic exceeds what is expected
The seasonal rise is worldwide, and an epidemic is limited to one country
The seasonal rise lasts months, and an epidemic lasts only a few days
The seasonal rise is caused by a virus, and an epidemic requires a bacterium
preguntas.explicacion: An epidemic is a larger than expected number of cases in a short time within a region, so the word rests on what was expected. Influenza climbing every winter is the expected pattern; a winter with an unusually large number of cases in particular regions is what qualifies. Going worldwide would make it a pandemic.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.1 The Language of Epidemiologists, Patterns of Incidence

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with chronic kidney disease heard he should stop eating protein entirely. How should that be corrected?
opciones: Some patients moderate protein, and too little brings malnutrition
Protein is stopped completely once kidney disease has been diagnosed
Protein is raised sharply so the kidneys have material to repair with
Protein is left untouched, since only sodium affects the kidneys
preguntas.explicacion: Protein builds and maintains muscle, bone, skin, organs and blood, and helps wounds heal. As the body uses it, waste is left for the kidneys to clear, so some patients are asked to keep protein moderate. Cutting it too far causes malnutrition, which is why the balance is set with a dietitian rather than by the patient.
preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Eating Right for Chronic Kidney Disease — Protein
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(f)

preguntas.pregunta: For a blood cortisol test, when are the samples usually drawn?
opciones: Once in the morning and again around 4 p.m. on the same day
Once at midnight, when cortisol is normally at its peak
Once in the morning only, after a strict 12-hour overnight fast
Every hour for 2 to 3 hours after a sugary glucose drink
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples are usually taken twice in one day: in the morning, when cortisol is normally highest, and again around 4 p.m., when it is normally much lower, which is why the patient needs two appointments. The physiology matches: peak near awakening, lowest at night. A 12-hour morning fast describes iron, and hourly samples describe the tolerance test.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Cortisol Test, section What happens during a cortisol test

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a two-month sabbatical without telling patients or arranging cover. What is the exposure?
opciones: Inadvertent abandonment, which is actionable even without intent to end care
An ethics complaint at most, since the answering service took messages
A licensing violation only, since no single patient can show harm from it
A breach of contract only, since the office visit fee was already collected
preguntas.explicacion: A clinician does not have to mean to end the relationship to be liable. Being unavailable for a long stretch — an extended vacation or sabbatical with no notice and no emergency coverage — is given as an example of inadvertent abandonment, as are unanswered calls or emails and failure to follow up after surgery or after starting a new medication.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abandonment", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: What calorie level are the % Daily Values on the Nutrition Facts label based on?
opciones: 2,000 calories a day, used as general nutrition advice
2,500 calories a day, used as general nutrition advice
1,800 calories a day, the average for adult women
The calorie level the shopper enters in the MyPlate Plan tool
preguntas.explicacion: The footnote of the panel states that the percentages rest on a 2,000-calorie day, offered as general advice. A given person may need more or fewer calories depending on age, sex, height, weight and activity, which is why the label points readers to a personalized plan for their own estimate.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's order calls for every tube on the chart. Which one is filled ninth?
opciones: The pale yellow tube used for tissue typing and DNA work
The purple top tube used for haematology and cross-match
The light grey top tube used for glucose determinations
The light green tube used for chemistry panels on plasma
preguntas.explicacion: Position 9 belongs to the pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube, whose listed uses are HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies. EDTA is number 8 and the fluoride/oxalate tube number 10, so the ACD tube falls between them; the light green PST comes earlier, at position 7.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient without insurance asks where she can be seen for primary care on a sliding scale based on what she can pay. What fits?
opciones: A federally qualified health center, whose fees slide with the patient's ability to pay
An ambulatory surgical center, where Part B pays the facility fee for an approved surgery
A hospital emergency department, which evaluates a sudden illness that quickly worsens
A skilled nursing facility, where daily skilled nursing or therapy is given short term
preguntas.explicacion: Federally qualified health centers are federally funded nonprofit centers and clinics that serve areas and populations which are medically underserved. They furnish primary care regardless of the patient's ability to pay, and the fee follows a sliding scale tied to that ability. Centers also offer lower fees to people with limited income.

preguntas.pregunta: Which TRICARE plans are the premium-based ones available worldwide?
opciones: TRICARE Reserve Select, Retired Reserve and Young Adult
TRICARE Prime, Prime Remote and the Family Health Plan
TRICARE Select, Select Overseas and Prime Remote Overseas
TRICARE Prime, the Prime demonstration and TRICARE For Life
preguntas.explicacion: The premium-based group, the one available worldwide, holds TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve and TRICARE Young Adult. The plans listed for the United States are Prime, Prime Remote, the Uniformed Services Family Health Plan option, a Prime demonstration, Select and TRICARE For Life; the overseas group holds Prime Overseas, Prime Remote Overseas and Select Overseas.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a Medicare Advantage Plan?
opciones: A private plan under contract with Medicare that delivers Part A and Part B benefits
A private plan sold by insurers that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare
A federal plan that replaces Part A for patients treated in a network of hospitals
A state plan that covers premiums and deductibles for people with low income
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Advantage, also called Part C, is offered by private companies that contract with Medicare to provide all Part A and Part B benefits, usually with drug coverage as well; the types include health maintenance and preferred provider organizations. Private insurance that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare is Medigap, and help with premiums for people with low income comes through Medicaid.

preguntas.pregunta: Which total white blood cell count falls within the usual adult reference interval?
opciones: 7,800 cells/µL
3,200 cells/µL
13,500 cells/µL
150,000 cells/µL
preguntas.explicacion: The adult white blood cell count is usually 4,500 to 11,000 cells/µL, so 7,800 is within range. A count of 3,200 would be leukopenia and 13,500 leukocytosis; 150,000 is the lower limit of the platelet reference interval, not a white cell figure. Spurious values occur too: white cell clumping can lower the count, while platelet clumps and fibrin clumps can be counted as white cells and raise it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Normal and Abnormal Complete Blood Count With Differential", section White Blood Cell Tests; Platelet Tests

preguntas.pregunta: A relay call comes through 7-1-1 to book a fasting draw. How must the front desk handle it?
opciones: Accept it and treat it exactly like any other telephone call
Ask the caller to attend in person, since relay is not private
Transfer it to the interpreter line before a booking is made
Take the booking only once a hearing relative confirms it
preguntas.explicacion: The free nationwide telecommunications relay service, reached by dialling 7-1-1, uses communications assistants as intermediaries for people with hearing or speech disabilities. Covered entities are required to accept calls placed through relay and video relay services, and staff answering must treat them just like other calls; the assistant explains the system.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services and Effective Communication Provisions

preguntas.pregunta: A rapid fingerstick HIV antibody/antigen test in a community clinic is reactive. What does this mean for the patient?
opciones: Signs of infection were found, but a follow-up test is needed to confirm the diagnosis; the site arranges it
HIV infection is confirmed, because rapid antibody/antigen tests detect the virus itself and need no second test
The result is preliminary and is confirmed by repeating the same rapid test with a saliva sample the same day
Antiretroviral therapy should start at once and the confirmatory test can be skipped if the patient is symptomatic
preguntas.explicacion: Rapid tests use a drop of fingerstick blood, or saliva, and give results in about 30 minutes. A positive result means signs of HIV were found in the sample, but a follow-up test is required to confirm the diagnosis unless a NAT was done; when the test is performed at a medical office or community program, the testing site arranges the follow-up. Antiretroviral therapy starts once the confirmatory test is also positive. Counseling on what results mean is advised before HIV testing.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: HIV Screening Test, What happens during an HIV test?; What do the results mean?; CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Preparing the Patient

preguntas.pregunta: Cervical stretching during labor triggers oxytocin, which strengthens the contractions and stretches the cervix further. What does that loop illustrate?
opciones: Positive feedback, which intensifies a change until a definite end point
Negative feedback, which intensifies a change until a definite end point
Positive feedback, which reverses a change back toward the normal range
Negative feedback, which reverses a change back toward the normal range
preguntas.explicacion: Positive feedback pushes a change further instead of reversing it, and in the body it is normal only when there is a definite end point. Childbirth is one example: stretching, oxytocin and stronger contractions feed each other until the baby is born. The clotting cascade after a wound is the other standard example.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.5 Homeostasis, Positive Feedback
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: On a paediatric ward the child's wristband is found clipped to the cot rail rather than on the child. What does the WHO instruct?
opciones: Do not use it; ask the parent or guardian for the child's full name
Use it, because the cot is assigned to that child on the ward admission list
Use the cot number as the second identifier next to the form
Ask the child directly to state the full name and date of birth
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 6 says a wrist or foot band counts only if it is attached to the patient; a band on the bed or cot, and the bed number, are not to be used. When a parent or legal guardian is present, that person is asked for the child's first and last names, and the name, date of birth and hospital or file number on the laboratory form are matched to the child.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.1, Patient identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 k49 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E1 k124 · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of nutrients does the Nutrition Facts label flag as ones to get less of?
opciones: Saturated fat, sodium and added sugars
Saturated fat, sodium and dietary fiber
Total fat, total sugars and total carbohydrate
Cholesterol, protein and trans fat
preguntas.explicacion: The label separates nutrients to get less of, which are saturated fat, sodium and added sugars, from nutrients to get more of: dietary fiber, vitamin D, calcium, iron and potassium. Fiber belongs to the second list. Total sugars and trans fat carry no percentage at all, so they are not part of either guide.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to bring everything to a brown bag medicine review. What does that include?
opciones: Prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, supplements and herbals
Prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs, but not vitamins or supplements
Prescriptions only, since the rest are not entered in the medication list
Prescriptions and the pill organizer, but not the original containers
preguntas.explicacion: The review covers every prescription, every over-the-counter product, all vitamins, supplements and herbal medicines, plus topicals, liquids, injections and inhalants, and the pills in both their original bottles and any organizer. Seeing the actual containers is what reveals whether and why medicines are being taken wrong.

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old needs a finger-prick. Which puncture depth is recommended for that age?
opciones: 1.5 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
2.4 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
0.85 mm, the depth for any child who has not reached school age
2.2 mm, the longest lancet, because the finger has no bone risk
preguntas.explicacion: There are two finger-prick depths for children: 1.5 mm for a child over 6 months and below 8 years, and 2.4 mm for a child over 8 years. The 0.85 mm lancet is the one made for premature neonates. The 2.2 mm lancet is the longest typically used in an adult finger-prick because the depth there should not exceed 2.4 mm, and that limit exists precisely to protect bone.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A glucometer and its lancet platform are used for several inpatients during a round. What does best practice require?
opciones: Dedicate it to one patient, or clean and disinfect it between uses
Change the lancet and wipe the platform with a dry gauze pad
Rinse the platform under running water at the end of the round
Keep it in a clean bag between patients, which avoids contact
preguntas.explicacion: For small quantities of capillary blood the equipment is single-use: a lancet, or a retractable lancet, and a platform or glucometer that is either dedicated to one patient for the hospital stay or cleaned of all visible dirt and disinfected with alcohol between uses. The warning behind the rule is on the record: hepatitis infections have been transmitted to patients when platforms or glucometers were used on several people without that reprocessing.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Small quantities of capillary blood

preguntas.pregunta: An institution allows DOA, which some staff read as date of admission and others as dead on arrival. Which rule does that break?
opciones: A permitted abbreviation may carry only one universal meaning
A permitted abbreviation may be used only in handwritten orders
A permitted abbreviation may be used only by the ordering provider
A permitted abbreviation may be used only after a pharmacist reviews it
preguntas.explicacion: Two meanings behind one set of letters is exactly the failure the rules are meant to stop: if an abbreviation is permitted at all, it must have a single universal meaning, and DOA is the classic example of one that does not. The same policy requires that nothing on the approved list also appear on the banned list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7 · RMA I.B.3.a

preguntas.pregunta: A glucose drawn from the arm carrying a glucose infusion comes back far above the critical limit, and the patient looks well. What clears the picture?
opciones: Testing a second specimen collected properly from another site
Repeating the measurement twice on the same tube and averaging
Reporting the figure and letting the clinician judge the context
Diluting the specimen and correcting for the dilution factor used
preguntas.explicacion: Preanalytical influences are named outright as a frequent source of results that only look critical, and the example given is a glucose drawn through a venous catheter that had been used for a glucose infusion. Cases like that are normally settled by testing another, properly collected specimen; repeating the same contaminated tube only confirms the contamination.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the assistant to point out the PR segment on a printed strip. How does it differ from the PR interval?
opciones: The interval takes in the P wave and the segment starts after it
The segment takes in the P wave and the interval starts after it
The interval reaches the T wave and the segment reaches the QRS
The segment lies above the baseline and the interval below it
preguntas.explicacion: A segment is the stretch between two waves; an interval is a segment plus one or more waves. So the PR segment runs from the end of the P wave to the start of the complex, while the PR interval begins with the P wave, which is why it is the useful measurement.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A parent of a child with a peanut allergy asks where the allergen appears on a package. Where does the law require it?
opciones: In the ingredient list itself, or in a "contains" statement beside it
In the ingredient list itself, or in the Nutrition Facts panel below it
In a warning box on the front of the package, in bold red type
In the ingredient list only, since "contains" statements are voluntary
preguntas.explicacion: The food source of a major allergen has to be declared at least once, either inside the ingredient list or in a statement right after or next to it, worded like "Contains wheat, milk, and soy". The rule also forces the specific tree nut, fish species or shellfish species to be named.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Food Allergies: Major Food Allergens — label declaration

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD asks what those letters mean. Which expansion is correct?
opciones: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a lung disease
Chronic obstructive peptic disorder, a stomach disease
Congenital obstructive pulmonary defect, a lung disease
Chronic occlusive peripheral disease, an artery disease
preguntas.explicacion: COPD is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the long-standing lung condition that makes breathing hard. The look-alike abbreviations belong elsewhere: PUD is peptic ulcer disease, CHD is congenital heart disease and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, the arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.pregunta: Which device helps locate the dorsal hand veins and antecubital veins of a small child?
opciones: A transilluminator or pocket pen light
A tourniquet left in place for three minutes
A warm compress applied for a fixed 10 minutes
An ultrasound probe operated by the phlebotomist
preguntas.explicacion: To make paediatric venepuncture easier, a transilluminator or pocket pen light is used to display the dorsal hand veins and the veins of the antecubital fossa. Before that the child is kept warm, which may raise blood flow up to sevenfold, and warm cloths are applied to the site to dilate the vessels, without stating a temperature or time.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Preparation

preguntas.pregunta: A nasal cannula is running at 4 L/min. Roughly what oxygen concentration does that deliver?
opciones: Somewhere in the 24% to 40% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Somewhere in the 40% to 60% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Close to 50%, which is what a face tent reaches at high flow
Between 60% and 80%, the range of a mask with a reservoir bag
preguntas.explicacion: A cannula runs at one to six liters a minute and gives roughly 24% to 40% oxygen; the figure is approximate because how much room air is mixed in depends on the patient's rate and depth of breathing. A simple face mask at 5 to 10 L/min gives about 40% to 60%, a face tent up to 15 L/min about 50%, and a nonrebreather at 10 to 15 L/min more still.

preguntas.pregunta: A box of evacuated tubes is found to be past its expiration date. What two problems do expired tubes present?

Loss of sterility of the stopper, and a gel that no longer separates serum
A higher risk of haemolysis, and colours that no longer match the order of draw
Cracks in the plastic, and an anticoagulant that turns plasma into serum
preguntas.explicacion: Expiration dates matter because expired vacuum tubes have a decreased capacity to aspirate blood and their additives may be degraded, so even small deviations can affect the results. preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches a normal T wave?

Upright in aVR, and inverted in I, II and V3 through V6
Upright in all twelve leads, without a single exception
Inverted in V1 and V2 always, and upright in every other lead
preguntas.explicacion: Ventricular repolarization normally writes an upward T wave in I, II and V3 to V6, an inverted one in aVR, and something variable in V1 and V2. Height counts too: under 5 mm in the limb leads and under 10 mm in the chest leads.

preguntas.explicacion: The hemoglobin A1C test uses one sample, needs no fasting, and reports average blood glucose over the past 3 months. It delivers on weekdays and adds a Saturday run when the label is bought online
It delivers seven days a week only to post office box addresses in large markets
It delivers on any day agreed with the receiving office when the package is sent
preguntas.explicacion: Express is the fastest domestic service and it runs seven days a week, 365 days a year, with limited exceptions. Most addresses see it in one to three days, and the delivery time carries a money-back guarantee, which the two-to-three-day estimate of Priority Mail does not.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the relationship between an ethical principle and a patient right?
opciones: A right appears when a body with authority enforces an ethical standard
A right appears when a professional society publishes it in its own code
A right appears when a majority of patients in a survey come to expect it
A right and an ethical principle are the same thing under a different name
preguntas.explicacion: Human rights are the minimum standards for how people can expect to be treated; ethics are the customary standards for how people should treat others. preguntas.pregunta: A practice takes its first new patients through an online intake before any in-person visit. What does the notice rule require?

A paper notice mailed within thirty days of the electronic request for service being received
An electronic notice posted on the web site only, since online patients can read it there

Leave that element blank, which is read as not applicable
Copy the entry from a sheet for a similar product in the family
Move the element to section 16 with the other information

The donor washes in private, since observing would violate the donor's dignity
The donor washes only after handing over the specimen container
The donor uses gloves instead, because soap can adulterate the specimen

Shopping and cooking are basic; bathing and toileting are instrumental activities

Driving and using the telephone are basic; dressing and feeding are instrumental

Three: identify, detect and report to the police
Five: identify, detect, respond, update and insure
Two: identify the red flags and train the staff on them

Normal: a shift counts only past 5 mm at the J point
Normal: the segment is measured at the peak of the T wave
Abnormal only when the segment falls below the baseline
preguntas.explicacion: The ST segment should sit level with the PR interval. Seven years from the date of service, as with orders and certifications in Part B
Five years, as with the medical records a hospital keeps to take part in Medicare
Six years from creation, as with the documentation the privacy standards require
preguntas.explicacion: Every retention period in this area belongs to a different rule, and the trap is borrowing one for another. Open reduction, as opposed to closed reduction
Internal fixation, as opposed to closed reduction
Debridement, as opposed to open reduction
preguntas.explicacion: Setting a broken bone into its natural position by hand, with no incision, is a closed reduction; open reduction means surgery to expose the fracture and reset the bone. Generativity versus stagnation, the stage of adulthood
Intimacy versus isolation, the young adulthood stage
Trust versus mistrust, the very first stage in infancy
preguntas.explicacion: Old age is the eighth stage, integrity against despair; its virtue is wisdom and its malignancy is disdain, and the example given is contemplating and acknowledging one's own accomplishments. preguntas.pregunta: An adult has a body mass index of 41.2. How is that classified?

Class 2 obesity, the band that runs from 35.0 to 39.9
Class 1 obesity, the band that runs from 30.0 to 39.9
Obesity without a class, since the classes stop at 40.0
preguntas.explicacion: Obesity is divided into three classes: 30.0 to 34.9, 35.0 to 39.9, and 40.0 or greater, the last of which is also called severe obesity. Within 24 hours or the next business day, at room temperature in a locked room
Within 4 hours of the collection, on cold packs, with no storage permitted
Within one week, provided the tamper-evident seals stay unbroken
