preguntas.pregunta: Apart from reaching the optimal volume, why does the CDC require at least two blood culture sets per episode?
opciones: To decide whether a skin commensal that grows is a possible contaminant
To keep a spare set if the first one is lost during transport
To draw one set before the antibiotic and one after the first dose
To compare aerobic growth in one arm with anaerobic growth in the other
preguntas.explicacion: Two sets are required to determine whether the presence of a commensal organism can be classified as a possible contaminant; with one set there is no comparison to make. Both sets are drawn before antimicrobial therapy when possible, and each set already carries its own aerobic and anaerobic bottle, so the arms are not being compared by bottle type. A spare for transport is not a reason the CDC gives.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, Collect Multiple Sets to Achieve the Optimal Volume

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a yearly "Wellness" visit expecting a head-to-toe physical. How is the visit described?
opciones: A conversation to build a prevention plan, not a routine physical exam
A routine physical exam that also produces a written prevention plan
A conversation that replaces every screening test for the coming year
A routine physical exam that Medicare covers once every two years
preguntas.explicacion: The yearly visit is built around a conversation with the provider to create or update a personalized prevention plan, and it is explicitly not a routine physical. Specific health complaints belong in a separate appointment so the visit stays on prevention. The patient leaves with a written checklist of the screenings and vaccines due.

preguntas.pregunta: Which activity shows the medical home's commitment to quality and safety?
opciones: Measuring performance and patient experience, and sharing the results publicly
Keeping in-person hours long enough that urgent needs are seen the same day
Reaching most of a patient's physical and mental health needs in one practice
Passing the patient's information to the hospital before a planned admission
preguntas.explicacion: The quality and safety function shows in evidence-based medicine and decision-support tools that guide shared decision making with patients and families, in performance measurement and improvement, in measuring and responding to patient experience and satisfaction, and in population health management. Publishing quality and safety data marks a system-level commitment.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 5. Quality and Safety

preguntas.pregunta: Which laboratory values may a capillary sample falsely elevate?
opciones: Sugar, electrolytes and blood counts
Bilirubin, cholesterol and clotting times
Blood gases, lactate and ammonia
Hormones, drug levels and iron studies
preguntas.explicacion: Among the disadvantages of capillary sampling, it may give inaccurate results, such as falsely elevated sugar, electrolyte and blood count values, that only a limited amount of blood can be drawn, and that damage to blood cells during collection can force a repeat from a vein. Its advantages are ease of collection, especially in infants, several rotatable sites and home testing.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Capillary sample, Why the Test is Performed and Risks

preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls minutes before her video visit to say the picture keeps freezing. Which step is on the troubleshooting list the office hands out beforehand?
opciones: Closing every other application, and if that fails trying a different device
Removing the platform and installing it again so the settings are rebuilt
Carrying the router into the same room and starting the appointment again
Waiting for the clinician to drop the call so the visit can be rebooked
preguntas.explicacion: Patients feel easier when they already know what to do if something goes wrong, so the office gives them the common fixes in advance: restart the computer or device, check it is charged or plugged in, check that the connection is strong enough for the platform, close all other applications, update the browser, try another device, and call the number given for help.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology

preguntas.pregunta: A card of electrodes was left open to the air for weeks. Which problem do they cause?
opciones: A drifting baseline, from unstable electrode contact
Interference from the alternating current in the room
Muscle tremor coming from the arms and the legs
A standardization mark that comes out too short
preguntas.explicacion: The conductive hydrogel loses its performance when a card of electrodes is left open to the air, and a dried electrode is one of the six listed causes of unstable contact and therefore of drift. That is why unused cards are kept in their pouch or in a sealed plastic bag in a cool dry place.

preguntas.pregunta: A law restricting access to a harmful substance is described as which kind of prevention?
opciones: Primordial prevention, which acts on risks before they reach the person
Primary prevention, which reduces risk factors in people who are healthy
Secondary prevention, which finds and treats disease at an early stage
Tertiary prevention, which reduces the long-term burden of chronic illness
preguntas.explicacion: Primordial prevention is the fourth and newest category, and it operates above the individual: government or institutional action that restricts access to dangerous substances, or public education that keeps whole populations away from the exposure. The other three act once a person is at risk, is already ill, or is living with the consequences.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prevention Strategies", Primordial Prevention

preguntas.pregunta: A cannula hub is marked 24G and another 18G. What does the difference in number mean?
opciones: The 24G is the narrower of the two, since higher numbers are finer
The 24G is the wider of the two, since higher numbers are coarser
The numbers give the length in millimetres, not the internal bore
The numbers give the flow rate in millilitres per minute of fluid
preguntas.explicacion: Gauge describes the internal diameter, and a higher gauge number means a narrower device; the sizes commonly stocked run from fourteen through to twenty-four, with the hub colour-coded to the gauge. The same convention explains why sixteen to eighteen gauge is reserved for blood donation.

preguntas.pregunta: A tray of instruments will be opened into a wound and will enter sterile tissue. Under the Spaulding scheme, what does that require?
opciones: Sterilization, because any microbe on an item entering sterile tissue can transmit disease
High-level disinfection, the minimum set for items touching mucous membranes or broken skin
Intermediate-level disinfection, the level used for surfaces that briefly touch broken skin
Low-level disinfection, the level listed in the tables for items that touch only intact skin
preguntas.explicacion: Spaulding sorts items by the risk their intended use carries. Anything entering sterile tissue or the vascular system is critical and must be sterile, because any contamination at all could transmit disease. High-level disinfection is the floor for semicritical items; intermediate and low levels belong to items that meet intact or briefly broken skin.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Critical Items
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: While setting up, a phlebotomist's ungloved finger brushes the top of a blood culture bottle. Why does this matter?
opciones: The sterility of the culture bottle cap must be preserved, or the results are unreliable
The cap is where the bottle's vacuum is stored; touching it lets the vacuum escape early
Skin oils degrade the SPS anticoagulant inside the culture bottle within minutes
It does not matter, because the bottle is mixed 8 to 10 times after filling
preguntas.explicacion: Among the issues of concern in tube collection is contamination before, during or after the collection, with the specific example that the sterility of the cap of blood culture bottles must be ensured and kept from any potential source of contamination, or the results become incorrect and unreliable. Mixing 8 to 10 times combines blood and medium; it does not undo contamination of the cap.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Contamination

preguntas.pregunta: What fills the spaces between the cells of a tissue and gives that tissue much of its character?
opciones: The intercellular matrix, a nonliving material with salts and fibers
The interstitial fluid, a living material with salts and fibers
The cytoplasm, a nonliving material rich in salts and fibers
The nucleoplasm, a living material rich in salts and fibers
preguntas.explicacion: A tissue is a group of cells of similar structure working as a unit, and between them lies the intercellular matrix, a nonliving material that can be abundant in one tissue and scarce in another. Special substances in it, such as salts and fibers, are what make bone hard and other tissues soft. Cytoplasm and nucleoplasm are inside the cell.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Cells, Tissues and Membranes: Body Tissues
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A school screening letter uses the word scoliosis. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
A part meaning humped plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning an inflammation
A part meaning shape plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
preguntas.explicacion: Scoli- and scolio- mean twisted, and -osis is a condition, usually an abnormal one, so the term names something twisted. Its neighbors in the group of shapes are kypho-, humped, and morph- or morpho-, shape itself. Had the ending been -itis the word would have named an inflammation instead.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Physical Properties and Shapes; Good and Bad

preguntas.pregunta: Blood flows slowly from a heel puncture and the phlebotomist begins squeezing the heel firmly. What does this do to the specimen?
opciones: It dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid and increases the probability of haemolysis
It concentrates the specimen with red cells and raises the measured haematocrit
It speeds the flow safely, as long as the first drop has already been wiped away
It draws in skin flora, which is why the WHO limits capillary blood to a few tests
preguntas.explicacion: Squeezing the finger or heel too tightly dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid (plasma) and increases the probability of haemolysis, and excessive massaging or squeezing of fingers likewise causes haemolysis and impedes blood flow. The remedies for poor flow are warmth and having the parent rhythmically tighten and release the child's wrist.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: An 82-year-old woman arrives for a fasting draw. How should the phlebotomist address her?
opciones: By a formal title such as Ms. at first, then ask how she prefers to be addressed
By a friendly word such as dear, which settles an anxious older patient more quickly
By her first name from the start, since informality shortens the social distance
By asking the daughter beside her how her mother prefers to be addressed today
preguntas.explicacion: Older patients are often used to more formal terms of address, so the default is a title and a surname, and the simplest way to get it right is to ask the patient herself. Familiar words like dear read as disrespectful. The wider rule behind it is to speak to an older patient as a fellow adult: an impairment does not reduce an adult's maturity.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients

preguntas.pregunta: A county health department, acting under state law, asks the office to report a case of a communicable disease. What is required?
opciones: Nothing further, since a public health authority may receive the report without authorization
A signed authorization from the patient, because the diagnosis is sensitive information
A subpoena, because a government agency reaches records only through legal process
A business associate agreement with the department before the report can be transmitted
preguntas.explicacion: Public health activities are one of the twelve national priority purposes. Covered entities may disclose PHI to public health authorities that are authorized by law to receive it for preventing or controlling disease, injury or disability, and to authorities that receive reports of child abuse and neglect. The same paragraph also covers notifying a person who may have been exposed to a communicable disease when law authorizes it.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities

preguntas.pregunta: How is a temperature of 38.6 °C (101.5 °F) graded on the published grading of fever?
opciones: Moderate-grade fever, the band from 38.1 to 39.0 °C (100.6 to 102.2 °F)
Low-grade fever, which is the band from 37.3 to 38.0 °C (99.1 to 100.4 °F)
High-grade fever, the band from 39.1 to 41.0 °C (102.4 to 105.8 °F)
Hyperthermia, which is any recorded value above 41.0 °C (105.8 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: Fever is graded in bands: low from 37.3 to 38.0 °C, moderate from 38.1 to 39.0 °C, high from 39.1 to 41.0 °C, and above 41.0 °C the term used is hyperthermia. A value of 38.6 °C falls in the middle band. Grading the reading matters because the reporting thresholds a clinic sets are written in those terms.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: On one strip the baseline sits at a different height from one complex to the next; on another, small extra signals ride along the baseline of a shivering patient. What is each?
opciones: The first is baseline drift and the second is muscle tremor
The first is muscle tremor and the second is baseline drift
Both are drift, one from cold skin and one from movement
Both are tremor, one from the arms and one from the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Drift is a baseline that will not hold its level, which is why the quality check measures the vertical distance between neighboring complexes. Tremor is a separate signal thrown off by the arm and leg muscles of a patient who is tense, cold or has a nerve disorder.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6

preguntas.pregunta: How does a pulse oximeter arrive at the saturation it displays?
opciones: It compares how two wavelengths of light are absorbed by the pulsating tissue bed
It measures the electrical resistance of the fingertip as the blood volume changes
It samples a drop of capillary blood held against the sensor inside the clip
It reads the colour of the nail bed and matches it against a calibrated chart
preguntas.explicacion: Oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin absorb light differently, at 940 and 660 nanometres, and the device works out saturation from the difference across a pulsating bed. Nothing is sampled from the patient, which is why the test is painless and carries no known risk, and why perfusion at the site matters so much.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation

preguntas.pregunta: A patient was seen on March 22. What is the deadline for filing that Medicare claim?
opciones: March 22 of the following year, one full calendar year after the service
September 22 of the same year, six months after the date of the service
December 31 of the same year, the close of the calendar year of service
March 22 two years later, since Medicare allows 24 months for filing
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare claims must be filed no later than 12 months, one full calendar year, after the date the services were provided, and the program itself uses the example of a March 22 visit needing the claim by March 22 of the next year. Claims filed later are denied, and that denial is not an initial determination, so it cannot be appealed.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why the tube feels warm right after the draw. Compared with a core temperature of 37 °C, what is the normal temperature of blood?
opciones: About 38 °C (100.4 °F), a little above the core
About 37 °C (98.6 °F), the same as the core
About 37.5 °C, half a degree above the core
About 36.5 °C, half a degree below the core
preguntas.explicacion: The normal temperature of blood is about 38 °C (100.4 °F), slightly higher than the 37 °C (98.6 °F) of an internal body reading, and daily swings of 0.5 °C are normal. The extra heat comes from friction as blood flows against vessel walls, especially as vessels age and lose elasticity. Half a degree above or below 37 °C describes the daily variation, not the difference between blood and core temperature.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements must appear on the label of a shipped container of a hazardous chemical under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: Product identifier, signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, pictograms and supplier contact
Product identifier, CAS number, concentration, flash point, PEL and the date of preparation
Signal word, pictograms, the 16-section SDS summary, lot number, expiration date and PPE symbol
Chemical name, NFPA hazard rating, storage temperature, disposal method, supplier name and phone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 and OSHA's labeling brief list six elements for containers leaving the workplace: the product identifier, a signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, pictograms, and the name, address and telephone number of the manufacturer, importer or other responsible party. The product identifier must match section 1 of the SDS. CAS numbers, concentrations, flash points and exposure limits live in the SDS sections on composition, physical properties and exposure controls, not on the label; an HMIS-style PPE symbol may be added only as supplementary information.

preguntas.pregunta: How is child abuse and neglect defined for public health purposes?
opciones: Harm, or the threat of it, to a child under 18 by someone in a custodial role
Harm to a child under 12 caused by a parent or a legal guardian only
Any injury to a child under 18 that required treatment at a hospital or clinic
Any harm to a child under 18 caused by an adult outside the family
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers all types of abuse and neglect of a child under 18 by a parent, a caregiver, or another person in a custodial role such as a coach, a teacher or a religious leader, where the result is harm, potential harm or the threat of harm. It is not limited to injuries needing treatment, nor to people outside the family — the opposite is more common.

preguntas.pregunta: While dipping three urine specimens at once, a medical assistant reads all the strips four minutes after the last dip, well past the times printed on the bottle. Which error is this most likely to produce?
opciones: False positives from colors that kept developing after the specified reading time
False negatives on every pad, because all reagent pads fade within the first minute
No error, because reagent strip reactions stop on their own once the pad has dried out
Invalid results only on the pH pad, which is the single time-critical reaction on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Each pad must be read at the interval the manufacturer specifies, using a timer if indicated. Reading after the stated time can produce false positives from over-development of color, false negatives when a reaction fades, or invalid results when the reaction moves beyond the visible area; reading too soon gives invalid or false-negative results because sample and reagent have not finished reacting. Running several tests at once is exactly when timing slips.

preguntas.pregunta: Which wording puts the emphasis on accessibility rather than on disability?
opciones: The accessible restroom on the first floor
The handicapped restroom on the first floor
The special restroom on the first floor
The disabled restroom on the first floor
preguntas.explicacion: Signage and directions are written to emphasize the need for accessibility rather than the disability, so accessible parking and an accessible restroom replace the handicapped versions. Special sits with the words to avoid, alongside slow and afflicted, because it points at the person instead of the facility.

preguntas.pregunta: When the order of draw is summarized in four groups (sterile tubes, coagulation tubes, plain or gel tubes, additive tubes), where do the plain and gel tubes fall?
opciones: After the coagulation tubes and before the other additive tubes
Before the coagulation tubes and immediately after the sterile tubes
After all the additive tubes, at the very end of the sequence
Before the blood culture bottles, as the first tubes drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Compressed into four steps, the order runs: blood culture or sterile tubes first, coagulation tubes second, plain tubes and gel tubes third, and tubes with additives last. preguntas.pregunta: Two staff members are at the bedside of an unresponsive dying patient. What is advised?
opciones: Talk to the patient, and identify yourself on coming in
Talk about the patient quietly so as not to disturb them
Talk only out in the hallway and keep the room silent
Talk to the family alone and leave the patient in peace
preguntas.explicacion: Some clinicians hold that a dying person can still hear even when not conscious. The guidance is to talk to the person rather than about them, and to say who you are on entering the room. Sharing memories and letting family say what the relationship meant is described as bringing peace to everyone present.

preguntas.pregunta: Which leads are inspected when the rhythm is being read?

Leads V4, V5 and V6, looking at five separate points
Leads III, aVR and aVL, looking at five separate points
Leads I and aVF alone, looking at five separate points
preguntas.explicacion: Those four leads are the ones read for rhythm, and five things are checked in them: whether regular P waves are there, whether the QRS is narrow or wide, whether the P waves and the complexes go together, whether the spacing is regular, and what shape the P waves have.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient goes quiet after being told a biopsy has been ordered. What is the therapeutic response?
opciones: Stay with the silence and hold back from interrupting
Offer reassurance that the result will surely come back fine
Move on to the paperwork so the visit keeps its schedule
Give an opinion on how the patient ought to be taking it
preguntas.explicacion: Silence is itself a technique: it demonstrates attentiveness by minimizing interruption. False reassurance is a pitfall that can rupture the relationship badly if the hoped-for outcome never arrives, an abrupt change of subject can be taken as dismissive, and value judgments get in the patient's way.

The date of the last decontamination and the brand of disinfectant that was used
The single legend BIOHAZARD, in a color that contrasts with the background
The list of employees trained to enter and the date of their last training

Haemolysis, clotting and delayed transport to the bench
Contamination, clotting and an expired collection tube
Inaccurate labelling, clotting and an underfilled tube

preguntas.pregunta: What is done to the examination table between one patient and the next?

It is covered with a clean sheet and a blanket for the next patient
It is wiped down with alcohol and then left open to dry for a while
It is wiped down with a detergent solution after every two patients
preguntas.explicacion: Keeping infection out of the room rests on two habits: the equipment is cleaned and disinfected at regular intervals, and the table is covered with fresh examination paper once each patient is done. The wipe with a mild detergent belongs to the start of the stand.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of risk factors is listed for pelvic inflammatory disease?

Being over 50, obesity, smoking and a diet of fatty and spicy foods
Being over 65, immobility, low calcium intake and declining estrogen
Being under 2, attending day care and a recent upper respiratory infection
preguntas.explicacion: The risk factors are the ones shared with other sexually transmitted infections: age under 25, several partners, a partner with an infection or symptoms, early first sexual activity, a prior infection, inconsistent barrier use and bacterial vaginosis. Risk also rises in the first three weeks after an intrauterine device is placed, but not after that.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does an office check the List of Excluded Individuals and Entities before hiring?

Excluded people must be reported to the state licensing board first
The list shows which providers have been sanctioned by their payers
Hiring from the list requires prior approval from the contractor
preguntas.explicacion: An exclusion means federal health care programs will not pay for items or services furnished, ordered or prescribed by that person or entity, and payment is denied whoever submits the claim, including the employer. preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists DVT after a long hospital stay. Which problem does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A clot that has formed in a deep vein
A defect in the vessels of the circulation
A disturbance of the rhythm of the heart
A disease of the arteries outside the heart
preguntas.explicacion: DVT stands for deep-vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot. The abbreviations that sit near it name other circulatory problems: AVM is an arteriovenous malformation, a defect in the circulatory system; AFIB is atrial fibrillation, a disturbance of the heart's rhythm; and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, of arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.pregunta: During the interview before a draw, a patient mentions having fainted during a previous blood test. What should be done?
opciones: Have the patient lie down for the draw
Draw quickly while the patient stands
Postpone the draw until after a meal
Seat the patient with the head between the knees
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 asks about allergies, phobias and any history of fainting during injections or blood draws, and makes the patient comfortable in a supine position if possible; patients who faint with blood draws are told to warn the provider and be lying down when the test is done. Head between the knees is a measure for someone who has already fainted and cannot lie flat.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vaginal speculum is the wider of the two in common use and holds itself open once inserted?
opciones: The Graves speculum, generally kept for women who have already given birth
The Pedersen speculum, which is narrower and has to be held during the exam
The pediatric speculum, much shorter and narrower than the adult instruments
The anoscope, which is introduced with an obturator that is then taken out
preguntas.explicacion: Two styles cover most adult examinations. Graves is the wider one and it is self-retaining once in place, which frees a hand; it is generally reserved for parous women. Pedersen is narrower, usually more comfortable, and must be held throughout because it does not stay open on its own. Pediatric specula are a separate, much smaller size.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gynecologic Pelvic Examination", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k63 · CMA I.C.5.b

preguntas.pregunta: What separates a manual stethoscope from an electronic one?
opciones: The electronic one amplifies the sound electrically; the other is mechanical
The electronic one is meant for lung sounds and the other for heart sounds
The manual one carries only a bell and the electronic one only a diaphragm
The manual one is used over arteries and veins and the other over the chest
preguntas.explicacion: A manual stethoscope is a mechanical device that carries the sounds of the heart, the arteries, the veins and other internal organs. The electronic one does the same work with electrical amplification. Both are described for the same sounds, so what separates them is the amplification, not the part of the body they are used on.
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a tablet swallowed by mouth often need a larger dose than the same drug given by vein?
opciones: Much of the swallowed dose is broken down in the liver before it reaches circulation
Much of the swallowed dose is broken down by the kidney before it arrives at the liver
Oral drugs are absorbed in the stomach, whose surface is smaller than the intestine's
The stomach destroys the whole dose, so only a coated tablet is ever absorbed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Oral is the most convenient and most used route, and the small intestine is usually where absorption happens; how much crosses the intestinal epithelium sets the bioavailability. The portal system then carries the drug to the liver, where the first-pass effect turns part of the dose into inactive metabolites. Less active drug arrives, so the oral dose has to be bigger than the intravenous one.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Enteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k21 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(vi) · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: Which antiseptic has the fastest onset but almost no residual activity, and is a fire risk with electrocautery?
opciones: Isopropyl alcohol swab
Chlorhexidine gluconate
Povidone-iodine scrub
Chloroxylenol solution
preguntas.explicacion: Isopropyl alcohol damages membranes and denatures the proteins microbes need, working best at 60 to 90 percent in water. It is one of the weaker cleansing agents and leaves little residual activity, but it has the fastest onset of the antiseptics, and it is flammable in the setting of electrocautery, which is why it must be dry before any current is used.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Mechanism of Action and Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.j

preguntas.pregunta: A dying person is described as needing care in four areas. Which set is it?
opciones: Physical comfort, mental and emotional, spiritual, practical
Physical comfort, financial, legal and funeral arrangements
Physical comfort, nutrition, mobility and skin integrity
Physical comfort, medication, monitoring and transportation
preguntas.explicacion: The four areas are physical comfort, mental and emotional needs, spiritual needs, and practical tasks. The family of the dying person needs support as well, both with the practical jobs and with their own distress, which is why help with everyday chores is treated as part of end-of-life care.

preguntas.pregunta: A pleural fluid aspirate is split for cell count, chemistry and culture. How is the portion for microbiological culture transported?
opciones: Promptly, at room temperature, to keep the organisms viable
Promptly, on wet ice, to slow down cellular degeneration
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C until the culture can be set up
Frozen at −20 °C if the culture cannot be set up the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Pleural, peritoneal, synovial and pericardial fluids are aspirated aseptically into sterile containers, their colour, turbidity, viscosity and clots are recorded, and portions go to cell count and differential, protein and glucose, culture and cytology; the culture portion is sent promptly at room temperature so the organisms stay viable. As with CSF for culture, the fluid is not chilled; ice, refrigeration and freezing are instructions for other specimen types.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Body Fluid Samples)

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen tested six hours after collection, unrefrigerated, reads pH 8.5 with trace protein, although the patient's previous urinalyses were normal. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: Bacteria in the standing urine broke down urea into ammonia, and the alkaline pH can falsely raise the protein pad
The patient has early renal tubular acidosis, which raises the urine pH and lets albumin leak through the glomerulus
The specimen became too concentrated while standing, and concentrated urine lowers the pH while raising the protein
The patient ate a high-protein meal before voiding, which alkalinizes the urine and produces transient proteinuria
preguntas.explicacion: The most common cause of an alkaline urine is a stale specimen: bacteria multiply and break down urea, releasing ammonia and pushing the pH up. An alkaline pH, in turn, is a listed cause of false-positive protein on the strip. Renal tubular acidosis can produce alkaline urine but is not the likely reading for a six-hour-old specimen, and a high-protein diet is associated with acid, not alkaline, urine.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Chemical Examination: pH; Proteins)

preguntas.pregunta: Two blood culture sets were drawn five minutes apart. One grows Staphylococcus epidermidis; the other stays negative. How is the positive set generally classified?
opciones: A probable contaminant: a commensal in one of several sets
True bacteremia that calls for empiric vancomycin
A single-set culture that must be recollected in full
A catheter-associated bloodstream infection of the line
preguntas.explicacion: A contaminated blood culture is generally defined as one set out of multiple sets being positive for a commensal organism, and the CDC's worked example uses exactly this case, a coagulase-negative staphylococcus in one of two sets, to compute a contamination rate. That is one reason two sets are required: a single set gives no way to judge whether a commensal is a contaminant. Nothing in the scenario involves a catheter.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Blood Culture Contamination: An Overview for Infection Control and Antibiotic Stewardship Programs (2022), Tracking the Blood Culture Contamination Rate

preguntas.pregunta: Which complication is specific to the site chosen for an intramuscular injection?
opciones: Nerve injury: the sciatic in a gluteal site, the radial in the deltoid
Nerve injury: the sciatic in the deltoid, the radial in a gluteal site
Abscess formation, which happens only when the deltoid is the site used
Glass particles injected, which happens only when a vial is used for the dose
preguntas.explicacion: The nerve at risk depends on where the needle goes: the sciatic nerve with a gluteal injection, the superior gluteal nerve with a dorsogluteal one, the femoral nerve at the vastus lateralis and the radial nerve at the deltoid. The other complications listed are not site specific: persistent pain, muscle fibrosis and contracture, abscess, gangrene, skin slough, periostitis, vascular injury, and glass particles from ampoules and vials.

preguntas.pregunta: When must safety data sheets be accessible to laboratory employees under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: During each work shift, while employees are in their work areas
Within 10 working days of a request, through the safety officer
During business hours only, in the administrator's office
At the annual training, when the chemical inventory is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 requires employers to keep the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments of hazardous chemicals and to make them readily accessible during each work shift to laboratory employees when they are in their work areas; the same wording applies to sealed-container operations in (b)(4)(ii). Employers must also keep labels on incoming containers intact and give the training of paragraph (h). A sheet that can only be obtained days later, or only in an office during business hours, does not meet the test.

preguntas.pregunta: How many vertebrae are in the cervical, thoracic and lumbar regions of the spine?

Five cervical, twelve thoracic and seven lumbar
Twelve cervical, seven thoracic and five lumbar
Seven cervical, five thoracic and twelve lumbar
preguntas.explicacion: The vertebral column runs seven cervical vertebrae in the neck, twelve thoracic ones that carry the ribs, and five lumbar ones in the small of the back, ending in the sacrum and the coccyx. The count matters when a report places a finding at a numbered level.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does CLIA require the requisition to name a contact person for the authorized person who ordered the test?
opciones: So that imminently life-threatening results or panic values can be reported to someone
So that the laboratory can bill the correct account for the tests performed
So that the patient can be called back if a second specimen is needed
So that the courier knows whom to hand the specimen to when it is sent back to the office
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(1) ties the contact person on the requisition to one purpose: making it possible to report imminently life-threatening results and panic or alert values. Billing, recollection calls and courier logistics are not what the regulation names.

preguntas.pregunta: The patient's medicine list shows a blood thinner. Which team member does the phlebotomy guidance say to consult?
opciones: The pharmacist, about medicines that might cause complications
The pathologist, who supervises the laboratory that will test it
The phlebotomist, who chooses which tube additive will be used
The ward clerk, who records the medicines on the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Providers must know the patient's medical history and any pre-existing conditions, and pharmacists should be consulted where the patient is on blood thinners or other medicines that might cause unwanted complications. For complex cases with difficult venous access it is a certified phlebotomist who is consulted; the pathologist supervises the laboratory itself.

preguntas.pregunta: Records submitted for review carry initials nobody can identify. Which document is meant to resolve that?
opciones: A signature log matching the printed name of the author to the initials used
An amendment adding the missing names to each of the disputed chart entries
A business associate agreement with the company that scanned the paper charts
An accounting of disclosures listing everyone who has opened the record so far
preguntas.explicacion: A signature log lists the typed or printed name of an author alongside the initials or the illegible signature used in the documentation. It may sit on the page itself or stand as a separate document. Reviewers are told to consider every log submitted regardless of when it was created, and may not deny a claim just because the log leaves out credentials, although listing them is encouraged.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports a critical glucose value three hours after it was measured because the result sat unreviewed. In which phase of the total testing process did this error occur?
opciones: Post-analytical, which includes failure or delay in reporting critical values
Analytical, which includes undetected failure of the quality control system
Pre-analytical, which includes sorting, routing and labeling of specimens
Post-post-analytical, which includes the clinician's delayed reaction to the report
preguntas.explicacion: The post-analytical phase, 13 to 20 % of errors, covers wrong validation of data, failure in reporting or addressing the report, excessive turnaround time, transcription mistakes and failure or delay in reporting critical values, which is exactly a result left unreviewed for three hours. The clinician's own delayed reaction to a report that did arrive would be post-post-analytical.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient moves to a skilled nursing facility and stays thirty days. What does Part A leave her to pay in 2026?
opciones: Nothing for the first twenty days, then $217 for each of the ten that follow
No charge for the first sixty days, then $434 for each of the ten that follow
A charge of $217 for every one of the thirty days, counting from admission
The whole cost herself, because a skilled nursing stay sits outside Part A
preguntas.explicacion: A skilled nursing facility stay costs the patient nothing for days one to twenty, then $217 a day for days twenty-one to a hundred, and everything from day a hundred and one onwards. preguntas.pregunta: Insufficient volume was the second most common reason for rejection in the emergency laboratory. Which measure did the laboratory adopt for pediatric, geriatric, oncology and neonatal ICU patients?
opciones: Preferring microtainers and microtubes, together with analyzers that need minimal specimen and dead volume
Drawing a second full set of tubes from every such patient so that one set can serve as a backup
Accepting any fill level from these units and adding a comment on the ratio to the report
Pooling the blood from two partially filled tubes of the same patient before centrifugation
preguntas.explicacion: Because collecting enough blood from newborns, children, oncology and intensive care patients is difficult, and because frequent draws put children at risk of anemia, the laboratory prefers microtainers and microtubes for those groups and uses automated instruments with minimized specimen and dead volume. With a Doctor of Pharmacy degree and a state pharmacy license
With an associate's degree and a national certification exam
With a bachelor's degree and supervised clinical experience
preguntas.explicacion: Pharmacy technicians typically need a high school diploma or the equivalent and learn their duties through on-the-job training, though some complete a postsecondary program in pharmacy technology. preguntas.pregunta: According to WHO step 9, which information does the laboratory typically require on the tube label?

Names, room number, date of birth, and the ordering physician's full name
Names, file number, diagnosis code, and the phlebotomist's initials
Names, date of birth, the tests ordered, and the tube's additive
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 asks the phlebotomist to check the label and forms for accuracy and describes the usual content: the patient's first and last names, the file number, the date of birth, and the date and time the blood was taken. preguntas.pregunta: During a heel-prick the phlebotomist presses the lancet device hard against the skin to be sure it fires. What is the problem with this?
opciones: Too much compression can produce a deeper puncture than is needed for good flow
Too much compression makes the puncture shallower, so a second stick is usually needed
Pressing hard is required, because a lancet held loosely will not reach 2.4 mm
Pressing hard is acceptable on the heel but not on the finger, where bone is closer
preguntas.explicacion: Too much compression is avoided because it may cause a deeper puncture than is needed to get good flow. Pressure compresses the skin, so the actual puncture is slightly deeper than the lancet length. That is also why one chooses a lancet slightly shorter than the estimated depth.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these patient situations is associated with a higher hematocrit rather than a lower one?
opciones: Living permanently at high altitude
Being in the later months of pregnancy
Retaining too much water in the body
Having chronic kidney disease for years
preguntas.explicacion: Persistent hypoxia at high altitude raises the red cell count, so inhabitants of high altitudes have a higher hematocrit; smokers and patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are high for the same reason. Pregnancy lowers the hematocrit through hemodilution, and too much water in the body and chronic kidney disease are both listed causes of a low hematocrit. Newborns start high and adult men run higher than women.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declines to attempt an arterial puncture she has not been trained to perform. Which ethical principle does this reflect?
opciones: Nonmaleficence: avoiding a risky procedure outside one's competence
Beneficence: bringing goodness by attempting any procedure the patient needs
Justice: giving each patient the same procedures regardless of skill
Autonomy: the phlebotomist's right to choose which tasks to do
preguntas.explicacion: Nonmaleficence means not bringing harm, and the Hippocratic tradition lists attempting a risky procedure outside the practitioner's competence among the things to avoid, together with violating privacy. Staying within one's training is therefore an ethical duty as well as a scope-of-practice rule. Beneficence would be misread if it meant attempting anything a patient needs regardless of skill; justice concerns fair distribution of resources; and autonomy in medical ethics refers to the patient's self-determination, not the worker's preferences.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Nonmaleficence

preguntas.pregunta: An 80-year-old arrives with a new tremor and takes nine medications. What does the assessment call for first?
opciones: A full medication reconciliation, since new symptoms may come from the drugs
A referral for imaging of the head, since the tremor is a new neurological sign
A repeat set of vital signs, since polypharmacy is only reviewed once a year
A cognitive screen, since tremor in this age group points to early dementia
preguntas.explicacion: In an older patient, any new sign or symptom is treated as possibly caused by the medications until shown otherwise, so the list is scrutinized first. Reconciliation is done at least yearly and after every transition of care, and a published list of drugs to avoid in older adults guides what should come off.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Geriatric Care Special Needs Assessment", Issues of Concern: Polypharmacy

preguntas.pregunta: A patient spent two nights in the hospital under observation, then one night as an admitted inpatient. Does that meet the qualifying stay for a SNF?
opciones: No, because time spent under observation does not count toward the three-day stay
Yes, because three nights inside the building satisfy the three-day qualifying stay
Yes, because observation nights count whenever the patient is later admitted
No, because a qualifying stay has to reach seven days counting the discharge day
preguntas.explicacion: Time under observation services or in the emergency department before admission does not count toward the three-day qualifying inpatient stay, even overnight. Only days as an admitted inpatient count, starting the day of admission and leaving out the day of discharge. A doctor in an ACO approved for a three-day rule waiver, or a Medicare Advantage plan, may set the requirement aside.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Coverage details

preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory form arrives with the tests listed but no date of birth printed on it. Which step cannot be completed as it stands?
opciones: Matching the laboratory form to the patient's identity before the draw
Placing the requisition in the outer pocket of the transportation bag
Inverting the additive tubes the number of times the laboratory sets
Cleaning the entry site with 70% alcohol and letting it dry completely
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 has the health worker introduce themselves, ask the patient to state the full name, and then check that the laboratory form matches the patient's identity. A form with no date of birth cannot be matched that way, and the paediatric section spells out name, date of birth and hospital or file number as what the form should carry. The other three steps come later.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is exposed to a pathogen but feels nothing for several days. Which period of disease is that, and what is happening?
opciones: The incubation period, while the pathogen multiplies below the level that causes signs
The prodromal period, while the pathogen multiplies below the level that causes signs
The period of decline, while the pathogen multiplies below the level that causes signs
The convalescent period, while the pathogen multiplies above the level that causes signs
preguntas.explicacion: Disease runs through five periods: incubation, prodromal, illness, decline and convalescence. During incubation the pathogen is already multiplying but has not reached the numbers needed to produce signs and symptoms, so the patient has no idea anything has begun. General complaints such as fever and aching mark the prodromal period that follows.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Periods of Disease

preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, when must an employee wash their hands after removing gloves?
opciones: Immediately, or as soon as feasible, after the gloves come off
Only when blood or OPIM reached the skin beneath the gloves
At the end of the work shift, as with contaminated work surfaces
Not at all, if an antiseptic hand cleanser was used instead of soap
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(v) puts the duty on the employer: employees wash their hands right away, or as soon as it is feasible, once gloves or any other protective equipment come off. The rule does not wait for blood to reach the skin; that is a separate trigger in (d)(2)(vi). End of shift is the timing the standard gives for possibly contaminated surfaces, not for hands. And paragraph (d)(2)(iv) allows antiseptic cleansers or towelettes only where handwashing facilities are not feasible, adding that hands still have to be washed, with soap and running water, as soon as it is feasible afterwards.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(iv) and (d)(2)(v), Methods of Compliance

preguntas.pregunta: The last tube has been filled from the syringe. What does the guidance forbid at that point?
opciones: Recapping the needle and taking it off the syringe by hand
Placing the syringe and needle together into the sharps bin
Inverting the additive tubes before they leave the bedside
Checking the labels against the request form a second time
preguntas.explicacion: The step that covers filling tubes ends with an instruction not to recap and remove the needle. If a used needle really has to come off a syringe it is re-sheathed with a one-hand scoop and taken off with a removal device, never with bare hands, and discarded at once.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a red eye with thick discharge that keeps coming back after it is wiped away and sticks to the lashes. Which cause does that discharge suggest?
opciones: Bacterial conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Viral conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Allergic conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Toxin-induced conjunctivitis, which gives purulent discharge and no redness
preguntas.explicacion: The type of discharge is the most useful clue. Bacterial conjunctivitis produces purulent discharge that reforms after it is removed, or thicker mucopurulent discharge that clings to the lashes. In both viral and allergic conjunctivitis the discharge is watery instead, and a swollen node in front of the ear points to the viral kind.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conjunctivitis", History and Physical

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the arm is the preferred site for a limb electrode, and why?
opciones: The inside of the lower arm, where the skin is thinner
The outside of the upper arm, where the skin is thinner
The inside of the upper arm, where the muscle is thicker
The back of the forearm, where there is the least hair
preguntas.explicacion: The inner surface of the lower arm is chosen because the skin there is thinner, which gives a better signal. The tab of the electrode points up toward the arm, and the clip connector is attached to the tab once the electrode is pressed down.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: What makes the first heart sound?
opciones: The mitral and tricuspid valves closing as systole begins
The aortic and pulmonic valves closing as systole begins
The mitral and tricuspid valves opening as diastole begins
The aortic and pulmonic valves opening as diastole begins
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure in the ventricle passes that of the atrium, the mitral valve shuts together with the tricuspid, and that closure both marks the start of systole and produces the first sound. The second comes at the other end, when the aortic and pulmonic valves close.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cardiac Cycle", Mechanism

preguntas.pregunta: After finishing an interview at the bedside, which set of checks is made before leaving the room?
opciones: Call light within reach, bed low and locked, side rails secured, table reachable, floor clear
Head of the bed at 45 degrees, side rails down, and the brakes released so it can be moved
Bed raised to a safe working height with the rails lowered and a wheelchair set at 45 degrees
The room lights switched off, the door pulled shut and the privacy curtain drawn round the bed
preguntas.explicacion: Five safety measures close every bedside encounter: the call light in reach, the bed in its lowest position with the brakes on, the side rails secured, the table in reach, and the room scanned so nothing is left to trip over. A raised bed with the rails down and a wheelchair at an angle describes the start of a transfer, not the state a patient is left in.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.11: Checklist for Obtaining a Health History
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A1 · NCMA 2A.5

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's video remote interpreting picture is choppy and grainy. Under the ADA rules, what follows?
opciones: The service falls short of the performance standards set for that method
The service is acceptable, since remote interpreting carries no standards
The patient must accept it, because an on-site interpreter costs far more
The patient must supply a relative to interpret until the link is fixed
preguntas.explicacion: Where video remote interpreting is chosen, specific performance standards must all be met: real-time full-motion video and audio over a dedicated high-speed or wireless connection delivering quality images with no lags or choppy, blurry or grainy pictures; an image sharp and large enough to show face, arms, hands and fingers; clear audio; and staff trained to set it up.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory receives a urine in a boric acid tube and is asked to run both a culture and a reagent strip on it. What is the concern with the strip?
opciones: Boric acid can produce false-negative strip results for protein, leukocytes and ketones, and it alters the pH
Boric acid can produce false-positive strip results for leukocyte esterase, glucose and urobilinogen
Boric acid dissolves pus cells, so the leukocyte pad reads falsely high while the culture stays valid
Boric acid raises the pH above 7, which produces a false-positive protein reaction on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the usual preservative for culture: it keeps the pH below 7 and prevents pus cells from dissolving, but it interferes with several strip pads and is linked to false-negative protein, leukocyte and ketone readings, which limits combining strip testing and culture in one tube. False-positive leukocyte esterase, glucose and urobilinogen are the effects of formaldehyde, and an alkaline pH is what boric acid prevents.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Interfering Factors (Preservatives)

preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are described as more likely to have a vasovagal faint during a venous procedure?
opciones: Those seated rather than lying, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those lying rather than seated, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those seated rather than lying, when more than three tubes are drawn
Those lying rather than seated, when the needle is larger than 21 gauge
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting of this kind is reported more often in people who are sitting up than in those lying down, and in people who have fainted before or who are markedly anxious about blood or needles. Those are exactly the patients who are asked about earlier faints and offered a lying position.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications

preguntas.pregunta: What is the maximum civil money penalty for all violations of an identical HIPAA provision in one calendar year?
opciones: $1.5 million for all identical violations
$50,000 for all identical violations
$25,000 for all identical violations
$100,000 for all identical violations
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH set a ceiling of $1.5 million for all violations of an identical provision, and the regulation repeats that figure as the annual cap in each of the four tiers. The $50,000 figure is the per-violation maximum inside a tier, and $25,000 was the annual cap that applied to identical violations occurring before February 18, 2009. These amounts are adjusted for inflation and published at 45 CFR part 102.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, HITECH Act Enforcement Interim Final Rule; 45 CFR 160.404

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant's forearm brushes the edge of the sink partway through the scrub. What is required?
opciones: Wash that area for an extra minute before going on with the rest of the scrub
Start the whole scrub again from the nail cleaner, since the count has been broken
Carry on, because the sink is scrubbed between cases and counts as a clean surface
Rinse that arm at once and then resume, since rinsing removes what the sink deposited
preguntas.explicacion: Touching an already-scrubbed area, or bumping the sink, means washing that area for an extra minute and continuing. The rule hardens once the scrub is finished: from then on touching any nonsterile surface means scrubbing again from the start. Rinsing is not begun until both hands and arms are done.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method

preguntas.pregunta: Why do the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions supply many of the same organs?
opciones: One stimulates and the other inhibits, and the balance maintains homeostasis
Both stimulate together, and the doubled signal maintains homeostasis
One carries sensory fibers and the other motor fibers to the same organ
One works during the day and the other only during sleep at night
preguntas.explicacion: Many visceral organs receive fibers from both autonomic divisions, and the two work against each other: where one stimulates, the other inhibits. That antagonistic relationship is not waste but a brake and an accelerator on the same organ, and the balance between them is what holds the internal setting steady.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Peripheral Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who had surgery on the right knee is being taught to use a cane. In which hand does it go?
opciones: The left hand, opposite the leg that is weaker or was operated on
The right hand, on the same side as the leg that was operated on
Either hand, as long as the tip lands ahead of the stronger leg
The right hand, changing to the left once the knee bears weight
preguntas.explicacion: The cane is held on the side away from the weak leg. Cane and weak leg then swing forward together and land level with each other, some of the load shifts onto the cane, and the strong leg steps past. Turning is done by pivoting on the strong leg. The tip, or all four prongs, must be flat on the floor before any weight goes onto the cane.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Cane Basics
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14

preguntas.pregunta: Which change tells you a patient with heat illness has reached heat stroke?
opciones: A temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) with confusion, and sweating may stop
A temperature above 100 °F (38 °C) with heavy sweating and severe thirst
A temperature below 95 °F (35 °C) with shivering and cool moist skin
A temperature above 102 °F (38.9 °C) with cramps in both of the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Heat stroke is the point where the body can no longer control its temperature and the temperature keeps climbing: fever above 104 °F (40 °C), confusion, irrational behavior, slurred speech, seizures or unconsciousness, and sweating may stop. It can cause shock, brain damage, organ failure and death, so the emergency number is called at once.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heat emergencies", Symptoms

preguntas.pregunta: At what age does stranger anxiety typically appear?
opciones: Between 6 and 12 months of age
Between 2 and 4 months of age
Between 18 and 30 months of age
Between 3 and 5 years of age
preguntas.explicacion: Between 6 and 12 months an effective attachment forms with a responsive caregiver, and stranger anxiety emerges as the infant starts telling the familiar from the unfamiliar; distress at separation belongs here too. Recognizing the primary caregiver by sight comes earlier, at around 5 months.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops an infection at a surgical site after an operation. Which two labels describe that disease?
opciones: Iatrogenic, contracted as the result of a medical procedure, and nosocomial
Zoonotic, transferred from an animal to a human, and noncommunicable
Congenital, present at or before birth, and degenerative in its course
Idiopathic, of unknown cause, and inherited from parent to offspring
preguntas.explicacion: Iatrogenic diseases are contracted as the result of a medical procedure, such as a wound treatment, a catheterization or surgery whose site becomes contaminated. Diseases picked up in a hospital are called nosocomial, and the two often describe the same event. A zoonosis, by contrast, passes from an animal to a person.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Classifications of Disease

preguntas.pregunta: A new transdermal patch is being applied. Which sequence is correct?
opciones: Remove the old patch, clean and dry the skin, then press the new one 10 seconds
Apply the new patch beside the old one, and remove the old one the following day
Clean the skin with alcohol, apply the patch, and rub the medication surface in
Warm the skin first, apply the patch, and cover it with an occlusive dressing
preguntas.explicacion: Gloves are worn and the rights are checked as for any medication. The previous patch comes off first, the skin around it is assessed for irritation, and the site is cleansed and dried. The clear plastic backing is removed without touching the medication surface, the patch goes on an area the manufacturer allows, such as the upper arms or chest, and it is pressed firmly for ten seconds. Broken or irritated skin is avoided.

preguntas.pregunta: Which group of workers does the medical home model name as part of the care team?
opciones: Advanced practice nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists and social workers
Only the physician and the nurse, with other disciplines seen on referral
Hospital case managers and payer staff, who direct the practice's decisions
The hospice nurse, the chaplain and the medical director of the agency
preguntas.explicacion: Providing comprehensive care requires a team of care providers, and the model names physicians, advanced practice nurses, physician assistants, nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists, social workers, educators and care coordinators. preguntas.pregunta: A patient on Medicare is told her skilled nursing coverage ends on Friday and she believes she still needs it. What is she entitled to?
opciones: A fast appeal, plus a written notice before the services end telling her how to ask
A fast appeal, but only once the standard first-level appeal has been decided
A standard appeal, since fast appeals cover only inpatient hospital stays
A standard appeal, since fast appeals cover only drugs a plan refuses to pay
preguntas.explicacion: The fast appeal exists for the patient who thinks Medicare-covered services are ending too soon, and it reaches services from a hospital, a skilled nursing facility, a home health agency, a comprehensive outpatient rehabilitation facility or hospice. The provider has to give a written notice before the services stop that explains how to ask for one, and the patient should ask for that notice if it does not arrive.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls asking for a refill on a Schedule II prescription. What does federal regulation allow?
opciones: No refill at all; the practitioner may issue multiple prescriptions for a 90-day supply
Up to five refills within six months, counted from the date the prescription was issued
One refill only, if the pharmacist records the date and quantity on the back of it
Refills with no set limit, as long as the prescription is less than six months old
preguntas.explicacion: Refilling a Schedule II prescription is prohibited outright. What the practitioner may do instead is issue several prescriptions on the same occasion that together authorize the patient to receive up to a 90-day supply, each one written for a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of practice. Five refills inside six months is the Schedule III and IV rule, and it does not extend to Schedule II.

preguntas.pregunta: A strip was cut short and carries only two complete complexes in each lead group. Why does it fail the quality check?
opciones: Four standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Ten standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Six standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Two standard complexes have to appear in every lead
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptance list is short and mechanical: the complexes clearly drawn with the P wave in plain view, the P wave and the QRS upright in lead I, a baseline that does not wander past 5 mm, and four standard complexes on the tracing. A short strip fails on the last one.

preguntas.pregunta: What information does the guideline require on the label of a sterilized item?
opciones: A load number naming the sterilizer, the cycle or load, the date, and any expiration date
The initials of the person who wrapped it, the cycle length, and the chamber temperature
The names of the instruments inside, the wrap material used, and the date of the last service
The department it belongs to, the number of previous cycles, and the shelf it is stored on
preguntas.explicacion: Labeling exists so a pack can be traced back to its run. The label carries a load number identifying which sterilizer was used, the cycle or load number, the date it was processed and, where it applies, an expiration date. That is what makes a recall possible when a spore test later comes back positive.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why one lab result is labeled hyperglycemia and another hypoglycemia. Which pair of prefixes explains the difference?
opciones: Hyper- means above or excessive; hypo- means under or deficient
Hyper- means quick or rapid; hypo- means slow or delayed
Hyper- means large or long; hypo- means small or short
Hyper- means outer or outside; hypo- means within or inner
preguntas.explicacion: These two prefixes sit in the group of numbers and amounts: hyper- is above, beyond or excessive, and hypo- is under or deficient. Attached to the root for sugar and the ending -emia, a blood condition, they name too much and too little glucose in the blood. Fast and slow are tachy- and brady-; large and small are macro- and micro-.

preguntas.pregunta: What does organizational health literacy add to the definition?
opciones: The duty of organizations to equitably enable people to use health information
The duty of organizations to test each patient's reading level at intake
The duty of organizations to publish their materials in at least six languages
The duty of patients to tell the practice when a handout is too difficult
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside personal health literacy the 2020 definitions name organizational health literacy: how far an organization equitably enables people to find, understand and use information and services for their own health decisions. preguntas.pregunta: The morning reading shows the sample refrigerator drifted above its acceptable range some time overnight. What is the required sequence?
opciones: Stop testing, ask the person who supervises testing, and document what was done
Move the samples to a second refrigerator and carry on with the day's testing
Repeat the reading in an hour and act only if it is still out of range
Discard every reagent in the unit and record the loss in the maintenance log
preguntas.explicacion: If the temperature falls outside the recommended range for any length of time, testing stops and the person who directs or supervises the testing is contacted for guidance on the next steps, which include whether the affected reagents, kits, controls or samples have to be discarded and when testing may resume. Every corrective action taken is documented.

opciones: The GAD-7, for generalized anxiety disorder
The GAD-7, for major depressive disorder
The PHQ-9, for generalized anxiety disorder
The PHQ-9, for post-traumatic stress disorder
preguntas.explicacion: The 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale has been validated both to help make the diagnosis and to grade severity, and it is also used to follow patients over time. The 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire is the self-report depression scale used in primary care for screening and monitoring.

preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is asked by a classmate to describe the questions on the exam he just sat. What is the risk if he does?
opciones: Misconduct, which can void scores, revoke the credential and bar retesting
A written warning, after which the credential continues without change
A delay in scoring, which is lifted once the candidate signs an attestation
A fee for re-registration, which the candidate pays before the next attempt
preguntas.explicacion: Misrepresenting eligibility, giving a false attestation, breaking the testing rules of conduct or failing to follow the codes of ethics all count as misconduct. Anything that could compromise the security, validity or integrity of an exam draws discipline, which can run to invalidating scores, revoking the credential and banning the person from that exam or any other one offered.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a suspected wrist fracture is sent for the least expensive study that shows bone well. Which one is it, and why does it work?
opciones: A plain X-ray, because hard tissue blocks the beam and shows up light
A plain X-ray, because hard tissue absorbs no beam and shows up dark
An ultrasound, because sound waves pass easily through cortical bone
A PET scan, because the tracer collects in the mineral part of bone
preguntas.explicacion: X-rays are only slightly slowed by soft tissue, which comes out gray, while bone and teeth block most of the beam and leave a light shadow on the plate. That contrast is why the X-ray is still the workhorse for fractures and for dentistry. Ultrasound cannot get through bone or gas at all.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging, X-Rays

preguntas.pregunta: Which Korotkoff phases mark the systolic and the diastolic pressures?
opciones: Phase I marks the systolic and phase V, when all sound goes, marks the diastolic
Phase I marks the systolic and phase IV, the abrupt muffling, marks the diastolic
Phase II marks the systolic and phase V, when all sound goes, marks the diastolic
Phase III marks the systolic and phase IV, the abrupt muffling, marks the diastolic
preguntas.explicacion: Phase I is the clear tapping heard for at least two beats in a row, and that is the systolic pressure. Phase IV is the sudden muffling into a soft blowing sound, and phase V is silence, which is the diastolic. Phases II and III, the swishing and the return of sharper sounds, have no known clinical meaning.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Mechanism

preguntas.pregunta: Besides limiting who may receive information from a chart, what else must a hospital's confidentiality procedure prevent?
opciones: Unauthorized people gaining access to the records or altering what is in them
Authorized staff consulting a record outside the hours the department is open
Clinicians correcting an entry that they themselves made earlier in the same day
Copies leaving the department without the medical record service's own stamp
preguntas.explicacion: The condition asks for a procedure that keeps the records confidential in two directions: information and copies go only to authorized individuals, and unauthorized individuals must not be able to reach the records or change what they contain. Originals leave the hospital only under federal or state law, a court order or a subpoena.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these findings is an underlying cause of petechiae?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia
Hemoconcentration
Hypoglycemia
Venous fibrosis
preguntas.explicacion: Petechiae have four primary causes: thrombocytopenia, platelet dysfunction, disorders of coagulation and loss of vascular integrity. Hemoconcentration is the tourniquet artifact in the phlebotomy chapter, hypoglycemia is a mimic of syncope, and venous fibrosis is a local contraindication to puncture; none is listed as a cause of petechial bleeding.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Continuing Education Activity

preguntas.pregunta: How are the wax pencil marks taken off the chest once the recording is over?
opciones: With gauze and baby oil, after the electrodes are removed
With gauze and alcohol, after the electrodes are removed
With soap and warm water, before the patient gets dressed
They are left in place for the next recording on that patient
preguntas.explicacion: After the tracings are taken from the machine and labeled and the electrodes are peeled off, the cosmetic pencil marks are wiped away with gauze and baby oil, and the patient puts the gown back on. Alcohol has a different job: cleaning the sites beforehand.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of signs marks the stress response that can block a conversation?
opciones: Irritability, sweaty palms, a racing heart, poor sleep
Fever, chills, muscle aches and a productive cough
Confusion, slurred speech and one-sided weakness
Yearning, numbness and a sense of a person's presence
preguntas.explicacion: The stress response is a common psychological barrier that changes both how a message is sent and how it is received, and its symptoms are irritability, sweaty palms, a racing heart, trouble concentrating and impaired sleep. Yearning, numbness and a sense of presence are emotional and cognitive signs of grief.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Managing the Stress Response

preguntas.pregunta: How long must intense grief persist in an adult before prolonged grief disorder is considered?
opciones: More than 1 year, against 6 months in children
More than 6 months, against 1 year in children
More than 3 months, against 6 weeks in children
More than 2 years, against 1 year in children
preguntas.explicacion: Most adults process grief adequately within a year, and children and adolescents within six months; that does not mean forgetting, only that daily life is no longer severely limited. Prolonged grief disorder is the failure to move from acute to integrated grief, and it reaches as many as 7 percent of bereaved people.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Grief and Prolonged Grief Disorder", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Types of grief · CCMA 1E k34

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's point-of-care hemoglobin reads 19 g/dL. A new assistant wants to flag it as dangerously high. How should the result be interpreted?
opciones: It is within the newborn reference range of about 14 to 24 g/dL and is not abnormal for this age
It exceeds the adult male upper limit of 17.2 g/dL and should be reported to the provider as critical
It is above the infant range of 9.5 to 14 g/dL, so the sample was probably too concentrated
It is high for any age and suggests chronic low oxygen, which is the usual cause of a raised hemoglobin
preguntas.explicacion: Reference values depend on age: adult men run about 13.8 to 17.2 g/dL and women 12.1 to 15.1, but newborns normally measure 14 to 24 g/dL, and infants 9.5 to 14. A value of 19 g/dL in a newborn is therefore expected, not critical. Chronic hypoxia is the most common cause of a truly high hemoglobin in other patients, and laboratories' ranges vary slightly, so the age-specific range is what should be checked.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Hemoglobin (003645), Normal Results; What Abnormal Results Mean

preguntas.pregunta: A child has a bead lodged in the ear canal. Which approach succeeds on the first attempt most often?
opciones: Taking hold of it with forceps, which works about four times in five
Flushing it out with saline irrigation, which works about two in three
Sticking it to a cotton-tipped applicator with tissue adhesive
Hooking it out with a Katz extractor passed beyond the object
preguntas.explicacion: Forceps — alligator, bayonet, mosquito or straight — are the instrument reached for most often and had the highest first-pass success at 78.3 %. Saline irrigation came next at 65.2 %. Tissue adhesive on a cotton-tipped applicator reached 19.1 % and the Katz extractor 16.5 %.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Foreign Body Removal", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k63

preguntas.pregunta: By which route and at which site is epinephrine given for anaphylaxis?
opciones: Intramuscularly, into the outer middle part of either thigh
Subcutaneously, into the fatty layer over the back of the arm
Intramuscularly, into the deltoid muscle of the dominant arm
Intravenously, at the concentration used for an intramuscular dose
preguntas.explicacion: Epinephrine goes into muscle, and the thigh is preferred over the deltoid. Intramuscular delivery works faster and gives better outcomes than the subcutaneous or the intravascular route. The intravenous route uses a different, more dilute concentration and carries a much higher risk of cardiovascular complications.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Treatment / Management: Epinephrine
