preguntas.pregunta: How is the temperature of a vaccine storage unit monitored?
opciones: With a digital data logger recording at least every 30 minutes, probe in the middle
With a household thermometer read twice a day and written on a paper log sheet
With a digital data logger recording once a day, its probe taped to the door frame
With an alarm that sounds only when the unit passes the upper limit of the range
preguntas.explicacion: Every storage unit needs a reliable temperature monitoring device, and the CDC recommends a continuous recording digital data logger set to record at intervals no longer than every 30 minutes. A detachable probe buffered with glycol, glass beads, sand or Teflon tracks vaccine temperature more closely than a standard thermometer, which follows the air. The device sits in the centre of the unit with vaccines around it.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 5: Temperature Monitoring Devices
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k74 · CMA I.D.3.a(5)

preguntas.pregunta: Which heart valve has two cusps, and where is it located?
opciones: The mitral valve, between the left atrium and left ventricle
The tricuspid valve, between the right atrium and right ventricle
The aortic semilunar valve, at the base of the ascending aorta
The pulmonary semilunar valve, at the base of the pulmonary trunk
preguntas.explicacion: The mitral valve, also called the bicuspid or left atrioventricular valve, has two cusps tied by chordae tendineae to two papillary muscles and guards the opening between the left atrium and ventricle; in clinical use it is called mitral. The tricuspid has three flaps, and the two semilunar valves, pulmonary and aortic, each have three flaps and no chordae tendineae.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Valve Structure and Function

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is preparing the skin. For which collection does the thirty-second alcohol swab instruction not apply?
opciones: A blood culture set
A coagulation panel
A fasting glucose
A cross-match sample
preguntas.explicacion: The alcohol swab for thirty seconds with thirty seconds of drying is written for routine draws, and the exception named is a blood culture, which is prepared differently. Alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine for the routine case, because iodine can raise potassium, phosphorus and urate.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, requires the log to contain at least the type and brand of device involved, the department or work area where the exposure incident occurred, and an explanation of how it occurred, all recorded in a way that protects the injured employee's confidentiality. Names, source status and prophylaxis belong to the confidential medical record; training details belong to the training record; and the route of exposure and written opinion are part of the post-exposure evaluation file.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the median cubital vein the most common choice for a blood draw?
opciones: Its thick walls tolerate the negative pressure of the draw
It is the only vein in the fossa that lacks an accompanying nerve
It is the preferred location for establishing an intravenous site
It is the most prominent vein without any tourniquet applied
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is superficial, sits over the bicipital aponeurosis and is the usual choice because its thick walls can withstand the negative pressures used when drawing blood. The dorsum of the hand, not this vein, is described as the preferred site for an IV; and the chapter does not claim the vein is nerve-free or always visible without a tourniquet.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology

preguntas.pregunta: The glucometer's liquid control reads outside the range printed on the bottle. Three patients are waiting. What should the operator do?
opciones: Hold patient results, look for the cause, correct it, repeat the control, then retest the patients
Test the patients now and note on each result that the control was out of range that morning
Repeat the control once; if it is still out, average the two readings and proceed if within range
Switch to a new bottle of control solution and report the patients if the second control passes
preguntas.explicacion: An unexpected control result, internal or external, stops patient reporting until the problem is found and fixed. The checklist: were the instructions followed, are the reagents, kits or controls outdated, were they stored correctly, could caps have been switched and cross-contaminated the vials, and what do the insert's troubleshooting steps say. Only after acceptable repeat QC are patient samples retested and final results reported.

preguntas.pregunta: The morning temperature log for the specimen refrigerator reads 10 °C (50 °F). Why does this reading call for action?
opciones: A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F), so 10 °C is above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 15 and 30 °C (59 to 86 °F), so 10 °C is below range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), so 10 °C is far above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 0 and 4 °C (32 to 39 °F), so 10 °C is above range
preguntas.explicacion: A refrigerator used to store patient samples is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F); the 15 to 30 °C band is room temperature for testing and storage, and −25 to −15 °C is the usual sample freezer. The acceptable range for any unit is fixed by the manufacturer's instructions for the reagents, kits, controls and samples inside it, and the temperature is checked and recorded daily even when the unit has an alarm or a data logger.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Temperature Log Instructions

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is wrapping up a long intake interview. Which technique both shows active listening and can close it?
opciones: Summarizing what was said, in the interviewer's own words
Reflecting the patient's words back, at times word for word
Offering social pleasantries that put the patient at ease
Providing the rationale for why the information is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Summarizing pulls together what the patient said in the interviewer's own words. It demonstrates active listening, builds a shared understanding, and occasionally serves to complete the interview. Social pleasantries belong at the start, and reflecting repeats a single statement rather than gathering several.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: In what order does the CDC-recommended sequence put on personal protective equipment?
opciones: Gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection, then gloves
Gloves, then gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection
Mask or respirator, then gloves, then gown, then eye protection
Eye protection, then mask or respirator, then gown, then gloves
preguntas.explicacion: The donning order is gown first, covering neck to knees and wrapping the back; then the mask or respirator, with the nose band fitted and a fit check for respirators; then goggles or a face shield; and gloves last, pulled over the cuffs of the gown. Donning takes place outside the patient room. Gloves go on last so that they are the cleanest item when patient contact begins and so that they cover the gown cuffs.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Proper Donning

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on a strong opioid is breathing 9 times a minute. Which term and which mechanism fit?
opciones: Bradypnea, which sedatives and opioids cause by depressing the drive to breathe
Bradypnea, which opioids cause by stiffening the chest wall against expansion
Hypoventilation, which in this patient comes from weakness of the breathing muscles
Apnea, which is the term for any rate under 12 breaths per minute in an adult
preguntas.explicacion: Fewer than 12 breaths a minute in an adult is bradypnea, and the usual company it keeps is sedative or opioid use, alcohol intoxication, hypothyroidism and traumatic brain injury. Neuromuscular disease causes hypoventilation through muscle weakness, and apnea means breathing has stopped, not that it has slowed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: How does the telehealth guidance want the setup steps delivered to a patient who has never used the platform?
opciones: As written step-by-step instructions, or as direct personal support from staff
As a single reminder message sent on the morning the appointment is due to start
As a printed leaflet given to her at the next office visit she attends in person
As a spoken summary during the opening minutes of the video appointment itself
preguntas.explicacion: Every patient arrives with different skills and comfort, and with older computers, out-of-date software or low bandwidth, so what is reviewed varies. The instruction is to provide written instructions that go through the entire process step by step, and the tip added is to have a coordinator, nurse, administrative staff member or community health worker walk her through it.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology

preguntas.pregunta: What does the term "CLIA-exempt" formally refer to?
opciones: A laboratory in a state whose licensure program CMS has found equal to or stricter than CLIA
A test system so simple that CLIA does not regulate the site that performs it
A test cleared by the FDA as substantially equivalent to one already on the market
A waived test that a Certificate of Waiver site may run without any inspection
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA-exempt describes a laboratory, never a test. It is a laboratory licensed or approved by a state whose laboratory laws CMS has judged equal to or more stringent than CLIA, with a CMS-approved licensure program; Washington and New York are the two states with approved programs. The substantially-equivalent wording is the definition of FDA-cleared, and simple low-risk tests are waived tests.

preguntas.pregunta: What does holistic care take into account?
opciones: Physical, mental, spiritual, cultural and social needs
Physical findings plus the current medication list
Insurance coverage plus the billing code for the visit
Provider orders plus the written policies of the office
preguntas.explicacion: Holism means treating the whole person: care is holistic when the patient's physical, mental, spiritual, cultural and social needs are all folded into it. preguntas.pregunta: Which minimum exposure is recognized for wrapped supplies in a gravity displacement steam sterilizer?
opciones: 30 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
45 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
15 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
60 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: The two working steam temperatures are 121 °C (250 °F) and 132 °C (270 °F), and the recognized minimums for wrapped supplies are 30 minutes at the lower one in a gravity displacement machine and 4 minutes at the higher one in a prevacuum machine. Forty-five minutes at 121 °C is the figure for decontaminating microbiological waste, where trapped air slows the steam.

preguntas.pregunta: What belongs in a letter terminating care?
opciones: The end date, cover until then, emergency resources and a records release
The end date, the clinical reason, and the name of the replacing clinician
The end date, the balance owed, and the date the account goes to collections
The end date, a copy of the chart, and the patient's signed acknowledgement
preguntas.explicacion: The letter states the date the relationship ends, says the clinician stays available for care and medication refills until then, points to emergency resources such as local crisis centers, and offers to send the records to a new clinician once the patient authorizes it, with a release form enclosed. Giving a reason is usually optional, and naming specific colleagues is debated.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Clinical Significance: Standardized notification

preguntas.pregunta: Which strategy fits a patient whose speech is impaired?
opciones: Phrasing questions so a yes or a no can answer them
Phrasing questions so only a long answer will serve
Directing the questions to the family member instead
Speaking louder and faster to shorten the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Phrase questions so the patient can answer yes or no, while staying alert that expressive aphasia can produce an automatic answer that is wrong. Cut excess noise, offer a writing tablet, flash cards or a picture board, present one idea at a time, speak slowly without shouting, and repeat back what was said.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Strategies to Improve Communication with Patients with Impaired Speech

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the three legal approaches to adequate informed consent do many states apply?
opciones: The reasonable patient standard, built on what a typical patient needs to know
The reasonable clinician standard, built on what a typical clinician would say
The subjective standard, built on what this one patient needs to understand
The documentation standard, built on what the consent form has room to hold
preguntas.explicacion: The state decides the standard, and three approaches are recognised: subjective, reasonable patient and reasonable clinician. Many states work from the reasonable patient standard because it turns on what the average patient needs in order to take part in the decision. Even so, the clinician determines which approach fits a given situation.

opciones: Gold separator tube, then dark green heparin, then light grey fluoride
Dark green heparin, then gold separator tube, then light grey fluoride
Light grey fluoride, then gold separator tube, then dark green heparin
Gold separator tube, then light grey fluoride, then dark green heparin

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient is treated for a back injury he suffered at work, and workers' compensation is open. Where does the claim go first?
opciones: To workers' compensation, which pays first for the job-related injury care
To Medicare, which pays first and then recovers from workers' compensation
To the patient, who pays and files for reimbursement from both payers
To the group health plan, which pays first for any injury of an employee
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation pays first for health care items and services related to a job-related illness or injury, and claims to a non-group health plan go to that insurer before Medicare. Medicare may make a conditional payment when a contested case drags on, but that is an exception it later recovers, not the normal first step. Billing the patient up front is prohibited when another payer is primary.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1 and Conditional Payments

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with heavy bleeding from a leg wound turns pale, cool and clammy and cannot answer questions clearly. How is the patient positioned?
opciones: Flat on the back with the legs raised about 12 inches (30 cm), head not raised
Sitting upright in a chair with the injured leg resting on a low stool
Flat on the back with the head raised about 12 inches (30 cm) on pillows
On the left side with the knees drawn up and the injured leg supported
preguntas.explicacion: The shock position is supine with the legs lifted roughly 12 inches, or 30 centimeters, and the head left down. It is used only when the patient is conscious and has no injury to the head, neck, spine or leg; if raising the legs causes pain or harm, the patient is left flat. The patient is kept warm and tight clothing is loosened.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A physician calls asking why no result was issued for a specimen sent that morning. The specimen had been rejected. What does the emergency laboratory do with rejected samples?
opciones: Stores them up to 24 hours at 4 °C and issues an immediate LIS report stating the sample was not processed
Discards them at once as biohazardous waste and telephones the ward within 30 minutes of rejection
Runs the tests anyway and reports the results with a comment noting the reason for rejection
Freezes them at –20 °C for one week in case the physician asks for the analysis to be repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Unsuitable samples are recognised at arrival by visual inspection and serum indices; those rejected are kept for up to 24 hours at 4 °C, and a report goes out immediately through the laboratory information system saying the sample was not processed. That report is how the ordering physician learns that a new specimen is needed; testing a rejected tube or discarding it unrecorded defeats the purpose.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I 5F · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a

preguntas.pregunta: What is the chain of custody for a specimen?
opciones: The sequential record of custody, control, transfer, analysis and disposal
The list of tests ordered on the specimen and the results each one returned
The temperature and light conditions the specimen was kept under in transit
The signed authorization the patient gives before the specimen is collected
preguntas.explicacion: It is the documented, sequential account of who held the specimen, who controlled it, every transfer, the analysis and the final disposal, from collection through to the point it is admitted in court. Its job is to prove the item is the same one collected and was never altered or tampered with, and every transfer is entered with a signature, the date and the time.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", Definition/Introduction; and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Specimen handling · CCMA 3D k121 (chain of custody)

preguntas.pregunta: What do effective teams frame every offer and request for assistance around?
opciones: Patient safety, which is the context for asking and offering
The staffing plan, which sets who may take on extra work
The chain of command, which settles who asks whom for help
The workload the team leader balanced at the start of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Task assistance builds a trusting team, and effective teams place all offers and requests for help in the context of patient safety. Members are expected to protect each other from overload and to make asking for help normal; resilience is strengthened by something as simple as offering ten free minutes to a colleague.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Task Assistance
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21

preguntas.pregunta: A woman of 32 who eats no meat asks how to get her iron. What is the best guidance?
opciones: Pair plant iron with vitamin C foods, since nonheme iron absorbs poorly
Pair plant iron with calcium-rich foods, since calcium carries iron in
Plant iron absorbs the same as meat iron, so no pairing is needed
Take a vitamin C supplement daily, which is what corrects hemochromatosis
preguntas.explicacion: Food iron comes as heme iron, in meat, seafood and poultry, and nonheme iron, in plant foods and fortified products. The body takes up nonheme iron less readily, so vegetarians need close to twice the listed amount, which for women 19 to 50 is 18 mg a day. Vitamin C foods eaten alongside improve that absorption.
preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Iron — Consumer
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(d) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(d) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a

preguntas.pregunta: The solution seen in the window of an epinephrine autoinjector looks cloudy. What does that mean?
opciones: The medication has probably met extreme temperatures and is not usable
The medication has settled and becomes clear again once the device is shaken
The medication is concentrated, so a smaller part of the dose is enough
The medication is fine as long as the printed expiration date has not passed
preguntas.explicacion: The viewing window on the side of the device lets the medication be seen. If the solution looks opaque or murky, it has probably been exposed to extreme temperatures and is no longer viable, and another autoinjector has to be found. The expiration date is printed on the side too, and an expired device will not save the patient, so both checks are made before the device is relied on.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Safe and Effective Administration of Vaccines and Epinephrine Autoinjection", Anaphylaxis and Epinephrine Autoinjector
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.e

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on peritoneal dialysis with an icodextrin solution has a fingerstick glucose done on the clinic's meter. What interference should the tester be aware of?
opciones: Some meter systems read falsely high glucose in patients exposed to icodextrin, maltose, galactose or xylose
Some meter systems read falsely low glucose in dialysis patients because the dialysate dilutes the capillary blood
There is no interference, because glucose meters measure glucose specifically and ignore all other sugars
The interference affects only urine glucose strips, so the blood meter result can be reported as usual
preguntas.explicacion: Reading the manufacturer's instructions or package insert matters because certain substances interfere with a device: some point-of-care glucose systems report erroneously elevated glucose in patients treated with maltose, icodextrin, galactose or xylose. Hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can also produce inaccurate or incalculable results, and patients with poor peripheral circulation may give inadequate capillary samples.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Sugar interference on meters · PBT IV.A.4 / IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 k111 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii

preguntas.pregunta: A biological indicator from the same lot is left unexposed and then incubated alongside the tested one. What is that for?
opciones: To verify that the spores were alive to begin with and that the incubation itself was proper
To give a second reading of the load, so a single doubtful result never stands on its own
To measure how long the spores survive at room temperature before the next lot is opened
To compare two manufacturers, which is how a product defect in the lot is normally found
preguntas.explicacion: The unexposed control is what proves the test was valid: it confirms the spores were viable before sterilization and that the incubator ran correctly. Using a control with every run is the most conservative practice, though weekly may be enough. Pairing indicators from different manufacturers is a separate move, used when a product defect is suspected.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic proposes storing vaccine in a dormitory-style combined refrigerator and freezer. What is the problem?
opciones: These units risk freezing the vaccine, even when the storage is temporary
These units cannot be fitted with a probe, so the temperature is unrecorded
These units run warm, so refrigerated vaccine drifts above 8 degrees Celsius
These units are allowed only if the door is opened fewer than five times a day
preguntas.explicacion: A dormitory-style or bar-style combined unit must never hold vaccine of any kind. These units usually have a single exterior door and an evaporator plate or cooling coil sitting in the icemaker or freezer compartment, and that arrangement carries a significant risk of freezing the vaccine. The prohibition holds even for temporary storage, and no monitoring arrangement makes such a unit acceptable.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 5: Vaccine Storage Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k74 · CMA I.D.3.a(5)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses the portal at midnight to book a visit for chest pain that started an hour earlier. What is wrong with that use of the portal?
opciones: Portal self-scheduling is offered for non-urgent appointments, which this is not
Portal self-scheduling is offered only to patients seen within the past year
Portal self-scheduling is offered only during the hours the office is open
Portal self-scheduling is offered only for visits with her own primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: A portal gives secure access at any hour from any internet connection, and beyond viewing her record some portals let a patient message the clinician securely, request refills, schedule non-urgent appointments, check benefits and coverage, update her contact details, make payments and download forms. The non-urgent limit is part of the scheduling feature itself.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-scheduling limits · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Why might a tracing be ordered for a patient who already has a pacemaker?
opciones: To check the device is working and pacing as programmed
To decide whether the device should be switched off first
To measure the battery charge left inside the device
To confirm the device is safe before an MRI is done
preguntas.explicacion: One of the listed indications is detecting malfunction of a pacemaker or defibrillator, evaluating how the device is programmed and functioning, checking its reading of arrhythmias and confirming that the pacing is being delivered as it should.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is sent to draw blood from a patient on Contact Precautions for a multidrug-resistant organism. Which PPE does the CDC call for?
opciones: A gown and gloves, put on when entering the room and discarded before leaving
A surgical mask put on at the door, with gloves only for the venipuncture itself
A fit-tested N95 respirator, with gown and gloves added only if the patient has a draining wound
Gloves alone, since Standard Precautions already cover blood contact during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: For Contact Precautions the CDC recommends a gown and gloves for every interaction that may involve the patient or the patient's environment, donned on room entry and discarded before exit to contain the pathogen. A mask on entry is the Droplet Precautions rule, and the fit-tested N95 belongs to Airborne Precautions. Standard Precautions still apply underneath, so the gloves the phlebotomist would wear anyway are not enough by themselves; the gown is added because the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient and surroundings.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Contact Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Contact Precautions PPE · CPT D1 1I k34 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: How many tastes are recognized within the sense of gustation, and where do the receptors for smell sit?
opciones: Five tastes, and the smell receptors sit high in the nasal cavity
Four tastes, and the smell receptors sit high in the nasal cavity
Five tastes, and the smell receptors sit on the surface of the tongue
Four tastes, and the smell receptors sit within the pharynx and larynx
preguntas.explicacion: Taste long counted four submodalities, sweet, salty, sour and bitter, and umami was recognized as the fifth in the mid-1980s. Smell works on chemicals too, but its receptor neurons live in a small patch of olfactory epithelium high in the nasal cavity, where inhaled molecules dissolve in the mucus and reach the dendrites.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Gustation and Olfaction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: How far from another hospital must a critical access hospital normally be located?
opciones: More than a 35-mile drive on primary roads, or 15 miles in mountainous terrain
More than a 15-mile drive on primary roads, or 35 miles in mountainous terrain
More than a 25-mile drive on primary roads, with no exception for the terrain
More than a 50-mile drive on primary roads, or 25 miles where roads are secondary
preguntas.explicacion: The condition of participation places the hospital more than a 35-mile drive on primary roads from another hospital or critical access hospital. Where terrain is mountainous or only secondary roads exist, the distance drops to a 15-mile drive. A primary road means a numbered federal or state highway with two or more lanes each way. States could also certify a necessary provider before 2006.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 485.610(c); and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006400 Information for Critical Access Hospitals
preguntas.subtema: Critical access hospital location · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: A physician phones the laboratory to order a test and says the written order will follow. Under CLIA, how long does the laboratory have to obtain the written or electronic authorization?
opciones: 30 days from the oral request
7 days from the oral request
24 hours from the oral request
90 days from the oral request
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(b) lets a laboratory accept an oral test request as long as it asks for a written or electronic authorization within 30 days and keeps either the authorization or proof of its attempts to get it. The requirement is a written or electronic request from an authorized person in the first place; the oral route is the exception, and 30 days is its limit, not one day, one week or three months.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(b), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D k112 · NCMA 2C.1 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has to give discharge steps to a patient with impaired hearing. Where should the assistant stand?
opciones: Two to three feet away, facing them in good light
Ten to twelve feet away, so the whole face is in view
Just behind the patient's better ear while speaking
At the doorway, with the voice raised to carry over
preguntas.explicacion: Get the patient's attention first, cut the background noise, and position yourself two to three feet away. Facing them directly in a well-lit room is what makes lip reading possible; turning away mid sentence undoes it. Gestures help, shouting does not, and the preferred method of communication goes in the record.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Strategies for Communicating with Patients with Impaired Hearing and Vision
preguntas.subtema: Hearing impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: Tort cases are decided by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, or greater than 50 percent; the criminal standard of beyond a reasonable doubt does not apply, and depending on the state a verdict against a tortfeasor may not require the whole jury to agree. One is liable for a tort, not guilty of it. Damages themselves must be proved to a certainty rather than estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that requirement concerns the amount awarded, not the burden for establishing liability.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance and Issues of Concern (damages)
preguntas.subtema: Burden of proof · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31

preguntas.pregunta: After the stinger is out of an insect sting, how is the site treated?
opciones: Washed with soap and water, then ice wrapped in cloth, 10 minutes on and off
Washed with soap and water, then ice put straight onto the skin for an hour
Left dry and covered, with a warm compress applied every 10 minutes
Rubbed with alcohol and left open, with the area kept above heart level
preguntas.explicacion: The stinger is scraped off with a straight edge such as a credit card, never squeezed with tweezers, and the site is washed thoroughly with soap and water. Ice wrapped in a washcloth goes on for 10 minutes and off for 10 minutes, repeated. An antihistamine or an anti-itch cream may be used, and the site is watched for days for signs of infection.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Insect bites and stings", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.r · 2027 I.B.8.r · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: How far into a fast are the liver's glycogen stores described as running out?
opciones: After about 24 hours
After about 8 hours
After about 12 hours
After about 72 hours
preguntas.explicacion: During a fast, blood glucose is first held up by glycogen in the liver and skeletal muscle, and the liver carries the greatest part of that work through the first 24 hours. After roughly 24 hours the stores are depleted and the body turns to fat and protein. Eight and twelve hours are fasting windows asked of patients, not the glycogen limit.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fasting", section Cellular Level
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: An imaging report describes hepatomegaly. Which ending carries the meaning of enlargement?
opciones: -megaly, which is added to the root for the organ
-sclerosis, which is added to the root for the organ
-ectasis, which is added to the root for the organ
-trophy, which is added to the root for the organ
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -megaly means enlargement, and hepat- names the liver, so hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver. The near neighbors mean other things: -sclerosis is a hardening, -ectasis an expansion or dilation of a hollow structure, and -trophy is growth in the sense of nourishment, as in atrophy and hypertrophy.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A molecular laboratory sees sporadic false-positive results in negative specimens. Which workflow controls does the review recommend against sample and amplicon contamination?
opciones: Separate pre- and post-amplification areas with one-way workflow, frequent glove changes and aerosol-barrier pipette tips
A single shared bench for extraction and amplification, so that every step is handled by the same pair of gloves
Reusing pipette tips within one patient's series of tubes, so that no foreign template can enter the reaction
Leaving opened sample tubes uncapped in the post-amplification area to let aerosols settle before analysis
preguntas.explicacion: Because amplification makes millions of copies from a few templates, a positive sample or its amplicons can contaminate a negative one at collection, processing or analysis. Guidelines therefore ask for separate pre- and post-amplification areas, ideally physically apart, a one-way workflow from pre to post, separate clean protective equipment for each area with frequent glove changes, dedicated equipment, aerosol-barrier tips and pipetting technique that limits aerosols, plus routine cleaning with 10 to 15 % bleach and wipe-tests of the environment.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.4 Specimen contamination
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has just explained how to use a new inhaler. How does a teach-back confirm the patient understood?
opciones: The patient explains the information in their own words
The patient signs the instruction sheet before leaving
The patient answers yes when asked whether it was clear
The staff member repeats the instruction a second time
preguntas.explicacion: In a teach-back the sender asks the patient or family member to say back, in their own words, the information they need to know or the actions they need to take. It checks that the sender explained clearly, which a yes-or-no question and a signature on a sheet of paper cannot do.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Teach-Back
preguntas.subtema: Patient education · CCMA 4F k160 · CMAA 2G

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her copayment for one drug is higher than for another in the same plan.
opciones: The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers cost more
The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers are generic
The plan charges more for drugs bought before the deductible has been met
The plan charges more for drugs a specialist prescribed than for others
preguntas.explicacion: Plans place covered drugs in tiers, and a drug in a lower tier generally costs the patient less. In the example given, tier 1 holds most generic drugs with the lowest copayment, tier 2 preferred brand-name drugs, tier 3 non-preferred brand names, and a specialty tier the very high-cost drugs. Generics sit at the bottom, not the top, and the tier does not depend on who wrote the prescription.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare drug plans work, Tiers
preguntas.subtema: Drug formulary · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: What is a contracture?
opciones: The loss of full passive motion from a joint, muscle or soft tissue limit
The loss of muscle bulk that follows a long stretch of time spent in bed
A joint that moves further than it should because the tissues have slackened
A painful spasm that locks a muscle group for a few minutes at a time
preguntas.explicacion: A contracture is the lack of full passive range of motion caused by a limitation in the joint, the muscle or the soft tissue. It is what long-term range-of-motion programmes are meant to prevent in conditions such as spinal cord injury, stroke, neuromuscular disease and traumatic brain injury.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65

preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. The notice of privacy practices must reflect the more stringent law when it limits a use or disclosure. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Where is the HIPAA Privacy Rule Applicable; 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Stricter state law · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.a(2) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: A dose is drawn up wrong but caught before it reaches the patient. How is that event described?
opciones: A near miss: an error that could have harmed but was intercepted
A sentinel event: an error that reached the patient and caused harm
A reckless act: a deliberate choice to work outside the safe procedure
A latent condition: a flaw in the system that has yet to cause an error
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error with the potential to harm a patient that fails to do so by chance or because someone intercepted it. Near misses are investigated the same way as worse events, because they usually come from poor communication, weak teamwork, memory overload or unstandardized procedures rather than from a careless person.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 5: Safety, Near Misses
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · NCMA 4.10

preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count is ordered. Which tube is used, and what does the CBC measure?
opciones: A lavender EDTA tube; red cells, white cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and MCV
A light blue citrate tube; the seconds the sample takes to clot and the INR
A grey fluoride tube; plasma glucose and the average glucose of recent months
A gold serum separator tube; electrolytes, kidney waste products and the liver enzymes
preguntas.explicacion: Hematologic assays go in the lavender EDTA tube, and a CBC counts the blood cells: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and the mean corpuscular volume. Clotting seconds and the INR belong to the PT/INR in citrate, glucose to the grey tube, and electrolytes, BUN, creatinine and liver enzymes to the metabolic panels run on serum.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Complete Blood Count (CBC), What is a complete blood count?; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", Lavender

preguntas.pregunta: A cough preparation holds no more than 200 mg of codeine per 100 mL. Which schedule does it belong to?
opciones: Schedule V, whose preparations hold limited quantities of certain narcotics
Schedule IV, whose potential for abuse is lower than that of Schedule III
Schedule III, where a product holds up to 90 mg of codeine per dosage unit
Schedule II, which is where codeine on its own is listed as a narcotic drug
preguntas.explicacion: Schedule V carries the lowest abuse potential relative to Schedule IV and consists mainly of preparations containing limited quantities of certain narcotics; the example given is exactly a cough preparation with no more than 200 milligrams of codeine per 100 millilitres or per 100 grams. A product with up to 90 milligrams of codeine per dosage unit is Schedule III, and codeine on its own is a Schedule II narcotic.
preguntas.fuente: DEA Diversion Control Division, Definition of Controlled Substance Schedules: Schedule V

preguntas.pregunta: What do the Purkinje fibers do once the impulse reaches the apex of the heart?
opciones: They carry it to the ventricular muscle cells in about 75 ms
They carry it back to the atrial muscle cells in about 75 ms
They hold it for about 75 ms before the ventricles contract
They slow it for about 75 ms so the atria can empty first
preguntas.explicacion: These fibers conduct fast and fan out from the apex toward the base, reaching every ventricular muscle cell in roughly 75 ms. Because the stimulus starts at the apex, the squeeze also starts at the apex and travels upward, which drives blood into the aorta and the pulmonary trunk.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Purkinje Fibers
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital introduces safety-engineered needles but its needlestick rate does not fall. Which contributing factors were most often reported in a study that found this pattern?
opciones: Difficulty operating the safety mechanism and continued improper needle disposal
Reuse of needle holders and the mixing of components from different manufacturers
Prolonged tourniquet time and failure to activate the feature with one hand
Overfilled sharps containers and the absence of double gloving

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports nausea and fatigue, and the exam records a fever and a rash. Which entries are symptoms and which are signs?

Nausea and fatigue are signs; fever and rash are symptoms
All four are symptoms, since the patient came in reporting them
All four are signs, since a provider recorded them in the chart

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of findings fits a patient who is going into shock?
opciones: Rapid weak pulse, shallow breathing, pale clammy skin and confusion
Slow bounding pulse, deep slow breathing, flushed dry skin and euphoria
Rapid strong pulse, deep rapid breathing, warm dry skin and hunger
Slow weak pulse, noisy breathing, blue lips and a raised temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Shock is circulatory failure, so blood pressure falls very low and the picture is a fast but weak pulse, shallow breathing, skin that is pale, cool and clammy, low or absent urine output, and anxiety, restlessness or confusion. Bluish lips and nails may appear. One in five people who go into shock die of it, so help is called at the first signs.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with capacity refuses a treatment that the whole team believes would help him. What is the legal position?

He may refuse once a second clinician has confirmed it
He may refuse only treatments that are not life-sustaining
He may refuse only after signing a form releasing the team

Book no video visits at all until every one of them confirms the update is installed
Send the instructions only to the patients whose first video visit is still to come

preguntas.pregunta: Which situation is a recognized exception to the requirement for informed consent?
opciones: A life-threatening emergency with no time to obtain consent
A test the clinician considers clearly in the patient's interest
A patient who speaks a different language from the staff
A patient carrying a psychiatric diagnosis such as schizophrenia
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized exceptions are three: the patient is incapacitated, a life-threatening emergency leaves no time, or the patient voluntarily waives consent. preguntas.pregunta: Which type of cell division produces the eggs and sperm, and how many chromosomes does each of those cells carry?
opciones: Meiosis, and each gamete carries 23 chromosomes
Mitosis, and each gamete carries 23 chromosomes
Meiosis, and each gamete carries 46 chromosomes
Cytokinesis, and each gamete carries 46 chromosomes
preguntas.explicacion: Every body cell except the gametes reproduces by mitosis, which yields two cells identical to the parent. Eggs and sperm come from meiosis, where the chromosome number is halved to 23, so that fertilization restores the usual 46. Cytokinesis is not a kind of division but the splitting of the cytoplasm.

preguntas.pregunta: A reading of 120/80 mm Hg is written in the chart. What else belongs beside it?
opciones: The arm used and the position the patient was in during the measurement
The size of the cuff and the make of the sphygmomanometer that was used
The rate at which the cuff was deflated and the peak pressure it reached
The time since the patient last ate, since food shifts the reading upward
preguntas.explicacion: The pair of numbers alone cannot be compared with the next visit's. Both arms are measured at the first evaluation because the sides can differ, and any position other than the standard one alters the value, so the arm and the position are recorded with the reading. Later comparisons then rest on the same conditions.

preguntas.pregunta: Two patients on the same dose of the same drug show different levels. Which factors are named for that?
opciones: Ageing, pregnancy, illness and infection change how a drug is processed
The colour of the tube stopper and the order in which the tubes filled
The arm chosen for the draw and how long the tourniquet stayed on
The time of day alone, since every drug level follows a diurnal rhythm
preguntas.explicacion: As soon as a medicine is taken the body begins to process and remove it, so the level in the blood varies over time, and ageing, pregnancy, illness and infection all affect how quickly that happens. Levels also differ between individuals on the same dose because of absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion, and of diet and other drugs taken alongside.

preguntas.pregunta: A pulse is described as irregularly irregular, with no pattern at all to the spacing. Which rhythm does that describe?
opciones: Atrial fibrillation, whose beats fall without any repeating pattern
Sinus arrhythmia, whose rate changes in step with the breathing cycle
Sinus bradycardia, whose beats are widely spaced but evenly spread
Sinus tachycardia, whose beats are closely spaced but evenly spread
preguntas.explicacion: Rhythm is sorted into three descriptions: regular, regularly irregular, and irregularly irregular. The middle one covers patterns that repeat, such as the mild variation with breathing known as sinus arrhythmia. The last one, with no pattern whatever, is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation and is reported.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the birthday rule, which part of a parent's date of birth matters?
opciones: The month and the day, since the year of birth is left out of the rule
The month and the year, since the older parent's plan is treated as primary
The year alone, since the parent covered longer holds the primary plan
The day alone, since the earlier day of the month decides the order
preguntas.explicacion: The model regulation defines birthday as referring only to the month and day in a calendar year, and it expressly leaves out the year the parent was born, so the older parent has no advantage. preguntas.pregunta: A patient in an HMO calls to book with a cardiologist and has no order from her primary care doctor. What is missing?
opciones: A referral, the written order from her primary care doctor for the visit
A preauthorization, the plan's decision that the visit is medically necessary
A claim, the request for payment the office sends after the appointment
An accounting of disclosures covering the records the specialist will receive

preguntas.pregunta: Whose health does the family history section ask about?
opciones: Blood relatives such as parents, grandparents and siblings, with age and cause of death
Everyone living in the household, a spouse and any stepchildren included in the list
Only relatives who died before the age of fifty, since the early deaths carry the risk
Every relative the patient can name, so that the note holds the whole family tree
preguntas.explicacion: The point is inherited risk, so the questions follow the bloodline: parents, grandparents and siblings, their health status, their age, and the cause of death where it applies. preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes come back faulty from the same phlebotomist: one is haemolysed and one holds small clots. What separates the two errors?
opciones: Too much mixing haemolyses the sample; too little leaves small clots
Too little mixing haemolyses the sample; too much leaves small clots
Too much mixing leaves clots; a short draw is what haemolyses a sample
Both faults come from mixing too little, at different points in the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant are inverted in a figure-of-8 until the blood and additive are properly combined. Push it too far and haemolysis appears; stop too soon and small clots form. Both faults make the specimen unusable, and both are decided at the bedside, not in the laboratory.

preguntas.pregunta: The requisition says 'Robert', but the patient introduces herself as Roberta and uses she/her. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Use the name and pronouns she gives, and note them in the record for next time
Use the legal name on the requisition until the record has been formally amended
Ask the partner who accompanies her which pronouns you should use
Avoid using any name or pronoun for the rest of the visit, to be safe
preguntas.explicacion: Staff should refer to patients by their name and chosen descriptive pronouns, to follow the patient's lead and ask when in doubt, and to make a note in the record so the same pattern is followed at future visits, modifying the electronic record if needed. Identification for the specimen is a separate step that uses the identifiers on file.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates fraud from abuse in the Medicare program?
opciones: Fraud involves knowing deception; abuse causes needless program cost without it
Fraud is committed by providers only; abuse is committed by patients and staff
Fraud is billed to a federal program; abuse is billed to a commercial insurer
Fraud is punished by the payer; abuse is punished only by the state licensing board
preguntas.explicacion: Fraud typically means knowingly submitting false claims, misrepresenting facts, or paying or taking remuneration for referrals. preguntas.pregunta: A smear shows platelets sticking to the white cells rather than to each other. What is that finding called?

Platelet clumping
Rouleaux formation
Pseudo-polycythaemia

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a valid HIPAA authorization contain?
opciones: An expiration date or event, plus the individual's signature and date
A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements in 164.508(c)(1) are a specific description of the information, the person or class authorized to disclose it, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date, with the authority of any personal representative described. The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. It must be in plain language and the individual receives a copy. Notarization is not required, and a no-revocation clause would contradict the rule.

Loops in them can shorten the life of the patient cable
Loops in them can slow the paper as it feeds through
Loops in them can reverse the polarity of that lead

opciones: Focused on the cough, with the immunosuppression from the chemotherapy kept in mind
Comprehensive, starting again from childhood illnesses and every past operation
Focused on the cancer treatment plan, which outranks the reason for today's visit
Deferred until the oncology notes from the previous visits have all been reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: A problem-focused visit calls for a focused history: the presenting complaint, plus what has changed since the last encounter, such as hospitalizations, emergency visits or medication adjustments. Radio waves and magnets, which show the heart in detail
X-rays with a contrast dye, which outline the vessels
A radioactive tracer, which shows where the blood flows

Every three years, the period for which training records are kept
Once at installation, and again only after a spill occurs inside it
Every six months, and after each change of the exhaust air filter

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the male reproductive system?
opciones: Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, prostate and penis
Testes, epididymis, ureters, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, bladder and penis
Testes, Fallopian tubes, vas deferens, accessory glands, prostate, urethra and penis
Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, adrenal glands, seminal vesicles, kidney and penis
preguntas.explicacion: The male system is a pair of testes plus a network of excretory ducts, namely the epididymis, the ductus or vas deferens and the ejaculatory ducts, together with the seminal vesicles, the prostate, the bulbourethral glands and the penis. preguntas.pregunta: A single-dose vial of lidocaine contains far more than one patient needs. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Do not keep the remainder for later or another patient; buy the smallest vial that meets the need
Label it with the date and use it for up to 28 days, as with a multi-dose vial
Pool the leftover contents with other single-dose vials in a clean preparation area
Save the remainder for the same patient's next visit, since it is dedicated to one person
preguntas.explicacion: A single-dose vial is approved for one patient for one case, procedure or injection, typically lacks a preservative, and must never be used for more than one patient. If it holds more than needed, the remainder is not retained for future use even on the same patient, leftover contents are not pooled or stored, and the practical advice is to purchase the smallest vial necessary. preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fasted asks when she can eat again. What is the answer?
opciones: As soon as the test is over; bringing a snack helps, since light-headedness is common
One hour after the draw, once the laboratory has confirmed the sample is usable
Only after the provider has reviewed the results and cleared her to eat
After a second sample is collected two hours later, as in a tolerance test

preguntas.pregunta: Under CMS rules, are operators of waived tests subject to the CLIA competency assessment requirement?
opciones: No; waived tests are excluded, although state law or an accrediting body may still require assessment
Yes; every operator must complete the six-element assessment before running any waived test
Yes, but only for waived tests whose results adjust medication doses, such as PT/INR and glucose
No; competency applies only to high complexity personnel, never to moderate or waived testing
preguntas.explicacion: Most point-of-care tests are waived, and waived tests are excluded from the competency assessment requirement under CMS; nonwaived tests, including the moderately complex ones, are subject to proficiency testing, quality control and personnel standards. 20 to 30 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
8 to 12 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
30 to 60 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern

Four regions and nine quadrants
Six regions and three quadrants
Twelve regions and six quadrants

Hydrogen, in several venipuncture samples before and after a lactose drink
Lactose, in a single venipuncture sample two hours after a lactose drink

preguntas.pregunta: Which two conditions must a patient meet at the same time for Medicare to cover home health services?
opciones: Needing part-time or intermittent skilled services, and being homebound
Needing daily skilled services, and a prior inpatient stay of three days
Being homebound, and having a prognosis certified as 6 months or shorter
Needing custodial help with daily living, and a doctor's order for an aide
preguntas.explicacion: Home health coverage rests on two conditions at once. The patient must need skilled services on a part-time or intermittent basis, and must be homebound, which means leaving home is not recommended or takes considerable effort and help. Someone who needs more than part-time or intermittent skilled care does not qualify for the benefit.

preguntas.pregunta: A 52-year-old patient with obesity and no symptoms asks whether he should be tested for diabetes. What applies?
opciones: Yes; screening covers adults 35 to 70 who have overweight or obesity
Yes; screening covers every adult 35 to 70 regardless of body weight
No; screening starts at 45 for adults who have overweight or obesity
No; screening applies only once symptoms of high blood glucose appear
preguntas.explicacion: Screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes is recommended in asymptomatic adults aged 35 to 70 who have overweight or obesity, and it carries a B grade. The point of screening is to find the condition before symptoms, and patients found to have prediabetes are offered or referred to preventive interventions.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a routine venipuncture, what does the WHO's Step 4 require for hand hygiene and gloves?
opciones: Soap and water, or 3 ml of alcohol rub if hands are not visibly soiled, then well-fitting non-sterile gloves
Use 3 ml of alcohol rub in every case, even on visibly soiled hands, then put on sterile gloves
Wash with soap and water, dry with a reusable towel, then put on sterile gloves for every patient
Put on well-fitting non-sterile gloves first, then clean the gloved hands with alcohol rub
preguntas.explicacion: Step 4 gives two options: wash the hands with soap and water and dry them with single-use towels, or, if they are not visibly contaminated, rub 3 ml of alcohol rub over palms, fingertips and backs of the hands until dry; only then are well-fitting non-sterile gloves put on. Sterile gloves are reserved for blood cultures. Gloves are never a substitute for hand hygiene.

preguntas.pregunta: What are the federal limits on refilling a prescription for a Schedule III or IV controlled substance?
opciones: No more than five refills, and none more than six months after the date of issue
No more than three refills, and none more than one year after the date of issue
No more than five refills, and none more than twelve months after the issue date
No more than six refills, and none more than five months after the date of issue
preguntas.explicacion: A prescription for a Schedule III or IV substance may not be filled or refilled more than six months after the date it was issued, and one that authorizes refills may not be refilled more than five times. Each refill is entered on the back of the prescription or in another record that is uniformly kept and readily retrievable, whether the record is on paper or part of the electronic prescription file.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with polycythemia has a hematocrit of 60%. What should be considered when collecting a citrate specimen from this patient?
opciones: The high hematocrit raises the citrate effect, so the anticoagulant volume may need adjusting
The high hematocrit lowers the citrate effect, so the tube should be filled only halfway
The tube is collected as usual, since hematocrit affects the EDTA tube and not the citrate tube
A larger 16 to 18 G needle is used so the viscous blood reaches the 9:1 ratio faster
preguntas.explicacion: Inadequate filling or a hematocrit above 55% increases the citrate level in the sample and interferes with the recalcification performed during analysis, and with a high hematocrit the anticoagulant volume may need to be adjusted. Half filling would make the citrate excess worse. The 16 to 18 gauge belongs to blood donation in the WHO needle table, not to coagulation draws, for which 19 to 22 G is suggested.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling

preguntas.pregunta: Which order of steps does the guideline require before an instrument can be high-level disinfected or sterilized?
opciones: Clean it thoroughly first, because leftover organic and inorganic matter blocks the process
Soak it in the germicide first, so the softened soil rinses off with less friction afterward
Disinfect at a low level first, so the item is safe for the person who will scrub it later
Rinse it in sterile water first, so tap-water organisms cannot dry onto the working surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Cleaning always comes first. Material left on the surface interferes with the process in two ways: it reacts chemically with the germicide, using it up, and it shields microbes as a physical barrier. Meticulous cleaning also lowers the bioburden, which shortens the exposure needed. Sterile-water rinsing is what follows high-level disinfection, not what precedes it.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning

preguntas.pregunta: Which framework does the CDC recommend for taking a sexual history?
opciones: The 5 Ps: partners, practices, protection, previous infections and prevention of pregnancy
The PQRSTU mnemonic, applied to the symptoms of any sexually transmitted infection reported
OLDCARTS, which sets out the onset, location and duration of each reported exposure
Gordon's functional health patterns, whose sexuality category covers the same ground
preguntas.explicacion: The five headings are partners, practices, protection from sexually transmitted infections, previous history of such infections, and prevention of pregnancy. The framework matters because sexual histories are often left incomplete in routine practice, and a complete one makes appropriate education, counseling and testing far more likely.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Social History

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample looks pink after centrifugation. Which result on the chemistry panel should the processor expect the laboratory to question first?
opciones: Potassium
Magnesium
Chloride
Glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Among frequent chemistry tests, the analytes most sensitive to hemolysis are lactate dehydrogenase, creatine kinase and its MB isoenzyme, potassium, conjugated bilirubin, ALT, AST and iron; potassium is the one whose distortion most often changes patient management, which is why one hospital measures the hemolysis index on every potassium sample. Albumin, glucose and other analytes showed biases that stayed within CLIA limits in the study on graded hemolysis, as did magnesium and chloride.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must a bloodborne pathogens training record include?
opciones: Dates, a summary of the content, the trainer's name and qualifications, and attendees' names and titles
Dates, the trainer's name, and each attendee's hepatitis B vaccination status and serology
Dates, the content, and the type and brand of any device that caused an injury during the year
Dates, the attendees' names, and a copy of each attendee's signed declination or consent
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(i) lists four items for the training record: the dates of the sessions, the contents or a summary, the names and qualifications of whoever conducted the training, and the names and job titles of everyone who attended. Vaccination status and serology belong to the confidential medical record of (h)(1); the type and brand of a device belong to the sharps injury log of (h)(5); and the signed declination of Appendix A is a separate document required by (f)(2)(iv).

preguntas.pregunta: Which entity collects, manages and reports the other insurance coverage a Medicare patient holds?
opciones: The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, working for the secondary payer program
The Medicare Administrative Contractor, working for the secondary payer program
The Commercial Repayment Center, working for the secondary payer program
The clearinghouse, working for the providers that route their claims through it
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare Secondary Payer program keeps Medicare from paying first where it should not, and coordination of benefits rules settle which payer goes first. Gathering, managing and reporting other insurance coverage for beneficiaries is the job of the Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center. The Commercial Repayment Center does something else entirely: it pursues recovery when a group health plan should have paid first.

preguntas.pregunta: Which element has to appear on a medication order before the order is carried out?
opciones: The date and the time of the order, with the name and signature of the prescriber
The insurance plan of the patient and the identifier that the payer has assigned
The name of the pharmacy that is going to dispense the medication being ordered
The diagnosis code that justifies the medication for the condition being treated
preguntas.explicacion: An order for a drug has to carry the patient's name, the age or date of birth, the date and time of the order, the drug name, the dose, frequency and route, and the prescriber's name and signature, plus the weight when the dose depends on it and the strength, quantity or specific instructions where they apply. When something is missing, the prescriber is contacted for clarification before anything is administered.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is booked for one-step gestational testing. What should she be told to expect?
opciones: An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 100 g drink, and about 3 hours in the office
No fast at all, a 50 g drink, and about 1 hour in the office
A 3-day carbohydrate diet, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
preguntas.explicacion: One-step testing means nothing to eat or drink except sips of water for 8 to 14 hours, a liquid holding 75 g of glucose, and draws before the drink and every 60 minutes for two hours, so at least two hours should be allowed. The 100 g / 3-hour version is the second step of the other pathway, and the 50 g nonfasting drink is its first step. Nothing may be eaten during the test.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the FDA's design recommendations for sharps injury prevention features, what must be true once the feature has been activated?
opciones: It cannot be deactivated and stays protective through disposal
It can be reset once so the device can be used on the same patient
It stays protective until the device reaches the sharps container
It may be released by a second single-handed action if needed
preguntas.explicacion: Table 1 of the FDA guidance lists, for all feature types, that the user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be deactivated and should remain protective through disposal. Resetting or releasing the feature is the opposite of that recommendation, and protection that ended at the container would not cover the disposal step.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is torn between staying in her current post and going back for a degree. Which type of conflict is that?
opciones: Intrapersonal conflict
Interpersonal conflict
Inter-sender conflict
Intragroup conflict
preguntas.explicacion: Intrapersonal conflict is the internal struggle among competing values, goals or role demands, and weighing bedside work against further study is the example given. Interpersonal conflict is between two people, inter-sender conflict comes from incompatible instructions from two legitimate authorities, and intragroup conflict is tension inside one team.

preguntas.pregunta: Joint fluid has been aspirated from a swollen knee. What does the laboratory look for that is specific to this fluid?
opciones: Crystals, which point to gout, along with cell counts and a culture
Casts, which point to renal disease, along with cell counts and a culture
Ova and parasites, which point to infestation, along with a cell count
Acid-fast bacilli only, since joint fluid is cultured for no other organism
preguntas.explicacion: Synovial fluid is normally a thick, straw-colored liquid present in small amounts. After the skin is cleaned, a sterile needle enters the joint space and fluid is drawn into a sterile syringe. The laboratory notes color and clarity, counts red and white cells, looks under the microscope for crystals as in gout or for bacteria, measures glucose, protein, uric acid and LDH, and cultures the fluid.

preguntas.pregunta: A man scheduled for a semen analysis asks how long he should abstain from ejaculation beforehand. What is the usual instruction?
opciones: From 2 to 3 days, and in no case longer than 5 days before the test
From 2 to 3 hours, and in no case longer than 5 hours before the test
At least 7 days, and preferably 10 days or more before the test
No abstinence at all, since recent activity does not change the count
preguntas.explicacion: To get an adequate sperm count the patient avoids any sexual activity that ends in ejaculation for 2 to 3 days, and the interval should not stretch past 5 days because quality falls off after that. The StatPearls account of the same test sets the window differently, at a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 7 days, so the figure a candidate quotes depends on which reference the laboratory follows.

preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, may a facility apply Standard Precautions instead of Universal Precautions?
opciones: Yes, as an alternative, if the facility follows all other provisions of the standard
No; Universal Precautions is the only approach the standard's definitions recognize
Yes, but only in hospitals accredited by a CMS-approved accreditation organization
Yes, and doing so exempts the facility from the exposure determination requirement
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool explains that Body Substance Isolation and Standard Precautions define all body fluids and substances as infectious, and that OSHA permits them as alternatives to Universal Precautions provided the facility adheres to every other provision of the bloodborne pathogens standard. OSHA's hazard page dates Standard Precautions to 1996 and describes them as expanding on Universal Precautions with added infection prevention elements. The exposure determination of (c)(2) is still required, and accreditation is a CLIA matter, not a condition here.

preguntas.pregunta: Instruments are being loaded into a washer-disinfector. Which loading practice does the guideline call for?
opciones: Open hinged instruments fully, take apart what comes apart, and do not stack the pieces
Close hinged instruments fully, keep assemblies together, and stack them to fit one load
Open hinged instruments fully, keep assemblies together, and stack the heavier ones on top
Close hinged instruments fully, take apart what comes apart, and lay them flat in one layer
preguntas.explicacion: The detergent solution has to reach every surface, so hinged instruments are opened all the way, items are disassembled as far as they will go, and stacking is avoided because one piece shields another. The same logic governs the sterilizer later: only surfaces the agent actually reaches get processed.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three levels of nurse does a state's Nurse Practice Act define?
opciones: Licensed practical or vocational nurse, registered nurse, advanced practice nurse
Nursing assistant, licensed practical nurse and registered nurse, in that order
Registered nurse, clinical nurse specialist and nurse anesthetist, in that order
Patient care technician, registered nurse and nurse practitioner, in that order
preguntas.explicacion: Each state's Nurse Practice Act defines three levels of nurse: the licensed practical or vocational nurse, the registered nurse, and the advanced practice registered nurse. Nursing assistants and patient care technicians are unlicensed assistive personnel who take on tasks a nurse delegates. Clinical nurse specialists and nurse anesthetists are two of the four advanced practice categories.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient turning 65 next month asks how long the first chance to sign up for Medicare lasts.
opciones: Seven months: the three before the birthday month, that month, and the three after
Seven months: the six before the birthday month and the birthday month itself
Three months: the month of the birthday and the two months that follow it
Twelve months: the whole calendar year in which the person turns 65 years old
preguntas.explicacion: The Initial Enrollment Period runs 7 months, starting 3 months before the month of the 65th birthday and ending 3 months after it, so it is centered on that month rather than placed before or after it. preguntas.pregunta: A small rural hospital wants to be certified as a critical access hospital. What is the limit on its inpatient capacity?
opciones: No more than 25 beds used for inpatient or swing bed services at any one time
No more than 10 beds, the same cap that applies to a distinct part psychiatric unit
No more than 50 beds, half of which must be set aside for swing bed services
No more than 100 beds, above which the hospital is paid as an acute care hospital
preguntas.explicacion: A certified critical access hospital may not exceed 25 inpatient beds for inpatient or swing bed care. It may also run a distinct part rehabilitation unit and a distinct part psychiatric unit, each with up to 10 beds, and those beds sit outside the 25. Beds dedicated to hospice care do count toward the maximum of 25.

preguntas.pregunta: What sets a rural health clinic apart from other Medicare outpatient clinics?
opciones: It sits in a non-urbanized area designated a shortage area and gives primary care
It runs only for surgery on patients who do not need to be kept in a hospital bed
It gives 24-hour emergency services with on-site or on-call staff every day of the week
It provides an intensive rehabilitation program with continued medical supervision
preguntas.explicacion: Rural health clinics sit in non-urbanized areas and give outpatient primary care and preventive services in rural shortage or underserved areas. preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to drop a patient he finds difficult and demanding. What do the ethical guidelines say?
opciones: Being a challenging patient is not on its own a ground for ending the relationship
Any patient may be dismissed at will, since the relationship rests on mutual consent
Dismissal is allowed once the patient has been rude to a member of the office staff
Only the health plan may end the relationship, by removing the patient from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The clinician-patient relationship usually begins by mutual consent and is governed by State law. Ethical guidance holds that a clinician may not terminate it merely because someone is a challenging patient, and that irresponsible health behaviors do not release the professional from the duties of the relationship. The expected route is to try to resolve the conflict and, failing that, seek help from a consultant.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice manager asks who in the office needs health literacy training. What does the toolkit call for?
opciones: Everyone, from front office staff through the medical director
Only the clinicians, since they are the ones who explain diagnoses
Only the medical assistants, who do most of the patient teaching
Only staff assigned to patients flagged as having low literacy
preguntas.explicacion: Putting universal precautions in place asks every staff member, from the front desk to the medical director, to know what health literacy is and to work at making care clearer.
