preguntas.pregunta: What is the correct way to take off a gown after caring for a patient?
opciones: Release the ties, touch only the inside, and turn it inside out
Release the ties, roll it from the sleeves toward the neckline
Pull it over the head without untying, keeping the front outward
Fold it front to front and hang it for the rest of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: The gown is third in the doffing sequence. Its ties or straps are released, and it is removed touching only the inside, pulled away from the neck and shoulders, turned inside out so the contaminated face ends up enclosed, and placed in the proper container. The bloodborne pathogens standard adds the companion rule: a garment penetrated by blood comes off immediately, in a way that avoids contact with its outer surface, and a gown is never hung up for reuse.

preguntas.pregunta: A deep burn appears white and the area is oddly not very painful. Why is the lack of pain a bad sign?
opciones: The burn has destroyed the nerve endings along with the dermis
The burn has cooled the nerve endings without harming the dermis
The burn has flooded the nerve endings with the fluid lost from cells
The burn has stretched the nerve endings across the swollen dermis
preguntas.explicacion: A third-degree burn goes through epidermis and dermis, destroying tissue and taking the nerve endings and sensory function with it, and a fourth-degree burn reaches muscle and bone. That is why the deepest burns hurt less than the shallow ones. They also cannot heal on their own and need debridement and grafting.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.4 Diseases, Disorders and Injuries of the Integumentary System, Burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(1) (2027 I.C.6.g(1)) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A work surface in the draw room is splashed with blood during a procedure. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Decontaminate it with an appropriate disinfectant immediately or as soon as feasible
Decontaminate it at the end of the work shift, the time the standard sets for possibly contaminated surfaces
Remove and replace the protective covering at the end of the shift, as with plastic wrap over equipment
Flush it with water immediately, as the standard requires for skin and mucous membranes
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(A) names three moments for decontaminating a work surface with a suitable disinfectant: when a procedure is finished; right away, or as soon as feasible, when the surface is visibly contaminated or blood or OPIM has been spilled on it; and at the end of the shift if it may have been contaminated since the last cleaning. A visible spill falls under the second case and does not wait for the shift to end. Protective coverings, in (d)(4)(ii)(B), are likewise replaced as soon as feasible once overtly contaminated. Flushing with water is the rule for eyes and mucous membranes in (d)(2)(vi), not for surfaces.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(A), Housekeeping
preguntas.subtema: Decontamination of surfaces and spills · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C k97 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b I.B.6.b · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic wants to check each new hire's antibody level first and offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to those who are not immune. What does the standard say?
opciones: Screening may not be made a condition of receiving the vaccine that is offered
Screening is required before the first dose, and has to be repeated a year later
Screening replaces the vaccine when the employee signs the declination form
Screening is allowed only within ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Two sentences have to be read together. Paragraph (f)(2)(i) says the vaccine is offered after training and within ten working days of initial assignment, unless the employee already completed the series, antibody testing has shown immunity, or the vaccine is medically contraindicated. Paragraph (f)(2)(ii) then forbids making participation in a prescreening program a prerequisite for receiving it. So a result that already exists can spare the offer, but no employee can be told to be screened in order to qualify.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports repeated haemolysis from one phlebotomist. Which needle choices raise that risk?
opciones: A gauge of twenty-three or finer, or one too wide for the vessel
A gauge of twenty-one or finer, or one too short for the forearm
A gauge of sixteen or wider, or one too long for the antecubital
A gauge of twenty-three or finer, or one too short for the vessel
preguntas.explicacion: Both extremes of gauge appear on the list of factors that raise haemolysis: a needle of twenty-three gauge or under, and a needle too large for the vessel it is being put into. The wider figures, sixteen to eighteen, belong to blood donation rather than to routine sampling.

preguntas.pregunta: A contaminated wound with no major tissue loss is irrigated, debrided and watched for several days before it is closed. Which type of healing is that?
opciones: Tertiary intention, also called delayed primary closure
Secondary intention, in which granulation fills the defect
Primary intention, in which the edges are approximated at once
Maturation, the last of the four phases that every wound goes through
preguntas.explicacion: Tertiary intention, or delayed primary closure, is the route for a grossly contaminated wound that has not lost much tissue: it is explored, irrigated, debrided and observed for roughly three to seven days before it is closed or grafted. Primary intention is closure at once with sutures, staples or glue; secondary intention leaves the wound open to granulate and contract.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has fainted in the chair and been eased to the floor. How high should the feet be raised?
opciones: About 12 inches (30 cm) above the level of the heart
About 4 inches (10 cm) above the level of the heart
About 3 feet (90 cm), by resting the legs on the chair seat
Level with the heart, with the head turned to the side
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps after a faint are: check airway and breathing, loosen tight clothing around the neck, raise the feet above heart level by about 12 inches or 30 centimeters, turn the person on the side if they have vomited, and keep them lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes. The side position is for vomiting; it does not replace elevating the legs.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient recovers from a faint during a draw. Which finding afterwards is a red flag pointing away from a simple vasovagal episode?

Pallor and sweating during the event itself
A slow pulse and low blood pressure during the event
Generalized weakness for a few minutes after waking

preguntas.pregunta: How is a side effect related to an adverse drug reaction?
opciones: It is one category of adverse reaction, predictable and often dose related
It is the opposite of an adverse reaction, since a side effect is never harmful
It is unrelated: side effects come from the disease and not from the medication
It is any reaction the pharmacological properties of the drug fail to predict
preguntas.explicacion: A side effect is a predictable or dose-dependent effect of a drug other than the principal one it was given for, and it may be desirable, adverse or of no consequence. Side effects are one of the categories inside Type A adverse reactions, along with overdose and drug interactions. Gastritis after an NSAID and diarrhea after an antibiotic are the kind of example given. What pharmacology fails to predict is a Type B reaction.

One appointment, with two tubes drawn back to back
Three appointments, spread across the same morning
One appointment, followed by a 24-hour urine jar

Samples are usually taken twice: once in the morning, when levels are normally at their highest, and again around 4 p.m., when they are normally much lower. preguntas.pregunta: Roughly what share of a person's daily calories do the Dietary Guidelines say is needed just to meet food group recommendations in nutrient-dense forms?
opciones: About 85 percent, leaving about 15 percent for other uses
About 50 percent, leaving about 50 percent for other uses
About 70 percent, leaving about 30 percent for other uses
About 95 percent, leaving about 5 percent for other uses
preguntas.explicacion: Meeting the food group amounts in nutrient-dense forms takes about 85 percent of the day's calories. The remaining 15 percent, roughly 250 to 350 calories in the patterns most people use, is what is left for extra added sugars, extra saturated fat, larger servings of a food group, or alcohol. A few easy steps toward a health goal, written by the clinician alone
The full treatment plan for a chronic condition, signed by the patient
A schedule of the follow-up appointments the practice has booked
preguntas.explicacion: An action plan lays out one or more easy steps toward a health goal, such as losing weight or managing a chronic condition better, and patient and health professional create it together. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep her worklist on a personal flash drive and check it over the clinic's open wireless network. What is the guidance?

Store it on the drive but keep the drive locked in the staff room
Use the open network, since the worklist holds no test results
Store it on the drive after deleting the names, keeping the numbers
preguntas.explicacion: Portable media are a documented source of breaches: laptops and flash drives get stolen, so workers are told not to keep patient data on them, and to encrypt it if it must be kept, or better, to view the data without storing it. Where several computers reach records over a wireless network, the network's encryption has to be switched on, and staff must stop using an unencrypted one because of the risk of interception.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates active listening from passive listening?
opciones: The listener verifies their understanding with the speaker
The listener stays quiet and never interrupts the speaker
The listener concentrates on presenting their own viewpoint
The listener assumes the message was understood correctly
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of listening get named: competitive, where you are busy with your own point of view; passive, where you assume you understood without checking; and active. In active listening you show interest and then verify, often by restating what was said. That verification is the dividing line.

preguntas.pregunta: What holds a working heart muscle cell depolarized for so long after the rapid upstroke?
opciones: A plateau of about 175 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
A plateau of about 75 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
A plateau of about 250 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
A plateau of about 5 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
preguntas.explicacion: The rapid depolarization of a contractile cell lasts only 3 to 5 ms. Then the membrane potential falls very slowly for roughly 175 ms while calcium enters and little potassium leaves; repolarization takes about 75 ms more, and the whole event runs 250 to 300 ms.

preguntas.pregunta: Minutes after the gloves touched her arm a patient has trouble breathing and cold, clammy skin. What does this suggest?
opciones: A severe allergic reaction, an emergency needing treatment at once
Irritant contact dermatitis, treated by washing and a steroid cream
Latex-fruit syndrome, which shows as an itchy mouth after eating
A delayed type IV reaction, the one behind allergic dermatitis
preguntas.explicacion: Signs of a severe reaction usually involve more than one part of the body: difficulty breathing or swallowing, dizziness or fainting, confusion, vomiting, diarrhoea or cramps, pale or red skin, and shock with shallow breathing and cold, clammy skin. A severe allergic reaction is an emergency and has to be treated right away.

preguntas.pregunta: An 8-year-old with fever and exudative tonsils has a negative rapid strep test. What does current guidance recommend?
opciones: Send a throat swab for culture, because a negative rapid test in a child or adolescent is backed up by culture
Accept the negative result as final, because the rapid antigen test is highly specific for group A streptococcus
Repeat the rapid test at once with a second swab, and treat only if the second cassette also turns positive
Order a throat culture only if the rapid test had been positive, to identify which streptococcal group is present
preguntas.explicacion: A rapid strep test detects group A streptococcal antigen in 10 to 20 minutes, but a throat culture, which takes 24 to 48 hours, sometimes finds infections the rapid test misses. Culture after a negative rapid test is therefore important in children and teens, who can develop rheumatic fever from untreated strep. High specificity means a positive is trustworthy; it says nothing about the negatives the antigen test misses.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the five categories of grief?
opciones: Anticipatory grief, felt before the loss arrives
Displaced grief, aimed at a substitute target
Reactive grief, produced by another person's response
Suppressed grief, blocked on purpose by the family
preguntas.explicacion: The five categories are anticipatory, acute, normal, disenfranchised and complicated grief. Anticipatory grief comes before the loss, tied to an acute, chronic or terminal diagnosis, and patients, families and caregivers all feel it; it has been shown to cushion the bereavement reaction that follows.

Within thirty days of the first visit, matching the deadline for responding to an access request
At the second visit, once the office knows the patient intends to keep using the practice
Only if the patient asks for it, since the notice is posted in the reception area anyway

preguntas.pregunta: When an evacuated tube is used for a paediatric venipuncture, which tube is chosen?
opciones: A small-volume tube, 1 mL or 5 mL, with a low vacuum, to avoid collapsing the vein
A standard 10 mL tube, since a partial fill still keeps the correct blood-to-additive ratio
A 1 mL or 5 mL tube with a high vacuum, so that the small needle fills it quickly
A non-additive tube only, because additive tubes cannot be filled through a butterfly
preguntas.explicacion: When an evacuated tube is used in a child, choose one that collects a small volume, 1 mL or 5 mL, and has a low vacuum; this helps avoid collapse of the vein and may decrease haemolysis. preguntas.pregunta: While washing hands at a sink for routine hand hygiene, which technique detail is correct?
opciones: Keep the hands below the elbows and turn off the faucet with a towel
Keep the hands above the elbows, as in the surgical scrub, and rinse toward the fingertips
Turn off the faucet with clean hands so the towel stays dry for drying
Dry the hands on a shared cloth towel and apply lotion before gloving
preguntas.explicacion: Routine handwashing is done with the hands kept below the elbows so water runs from less to more contaminated areas, 3 to 5 mL of soap, at least 15 to 20 seconds of friction over palms, backs, wrists, finger webs, fingertips, thumbs and nails using WHO's six-step pattern, a thorough rinse, drying with a clean or disposable towel, and using a towel to turn off the water so the clean hands are not recontaminated. The full sixteen-section data sheet printed and taped to the bottle
The date it was filled and the initials of the employee who filled it

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant finds an adult unresponsive, not breathing, and with no pulse. In what order are the steps of CPR performed?
opciones: Chest compressions first, then the airway, then rescue breathing
The airway first, then rescue breathing, then chest compressions
Rescue breathing first, then the airway, then chest compressions
The airway and two breaths, then a pulse check, then compressions
preguntas.explicacion: Circulation is handled first: compressions are started before the airway is opened and before any breath is delivered. The older airway-first order was set aside in 2010 after research showed that beginning compressions early gave better results than managing the airway first. A lone rescuer compresses and leaves ventilation for a second responder.

preguntas.pregunta: Sounds are heard, fade to silence, and then come back as the cuff keeps deflating. What has happened?
opciones: An auscultatory gap: listening continues, and the diastolic is the final silence
A false start: the cuff was underinflated, and the first sounds heard were artifact
A normal phase II, in which the swishing quality always drops below hearing
A leaking valve: the pressure fell too quickly and the sounds were skipped over
preguntas.explicacion: In some patients, particularly those with a wide pulse pressure, the sounds vanish between phase II and phase III and then return. Stopping at that silence underestimates the systolic value or records the diastolic too early. Auscultation carries on, and the diastolic is taken at the last disappearance of sound.

preguntas.pregunta: What is being felt when a clinician palpates a peripheral pulse?
opciones: A pressure wave that distends the arterial wall after the ventricle empties
The blood itself moving past the fingertips at the speed of the circulation
The contraction of the smooth muscle in the wall of the artery being pressed
The vibration carried down the vessel from the closure of the aortic valve
preguntas.explicacion: Each ventricular contraction throws a high-amplitude wave of blood across the aortic valve. That wave stretches the walls of the elastic arteries, and their recoil carries it onward, giving a waveform with a sharp upstroke and a sloping plateau. What the fingers detect is that wall movement, not the blood arriving.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which organs lie in the pelvic portion of the ventral cavity. Which answer is right?
opciones: Most of the urogenital system, together with the rectum
Most of the gastrointestinal tract, with the kidneys
The heart and the lungs, with the large blood vessels
The brain in the upper part and the spinal cord below
preguntas.explicacion: The ventral cavity is divided by the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity above, which holds the heart, lungs, trachea, esophagus, large vessels and nerves, and the abdominopelvic cavity below. That lower one splits again: the abdominal portion holds most of the gastrointestinal tract with the kidneys and adrenal glands, the pelvic portion most of the urogenital system and the rectum.

preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial is carried into a patient's room for an injection. What does the CDC say about that vial afterwards?
opciones: Dedicate it to that single patient; it may not go back into use for others
Return it to the clean medication room and keep using it for up to 28 days
Discard it immediately, since any vial entering a patient area is contaminated
Wipe the septum with alcohol and continue using it for other patients
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC asks that multi-dose vials be assigned to a single patient whenever possible and, when used for several patients, kept and accessed only in a clean medication preparation area away from immediate patient treatment areas. If a multi-dose vial enters an immediate patient treatment area, such as a procedure room, a cart or a patient room or bay, it is dedicated to single-patient use only. It does not have to be thrown away at once, but it can no longer serve other patients, and the 28-day limit still applies to it.

preguntas.pregunta: A blood donor asks how long the red cells she just gave would have lived. What is the lifespan of an erythrocyte, and what removes it?
opciones: About 120 days; macrophages in spleen, liver and marrow remove them
About 10 days, after which macrophages phagocytize them in the spleen
About 4 to 6 weeks, the time the body needs to replace donated cells
A few hours to a few days, like most of the granular leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Erythrocytes live up to 120 days in the circulation and are then removed by macrophages located mainly in the bone marrow, liver and spleen. The 10-day figure is the platelet lifespan, the 4 to 6 weeks is how long it takes the body to replace the cells lost in a blood donation, and hours to days is the lifespan of most white cells.

preguntas.pregunta: A family moving to another state asks whether their child's Medicaid lab work will still be covered. Which service must every state Medicaid program cover?
opciones: Laboratory and X-ray services, which federal law lists as mandatory
Eyeglasses and dentures, which federal law lists as mandatory benefits
Physical therapy, which federal law lists as mandatory for adult patients
Prescription drugs, which federal law lists as mandatory for every state
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law splits Medicaid benefits into mandatory and optional. Mandatory benefits, which every state must provide, include inpatient and outpatient hospital care, laboratory and X-ray services, physician services, nursing facility care, home health, family planning and the screening program for children. Prescription drugs, eyeglasses, dentures and physical therapy are on the optional list, which is why coverage differs from state to state.

preguntas.pregunta: Why do most people pay no premium for Medicare Part A?
opciones: They or a spouse paid Medicare taxes while working, usually for 10 years or more
They or a spouse enrolled in Part B, which pays the Part A premium for them
They enrolled during the Initial Enrollment Period rather than waiting to sign up
They receive care from providers who accept the Medicare-approved amount in full
preguntas.explicacion: Premium-free Part A goes to people who, or whose spouse, paid Medicare taxes long enough while working, generally at least 10 years; those who did not qualify may be able to buy Part A. preguntas.pregunta: How is an infrared temporal artery thermometer used?
opciones: It is drawn slowly from the middle of the forehead across to the lateral hairline
It is held a short distance from the frontal bone without touching the skin at all
It is pressed on the forehead and held still until the display stops changing
It is drawn from the lateral hairline down the neck over the carotid pulse point
preguntas.explicacion: This device is moved slowly from the centre of the forehead over to the hairline at the side, reading infrared radiation from the skin above the superficial temporal artery and reporting the highest of the many values it samples. The instrument that is held away from the skin without contact is the infrared forehead thermometer.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature a · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hematocrit result comes back as 42. What does that number mean?
opciones: That 42% of the blood volume is made up of red blood cells
That 42% of the blood volume is plasma, the liquid portion
That the red blood cell count is 4.2 million per microliter
That 42% of the formed elements are white cells and platelets
preguntas.explicacion: A hematocrit is reported as the percentage of the blood that consists of red cells; the rest of the sample is white cells, platelets and plasma. The usual figure is about 45 percent, with women at 37 to 47 (mean 41) and men at 42 to 52 (mean 47). White cells and platelets together form under 1 percent of a sample, so they are not counted in the hematocrit, and 4.2 million per microliter would be a cell count, not a percentage.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Hematocrit Test, What do the results mean?; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D4 4G hematocrit) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A family assumes Medicare will pay for their mother's nursing home stay for help with bathing and dressing. What should they be told?
opciones: Medicare does not pay for long-term care, though Medicaid may if the state's rules are met
Medicare pays in full once a doctor certifies that daily personal care is necessary
Medicare pays after the patient has used all 100 days of the skilled nursing benefit
Medicare pays whenever the nursing home is certified and accepts Medicare assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Long-term care, also called custodial care, is medical and non-medical help for people with a chronic illness or disability, mostly assistance with the basic tasks of everyday life. Because most of it is non-medical, neither Medicare nor most health insurance, Medigap included, pays for it. A person may qualify through Medicaid if the state's rules are met, or buy private long-term care insurance.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Long-term care: Description, Coverage details and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Long-term care coverage · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: An inspector asks a hospital laboratory about specimens collected at a distant clinic it neither staffs nor supervises. What does the accreditation checklist expect?
opciones: A quality management system covering transport problems from those sites too
A signed agreement placing responsibility for those specimens on the clinic
A separate rejection policy applied only to specimens from outside sites
Proof that a member of laboratory staff visits each site once a year
preguntas.explicacion: Two items of the general checklist ask for a quality management system for problems in specimen transport, and they say explicitly that this includes remote sites and sites not under the laboratory's control. Other items in the same list require two identifiers before collection and two identifiers on the primary container, so the chain is expected to hold outside the building.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.2, items GEN.40535 and GEN.40540

preguntas.pregunta: Which service does the Postal Service describe as the affordable ground option for packages, with insurance included?
opciones: USPS Ground Advantage, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
Priority Mail Express, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
First-Class Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
Certified Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is presented as an affordable and reliable way to send packages up to 70 pounds inside the country, with expected delivery in two to five days and up to one hundred dollars of insurance included, and additional coverage available up to five thousand. It is also the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot travel by air.

preguntas.pregunta: What makes a measure an electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM)?
opciones: It is specified in a standard format and pulls its data from the EHR
It is specified in a standard format and is abstracted by hand from charts
It is any quality measure reported to CMS through an online portal
It is any measure of how quickly the EHR responds during a patient visit
preguntas.explicacion: An eCQM is written in a standard electronic specification and draws data extracted electronically from electronic health records or clinical IT systems. Capturing the data automatically cuts the manual abstraction and the human error that come with it, and applies the same rules and coding across health systems.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, eCQI Resource Center: Get Started with eCQMs

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's voice breaks while she describes her diagnosis. The assistant names the emotion and reflects it back. Which technique is that?
opciones: Exploring feeling tones
Providing the rationale
Summarizing the visit
Clarifying the account
preguntas.explicacion: Exploring feeling tones is listed as identifying and empathizing with the patient's emotional state and reflecting it back to them. Providing rationale explains why information is needed, summarizing restates the content in the provider's own words and can close the interview, and clarifying draws out detail from a statement that was not clear.

preguntas.pregunta: Which program replaced the electronic health record incentive program for eligible clinicians?
opciones: The Merit-based Incentive Payment System, created by MACRA in 2015
The Hospital Value-Based Purchasing program, created for inpatient care
The Medicare Shared Savings Program, created for accountable care groups
The Quality Improvement Organization review of hospital discharge decisions
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 ended the electronic health record incentive program for eligible professionals and folded similar requirements into the Merit-based Incentive Payment System, where promoting interoperability is one of the four performance categories. Hospitals and critical access hospitals continue under their own promoting interoperability program.

preguntas.pregunta: After a knee replacement a machine flexes and extends the patient's knee while the patient lies still in bed. Which kind of range of motion is that?
opciones: Passive, because the movement comes entirely from an outside force
Active assist, because the machine only shares part of the effort
Active, because the patient's own joint is the one being carried
Passive assist, because the patient is lying down while it happens
preguntas.explicacion: Passive range of motion is movement applied to a joint only by another person or by a machine, with the patient's joint completely relaxed. The continuous motion machine used after a knee replacement is the example given. Active assist would mean the patient supplies part of the movement, which is not the case here.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises

preguntas.pregunta: During a lumbar puncture, how much cerebrospinal fluid is collected and into how many containers?
opciones: 1 to 10 mL, collected into 4 or more vials once the pressure has been measured
1 to 10 mL, collected into a single vial once the pressure has been measured
20 to 30 mL, collected into 4 or more vials once the pressure has been measured
1 to 10 mL, collected into 4 or more vials before the pressure is measured at all
preguntas.explicacion: The patient lies on one side with the knees drawn toward the chest and the chin tucked down, the back is cleaned, a local anesthetic goes in and the spinal needle is placed, usually between L3-L4 or L4-L5. An opening pressure may be taken first, and then 1 to 10 mL is collected into 4 or more vials. Normal pressure runs 90 to 180 mm H2O.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CSF collection (003428), How the Test is Performed and Normal Results; and StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples

preguntas.pregunta: Which event most often opens the door to acute otitis media in a child?
opciones: A viral upper respiratory infection that disturbs Eustachian tube function
A viral upper respiratory infection that perforates the tympanic membrane
A build-up of cerumen that blocks the external auditory canal completely
A rise in middle ear pressure caused by hearing loss in the affected ear
preguntas.explicacion: Acute otitis media comes out of the meeting of pathogens, host susceptibility and environment, and the usual trigger is a viral upper respiratory infection that disturbs the working of the Eustachian tube. Once drainage fails, the middle ear inflames and microbes multiply. Immunocompromise and genetic predisposition raise the risk further.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Otitis Media", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: When should anti-HBs be tested to document a healthcare worker's response to the hepatitis B vaccine series?
opciones: 1 to 2 months after the final dose
6 months after the final dose
Within 10 working days of the final dose
Every year, at the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Postvaccination serologic testing for anti-HBs is done 1 to 2 months after the third dose, so that the worker's response status is on record for any future exposure; a level of 10 mIU/mL or more after a documented series is the correlate of protection. For workers who also received HBIG, testing may have to wait until the HBIG antibody has cleared, about 6 months after it was given. Ten working days is the OSHA deadline for offering the vaccine, and annual testing is not recommended for immunocompetent responders.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccine protection and anti-HBs testing; CDC, Exposure to Blood (2003), Treatment: HBV
preguntas.subtema: Post-vaccination testing · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: After a capillary draw on a 5-year-old, what follow-up care is suggested for the child beyond the requisition?
opciones: A gesture that leaves the child on a positive note, such as praise, a handshake or a fun sticker
A dose of oral sucrose, 0.012 to 0.12 g, which the WHO recommends as analgesia at any age
An explanation of every result the laboratory will report, so the child feels informed
A brief period lying flat, since children faint more often than adults after skin punctures
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up has two parts, completing the requisition and providing comfort and reassurance; a simple gesture, verbal praise, a handshake, a fun sticker or a pat on the back, is all it takes to leave the child on a positive note. The sucrose dose of 0.012 to 0.12 g is for newborns undergoing venepuncture or heel-pricks, not for older children.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Comfort and reassurance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B pediatric collection, D3 3Q post-procedural care · PBT II.B age-specific needs · CCMA 3E9 · NCMA 2C.10

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose period is two days late drank several glasses of water before giving a random urine sample, and the office pregnancy test is negative. How should this result be handled?
opciones: It may be a false negative from dilute urine or early testing; a repeat on first morning urine in about a week is advised
It is reliable, because office cassettes detect hCG from 10 days after conception regardless of urine concentration
It should be repeated immediately with a second cassette from the same kit, since a single negative can never be reported
It confirms that the patient is not pregnant, because urine tests are 97 to 99 % accurate at any point after a missed period
preguntas.explicacion: Drinking large amounts of fluid before collecting the sample can dilute the hCG so that it does not show on the test, and testing too soon after conception may precede detectable hormone levels; both produce false negatives. First morning urine is the most concentrated. Because hCG rises daily in early pregnancy, a negative test is repeated about a week later, and a still-suspected pregnancy is referred to the provider. The 97 to 99 % accuracy figure applies to tests done a week or two after a missed period.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pregnancy Test, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; What do the results mean?; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: HCG in urine (003619)
preguntas.subtema: False-negative urine hCG · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.d.(4) · RMA III.C.4.b.iv · NCMA 2B.19

preguntas.pregunta: What does an automated external defibrillator do once its pads are on the chest?
opciones: It reads the heart rhythm and shocks only when the rhythm calls for a shock
It delivers a shock as soon as the pads are attached to an unresponsive patient
It paces the heart at 100 to 120 beats a minute while compressions go on
It confirms the pulse and holds compressions until a pulse can be felt
preguntas.explicacion: The device analyzes the rhythm on its own and delivers a shock if, and only if, a shock is what that rhythm needs; the rescuer follows its spoken instructions exactly. When a shock is advised, compressions pause and everyone stands clear; the moment the shock is delivered, or if none is advised, CPR resumes without delay.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38

preguntas.pregunta: A conventional 12-lead ECG is being set up. How many wires are attached to the patient?
opciones: Ten: four on the limbs and six across the chest
Twelve: four on the limbs and eight across the chest
Six: two on the limbs and four across the chest
Fourteen: six on the limbs and eight across the chest
preguntas.explicacion: Twelve leads are produced from ten wires. Four limb electrodes generate the six limb leads, and each of the six chest positions has its own wire. The limb leads look at the heart in the vertical plane and the chest leads record it in the horizontal plane, which is why both groups are needed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k147 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4

preguntas.pregunta: A superficial laceration is closed with cyanoacrylate skin glue. What should the patient be told to expect?
opciones: It gives a water-tight seal and tends to come away on its own after about 7 to 10 days
It gives a water-tight seal and has to be dissolved off with acetone at the follow-up visit
It gives a water-tight seal and is removed with a staple extractor once the wound is closed
It gives a water-tight seal and stays on until the scar has finished maturing at 12 months
preguntas.explicacion: Skin glue provides a water-tight seal and tensile strength while it lasts, and it generally falls off after roughly seven to ten days. It is quick and comparatively painless, which suits pediatric and percutaneous wounds, but it is only good for superficial lacerations: anything deeper needs a layered suture closure underneath.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Facial Laceration Repair", Special Considerations for Suture Choice
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: How much of its original strength does a healed incision regain, and when does maximal tensile strength arrive?
opciones: About 80 percent, reached at roughly 11 to 14 weeks after the injury
About 80 percent, reached at roughly 4 to 6 weeks after the injury
About 100 percent, reached at roughly 11 to 14 weeks after the injury
About 50 percent, reached at roughly 9 to 12 months after the injury
preguntas.explicacion: The remodeling phase starts around week three and can run up to twelve months; excess collagen degrades and contraction peaks around week three. Maximal tensile strength of an incision wound comes at roughly 11 to 14 weeks, and the scar never regains full strength, settling at about 80 percent of the original.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Healing Phases", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l

preguntas.pregunta: When a stool specimen is collected for the laboratory, which portions should be included?
opciones: Any visible pus, mucus or blood, plus material from the first, middle and last parts of the stool
Only the formed central portion, and never any mucus or blood, which would contaminate the culture badly
The last part of the stool only, since it has been in contact with the rectal mucosa longest
About 1 mL mixed with 9 mL of saline, the preparation used for every stool culture
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen is passed into a clean, dry container with a tight lid and then moved to a labeled transport container. It should deliberately include portions with visible abnormal material such as pus, mucus or blood, and represent the first, middle and last parts of the stool. Mixing about 1 mL with 9 mL of buffered saline and freezing the supernatant is the preparation for suspected viral infection, not a general rule.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Specimen Collection (Fecal Samples)

preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to know how hard its forms and its system really are for patients. Which method does the toolkit describe?
opciones: Shadowing: an observer follows diverse patients through the whole visit
Mailing a satisfaction survey to every patient after the visit ends
Asking the staff to rate how clear they believe their own forms are
Timing how long each patient takes to fill out the intake paperwork
preguntas.explicacion: Practices are usually unaware of how much trouble patients have reading forms, understanding information and moving through the system, and patients are the ones who can point it out. In shadowing, someone quietly follows a patient from arrival to departure, asks afterward what went well and what was hard, and fills out an observation form.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 17: Shadow patients
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k167 team roles · CMAA 2F

preguntas.pregunta: How does a secondary plan decide what it pays on a claim?
opciones: It pays after the primary plan, so the total stays within the allowable expenses
It pays at the same time as the primary plan, each covering half of the claim
It pays the full balance the patient still owes, deductibles and copays included
It pays the difference between the billed charge and what the primary plan paid
preguntas.explicacion: The secondary plan waits until the primary plan has paid, then covers part or all of the allowable expenses left unpaid, reducing its benefits so the combined payments do not exceed the total allowable expenses for the claim. An allowable expense is a health care cost, deductibles, coinsurance and copayments included, that at least one of the plans covers, so an uncovered charge is outside the calculation altogether.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Effect on the Benefits of This Plan
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185

preguntas.pregunta: For which patients is the advice to sit near and hold eye contact given with caution?
opciones: Patients with psychotic disorders or paranoia, whom it may destabilise
Patients with hearing loss, who need to watch the speaker's lips move
Patients with dementia, who need one idea presented at a time
Patients who use sign language and watch the interpreter instead
preguntas.explicacion: The note under the table of techniques warns that eye contact and sitting near the patient could be destabilising for some individuals, including those with psychotic disorders and paranoia, and should be used with caution; where provider safety is uncertain, sit at a safe distance without leaving the patient feeling isolated. Hearing loss and dementia call for other changes.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), note on eye contact
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k16 · CCMA 6 k197 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: What is done to the work surface itself before any sterile supply is placed on it?
opciones: It is disinfected and then allowed to dry completely
It is disinfected and covered while still visibly wet
It is wiped with sterile water and dried with a towel
It is covered with a second drape without being wiped
preguntas.explicacion: The surface is disinfected and left to dry all the way through before anything sterile goes down on it. A surface still wet with disinfectant lets moisture wick through the drape, and moisture wicked from an unsterile area contaminates the field within an inch of where it appears. Only sterile supplies are allowed onto the field once it is established.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.g · NCMA 2B.11

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant hands a patient a pamphlet about her new diagnosis and moves on. Why is that not enough?
opciones: Material works only inside a teaching plan: review it and check understanding
Material works only if it is written at or below the fourth grade level
Material works only when it is mailed home instead of handed over in person
Material works only when the patient signs that she received the pamphlet
preguntas.explicacion: Handing over a pamphlet or pointing at a website does not by itself produce understanding or a change in behavior. When the information matters, someone in the practice goes through it with the patient and the caregiver, circling or highlighting key points, personalizing it, and confirming with teach-back.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 12: Use Health Education Material Effectively

preguntas.pregunta: In a facilitated virtual visit, what is the role of the medical assistant at the patient's site?
opciones: Collecting objective data with equipment and transmitting it to the remote clinician
Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit
Recording the encounter so the clinician can review the video after the appointment
Waiting outside the room, since a facilitated visit requires the patient to be alone
preguntas.explicacion: In this synchronous model the patient sits at an accessible site, such as a clinic with diagnostic equipment, while the clinician is elsewhere. A telehealth facilitator, described as a medical assistant or nurse, gathers objective data with tools such as a digital stethoscope, a thermometer or a pulse oximeter and sends the information to the clinician for evaluation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Facilitated virtual visit · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Early research found that confronting a patient about a behavior tends to produce what?
opciones: Resistance, either refusing care or not complying
A quicker move from contemplation into preparation
More change talk and fewer sustain-talk statements
A durable rise in the patient's own self-efficacy
preguntas.explicacion: Confrontation was found to push people to resist, directly by refusing care or indirectly through noncompliance. The approach that works instead is drawing out the reasons behind the ambivalence and reinforcing the patient's own self-motivating statements, since the decision remains theirs.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Motivational Interviewing", Function

preguntas.pregunta: A patient submits a written request for a copy of her chart on March 3. By when must the office act on it?
opciones: No later than 30 calendar days from receipt of the request, and sooner where possible
No later than 60 calendar days from receipt, the same period allowed for an amendment
No later than 10 working days, the period set for verifying the requester's identity
No later than 6 years from receipt, matching the accounting of disclosures period
preguntas.explicacion: Access has to be provided within 30 calendar days of receiving the request. OCR treats that as an outer limit and encourages faster responses, noting that a portal or personal health record can make access almost immediate, and that patients reasonably expect speed from an office that uses health information technology every day.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in shock begins to vomit and a spinal injury is suspected. How is the patient turned?
opciones: By log rolling, keeping head, neck and back aligned as one unit
By turning only the head to one side and leaving the body flat
By raising the legs higher so the airway drains toward the mouth
By sitting the patient forward with support under both shoulders
preguntas.explicacion: Turning the head alone is what is done when no spinal injury is suspected. If the spine may be injured, the patient is log rolled: head, neck and back stay in line and the body and head move together. A patient with a known or suspected spinal injury is otherwise not moved at all, and two people are needed if moving cannot be avoided.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", If the person vomits or drools
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's condition worsens after appropriate treatment and the family talks about suing. Does the outcome alone show negligence?
opciones: No: an undesirable result can happen even when the care was appropriate
No: a result only counts once the state licensing board has reviewed it
Yes: a worsening condition after treatment is what negligence means
Yes: any deviation from the expected recovery is a compensable injury
preguntas.explicacion: A medical intervention can leave the patient better, worse or unchanged, and all three are possible with entirely appropriate care. Negligence cannot be read off an unexpected result, a failure to cure or a failure to recover. Even an error that fell below the standard may have caused no damages, in which case there is probably nothing to claim.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Introduction: Medical Errors Compared to Medical Negligence

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who never worked long enough to earn premium-free Part A asks what buying it will cost her in 2026.
opciones: Either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long she or her spouse paid the taxes
A flat $202.90 a month, which is what every enrollee pays for Part A in 2026
A flat $283 a year, payable once the first hospital benefit period has opened
A flat $1,736 a year, the same figure as the inpatient hospital deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Part A costs nothing for most people because they or a spouse paid Medicare taxes long enough, generally ten years. Someone who does not qualify may be able to buy it, and the 2026 amount is either $311 or $565 a month according to how long those taxes were paid. Part B has to be taken as well in order to buy Part A.

preguntas.pregunta: Which Safety Data Sheet section tells the reader which gloves and eye protection to use with a chemical and lists its exposure limits?
opciones: Section 8, Exposure Controls/Personal Protection
Section 7, Handling and Storage, with incompatibilities
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with routes of exposure
Section 1, Identification, with the emergency phone number
preguntas.explicacion: Section 8 brings together the OSHA permissible exposure limits and ACGIH threshold limit values, the engineering controls such as local exhaust ventilation, and the personal protective measures, down to the glove material, for example nitrile or PVC, and its breakthrough time. Section 7 gives safe handling and storage conditions and incompatible chemicals; Section 11 describes toxic effects, symptoms and carcinogen listings; Section 1 identifies the product and supplier and gives the emergency telephone number.

preguntas.pregunta: What has to be retrievable by prescription number each time a Schedule III or IV prescription is refilled?
opciones: Drug name and form, the date, the quantity, the pharmacist's initials and the total
Registration number of the prescriber, the diagnosis, and the plan that is billed
The date, the quantity, and the number of the order form the substance came on
Only how many refills are left, since the original prescription holds all the rest
preguntas.explicacion: Each refill is entered on the back of the prescription or in another document or electronic record that is uniformly maintained and readily retrievable. What has to be retrievable by the prescription number is the name and dosage form of the controlled substance, the date filled or refilled, the quantity dispensed, the initials of the dispensing pharmacist for each refill, and the total number of refills for it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which religious observance is a month-long fast from food and drink during daylight hours?
opciones: Ramadan, in the Islamic tradition
Yom Kippur, in Judaism
Great Lent, in Eastern Orthodoxy
The month of Ala, in the Baha'i faith
preguntas.explicacion: Ramadan is a month-long fast from food and drink during daylight, lasting 29 or 30 days, with children, pregnant women and the ill possibly exempt. Yom Kippur is a single day without eating or drinking; the Orthodox Great Lent is a 40-day fast from meat, dairy and oil; and the Baha'i fast runs March 2 to 20, sunrise to sunset.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a practice starts booking video visits it is told to settle several scheduling questions. Which one belongs on that list?

How the clinician will write the visit up in the record once the video call ends
How the practice will train its current health care team to use the new platform
How the practice will support a caregiver who is helping the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Under scheduling, the questions are when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether patients will book online or by telephone, how the office will judge whether a telehealth appointment is appropriate, and how and when reminders go out. Training the team is a staffing question, supporting a caregiver falls under meeting patient needs, and documentation comes afterwards.

preguntas.pregunta: A blood culture bottle has just been filled. Which anticoagulant does it hold, and how is it mixed?
opciones: Sodium polyanethole sulfonate; the bottle is mixed eight to ten times
Sodium citrate at 3.2 per cent; the bottle is inverted three to six times
Sodium fluoride with oxalate; the bottle is inverted three to six times
Lithium heparin with a gel; the bottle is mixed eight to ten times over
preguntas.explicacion: Culture bottles contain sodium polyanethole sulfonate, which acts as an anticoagulant and blocks activation of complement, and the bottle is mixed eight to ten times once filled. Three to six inversions is the figure for the citrate tube, and fluoride with oxalate belongs to the glucose tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory benchmarks its critical result communication against the IFCC WG-LEPS preliminary quality specifications. Which pair of figures marks optimum performance?
opciones: Average communication time under 50 minutes, and more than 96 % of critical results communicated
Average communication time under 15 minutes, and more than 99 % of critical results communicated
Average communication time under 50 minutes, and fewer than 0.4 % of critical results communicated late
Average communication time under 30 minutes, and more than 90 % of critical results communicated
preguntas.explicacion: The IFCC working group on laboratory errors and patient safety, from data of 39 laboratories collected in 2008-2009, classified an average time under 50 minutes for critical result communication and more than 96 % of critical results communicated as optimum, alongside fewer than 0.4 % misidentified samples on the pre-analytical side. A CAP Q-Tracks study showed the best quarter of US laboratories above 99 %, so laboratories already past the benchmark are expected to aim higher.

preguntas.pregunta: A tracing is being read beside a pressure curve. When does ventricular contraction actually begin?
opciones: As the QRS complex reaches the peak of the R wave
As the P wave returns to the baseline of the tracing
As the T wave reaches its highest point on the tracing
As the ST segment begins to climb above the baseline
preguntas.explicacion: Electrical activity comes first and the muscle follows a moment later. The QRS complex is ventricular depolarization, and the ventricles start to squeeze as that complex peaks at the R wave, which is why the QRS sits just before the rise in ventricular pressure. The T wave is the recovery phase, not the contraction.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cardiac Cycle", Cellular Level
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee asks how often laboratory errors actually affect patients. What do the published data indicate?
opciones: About 24 to 30 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, and actual or potential harm occurs in 3 to 12 %
About 3 to 12 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, and actual or potential harm occurs in under 1 %
About 46 to 68 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, and actual harm occurs in 24 to 30 % of them
About 62 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, matching the share that arises in the pre-analytical phase
preguntas.explicacion: Published data suggest that 24 to 30 % of laboratory errors have an effect on patient care, while actual or potential patient harm occurs in 3 to 12 %, with some areas such as molecular genetics reaching much higher harm rates; a five-point scoring study found that most errors scored lowest for actual impact yet highest for potential impact. The 46 to 68 % figure is the share of errors in the pre-pre-analytical phase and 62 % the pre-analytical share in the Italian stat laboratory.

preguntas.pregunta: Why may the timing of a therapeutic drug monitoring draw differ between two patients on the same drug?
opciones: The reason differs: dose adjustment, adverse effects, or suspected intoxication
The tube additive differs between morning and afternoon collections
The half-life of the drug is reset by each meal the patient eats
Peaks are always drawn at 4 p.m. and troughs at 8 a.m. regardless of dosing
preguntas.explicacion: For therapeutic drug monitoring the timing of the draw may differ according to the specific reason for the test, whether to justify a dose, to monitor adverse effects or to rule out intoxication, and that diurnal sampling may be requested for markers with a circadian pattern. Fixed clock times and tube additives have nothing to do with it.

preguntas.pregunta: After a likely exposure to an allergen, how many body systems must be involved before anaphylaxis is considered?
opciones: Two or more systems, such as skin plus breathing or skin plus gut
Three or more systems, one of which has to be the airway itself
One system only, and only when that system is the skin with hives
Four or more systems, including a fall in the systolic pressure
preguntas.explicacion: With a likely exposure, involvement of any two of skin or mucosa, breathing, blood pressure and gastrointestinal symptoms meets the criteria, even without airway swelling or hypotension. Known exposure plus hypotension alone also counts. The criteria are a guide for recognition: treatment is never held back to make them fit.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Evaluation: Clinical Criteria for Anaphylaxis

preguntas.pregunta: Which charge is not an allowable expense when two plans coordinate benefits?
opciones: A service that neither of the two plans covers for that patient
A copayment the patient owes under the terms of the primary plan
A deductible amount applied by the primary plan to the claim
A coinsurance percentage left unpaid after the primary plan pays
preguntas.explicacion: An allowable expense is a health care expense covered at least in part by one of the plans, and deductibles, coinsurance and copayments all count. An expense that no plan covering the person covers is not allowable, and neither is an amount a provider is barred by law or contract from charging, nor a reduction the primary plan made because the patient ignored a plan rule such as precertification.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Definitions

preguntas.pregunta: How is the paper of a standard 12-lead recording laid out?
opciones: Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Three lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in three groups of four
Twelve lines of graph, with one lead printed on each of them
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing paper is set out in six channels. The twelve leads are written in four groups of three, so the first three channels carry lead I with aVR, V1 and V4, then lead II with aVL, V2 and V5, then lead III with aVF, V3 and V6.

preguntas.pregunta: What should tell a phlebotomist arriving at a room which protective equipment that patient requires?
opciones: An easily visible sign posted outside the room or contact zone
The color of the wristband the patient was given at admission
The order in the chart, which names the equipment to be worn
The container by the door, whose contents indicate what to wear
preguntas.explicacion: Easily visible signs are placed outside patient rooms and contact zones listing the protective equipment a given encounter requires, which is what lets a visiting worker gear up correctly before going in. It fits the rest of the system: donning happens outside the room, and the precautions in force decide which items are needed, since not every component is required for every patient.

preguntas.pregunta: A provider wants to sign chart notes with a rubber stamp because handwriting is slow. What does CMS say?
opciones: Stamped signatures are not typically acceptable, apart from a disability accommodation
Stamped signatures are acceptable whenever the provider keeps the stamp locked away
Stamped signatures are acceptable if a signature log lists the stamp and its owner
Stamped signatures are acceptable on orders but never on progress notes or reports
preguntas.explicacion: A handwritten signature is a mark by an individual signifying knowledge, approval, acceptance or obligation. CMS states that stamped signatures are not typically acceptable, and permits a rubber stamp only under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 for an author with a physical disability who can prove to a contractor that the disability prevents signing. A signature log is a separate device, for matching initials or an illegible signature to a name.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4

preguntas.pregunta: The record describes the same condition as both acute and chronic, and the Index has separate subentries at the same level. What does the coder do?
opciones: Code both of them, and sequence the acute or subacute code first
Code both of them, and sequence the chronic code first of the two
Code the chronic one alone, since it is the longer-standing problem
Code the acute one alone, since it is what brought her in this time
preguntas.explicacion: Where the same condition is described as both acute or subacute and chronic, and separate subentries exist in the Alphabetic Index at the same indentation level, both are coded and the acute or subacute code is sequenced first. Signs and symptoms routinely associated with a disease process are not added as extra codes unless the classification says otherwise.

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the conduction system sets the rate and rhythm of a normal heartbeat?
opciones: The sinoatrial node, in the upper wall of the right atrium
The atrioventricular node, in the lower right atrium
The atrioventricular bundle, inside the interventricular septum
The Purkinje fibers, spread through the ventricular walls
preguntas.explicacion: The sinoatrial node depolarizes faster than any other part of the system, reaches threshold first, and imposes its pace on everything downstream. That is why it is called the pacemaker and why the pattern it produces is called sinus rhythm. The other structures can fire on their own, but only at slower inherent rates.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A tube is being filled by injecting through its rubber stopper. Which precaution applies?
opciones: The tube stands in a sturdy rack and is not held in the other hand
The tube is held in the other hand so the angle can be corrected
The tube is laid flat on the tray so the blood runs down its wall
The tube is held by an assistant while the worker steadies it
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratory sample tubes are placed in a sturdy rack before the needle goes through the stopper, and the paired prohibition is not to inject into a tube while holding it in the other hand. Where a rack is not available, one hand fills the tube or a needle shield protects the other.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is plain gauze moistened before it is used as wound packing?
opciones: Because dry gauze sticks to the wound base and injures the granulation tissue
Because dry gauze absorbs too much exudate and dries the wound bed out entirely
Because dry gauze cannot be cut to shape unless it has been softened with saline
Because dry gauze loses its sterility once it is in contact with the periwound skin
preguntas.explicacion: Gauze is the least expensive dressing and has to be changed often, at least daily, but left unmoistened it adheres to the wound base and damages the granulation tissue when it comes off. Packing gauze is dampened with sterile normal saline and wrung out so it is damp rather than wet, because gauze that is too wet macerates tissue and absorbs less.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.5 Wound Dressings
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.k

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist spots two tubes carrying the wrong patient's label and pulls them before they reach the analyzer. How is this classified in patient safety terms?
opciones: A near miss, because the error occurred but was intercepted before it could reach the patient
A sentinel event, since any wrong-patient error meets the severity threshold set for those
A preventable adverse event, since harm from a labeling error is assumed until it is disproved
An error of execution that reached the patient but produced no harm that could be measured
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error that happens but does not reach the patient, whether through timely intervention or through luck. Nothing was reported, so no harm followed and neither of the harm-based categories fits: a preventable adverse event needs harm caused by the error, and a sentinel event needs death, severe or permanent harm. Near misses are still worth reporting, because they show where the system is thin.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Function
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement, incident reporting · CCMA 6 k211 · CMAA 3E k44

preguntas.pregunta: What safety step is taken before and after removing a run of staples?
opciones: Count the staples first and compare the count with the number actually taken out
Photograph the incision first and compare the image with the line after removal
Measure the incision first and compare that length with the length after removal
Palpate the incision first and compare the firmness with the firmness after removal
preguntas.explicacion: The staples are counted before the procedure begins and the removed ones are counted against that number at the end, so none is left behind. The wound is also inspected first for uniform closure, drainage, redness and swelling, and it is irrigated with sterile normal saline to lift debris and crusted exudate before the extractor is used.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.11 Checklist for Staple Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m

preguntas.pregunta: Which is the first stage of heat illness?
opciones: Muscle cramps, most often in the legs or the abdomen
Cool moist skin with dark urine and severe thirst
Confusion and slurred speech with a very high temperature
A rapid weak pulse with rapid shallow breathing at rest
preguntas.explicacion: Cramps in the legs or abdomen are the first stage; fatigue, thirst and very heavy sweating come with them. If exposure goes on untreated, heat exhaustion follows with cool moist skin, dark urine, dizziness, headache, nausea and a rapid weak pulse, and after that heat stroke.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heat emergencies", Symptoms

preguntas.pregunta: A pathology department wants to attack ordering errors, which a review puts at roughly seven orders in ten. Which measures are described as effective?
opciones: Governance of ordering, decision support, reflex algorithms and feedback to prescribers
A ban on panel ordering, a paper countersignature and a monthly audit of each ward
Restriction of ordering rights to consultants and a fixed weekly quota per patient
Automatic cancellation of any test repeated within a week of a normal result
preguntas.explicacion: Ordering is an easily overlooked step, and about 70 % of orders carry some sort of error: a test ordered twice, a test forgotten, or simply the wrong test. Governance programmes, clinical decision support, reflex testing with interpretation and algorithms, feedback to the ordering physician and diagnostic stewardship have all been shown to cut inappropriate ordering and improve turnaround.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the 'therapeutic range' of a monitored medicine?
opciones: The range of blood levels that is medically helpful without being dangerous
The range of doses a pharmacist may dispense without a new prescription
The time window before the next dose during which a trough is drawn
The reference range printed for healthy people who do not take the drug
preguntas.explicacion: TDM results show whether medicine levels fall in a range that is medically helpful but not dangerous, called the therapeutic range, which varies with the drug and the patient; if levels are outside it the provider adjusts the dose and repeats the test. The pre-dose window is the trough timing, a separate concept.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, section What do the results mean

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks which part pays for the doctor visit and the walker ordered today.
opciones: Part B, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part A, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part D, which covers provider services and the equipment ordered during them
Medigap, which covers provider services once Part A benefits are exhausted
preguntas.explicacion: Part B is the medical insurance half: services from doctors and other providers, outpatient care, home health, durable medical equipment such as walkers and wheelchairs, and many preventive services. Part A is hospital insurance, Part D pays for prescription drugs, and Medigap is private supplemental insurance that helps with the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than covering new categories.

preguntas.pregunta: Which patients qualify for Medicare chronic care management services?
opciones: Those with 2 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months
Those with 2 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 3 months
Those with 1 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months
Those with 3 or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: Chronic care management covers a patient with multiple chronic conditions, meaning two or more, that are expected to last at least twelve months or until the patient dies, and that place the patient at real risk of death, acute worsening or functional decline. The services themselves are non-face-to-face.

preguntas.pregunta: How long does a practitioner have to keep the records of controlled substances?
opciones: At least two years, available for inspection and copying by DEA officials
At least six months, the span for which a Schedule IV prescription is valid
At least seven years, the span used for retaining the patient's own record
At least thirty days, after which the next inventory replaces those records
preguntas.explicacion: Complete and accurate records are kept on a current basis for every controlled substance purchased, received, sold, stored, distributed, dispensed or otherwise disposed of, and they are maintained at least two years for inspection and copying by authorized DEA officials. Records and inventories of Schedule II substances are kept separately from all others; those for Schedules III to V may be separate or readily retrievable.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are the chest marks drawn again right after the sites are scrubbed?
opciones: The rubbing takes the marks off and the spots are lost
The alcohol makes the wax pencil marks hard to read
The marks have to be moved a space down after cleaning
The marks are copied onto the log sheet for the record
preguntas.explicacion: Each chest site is briskly rubbed with alcohol and gauze, and the cosmetic pencil marks come off with the oil and dead skin. The recommended habit is to keep an eye on the spot while cleaning it and re-mark it immediately, so the landmark work does not have to be repeated.

preguntas.pregunta: A staff member repeats a false and damaging claim about a patient out loud in the break room. Which tort is that, and what does it require?
opciones: Slander, and unlike libel the damages have to be proven by the person suing
Slander, and like libel the damages are presumed from the fact of publication
Libel, and the damages have to be proven by the person bringing the lawsuit
Libel, and the damages are presumed once the statement has been repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Defamation is a statement that harms someone's reputation, and it splits in two: libel is generally written or otherwise recorded, slander is generally spoken. With slander, damages are not presumed and the party suing has to prove them. Traditional libel rules go the other way and take the injury as given once the statement was published.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's skin is oily at the electrode sites. How is each site prepared?
opciones: Rub it with alcohol and gauze about ten times
Rub it with alcohol and gauze about three times
Wipe it with dry gauze and then let it air dry
Part the hair and press the electrode down firmly
preguntas.explicacion: Each site is scrubbed vigorously with alcohol and gauze roughly ten times to take off oil, sweat and scaly skin. Applying an electrode to a surface that was not cleaned that way is one of the causes of a drifting baseline. Parting the hair is a separate trick, and it helps the electrode stick.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses the plan the clinician is convinced is best. What does respect for autonomy require?
opciones: The clinician stops, having explained the reasoning and listened first
The clinician proceeds, since beneficence outranks the patient's refusal
The clinician presses until the patient accepts, then documents consent
The clinician transfers the patient, since the relationship has broken down
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient does not agree that the clinician's plan is the best option, the clinician stops, and that is respect for autonomy. Restricting a patient's freedom against their will on the argument that they will be better off is paternalism, and pushing someone toward the course the clinician prefers serves neither autonomy nor beneficence.

preguntas.pregunta: What may a research consent form never contain?
opciones: Wording that releases the investigator from liability for negligence
Wording about whom to contact if the subject is injured by the research
Wording that the study may end without the subject's own agreement
Wording that identifiers may be stripped for later, unrelated studies
preguntas.explicacion: Exculpatory language is barred: no consent may make the subject waive, or seem to waive, legal rights, or release the investigator, sponsor or institution from liability for negligence. The other three belong in a form. A contact for research injury is a basic element, and early termination by the investigator and future use of de-identified material are additional elements.

preguntas.pregunta: Under which part of the disability law is a privately owned medical office covered?
opciones: Title III, which reaches businesses and non-profits that serve the public
Title I, which reaches employers with fifteen or more people on the payroll
Title II, which reaches the services and programmes of state and local government
Title IV, which reaches the companies that provide telephone and relay services
preguntas.explicacion: A private hospital or medical office is a place of public accommodation, and doctors' offices and hospitals are named among the businesses that serve the public. preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube was drawn to only 67 % of its nominal volume. According to the fill-level study cited in the rejection paper, which coagulation result remains relatively reliable at that fill?
opciones: Prothrombin time
Activated PTT
Fibrinogen level
Factor VIII level
preguntas.explicacion: Lippi and colleagues found a clinically significant bias once tubes fall below 89 % of total fill for aPTT, below 78 % for fibrinogen and below 67 % for factor VIII, whereas prothrombin time and activated protein C resistance stayed relatively reliable even at 67 % of nominal volume. The laboratory still sets its acceptance line at 80 %, so the practical answer is a redraw, but PT is the test least disturbed by the short fill.

Reporting either code, but never the two of them for the same encounter
Reporting the excluded code alone, since it takes the place of the other
Reporting both codes only when the record documents an inpatient stay

preguntas.pregunta: What must a person do in order to hold a registered nurse license?
opciones: Graduate from an approved nursing program and pass a qualifying examination
Complete a one-year vocational program and pass a competency examination
Earn a graduate degree and pass a national certification examination
Finish a training program and be certified by a professional association

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the lateral position often chosen for a pregnant patient who must lie down for a while?
opciones: It keeps the inferior vena cava from being compressed, so blood flow to the fetus holds up
It raises the pubic symphysis above the trunk, which increases the return of venous blood
It presses the abdominal contents upward, so that the diaphragm can move more freely
It lets the uterus rest against the table, so that fundal height can be measured better
preguntas.explicacion: Lying on one side with the top leg flexed over the bottom one takes pressure off the coccyx and, in pregnancy, keeps the weight of the uterus off the inferior vena cava so that blood keeps flowing to the fetus. Tilting the pubic symphysis to the highest point of the trunk is Trendelenburg, and pushing the abdomen into the diaphragm is what that position does wrong.

preguntas.pregunta: A remittance advice carries an adjustment that is not attached to any of the claims listed on it. How is that one explained?
