By a claim adjustment reason code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a remittance advice remark code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a claim adjustment group code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
preguntas.explicacion: Adjustments can fall at line, claim or provider level. Line and claim adjustments are explained by the group code, the reason code and the remark code together. A provider level adjustment usually has nothing to do with any particular claim on that remittance, and provider level balance reason codes carry it: interest added because Medicare paid a clean claim late, a deduction for an earlier overpayment, or an increase under an incentive plan.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has been told to connect early asks what she will see while she waits. What does the guidance say to describe for her?

A message telling her to ring the front desk so that she can be let in
A form she has to finish on screen before the video will start at all
A recorded message that reads out the practice's policy on cancelling appointments
preguntas.explicacion: Appointment setup guidance tells the office to describe what the patient will meet when she connects early, and names the virtual waiting room and hold music. preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the phases of wound healing occur?
opciones: Hemostasis, inflammatory, proliferative, maturation
Inflammatory, hemostasis, maturation, proliferative
Proliferative, hemostasis, inflammatory, maturation
Hemostasis, proliferative, inflammatory, maturation
preguntas.explicacion: Vessels constrict and clotting factors act first, which is hemostasis and lasts up to an hour depending on the injury. Vasodilation then lets white cells in to clean the bed, showing as swelling, redness and exudate. The proliferative phase brings epithelialization, angiogenesis, collagen and contraction, and maturation lays down more collagen for strength.

By joining a separate Medigap policy run by a private company
By asking the pharmacy to bill Part B for the drugs bought there
By enrolling in Part A, which adds drug coverage after the first year

Not less than 8 hours after the last alcoholic drink
Not less than 24 hours after alcohol, with no limit on food
Not less than 2 hours after any food or drink

Ask the visitors to stay at the bedside so that the patient feels supported
Keep the curtain open so that a colleague can observe the draw
Explain that privacy is not required for such a short procedure

preguntas.pregunta: Several staff members would normally each gather part of an older patient's history. What does the guidance advise?

Have each staff member ask again, so that errors are caught
Have the caregiver give the history so the patient can rest
Have the history taken from scratch again at every follow-up

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen was left uncapped on a sunny windowsill for two hours before dipping. Which two strip results are most likely to be falsely decreased?
opciones: Bilirubin and urobilinogen, which break down when exposed to light
Glucose and ketones, which evaporate from an uncovered container
Protein and specific gravity, which fall as the urine warms up
Nitrite and leukocyte esterase, which are consumed by bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: Bilirubin and urobilinogen are unstable when a specimen is exposed to light and warmth for a considerable time, so they decompose and the pads read falsely low. Room temperature also favors bacterial growth, which can produce a false-positive blood reaction and shift the pH. Glucose in the specimen may be metabolized by microorganisms, lowering the pH, but the light-sensitive pair is bilirubin and urobilinogen.

preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes the amount a person pays every month for their health insurance, whether or not they use any care?
opciones: Premium
Deductible
Copay
Network
preguntas.explicacion: The premium is the monthly price of the coverage itself, owed whether or not any service is used. HealthCare.gov adds that, on top of it, the patient usually pays other costs when care is actually received: a deductible, copayments and coinsurance. Its glossary describes a copay as a fixed amount per covered service, such as $30. The network is the set of contracted providers, not a payment at all.

Six months in which to switch, matching the Medigap open enrollment period
Thirty days in which to switch, after which the policy holds for the whole year
No right to switch, since every policy with the same letter is the same anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Some states also sell a kind of Medigap policy called Medicare SELECT, and a buyer of one has the right to change her mind within twelve months and move to a standard Medigap policy. 21 to 38 grams, against an actual average of about 30 grams
10 to 20 grams, against an actual average of about 16 grams
40 to 60 grams, against an actual average of about 30 grams

From the outside toward the centre, covering at least 2 cm
Back and forth over the vein until the skin looks clean
In one pass along the vein, from the tourniquet toward the hand

It is measured in the dominant arm and only that arm from then on
It is measured in one arm sitting and the other arm lying down
It is measured in the arm and again at the ankle for comparison
preguntas.explicacion: At the first evaluation the pressure is taken in both arms, because a difference between the two sides is itself a finding. Three readings, and the largest of the three is what gets recorded
Two readings, and the larger of the two is what gets recorded
One reading, taken after the joint has gone through its full range

Not to drink water for 3 hours and not to eat for 12 hours
Not to take any regular medicine on the day of the test

Both pay half of the allowed amount for each Medicare-covered service

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the bladder is very full and asks whether that matters. What is the effect?
opciones: A full bladder adds roughly 10 mm Hg, so the patient empties it before the reading
A full bladder lowers the reading by roughly 10 mm Hg through a vagal reflex

preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls the next day about a painful bruise at the puncture site. What first-aid advice applies to a bruise?
opciones: Ice wrapped in a towel for up to 15 minutes each hour, never directly on the skin, with the area raised above the heart
Ice placed directly on the skin for 30 minutes at a time, with the arm kept below the level of the heart
A warm compress for 15 minutes each hour and vigorous massage to disperse the pooled blood under the skin
A tight adhesive strip over the bruise for 24 hours, kept on until the colour turns greenish-yellow

preguntas.pregunta: What has to happen before a clinician begins a surgical hand antisepsis procedure?
opciones: Rings, watches and bracelets come off and the skin is inspected
The sterile gloves are opened and laid out on the sterile field
The antiseptic is poured into a basin and warmed to body heat
The nails are trimmed with the kit's clipper at the scrub sink
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation comes before the water: all jewelry, rings, watches and bracelets, is removed, and the hands and forearms are checked for cuts, abrasions or broken skin. Debris under the nails is removed with a nail cleaner under running water once the rinsing has started, and the sterile gloves go on only after the hands are dry.

preguntas.pregunta: An employee asks for a copy of her exposure record for the first time. What may the employer charge her?
opciones: Nothing for that first copy; a later request for another copy may be charged
A reasonable search and copying fee, since the record is the employer's own
No charge at any time, since copies of these records are free to employees
A flat administrative fee set by the employer and applied to every request
preguntas.explicacion: The employer has to provide the copy without cost, or lend the record so a copy can be made, or make copying facilities available free. Once a record has been provided without cost, reasonable, non-discriminatory administrative costs may be charged for further copies, except for a first request covering new information added since.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says a friend told him to cut carbohydrates out almost completely. What does the body do when carbohydrate is restricted that severely?
opciones: It shifts to burning fat for energy, a state called ketosis
It shifts to burning muscle protein first, a state called ketosis
It stores the fat that is eaten instead, a state called ketosis
It turns dietary fiber into glucose to keep blood levels steady
preguntas.explicacion: Cutting carbohydrate that far pushes the body into ketosis, where fat is used for energy because food is not supplying enough carbohydrate. The opposite excess matters too: too much processed, starchy or sugary carbohydrate raises total calories and can crowd out fat and protein. Fiber is never broken down for glucose.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Carbohydrates — Side Effects

preguntas.pregunta: An insurer's letter uses the word precertification. Which term means the same thing?
opciones: Prior authorization, another name the federal glossary gives the same decision
Predetermination, the plan's estimate of the dollars it expects to pay later
Coordination of benefits, the way payers settle which of them pays first
Assignment of benefits, the patient's permission to pay the office directly
preguntas.explicacion: The federal glossary lists prior authorization, prior approval and precertification as other names for preauthorization, the plan's decision that a service is medically necessary before it is delivered. Coordination of benefits sorts out the order in which two payers pay a claim, and assignment of benefits is a form the patient signs so the plan pays the office rather than the patient.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the Dietary Guidelines allow for added sugars. What is the limit for anyone age 2 and older?
opciones: Less than 10 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 20 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 15 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 5 percent of the calories eaten in a day
preguntas.explicacion: The fourth guideline caps added sugars below a tenth of daily calories from age 2 on, and tells caregivers to keep added sugars out of the diet entirely before that age. The 15 percent figure is what is left over after food group needs are met; 5 and 20 percent are the label's low and high marks for a nutrient, not a sugar limit.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three things does WHO step 2 have the worker ask about before positioning the patient?
opciones: Allergies, phobias, and fainting during earlier injections or draws
Allergies, medicines taken today, and fainting during earlier draws
Phobias, recent surgery, and fainting during earlier injections
Allergies, phobias, and the arm the patient prefers for the puncture
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 has the worker introduce themselves, ask the patient to state their full name, and check the laboratory form against that identity. Then comes the question of whether the patient has allergies, phobias, or has ever fainted during previous injections or blood draws. Only after that does the anxious patient get reassurance and the comfortable supine position.

preguntas.pregunta: An adult patient has a body mass index of 27.4. Which category is that?
opciones: Overweight, the band from 25.0 to 29.9
Healthy weight, the band from 18.5 to 29.9
Obesity class 1, the band from 25.0 to 34.9
Underweight, which covers everything below 30.0
preguntas.explicacion: For adults of 20 and over the bands are: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 healthy weight, 25.0 to 29.9 overweight, and 30.0 or more obesity. Obesity is then split further into class 1 at 30.0 to 34.9, class 2 at 35.0 to 39.9 and class 3, also called severe obesity, at 40.0 or more.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Adult BMI Calculator: BMI Category Ranges
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3

preguntas.pregunta: Why can heart muscle not be stimulated again right after a beat?
opciones: An absolute refractory period of about 200 ms stands in the way
An absolute refractory period of about 50 ms stands in the way
An absolute refractory period of about 500 ms stands in the way
An absolute refractory period of about 25 ms stands in the way
preguntas.explicacion: The absolute period runs about 200 ms and the relative one about 50 ms more, some 250 ms in all. That length is the point: the muscle has to finish contracting to move blood, and without it premature contractions would follow one another and life could not go on.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Membrane Potentials in Cardiac Contractile Cells
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: Which vein of the antecubital fossa does the WHO describe as usually the easiest to puncture, and why is the basilic vein riskier?
opciones: The median cubital vein, which lies between muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein
The basilic vein, between the muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the median cubital vein
The cephalic vein, since it is visible with no tourniquet; the basilic is where veins are diverting
Whichever vein already has a peripheral venous access in place; the basilic is too deep to reach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 of the guideline singles out the median cubital vein: it sits between muscles and is usually the easiest to puncture. The basilic vein has an artery and a nerve running beneath it, so a puncture there risks damaging one of them and tends to hurt more; swapping the two veins reverses the guideline. The same step warns against putting the needle in where veins branch, because that raises the chance of a haematoma, but it does not say that of the basilic vein, and it does not single out the cephalic vein at all. And in hospitalized patients it says NOT to draw from an existing peripheral venous access, because the result may be false.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement best describes the analytical phase of laboratory medicine compared with the rest of health care?
opciones: It performs close to 5 sigma, an error rate of about 0.002 %, among the best sectors in health care
It performs at 1 to 2 sigma, roughly the same level as health care as a whole
It produces four to five times more errors than the pre-analytical and post-analytical phases combined
It accounts for 46 to 68 % of all laboratory errors because of instrument malfunction
preguntas.explicacion: The analytical work of the laboratory reaches nearly 5 sigma, about 0.002 %, more than 3,000 times lower than infection and medication error rates, which is why it is called the best-performing sector in health care; health care overall sits at 1 to 2 sigma. It is the extra-analytical phases that carry four to five times more errors, and the 46 to 68 % share belongs to the pre-pre-analytical phase.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: After a visit, the office sends the insurer a request for payment for the services provided. What is that request called?
opciones: A claim
A copay
A referral
A denial
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a claim as the request for payment that the patient or the provider sends to the insurer for items or services believed to be covered. It comes AFTER the care. A copay is the fixed amount the patient pays for a covered service, a referral is the primary care doctor's written order to see a specialist, and a denial is an answer the plan gives, not a request the office sends.

preguntas.pregunta: What is described as perhaps the most important step in recovering from a service failure?
opciones: Letting the person tell the story and vent the frustration
Handing the person a written apology signed by a manager
Offering a free service to make up for what went wrong
Explaining the process that let the failure happen at all
preguntas.explicacion: Recovery is psychological as well as physical, and the step that matters most is listening while the person tells their story and describes what the failure cost them. Work in a spirit of partnership toward the fix, though not by opening with a question about what they want you to do about it.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P The Axioms of Service Recovery

preguntas.pregunta: At what frequency does CLIA require a laboratory to calibrate a test system?
opciones: Following the manufacturer's instructions, at least as often as the manufacturer recommends
Once every 6 months, using the same three-level materials that calibration verification uses
Every day that patient specimens are assayed, before the first control material is run
Whenever a newly trained operator begins to run patient testing on the instrument
preguntas.explicacion: Calibration follows the manufacturer's test system instructions, with the calibration materials it provides or specifies and at least at the frequency it recommends, using criteria the laboratory has verified. It is also repeated whenever calibration verification fails the laboratory's acceptable limits. The 6-month cycle is for verification, and daily runs and new operators are quality control triggers.

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must appear on a written consent to disclose substance use disorder records?
opciones: A description of each purpose for which the disclosure is being made
A notarized signature witnessed by two members of the program staff
A statement that the consent cannot be revoked before it expires
A copy of the recipient's own privacy notice attached to the form
preguntas.explicacion: The written consent, on paper or electronic, must carry the patient's name, who is authorized to disclose, a specific description of the information, the recipient, a description of each purpose, how the patient may revoke it, an expiration date or event, the signature and the date. Revocation is a required element, not something the form can waive.
preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(1) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: Which managed care plan lets the member choose between the HMO and the PPO arrangement each time care is needed?
opciones: A point-of-service plan, which keeps the choice open at each visit
A preferred provider organization, which pays more inside the network
A health maintenance organization, which pays for network care only
An accountable care organization, which shares the savings it earns
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of managed care plan are named. A health maintenance organization usually pays only for network care and asks the member to pick a primary care doctor. A preferred provider organization usually pays more inside the network and still covers part of the cost outside it. A point-of-service plan lets the member choose between an HMO and a PPO each time care is needed.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Managed Care: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: How does a tort differ from a crime?
opciones: A tort is a private wrong and aims to compensate; a crime wrongs society
A tort is heard by a jury and a crime is decided by a judge alone
A tort applies to institutions and a crime applies only to individuals
A tort is defined by state statute and a crime only by federal statute
preguntas.explicacion: Crimes are wrongs against the state or society at large, and criminal liability exists to enforce public justice. Tort law deals with private wrongs, and its central purpose is compensating the victim rather than punishing the wrongdoer. The same act can be both: gross negligence that endangers other people's lives can be a tort and a crime at once.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: tort (Distinguishing Torts)
preguntas.subtema: Civil and criminal acts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4 · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: A baby's head circumference is growing much faster than expected. Why does the provider follow it up?
opciones: Faster than normal head growth can be a sign of problems such as fluid on the brain
Faster than normal head growth is the earliest sign that the child is overweight
Faster than normal head growth is expected only in children born after 40 weeks
Faster than normal head growth is measured only to fix the size of a helmet later
preguntas.explicacion: A head larger than normal or growing faster than normal can point to several problems, hydrocephalus among them, while a very small head or very slow growth may mean the brain is not developing as it should. That is why the measurement belongs to routine well-baby care rather than being taken only when something looks wrong.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Head circumference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: Which categories of blood sampling are singled out as requiring specialist training?
opciones: Arterial gases on ventilated patients, neonatal sampling and capillary sampling
Routine adult venous draws, cross-match sampling and coagulation sampling
Arterial gases on ventilated patients, adult venous draws and donor collection
Neonatal sampling, adult venous draws and blood collection for transfusion
preguntas.explicacion: Most sampling is done for ordinary laboratory testing, but three categories are listed as needing specialist training: arterial blood gases in patients on mechanical ventilation, neonatal and paediatric sampling by heel-prick or scalp vein, and capillary sampling at any age.

preguntas.pregunta: What is an electronic remittance advice?
opciones: The plan's explanation to the provider of how a claim's charges were adjusted and paid
The plan's explanation to the patient of what the visit cost and what remains to be paid
The provider's electronic request for payment sent to the plan after the visit
The bank message that moves the plan's payment into the provider's account
preguntas.explicacion: An electronic remittance advice explains to the provider how the health plan adjusted the charges on a claim, taking account of contract terms, secondary payers, benefit coverage and expected copayments and coinsurance. The document sent to the patient is the explanation of benefits or, in Original Medicare, the summary notice; the request for payment is the claim; and the money itself moves by electronic funds transfer.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks how a filled additive tube should be moved to mix it. Which pattern is described?
opciones: Inverting the tube in a figure-of-8 pattern
Rolling the tube between both palms briskly
Shaking the tube eight to ten times in a row
Inverting it once and standing it in the rack
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant need enough mixing, and the movement described is inversion following a figure-of-8. Overmixing can produce haemolysis and inefficient mixing leaves small clots, so neither brisk shaking nor a single inversion serves. Eight to ten mixes is the figure given for culture bottles.

preguntas.pregunta: How long is a CLIA Certificate of Waiver effective, and what must the site do to keep it?
opciones: Two years; pay the waiver fee and renew every two years
One year; pay the waiver fee and renew every year
Five years; renew after a routine survey by the state agency
Indefinitely, as long as ownership does not change
preguntas.explicacion: All CLIA certificate types are generally effective for two years. A site with a Certificate of Waiver or a PPM certificate pays only a waiver or PPM fee on that two-year cycle, with no registration or compliance survey fees. Renewal does not depend on an inspection, because waived sites are not subject to routine surveys, but the certificate must be kept current.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient stays overnight in the hospital after a doctor writes an order admitting her. How is that stay classified?
opciones: Inpatient care, because a doctor's order admitted the patient to the hospital as an inpatient
Outpatient hospital service, the category that covers observation and same-day surgery
Skilled nursing facility care, which also supplies a semi-private room, meals and nursing
Long-term custodial care, the help with daily living given in chronic illness or disability
preguntas.explicacion: Inpatient care is what a person receives once admitted as an inpatient to a facility such as a hospital or a skilled nursing home. Two conditions apply: a doctor orders the admission because inpatient treatment is needed, and the hospital takes Medicare. Observation and same-day surgery are paid instead as outpatient hospital services.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC say that aspiration is not needed before a vaccine is injected?
opciones: The vessels near the recommended sites are too small to take a push of vaccine
The vaccine does no harm if it enters a vein, so the check adds no safety here
Aspiration is skipped only when the site chosen for the vaccine is the deltoid
Aspiration is replaced by injecting slowly, which does the same job more gently
preguntas.explicacion: Aspiration was recommended originally for theoretical reasons and has never been evaluated scientifically. The veins and arteries a needle can reach at the sites recommended for vaccination are too small to allow an intravenous push without blowing the vessel out. Aspirating also adds pain, through longer needle dwell time and the shearing of tissue; injecting rapidly without it hurt infants less in one study.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 6: Inject Vaccines Rapidly Without Aspiration

preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the blood filling the tube is dark red rather than bright red. What does that color indicate?
opciones: Venous blood carrying deoxyhemoglobin, which is a darker red
Arterial blood carrying oxyhemoglobin, which is bright red
Hemolyzed blood in which hemoglobin has left the red cells
Blood with a high hematocrit from living at high altitude
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin is a pigment whose color depends on oxygen: freshly oxygenated blood is bright red, and blood that has given up oxygen in the tissues is a duskier, darker red. Oxyhemoglobin is the bright red form and deoxyhemoglobin the darker form. Dark red is therefore the expected color of venous blood, not a sign of hemolysis or of a high hematocrit.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood

preguntas.pregunta: A retractable safety needle is activated after the draw. What has to be true of the sharp afterwards?
opciones: It is fully retracted within the housing of the device
It is fully covered by a cap held on with adhesive tape
It is bent back on itself so it cannot be straightened
It is left partly visible so the worker can confirm it fired
preguntas.explicacion: For a retractable design the recommendation is that the sharp ends up fully retracted inside the housing. That sits alongside two rules for every design: the user should be able to tell easily that the feature has fired, and once fired it cannot be undone and stays protective through disposal.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is about to take a history through a medical interpreter. Which practice applies?
opciones: Speaking in the first person and keeping idioms out of it
Speaking in the third person so the meaning stays clear
Grouping several questions so the exchange moves faster
Shortening the visit, since two people now do the talking
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines say to speak in the first person, to avoid idioms, abbreviations, slang, jokes and jargon, to use short sentences and ask one question at a time, and to let the interpreter finish before starting the next topic. Extra time is set aside for these visits rather than cut, and questions are never stacked.

preguntas.pregunta: When is allergen immunotherapy indicated?
opciones: When an IgE-mediated reaction is shown and matches the patient's symptoms
When the patient reports symptoms, whether or not IgE testing is positive
When IgE testing is positive, even if exposure and symptoms do not match
When an antihistamine has failed, as the next step for any allergic disease
preguntas.explicacion: Immunotherapy is indicated for moderate to severe allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, allergic conjunctivitis, atopic dermatitis, IgE-mediated food allergy and insect allergy with significant local reactions or anaphylaxis, but only where an IgE-mediated reaction is demonstrated and correlates with the clinical picture. A negative specific IgE, or a positive test that does not match exposure and symptoms, predicts failure.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is charting about a patient who gets around in a wheelchair. Which phrasing follows people-first language?

A wheelchair-bound patient
A person confined to a wheelchair
A handicapped person in a wheelchair
preguntas.explicacion: People-first language puts the person ahead of the disability, using constructions such as a person who or a person with, and it promotes understanding, dignity and respect. preguntas.pregunta: Ideally, how long should urine have been held in the bladder before a clean-catch sample for culture is collected?
opciones: About 2 to 3 hours
At least 1 hour
At least 8 hours
About 15 to 20 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Both the clean-catch instructions and the urine culture instructions ask, when possible, for urine that has been in the bladder for 2 to 3 hours. One hour is the minimum wait before a catheterized specimen or a urethral swab, and 15 to 20 minutes is how long before a catheterization a patient may be told to drink a glass of water if there is no urge to void. preguntas.pregunta: Two further drawbacks are listed for auto-disable syringes in a blood-drawing context. Which are they?

The mechanism cannot be reset, and the needle is too short for adult veins
The mechanism can trip while probing, and the barrel cannot hold two tubes
The mechanism jams when cold, and air in the syringe dilutes the additive
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond the fact that this device is designed against reuse rather than against needle-sticks, the table warns that the safety mechanism can be activated while the worker is probing, forcing a fresh venepuncture, and that air in the syringe can affect test results. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given a guaiac card kit for occult blood at home. How are the samples taken?
opciones: From several areas of the stool, repeated on three separate days
From one area of a single stool, repeated only if the result is positive
From several areas of the stool, all taken from one bowel movement
From the toilet water below the stool, on three consecutive mornings
preguntas.explicacion: Bleeding into the gut is intermittent and blood is not spread evenly through stool, so the sample is taken from more than one spot and the collection repeated over three separate days. The stool must not touch toilet water first, because hemoglobin leaches out of it and bowl sanitizers interfere. Dried cards keep at room temperature for up to 14 days.

preguntas.pregunta: What does closing the door or the curtain before an interview demonstrate?
opciones: Respect for privacy, and it holds down interruptions
Compliance with the personal zone of 18 inches to four feet
A check-back that confirms the patient heard the question
Cultural negotiation over who may stay in the room
preguntas.explicacion: Respecting privacy and minimizing interruptions is listed as a technique in its own right: depending on the setting, close the door or draw the curtain. The personal zone is a proxemics measurement, a check-back confirms a message between staff, and cultural negotiation settles competing care needs.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a general sense rather than a special sense?
opciones: Somatosensation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Gustation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Olfaction, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Equilibrium, whose receptors are spread through many organs
preguntas.explicacion: The special senses each have their own organ: taste, smell, hearing, balance and vision. Somatosensation is a general sense instead, a group of modalities including pressure, vibration, light touch, temperature, pain and proprioception, and its receptors sit in skin, muscles, tendons, joints and the walls of the viscera.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Somatosensation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12

preguntas.pregunta: What does the chain of custody document for a forensic specimen?
opciones: Its continuity of possession from collection through to the courtroom
The analytical methods each laboratory used to examine the specimen
The consent the patient gave before the specimen was ever collected
The storage temperature the specimen was held at while in the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The chain of custody is the continuity of possession of a piece of evidence and of its movement and location, from the point of discovery and recovery, through transport to the laboratory, until it is admitted in court. It exists to assure the court that what is examined is the same material that was seized and that it was never unaccounted for. Storage conditions are recorded within it, not instead of it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Definition/Introduction
