preguntas.pregunta: An enema is about to be given. Which description matches the position asked for?
opciones: Halfway between supine and prone, legs flexed and a pillow under the top leg
Flat on the back with a small pillow supporting the head and both of the knees
Sitting up with the head of the bed raised and the hips slightly flexed
On one side with the top leg crossed over the bottom one and arms forward
preguntas.explicacion: Sims is the side-lying position placed between supine and prone: the legs are flexed, a pillow goes under the upper leg, and the arms rest beside the patient rather than trapped underneath. It is the position used for an enema and it also serves for anal procedures. Plain lateral, by contrast, keeps the top leg simply flexed over the bottom one.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Sims Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(6) · RMA III.F.2.a.i · NCMA 2B.9

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO procedure, at what point is the tourniquet applied in relation to finding the vein?
opciones: After a vein is located that is visible without it; it is then applied and the vein re-examined
Before looking for any vein, so that all the veins stay engorged during the whole of the inspection
Only if no vein is visible after the site has been disinfected and allowed to dry
Immediately after the needle enters, to keep the vein distended while the tubes fill
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says the vein should be visible without applying the tourniquet, that locating it helps decide the needle size, and that the tourniquet is then applied four to five finger widths above the site and the vein examined again. Disinfection is Step 5 and comes after the site is chosen; and the tourniquet is in place before the needle enters, not applied afterwards.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection and tourniquet · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9

preguntas.pregunta: A vaccine has just been administered. Where do the used syringe and the empty vial go?
opciones: The syringe into a sharps container; the vial into medical waste per state rules
Both into the sharps container, since the vial held a parenteral product as well
The syringe into a sharps container; the vial into the ordinary office wastebasket
Both into medical waste, once the needle has been recapped and taken off the barrel
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe and needle go straight into a sharps container with the safety shield applied and without recapping, because recapping is how needlestick injuries happen. Empty or expired vaccine vials count as medical waste and are disposed of according to state regulations, with the state or local immunization program or environmental agency as the source of any further guidance.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: After the Visit, Vaccine and Supply Disposal; Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.j · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: Which cost may a practice include in the fee it charges a patient for a copy of her record?
opciones: The labor of copying the information, plus postage when she asks to have it mailed
The time staff spend searching for and retrieving the chart from the storage room
The share of the electronic system's annual license attributable to storing her data
The cost of verifying her identity and documenting the request in the practice log
preguntas.explicacion: The fee has to be reasonable and cost based, and only four components may go into it: labor for copying, whether on paper or electronically; supplies such as a CD or USB drive if portable media are requested; postage where the copy is mailed; and preparing an explanation or summary if the patient agreed to one. Verification, documentation, search and retrieval, and system maintenance may not be charged, even where state law allows it.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Fees for Copies
preguntas.subtema: Access fees · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which information is excluded from the HIPAA right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a legal proceeding
Laboratory results, which belong to the ordering physician until released
Billing records, which are financial rather than clinical
Records older than 6 years, which need not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access in 164.524(a)(1) covers PHI in a designated record set for as long as it is kept, with two exceptions: psychotherapy notes, and information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal or administrative proceeding. Access may also be denied without review in limited cases such as certain correctional and research situations, and with a right to review when a licensed professional judges that access is likely to endanger someone. Laboratory and billing records are part of the designated record set and remain accessible.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(a)(1)-(4), Standard: Access to protected health information
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to access · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is listed as an exception to a patient's confidentiality rights?
opciones: Sharing what is needed to head off imminent danger to someone
Sharing a diagnosis with a coworker who asks out of concern
Sharing a chart with a relative who is not involved in the care
Sharing a record with a magazine once the name is left out
preguntas.explicacion: The exceptions are named and narrow: sharing within the organization or with its business partners for medical, revenue, quality or risk management purposes; to head off imminent physical danger to the patient or to others; to assist a criminal investigation when a law official demands it; to preserve public health, which is why certain infections are reportable; and to communicate with a surrogate when the patient lacks the legal capacity to decide. Concern for a colleague's patient is not on the list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Health Information Privacy and Control
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: Where does an intramuscular vaccine go in a 4-month-old infant, and with which needle?
opciones: Vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh, with a 1-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle
Vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh, with a 5/8-inch 23 to 25 gauge needle
Deltoid muscle of the arm, with a 5/8-inch to 1-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle
Ventrogluteal site, with a 1 to 1.25-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle, thigh in reserve
preguntas.explicacion: For infants from 1 to 12 months the intramuscular site is the vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh and the needle is 1 inch, 22 to 25 gauge. A neonate of 28 days or younger takes five eighths of an inch at the same site. The deltoid becomes the preferred site from 3 years onward, and 5/8 of an inch with 23 to 25 gauge is the subcutaneous needle at every age.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: During the Visit, Needle Length and Gauge Charts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(1) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is 155,000 per microliter. Is that typical, and where is about a third of the body's platelets kept?
opciones: Yes, typical is 150,000 to 160,000 per µL; about a third is held in the spleen
Yes, typical is 150,000 to 160,000 per µL; about a third is held in the liver
No, typical is 5,000 to 10,000 per µL; about a third is held in the spleen
No, typical is 2,000 to 3,000 per µL; about a third is held in the red marrow
preguntas.explicacion: A typical platelet count is 150,000 to 160,000 per microliter, so 155,000 fits. After entering the circulation, about one third of the platelets migrate to the spleen, where they are stored and released when a vessel ruptures. The 5,000 to 10,000 figure is the leukocyte count, and 2000 to 3000 is the number of platelets one megakaryocyte releases in its lifetime.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: In an acute hemorrhage with no time to cross match, type O negative blood is transfused. Why is O negative called the universal donor?
opciones: Its cells lack A, B and Rh D antigens, so recipient antibodies do not react
Its plasma lacks anti-A and anti-B, so it cannot agglutinate any cells
Its cells carry both A antigen and B antigen, matching every recipient
It is the most common type, so it is the one always kept in stock
preguntas.explicacion: Type O erythrocytes display neither A nor B antigen, so the anti-A or anti-B antibodies in the recipient's plasma find nothing on the donated cells to attack, and Rh negative cells also lack the D antigen. One caution: type O plasma does carry anti-A and anti-B, but the transfused volume is small compared with the recipient's own blood, so the effect is usually limited.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, ABO Transfusion Protocols
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: What must the employer's written cleaning and decontamination schedule take into account?
opciones: The location, the kind of surface, the soil present, and the tasks done there
The brand of disinfectant and the date its container was first opened
The number of employees on each shift and the dates of their training
The volume of regulated waste the area produced during the past year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(i) makes the employer keep the worksite clean and sanitary, and then requires a written schedule for cleaning and a method of decontamination decided from four things: where in the facility the area is, what kind of surface has to be cleaned, what kind of soil is on it, and which tasks or procedures are performed there. A draw room and a storage corridor therefore do not get the same schedule. Disinfectant brands, staffing and waste volume are not the criteria the paragraph names.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(i), Housekeeping: General
preguntas.subtema: Written cleaning schedule · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5 · RMA III.A.4 III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO describe the order of draw for skin-puncture (capillary) specimens compared with venipuncture?
opciones: It is the reverse: haematology first, then chemistry and blood bank
It is the same: culture first, then coagulation, then the additive tubes
It is the reverse: chemistry and blood bank first, then haematology
It has no fixed order, because microtubes hold too little for carry-over
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.3 says that with skin punctures the haematology specimen is taken first, followed by chemistry and blood bank, and that this is the reverse of the venipuncture order. The reason given is to limit the effect of platelet clumping. The same section adds that when more than two specimens are needed, venipuncture may give more accurate results.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.3, Order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw, capillary vs venous · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.H.2 · CCMA 3E6 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reuses the same elastic tourniquet all morning without cleaning it. Why is that a problem?
opciones: Tourniquets have been found carrying hospital-acquired bacteria
Tourniquets lose their elasticity after several patients in a row
Tourniquets absorb the alcohol used to prepare the puncture site
Tourniquets have to be discarded after each patient is finished
preguntas.explicacion: Best practice for the tourniquet is a clean elastic band that is reprocessed between patients, and the reason given is direct: contamination with nosocomial bacteria has been documented on tourniquets, so one that travels from arm to arm carries them along. The related warning is that a latex glove must not be used as a tourniquet on a patient with a history of latex allergy.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Safe blood-sampling equipment, Tourniquet
preguntas.subtema: Cleaning the tourniquet · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k104 · CMA I.B.5 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee reviews a one-year audit of an emergency laboratory that received 453,171 specimens. Which test group carried the highest rejection ratio?
opciones: Coagulation testing, rejected at about 13 % of what arrived
Blood gas analyses, rejected at about 10 % of everything arriving
Urine analyses, rejected at about 9 % of what arrived
Biochemistry testing, rejected at about 3 % of what arrived
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation led that audit at 13.3 %, with therapeutic drug monitoring close behind at 12.8 % and hormone testing around 12 %. Blood gases reached 9.8 % and urine 9.2 %, while biochemistry at 2.5 % and the complete blood count at 3.2 % were the least affected. Coagulation suffers most because red cell clots and a wrong blood-to-anticoagulant ratio are exactly what ruin a citrate tube.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory audits its identification errors and finds that most of them share one feature. Based on a seven-year study of preanalytical errors, which feature is that?
opciones: The sample carried fewer than two patient identifiers
The barcode had been printed for a different test panel
The sample had been labeled after arriving in the laboratory
The requisition and the tube listed different collection times
preguntas.explicacion: In the laboratory that measured its preanalytical quality indicators, identification problems were the second most frequent error, and most of them consisted of a label with fewer than two identifiers; in newborns the rate was ten times higher because the small tubes leave little room to write two. Wrong panels, late labeling and time mismatches are other errors, not the one that dominated.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A prescription is filled by a compounding pharmacy. What should the patient be told about the product?
opciones: It is not FDA approved, so the agency did not review it before marketing
It is FDA approved under the same pathway used for any generic medicine
It is FDA approved only when an outsourcing facility prepares the mixture
It is exempt from any oversight, since a licensed pharmacist prepared it
preguntas.explicacion: Compounding is a licensed pharmacist or physician, or someone supervised by a pharmacist in an outsourcing facility, combining, mixing or altering ingredients to make a medication for an individual patient's needs. Compounded drugs are not FDA approved, so the agency does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are marketed. They meet real medical needs and they also carry risks.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Human Drug Compounding: Drug Compounding
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k86

preguntas.pregunta: A nine-month-old lifts a cloth to find the toy hidden under it. Which achievement is that?
opciones: Object permanence, which closes the sensorimotor period
Conservation, an achievement of the concrete operations
Semiotic function, the mark of the preoperational period
Hypothetical thought, which belongs to formal operations
preguntas.explicacion: The sensorimotor period runs from birth through the first 18 to 24 months and culminates in object permanence: knowing that objects exist apart from the child's own contact with them. Recovering a hidden toy, or knowing a parent still exists after leaving the room, are the classic examples.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Piaget", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · RMA I.D.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: How is a wet mount prepared, and how does it differ from a fixed preparation?
opciones: The specimen goes into a drop of liquid under a coverslip and stays alive, while fixing kills it
The specimen goes into a drop of liquid under a coverslip and is killed, while fixing keeps it alive
The specimen is smeared and heated, then a coverslip is added over a drop of immersion oil
The specimen is placed dry on the slide and a coverslip holds it down without any liquid
preguntas.explicacion: A wet mount is the simplest preparation: the specimen sits in a drop of liquid, water or a stain, and a coverslip goes on top. Some specimens, such as a drop of urine, are already liquid; a solid one like a skin scraping goes on first and the liquid after. Fixing, by heat or by a chemical such as formalin, attaches the cells to the slide and kills the organisms while preserving their structures.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 2.4 Staining Microscopic Specimens, Preparing Specimens for Light Microscopy
preguntas.subtema: Wet mount versus fixation · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.e-f (8.e desde 2027) · RMA III.C.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which reading is usually described as hypotension in an adult?
opciones: Under 90 systolic or under 60 diastolic, read together with the symptoms
Under 100 systolic or under 70 diastolic, read together with the symptoms
Under 120 systolic or under 80 diastolic, which is the lower limit of normal
Under 80 systolic alone, since the diastolic value carries no weight here
preguntas.explicacion: There is no universal cut-off, but clinicians commonly speak of hypotension below 90 systolic or below 60 diastolic. The diagnosis leans on the context and the symptoms: light-headedness, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea and weakness. Dehydration, acute illness and medicines are the usual causes.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: Before home health services are certified for a patient, what has to happen?
opciones: A provider assesses the patient face to face and orders care from a certified agency
A hospice physician meets the patient face to face and recertifies the prognosis
The patient completes three days as an inpatient in a hospital that accepts Medicare
The agency files a claim so that the contractor can decide medical necessity in advance
preguntas.explicacion: A health care provider, a nurse practitioner for example, must assess the patient face to face before certifying the need for home health. A provider has to order the care and a Medicare-certified home health agency has to deliver it. The three-day inpatient stay belongs to skilled nursing coverage and the recertified prognosis to hospice.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Provider requirements
preguntas.subtema: Coordinating home health · CCMA 4E · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the light grey top tube (sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate) the usual choice for a glucose specimen?
opciones: Its antiglycolytic additive keeps the glucose level stable for days
Its gel separator keeps the plasma away from the cells after spinning
Its clot activator produces serum faster than a plain red top tube
Its broth mixture keeps microorganisms alive until they can be cultured
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table describes the additive of the grey tube as an antiglycolytic agent, that is, one that blocks the breakdown of glucose, and says it keeps the glucose value stable for up to five days. Glucose is the use the table gives for it, with a note that it needs a full draw because a short draw may cause haemolysis. Gel separators belong to the serum separator and PST tubes, the clot activator to the red top, and the broth to the blood culture bottle.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through a suture removal the wound edges begin to gape. What is done?
opciones: Stop removing, apply Steri-Strips to pull the edges together, and notify the provider
Remove the rest quickly, since a partly sutured line pulls unevenly on the wound edges
Stop removing, cover the line with a dry sterile dressing, and reassess in seven days
Remove the rest and close the gap with a skin adhesive, then dress the line as usual
preguntas.explicacion: Open edges mean the removal stops there. Steri-Strips are cut and applied with tension so they draw the edges back together, and the provider is notified. The wound line is watched for separation the whole time the sutures are coming out, and the procedure is halted at any concern, because dehiscence is what removing them too early causes.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.10 Checklist for Intermittent Suture Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16

preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks which abilities are typical during the first year. Which set fits that age?
opciones: Social smile, rolling over, sitting alone and pulling up to stand
Skipping, drawing a circle and catching a bounced ball
Riding a bicycle, reading first words and doing things independently
Saying a first and last name, pedaling a tricycle and dressing with help
preguntas.explicacion: Within the first year an infant usually drinks from a cup, sits without support, babbles, smiles socially, gets a first tooth, plays peek-a-boo, pulls up to stand, rolls over and walks holding onto furniture. The other lists belong to the toddler and preschool years. These are general patterns, not precise guidelines: children move at different paces.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Developmental Milestones Record (Medical Encyclopedia)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.a and I.C.6.b (2027 I.C.6.a)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient rates his incision pain a 7 and is due for discharge teaching. What should happen first?
opciones: Give the ordered pain relief, then start the teaching
Give the teaching quickly so the patient can rest sooner
Have the patient sign the instruction sheet, then teach
Wait for the sedative given earlier to take full effect
preguntas.explicacion: Pain is a physiological barrier: a patient in pain is less likely to hear and remember, so relief is provided before teaching. Sedatives and some pain medicines impair the ability to receive and perceive a message, which is why health care documents are not signed after they are given.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i

preguntas.pregunta: Which identifiers are acceptable for confirming the right patient before a medication is administered?
opciones: The full name, the date of birth, or the identification number the facility assigns
The room number and the bed letter, both of which the chart lists on admission
The full name on its own, since two patients never share a name on one unit
The barcode scan on its own, which was brought in to replace two identifiers
preguntas.explicacion: Acceptable identifiers include the patient's full name, an identification number assigned by the facility, and the date of birth, confirmed against the wristband, an identification card, the patient's own statement where possible, or another method the policy allows. A room number is never used, because patients move. Barcode scanning adds a layer of safety but does not replace the requirement for two identifiers.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Right Patient
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5

preguntas.pregunta: A digital thermometer has just been used on one patient and is picked up for the next. What has to happen before that second reading?
opciones: The device is reset to a value below 35 °C (95 °F) before the new measurement
The device is left to cool for five minutes so the sensor returns to room level
The device is calibrated against a glass thermometer at least once every shift
The device is switched to the rectal setting, which resets the display to zero
preguntas.explicacion: A digital thermometer holds the last value it read. Before each new measurement it is reset below 35 °C (95 °F), otherwise the retained figure can be mistaken for the new patient's temperature. Waiting for the sensor to cool is not the instruction, and these devices are not calibrated against a glass probe at the bedside.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature a

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of a universal goniometer is laid over the joint together with the body and can be tightened to hold the moving arm still?
opciones: The fulcrum, the screw at the centre of the body of the instrument
The stationary arm, which lines up with the fixed part of the joint
The moving arm, which lines up with the part of the joint that moves
The scale of the body, which is read once both arms are lined up
preguntas.explicacion: A universal goniometer comes in three parts: a body shaped like a protractor and carrying the scale, a fulcrum, and the two arms. The fulcrum is a screw in the middle of the body; tightening it fixes the moving arm in one position and loosening it lets the arm swing. It is the fulcrum and the body that go over the joint.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Goniometer", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.c · RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62

preguntas.pregunta: How far from the floor, the ceiling and the outside walls should sterile supplies be stored?
opciones: 8 to 10 inches from the floor, 5 from the ceiling and 2 from the outside walls
2 to 4 inches from the floor, 8 from the ceiling and 5 from the outside walls
12 to 18 inches from the floor, 2 from the ceiling and 8 from the outside walls
5 to 8 inches from the floor, 18 from the ceiling and 10 from the outside walls
preguntas.explicacion: The clearances exist for air circulation, ease of cleaning and local fire codes: 8 to 10 inches up from the floor, 5 inches down from the ceiling and 2 inches away from outside walls, with supplies kept at least 18 inches below any sprinkler head. Twelve to eighteen inches is the separation used for furniture from the walls when a sterile field is being set up.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Storage
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a culture where health decisions are made collectively hesitates to sign a consent form. What is the culturally aware reading of that?
opciones: Written consent may be seen as a sign of mistrust; the process should allow for the family's role
Hesitation to sign means the patient lacks capacity and a surrogate must be sought
The patient is refusing care and the refusal should be documented at once
The form must be signed regardless, since the signature is the legal proof of consent
preguntas.explicacion: In certain cultures decisions are made collectively rather than by an individual signature, written consent may be perceived as a sign of mistrust, and the process may involve consulting a family patriarch or a designated male representative; undocumented immigrants may also fear signing. Cultural sensitivity is part of the consent process, and the emphasis on the signature as proof of understanding is itself being questioned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Cultural Differences
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A 2F k17 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician cannot find a pulse on the top of a patient's foot but finds every other pulse. What is one explanation?
opciones: That pulse is missing in roughly 10% of people because of anatomical variation
That pulse is missing in roughly 10% of people because of arterial stiffening with age
That pulse is felt only while the patient holds the first toe fully extended
That pulse disappears whenever systolic pressure falls below 100 mm Hg in the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The dorsalis pedis lies on the front of the foot, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus, and it is absent in about 10% of people for anatomical reasons. Asking the patient to extend the big toe lifts the tendon and helps find it when it is there. When pedal pulses are felt on both sides, peripheral arterial disease is unlikely.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A woman has pendulous breast tissue sitting over the V4 landmark. What is done?
opciones: The electrode goes on its landmark, even on top of the breast
The electrode goes below the breast, off its usual landmark
The breast is taped upward so the electrode sits on the wall
The electrode is left off and the tracing runs on five leads
preguntas.explicacion: The breasts are allowed to fall naturally, and the chest electrodes are placed on their landmarks even when that means placing one over breast tissue: correct position counts for more than closeness to the chest wall. The patient must stay very still so the tissue does not shift the electrode.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k150 k151 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2

preguntas.pregunta: About how far above the intended puncture site is the tourniquet applied, measured in inches?
opciones: About 3 inches above the site
About 1 inch above the site
About 6 inches above the puncture site
About 2 cm above the site
preguntas.explicacion: A preferably disposable tourniquet goes almost 3 inches above the targeted venipuncture site, tight enough to stop venous flow while arterial flow continues. The WHO expresses the same distance as four to five finger widths. Two centimetres is the minimum area the alcohol swab must cover in the WHO's Step 5, not a tourniquet distance.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (tourniquet application)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9

preguntas.pregunta: When does an exercise stress test come to an end?
opciones: At the target rate, or on symptoms or worrying tracing changes
At the target rate alone, no matter what the patient reports
After a fixed 20 minutes on the treadmill in every case
When the systolic pressure has climbed by 10 mm Hg or more
preguntas.explicacion: The test runs until the target heart rate is reached, or until chest pain or a worrying blood pressure change appears, or the tracing suggests the heart muscle is short of oxygen, or the patient is too tired or has leg pain. A rising pressure with each stage is the expected response, not a reason to stop.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Exercise stress test
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is frightened because a child's fever reached 40 °C (104 °F) and fears brain damage. What does the evidence show?
opciones: Brain damage is not expected below 42 °C (107.6 °F), a level infection rarely reaches
Brain damage begins above 40 °C (104 °F), which is why a reading that high is an emergency
Brain damage depends on how long the fever lasts, not on the temperature reached
Brain damage follows any febrile seizure, so a seizure with fever means lasting harm
preguntas.explicacion: Damage to the brain is not expected from fever unless the temperature climbs above 42 °C (107.6 °F), and untreated fevers from infection seldom pass 40.6 °C (105 °F) except when the child is bundled up or kept somewhere hot. Most febrile seizures are over quickly and leave no lasting harm.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: At what concentration in water are ethyl and isopropyl alcohol most bactericidal?
opciones: 60 to 90 percent
30 to 50 percent
95 to 100 percent
40 to 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohols work by denaturing protein, and protein denatures faster with water present, so absolute alcohol is weaker than a mixture. The optimum band runs from 60 to 90 percent in water, and cidal activity drops sharply once the solution is diluted below 50 percent. They are rapidly bactericidal, tuberculocidal, fungicidal and virucidal, but never sporicidal.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Alcohol: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: A collection agency working the practice's old accounts telephones a patient at seven in the morning. What does the statute presume?
opciones: That a convenient hour runs from eight in the morning to nine at night, where she is
That a convenient hour runs from nine in the morning to eight at night, where she is
That any hour suits until the consumer says otherwise to the collector in writing
That any hour suits once the collector has sent the written validation of the debt
preguntas.explicacion: A debt collector may not communicate with a consumer at an unusual time or place, or one it knows or should know is inconvenient. Without knowledge to the contrary, the collector must assume that the convenient window is after eight in the morning and before nine at night, local time where the consumer is. Only the consumer's consent or a court order changes that.
preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(a)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187

preguntas.pregunta: What does the net collection rate measure, and what is its benchmark?
opciones: The share of expected revenue collected on bills over 120 days old; above 95%
The share of claims paid on the very first submission with no rework; above 95%
The share of claims that pass every edit before they are sent out; above 95%
The share of accounts still unpaid after ninety days have gone by; under 15%
preguntas.explicacion: Net collection rate is the percentage of the revenue a practice expected that it actually collected on bills more than a hundred and twenty days old, and the benchmark is above ninety-five per cent. A low figure means the receivables team is not working the older balances, which is treated as a follow-up opportunity rather than a loss. The other three figures are real benchmarks too, but they belong to first-pass resolution, clean claims and receivables past ninety days.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Net Collection Rate
preguntas.subtema: Aging of accounts · CMA III.G.9.b (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187

preguntas.pregunta: An IUD is about to be placed. The tray holds a speculum, a tenaculum, a sterile uterine sound and long-handled scissors. What is the sound there for?
opciones: To find how deep the uterine cavity runs before the device goes in
To hold the cervix still while the device is pushed through the os
To open the cervical canal step by step until the device will pass
To scrape a sample of the lining out and send it to the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The sound is passed into the uterine cavity to determine its depth. Steadying the cervix is the job of the tenaculum lying on the same tray, opening the canal belongs to a set of dilators, and scraping the lining out is what a curette does.
preguntas.fuente: 21 CFR 884.4530(a)(12); and StatPearls, "Intrauterine Device Placement and Removal", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · CCMA 3B4 k63

preguntas.pregunta: Booking a patient who uses a wheelchair, a receptionist tells her to bring somebody along who can help her onto the table. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, she may come alone and the practice provides the assistance she needs
No, unless the office has no lift and no member of staff trained to transfer
Yes, so long as the same is asked of every patient who uses a wheelchair
Yes, because helping a patient undress falls outside a receptionist's duties
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may bring a friend or relative if she wishes, but she may equally come by herself, and the provider then gives the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help with dressing, with getting on and off the table, with positioning, and with staying balanced once there. The staff member asks the patient what help she wants and how.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Commonly Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: Assistance at the visit · CCMA 4 k157 · CMA II.F.3.c · RMA I.D.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair correctly matches an everyday word with the root used for the same structure?
opciones: Windpipe with trache-, and voice box with laryng-
Windpipe with laryng-, and voice box with trache-
Windpipe with pharyng-, and voice box with bronch-
Windpipe with bronch-, and voice box with pharyng-
preguntas.explicacion: The trachea is the windpipe and the larynx is the voice box, so trache- and laryng- go with those plain words. The other two roots name neighbors along the same route: pharyng- is the throat, and bronch- the large airway that leads from the trachea into a lung.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k9

preguntas.pregunta: What advantage does a prefilled syringe give over drawing the dose from a vial?
opciones: A premeasured dose, less waste, and less chance of an inadvertent needlestick
A premeasured dose that staff can adjust at the bedside to any ordered amount
A filter inside the hub that holds back glass particles from the drawn dose
A gauge and a length that suit every route, so no needle is ever exchanged
preguntas.explicacion: Prefilled syringes cut the risk of an inadvertent needlestick and of exposure to toxic products, both of which come with withdrawing medication from vials. Because the dose is already measured, they also reduce dosing errors and waste, and they are particularly useful in urgent situations that call for rapid administration. The filter belongs to the blunt fill needle used with an ampule.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Prefilled Syringes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.h(iv)

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs to the accessible services function of the medical home?
opciones: Around-the-clock telephone or electronic access to a care team member
A shared decision-making aid used with the patient during an office visit
A written plan of care built together with the patient and the whole team
A registry that tracks the practice population for chronic disease care
preguntas.explicacion: Accessible services means shorter waiting times for urgent needs, enhanced in-person hours, telephone or electronic access to a member of the care team at any hour, and other ways to communicate such as email and care by phone. The practice answers to what patients prefer about access. Decision-support tools and population health management sit under quality and safety.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 4. Accessible Services
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: Two terms sit side by side in one report: arteriosclerosis and stenosis. Which contrast between those endings is correct?
opciones: The first names a hardening and the second a narrowing or blockage
The first names a narrowing and the second a hardening or stiffening
The first names a hardening and the second an expansion or dilation
The first names a blockage and the second a softening or weakening
preguntas.explicacion: Sclera- and sclero- mean hardness, and -sclerosis is a hardening; on the artery root that gives hardened arteries. Sten- and steno- mean narrowed or blocked. Two more parts fall into that space and mean the opposite or something else: -ectasis is an expansion or dilation, and -malacia is a softening.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor sits two staff members down to work through a dispute. What comes before the substance is discussed?
opciones: Ground rules on respectful language, equal time and privacy
A list of possible solutions, hybrids included, from both sides
A written plan naming who will do what and by which date
A checkpoint set to see whether the agreement is holding up
preguntas.explicacion: The stepwise approach opens with ground rules agreed before substantive discussion: respectful language, equal speaking time and confidentiality. Separating the people from the problem comes next. Generating options, agreeing on a concrete plan and scheduling follow-up are all real steps, but they sit later in the same sequence.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: A Practical Stepwise Approach
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starts breathing again during CPR while the office waits for the ambulance. What is done next?
opciones: Roll the patient onto one side and keep watching the breathing
Sit the patient upright in a chair and offer small sips of water
Keep the patient flat on the back and raise the legs about 12 inches (30 cm)
Resume compressions at once, since breathing after a code is agonal
preguntas.explicacion: Once breathing returns, the patient is rolled onto one side with the lower arm supporting the head and the upper knee bent to a right angle, and breathing is rechecked until help arrives. Raising the legs about 12 inches belongs to shock and fainting, and compressions on someone who is breathing, coughing or moving can stop the heart.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for a scar left by a burn two years ago. How is that coded?
opciones: With two codes, the residual condition first and the sequela code second
With two codes, the sequela code first and the residual condition second
With one code only, since a sequela is a combination code by definition
With no sequela code, because more than a year has passed since the burn
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is the residual effect left after the acute phase of an illness or injury has ended, and the examples given include a scar left by a burn, a deviated septum after a nasal fracture and infertility after old tuberculosis. Coding one generally takes two codes: the condition or nature of the residual is sequenced first and the sequela code second. There is no time limit.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.10
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: Under Original Medicare in 2026, what does a patient generally pay for a covered Part B service after the yearly deductible?
opciones: 20% of the Medicare-approved amount, when the provider accepts assignment
20% of the provider's own charge, which may sit above the approved amount
A fixed copayment of $20 for each service, set by the Medicare fee schedule
A share of 20% for equipment only, since visits are paid in full by Part B
preguntas.explicacion: Part B coinsurance is usually 20% of the Medicare-approved amount for each covered service or item once the yearly deductible, $283 in 2026, has been paid, and it applies when the provider accepts the approved amount as full payment. The share is figured on that approved amount, not on the provider's own charge; it is not limited to equipment, since doctor visits carry the same 20%; and Part B has no single fixed copayment per service.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs, Part B table
preguntas.subtema: Government plans and patient cost · CMAA 5C k76, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument is used for blunt dissection after the abscess is opened during an incision and drainage?
opciones: A curved hemostat, worked inside the cavity to break up the loculations
A staple extractor, worked inside the cavity to lift the cavity wall apart
A periosteal elevator, worked inside the cavity to strip the lining free
A needle holder, worked inside the cavity to spread the deeper pockets open
preguntas.explicacion: The incision is made with the scalpel straight over the center of the abscess and parallel to skin tension lines, until pus comes out; then a curved hemostat is used for blunt dissection to break up the loculations inside. Copious irrigation with sterile normal saline follows, and the wound is left to close by secondary intention.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Incision and Drainage", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.B.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: Besides written policies, which administrative duties does the Privacy Rule place on a covered entity?
opciones: Naming a privacy official and a contact for complaints, and training the whole workforce
Naming a privacy official whose approval is needed before any record leaves the office
Training only the staff who handle claims, since billing carries the greatest privacy risk
Filing the practice's privacy policies with the Office for Civil Rights before they take effect
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity must designate a privacy official responsible for its policies and procedures and a contact person or office to receive complaints and answer questions. It must train all workforce members as appropriate to their functions, apply sanctions to those who violate the policies, mitigate harm it learns about, and refrain from retaliating against anyone who exercises a right or files a complaint.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Administrative Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Privacy administration · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the purple EDTA tube before the serum separator tube that will be used for a chemistry panel. What problem does this kind of error create?
opciones: Anticoagulant on the needle can be carried into the following tube and contaminate it
The serum tube will fail to clot within the 10 to 15 minutes expected before it is spun
The vacuum of the second tube is lost, so it fills only partially or not at all
The EDTA tube will show platelet clumping and a falsely low platelet count
preguntas.explicacion: Under Issues of Concern, the tube review describes contamination in which anticoagulant from one tube sticks to the vacutainer needle and passes into the next tube; that is why the sequence matters. Clotting time, loss of vacuum and EDTA-related platelet clumping are all real issues in the same material, but none of them is caused by drawing the tubes out of order.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Contamination
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 k9 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD reads 93% and is upset at not being in the usual range. What is the explanation?
opciones: Somewhat lower values can be acceptable in chronic lung disease and at high elevation
Any value under 95% is abnormal for everyone, and oxygen is started at that point
Chronic lung disease raises the acceptable floor, so 93% is lower than it should be
The reading has to be repeated on the earlobe, which is the site used in lung disease
preguntas.explicacion: The normal band of 95% to 100% describes healthy adults at sea level. In someone with COPD or pneumonia, or someone living where the air holds less oxygen, a value below that can be acceptable, and what matters is the patient's own usual level and the trend. The reporting thresholds of 92% and 88% still stand.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: Two blood culture sets are collected from an adult, each with one aerobic and one anaerobic bottle filled to the CDC target. What total volume of blood has been drawn?
opciones: 40 mL
20 mL
30 mL
80 mL
preguntas.explicacion: At 10 mL per bottle, one set of two bottles holds 20 mL and two sets hold 40 mL. That is the figure the CDC uses when it describes the two-set collection. An adult set is expected to contain 20 to 30 mL per venipuncture, and at least two sets, 40 to 60 mL in all, are needed to optimize the detection of pathogens; 20 mL is only one set, and 80 mL would be four sets.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, SOP model step 6 and Collecting Adult Blood Culture Sets
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture volume · CPT D4 4A k77 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139

preguntas.pregunta: How does an under-filled citrate tube distort coagulation results?
opciones: PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out longer and fibrinogen comes out lower
PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out shorter and fibrinogen comes out higher
PT and aPTT are unchanged, but the platelet count comes out falsely low
PT comes out longer while aPTT and fibrinogen are unaffected by the fill level
preguntas.explicacion: When too little blood meets a fixed volume of citrate the sample-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong, and the clotting times PT, aPTT and thrombin time become significantly longer while fibrinogen levels come out significantly lower. The direction matters for the exam: the error mimics a bleeding tendency, not a hypercoagulable one, and it touches the citrate tube, not the platelet count from the EDTA tube.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient who has fainted kept lying flat rather than allowed to sit up right away?
opciones: Standing up too soon can bring the episode back before the postural hypotension has resolved
Sitting up compresses the abdomen and forces blood down into the legs, raising the heart rate
The horizontal position lets the tourniquet be reapplied safely for the remaining tubes
Sitting up too soon converts the faint into a seizure with tonic-clonic activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should sit or lie down quickly with the legs raised to recover from reflex postural hypotension, and they should be kept horizontal after the event while being prevented from standing up too soon. The chapter does not describe abdominal compression, does not say a faint turns into a seizure, and nothing in it involves resuming the draw.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12

preguntas.pregunta: A surgeon repairs a torn tendon and the operative report names the procedure with the ending -rrhaphy. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: Suturing the structure named by the root
Crushing the structure named by the root
Binding the structure named by the root
Puncturing the structure named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -rrhaphy is a suture, so a tendon repair with stitches carries it. Its neighbors on the same list name other acts: -desis is a surgical binding, -tripsy a crushing, and -centesis a surgical puncture that draws off fluid. Two more, -pexy and -plasty, anchor a part in place and rebuild it.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery

preguntas.pregunta: What happens during charge capture?
opciones: The visits, services and facility fees documented are assembled for the billing team
The payer's decision on each service is recorded against the patient's account
The patient's coverage and billing address are confirmed with the health plan
The unpaid balances older than 90 days are separated for collection follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Charge capture starts immediately after care is delivered: the documented visits, the services provided and the facility fees are gathered and sent to the billing department, and copayments collected are recorded at the same time. Posting the payer's decisions belongs to remittance processing, confirming coverage is patient data verification, and sorting aged balances is accounts receivable follow-up.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Charge Capture
preguntas.subtema: Revenue cycle phases · CMAA 6 k81, 6B · CCMA 5K k181

preguntas.pregunta: The practice decides to deny part of an access request. What must the written denial contain?
opciones: The basis for the denial in plain language and how to complain to the practice or to OCR
The name of the workforce member who located the records and the date they were pulled
A copy of the practice policy on retention and disposal of protected health information
The fee schedule for copies, so the patient can decide whether to renew the request later
preguntas.explicacion: A denial, whole or partial, has to reach the individual in writing within 30 calendar days of the request, or 60 if an extension was announced. It must be in plain language and describe the basis for denial, the right to have the decision reviewed and how to ask for that review where it applies, and how to complain to the covered entity or to the HHS Office for Civil Rights. Anything not covered by the ground for denial still has to be released.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Denial of Access
preguntas.subtema: Denial of access · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what she can see through the practice's patient portal at two in the morning.
opciones: Recent visits, discharge summaries, medications, immunizations, allergies and lab results
Only the balance she owes the practice and the date of her next scheduled appointment
Only the documents a staff member has chosen to release to her during office hours
The complete record of every patient the practice treats, filtered by her search terms
preguntas.explicacion: A patient portal is a secure web site giving convenient, 24-hour access to personal health information from anywhere with an Internet connection, reached with a secure username and password. What patients can view includes recent doctor visits, discharge summaries, medications, immunizations, allergies and laboratory results.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Patient portal · CCMA 5U · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 4E k56 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: What share of a healthy adult's total calorie needs should come from protein?
opciones: 10 percent to 35 percent of total calories
10 percent to 20 percent of total calories
20 percent to 45 percent of total calories
35 percent to 50 percent of total calories
preguntas.explicacion: Protein intake is written as a band of total calories, 10 to 35 percent, so it moves with how many calories the person needs. preguntas.pregunta: In which of these situations should 911 be called for a person who has fainted?

The person is pale and weak for a few minutes after waking
The person fainted while seated and woke up within a minute
The person reports having fainted once before during a blood draw
preguntas.explicacion: Call 911 or the local emergency number if the person who fainted fell from a height, especially if injured or bleeding, does not become alert quickly (within a couple of minutes), or is pregnant. In section 15, with the other regulatory information on the product
In section 10, with the stability and the incompatible materials
In section 16, with the revision date and any other information

Do it, but only on surfaces that a patient with broken skin has actually been resting on
Do it, since a stronger agent than the counter needs can never leave the surface underprocessed

preguntas.pregunta: Where do the cephalic and basilic veins of the arm begin, and which side of the limb does each drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch of the hand; cephalic on the radial side, basilic on the medial side
From the palmar venous arches of the hand; cephalic on the medial side, basilic on the radial side
From the brachial vein, which splits at the elbow into a lateral cephalic and a medial basilic branch
From the median antebrachial vein of the forearm, which divides into both of them below the elbow

The tourniquet limit is exceeded

Removing the stopper lets the additive evaporate
Removing the stopper activates the safety mechanism
Removing the stopper breaks the order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: The last of three tubes has just started to fill. What should the phlebotomist do at this moment?

Ask the patient to bend the arm
Withdraw the needle and apply gauze
Invert the collected tubes 8 to 10 times

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Privacy Rule, in which two situations must a covered entity disclose protected health information rather than merely being permitted to?
opciones: To the individual who asks for access or an accounting, and to HHS during an enforcement review
To the individual who asks for access or an accounting, and to any provider treating that person
To the ordering provider on request, and to the health plan that is paying for the encounter
To law enforcement when a crime is suspected, and to the state agency during an inspection
preguntas.explicacion: Almost everything in the Privacy Rule is permission, not obligation. Only two disclosures are required: to individuals or their personal representatives when they request access to their own information or an accounting of disclosures, and to HHS when it is conducting a compliance investigation, review or enforcement action. Treatment, payment and operations are permitted uses, which is a different thing.

A 2-hour 75 g glucose tolerance test after an overnight fast
A 3-hour 100 g glucose tolerance test after an overnight fast
A 1-hour 75 g glucose challenge given at the first prenatal visit

preguntas.pregunta: Only a tiny drop of blood appears after the needle enters and the flow stops. What is the likely cause and the adjustment?
opciones: The bevel may still be partly outside the vein; flatten the angle and advance 1 to 2 mm
The vein has been passed through completely; withdraw the needle fully and re-puncture above
The tube has lost its vacuum; pull the needle back out of the skin and change the tube
The tourniquet is too tight; remove it entirely and wait for the flow to return
preguntas.explicacion: If only a small drop of blood is seen, the needle bevel may remain partially outside the vein, and the device should be flattened slightly and advanced in 1 to 2 mm increments until flow is adequate. preguntas.pregunta: Which detail turns a fainting episode into a call for the emergency number?
opciones: The patient does not become alert again within a couple of minutes
The patient felt dizzy and nauseated for a moment before going down
The patient was standing in a warm room and had not eaten breakfast
The patient looks pale and sweaty for a minute after coming round
preguntas.explicacion: Help is called when the patient does not become alert within a couple of minutes, or fell from a height, is pregnant, is over 50, has diabetes, reports chest pain or an irregular heartbeat, cannot speak, see or move a limb, or had convulsions or loss of bladder control. preguntas.pregunta: A plasma sample will be tested for viral load now and possibly retested several times over the coming months. Why is it aliquoted before freezing?
opciones: So each retest thaws a fresh portion, avoiding the loss seen after repeated freeze-thaw cycles
So the erythrocytes settle in one portion and the plasma stays free of heme when it thaws
So the laboratory can send one portion to a reference laboratory without a referral record
So the heparin concentration falls below the level that inhibits amplification in each portion
preguntas.explicacion: Serum and plasma tolerate freezing, but the number of freeze-thaw cycles a target survives varies: one study saw a 16 % fall in HCV RNA titres after five cycles and recommended aliquoting the sample to limit the loss, while others found no loss after eight or ten. Splitting the sample lets each retest use a portion thawed only once. Erythrocytes are removed before freezing, not by aliquoting, and heparin is a reason to reject the tube, not to split it.

preguntas.pregunta: Before claims leave the office, software checks them for formatting errors, wrong codes and unsupported documentation. What is this step called?

Adjudicating the claims, done during submission to settle what the payer will pay
Posting the claims, done after payment to record the money against each account
Auditing the claims, done yearly to sample records for the compliance program
preguntas.explicacion: In the claim submission step of the revenue cycle, scrubbing is the review that detects coding errors, formatting problems and unsupported documentation before claims reach the payers. Adjudication is what the payer does afterwards, posting records payments once the remittance advice arrives, and a compliance audit is a periodic review of records rather than a check on outgoing claims.

preguntas.pregunta: How many times are the rights of medication administration verified before a dose is given to a patient?

Once, at the bedside, at the moment the medication is handed to the patient
Twice, once against the written order and once against the pharmacy label
Five times, one for each of the five traditional rights of administration

preguntas.pregunta: How do anti-Rh antibodies differ from the anti-A and anti-B antibodies of the ABO system?
opciones: They form only in Rh− people after exposure to Rh+ cells (sensitization)
They are preformed from early exposure to antigens in foods and microbes
They form in Rh+ people after a first transfusion of Rh− blood
They are present in all type O plasma along with anti-A and anti-B
preguntas.explicacion: The two systems differ: ABO antibodies are preformed because A and B antigens are met early in life in food and microbes, whereas antibodies to the Rh antigen are made only by Rh negative individuals after exposure to Rh positive cells, a process called sensitization, which follows an Rh-incompatible transfusion or, more often, the birth of an Rh positive baby to an Rh negative parent.

So that blood pressure can be taken on the upper arm at once

preguntas.pregunta: A patient becomes overheated. Which set of responses does the heat-loss center of the brain set off?
opciones: Skin vessels widen, sweat glands step up output, and breathing deepens
Skin vessels narrow, sweat glands shut down, and breathing grows shallow
Skin vessels widen, the thyroid speeds metabolism, and shivering begins

preguntas.explicacion: When the temperature center reads a value above the normal range it stimulates the heat-loss center, and three things follow: vessels in the skin dilate so core blood can radiate heat at the surface, sweat glands increase output so evaporation carries heat away, and respiration deepens. Running is acceptable as long as he drank only plain water
preguntas.explicacion: Stress and exercise can raise cortisol levels, so the patient may need to rest before the test, and a blood cortisol needs two appointments in one day. General preparation also bans on excessive physical activity in the 24 hours before outpatient sampling. No fast is imposed for cortisol, and 4 p.m. is the low point, not the peak.

preguntas.pregunta: Why do patients in the period of decline become vulnerable to a second infection?
opciones: The primary infection has weakened the immune system while symptoms fade
The primary infection has strengthened the immune system while symptoms fade
The pathogen count rises again in that period and overwhelms the defenses
The convalescent period always begins with a relapse of the first infection
preguntas.explicacion: In the period of decline the number of pathogen particles falls and the signs and symptoms ease off, but the immune system has been worn down by the primary infection, so a secondary infection can take hold just as the patient seems to be improving. Recovery proper comes in the convalescent period.

preguntas.pregunta: An erythrocyte sedimentation rate rack stands on a bench beside a centrifuge, leaning a few degrees off the vertical. What does that do to the result?
opciones: The rate rises, and a tilt of only 3° can add as much as 30 % to it
The rate falls, because tilted red cells settle against the tube wall
The rate is unchanged, since the reading is corrected for the angle
The rate rises, but only when the tube was also underfilled at collection
preguntas.explicacion: Technical conditions move this test more than most. A tube tilted 3° from the vertical can raise the value by as much as 30 %, and vibration from nearby equipment raises it too. A warm room lowers blood viscosity and pushes the rate up, and direct sunlight also raises it. Underfilling adds air bubbles, which lift the reading as well, so the rack belongs upright, still and out of the sun.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: A haematoma forms at a site where the technique looked correct throughout. Which omission is the likely explanation?
opciones: Pressure was not kept up during and after the needle came out
Pressure was kept up too long after the needle had come out
The tourniquet was released before the needle was withdrawn
The site was cleaned with alcohol rather than povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A haematoma can form when adequate pressure is not applied during and after the draw, which is why the gauze is taped down to give continuous pressure. Releasing the band before the needle comes out is the correct order, and alcohol is the preferred antiseptic for a routine draw.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient complains loudly that nobody called back with her results. Which two steps open service recovery?
opciones: Apologize and acknowledge, then listen and ask openly
Fix it quickly and fairly, then offer some atonement
Follow up afterward, and remember what was promised
Document the complaint, then route it to a manager
preguntas.explicacion: The six-step process runs: apologize and acknowledge; listen, empathize and ask open questions; fix the problem quickly and fairly; offer atonement; follow up; and remember your promises. Fixing and atoning come only after the person has been heard, which is where recovery is won or lost.

A vertical distance of no more than 1 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 10 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 25 mm between them
preguntas.explicacion: A recording is accepted only against a short list of minimums, and one of them puts a ceiling on drift: measured from one complex to the next, the baseline may not climb or fall by more than 5 mm. Anything beyond that is sent back to be run again.

preguntas.pregunta: A vaccinated phlebotomist with a documented anti-HBs level of 10 mIU/mL or more is exposed to an HBsAg-positive patient. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: No post-exposure treatment and no source testing; the documented response is protective
One dose of HBIG plus a vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months afterward
Two doses of HBIG one month apart, since vaccinated workers cannot be revaccinated
A repeat anti-HBs test now, with HBIG only if the level has fallen below 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: For a clinician with written documentation of a complete series and a recorded anti-HBs of 10 mIU/mL or more, the CDC says testing the source for HBsAg is unnecessary and no post-exposure prophylaxis is needed regardless of the source's status; the table lists a documented responder as needing no action. Immunocompetent responders have long-term protection and do not need periodic retesting, even though antibody levels wane. HBIG with revaccination is for those found below 10 mIU/mL without prior documentation, and two HBIG doses are for non-responders after two series.

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the brain is the largest, and what connects its two halves?
opciones: The cerebrum, whose hemispheres are joined by the corpus callosum
The cerebellum, whose hemispheres are joined by the corpus callosum
The brain stem, whose halves are joined by the corpus callosum
The diencephalon, whose halves are joined by the corpus callosum
preguntas.explicacion: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and a deep longitudinal fissure splits it into two hemispheres, joined by an arching band of white fibers called the corpus callosum. The cerebellum, below the occipital lobes, is the second largest part, and the brain stem lies between the diencephalon and the cord.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the premium tax credit?
opciones: Help that lowers the monthly cost of a Marketplace plan, based on income
Help that lowers the deductible of a Marketplace plan, based on family size
A refund of premiums paid for job-based coverage during the previous year
A discount an insurer applies for staying with the same plan several years
preguntas.explicacion: The premium tax credit is financial help that lowers the monthly payment for a plan bought through the Marketplace, figured from household information and estimated income; incomes between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level qualify in every state. Discounts on what is paid at the point of care are cost-sharing reductions, a different item, and the credit is available only through the Marketplace.

preguntas.pregunta: A marathon runner has a resting pulse of 48 beats per minute and no symptoms. How is this read?
opciones: It fits the 40 to 60 band reported for well-trained athletes at rest
It is bradycardia in any adult and is reported to the provider before the visit ends
It is a counting error, since a rate under 60 cannot be palpated at the wrist
It fits the range for adults over 65, in whom the resting rate falls with age
preguntas.explicacion: Well-trained athletes rest at 40 to 60 beats per minute, so 48 with no symptoms fits that group rather than signalling disease. The general adult floor is 60, and resting heart rate does not fall simply because a person is older: what declines with age is the maximum rate reached on exertion.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient's daughter stays for the whole visit. When does the guidance suggest asking her to step out?
opciones: For part of the visit, so sensitive topics can be raised in private
Only once the patient signs a release form naming her as a contact
As a rule never, since a companion may stay through the whole visit
Only when the patient is being asked about paying for the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Companions can help the patient express concerns and reinforce what is said, but the patient is first asked how they see the companion's role. Asking the companion to step out for part of the visit gives the patient private time for sensitive matters, and it stops the companion answering for the patient or covering cognitive lapses during a test of thinking.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a home reading of 99.5 °F. Which Celsius value is charted, and what does it mean by mouth in a child?
opciones: 37.5 °C, which is exactly the oral threshold for fever in a child
37.2 °C, which is the axillary rather than the oral threshold in a child
38.0 °C, which is the rectal rather than the oral threshold in a child
36.5 °C, which is the lower edge of the normal adult reference range
preguntas.explicacion: Clinical sources publish the two scales as pairs: 99 °F is 37.2 °C, 99.5 °F is 37.5 °C and 100.4 °F is 38 °C. The middle pair is the point at which an oral reading counts as fever in a child, and in an adult the mouth is said to show fever above roughly 99 to 99.5 °F, depending on the hour of the day.

preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on serum. Which tubes from the WHO table will provide it?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the red-grey or gold serum separator tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube and the light green plasma separator tube
The purple EDTA tube and the light blue sodium citrate tube
The light grey oxalate/fluoride tube and the pale yellow ACD tube
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3 the clot activator tube lets the blood clot so the serum can be separated by centrifugation, and the serum separator tube holds a gel that separates blood from serum when spun. Every other tube listed carries an anticoagulant, so the liquid it yields is plasma: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA and citrate in the purple and light blue, oxalate in the grey and ACD in the yellow.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic tests three walk-in patients for influenza at the same time on cassettes. When and how should each cassette be identified?
opciones: Label each cassette with a patient identifier before the sample is collected, and label samples with two identifiers
Label each cassette after the result has developed, so that the ink does not interfere with the reading window
Write the patient's initials in the log next to the result instead of on the cassette, which stays unmarked
One identifier, the patient's last name, is enough on site because the cassettes never leave the testing area
preguntas.explicacion: Samples are labeled immediately after collection with at least two unique patient identifiers, such as name and date of birth, to prevent mix-ups; the label may also carry the date, time and collector. When a test requires the sample to be applied directly to the test device, a strip or cassette, the device is labeled with a patient identifier before the sample is collected. Improperly labeled samples are among the problems that must be documented and reported.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist cleans the antecubital site with an alcohol-containing disinfectant and, to save time, inserts the needle while the skin is still wet. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: The disinfectant has to dry on the skin before the culture is drawn
Alcohol must be replaced by a water-based iodine prep for cultures
The site should have been re-palpated with a bare finger after cleaning
Alcohol is only for the bottle septum, never for the venipuncture site
preguntas.explicacion: For blood cultures the skin is disinfected with an alcohol-containing product and allowed to dry before the draw; improper antisepsis is a recognised cause of contamination. The alcohol removes the normal skin oils so that a water-based preparation can reach the skin surface, which is why alcohol is part of the prep rather than something to replace. Touching the cleaned site again is prohibited by the WHO's venipuncture steps, and 70% isopropyl alcohol is also the agent for the septum.

preguntas.pregunta: Sterile gloves are on for a dressing change. What does non-touch technique still require?
opciones: Handling key parts only when needed, and applying the dressing by its edges
Handling key parts freely, since sterile gloves make the whole surface sterile
Handling key parts with forceps only, since gloved fingers may never touch them
Handling key parts after a second pair of gloves is pulled over the first pair
preguntas.explicacion: Non-touch remains the goal even when sterile gloves are worn. Contact with key parts and key sites is limited, deliberate and only when needed: syringes are held away from the hub, key parts are handled at the moment they are assembled or used, and bandages are applied by the edges away from the part that will meet the wound.

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist says she was vaccinated against hepatitis B as a child but has no records. How does the CDC treat her?
opciones: As unvaccinated: only written, dated records count, so she should complete the series
As vaccinated: a single anti-HBs test of 10 mIU/mL or more proves immunity
As vaccinated: childhood vaccination is routine and needs no post-vaccination testing
As a non-responder: she should receive HBIG at hire and be tested every year
preguntas.explicacion: Only written, dated records count as evidence of hepatitis B vaccination, so clinicians who cannot document three doses are considered unvaccinated and should complete the series, with anti-HBs tested 1 to 2 months after the third dose. An anti-HBs of 10 mIU/mL or more is a reliable marker of protection only when testing follows a documented three-dose series, so a lone test in someone without records should not be read as immunity. Facilities are encouraged to look for old records and enter doses in the state immunization system.

preguntas.pregunta: A digital sublingual thermometer is chosen over a glass one for a busy intake. Which advantage does it offer?
opciones: It reports in about 10 to 20 seconds, against the 3 to 5 minutes a glass probe needs
It reports in about 3 to 5 seconds, against the 20 seconds a glass probe needs
It reaches core temperature values that a glass probe under the tongue cannot reach
It removes any need to ask about hot or cold drinks taken shortly before the reading is done
preguntas.explicacion: Digital sublingual thermometers take a disposable probe cover and give a result in roughly 10 to 20 seconds; a glass probe needs 3 to 5 minutes in place.
