preguntas.pregunta: Why is important information delivered face to face rather than by email or text when possible?
opciones: Tone, facial expression and body language travel with it
A written message cannot be stored in the medical record
A written message reaches the receiver much more slowly
A spoken message needs no feedback from the receiver
preguntas.explicacion: Providing information by email or text is often less effective than speaking in person: the receiver cannot see the nonverbal communication that goes with the message — tone of voice, facial expression, general body language — and misinterpretation follows. Face to face keeps those signals attached.

preguntas.pregunta: A fungal culture of the blood is requested. Which container is used, and where does it fall in the sequence?
opciones: The culture bottle with broth, drawn first of all the containers
The culture bottle with broth, drawn after the coagulation tube
The pale yellow ACD tube, drawn first of all the containers used
The purple EDTA tube, drawn before any of the serum tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: The yellow and black striped culture bottle holds a broth that keeps micro-organisms viable, and its listed uses are aerobes, anaerobes and fungi. It is number 1 in the sequence, ahead of every other container. The ACD tube preserves nothing microbiological: it is used for tissue typing and DNA.

preguntas.pregunta: The swabs packaged with a rapid strep kit have run out, and sterile swabs from the culture supply are available. May they be used to collect the throat sample?
opciones: No; only the swabs supplied with the collection or test kit are used, because different swab materials can interfere with the result
Yes, if they are sterile and individually wrapped, since sterility is the only property the manufacturer's instructions require
Yes, if they are the same length and tip size, since only the physical dimensions of the swab affect the antigen extraction
Yes, but only from another kit made by the same manufacturer, since the swab material is standardized across all of its products
preguntas.explicacion: Collection devices must be used according to the current manufacturer's instructions, which means using only the swabs that come in the sample collection kit or the test kit. Fingerstick and venipuncture devices are single-use and never reused, and some collection devices deliver a set sample volume or contain additives the test depends on.

A hollow needle with a bevel that draws blood into an attached tube
A tubing system with a needle used to deliver drugs into the body
A needle that connects to tubing for transferring fluids in and out

preguntas.pregunta: What is Maslow's hierarchy of needs used for in care planning?

To decide which team member takes each assignment
To classify the patient by their developmental stage
To document the education a patient has received
preguntas.explicacion: The hierarchy is one of the concepts used to prioritize, alongside airway, breathing and circulation and the acute-versus-chronic distinction. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the light grey fluoride tube before the purple EDTA tube. What is the main risk?

Loss of the vacuum in the purple tube as soon as it is pushed on
A short draw in the grey tube, which can haemolyse that specimen
Clotting in the purple tube, because its additive was left unmixed

preguntas.pregunta: Which password practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance?
opciones: Unique passwords for each user, never shared, written down or emailed
A single department password changed each year at annual training
Passwords posted near the workstation so that coverage staff can log in quickly
Passwords of consecutive digits, which are easier to audit
preguntas.explicacion: Every worker who accesses patient records needs a unique, strong password that mixes letters, numbers and symbols, is changed periodically, is never shared, verbalized, written down near the computer or emailed, and is not built from consecutive digits or easily guessed information; the IT department checks password quality before granting access. Uniqueness matters because HITECH requires systems to track each user's activity. Passwords alone are considered weak protection, which is why some institutions add biometric authentication.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with asthma is wheezing and struggling to breathe in the waiting room. What is done?
opciones: Call for help, loosen tight clothing and help with the prescribed inhaler
Give a cup of warm water to sip and walk the patient to an exam room
Place a pillow behind the head and let the patient lie down to rest
Wait to see whether the wheezing settles before the call is made
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency help is called right away for breathing difficulty; then airway, breathing and pulse are checked, tight clothing is loosened, and the patient is helped to take their own prescribed medicine such as an asthma inhaler or home oxygen. Nothing is given to eat or drink, and a pillow under the head can close the airway.

preguntas.pregunta: A sterile drape hangs four inches below the edge of the tray table. What is the status of the part that hangs down?
opciones: Contaminated, since anything extending below the planar surface no longer counts as sterile
Sterile, since it came out of the same package and has touched no unsterile surface yet
Sterile, but only until someone walks past it, at which point it must be lifted back up
Contaminated, but it can be folded back onto the tray as long as sterile gloves are worn
preguntas.explicacion: Any part of a field that drops below the plane of the tabletop is contaminated, and it cannot be brought back: lifting it would carry the contamination onto the field. The same list rules out anything below waist level or above shoulder level, anything within an inch of the edge, and anything the person has stopped watching.

preguntas.pregunta: A skin puncture must supply a haematology specimen, a chemistry specimen and a blood bank specimen. In what order are they collected?
opciones: Haematology, then chemistry, then blood bank
Blood bank, then chemistry, then haematology
Chemistry, then haematology, then blood bank
Blood bank, then haematology, then chemistry
preguntas.explicacion: With skin punctures the haematology specimen is collected first, followed by the chemistry and blood bank specimens, an order that is essential to minimize the effects of platelet clumping. It is the reverse of the order used for venepuncture. If more than two specimens are needed, venepuncture may give more accurate results.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.3 Order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: Fluid is drawn off from around a lung in a procedure called a thoracentesis. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: A surgical puncture made in order to remove fluid
A surgical opening made from an organ to the outside
A surgical binding that fixes two structures together
A crushing of something hard that has formed inside
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid, and thorac- names the chest, so the two together say where and what. The endings around it name other acts: -ostomy and -stomy make an opening, -desis is a surgical binding and -tripsy is a crushing, as in the treatment of a stone.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery

preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a privacy complaint against a clinic. What does HIPAA say about how the clinic may respond?
opciones: It may not intimidate or retaliate against the patient for filing the complaint
It may decline further treatment, since the relationship of trust has been broken
It may require the patient to waive the complaint as a condition of care
It may share the complaint with other providers so they are warned
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(g) forbids a covered entity from intimidating, threatening, coercing, discriminating against or retaliating against any individual for exercising a right under the rule or taking part in any of its processes, including filing a complaint, and 164.530(h) forbids requiring individuals to waive their rights as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits. The entity must have its own complaint process, document complaints and their disposition, and mitigate any harm from a violation. Sharing the complaint with other providers would itself be an unpermitted disclosure.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(d), (f), (g) and (h), Administrative requirements
preguntas.subtema: No retaliation · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: An automated reading shows 186/122 mm Hg and the patient feels well. What does the value call for?
opciones: The provider is contacted immediately: above 180 or above 120 is a hypertensive crisis
A recheck at the next visit, since a single high value cannot diagnose hypertension
A repeat reading in five minutes and no report unless the second one is also high
Documentation only, because a patient free of symptoms is not held to be in danger
preguntas.explicacion: Readings above 180 systolic or above 120 diastolic are dangerously high and call for immediate medical attention, whatever the patient reports: high blood pressure usually carries no warning signs at all. That threshold is separate from the rule that diagnosing hypertension needs three or more measurements at separate visits.
preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, High Blood Pressure: Diagnosis, Blood Pressure Levels
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: Why should a compromise not be counted as collaboration?
opciones: In a compromise no party fully reaches its own goals
In a compromise only one of the parties gives way
In a compromise the issue is postponed, not settled
In a compromise the more assertive party gets its way
preguntas.explicacion: Compromising is moderate on both axes: each side concedes something to reach an expedient middle ground, and because nobody fully gets what they wanted it should not be confused with collaboration, which works out an integrative solution meeting the substantive needs of all sides. One side yielding is accommodating and postponement is avoiding.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26

preguntas.pregunta: A phenytoin level is ordered and the phlebotomist draws it into a serum separator tube with gel. Why will the laboratory not accept that tube for therapeutic drug monitoring?
opciones: The barrier gel can absorb drugs such as phenytoin, phenobarbital, lidocaine and carbamazepine
The clot activator in the gel tube breaks down phenytoin before the serum can be separated
The gel prevents the sample from being carried on ice and in the dark as drug levels require
The gel tube cannot be centrifuged, and drug assays are run only on centrifuged specimens
preguntas.explicacion: For therapeutic drug monitoring the laboratory refuses tubes with serum separator gel because the barrier gel can absorb some drugs, phenytoin, phenobarbital, lidocaine and carbamazepine among them, which was shown by recovering the drugs from the gel after extraction with methanol; standard tubes without gel are suggested instead. Ice and darkness are the rule for methotrexate, not a property of the tube.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k136 k139 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)

preguntas.pregunta: How common is intimate partner violence over a lifetime in the United States?
opciones: More than 1 in 3 women and more than 1 in 6 men
About 1 in 10 women and about 1 in 20 men
About 1 in 4 women and about 1 in 3 men
More than 1 in 2 women and more than 1 in 4 men
preguntas.explicacion: Lifetime figures are more than 1 in 3 women, nearly 43.5 million, and more than 1 in 6 men, 20.7 million, who have experienced contact sexual violence, physical violence or stalking by an intimate partner. Among women, roughly 1 in 5 experienced contact sexual violence and nearly 1 in 4 physical violence. It affects millions of people every year.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Intimate Partner Violence (how big is the problem)
preguntas.subtema: Abuse of a partner · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c (E.5.b from 2027) · NCMA 4.10

preguntas.pregunta: Which term names the form of case management aimed only at patients who share one diagnosis?
opciones: Disease management, the narrower form directed at a single condition
Care management, the umbrella term used in the payer's own context
Care coordination, the term seen in the population health context
Utilization control, one of the components of managed care itself
preguntas.explicacion: Case management is a basic element of care management, care coordination and disease management, and the terms overlap. Care management is an umbrella term used in the payer context, covering a broad set of services, supports and benefits. Care coordination sits in a wider programmatic and population health context. Disease management is the narrower form, aimed at patients who share one diagnosis or condition.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Case Management: Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Case manager role · CCMA 4E k163 · CMA II.F.4.b / 2027 II.F.2.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has coverage as an employee under her own plan and as a dependent under her husband's plan. Which plan pays first for her care?
opciones: Her own plan, since coverage other than as a dependent comes first
Her husband's plan, since coverage as a dependent comes first
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday in the year
The plan that has covered her for the longer period of time
preguntas.explicacion: The first rule in the order of benefit determination is the non-dependent or dependent rule: the plan covering the person as an employee, member, policyholder, subscriber or retiree is primary, and the plan covering that same person as a dependent is secondary. The birthday rule applies to a dependent child, and length of coverage is reached only when the earlier rules fail to settle the order.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: What advantage does an electronic remittance advice have over the standard paper remittance?
opciones: Payments and adjustments can be posted automatically to the billing system
Payments arrive sooner because the money travels with the remittance file
Denied claims are automatically resubmitted to the payer for a second review
The patient's share is waived on claims the payer reports on an electronic file
preguntas.explicacion: The amount payable for each line or claim, and each adjustment applied to it, can be posted automatically from an electronic remittance into accounting or billing software, which removes the manual keying a paper remittance demands; electronic files also carry more detail. The money itself travels separately as an electronic funds transfer, denials still have to be worked, and nothing waives the patient's share.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79, 6B · CCMA 5K k182

preguntas.pregunta: The server holding the record system is about to be carried to a new suite. Which physical safeguard specification speaks to that move?
opciones: Data backup and storage: a copy that can be retrieved exactly is made before the move
Contingency operations: facility access is arranged so that lost data can be restored
Disaster recovery plan: the written procedures that restore data once it has been lost
Emergency mode operation: the critical processes keep running while systems are down
preguntas.explicacion: Three of these belong to the contingency family and answer what happens after an emergency. The one written for a planned movement of equipment is data backup and storage, an addressable specification of device and media controls: copy the information first, so that a mishap in transit does not take the only version with it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which form is the standard paper claim that a physician office sends for professional services?
opciones: The CMS-1500, designed and maintained by the National Uniform Claim Committee
The CMS-1500, designed and maintained by the American Medical Association
The CMS-R-131, used when the office expects Medicare to deny the service
The CMS-1490S, used by a patient who has to file the claim personally
preguntas.explicacion: CMS-1500 is the paper claim non-institutional providers and suppliers use to bill Medicare administrative contractors and many other payers, and the National Uniform Claim Committee designs and maintains it. The American Medical Association maintains the CPT code set instead. CMS-R-131 is the advance beneficiary notice, and CMS-1490S is the request a patient files to be paid back directly.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to hand every Medicare patient an advance written notice of non-coverage as a matter of routine. When is that permitted?
opciones: For experimental care, frequency limits, certain supplier cases and always-denied items
Whenever the office suspects the claim may come back denied over a coding error
Whenever the patient asks for an estimate before agreeing to go ahead with care
Under no circumstances, since a routine notice is forbidden without exception
preguntas.explicacion: There is no reason to issue the notice routinely, and the exceptions are four: experimental items and services; services with frequency limits set by statute, regulation or a national or local coverage determination; equipment or supplies denied because the supplier had no supplier number or made an unsolicited call; and care that is always denied as medically unnecessary.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Routine Notice Prohibition
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186

preguntas.pregunta: When is CPR started on a patient who has just had a seizure?
opciones: Only once the seizure has clearly ended and breathing or pulse is absent
As soon as breathing pauses during the stiff phase of the seizure
As soon as the lips turn blue, even while the jerking continues
Only after the patient has been fully awake for several minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are not begun while the convulsion is running: CPR waits until the seizure has clearly stopped and the patient is found not breathing or without a pulse. A temporary stop in breathing and clenched teeth are part of the seizure itself. Every seizure is reported to the patient's provider afterward.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", Home Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 k83 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being taught to stand up from a chair using a walker. What is the instruction?
opciones: Push up from the chair arms first, then take hold of the walker handles
Pull up on the walker handles, tilting it back for leverage while rising
Push up from the chair arms while a helper holds the walker steady in place
Pull up on one walker handle and one chair arm, rising toward the strong side
preguntas.explicacion: The walker is set in front with the open side facing the patient and all four tips on the floor. The patient leans slightly forward and pushes up with the arms from the chair arms or handrails, and only then grasps the handles. Pulling on the frame or tilting it to rise is what tips it over. Standing still until steady comes before the first step.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a walker — Going from Sitting to Standing
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.iii · CCMA 3B4 k65

preguntas.pregunta: During a draw, an evacuated tube that was briefly uncapped earlier is pushed onto the needle and no blood enters it. What is the likely cause?
opciones: The vacuum inside the tube was lost when it was uncapped
The anticoagulant was missing from the tube during packaging
The needle bevel is lying against the wall of the vein
The tube was drawn out of sequence and its additive was spent
preguntas.explicacion: Among the issues of concern, the review notes that tubes can be damaged and that the vacuum can be lost when a tube is uncapped; without vacuum the tube cannot pull blood. A missing anticoagulant is listed as a separate packaging defect that turns plasma into serum, not a cause of no flow, and tube order affects additive carry-over rather than filling.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Problems with the collection tube

preguntas.pregunta: How are an interpreter and a translator distinguished in the health-literacy guidance?
opciones: Interpreters listen or watch then speak or sign; translators work in writing
Interpreters work in writing; translators listen and then speak or sign
Interpreters must be certified by the state; translators need no training
Interpreters handle spoken tongues; translators handle sign language only
preguntas.explicacion: They are described as different professionals with different skill sets. An interpreter listens or watches in one language and then speaks or signs in another; a translator reads text in one language and writes what it meant in another. Where materials are not available in the patient's language, an interpreter trained in sight translation reads the document aloud.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Provide written materials and videos in patients' languages

preguntas.pregunta: A 16 G needle is used on a small forearm vein and a large haematoma forms. According to WHO Chapter 3, what is the effect of a needle that is too large, and of one that is too small?
opciones: Too large tears the vein and causes bleeding; too small damages the cells and invalidates whole-cell tests
Too large damages the blood cells and invalidates the tests; too small tears the vein and causes a haematoma
Too large slows the draw so the sample clots in the tube; too small lets air into the tubing of the set
Too large causes haemoconcentration of the sample; too small causes the tube to lose its vacuum early
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says that a needle too large for the vein will tear it and cause bleeding, a haematoma, while a needle too small will damage the blood cells during sampling and invalidate tests that need whole cells, haemoglobin or free plasma. It adds that transfusion collection needs a larger gauge than blood drawing, and Table 3.1 reserves 16 to 18 G for blood donation.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Choice of gauge
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge and complications · CPT D3 k56 k55 k68 · PBT II.J II.I · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: A donor refuses to put their initials on the tamper-evident seals of the two bottles. What is the consequence?
opciones: It is noted on the remarks line and the collection is completed as usual
It is recorded as a refusal to test and the urine is discarded at once
The collector initials the seals instead and the specimen goes out normally
A second collection is done under direct observation with new bottles
preguntas.explicacion: The donor is asked to initial each label or seal, but a failure or a refusal to do so is noted on the remarks line of the chain of custody form and the collection is finished; it is not treated as a refusal to test. Refusing to give donor information or to sign the certification statement is handled the same way. What does count as a refusal is leaving before the process ends or refusing a second attempt.
preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection steps 22 and 24a

preguntas.pregunta: A grieving teenager pours his aggression into competitive sport. Which mechanism is that?
opciones: Sublimation, turning the feeling into a valued pursuit
Humor, using comedy against the negative emotion
Anticipation, working on problems before they arrive
Isolation of affect, keeping the emotion out of it
preguntas.explicacion: Sublimation transforms anxiety or emotion into pursuits that societal or cultural norms consider more useful, and channeling aggression and energy into sports is the example given. Humor combats the emotion with comedy, anticipation solves problems in advance, and isolation of affect keeps the feeling out of the account.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Defense Mechanisms", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Defense mechanisms · CCMA 1E k33

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair gives the usual reference ranges for urine specific gravity and urine pH?
opciones: Specific gravity 1.002 to 1.035; pH 4.5 to 8
Specific gravity 1.002 to 1.035; pH 7.2 to 8.0
Specific gravity 1.010 to 1.050; pH 4.5 to 8
Specific gravity 1.002 to 1.035; pH 5.5 to 9
preguntas.explicacion: Specific gravity normally falls between 1.002 and 1.035 (most often 1.016 to 1.022) and pH between 4.5 and 8 (most often 5.5 to 6.5); both are laboratory dependent, and a value of 1.010 corresponds to roughly 300 mOsm/kg. Urine is slightly acidic in health, and the commonest cause of an alkaline reading is a stale specimen in which bacteria have split urea into ammonia. A pH of 7.2 to 8.0 is the semen reference range.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Specific Gravity; pH)
preguntas.subtema: USG and pH ranges · PBT V.A physiology · CCMA 3D k116 · CMA I.C.10.a.(1)-(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.v

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports cycles of 25, 28 and 34 days. What decides whether that counts as regular?
opciones: The patient's age: a 9-day spread is regular at 43 but irregular at 26
The average length: any set of cycles averaging under 30 days is regular
The longest cycle: a cycle of 34 days is itself outside the normal frequency
The shortest cycle: a cycle of 25 days already counts as frequent menstruation
preguntas.explicacion: Regularity is judged by the spread between the shortest and the longest cycle, and the allowance changes with age: 7 days or less between ages 26 and 41, and 9 days or less from 18 to 25 and from 42 to 45. The same 9-day spread is therefore regular at 43 and irregular at 26. Infrequent menstruation means cycles longer than 38 days.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Menstrual Cycle", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k54 · RMA III.E.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: A provider bills visits at a higher level of complexity than the record supports. What is that?
opciones: Upcoding, an example of fraud when it is done knowingly
Unbundling, an example of fraud when it is done knowingly
A medically unlikely edit, which the contractor applies to the claim
A contractual adjustment, which the office posts after payment
preguntas.explicacion: Knowingly billing for a level of service higher than what was provided or documented in the medical record is upcoding, and it is listed among the examples of Medicare fraud; misusing codes that way also appears as an example of abuse, since the line depends on intent. Unbundling splits one service into parts, an edit is a payment control, and an adjustment is a bookkeeping entry.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244)
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 6 · CMA III.G.1.a(2), III.G.2 · NCMA 4.6

preguntas.pregunta: An irregular strip carries 14 QRS complexes across the ten-second recording. What rate goes on the report?
opciones: 84 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by six
70 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by five
140 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by ten
56 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by four
preguntas.explicacion: The square methods assume evenly spaced beats, so an irregular rhythm is counted across the whole ten-second strip and the count is multiplied by six. Fourteen complexes give 84 per minute, which falls inside the band of 60 to 100.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the pain is tolerable and then rates it a 7 out of 10. What does the interviewer do?
opciones: Ask more focused questions until the gap between the two answers is explained
Record the number, because a rating on a scale outranks the words the patient chose
Record the word tolerable, because the patient's own words outrank any number
Repeat the pain scale later in the visit and keep whichever value comes out lower
preguntas.explicacion: Answers that do not line up are a signal to keep going, not a reason to pick one. Following up often shows that both are true of different moments: a 7 in the knee during physical therapy exercises, and tolerable while resting in bed. That detail is what lets the care be tailored, and it disappears if one of the two answers is simply thrown away.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.5: Chief Complaint
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.3.a · CCMA 3A3 · NCMA 2B.4

preguntas.pregunta: Which two practices are forbidden once a sharps container is in service?
opciones: Overfilling it, and emptying its contents out to use it again
Sealing it with a lid, and moving it closer to the drawing chair
Labelling it, and keeping it within arm's reach of the worker
Overfilling it, and sealing it before it has been fully filled
preguntas.explicacion: The container is sealed with a tamper-proof lid, and the two things not to do are overfilling it and decanting it. Keeping it within arm's reach and clearly visible is the correct practice, since the used device is meant to go in immediately rather than travel across the room.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2; and Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the National CLAS Standards?
opciones: Building culturally appropriate ways to resolve complaints
Collecting demographic data to monitor the impact of CLAS
Partnering with the community to design and evaluate services
Reporting the organization's CLAS progress to the public
preguntas.explicacion: All four appear in the fifteen standards, and the one that covers complaints sits in the engagement and accountability group: creating culturally and linguistically appropriate processes to identify, prevent and resolve conflicts, complaints or grievances. The other three are the standards on data, community partnership and public reporting.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Engagement, Continuous Improvement, and Accountability
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2B k16

preguntas.pregunta: Why are range-of-motion exercises started as early as possible in a patient who cannot walk?
opciones: Changes in the joints can set in after three days of immobility
Changes in the joints can set in after three weeks of immobility
Muscle strength falls away within the first eight hours in bed
The joints stiffen only once the patient has been in bed a month
preguntas.explicacion: Range-of-motion exercises are prescribed when a patient cannot walk or has an injured limb, and they should begin as soon as possible because changes in the joints can occur after three days of immobility. Long-term programmes exist to prevent contractures in conditions such as spinal cord injury and stroke.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the respiratory rate charted in an office often inaccurate?
opciones: It is estimated by eye rather than counted by a standardized method
It is counted while the patient talks, which raises the rate artificially
It is counted over 15 seconds, which is too short to be multiplied up
It is recorded from the oximeter, which reports a rate that is always low
preguntas.explicacion: Outside intensive care the respiratory rate is the least reliably measured of the vital signs: it is frequently estimated visually instead of counted by a set method, so accuracy and reproducibility both suffer. Documentation rates in one review ranged from under 1% to about 82%, and substituting an oximeter reading was one of the problems named.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Patient Safety and Early Detection of Clinical Deterioration

preguntas.pregunta: What is going on between the closing of the mitral valve and the opening of the aortic valve?
opciones: Pressure is building while no blood leaves the ventricle
Blood is being driven quickly out of the ventricle
The ventricle is filling from the atrium above it
Pressure is falling as the ventricle starts to relax
preguntas.explicacion: That short stretch is isovolumic contraction: the muscle squeezes and pressure climbs, yet nothing leaves the chamber until the ventricle beats the pressure in the arteries and the aortic valve opens on ejection. The mirror stretch, after that valve shuts, is relaxation.

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant is about to take a carotid pulse. Which precaution applies?
opciones: Only one side is palpated at a time, and the patient sits or lies down first
Both sides are palpated together so that the two can be compared for symmetry
The patient stands, so that the vessel fills better against gravity in the neck
Firm pressure is applied over the thyroid cartilage until the beat is felt clearly
preguntas.explicacion: The neck vessels are pressure sensitive in some people, and pressing them can bring on fainting or slow the heart, so the patient sits or lies down before the pulse is taken. Help with dressing, bathing and using the bathroom given by a trained personal aide
Housing and meals with staff on hand around the clock for residents who live there
Comfort measures for a terminal illness, arranged and supervised by a hospice team

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finds the sharps container at her station filled to the marked line. What does the standard require before it is carried away?

Press the contents down so the lid will close, then carry it to the soiled utility room
Open the lid and tip the sharps into a red bag that is closed before it is removed
Leave it in place until the end of the shift, the deadline set for contaminated surfaces

Paragraph (A)(2) already required the container to be replaced routinely and never allowed to overfill, so pressing the contents down is the opposite of the rule, and (A)(4) forbids opening or emptying a reusable container by hand. preguntas.pregunta: What is gained by teaching a patient to recognize the warning signs of a faint?
opciones: The faint is often prevented and the risk of a traumatic fall drops
The faint is shortened, although the risk of a traumatic fall is unchanged
The blood pressure stays high enough for the draw to be completed
The pulse rate rises enough that the tourniquet may be left in place
preguntas.explicacion: Knowing the symptoms often prevents the episode outright and reduces the risk of a traumatic fall, because the patient lies down before consciousness goes. preguntas.pregunta: How often must a nonwaived laboratory perform calibration verification, and what materials does it use?
opciones: At least every 6 months, with a low or zero, a mid-point and a high value near the top of the range
At least every 12 months, with two control materials of different concentrations run in duplicate
Only when a control fails, with a calibrator from the same lot that was used to calibrate the system
Each day of testing, with a single calibrator traceable to a certified reference material
preguntas.explicacion: Calibration verification confirms the system is still accurate across its reportable range. It is done at least once every 6 months and also after a complete reagent change, after major maintenance or replacement of critical parts, when controls show an unusual trend or fall outside limits that other corrective steps cannot fix, and whenever the laboratory's own schedule calls for it. Materials cover a minimal, a mid-point and a maximum value.

The toenail bed, the wrist over the radial artery or the inner elbow
The earlobe, the neck over the carotid artery or the top of the foot
The forehead, the upper arm under the blood pressure cuff or the ankle
preguntas.explicacion: Fingernail and toenail beds are the usual sites, and the earlobe, forehead, nasal alar and lips have been used successfully. Bright yellow with a black skull and crossbones, the GHS pictogram for acute toxicity
Red with white lettering, matching the red bags that may replace the label
Fluorescent orange-red with a black frame set on a point, as on chemical labels
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(B) and (C) require the BIOHAZARD legend and symbol on labels that are fluorescent orange or orange-red, or predominantly so, with lettering and symbols in a contrasting color, affixed so they cannot be lost or removed by accident. Red bags or containers may substitute for the label under (g)(1)(i)(E), but the label itself is not specified as red with white text. preguntas.pregunta: In the three-step assessment of an occupational HIV exposure, what does the first step establish?
opciones: Whether an infectious fluid was involved, and by which route and how severe
Whether the source patient is on treatment and what the viral load is
Whether prophylaxis is indicated or observation alone is enough
Whether the worker completed the hepatitis B vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The three steps run in order. First comes the exposure itself: was blood, another infectious body fluid, or an instrument contaminated with blood involved, and if so by what route and how badly. Contact with intact skin carries no meaningful risk; for a mucous membrane the volume and duration count; for a percutaneous injury it matters whether the needle was solid or hollow-bore and whether it had been in a vein or artery. The source patient's status is the second step, and the decision on prophylaxis the third.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient mentions she is thinking of stopping a medicine, and the phlebotomist tells her what to do. Which pitfall is that?
opciones: Unsolicited advice, which can feel intrusive and unempathetic
Providing false reassurance, which can rupture the relationship
Changing the subject abruptly, which can come across as dismissive
Responding defensively, which closes off the patient's own view
preguntas.explicacion: Advice the patient never asked for lands as intrusive and lacking in empathy, unless they have expressly asked to be advised. False reassurance risks a severe rupture in the relationship, above all when the desired outcome is not achieved; an abrupt change of subject can be perceived as dismissive; and a defensive answer leaves the patient no room to express frustration.

preguntas.pregunta: How is standing height measured with a stadiometer?
opciones: Buttocks, shoulder blades and heels touch the board, and footwear is removed first
Only the heels touch the board, and the patient looks upward at the headpiece
The patient leans back against the board with the knees slightly bent for balance
Buttocks and heels touch the board while the shoulders are rolled forward and relaxed
preguntas.explicacion: Shoes and hair ornaments come off, and the buttocks, shoulder blades and back of the head rest against the board while the headpiece is brought down onto the crown. The head is held in the Frankfort horizontal plane and the patient takes a deep breath, which straightens the spine and steadies the reading.

preguntas.pregunta: Which team member helps set up community resources according to a patient's financial needs?

The dietitian, who also teaches about regular and therapeutic diets
The pharmacist, who also guides safe and effective use of medicines
The prosthetist, who also fits and adjusts an artificial body part

preguntas.pregunta: Under 42 CFR 482.13(d), how may a hospital patient request access to their own medical records?
opciones: By oral or written request, in the format requested if readily producible
Only by written request notarized and signed by the attending physician
Only through an attorney, since records are hospital property
Only after discharge, once the record has been completed and coded
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard gives the patient the right to access their medical records, including current records, upon an oral or written request, in the form and format requested when readily producible, electronic included, or otherwise in a readable hard copy or an agreed format, within a reasonable time; the hospital may not frustrate legitimate efforts to obtain records and must meet requests as quickly as its record system permits. preguntas.pregunta: What does 'gender identity' mean?

The appearance, dress, mannerisms and speech associated with femininity or masculinity
The sex recorded for an infant on the basis of the external genitalia
The gender that an observer assigns to a person on first meeting them
preguntas.explicacion: The glossary defines gender identity as a personal sense of gender that correlates with the sex assigned at birth or can differ from it. A close seat directly facing them, with steady eye contact
A closed posture with folded arms, standing over them
A spot between the patient and the door of the room
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation overlaps with therapeutic technique but balances staff safety against patient comfort: keep a moderate distance without appearing guarded, use calm and open body language and tone, stand at a right angle with awareness of the exits, and leave the person able to walk out easily.

preguntas.pregunta: A small practice wants to keep sending paper claims to Medicare. When is that allowed?
opciones: When it meets an exception under the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act
When it prefers paper, since the choice of format is left to each practice
When the claim is for a patient who also has a commercial secondary payer
When the practice has fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees billing
preguntas.explicacion: Initial Medicare claims go electronically unless the biller qualifies for a waiver or an exception under the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act. The exceptions include practices with fewer than 10 full-time equivalent employees, roster billing by mass immunizers, demonstration projects, and certain secondary payer claims with more than one primary payer and more than one allowed amount. preguntas.pregunta: In published studies of laboratory errors, which phase of the total testing process consistently accounts for more than half of all errors?
opciones: The pre-analytical phase
The analytical phase
The post-analytical phase
The post-post-analytical phase
preguntas.explicacion: The two extra-analytical phases together carry four to five times the errors of the analytical phase, and the pre-analytical phase alone represents over half of all errors in the published series; an Italian stat laboratory found 62 % pre-analytical, 15 % analytical and 23 % post-analytical in both 1996 and 2006. Give her a written denial and refer her to the provider who first entered the data
Amend the record anyway, because a patient's own identifying data cannot be refused
Give her a written denial and forward the request to HHS for a compliance review
preguntas.explicacion: The right to amend covers information in the designated record set that is inaccurate or incomplete. A covered entity that accepts the amendment must make reasonable efforts to pass it to the people the individual names and to those who might rely on the old data to her detriment. opciones: Do not do it for routine purposes
Do it weekly in procedure rooms
Do it after every spill of blood
Do it in place of terminal cleaning
preguntas.explicacion: Fogging a room with disinfectant is not to be done for routine purposes in patient-care areas. Environmental surfaces are handled by cleaning housekeeping surfaces regularly and when they are visibly soiled, by wet-dusting horizontal surfaces with a cloth moistened in an EPA-registered product, and by decontaminating spills promptly.

A qualified sign language interpreter or captioning
A qualified speech-to-speech transliterator
A companion who reads and signs the form for him
preguntas.explicacion: For people who are blind or have vision loss, the ADA's auxiliary aids include a qualified reader, large print, Braille, an accessible electronic file for a screen reader, or an audio recording. preguntas.pregunta: A strip in sinus rhythm is checked wave by wave. Which P wave description is normal?

Five small squares wide, positive in leads I and aVR
Three small squares wide, negative in leads I and II
Two small squares wide, biphasic in leads I and II
preguntas.explicacion: A normal P wave is about three small squares wide and two and a half tall. In sinus rhythm it is always upright in leads I and II because atrial activation spreads downward from the sinoatrial node, it is consistently negative in aVR, and it is often biphasic in V1.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient sent to hospital and observed after an anaphylactic reaction has been treated successfully?
opciones: A biphasic reaction can recur, peaking 8 to 11 hours after the first one
A biphasic reaction can recur, peaking 30 to 60 minutes after the first one
The epinephrine wears off in 5 minutes and no further dose may be given
The tryptase level has to be drawn hourly to confirm what happened
preguntas.explicacion: Anaphylaxis can run a biphasic course in up to 20% of cases: symptoms return after the first episode has been managed, peaking 8 to 11 hours later. It is clinically significant in 4% to 5% of diagnosed patients, and the second reaction can be fatal, so it is not dismissed. Repeat doses of epinephrine may be given every 5 to 15 minutes if they are needed, and fluids are used for hypotension.

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the duty of care in a clinic come from?

From the written service agreement the patient signs at check-in
From the facility's accreditation by an outside review organization
From the professional licence the state issues to the practitioner

Use affectionate terms such as 'dear' to put the patient at ease quickly
Use the name the companion uses for the patient during the visit

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is least likely to manage crutches?

A patient with a sprained ankle who has been told to keep weight off it
A patient with full upper body strength recovering from knee surgery

preguntas.pregunta: A sealed instrument pouch is found lying on a shelf beneath a sink with a damp corner. What is its status?

Still sterile, because the heat seal is unbroken and moisture only affects woven wraps
Still sterile, because event-related shelf life counts only tears and punctures as events
Contaminated, but only if the pouch also passed the expiration date printed on its label

A change of provider, so the diagnosis gets reconsidered
A pause in all teaching until the anger settles on its own
A referral for laboratory testing to rule out depression
preguntas.explicacion: A long-term illness can bring fatigue, pain, changes in appearance, lost independence and money trouble, and those changes can produce stress, anxiety and anger. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck with a needle used on a patient known to have hepatitis C. What does the CDC say about prophylaxis?
opciones: No vaccine and no recommended PEP exist; follow-up testing finds infection early so it can be treated
Immune globulin is given within 24 hours, followed by baseline and 6-month antibody tests
A 28-day antiviral course is started within 72 hours, as for HIV
A single dose of vaccine plus HBIG is given if the worker's antibody level is under 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: There is no vaccine against hepatitis C and no post-exposure treatment that prevents infection; neither immune globulin nor antiviral therapy is recommended after exposure. The 2020 guidance does not recommend routine HCV PEP with direct-acting antivirals, noting a percutaneous transmission risk of about 0.2 percent, and instead sets a testing schedule so that infection is detected and treated early. Immune globulin and HBIG with vaccine are hepatitis B measures; the 28-day course within 72 hours is HIV PEP.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with chronic pain goes from 7 out of 10 to 5 out of 10 and can now shop and sleep. Which tool captures that gain?
opciones: The pain, enjoyment and general activity tool, which scores function alongside intensity
The numeric rating scale, whose two-point change already carries the whole story
The 4-item Patient Health Questionnaire, which screens for depression and anxiety
The Geriatric Pain Measure, a 24-item questionnaire covering the preceding week
preguntas.explicacion: A drop of two points looks small on its own. The tool that scores pain, enjoyment of life and general activity from 0 to 10 each, where higher means worse, shows the improvement in daily function that the intensity number misses. It is quick, repeatable and usable in any setting.

preguntas.pregunta: Immunizations, health screening and wellness teaching in a clinic belong to which level of health care?
opciones: Primary care, the level that promotes wellness and works to prevent disease
Secondary care, the level reached once a person has an illness or an injury
Tertiary care, the level that treats the long-term effects of a chronic condition
Palliative care, the level that treats the discomfort of a serious illness
preguntas.explicacion: Health care runs on several levels. Primary care promotes wellness and prevents disease through education, protection such as immunizations, early screening and attention to the environment; physician offices, public health clinics and school nursing are typical settings. Secondary care starts once someone has contracted an illness or injury, and tertiary care aims at restoring function after chronic disease.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Health Care Settings (Primary Care)

preguntas.pregunta: What does asystole look like on the monitor, and how is it handled?
opciones: A flat line with no P, QRS or T, and it is not shockable
A flat line with no P, QRS or T, and it is shocked at once
A wavy line with no clear complexes, and it is not shockable
A flat line between wide complexes, and it is shocked at once
preguntas.explicacion: Asystole is the complete stop of electrical and mechanical activity, so the monitor shows a flat line without P waves, QRS complexes or T waves. It is not a shockable rhythm: once it is confirmed on at least two leads, defibrillation is not attempted and high-quality compressions continue.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asystole", Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: The list of items expected to be denied will not fit on the advance written notice. What does the guidance allow the office to do?
opciones: Attach a sheet matching each item to a cost estimate and the reason for denial
Run the notice on to a second page, since the format may be extended as needed
Issue one notice for each item, each of them signed by the patient in its turn
Note the extra items in the record, since the patient has already been told of them
preguntas.explicacion: The notice cannot exceed one page. Attachments listing further items and services are permitted, and they have to match those items clearly to cost estimates and to the reason a denial is expected. The notice is also to be issued on the approved standardized format with every required blank completed, explained in full, and signed and dated after an option is chosen.

Once every 12 months, with the Part B deductible applied each time
Once every 6 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
Once every 24 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers the visit once every 12 months and the patient pays nothing when the provider accepts assignment; the Part B deductible does not apply to it. Costs can still appear if extra tests or services outside the preventive benefit are done during the same appointment.

A bachelor's degree in chemistry, and a state certificate
A master's degree in pharmacy, and a national certification
A postsecondary certificate, and moderate on-the-job training
preguntas.explicacion: Pharmacists typically need a Doctor of Pharmacy degree, and every state requires them to be licensed. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's urine is pink-red, yet the reagent strip is negative for blood. Which is a recognized cause of red urine of this kind?
opciones: Eating beets or blackberries, or taking rifampin
Eating asparagus, or taking methylene blue
Eating carrots, or taking phenazopyridine
Eating fava beans, or taking metronidazole
preguntas.explicacion: Foods and drugs can change the color, odor or pH of urine without any blood being present. Pink or red urine is associated with beets, blackberries, rhubarb, food dyes, rifampin, phenolphthalein and senna, among others. Asparagus and methylene blue turn urine green or blue, carrots and phenazopyridine orange, and fava beans and metronidazole brown to black. A sample that reddens on standing suggests porphobilinogen.

The name of the courier and the vehicle used
The temperature inside the transport container
The number of tubes drawn from each patient

preguntas.pregunta: What are health care institutions expected to maintain so that abbreviation use stays under control?
opciones: An approved list, a banned list and an audit process to check compliance
An approved list only, since a banned list duplicates the national one
A banned list only, because the approved ones are assumed safe
A yearly staff survey, since written policies have little practical effect
preguntas.explicacion: Each organization has to develop its own list of approved and not approved abbreviations, make sure nothing appears on both, and put a system or audit process in place to confirm that staff comply. Committees that oversee this usually include a physician, a nurse, a pharmacist and risk management staff.

preguntas.pregunta: The grey top tube holds two substances. Which one is the anticoagulant, and what does the other one do?
opciones: Potassium oxalate binds calcium; sodium fluoride blocks glycolysis
Sodium fluoride binds the calcium; potassium oxalate blocks glycolysis
Sodium citrate binds calcium; sodium fluoride preserves the cells
Potassium oxalate inhibits thrombin; sodium fluoride binds calcium
preguntas.explicacion: The grey tube contains potassium oxalate, which binds calcium and so prevents coagulation, together with sodium fluoride, which acts as an antiglycolytic agent; that combination is why the tube is used for plasma glucose and lactic acid. Swapping the two roles reverses the review, citrate belongs to the light blue tube, and thrombin inhibition is heparin.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives at the visit with an adult daughter. What is settled first?
opciones: How the patient sees the companion's role in the visit
How the daughter would summarize the medical history
Whether the daughter can sign the visit paperwork
Whether the patient will step out for a private word
preguntas.explicacion: To protect and honor privacy, ask the patient how they see the companion's role before going on. Sit so both can be addressed face to face and do not aim the remarks only at the companion. Asking the companion to step out comes later, for sensitive topics or a check of the patient's cognition.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the Bruce protocol organized?
opciones: In 3-minute stages, each one faster and at a steeper grade
In 5-minute stages, each one faster and at a steeper grade
In 3-minute stages, each one slower and at a flatter grade
In one long stage held at a fixed speed and a fixed grade
preguntas.explicacion: It is the protocol used most often on the treadmill, built from successive three-minute stages in which the patient walks faster and up a steeper slope, aiming for a total of six to twelve minutes. The modified version adds two easier stages ahead of stage one for patients who cannot exert themselves.

preguntas.pregunta: How is bleeding into the skin distinguished from simple redness (erythema)?
opciones: Bleeding into the skin does not blanch when pressed; erythema does
Bleeding into the skin blanches when pressed; erythema does not
Bleeding into the skin is always larger than 2 mm; erythema is smaller
Bleeding into the skin is warm to the touch; erythema is cool
preguntas.explicacion: Redness of the skin should not be mistaken for bleeding: areas of bleeding into the skin do not become paler when pressed, whereas the redness of erythema does. The same test defines a non-blanching spot: one that does not disappear after brief pressure. Size separates petechiae (under 2 mm) from purpura (over 2 mm), not bleeding from erythema.

preguntas.pregunta: How are the stages of grief meant to be applied to a patient?
opciones: As what to expect, not as a fixed order to work through
As a checklist, since every stage has to be completed
As a timeline, since each stage runs about one month
As a diagnosis, since skipping one signals a problem
preguntas.explicacion: Patients and families may move along a continuum, jump between stages repeatedly, or skip some altogether, and no one way of grieving is the right one. Knowing the stages matters less for predicting an order than for anticipating what someone may go through, so support and empathy can be offered.

preguntas.pregunta: What must be done as a mask or respirator is put on, before the eye protection?
opciones: Shape the band to the bridge of the nose and check the fit
Loop the straps under the chin so it can be pulled down later
Tuck the lower edge under the collar of the gown that is on
Wet the inner layer so it seals against the skin of the face
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the mask or respirator comes second, after the gown. Its ties or straps are placed around the head and neck, the flexible band is adjusted to the bridge of the nose so that it fits, and a respirator gets a fit check. Anyone required to use a respirator such as an N95 must also have been fit tested beforehand, and where fit testing cannot be done a powered air purifying respirator may be considered.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who signed a consent form for a procedure says she has changed her mind. What does patient-rights guidance say?
opciones: She may change her mind about consent at any time
She is bound by the signed form until the procedure is done
She may withdraw only if a second physician agrees
She may withdraw only in writing, with 24 hours' notice
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is a process in which the provider gives the information needed to decide, including the risks and benefits of the care and details of the condition, and the patient must understand it before consenting; a signature on a form is written consent, but the patient has the right to change her mind at any time. The CMS condition frames the same idea as the right to make informed decisions and to request or refuse treatment. No second opinion, notice period or written withdrawal is required to revoke consent.

preguntas.pregunta: A tube left the factory without the anticoagulant it should contain. What happens when it is used?
opciones: The blood clots and yields serum where plasma was required
The tube keeps its vacuum but draws only half its volume
The plasma settles above a gel barrier as in a PST tube
The red cells haemolyse because no additive protects them
preguntas.explicacion: Among the problems listed for collection tubes is an anticoagulant missing at packaging, which means serum is used for testing where plasma was meant to be. That is a different fault from a damaged tube whose vacuum was lost when it was uncapped, and no gel appears in a tube that never held one.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a new walker sets it two feet ahead and steps toward it. What should be corrected?
opciones: The walker goes only a short distance ahead, and the weaker leg steps in first
The walker goes a short distance ahead, and the stronger leg has to step in first
The distance is right, but both feet must move at once with the weight on the arms
The distance is right, but the walker has to be lifted rather than rolled forward
preguntas.explicacion: The walker is pushed or lifted a few inches, at most an arm's length, ahead. All four tips or wheels have to touch the floor before any weight goes on it, and then the weaker leg steps in first, followed by the other leg placed in front of it. Space is kept between the patient and the frame, with the toes inside it, or balance is lost.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set names medicines listed as commonly monitored by blood level?
opciones: Vancomycin, digoxin, phenytoin and lithium
Vancomycin, ibuprofen, phenytoin and insulin
Amoxicillin, digoxin, warfarin and lithium

preguntas.pregunta: Coagulation factor testing is ordered. Which needle gauge range is suggested for coagulation specimens, and which end of the range is preferred for factor assays?
opciones: 19 to 22 G, with 19 G preferred to limit hemolysis
19 to 22 G, with 22 G preferred to limit hemolysis
16 to 18 G, with 16 G preferred for a faster fill
23 to 25 G, with 23 G preferred to protect the vein
preguntas.explicacion: For most coagulation tests the suggested needle range is 19 G to 22 G, and a larger needle such as 19 G may be preferable for coagulation factor and platelet function testing to minimize hemolysis and keep the sample intact. The reasoning runs the opposite way from the second option, 16 to 18 G is the blood donation range, and 25 G is not given in any of the sources.

preguntas.pregunta: The practice has just merged with another and doubled its staff. Which Security Rule standard is triggered by a change of that kind?
opciones: Evaluation, a periodic technical and non-technical check of the safeguards in place
Assigned security responsibility, which names the official who runs the policies
Isolating clearinghouse functions, which walls off part of a larger organization
Response and reporting, which identifies and documents any security incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Evaluation asks for a periodic review, technical and non-technical, that establishes how far the policies and procedures still meet the requirements. preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage plan asks the office where the rules for appealing her plan's decision are written down.
opciones: In her own plan materials, since the plan must tell her in writing how to appeal
In the Medicare Summary Notice, which carries the appeal rules for every plan
In the remittance advice the plan sends the office once it processes the claim
In the plan's drug formulary, which carries the appeal rules for every benefit
preguntas.explicacion: Appeal rights depend on the kind of coverage. For a Medicare Advantage plan, another health plan or a drug plan, the details are in the plan's own materials, and the plan is obliged to put in writing how to appeal; its contact information is usually on the membership card. The Medicare Summary Notice goes to people in Original Medicare, and a remittance advice is sent to the provider, not to the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the National Provider Identifier assigned to a clinician?
opciones: A ten-digit number carrying no information about the provider
A nine-digit number that encodes the State where the provider practices
A ten-digit number that changes whenever the provider moves or is renamed
A number issued by each health plan for use in its own claims only
preguntas.explicacion: The NPI is a ten-digit numeric identifier that carries no information about the provider, such as the State of practice, the provider type or the specialization, and it does not change when name, address or taxonomy change. preguntas.pregunta: A patient keeps her medicines in the bathroom cabinet. What do you advise?
opciones: Move them to a cool, dry place, because heat and moisture damage medicines
Move them to the refrigerator, which is the correct place for any medicine
Leave them there, but transfer each one into a labelled weekly pill box
Leave them there, but add the cotton ball back into each bottle for dryness
preguntas.explicacion: Heat, air, light and moisture damage medicines, and the heat and moisture from a shower, a bath or a sink make the bathroom cabinet a poor place: pills can lose potency or spoil before the expiration date. A dresser drawer, a kitchen cabinet away from the stove and sink, a shelf or a closet is better. Medicines stay in their original container, and the cotton ball is taken out because it pulls moisture in.

preguntas.pregunta: An otoscope is about to be used on a 6-month-old. Which way is the pinna pulled?
opciones: Posteriorly and inferiorly, which is the direction used under 12 months
Posteriorly and superiorly, which is the direction used in adult patients
Anteriorly and inferiorly, which shortens the canal in a small infant
Straight outward without any traction, since the canal is already straight
preguntas.explicacion: Pulling the pinna straightens the external auditory canal so the tympanic membrane comes into view. Under 12 months the pull is back and down; in adults it is back and up. The hand not holding the otoscope does the pulling, and the speculum then goes in gently while the canal is inspected for inflammation, discharge, cerumen or infection.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Otoscopy", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic has no airborne infection isolation room and a patient with suspected measles arrives. What does the CDC advise?
opciones: Mask the patient and place them in a private room with the door closed until transfer or discharge
Place the patient in the waiting area at least 3 feet from others, as for Droplet Precautions
Seat the patient in an exam room with the door open so air can circulate freely
Turn the patient away, since Airborne Precautions cannot be implemented without an AIIR
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC anticipates settings without the engineering resources for an AIIR: masking the patient and placing them in a private room with the door closed reduces the likelihood of airborne transmission until the patient is transferred to a facility with an AIIR or sent home. The 3-foot separation is the fallback StatPearls describes for Droplet Precautions when rooms are unavailable, not for airborne pathogens; an open door defeats the purpose; and refusing care is not among the CDC's options.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a manually retractable evacuated tube system described as safer than a needle and syringe?
opciones: It needs no transfer of blood, and it allows many tubes per puncture
It needs no training, and it costs less than a needle and syringe does
It needs no tourniquet, and its vacuum is lower than in ordinary tubes
It needs no holder, so there is no disassembly step after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: This system is called safer because the blood never has to be transferred and several samples can be taken through one venepuncture, while its safety mechanism prevents reuse. preguntas.pregunta: In value-based care, why does the team ask about transportation, food and living conditions?
opciones: Because those nonmedical factors bear directly on the person's well-being
Because the plan needs them to set the premium the person will be charged
Because the state requires them before Medicaid eligibility can be decided
Because the coding rules require them on every claim the office sends out
preguntas.explicacion: Value-based care teams spend time understanding what could stand in the way of a person's care. Patients may be asked about nonmedical factors with a direct impact on well-being, such as access to reliable transportation or healthy food, relationships with family, and general living conditions, and about their own health goals. preguntas.pregunta: A 9-month-old's length and weight are plotted on the WHO charts. Which band is treated as the normal range on those charts?
opciones: The 2nd to the 98th percentile, two standard deviations either side of the mean
The 5th to the 95th percentile, the band that those particular charts mark out
The 10th to the 90th percentile, one standard deviation either side of the mean
The 3rd to the 97th percentile, three standard deviations either side of the mean
preguntas.explicacion: The two chart families draw the normal band differently. On the CDC charts it runs from the 5th to the 95th percentile, with the 85th to 95th marked as overweight or at risk. On the WHO charts normal is two standard deviations either side of the mean, z-scores of −2.0 to +2.0, which works out as the 2nd to the 98th percentile.

The other specified code, the one the Index marks with the abbreviation NEC

No code at all, until the provider has been queried about the missing detail

The Administration for Community Living, which widens access to local support

Lets it cool to 4 degrees for 60 minutes, which separates the sperm from the seminal plasma
Measures the volume and the pH first, before any liquefaction has been allowed to occur
Divides it into three numbered tubes, one each for count, motility and morphology
preguntas.explicacion: Liquefaction comes first: the sample is left on the bench or at 37 degrees Celsius, and within about five minutes it starts to turn homogeneous and watery, freeing sperm that were trapped in the coagulum. It can take as long as an hour. Only afterward are volume and pH measured and wet preparations made, and motility is best assessed within an hour of collection. Numbered tubes belong to cerebrospinal fluid.

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements make up the quality assurance framework set out for phlebotomy?

Training, written procedures, patient billing, sample volume, storage, satisfaction surveys
Equipment purchase, staff rotas, patient identification, tube colour, transport, audit visits
Training, tube colour coding, patient billing, sample condition, storage, incident reports
preguntas.explicacion: Quality assurance here is built from education and training, standard operating procedures, correct identification of the patient, the condition of the sample, safe transportation and a system for reporting incidents. Each element is there to keep one kind of mishap out of the process.

Eight guides in two groups, starting with the one on contingency planning
Three guides in eight sections, starting with the section on patient safety
Eight guides in three groups, starting with the group on clinical processes

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of abbreviations is confused with the other and appears on The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list?
opciones: MS or MSO4 for morphine sulfate, and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate
HCT for hydrocortisone, and HCTZ for hydrochlorothiazide on an order
MTX for methotrexate, and HCT for hydrocortisone written on an order
IU for the international unit, and IV for the intravenous route used
preguntas.explicacion: MS and MSO4 stand for morphine sulfate and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate, and each is read as the other; both carry the double asterisk that marks The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list, and the fix is to write the complete drug name. preguntas.pregunta: New capillaries begin to grow into a wound at about what point, and what is that process called?
opciones: About 24 hours after the injury, and it is called angiogenesis
About 24 hours after the injury, and it is called epithelialization
About three weeks after the injury, and it is called angiogenesis
About five to seven days after the injury, and it is called contraction
preguntas.explicacion: Capillaries start developing inside the wound roughly a day after the injury, during angiogenesis, and they bring oxygen and nutrients in. That is why dressing changes are done so as to protect the granulation tissue and its fragile new vessels. Epithelialization is the growth of new epidermis, and contraction closes the wound down at the end of the proliferative phase.

preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture (not a blood culture), how does the WHO say the site should be disinfected?
opciones: A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then let it dry completely, about 30 seconds
A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then insert the needle at once while the skin is still wet
Povidone iodine for 30 seconds, since it disinfects better than alcohol before a routine draw
A 70% alcohol swab kept wet for 10 minutes, the contact time given for bleach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 gives the numbers: a 70% alcohol swab applied for 30 seconds, then complete drying, which takes about 30 seconds more. Blood cultures are the one exception the step names. The guideline says that too little contact time raises the risk of contamination, so the drying is part of the disinfection rather than a delay, and inserting while wet skips it. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, because iodine can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results. Ten minutes wet is the contact time the guideline gives for a bleach solution on a blood spill, not for skin.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site

preguntas.pregunta: A bedside handoff is about to start in a room where a visitor is sitting. What has to be kept in mind?

Family may take part only if named as the health care agent
The report has to move out to the hallway before it starts
The report has to be written down rather than spoken aloud
preguntas.explicacion: Bedside reports are given face to face at the bedside with the patient and both the off-going and oncoming staff. preguntas.pregunta: An order arrives written as "amoxicillin 500 mg PO QD". Why should the frequency be clarified before the dose is given?
opciones: QD is read as QID, so a once-daily dose can be given four times in a day
QD is read as QOD, so a once-daily dose can be given every other day only
QD is read as PO, so an oral dose can be given by an entirely wrong route
QD is read as PR, so an oral dose can be given as a rectal suppository
preguntas.explicacion: QD stands for once a day and is mistaken for QID, four times daily, especially when the period after the q or the tail of a handwritten q is read as the letter i. That is a four-fold overdose of an antibiotic. The abbreviation carries the double asterisk of The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list, and the recommended practice is to write daily out in full rather than abbreviate the frequency at all.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician remembers an important detail three days after the visit. How should it go into the record?
opciones: As a late entry, stating when it was recalled and when it was entered
As an edit to the original note, so the chart reads as one account
As a note in the incident report, which is filed outside the record
As an addendum signed by a witness, since the visit is already closed
preguntas.explicacion: A medical record is never changed after the fact, least of all after an adverse event. When something pertinent comes to mind later, it is entered as a late entry that states plainly when it was remembered and when it was written down. Charts should be completed on time anyway: every record system logs when the note was finished, and a late one is easy to attack.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Issues of Concern: Documentation

preguntas.pregunta: How is a double-ended needle joined to the barrel of a vacuum system?
opciones: The end covered by a rubber cuff screws in, past a central thread
The end that enters the vein screws in, past a central thread
Both ends are pushed in, and a locking collar holds them together
The cuffed end clips on, and a luer connector seals the joint
preguntas.explicacion: The needle has a point at each end. The end sheathed in a rubber cuff is screwed into the barrel, also called the tube holder, and a thread between the two ends is where that connection is made. The barrel then holds the tube and keeps the worker away from direct contact with blood.

preguntas.pregunta: What should be arranged before an interview that will use an interpreter?

A relative on hand in case the interpreter loses the line
A written translation of each question that will be asked
A shorter appointment so the patient is not left overtired
preguntas.explicacion: Two of the guidelines are preparatory: allow extra time for the conversation, and whenever possible meet the interpreter beforehand to give background. preguntas.pregunta: A patient cuts a forearm on a broken specimen tube and the wound is bleeding freely. What is the first step?
opciones: Press directly on the wound with a sterile dressing or a clean cloth
Press on the artery above the wound at the nearest pressure point
Wrap a tourniquet above the elbow and write down the time it went on
Rinse the wound under running water until the bleeding slows down
preguntas.explicacion: Direct pressure is the first and most important step, and it stops most external bleeding; gloves go on first. Pressure points are no longer recommended, because collateral circulation defeats them. A tourniquet is a later step, for bleeding that continuous pressure has failed to control and that threatens life.

preguntas.pregunta: A certified assistant is arrested for a drug offense outside work. What does the AAMA Code of Conduct require of her?
opciones: To notify the association within a reasonable period of the violation
To notify the association only once a court has entered a conviction
To notify her employer, who then decides whether the board is told
To surrender the credential immediately and reapply after the case
preguntas.explicacion: One principle requires certificants to notify the association, within a reasonable period, of matters that can affect their ability to meet the certification requirements, including any violation of local, state or federal law.
