preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient walks in from the car park, sits down, and the phlebotomist reaches for the tourniquet at once. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Have him sit for at least 15 minutes first; posture changes alter results
He should lie down for 2 minutes first, the time it takes the veins to fill
He should stand for a few minutes first so the arm veins distend
Draw right away; posture matters only for coagulation samples
preguntas.explicacion: Changing a patient's position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is kept for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the draw, and office patients are advised to sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand. Any unavoidable change of posture is recorded so that the results can be interpreted.

preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists CVA in the problem list. Which event does that abbreviation record?

A cardiovascular arrest, that is, a heart attack
A central venous access, that is, a line placement
A chronic valvular anomaly, that is, a valve defect

preguntas.pregunta: A procedure note says the patient was placed prone. How was the patient lying?
opciones: Face down, the opposite of the supine face-up orientation
Face up, the opposite of the supine face-down orientation
On the left side, with the right shoulder turned upward
Sitting upright, with the trunk raised above the hips
preguntas.explicacion: A body lying down is described as either prone or supine. Prone is face down and supine is face up, and both terms turn up in the notes for physical examinations and surgical procedures. Confusing the two puts the patient the wrong way round for the procedure that follows.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant pulls up a chair to talk with a patient who has just been given a new diagnosis. What does the SOLER mnemonic call for?

Stand at eye level with the arms folded and keep the pace brisk
Stay four to ten feet away, on your feet, with the chart in hand
Sit within the patient's view and raise the voice to hold attention
preguntas.explicacion: SOLER is the mnemonic used for nonverbal communication: sitting with open posture, leaning in, good eye contact, done in a relaxed manner. preguntas.pregunta: Safety cannulae come with active and with passive mechanisms. How do the two differ?
opciones: Active ones need the user to act; passive ones deploy on withdrawal
Active ones deploy on withdrawal; passive ones need the user to act
Active ones retract the needle; passive ones bend the tip over safely
Active ones work only in adults; passive ones work only in children
preguntas.explicacion: Both kinds shield the needle once it leaves the cannula hub. An active system waits for the user, typically a button that pulls the needle into a plastic sheath, while a passive system puts a small guard out by itself as the needle is withdrawn. preguntas.pregunta: An order for a pain medication is marked PRN. What does that tell the person giving it?
opciones: It is given as needed rather than on a fixed schedule
It is given four times a day on a fixed schedule
It is given once at bedtime on a fixed schedule
It is given only by the intravenous route as ordered
preguntas.explicacion: PRN on a prescription means as needed, so the dose is tied to the patient's symptoms instead of the clock. preguntas.pregunta: Before running a waived test, where does the guidance say to look for medications or other substances that could interfere with the result?
opciones: In the Limitations section of the manufacturer's instructions for that test
In the Safety Data Sheet supplied by the manufacturer for the test reagents
On the CLIA Certificate of Waiver that is posted in the testing area
In the quality control log kept for the current lot of test kits
preguntas.explicacion: Part of preparing the patient is discussing pretest information, such as medical indications, medications or other interfering substances that could affect the result; that information is usually found in the Limitations section of the manufacturer's instructions. The site also verifies that pretest instructions, such as fasting for a glucose test, were followed. The Safety Data Sheet is kept for exposures, not for test interferences.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the laboratory for a copy of his own completed test report. How long does the Privacy Rule give the laboratory to act on that request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 60 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 30 days after receiving it, with no extension available in any case
No later than 10 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 20 days
preguntas.explicacion: The access clock runs 30 days from receipt of the request, and a covered entity that cannot meet it may take one extension of no more than 30 further days. preguntas.pregunta: At what moment does an intravenous drug such as vancomycin reach its serum peak concentration?
opciones: Immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed
Immediately before the intravenous infusion is started
About 12 hours after the intravenous infusion is completed
About 30 minutes before the following dose is administered
preguntas.explicacion: Vancomycin has a rapid onset, with the serum peak concentration reached immediately once the intravenous infusion finishes; that is the moment a peak sample represents. The 30-minutes-before-the-dose window is the trough, and 12 hours after the dose is the collection time for lithium, tacrolimus, cyclosporine and sirolimus, none of which are given as short intravenous infusions.

preguntas.pregunta: A sixteen-year-old is seen alone for treatment of a sexually transmitted infection. Who usually controls that information?
opciones: The minor, since state law commonly grants confidentiality here
The parent, who is the personal representative in every case
The school nurse, who must be told of a reportable infection
The insurer, which receives the record with the claim it pays
preguntas.explicacion: Where a patient lacks the legal capacity to decide, information is shared with a surrogate, and for children that is normally the parent. The exception is spelled out: state laws usually grant confidentiality to emancipated minors and to sexually active minors seeking contraception or treatment for a sexually transmitted infection. Reportable infections still go to public health authorities, which is a separate exception and not a message to a school.

preguntas.pregunta: A new urgent care wants to run only waived tests. What is the correct sequence to obtain its CLIA Certificate of Waiver?
opciones: Complete Form CMS-116, send it to the state agency, pay the fee, then test once the certificate arrives
Register with the FDA CLIA database, pay the fee to CMS, then begin testing the same day
Request an on-site survey from the state agency, pass it, then submit Form CMS-116 to CMS
Enroll in a proficiency testing program, submit the first results, then apply on Form CMS-116
preguntas.explicacion: The application for every certificate type is Form CMS-116. It goes to the state agency for the state where the site is located, which processes it and sends a fee coupon; after payment the certificate is mailed. preguntas.pregunta: Once a site holds a Certificate of Waiver, what is the ONLY CLIA requirement for how each waived test is performed?
opciones: Follow the current manufacturer's instructions for the test
Run external controls each day patient samples are tested
Enroll every analyte in an approved proficiency testing program
Have testing personnel who meet the CLIA education requirements

Five numeric digits, with the American Medical Association maintaining the set
One letter followed by six numeric digits, with the NUCC maintaining the set
Three to seven characters, with the National Center for Health Statistics in charge

preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the integrity standard of the Security Rule address?
opciones: Information being altered or destroyed when nobody was authorized to do so
Information being unavailable to a clinician who has the right to consult it
Information being seen by a member of staff whose role does not need it
Information being sent to the wrong recipient by a mistake at the keyboard
preguntas.explicacion: Integrity is defined as the property that data have not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner, and the standard asks for policies that protect against exactly that. preguntas.pregunta: A very thin patient with little fat at the chosen site needs a subcutaneous injection. Which angle is used?
opciones: 45 degrees, because 90 degrees is used for normal-sized and obese patients
90 degrees, because 45 degrees is used for normal-sized and obese patients
5 to 15 degrees, which is the angle chosen whenever the tissue layer is thin
15 to 45 degrees, adjusted within that range to the fold that can be pinched
preguntas.explicacion: A subcutaneous injection enters at 45 or 90 degrees depending on the size of the patient and how much adipose tissue lies at the site: 90 degrees for a normal-sized or an obese patient, 45 degrees for someone thin or with little fat there. The skin is pinched first and released once the needle is in. The 5 to 15 degree range is the intradermal angle, not a thin-patient version of this one.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the Do Not Use list ban IU for international unit?
opciones: It is misread as IV or as the number 10, so unit is written out
It is misread as mL or as the number 15, so unit is written out
It is misread as IM or as the number 11, so unit is written out
It is misread as ID or as the number 12, so unit is written out
preguntas.explicacion: IU sits on the list because it is taken either for IV, an intravenous order, or for the number 10, both of which change the order completely. preguntas.pregunta: A prescriber orders a drug level with the note 'is he actually taking it?'. Which listed use is that?

Finding the best dose when the medicine is first started
Watching for the symptoms of a serious side effect of the drug
Checking that an immune response has not rejected the drug
preguntas.explicacion: Therapeutic drug monitoring may also be used to make sure a patient is taking the medicine as prescribed. Patients with bleeding disorders
Premature neonates below 1500 g

The pressure in the arteries and the pressure returning through the veins
The pressure at the heart and the pressure measured out at the brachial artery
The average pressure over the cycle and the pressure added by each contraction

It needs no dietary restriction because it reads peroxidase far better
It detects bleeding in the upper gut, which the guaiac card cannot find
It can be read at home without a laboratory, which the guaiac cannot be

Compensated, uncompensated, refractory and irreversible
Hemorrhagic, non-hemorrhagic, traumatic and infectious

Yes: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for 72 hours, the same period given for DNA
Yes: EDTA whole blood is stable for RNA targets at 2 to 8 °C for 5 days, the figure the guideline gives for plasma
No: whole blood is never acceptable for RNA targets; only serum stored for 2 to 7 days at 2 to 8 °C can be used

After the needle is withdrawn, while gentle pressure is applied with clean gauze
After it has been in place for two minutes, even if more tubes remain to be filled
As soon as the needle enters the vein, before any blood flow is established

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hands are cold from the waiting room and the pulse feels weaker than usual. What explains that?
opciones: Cold constricts the vessels, and constriction reduces the intensity of the pulse
Cold thickens the blood, and the slower flow reaches the wrist with less force
Cold slows the heart, and the reduced rate is what the fingers read as weakness
Cold numbs the clinician's fingertips, so the pulse itself has not changed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse intensity follows arterial pressure and the distension it produces, and it is modified by other variables, ambient temperature among them: vasoconstriction from cold reduces the intensity felt. Only before the covered entity has received and acted on the request

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the stethoscope chest piece picks up low-frequency sounds?
opciones: The bell, while the diaphragm is the side for high-frequency sounds
The diaphragm, while the bell is the side for high-frequency sounds
The tubing, whose length is what sets the range of frequencies heard
The earpieces, whose seal is what selects the frequencies transmitted
preguntas.explicacion: The chest piece works as a bell for low-frequency sound and as a diaphragm for high; most carry both, either as two sides or as one side where the pressure applied switches between them. The earpieces do a different job: they seal the ear canal to keep out ambient noise, and the headset is angled to match the anatomy of the canal.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how far she can push back on a Medicare denial. How many levels does the appeals process have in Original Medicare?
opciones: Five levels, and a decision at one level can usually be taken to the next
Three levels, after which the decision of the contractor becomes final
Two levels, one before the contractor and one before a federal court
Five levels, but only the first two are open to the treating provider
preguntas.explicacion: There are 5 levels of appeal, and disagreeing with the decision at one level usually allows a move to the next, with each decision letter explaining how. The first is a redetermination by the Medicare administrative contractor; the last is judicial review in federal district court, which requires the case to meet a minimum dollar amount.

preguntas.pregunta: How are sharp instruments passed in a procedure room so that two people are not put at risk at once?
opciones: Through a neutral zone, so the device is never handed person to person
By the person who used it, who announces the pass before letting go
With the tip capped by hand, which is allowed whenever a device is passed
Inside the sharps container, which is carried between the two workers
preguntas.explicacion: Operating rooms and other procedural areas use a standardized neutral zone, or hands-free passing technique, so that the instrument is set down and picked up instead of travelling from one hand to another. Handing and passing devices during or after use accounts for about a tenth of hollow-bore needle injuries in surveillance hospitals, and collisions with a coworker for another eight percent. Capping a used needle by hand is prohibited unless no alternative is feasible.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Introduction; NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Figure 2

preguntas.pregunta: Three weeks after starting lisinopril a patient complains of a persistent dry cough. What is the usual next step?
opciones: Stop the ACE inhibitor and start an angiotensin receptor blocker in its place
Halve the dose, because the cough is dose related and settles within a week
Change to a different ACE inhibitor, since the cough belongs to lisinopril alone
Add a second-generation antihistamine, because the cough is histamine driven
preguntas.explicacion: Dry cough is the most frequent reaction to this class, reported in 10% to 20% of patients and starting anywhere from the first week to six months in. Stopping the drug usually clears it in one to four days, although it can drag on for a month. An angiotensin receptor blocker is the usual replacement because cough recurs less often with it; if it recurs there too, the class is changed altogether.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ACE Inhibitors", Adverse Effects

opciones: Draw a single light blue citrate tube and nothing else
Draw a non-additive tube first and discard it in every case
Draw a red clot activator tube first to prime the needle
Draw two light blue tubes and discard the first one
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 says that when a routine coagulation assay is the only test, one light blue tube alone may be collected. The plain tube drawn ahead of it is an option reserved for the case in which contamination by tissue fluids or thromboplastins is a concern; it is not a rule for every draw. Neither a red tube nor a duplicate citrate tube is mentioned as a primer.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood was collected with a syringe and now has to be transferred into a citrate tube, an SST and an EDTA tube. Does the WHO order of draw still apply?
opciones: Yes; the table is given for vacuum tubes or syringe and needle, so citrate, SST, EDTA
No; once the blood is already in the syringe, additive carry-over is no longer possible
Yes, but reversed, so the EDTA tube that needs a full draw is filled first
No; with a syringe the largest tube is always filled first to protect the vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 presents Table 2.3 as the recommended order for vacuum tubes or for syringe and needle, so the same sequence is followed when transferring: citrate (3), serum separator (5), EDTA (8). preguntas.pregunta: When is the Two-Challenge Rule best invoked?
opciones: When the patient or a team member is at high risk of harm
Whenever a request for clarification has been made at all
Only once the supervisor and the chain of command have failed
Only when the person being challenged outranks the challenger
preguntas.explicacion: It is best to limit the rule to situations where the patient or another team member may be at high risk of harm. It empowers anyone to stop the line over an essential safety breach, which is why it is not for every request for clarification, and the chain of command is where it goes next, not a condition for starting.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice switching to open access is warned that working down the appointments already booked is the hard part. What does that step take?
opciones: Six to eight weeks of extra work, helped by a date beyond which nothing is booked ahead
Six to eight months of extra work, which is how long the whole change is expected to take
Two or three weeks of extra work, after which the booked schedule empties by itself
No extra work at all, because demand for appointments drops the week the model starts
preguntas.explicacion: Reducing the backlog may take six to eight weeks of seeing more patients each day, and every study of practices that made the change found this the hardest part. A useful tactic is to set a target date and agree that no visit is pre-scheduled beyond it. The literature says the whole model can be in place within a few months. preguntas.pregunta: A treatment plan lists chemotherapy given by infusion. What do those two words describe?
opciones: Drugs that stop cancer cells from dividing, put into the bloodstream
Drugs that stop cancer cells from dividing, applied onto the skin
High-energy rays that kill cancer cells, aimed from outside the body
Care that reduces pain and improves quality of life during the illness
preguntas.explicacion: Chemotherapy is treatment with drugs that stop cancer cells from growing, either by killing them or by keeping them from dividing, and it can be given by mouth, by injection, on the skin or by infusion. Infusion means putting fluids, drugs included, into the bloodstream. High-energy rays are radiation therapy, and comfort-focused care is palliative care.

preguntas.pregunta: What is coordination of benefits?
opciones: The way of deciding which of two or more plans pays a medical claim first
The way of splitting a medical claim evenly between two plans that cover it
The way a plan divides its payment between the provider and the patient
The transfer of a patient's benefits from an old plan to a new plan
preguntas.explicacion: Coordination of benefits is how payers work out which one pays first when two or more plans are responsible for the same claim. The primary payer pays up to the limits of its coverage and passes the balance to the secondary payer; if the secondary payer does not cover the rest, the patient may owe it. It is an order of payment, not an even split, and not the sharing of one plan's payment with the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: A coding supervisor is told the target productivity rate is above ninety-five per cent. What does that mean day to day?
opciones: Under five per cent of the coding load should be waiting in a queue at any moment
Under five per cent of the codes assigned should prove to be wrong when audited
Over ninety-five per cent of claims should be paid on the first submission sent
Over ninety-five per cent of charges should reach billing within two days of care
preguntas.explicacion: Coding productivity is measured against a target above ninety-five per cent, which is spelled out as less than five per cent of the coding load stuck in a queue at any time. Adding coders is the obvious move and may do nothing if the real cause is a faulty process or the software. Coding accuracy is a separate indicator, also above ninety-five per cent and higher still for diagnosis related groups, and it is judged on audit.

preguntas.pregunta: Two pathology reports arrive, one headed carcinoma and the other sarcoma. What separates the two words?
opciones: Carcinoma starts in skin or lining tissue, sarcoma in bone or soft tissue
Carcinoma starts in bone or soft tissue, sarcoma in skin or lining tissue
Carcinoma starts in blood-forming tissue, sarcoma in immune system cells
Carcinoma starts in lining tissue, sarcoma in blood-forming tissue
preguntas.explicacion: These two names say where the cancer began. A carcinoma begins in the skin or in the tissues that line or cover internal organs. A sarcoma begins in bone or in the soft tissues, including cartilage, fat, muscle, blood vessels and other connective or supporting tissue, which is why one that forms in bone is called an osteosarcoma.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a reticulocyte count estimate, and what proportion of the red cells should reticulocytes normally be?
opciones: The rate of red cell production; about 1 to 2 percent of erythrocytes
The rate of platelet production; about 2 to 4 percent of formed elements
The share of immature neutrophils; about 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
The share of red cells being hemolyzed; less than 1 percent of the count
preguntas.explicacion: A reticulocyte is an erythrocyte in its first day or two in the circulation, still carrying remnants of organelles. Reticulocytes should be about 1 to 2 percent of the erythrocyte count, and that share serves as a rough gauge of how fast red cells are being produced; abnormally low or high values point to a production problem. Immature neutrophils are called bands, a different measure.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Shape and Structure of Erythrocytes

preguntas.pregunta: How does atrial flutter differ from atrial fibrillation on the strip?
opciones: Flutter is regularly irregular and shows a sawtooth pattern
Flutter is irregularly irregular and shows a sawtooth pattern
Flutter keeps its P waves, while fibrillation loses them
Flutter is a wide complex rhythm and fibrillation is narrow
preguntas.explicacion: Neither rhythm has usable P waves, so the spacing is what separates them: fibrillation is irregularly irregular, while flutter keeps a repeating pattern and is described as regularly irregular, with the sawtooth flutter waves in place of P waves.

preguntas.pregunta: An uncircumcised man is handed a clean-catch kit. What is the first cleaning step he should be told to perform?
opciones: Pull back the foreskin, then clean the head of the penis with a sterile wipe
Clean the head of the penis with a sterile wipe, leaving the foreskin in place
Wash the tip of the penis downward with soap and water, as for an infant
Wipe the urethral opening twice, front to back, with two separate wipes
preguntas.explicacion: The male instruction is to clean the head of the penis with a sterile wipe, and a man who is not circumcised has to retract the foreskin first so the wipe reaches the glans. Leaving the foreskin in place defeats the cleaning. Soap-and-water washing from the tip downward is the infant routine, and the two front-to-back wipes are the female instruction. He then voids a little into the toilet, stops, and collects until the cup is half full.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient collapses with wheezing and hives after an injection. What comes first?
opciones: Give the epinephrine, then call for help and arrange transport
Call for help, then wait for the team before giving epinephrine
Take a full set of vital signs, then decide whether epinephrine fits
Draw blood for a serum histamine level before giving any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Anaphylaxis is a treat-first, then call-for-help emergency. Providers have repeatedly been shown to wait too long before giving epinephrine, and the rapid benefit far outweighs the risk of withholding it. The patient is asked whether they can inject themselves or need help. Emergency services are called afterward, and the patient goes to hospital in case a second, biphasic crisis follows. Laboratory testing has little use.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Safe and Effective Administration of Vaccines and Epinephrine Autoinjection", Anaphylaxis and Epinephrine Autoinjector

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory with a 4 % hemolysis rate wants to know where it stands. What did the survey of 772 laboratories report?
opciones: Most of them, 71 %, stayed under 3 %, and 15 % fell between 3 % and 6 %
Most of them, 71 %, stayed under 1 %, and 15 % fell between 1 % and 3 %
Most of them exceeded 6 %, with emergency samples pulling the average up
Most of them clustered near 10 %, the figure reported for emergency rooms
preguntas.explicacion: In that survey 71 % of the laboratories had a hemolysis rate below 3 % and 15 % fell between 3 % and 6 %, with the highest values coming from emergency department specimens. A separate report put emergency samples at 10 % to 30 %. A laboratory at 4 % therefore sits in the upper range, which the authors of one such laboratory explained by their neonatal and emergency workload.

preguntas.pregunta: A tube reaches the lab with a label for the wrong patient. The unit calls and asks the technician to print a new label and stick it over the old one. What does good practice say?
opciones: Relabeling by laboratory, clinical staff or third parties is strongly discouraged; a new specimen is collected
Relabeling is acceptable if the nurse who drew the specimen confirms the patient's identity by telephone with the unit
Relabeling is acceptable when it is done by laboratory personnel and documented in the record system
Relabeling is acceptable for hematology tubes but never for specimens intended for blood bank testing
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are expected to have a clear procedure for unlabeled and mislabeled specimens, and relabeling, whoever does it, is strongly discouraged: once the link between patient and tube is lost, a telephone confirmation or a documented note cannot restore it. A mislabeled tube is a misidentification, which is associated with the worst clinical outcomes, so the safe course is a new specimen. There is no exception by test type.

preguntas.pregunta: During a clean-catch collection, at what point should the patient start filling the cup?
opciones: After voiding a small amount into the toilet and stopping, then collecting until the cup is about half full
As soon as the stream begins, collecting the first portion until the cup is about half full
After voiding a small amount into the toilet, then collecting every drop until the bladder is empty
After the stream has ended, collecting the last portion that remains and filling the cup to the top
preguntas.explicacion: The patient voids a small amount into the toilet, stops the flow, holds the cup a few inches from the urethra and fills it to about half, then finishes voiding into the toilet. The first portion carries the most contaminating cells and bacteria, which is why it is discarded; collecting every drop is the rule for a timed collection and for semen, not for a midstream sample. About 15 to 30 mL is enough for analysis, so the cup is never filled to the top.

A message exchange through the online patient portal, not face to face
A scheduled video visit that replaces the annual wellness exam
A monitoring device that sends the heart rate to the provider

Yes, leaving home for any reason other than treatment ends the benefit

preguntas.pregunta: A daughter asks about assisted living for a father who needs help dressing but no nursing care. How is assisted living described?
opciones: Housing and services for people needing some help with daily care but not nursing care
A facility where skilled nurses and aides are on hand around the clock for every resident
A residence run by a hospice where the interdisciplinary team gives short-term respite
A rural clinic that gives primary care and preventive services in a shortage area
preguntas.explicacion: Assisted living is housing plus services for people who need some help with daily care such as dressing, bathing, taking medicines and cleaning, but who do not need the medical care a nursing home provides. preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's red reflex is being checked with an ophthalmoscope. How is the room and the instrument set?
opciones: A dark or dimly lit room, the scope set at zero, held one to two feet away
A brightly lit room, the scope set at zero, held one to two feet away
A dark or dimly lit room, the scope set at plus ten, held six inches away
A brightly lit room, the scope set at plus ten, held about four feet away
preguntas.explicacion: The pupils have to be wide enough for light to get in, so the room is darkened; a bright room can leave the reflex absent for that reason alone. The direct ophthalmoscope is set at zero and light is shone on both eyes at once from one to two feet away, then the examiner moves in to look at each eye separately.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of measurements makes a Q wave pathological rather than the small septal one?
opciones: Over 40 ms wide, over 1 mm deep, or over 25% of the QRS
Over 40 ms wide, over 5 mm deep, or over 50% of the QRS
Over 120 ms wide, over 1 mm deep, or over 10% of the QRS
Over 200 ms wide, over 2 mm deep, or over 25% of the QRS
preguntas.explicacion: The ordinary septal Q wave is a tiny negative dip in leads I, aVL, V5 and V6, and its amplitude does not pass 0.1 mV, so it is not always visible. More pain than expected, and clotting inside the citrate tube
A mislabelled specimen, and possible injury to a nerve nearby
A short draw in the grey tube, and bruising around the site

preguntas.pregunta: A donor hands over a container with about 30 mL of urine. What does the collector do?
opciones: Discard it and begin a second collection with a new container and the same form
Pour the 30 mL into bottle A and leave bottle B empty for a later collection
Send it as an insufficient specimen and let the laboratory decide what to do
Keep it and ask the donor to add to the same container after drinking water
preguntas.explicacion: Below 45 mL the specimen is discarded and a second collection begins immediately, using a new collection container and the same chain of custody form; temperature and physical characteristics are checked again on the second one. preguntas.pregunta: The order reads 'liver function tests' with no note about fasting. When does that group call for a fast?

Always, because liver enzymes climb sharply after any meal is eaten
Never, because liver enzymes are not affected by food or by drink
Only when the patient also takes medicines that act on the liver

preguntas.pregunta: A subcutaneous heparin injection has just been delivered. What happens as the needle comes out?
opciones: Keep pinching until just before withdrawal, press gently, and do not massage
Release the pinch before injecting, then massage the site to spread the dose
Keep pinching until just before withdrawal, then massage to avoid a hematoma
Release the pinch before injecting, then hold firm pressure for five minutes
preguntas.explicacion: With heparin, and when an insulin pen is used, the skinfold is held throughout the injection and released immediately before the needle is withdrawn. The needle comes out quickly at the same angle it went in, and gentle pressure is applied with sterile gauze. preguntas.pregunta: A first-run potassium on an inpatient comes back far above the laboratory's critical limit. According to the published guidance on critical limits, what happens before the physician is called?
opciones: The value is confirmed by a second determination in the same sample, and a senior laboratory member verifies it
A new specimen is drawn by venipuncture, since the first tube is assumed to be hemolysed or contaminated
The result is released to the chart at once; confirmation is done only if the physician questions the value
The sample is recentrifuged and re-run on a second analyzer to rule out an instrument error before release
preguntas.explicacion: A critical result is not reported to the treating physician until it has been confirmed by a second determination in the same sample, and a senior laboratory member, such as the laboratory doctor, clinical chemist or senior technologist, verifies it and discusses it with the clinician. Preanalytical influences, like glucose drawn through a catheter used for a glucose infusion, are a frequent source of seemingly critical values, and those are cleared up by testing another, properly collected sample.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introductory text

preguntas.pregunta: Which accessory allows a winged needle to be used with an evacuated tube system?
opciones: A luer-lock connector
A rubber sleeve adapter
A screw-thread reducer
A one-hand scoop guard
preguntas.explicacion: Vacuum systems may also be used with a winged butterfly needle joined by luer-lock connectors, and winged butterfly needles come with safety-engineered features as well. The one-hand scoop is not a connector at all: it is the manoeuvre used to re-sheath a used needle.

preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous cannula has just been threaded and blood samples are wanted through it. What happens to the tourniquet?
opciones: It is loosened after threading and put back briefly to get adequate flow
It stays tight from the first puncture until the last tube has been filled
It is removed for good once the flashback appears in the chamber
It is moved down the forearm below the cannula before the tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: During cannulation the band is loosened or removed once the cannula is in and the needle is being withdrawn. If samples are to be taken at that point with a syringe or a phlebotomy adaptor, the band is put back for a moment to give enough flow, and then taken off again.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to give a saliva specimen for a molecular test and has just finished a coffee and brushed his teeth. Why does the collection instruction usually ask for a waiting period?
opciones: Food, non-water drinks, oral hygiene products and tobacco introduce substances that inhibit the molecular assay
Food and drink dilute the saliva so that its volume no longer reaches the minimum the collection device needs
Toothpaste raises the pH of saliva, which the assay reads as a positive result for most respiratory viruses
Coffee stains the collection swab, which blocks the optical reading of the amplification curve on the instrument
preguntas.explicacion: Saliva and buccal samples are normally collected only after a defined interval without food, non-water beverages, oral hygiene products or tobacco, because ingested material carries substances that interfere with molecular techniques, mainly polysaccharides, glycogen, enzymes such as the plasmin in milk products, and minerals such as calcium. In one study of children, interference from food was minimal when saliva was collected 20 minutes after a meal; the manufacturer's instructions fix the interval that applies.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.5 Inhibitors: Endogenous and exogenous

preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, what is a waived test?
opciones: A test HHS has found to meet the statutory criteria for waiver under the PHS Act
A test performed by a physician or midlevel practitioner during a patient visit
A test that a laboratory chooses not to perform and refers to an accredited laboratory
A test of moderate complexity that has been exempted from proficiency testing
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in 42 CFR 493.2 describe a waived test as a test system, assay or examination that HHS has determined meets the CLIA statutory criteria for waiver under section 353(d)(3) of the Public Health Service Act; everything else is a nonwaived test, of moderate or high complexity. Tests done by a physician, midlevel practitioner or dentist during a visit describe the provider-performed microscopy subcategory, which has its own certificate. Referring a specimen elsewhere does not change the test's category.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: Waived test, Nonwaived test, Certificate for PPM procedures

preguntas.pregunta: About how much protein does one ounce of most protein-rich foods supply?
opciones: About 7 grams of protein
About 4 grams of protein
About 14 grams of protein
About 21 grams of protein
preguntas.explicacion: One ounce, roughly 30 grams, of most protein-rich food carries about 7 grams of protein. An ounce of meat, fish or poultry, one large egg, or a quarter cup of tofu each land in that range. The number 4 is a different one: it is the calories that a single gram of protein supplies.

preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for a PT/INR comes back only about half full. What is the fill requirement for this tube, and why is a half-filled tube a problem?
opciones: Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 9:1 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to at least 50% of the tube volume, so that the 9:1 ratio is still within range
Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 1:9 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to the line only when the patient's hematocrit is above 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The tube has to be filled to within 90% of its full volume so that blood and sodium citrate stay in a 9 to 1 ratio; a half-filled tube breaks that ratio. The coagulopathies review adds that underfilling, like a hematocrit above 55%, raises the relative citrate level and disturbs the recalcification step of the assay. The ratio is nine parts blood to one of citrate, not the reverse.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling

preguntas.pregunta: How does a self re-sheathing needle and syringe protect the worker?
opciones: A sleeve is pushed forward over the used needle to guard it
A spring pulls the used needle back inside the syringe barrel
A hinged cap is snapped shut over the bevel with both hands
A blunt inner cannula slides out ahead of the sharpened tip
preguntas.explicacion: In this design a sleeve is moved forward over the needle, forming a guard around the used tip and preventing the device being used again. Retraction into the syringe body is the mechanism of the manually retractable device, which is a different row of the same table.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Self re-sheathing needles

preguntas.pregunta: Why are approving and disapproving responses treated as a pitfall?
opciones: They act as value judgments and can be experienced as intrusive
They offer a reassurance that the eventual outcome may not support
They move the conversation on before the patient has finished it
They repeat the patient's own words instead of exploring the feeling
preguntas.explicacion: Using approving or disapproving responses is listed as similar to placing value judgments on the patient, and both can be experienced as intrusive. False reassurance, changing the subject abruptly and unsolicited advice are other entries on the same table; reflecting the patient's words is a technique, not a pitfall.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory offers a practice free rent in exchange for sending it specimens. Which law does that implicate?
opciones: The Anti-Kickback Statute, which covers remuneration of any kind
The False Claims Act, which covers false statements on a claim form
The Exclusion Statute, which covers convictions for patient neglect
The Civil Monetary Penalties Law, which covers late claim filing
preguntas.explicacion: The Anti-Kickback Statute makes it a crime to knowingly and willfully offer, pay, solicit or receive remuneration to induce or reward referrals for items or services paid by federal health care programs, and remuneration includes anything of value, free rent among the examples given. Penalties include fines, imprisonment and exclusion, and under the penalties law up to three times the kickback amount.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 6 · CMA III.G.2

preguntas.pregunta: A fasting patient asks whether she may sip water on the way in. Why is she still encouraged to drink plain water?
opciones: Water keeps more fluid in the veins, which eases getting the sample
Water dilutes the sample, which lowers a falsely raised glucose
Water shortens the fast needed from twelve hours down to eight
Water clears the stomach so the fast counts from that moment on
preguntas.explicacion: Plain water is the one thing allowed during a fast; juice, coffee, soda and flavoured carbonated water are not, since they enter the bloodstream and affect results. Staying well hydrated makes the testing process a little easier, because water helps hold more fluid in the veins and so makes the sample easier to obtain.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, Can I drink anything besides water during a fast?

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's forearm shows no vein joining the cephalic and basilic veins at the elbow. Which pattern of the cubital fossa is that?
opciones: Type IV, in which no communicating branch links the two veins
Type II, in which the median cubital vein links the two veins
Type I, in which the median antebrachial vein links both veins
Type III, in which the median cubital vein is unusually large
preguntas.explicacion: The superficial veins here fall into four patterns. Type IV is the one with no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic; type II, where the median cubital vein joins them, is the commonest, followed by type I with a dominant median antebrachial vein. Type III has a poorly developed vein.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Physiologic Variants

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's CRP is ordered to monitor for perinatal infection and the serum returns a hemolysis index of about 800 µmol/L. What does the laboratory do with the CRP?
opciones: Rejects it and asks for a repeat sample, since an index above about 622 µmol/L can underestimate CRP
Reports it, since specific proteins such as CRP are immune to hemolysis interference at any index
Reports it with a note, since only indices above 2,000 µmol/L are considered severe in newborns
Dilutes the serum to bring the index below 31 µmol/L and reports the CRP measured on the dilution
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins are less sensitive to hemolysis than many chemistry tests, but severe in vitro hemolysis can still interfere: a hemolysis index above 622 µmol/L may cause underestimation of CRP, and in that series 199 newborn CRP requests were rejected for severe hemolysis, the highest index being 1,997 µmol/L. Each rejected CRP became reliable after the blood sampling was repeated two to five hours later. The 31 µmol/L figure is merely the index equivalent of 0.5 g/L free haemoglobin, the threshold that defines a hemolysed sample.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Materials and Methods; Results and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: During teach-back the patient says she will have coffee with sugar before the fasting draw. What is the next step?
opciones: Explain again using a different approach, then ask her to teach it back once more
Repeat the same words more slowly and then move on to the next topic
Have her read the instruction sheet aloud back to you, word for word
Record that she did not pass the teach-back and reschedule the test
preguntas.explicacion: When teach-back uncovers a misunderstanding, the clinician explains with a different approach and asks for teach-back again, repeating the cycle until the patient can describe the information correctly in their own words; parroting the words back, or reading the handout verbatim, does not show understanding. Teach-back is not a test that a patient fails.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method, Action
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: How are otoscope heads maintained between patients?
opciones: Wiped with a cloth dampened with aldehydes, surfactants or alcohol
Rinsed under running water and left to air dry on a clean paper towel
Autoclaved as a set at the end of each clinic session in a sealed pouch
Wiped only when visible cerumen or discharge is left on the speculum
preguntas.explicacion: More than 40% of otoscopes have been found carrying potentially pathogenic organisms, among them Pseudomonas, Staphylococcus, Aspergillus and Candida, so the heads are cleaned regularly with a cloth dampened in aldehydes, surfactants or alcohol, following whatever the manufacturer specifies. Any member of the team can be assigned the task.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Otoscopy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62

preguntas.pregunta: Where does a safety data sheet say how a chemical should be stored and which products it must be kept away from?
opciones: Section 7, which also gives the hygiene practices for handling it
Section 2, which also gives the classification and the signal word
Section 14, which also gives the shipping name and the UN number
Section 11, which also gives the toxicity figures and the symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7 is the day-to-day section: precautions for safe handling, including how to deal with incompatible chemicals, how to keep the product from being released, and general hygiene advice such as the ban on eating, drinking and smoking in work areas; and then the conditions for safe storage, incompatibilities and any specific requirement such as ventilation. Section 14, on transport, is one of the four sections OSHA does not enforce.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 7: Handling and Storage

preguntas.pregunta: A biochemistry laboratory graded each of its quality failures twice, once for the harm actually done and once for the harm that could have been done. What pattern emerged?
opciones: Most scored lowest for actual harm, yet most scored highest for potential harm
Most scored highest for actual harm, and most scored highest for potential harm
Most scored lowest for actual harm, and most scored lowest for potential harm
Actual and potential scores matched, because every error was caught in time
preguntas.explicacion: In that grading exercise 72.7 % of the errors carried an actual adverse impact score of 1, the least severe grade, while 65.9 % carried a potential adverse impact score of 5, the most severe. Nearly nine out of ten of the errors were preanalytical. The gap is the point: most near misses do no harm this time, and the same near miss could do the worst harm next time.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine collection bag is being applied to a male infant. Where does the bag go?
opciones: The whole penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the skin around it
Only the tip of the penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the diaper
The bag is taped over the two folds of skin on either side of the opening where urine flows out
The bag is laid loose inside the diaper, without adhesive, so that the voided urine drains into it
preguntas.explicacion: For a boy the entire penis goes into the plastic bag and the sticky strip is attached to the skin; for a girl the bag is placed over the two folds of skin on either side of the vagina. Before the bag goes on, the area around the urethra is washed thoroughly with the soap or wipes the provider supplied. A bag that is not sealed to the skin, or one that only holds the tip, will leak.

preguntas.pregunta: A pharmacist dispenses a Schedule II drug on an oral authorization in an emergency. What must the prescriber do next?
opciones: Deliver a written prescription within 7 days, marked Authorization for Emergency Dispensing
Deliver a written prescription within 48 hours, marked Authorization for Emergency Dispensing
Deliver a written prescription within 30 days, together with a copy of the DEA order form
No further step: the pharmacist's written note of the oral order is the only record
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency the quantity is held to what treats the patient through the emergency period, and the pharmacist immediately reduces the oral order to writing with everything the regulation requires except the prescriber's signature. Within 7 days the prescriber must have a written prescription for that quantity delivered to the pharmacist, bearing the words Authorization for Emergency Dispensing and the date of the oral order.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives at the office laboratory out of breath after climbing several flights of stairs. What is recommended before the draw, and why?
opciones: Have the patient sit for at least 15 minutes, since posture changes alter biochemistry results
Draw immediately, because exertion raises the venous pressure and makes the veins easier to find
Have the patient lie down for two to three minutes and then draw with a butterfly set
Postpone the draw for 24 hours, the interval the chapter sets after physical activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients in an office setting should stay seated for at least 15 minutes before the procedure, because statistically significant changes in several biochemistry parameters follow a change in position, and any unavoidable change should be recorded. The 24-hour rule in the same chapter concerns avoiding excessive physical activity before the collection, not a postponement.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position)

preguntas.pregunta: At the start of an interview the clinician says how much time there is. How does that help?
opciones: It lets the patient rank concerns and feel in control of them
It shortens the history so that the examination can begin
It keeps the patient from raising more than one problem
It replaces the prompting question about other concerns
preguntas.explicacion: Expressing the time allocation at the beginning helps the patient prioritize their concerns and empowers them to feel in control of the discussion. It does not replace the prompting question about anything else, which often has to be asked more than once because the main concern is rarely the first one mentioned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who smells strongly of alcohol refuses his draw and the nurse is unsure how impaired he is. What is directed?
opciones: Carry out the usual capacity assessment, since intoxication varies in degree
Draw anyway, because intoxication always removes the right to refuse care
Accept the refusal with no assessment, since the refusal is his to make
Wait for a court order before any decision about the draw is taken
preguntas.explicacion: Patients under the influence of alcohol or drugs may lack capacity, and where there is uncertainty about the level of intoxication, the typical assessment of capacity is performed. That impairment is often temporary: once sober, the same patient may make sound decisions again. Formal guardianship through a court belongs to long-term situations.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Intoxicated Patients

preguntas.pregunta: Pleural, peritoneal and synovial fluids have been aspirated for culture. How should they travel to the laboratory?
opciones: Promptly and at room temperature, which keeps the organisms viable
Promptly and refrigerated, which keeps the organisms viable in transit
Promptly and frozen, since the cell count is read from the thawed fluid
Whenever convenient, provided each container has been sealed and labeled
preguntas.explicacion: These fluids are aspirated aseptically into sterile containers, and their appearance, color, turbidity, viscosity and any clots are recorded. Portions go for cell count and differential, for protein and glucose, for culture and for cytology. For the microbiology portion, prompt transport at room temperature is what keeps the organisms alive, the same principle that governs cerebrospinal fluid.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Body Fluid Samples

preguntas.pregunta: Under which measure was the Institutional Review Board established in the United States?
opciones: The National Research Act, in 1974
The National Research Act, in 1984
The Belmont Report, issued in 1976
The Declaration of Helsinki revisions
preguntas.explicacion: The board was established in 1974 under the National Research Act, which brought in regulations for human research after unethical practices such as the Tuskegee syphilis experiments. The Belmont Report sets out respect for persons, beneficence and justice as guiding principles, and the Declaration of Helsinki is an ethical statement; neither created the board.

preguntas.pregunta: In most cases, how many hours do part-time or intermittent home health services come to?
opciones: Up to 8 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 28 hours in the week
Up to 8 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 40 hours in the week
Up to 4 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 20 hours in the week
Up to 12 hours a day combined, with no weekly maximum applied at all
preguntas.explicacion: Home health visits are unlimited in number for a patient who qualifies, but part-time or intermittent usually means skilled nursing and home health aide services together up to 8 hours a day, with a ceiling of 28 hours a week. More frequent care may be allowed for a short time, under 8 hours a day and up to 35 hours a week, when the provider decides it is necessary.

preguntas.pregunta: A fingerstick A1C on a clinic's point-of-care analyzer reads 6.6 % in a patient without a diabetes diagnosis. What should happen next?
opciones: The result is confirmed with a venous sample before any diagnosis, because capillary point-of-care A1C values are variable
Diabetes is diagnosed on the spot, because 6.5 % or higher on any A1C method is diagnostic without a second test
The fingerstick is repeated the same day and the two capillary results are averaged to reach the diagnostic value
The patient is scheduled for a repeat fingerstick A1C in three months, and diabetes is diagnosed if it is still 6.5 % or more
preguntas.explicacion: Because capillary point-of-care A1C testing is variable, any A1C obtained from a capillary sample should be confirmed with a venous sample before a diagnosis is made; point-of-care devices also tend to read about 0.5 % lower than laboratory assays. For screening and diagnosis, point-of-care A1C is restricted to FDA-approved devices run in CLIA-certified laboratories performing moderate complexity or higher testing, with certified methods.

preguntas.pregunta: Which superficial vein connects the cephalic and basilic veins in the cubital fossa?
opciones: The median cubital vein
The median antebrachial vein
The brachial vein
The dorsal venous arch
preguntas.explicacion: As the cephalic and basilic veins approach the cubital fossa they become joined by the median cubital vein, which has a median cephalic and a median basilic connection. The dorsal venous arch is where both veins begin on the back of the hand, the median antebrachial vein is the dominant vessel only in the type I fossa, and the brachial vein is deep.

preguntas.pregunta: An older office building has two steps at its entrance. What does the law ask of the practice inside it?
opciones: Remove the barrier where doing so is readily achievable, and otherwise serve by other means
Remove the barrier only when the building is next altered or the lease comes up for renewal
Remove the barrier only if a patient files a written complaint about the entrance first
Leave the entrance as it stands, since buildings raised before the law are not reached by it
preguntas.explicacion: Every building is subject to the requirements for existing facilities, whatever its age. Under Title III architectural barriers are removed where removal is readily achievable, that is, easily accomplishable without much difficulty or expense; where it is not, the services still have to be made available by alternative methods that are readily achievable.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first void of the morning considered the best representative urine specimen for testing?
opciones: It is the most concentrated, so it shows concentrating ability and reveals substances present in traces
It is the most dilute, so cells, casts and crystals stay intact in it until they can be examined
It has spent the least time in the bladder, so bacteria have had no chance to grow in it overnight
It is collected before meals, so it averages out the effect of food and of physical activity
preguntas.explicacion: Urine that has accumulated in the bladder through the night is the most concentrated of the day. That is what makes it the best representative sample: it shows how well the kidneys concentrate and it lets small amounts of a substance be detected that a diluted specimen would hide. Random, two-hour postprandial and 24-hour collections are ordered instead when the purpose calls for them.

preguntas.pregunta: Which children does the Children's Health Insurance Program cover?

Those in families earning too little for Medicaid but enough for a private plan
Those whose parents are enrolled in Medicare because of a lasting disability
Those living in a county that has a federally qualified health center nearby
preguntas.explicacion: The Children's Health Insurance Program provides health coverage to eligible children, through both Medicaid and separate CHIP programs. preguntas.pregunta: What does the allowed amount of a plan represent?

The most the patient will pay for a covered service before the plan pays its share
The most the patient will pay in a plan year before coverage of benefits reaches 100%
The total the provider charges for the service before any discount is applied to it
preguntas.explicacion: The allowed amount is the ceiling a plan will pay for a covered service, and the glossary also calls it the eligible expense, the payment allowance or the negotiated rate. What the patient pays first is the deductible; the yearly ceiling on patient spending is the out-of-pocket limit; and the provider's own charge is a separate figure, which is why a charge above the allowed amount can leave a balance.

preguntas.pregunta: A caregiver needs a break from caring for a hospice patient at home. What does the respite level of care allow?
opciones: A stay of no more than 5 days in a row in a Medicare-approved facility each time
A stay of no more than 3 days in a row in a Medicare-approved facility each time
A stay of up to 30 days in each benefit period in a hospice inpatient facility
Continuous nursing at home for 8 hours a day, at least half of it given by a nurse
preguntas.explicacion: Respite is the hospice level designed to relieve the caregiver. It is allowed for no more than five consecutive days per occurrence and is given in a Medicare-approved facility such as an inpatient hospice or a nursing home; those patients do not need skilled care. preguntas.pregunta: At which blood glucose level is a patient considered to be hypoglycemic?
opciones: Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), which can already do harm
Below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L), the lower end of the fasting range
Below 55 mg/dL (3.1 mmol/L), and never above that figure
Below 40 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L), when the patient loses consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: A blood sugar under 70 mg/dL, or 3.9 mmol/L, counts as low and can be harmful at or below that level. Symptoms may not appear until the glucose falls below 55 mg/dL, which is why the number matters and not only how the patient looks. Severe low blood sugar that ends in unconsciousness is what is called insulin shock.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a handoff report defined?

A written summary filed at the close of every nursing shift
A standing set of orders that follows the patient between units
A review of the record made before the next provider walks in
preguntas.explicacion: The definition used is a transfer and acceptance of responsibility for patient care achieved through effective communication, a real-time process of passing patient specific information from one caregiver or team to the next so that care stays continuous and safe. A filed summary or a set of orders is not that exchange.

preguntas.pregunta: How far back may a patient's accounting of disclosures reach, and which disclosures does it leave out?
opciones: Six years back, leaving out treatment, payment and operations and those made under an authorization
Six years back, leaving out only the disclosures made to public health and law enforcement agencies
Two years back, leaving out treatment, payment and operations and those made under an authorization
Ten years back, leaving out only the disclosures the covered entity made to its business associates
preguntas.explicacion: The maximum accounting period is the six years immediately before the request. The list of disclosures that need not be accounted for is long: treatment, payment and health care operations; those to the individual or the personal representative; those made under an authorization; a limited data set; facility directories and disaster relief; national security; and disclosures incidental to a permitted use.

As a rejection criterion applied once the specimen reaches the laboratory
As an interfering factor, noted in the comment field beside the result
As a postanalytical problem, handled when the report is interpreted
preguntas.explicacion: Contraindications are said to arise when results will not alter management, when testing imposes unnecessary harm, or when preanalytical requirements cannot be met. preguntas.pregunta: How is a blood pressure of 120 over 80 correctly recorded?

80/120 mm Hg, diastolic first because it is the resting value of the two
120/80 mm, since the unit of the gauge is millimetres of the column
120 over 80 kPa, the pressure unit used on automated office devices
preguntas.explicacion: The systolic value goes first, then a slash, then the diastolic, and the unit is millimetres of mercury: 120/80 mm Hg. The gauge on the cuff reads in that unit, and the arm used and the patient's position belong in the record beside the numbers, since both change the value.

Priority Mail Express, whose network is built around the fastest possible movement
First-Class Mail, whose light pieces travel with ordinary letters and small envelopes
Media Mail, whose slower schedule already allows for surface transport of the contents

preguntas.pregunta: Where should the needle enter the skin when performing venipuncture on an immobilized infant?
opciones: 3 to 5 mm distal to the vein, so the vein is not pushed away
Directly over the vein, so the needle enters on the first pass
3 to 5 mm proximal to the vein, so the needle tip travels with the flow
1 cm distal to the vein, the width the alcohol swab must cover
preguntas.explicacion: Once the infant or child is immobilized, the skin is punctured 3 to 5 mm distal to, that is away from, the vein, because this allows good access without pushing the vein away. If the needle ends up alongside the vein rather than in it, withdraw it slightly without removing it and angle it into the vessel. Blood is then drawn slowly and steadily.

preguntas.pregunta: A sterile drape has been opened over a treatment table. Which part of it counts as contaminated from the start?
opciones: The one-inch border running around the edge of the drape
The one-inch border running around the edge, plus the center
The half of the drape furthest from the person who opened it
The four corners where the flaps were folded before opening
preguntas.explicacion: An imaginary border one inch wide along the edges is treated as unsterile, so supplies are never tossed or slid into it. The same one-inch rule applies around any hole, tear or patch of moisture wicked in from an unsterile area. Peel-pack wrappers carry the same border, which is why items are not slid out near the edge of the pouch.

The citrate works by chelating calcium.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient planning a pregnancy asks about folic acid. What is recommended, and to whom?
opciones: 0.4 to 0.8 mg daily for everyone planning or able to become pregnant
0.4 to 0.8 mg daily, but only once the pregnancy has been confirmed
4 to 8 mg daily for everyone planning or able to become pregnant
0.4 to 0.8 mg daily, but only for those with a previous affected pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation carries an A grade and covers everyone who plans to become pregnant or could: a daily supplement holding 0.4 to 0.8 mg, that is 400 to 800 micrograms, of folic acid, to prevent neural tube defects. preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a telephone consult about a named patient from the phone in the hospital cafeteria. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The talk is allowed, but it has to happen away from the public
The talk is barred, since consults require written authorization
The talk is allowed only if the patient is on the line as well
The talk is barred, because phone lines are never encrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Consulting another provider is a permitted conversation; where it takes place is what matters. Such conversations are to be held away from the public and in private rooms, and a telephone consult from a cafeteria line, where others can hear, is the example given of how not to do it. Staff may still coordinate verbally at a nurses' station, and providers may discuss a patient's status by telephone.

preguntas.pregunta: When does the CDC say soap and water must be used rather than alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
opciones: When hands are visibly soiled, after using the restroom, or during C. difficile outbreaks
Before every aseptic task and after any contact with the patient's immediate surroundings
Whenever the sanitizer on hand contains less than 60 percent alcohol by volume
Whenever gloves have been worn for longer than the 20 seconds a hand rub takes
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC prefers alcohol-based hand sanitizer in most clinical situations unless hands are visibly soiled, and reserves soap and water for visibly soiled hands, before eating, after using the restroom, and during care of patients with suspected or confirmed infection in outbreaks of C. difficile and norovirus. StatPearls explains that spore-forming and non-enveloped organisms resist alcohol, so mechanical removal by washing is needed. Aseptic tasks and contact with surroundings are moments for hand hygiene by either method, not reasons to choose soap.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications

preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins of the cubital fossa are classified into four types. Which pattern is the most common?
opciones: Type II, in which the median cubital vein joins the cephalic and basilic veins (the M pattern)
Type I, in which a dominant median antebrachial vein joins both veins (the N pattern)
Type III, in which the brachial cephalic vein is poorly developed or missing
Type IV, in which there is no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic
preguntas.explicacion: Type II, with the cephalic and basilic veins connected by the median cubital vein and also called type M, is the most common pattern, followed by type I, the N type with a dominant median antebrachial vein. It adds that because of this variation, bruising, hematoma and sensory changes from mispuncture have been reported across health systems.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a spot tested to decide whether it is non-blanching?
opciones: Brief pressure is applied, and the spot does not disappear
Brief pressure is applied, and the spot fades then returns
The skin is stretched, and the spot spreads sideways with it
The skin is cooled, and the spot pales under the cold pack
preguntas.explicacion: A non-blanching spot is one that stays visible after brief pressure is put on the area. That single manoeuvre separates bleeding into the skin, which does not pale, from simple redness of the skin, which does. Both petechiae and purpura are defined as non-blanching.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory starts logging every preanalytical incident in one simple shared program instead of on paper notes. What does the literature credit that with achieving?
opciones: It harmonises incident reporting, which is otherwise commonly left undone
It removes the need for a written procedure covering unacceptable specimens
It shortens turnaround time by routing the rejected samples automatically
It covers the proficiency testing requirement for the preanalytical phase
preguntas.explicacion: Incidents in the preanalytical phase are commonly underreported, so the numbers a laboratory holds understate the problem. A simple and freely available program for recording those errors systematically was shown to be worthwhile precisely because it makes reporting comparable within one laboratory and even between laboratories in different countries.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the civil False Claims Act, what does the government have to prove about intent?
opciones: No specific intent to defraud is needed; reckless disregard is enough
A specific intent to defraud the program has to be shown for each claim
Only that the claim was denied by the payer after it had been reviewed
Only that the provider failed to refund an overpayment within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: The civil False Claims Act reaches anyone who knowingly submits or causes the submission of a false or fraudulent claim, and knowingly covers actual knowledge, deliberate ignorance and reckless disregard of the truth. Specific intent to defraud is not required. A denial by itself proves nothing, and the 60-day overpayment rule is a separate obligation whose breach can then create liability.

preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen from a neurology ICU arrives in a urine cup instead of a sterile CSF tube. How does the emergency laboratory handle it?
opciones: A laboratory medicine specialist decides whether this precious specimen is rejected or accepted
The accessioning clerk rejects it automatically, as with any specimen in an improper container
It is accepted without review, because CSF can never be recollected from the same patient
It is transferred by the clerk into a sterile tube and processed as an ordinary specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Improper container is a standing rejection criterion, and sending CSF in a urine cup is described as a common mistake in the neurology ICU; but for precious specimens such as CSF, bone marrow or aspirates received in unsuitable tubes or under wrong transport conditions, the decision to reject or accept is reserved to the laboratory medicine specialists rather than made automatically at the desk.

preguntas.pregunta: An adult woman weighing about 250 lb is to receive an intramuscular vaccine in the deltoid. Which needle is chosen?
opciones: A 1.5-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, because she weighs more than 200 lb
A 1-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, which is the choice below 130 lb
A 5/8-inch needle, 23 to 25 gauge, which is the subcutaneous choice
A 1-inch needle, 18 to 22 gauge, chosen for a thicker vaccine product
preguntas.explicacion: Needle length for an intramuscular vaccine in an adult follows weight. Below 130 lb, and from 130 to 152 lb, an inch is used; men from 153 to 260 lb and women from 153 to 200 lb take 1 to 1.5 inches; men over 260 lb and women over 200 lb take 1.5 inches. The gauge stays 22 to 25 throughout. Five eighths of an inch with 23 to 25 gauge is the row for the subcutaneous route at any age.

preguntas.pregunta: A child with Down syndrome is plotted below the usual curves. What does the technique call for?
opciones: A specialized chart for that condition is used in place of the standard one
The standard chart is kept, and the values below the curve are simply noted
The chart is dropped, and only the measurements themselves are recorded
The chart for a younger age group is used, since growth runs behind schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions that change the pattern of growth need their own plots to give a meaningful result, and specialized charts exist for Down syndrome, Turner syndrome, cerebral palsy, Williams syndrome, achondroplasia, Prader-Willi syndrome and Rett syndrome. Whatever chart is used, it contributes to the picture rather than making a diagnosis by itself.

preguntas.pregunta: Which disadvantage does the WHO device table attach to collecting blood with a hypodermic needle and syringe?
opciones: The blood has to be transferred, adding needle-stick and splash risk
It cannot be used for blood drawing in the paediatric population
It cannot be heparinized, so it is unsuitable for arterial blood samples
It requires more training than an evacuated tube system

preguntas.pregunta: When is compression-only CPR accepted instead of compressions with rescue breaths?
opciones: When the rescuer is untrained, or has no barrier device such as a rescue mask
When the patient is a child, whose arrest usually starts as a heart problem
When two rescuers are present and the compressor is being rotated often
When an advanced airway is already in place and the breaths are given separately
preguntas.explicacion: Compression-only CPR is an acceptable alternative for the untrained layperson, and also for a trained rescuer outside the hospital who has no barrier device such as a rescue mask. Once an advanced airway is in place the opposite happens: compressions run without interruption and breaths are given at 10 a minute, which is not compression-only CPR.

opciones: A report of the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be reviewed
A report of the claims paid under its identifier, to be matched against postings
A list of the patients whose coverage lapsed, to be corrected before the next visit
A bill for the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be paid monthly

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the only thing taken that morning before a fasting draw was a cup of black coffee, no sugar. Under the guidance on fasting samples, is the specimen acceptable?
opciones: No: during the fasting period water is acceptable, but coffee and other drinks such as energy drinks are not allowed
Yes: black coffee without sugar adds no calories and is treated the same way as plain water during a fast
Yes, provided the coffee was taken more than 2 hours before the draw and the patient then drank plain water
No: coffee is allowed only together with the morning medicines, which this patient did not take
preguntas.explicacion: Morning sampling after a fast of at least 12 hours since the last solid meal is the recommended condition; water during the fasting period is acceptable, but other drinks, coffee and energy drinks included, are not allowed on the morning of the procedure, and alcohol is avoided for the 24 hours before. Non-fasting samples are accepted only for patients who cannot tolerate the fast, for emergencies and for parameters that fasting does not affect; fasting status is double-checked once identification is verified.

preguntas.pregunta: A refrigerator that stores patient samples and control materials is typically kept in which temperature range?
preguntas.explicacion: The usual sample refrigerator runs between 2 and 8 °C, a sample freezer between −25 and −15 °C, and rooms used for testing and storage between 15 and 30 °C. The correct range for any unit is ultimately set by the acceptable storage range in the manufacturer's instructions for what is kept in it. Temperatures are checked and recorded daily, and the testing room before it is used, whatever monitoring device is installed.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's history shows a right radical mastectomy. Which precaution applies when choosing where to draw?
opciones: Avoid drawing from the arm on the side of the mastectomy
Draw from the right arm but use a smaller-gauge needle
Draw from the right hand only, never from the antecubital fossa
Draw from either arm, as long as the tourniquet stays under one minute
preguntas.explicacion: A history of ipsilateral radical mastectomy is listed among the site contraindications, together with scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or abscess, a vascular graft, a hematoma, venous fibrosis, and any venous access device such as a port, central catheter or IV. The same rule appears in capillary testing: avoid the side of a recent mastectomy or an ongoing infusion.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a copayment and coinsurance?
opciones: A copayment is a set dollar figure per service and coinsurance is a percentage of it
A copayment is a percentage of the service and coinsurance is a set dollar figure
A copayment is owed before the deductible and coinsurance replaces the deductible
A copayment is owed monthly for coverage and coinsurance is owed at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: A copayment is a fixed amount, $20 for instance, that the patient pays for a covered service. Coinsurance is a share expressed as a percentage of the allowed amount, 20% for instance, so the dollars change with the price of the service. Both are usually owed after the deductible is satisfied. The monthly amount owed for the coverage itself, used or not, is the premium.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with new angina is booked for a Holter as the first test. Why is that the wrong step?
opciones: Because a monitor that holds up urgent care is contraindicated
Because palpitations once a week are too rare for a monitor
Because a patient with a pacemaker cannot wear a monitor
Because strong fields at work would spoil the recording

preguntas.pregunta: How should paper records and prescription labels that contain PHI be disposed of?
