Placed in a red biohazard bag and treated as regulated waste
Handed to the person in charge of shredding to take home and destroy later
Kept in a locked cabinet indefinitely, since PHI may never be destroyed

preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the CDC say about squeezing the wound or applying bleach to it?

Squeezing is recommended to expel contaminated blood; bleach is not advised
Bleach at a 1:10 dilution is recommended on the wound; squeezing is not
Both are recommended right away, before the wound is washed with soap and water
preguntas.explicacion: No scientific evidence shows that using antiseptics or squeezing the wound reduces the risk of transmitting a bloodborne pathogen, and a caustic agent such as bleach is not recommended. That the plaintiff's account is proven beyond any reasonable doubt
That the plaintiff's account is supported by two expert witnesses
That the plaintiff's account is admitted by the treating clinician

preguntas.pregunta: A practice writes down which staff member took which laptop out of the building and when it came back. Which specification does that log satisfy?
opciones: Accountability, a record of hardware movements and of the person answering for them
Maintenance records, a record of repairs made to doors, walls and locks in the office
Workstation use, which fixes what may be done at a given class of workstation
Facility security plan, which guards the premises and its equipment against theft
preguntas.explicacion: Accountability sits under device and media controls, and it is the addressable specification that asks for a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and of who is responsible for them. Maintenance records look at the building itself, not at the equipment that travels.
preguntas.subtema: Media accountability · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands over a new insurance card at check-in. Which step protects the claim best?
opciones: Verifying coverage and benefits with the plan before the visit is billed
Filing the card in the paper chart and billing the plan listed last year
Asking the patient to state the group number aloud instead of copying it
Waiting for the remittance advice to reveal which plan is now primary
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of patient data prevents rejections, delays and denials: insurance eligibility belongs on the list of items to confirm before the claim goes out, along with the name, the age and the billing address. Billing last year's plan invites a denial for coverage that has ended, an oral group number adds an error, and learning it from the remittance advice means the denial already happened.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Patient Data Verification
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMAA 5B k66, 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: To save time, a phlebotomist prints and sticks labels on all the tubes at the nursing station before entering the patient's room. What is wrong with this practice?
opciones: Tube identification and labeling must be done in the presence of the patient to avoid misidentification
Labels printed in advance lose their adhesive and can peel off during centrifugation or refrigeration
Tubes must be labeled only after the draw is complete, and the label must be applied later at the accessioning desk
Pre-printed labels are acceptable only when the requisition is placed outside the transport bag
preguntas.explicacion: Both identifying the tube and applying its label are done with the patient present, so that the tube cannot be matched to the wrong person; before the draw the patient's identification data and the tube labels are double-checked against each other. Labeling away from the patient, whether before at the station or later at the accessioning desk, breaks that link. The transport bag pocket is a separate rule about the requisition, not about when to label.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and tube labeling)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which professionals may serve as her primary care provider. What is accurate?
opciones: Doctors, nurses, nurse practitioners and physician assistants may all serve
Only doctors of medicine and doctors of osteopathic medicine may serve
Only physicians who completed a family practice residency may serve
Any licensed health worker, a pharmacist or a dietitian included, may serve as one
preguntas.explicacion: Primary care providers include doctors, nurses, nurse practitioners and physician assistants. The primary care provider is the person a patient sees first for checkups and health problems and who helps manage overall health. Family practitioners, pediatricians, geriatricians, internists and obstetrician-gynecologists are among the physician types who take that role.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Primary care; and MedlinePlus, Choosing a primary care provider
preguntas.subtema: General vs specialty care · CCMA 1A k7 · NCMA 3.1

preguntas.pregunta: Setting newborns aside, where inside the hospital did the seven-year study find the highest proportion of hemolysed serum?
opciones: The emergency department, at 6.81 %, ahead of intensive care at 5.93 %
Intensive care, at 6.81 %, ahead of the emergency department at 5.93 % of sera
The inpatient wards, whose draws are done with a straight needle
The outpatient clinics, whose samples travel longest before separation
preguntas.explicacion: Across 1,882,721 serum samples the general patient population sat at 3.33 %, but the two areas where patients are sickest ran higher: 6.81 % in the emergency department, with 1.73 % of tests rejected, and 5.93 % in intensive care, with 0.97 % rejected. The authors read that gap as an argument for training the staff who collect in those areas.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Both parents of a covered child were born on May 12. Which plan is primary for the child?
opciones: The plan that has covered its parent for the longer period of time
The plan that has covered its parent for the shorter period of time
The plan of the parent who carries the family coverage at work
The plan of the parent who claims the child on the tax return
preguntas.explicacion: When both parents have the same birthday, the model rule turns to the plan that has covered the parent the longest, and that plan becomes primary for the child. The shorter coverage is therefore secondary. Which parent holds family coverage or claims the child as a tax dependent does not enter the order of benefit determination.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: What do senior centers funded under the aging network typically coordinate?
opciones: Congregate meals, community education, health screening and transportation
Congregate meals and skilled nursing care delivered inside the center
Long-term services counseling and help applying for disability programs
Legal protection and advocacy for the civil rights of older adults
preguntas.explicacion: Grants to states and territories fund multi-purpose senior centers, which pull together congregate meals, community education, health screening, exercise and health promotion programs, and transportation. Counseling about long-term services belongs to the resource centers, and rights advocacy to the protection and advocacy systems.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Administration for Community Living: Aging and Disability Networks
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4D k164 community resources · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Why is telehealth put forward as a way to reduce disparities in rural areas?
opciones: One in five people in the country live in rural and frontier areas
One in two people in the country live in rural and frontier areas
Rural residents are the only group a health center may enroll
Rural clinics may bill only for services given by telehealth
preguntas.explicacion: One in five people in the United States live in rural and frontier areas. Those communities have greater health care needs and more limited access to timely services, so telehealth is presented as a way to cut disparities by widening access to timely, high-quality care. Even without broadband, some services can go by phone, secure messaging and asynchronous care.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Telehealth for rural areas — Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Technology-based care · CCMA 1A k5

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these makes a seizure in the office an emergency call rather than something to watch?
opciones: It is the first seizure that this patient has ever had
The patient bit the side of the tongue during the event
The patient wears a medical bracelet with seizure instructions
The patient is sleepy and confused for a few minutes afterward
preguntas.explicacion: The emergency number is called for a first seizure, for one lasting more than 2 to 5 minutes, when a second begins soon after the first, when the patient does not wake or behave normally afterward, in water, in a patient who is pregnant, injured or diabetic, or with no medical bracelet. Postictal sleepiness and tongue biting are usual findings.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist greets an 80-year-old with 'Hi sweetie, I'm here for your blood.' What should change in that greeting?
opciones: Use a formal form of address such as Mr. or Ms., and give your own name and role
Use the patient's first name to build rapport, then state your job title
Speak louder and more slowly, because most older adults have hearing loss
Address the accompanying family member first, to save the patient effort
preguntas.explicacion: Formal terms of address are the default with older patients, and familiar words like 'dear' can be taken as disrespect; staff may ask how the patient prefers to be addressed. The technique table pairs that with introducing oneself by first and last name. Shouting distorts speech and that remarks should not be aimed only at the companion.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients; and StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2D k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: Into which two chemical families are local anesthetics divided, and which family does lidocaine belong to?
opciones: Amino amides and amino esters, and lidocaine is an amino amide
Amino amides and amino esters, and lidocaine is an amino ester
Amino amides and amino ketones, and lidocaine is an amino ketone
Amino esters and amino alcohols, and lidocaine is an amino alcohol
preguntas.explicacion: The two families are amino amides and amino esters, and they differ in how the body handles them: amides go through hepatic biotransformation. Lidocaine is an amide, alongside mepivacaine, bupivacaine, levobupivacaine, ropivacaine and etidocaine; procaine, chloroprocaine, tetracaine, benzocaine and cocaine are the esters.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Topical, Local, and Regional Anesthesia and Anesthetics", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.D.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the standard say about testing the source patient's blood?
opciones: Test it as soon as feasible for HBV and HIV once consent is obtained, unless consent is not legally required
Test it only if the exposed employee first agrees to have his or her own baseline blood drawn
Test it without asking, because a patient's blood already drawn belongs to the laboratory
Do not test it; the standard bases follow-up on the employee's serology and vaccination status alone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(ii) makes identification and documentation of the source individual part of the follow-up unless it is infeasible or barred by state or local law. Under (f)(3)(ii)(A) the source's blood is tested for HBV and HIV infectivity as soon as feasible after consent; if consent is refused, the employer documents that legally required consent could not be obtained, and where the law does not require consent, available blood is tested and the results recorded. Results go to the exposed employee together with the rules on disclosing the source's identity and status.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(3)(ii)(A) and (C), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Source individual testing · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: A light blue sodium citrate tube has just been filled for a PT/INR. How should it be mixed?
opciones: Inverted gently 3 to 6 times immediately after the draw
Inverted gently 8 to 10 times immediately after the draw
Shaken vigorously for a few seconds so the anticoagulant mixes
Left upright for 10 to 15 minutes before any mixing
preguntas.explicacion: Gentle mixing means inverting the citrate tube 3 to 6 times right after the sample enters the tube; vigorous shaking can froth or hemolyse the sample and distort coagulation results. Eight to ten inversions is the figure for blood culture bottles, and the 10 to 15 minute rest is the clotting time for plain red tubes before centrifugation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report calls a growth benign. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: It may keep growing, but it does not spread to other parts of the body
It has stopped growing, and it does not spread to other parts of the body
It is growing slowly, and it spreads only through the lymph system
It is not growing at all, and it will disappear without any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Benign means not cancer. A benign tumor can still get larger, and its size may cause trouble by itself, but it does not invade nearby tissue or travel elsewhere. The opposite term is malignant: those cells grow in an uncontrolled way, invade nearby tissue and spread through the blood and lymph system.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, benign
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which method is used to decide income eligibility for Medicaid for most children, pregnant women and adults?
opciones: Modified adjusted gross income, with no asset or resource test applied
Modified adjusted gross income, with an asset test set by each state
The federal poverty guidelines applied to gross monthly wages alone
The income rules of the Supplemental Security Income program instead
preguntas.explicacion: The health care law created the modified adjusted gross income method, which uses taxable income and tax filing relationships and allows no asset or resource test and no state-specific income disregards. It also decides eligibility for CHIP and for Marketplace savings. People whose eligibility rests on age 65 and older, blindness or disability are exempt and are generally assessed with the income methods of the Supplemental Security Income program.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178

preguntas.pregunta: On a 75-g OGTT the 2-hour plasma glucose is 210 mg/dL. What does that result mean?
opciones: Diabetes, to be confirmed by repeating the test on another day
Impaired glucose tolerance, the range just below diabetes
Normal, because the 1-hour value would be under 200 mg/dL
Impaired fasting glucose, since 210 is a fasting-type value
preguntas.explicacion: A 2-hour value of 200 mg/dL or more is diagnostic of diabetes, but a single abnormal OGTT is not enough: unless the result is grossly abnormal, the test is repeated on a separate day and should give a similar result, or another recommended screening test confirms it. Roughly a fifth of OGTTs come out nondiagnostic, which is why confirmation is built into the interpretation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Testing Procedures and Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: OGTT interpretation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139

preguntas.pregunta: An infant is found unresponsive and not breathing. How are chest compressions delivered?
opciones: With the two thumbs side by side over the sternum, below the nipple line
With the heel of one hand over the lower half of the sternum, as in a child
With two fingers over the upper third of the sternum, above the nipples
With both hands wrapped around the chest, squeezing from front and back
preguntas.explicacion: The rescuer's hands encircle the infant's chest and both thumbs press together on the sternum below the nipple line, to a depth of about 1½ inches (4 cm) at 100 to 120 per minute. Two fingers on the sternum just under the nipple line is the other accepted hand position. The heel of one hand is what a child of 1 year to puberty gets.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - infant", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: An order says a dose is due at a set hour. How far from that hour should the dose be given?
opciones: Within about half an hour, since a wider gap can alter the drug's bioavailability
Within about six hours, the widest interval an around-the-clock order would use
Within about four hours, the window written into a typical order given as needed
At any point in the shift, as long as the true time is charted in the record
preguntas.explicacion: The right time means administering the medication as close as possible to the hour the prescriber intended, and the guiding principle is not to stray from it by more than about half an hour, because a longer gap can shift bioavailability and other mechanisms. Drugs given by infusion must also run at the ordered rate. Four to six hours is the window inside an as-needed order, not a tolerance for timing.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Nursing Rights of Medication Administration", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5

preguntas.pregunta: What is the out-of-pocket maximum of a health plan?
opciones: The yearly cap on what the patient pays for covered in-network care; past it, the plan pays 100%
The most the patient pays per visit for covered services; the plan pays 100% of the rest
The most the patient pays in a plan year including premiums and out-of-network care
The 2026 Marketplace cap, $10,600 per individual, which applies only to premiums
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov describes the out-of-pocket maximum, or limit, as the ceiling on what the patient spends on covered services in a plan year, not per visit. Once deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for in-network care add up to that figure, the plan covers 100% of covered benefits for the rest of the year. The glossary lists what does not count toward it: monthly premiums, out-of-network care, services the plan does not cover, and charges above the allowed amount. The $10,600 figure is the 2026 Marketplace ceiling for an individual, and it caps cost sharing, never premiums.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Out-of-pocket maximum/limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: A patient worries she will forget what was said during a video visit. Which step does the patient guidance suggest to her?
opciones: Asking the clinician afterwards to send her a summary or notes of the appointment
Recording the appointment on her own telephone so she can play it back later
Asking the clinician for a direct mobile number she can use with any question later
Asking for the same appointment to be repeated in the office later that week
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling confident in a telehealth visit includes learning how it works, taking her time, choosing a clinician who listens, asking for anything unclear to be explained, and getting a summary: she is told to ask the clinician to send a summary or notes after the visit, which can include answers to the questions she raised. Writing a list beforehand is suggested for the same reason.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Post-visit summary · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic keeps its old paper charts in a locked room and its current records in an electronic system. Which of the two does the HIPAA Security Rule govern?
opciones: Only the electronic records, since the Security Rule reaches electronic information alone
Both, since the Security Rule reaches every form in which the information is being held
Only the paper charts, since physical safeguards are what the Security Rule is about
Neither, since the Security Rule binds business associates rather than covered entities
preguntas.explicacion: The Security Rule protects a subset of protected health information: the part created, received, maintained or transmitted in electronic form. Unlike the Privacy and Breach Notification Rules, it does not reach information held on paper or spoken aloud. It binds covered entities and business associates alike, and its physical safeguards protect the systems and media that hold electronic information.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule, What Information is Protected
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.1.b HIPAA Security · CMA II.E.1.e security of electronic transmission

preguntas.pregunta: A gait belt is about to be put on a patient who is being helped to stand. How is it applied?
opciones: Around the waist over the clothing or gown, fastened with a buckle
Around the waist against the bare skin, fastened with a buckle
Around the chest over the clothing or gown, fastened with a buckle
Around the hips against the bare skin, tied rather than buckled
preguntas.explicacion: The gait belt is a two-inch-wide belt, with or without handles, that goes around the patient's waist and buckles shut. It is applied on top of clothing or a gown, which protects the patient's skin. Belts of this kind are used for standing, walking and moving from bed to chair.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Gait Belts
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA 2A.5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with obesity is discouraged because she has lost only 6 percent of her weight. How should that be framed?
opciones: Reaching 5 percent already counts as a successful response to treatment
Reaching 5 percent is a starting point but no benefit appears before 15
Reaching a healthy BMI is the only result that counts as a success
Reaching 25 percent is the target set for every patient with obesity
preguntas.explicacion: At least 5 percent weight loss is the recommended initial goal in obesity management, and hitting it counts as a success when the response to treatment is judged. Losing 5 to 10 percent already lowers the risk of diabetes and coronary artery disease. Realistic goals are advised precisely because slow progress makes people quit.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dietary Approaches to Obesity Treatment", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a)

preguntas.pregunta: On the PHQ-9, which score points toward possible major depression?
opciones: A score of 10 or more, out of a possible 27
A score of 5 or more, out of a possible 27
A score of 15 or more, out of a possible 21
A score of 20 or more, out of a possible 30
preguntas.explicacion: The 9 items track the diagnostic criteria and also gauge psychosocial impairment. The scale runs from 0 to 27, and a score at or above 10 indicates possible major depression. In hospital settings the clinician-administered Hamilton scale is the one more often used.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Major Depressive Disorder", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Mental health conditions · CCMA 1E k30

preguntas.pregunta: How much paper capacity does the SAFER contingency practice expect each patient care area to hold for a downtime?
opciones: Enough forms to care for its patients for at least eight hours
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least three days
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least thirty days
Enough forms to care for one shift of scheduled visits only
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended practice is that paper forms be available to replace key EHR functions during downtimes, because clinical and administrative operations have to continue. The implementation guidance sets the stock at enough forms in each patient care area to care for its patients for at least eight hours, including the forms needed to enter orders and to document medications, laboratory and radiology tests.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which question is a proper teach-back after explaining a 12-hour fast?
opciones: 'So I know I explained it well, what will you do the night before the test?'
'Does that make sense to you, or should I go over it once more?'
'Do you have any questions about the fasting instructions I gave?'
'You'll remember all of this tomorrow morning, won't you?'
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back is framed as a non-shaming check on how well the clinician explained, with examples such as asking what the patient will tell a partner about the visit. The question must require the patient to restate the plan in their own words. 'Does that make sense' and any yes-or-no form are excluded, and inviting questions is a separate step in Tool 4.

preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor reviews haemolysed samples from a children's clinic. Which two examples of too great a vacuum are given?
opciones: An oversized tube on a child, or a syringe of ten to twenty millilitres
An oversized tube on an adult, or a syringe of one to two millilitres
A reduced-vacuum paediatric tube, or a syringe of two to five millilitres
A butterfly set on an adult, or a syringe of ten to twenty millilitres
preguntas.explicacion: Excessive vacuum is listed as a cause of haemolysis, and the two examples given are a tube too large for a paediatric patient and a syringe of ten to twenty millilitres. The matching remedy in the device table is a smaller tube of one to five millilitres with a lower vacuum for children.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient using a home oximeter reads 87%. What is the instruction?
opciones: Seek immediate medical attention: 88% or lower calls for emergency care
Call the provider during office hours, as 92% or lower is the reporting level
Repeat the reading in the morning, since a single value is not acted upon
Change the sensor to the other hand and act only if the value stays under 80%
preguntas.explicacion: Two thresholds are given for home monitoring: at 92% or lower the provider is contacted, and at 88% or lower the patient seeks immediate attention. A reading of 87% is in the second group. Bluish lips or nails, trouble breathing, chest tightness and a fast heart rate are the signs that go with a low value.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry

preguntas.pregunta: Which service does Medicare refuse to pay for under the home health benefit?
opciones: Care in the home 24 hours a day, and meals delivered to the house
Wound care for a pressure sore given by a visiting skilled nurse
Physical therapy, occupational therapy and speech-language services
Osteoporosis injections for women who meet the stated criteria
preguntas.explicacion: The benefit does not pay for care at home around the clock, for meals delivered to the house, for homemaker work such as shopping and cleaning unrelated to the care plan, or for custodial personal care when that is the only care the patient needs. It does pay for skilled nursing, the three therapies, medical social services, equipment and supplies used at home.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Coverage details

preguntas.pregunta: Before a Medicare deductible or coinsurance amount can be written off as bad debt, how long must the collection effort last?
opciones: At least 120 days from the billing that started the collection effort
At least 30 days from the billing that started the collection effort
At least 12 months from the date the service was given to the patient
Until a collection agency reports that the account cannot be collected
preguntas.explicacion: For cost reporting periods that start on or after October 1, 2020, the bill reaches the beneficiary within 120 days of the remittance advice or the secondary payer's response, and the collection effort must then continue at least 120 days before the amount is written off as uncollectible. A payment received inside that window starts a new 120-day period, and the effort has to match what the provider does for non-Medicare patients.

preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old is crying and squirming while you try to count the pulse. Which approach suits the arteries of a child that age?
opciones: Use the pads of two fingers with gentle pressure, and settle the child first
Press until the beat disappears and then ease off slowly to pick it up again
Press hard with a single fingertip, since small arteries sit deep in the tissue
Count during the crying, since crying steadies the rate and makes it easier
preguntas.explicacion: A young child's arteries are smaller and closer to the surface than an adult's, so they compress easily and are harder to find. The pads of the index and middle fingers keep the examiner's own pulse out of the count and apply pressure gentle enough not to close the vessel. preguntas.pregunta: What defines a sentinel event, as opposed to a preventable adverse event?
opciones: The severity of the outcome, rather than what caused it
The cause being a medical error, rather than the outcome
The event reaching a patient, rather than being a near miss
The event being reported to an accrediting organization
preguntas.explicacion: A preventable adverse event is defined by causation: harm produced by a medical error or by inaction. A sentinel event is defined by outcome severity, a safety event that reaches a patient and results in death, severe harm or permanent harm. preguntas.pregunta: Besides acting as a barrier, which vitamin does the skin synthesize when it is exposed to ultraviolet light?

Vitamin A, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what counts as a drug interaction. What is the answer?
opciones: A reaction between a drug and another drug, a food, a supplement or a disease
A reaction between a drug and another drug taken at the very same hour only
A reaction between a drug and a food, which no prescription drug can produce
A reaction between two drugs that share the same active ingredient exactly
preguntas.explicacion: An interaction is a reaction between a drug and other drugs, foods, beverages, supplements or diseases, and it is counted among the Type A adverse reactions. The coronal plane, a vertical plane running from side to side
The transverse plane, a horizontal plane through the body
The oblique plane, an angled cut across the other three

preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker exposed to hepatitis B, how well does immune globulin plus starting the vaccine work?
opciones: More than 90% effective at preventing infection
About 50% effective at preventing the infection
About 60% effective, like a booster dose alone
Around 30% effective, as the vaccine alone is

Because Medicare pays interest on the claim only when the code is entered right

Alcohol evaporates from an open jar and is too weak to prepare the skin
Cotton fibres stick to the puncture site and cause the wound to keep oozing

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between active and passive immunity?
opciones: Active is made by the person's own immune system and usually lasts for years
Active is transferred antibody, so protection is immediate but wears off fast
Active comes only from surviving the disease, never from being vaccinated
Active is the antibody an infant receives across the placenta before birth
preguntas.explicacion: Active immunity is protection produced by the person's own immune system after an antigen stimulates antibody-mediated and cell-mediated responses, and it usually lasts for years or for life; surviving the infection and being vaccinated are the two ways to acquire it. preguntas.pregunta: What separates a Type A adverse drug reaction from a Type B one?

Type A is immune mediated and rare, while Type B follows the known pharmacology
Type A appears only in children, while Type B appears only in older patients
Type A is reported to the FDA, while Type B is handled inside the practice alone
preguntas.explicacion: Type A reactions arise from the known pharmacological properties of the drug and can happen to anyone given a sufficient dose; they make up 85% to 90% of adverse reactions and cover overdose, side effects and drug interactions. preguntas.pregunta: In the common pathway of coagulation, what is the job of thrombin?

Turns inactive prothrombin into its active form
Cross-links and stabilizes the fibrin clot
Degrades the fibrin once the vessel has healed

preguntas.pregunta: A fasting plasma glucose of 112 mg/dL on the baseline sample of an OGTT falls into which category?
opciones: Impaired fasting glucose (100 to 125 mg/dL)
Normal fasting glucose (60 to 99 mg/dL)
Diabetes (126 mg/dL or higher on two tests)
Impaired glucose tolerance (140 to 199 mg/dL)
preguntas.explicacion: Impaired fasting glucose is a fasting plasma glucose of 100 to 125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L); the WHO and some other bodies set the lower limit at 110. A normal fasting value runs 60 to 99 mg/dL, and 126 mg/dL or higher on two different tests diagnoses diabetes. Impaired glucose tolerance is defined by the 2-hour post-load value, not by the fasting sample.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has some muscle strength but cannot get from sitting to standing alone. Which device is made for that?
opciones: A sit-to-stand lift, for weight-bearing patients who lack the strength
A mechanical lift with a sling, for patients who cannot bear weight
A slider board, for moving a patient lying supine between surfaces
A gait belt with handles, for a patient who cannot bear weight at all
preguntas.explicacion: Sit-to-stand lifts are for patients who bear weight but cannot rise on their own strength; some are mechanized and some are not. The hydraulic lift with a sling is for the patient who cannot bear weight at all, and the slider board moves a patient who is lying flat from one surface to another.

preguntas.pregunta: How does CHAMPVA pay for the care its beneficiaries receive?
opciones: It shares the cost of certain covered services and supplies with the beneficiary
It pays the full cost of every service the beneficiary receives from any provider
It reimburses the beneficiary only after the private insurer has denied the claim
It pays a fixed amount to the beneficiary each month toward medical expenses
preguntas.explicacion: CHAMPVA is described as a cost-sharing program: once the person is enrolled, the Department of Veterans Affairs shares the cost of certain health care services and supplies with the beneficiary, so it neither covers everything nor sends a monthly allowance. preguntas.pregunta: A patient on a sodium restriction reads 20% Daily Value for sodium on a label. How should he read that number?
opciones: That serving is high in sodium, since 20% or more counts as high
That serving is moderate in sodium, since high starts at 40%
That serving is low in sodium, since low means under 25% DV
That serving supplies a fifth of the sodium he is allowed each week
preguntas.explicacion: The general guide on the label puts 5% of the Daily Value or less at the low end and 20% or more at the high end, for any nutrient. The specific situation or behavior, with concrete data
How the situation makes the speaker feel about it
The alternatives on offer, while seeking agreement

opciones: One check or funds transfer, covering all the benefits due on that remittance
One check or funds transfer for each claim itemized on that same remittance
One check for the claims paid in full and a second for those paid in part
One funds transfer each week, however many remittances it happens to cover

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic keeps a tidy temperature log that nobody has ever countersigned. Who is supposed to sign it, and how often?

The staff member who took the readings, at the end of every working week
The laboratory director of the reference laboratory, once a calendar quarter
The manufacturer's field representative, at each preventive maintenance visit
preguntas.explicacion: Each reading is dated and initialled or signed by whoever took it, and on top of that the person who directs or supervises the testing reviews and signs the log once it is complete for the month. Repeating the patient's words back to show she is being followed
Putting the patient's account into the listener's own words
Offering guiding statements so the patient makes a point clearer
preguntas.explicacion: Nodding and small phrases such as “Uh-huh”, “I see” or “Go on” are listed as verbal and nonverbal cues that keep the conversation going and show the patient is being listened to. preguntas.pregunta: Which assembly generates the pressure recommended for irrigating a laceration?
opciones: A 35 to 50 mL syringe with a 19-gauge catheter, giving 25 to 40 PSI
A 35 to 50 mL syringe with no catheter, poured gently over the wound
A 10 mL syringe with a 25-gauge needle, giving well above 70 PSI
A bulb syringe held against the skin, giving 25 to 40 PSI of pressure
preguntas.explicacion: A large syringe with a plastic catheter on the end, pushed with both hands, produces about 25 to 40 pounds per square inch, which is enough to lift debris and bacteria out without driving them deeper; above 70 the tissue itself is injured. Normal saline is the usual solution, and roughly 50 mL is used for each centimeter of wound length.

Only the clinician, at the end of the consultation that ordered the test

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.13, when must a hospital inform patients of their rights?
opciones: In advance of furnishing or discontinuing care, whenever possible
Within 30 days of admission, in a written notice signed by the patient
Only when the patient or a representative files a formal grievance
At discharge, together with the billing statement and visitation policy
preguntas.explicacion: The first standard of 482.13, notice of rights, requires the hospital to inform each patient, or the patient's representative where state law allows, of the patient's rights in advance of furnishing or discontinuing care whenever possible. The same standard requires a grievance process with a clear procedure for written or verbal grievances, time frames for review and a written decision naming the contact person, the steps taken and the result. Visitation rights are explained at the same time as the other rights, not at discharge.

preguntas.pregunta: A front desk moving to open access is told its single rule is to do today's work today. Which habit does that ask the staff to drop?
opciones: Sorting callers by clinical urgency, since demand is now sorted by clinician instead
Booking the follow-up visits a clinician asked for, since those slots are needed today
Offering a caller a later day, since under this model nobody may decline the same-day slot
Counting how many slots were free yesterday, since only the supply of time is measured
preguntas.explicacion: The model breaks with the traditional split between urgent and routine, which is what pushes routine care back. Instead of triaging callers by urgency, reception simply sorts the demand by clinician. Clinically necessary follow-ups are still booked ahead, patients may still choose a later day, and the practice has to measure both supply and demand as precisely as it can.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention

Reading the explanation of benefits her insurer prepared for the last visit
Setting the allowed amount her plan will pay for the appointment she booked

preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, protective equipment counts as appropriate only when it does what?
opciones: Keeps blood from reaching work clothes, skin, eyes or mouth for as long as it is worn
Carries the manufacturer's label with the biohazard symbol printed in orange-red
Is picked by the employee from the sizes the supplier keeps in stock at the site
Is worn over the uniform, which the standard also counts as protective clothing
preguntas.explicacion: The definition of appropriate in paragraph (d)(3)(i) is a performance test, not a brand or a label: under normal conditions of use, and for the whole time it will be worn, the item must not let blood or other potentially infectious materials through to the work clothes, street clothes, undergarments, skin, eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes. Paragraph (d)(3)(iii) is what puts the right sizes within reach; and the definitions in (b) exclude ordinary uniforms, pants and shirts from being protective equipment at all.

preguntas.pregunta: The provider documents that a condition is probable, with testing still pending, at an office visit. How is it coded?
opciones: Code the signs and symptoms, since uncertain diagnoses are not coded in the office
Code the probable condition, since the provider named it in the encounter note
Code the probable condition and add the symptoms as additional diagnoses after it
Hold the claim until the testing confirms or rules out the suspected condition
preguntas.explicacion: For outpatient services and office visits, terms such as probable, suspected, questionable, rule out or working diagnosis are not coded. The encounter is coded to the highest degree of certainty available: symptoms, signs, abnormal test results or another reason for the visit. That practice differs from the inpatient rules, which is why the guidelines flag it, and nothing requires holding the claim.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the red-grey tiger top or gold serum separator tube separate the serum, according to the WHO table?
opciones: A gel at the bottom of the tube separates blood from serum when it is centrifuged
A clot activator on the tube wall makes the blood clot so the serum can be poured off
Lithium heparin keeps the blood liquid and a gel separates the plasma on spinning
Sodium citrate binds calcium and the serum rises above the cells within an hour
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists no additive for the serum separator tube and describes its action as a gel at the bottom that separates blood from serum on centrifugation, for chemistries, immunology and serology. The clot activator belongs to the plain red tube; lithium heparin with a gel is the light green PST, which yields plasma; and sodium citrate is the coagulation tube, which never yields serum.

preguntas.pregunta: A 60-year-old reports knee pain that worsens with activity and eases with rest, plus morning stiffness that clears in about twenty minutes. Which diagnosis fits?
opciones: Osteoarthritis, the most common form of arthritis
Osteoporosis, the most common form of arthritis
Rheumatoid arthritis, the most common form of arthritis
Osteomalacia, the most common form of arthritis
preguntas.explicacion: Osteoarthritis is a clinical diagnosis, and the picture is consistent: pain worse with activity and better with rest, age over 45, morning stiffness under thirty minutes, bony joint enlargement and limited range of motion. Osteoporosis is loss of bone mass, not a joint disease, and it usually causes no symptoms until something breaks.

preguntas.pregunta: Which routinely recommended vaccines are live, attenuated products?
opciones: MMR, varicella, rotavirus and intranasal influenza
MMR, varicella, hepatitis B and injected influenza
Rotavirus, tetanus, pneumococcal and hepatitis A
Varicella, polio by injection, HPV and pneumococcal
preguntas.explicacion: The live, attenuated viral vaccines routinely recommended in the United States are MMR, varicella, rotavirus and the intranasal influenza vaccine. Adenovirus, typhoid Ty21a and BCG are live but not routinely recommended. Because a live vaccine replicates, it can cause severe infection in someone whose immune system is weakened by leukemia, certain drugs or HIV infection, which is why screening comes first.

preguntas.pregunta: A worker who never reached a protective anti-HBs level after two complete vaccine series is exposed to an HBsAg-positive source. Per the CDC table, what is given?
opciones: Two doses of HBIG, the first right away and the second one month later
One dose of HBIG plus the start of a third complete vaccine series
A single vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months later
No further treatment, since two series show the worker is a documented responder
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's guidance for vaccinated clinicians with anti-HBs below 10 mIU/mL after two complete series says that if the source is HBsAg-positive or unknown, the clinician receives two doses of HBIG, the first as soon as possible and the second 1 month later, and that further vaccine is not recommended because two series have already failed. If the source is HBsAg-negative, neither HBIG nor vaccine is needed. WHO's Table D.1 groups known non-responders with the unvaccinated for HBIG, but the CDC table is the more specific source here.

No, but a small practice may write a note in the contingency plan in place of it

preguntas.pregunta: While transferring blood from a syringe, a phlebotomist pushes the plunger to speed up filling of a slow tube. What does the WHO say about this?
opciones: Do not press the plunger; the extra pressure raises the risk of haemolysis
Press the plunger only for tubes with additives, which need a full draw
Press the plunger gently once the stopper has been removed from the tube
Pressing is acceptable for the last tube, once the tourniquet has been released
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 instructs the phlebotomist to pierce the stopper from directly above with slow, steady pressure and not to press the syringe plunger, because additional pressure increases the risk of haemolysis; for tubes without a rubber stopper it asks for an extremely slow injection for the same reason. There is no exception for additive tubes, for the last tube, or after removing the stopper.

preguntas.pregunta: An unvaccinated phlebotomist is stuck by a needle used on an HBsAg-positive patient. According to the CDC, what is given and when?
opciones: HBIG and the first vaccine dose, as soon as possible and preferably within 24 hours, at separate sites
The vaccine series only, started within 7 days, since HBIG is reserved for known non-responders
HBIG only, repeated one month later, since starting the vaccine after exposure is too late
A 28-day antiviral course started within 72 hours, followed by the vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's table for unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated clinicians exposed to an HBsAg-positive or unknown source calls for one dose of HBIG plus the hepatitis B vaccine, given as soon as possible, at a different anatomical site such as a separate limb, with the series completed on schedule and anti-HBs tested 1 to 2 months after the last dose. The older brochure says HBV post-exposure treatment should start preferably within 24 hours and no later than 7 days. Two HBIG doses a month apart are for non-responders after two series; the 28-day antiviral course is HIV PEP.

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of definitions is correct for morbidity and mortality?
opciones: Morbidity is the state of being diseased; mortality refers to death
Morbidity refers to death; mortality is the state of being diseased
Morbidity is the cause of a disease; mortality is its likely outcome
Morbidity is the spread of a disease; mortality is its rate of cure
preguntas.explicacion: Morbidity is the state of being diseased and can be given as a plain count or as a rate per 100,000 of the population. Mortality is death, and its rate is expressed the same two ways. Cause and likely outcome are etiology and prognosis, which answer different questions altogether.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is called to draw blood in the fluoroscopy suite while imaging is under way. Which protection is meant for that setting?
opciones: A lead apron, leaded glasses and cap, and a thyroid collar
A fluid-resistant gown, a face shield and two pairs of gloves
An N95 respirator with eye protection, as for airborne cases
A chemical-resistant suit with a self-contained air supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where x-ray and gamma radiation are in use, especially in fluoroscopy and other image-guided procedures, the protective equipment is leaded: an apron or vest, leaded glasses, a leaded cap and a protective collar, all of which reduce the dose received. Dose monitoring with a personal dosimeter is required for workers who enter a high radiation or restricted area, or who receive more than a quarter of the occupational limit in a calendar quarter.

opciones: Read it for any excursion during transit and then discard it, since it is single use
Read it for any excursion during transit and place it inside the storage unit
File it with the packing list as the record of the temperature during transit
Return it to the distributor with the shipping container for its next journey

preguntas.pregunta: What does the guideline say about flash sterilizing an implantable device?
opciones: Avoid it; if it is unavoidable, record the load, the patient and the biological indicator result
Avoid it; if it is unavoidable, extend the cycle to 45 minutes so the lethality is comparable
It is acceptable routinely, as long as the item is cleaned before it goes into the container
It is acceptable routinely, as long as the item is cooled in sterile saline before it is used
preguntas.explicacion: Because the infections that follow can be serious, flash sterilization is not recommended for devices placed into a body cavity. When it cannot be avoided, the load identification, the patient identifier and the biological indicator result have to be recorded so the item can be traced. Cleaning first and cooling before use are required anyway, and neither makes the practice routine.

preguntas.pregunta: What are absorbable sutures mainly used for?
opciones: Deep, temporary closure that holds tissue layers together until the tissue itself heals
Long-term closure such as vessel anastomosis and permanent ligation of internal structures
Superficial closure of the face, where they leave the least inflammation and scarring
Closure of fascia and tendon, tissues that heal too slowly for a dissolving material
preguntas.explicacion: A suture counts as absorbable when it loses most of its tensile strength over weeks to months, which suits deep, temporary closure: approximating tissue layers, closing dead space and defects inside a multi-layered repair. Used superficially they cause more inflammation and scarring, so a rapidly absorbing one is chosen there. Slow-healing fascia and tendon call for non-absorbable material.

preguntas.pregunta: How long must a practice keep its privacy policies, its notices and its records of complaints?

Five years from creation, the period Medicare sets for hospital medical record retention
Seven years from creation, the period set for documentation of orders and certifications
Thirty years from creation, the period OSHA sets for employee exposure records

The five, seven and thirty year figures come from Medicare and OSHA rules about other kinds of record.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports taking high-dose vitamin C supplements. Which two dipstick pads are most likely to give a false-negative result?
opciones: Occult blood and glucose
Protein and bilirubin
pH and specific gravity
Ketones and urobilinogen
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is listed as a cause of false-negative reactions on exactly two pads, blood and glucose, alongside an elevated specific gravity for each. The blood pad detects the peroxidase activity of erythrocytes, hemoglobin and myoglobin, and the glucose pad turns positive once the filtered glucose exceeds what the tubules reabsorb. Protein, bilirubin, ketones and pH have other listed interferents, such as alkaline urine for protein or a stale specimen for bilirubin.

preguntas.pregunta: Which facility falls outside the CLIA definition of a laboratory?
opciones: A draw station that only collects and prepares specimens, with no testing
A physician office that performs only waived tests on its own patients
A hospital laboratory accredited by a CMS-approved organization
A mobile unit that performs hematology testing on human specimens
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA defines a laboratory as a facility that examines materials from the human body, by biological, microbiological, serological, chemical, hematological or similar methods, to provide information for diagnosis, prevention, treatment or health assessment, and it states that facilities that only collect or prepare specimens, or only serve as a mailing service, without performing testing are not laboratories. A waived-testing office and a mobile unit that runs hematology tests both perform examinations and therefore need a certificate; a pure collection site does not.

preguntas.pregunta: In which forms is medication supplied for the vaginal route?
opciones: Foams, creams, tablets and suppositories that melt with the heat of the body
Foams, creams and coated tablets that are swallowed with a full glass of water
Powders for reconstitution and metered aerosols delivered through a spacer device
Ointments and skin patches that are pressed firmly in place for about ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Vaginal instillation is used mostly for hormone therapy and antifungal treatment, and the medication comes as foam, cream, tablet, or a suppository that melts at body heat. The patient is asked to void first and is positioned on the back with the knees flexed; perineal care is done, gloves are changed, and the applicator is filled and inserted. Privacy is part of the procedure, not an extra.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a formal referral agreement between a practice and a specialist group spell out?
opciones: Which patients to refer, what information is shared, and each side's role afterward
The fee the specialist will charge and how the two practices split the payment
The number of patients the practice promises to send in a calendar year
Which insurance plans the specialist agrees to accept from those patients
preguntas.explicacion: Referral agreements set out mutual expectations: which patients are appropriate to refer, how the referral is transmitted, what information travels before and after it, appointments held open for urgent referrals, and what each side does once the referral is made. Making the process easy raises the odds the patient follows through.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of the safety devices and sharps containers a draw station uses every day?
opciones: They are examined and maintained or replaced on a regular schedule so they keep working
They are examined only after an exposure incident has been reported and logged
They are replaced every three years, the period set for keeping training records
They are checked by the manufacturer at installation and then left in service
preguntas.explicacion: Engineering controls are the devices that take the hazard away from the worker: sharps disposal containers, self-sheathing needles, needleless systems. Paragraph (d)(2)(ii) says they have to be examined and either maintained or replaced on a regular schedule, so that they still do what they were bought to do. Waiting for an injury reverses that logic, and the three-year figure is the retention period for training records in (h)(2)(ii), not a replacement interval.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes is too drowsy to swallow and the glucose meter reads 42 mg/dL. Which emergency medicine is indicated?
opciones: Glucagon, given into the muscle or by the newer intranasal form
Glucose tablets, placed under the tongue until they dissolve there
Epinephrine, injected into the outer part of the thigh right away
Insulin, given subcutaneously to move the glucose into the cells
preguntas.explicacion: A conscious patient who can swallow gets a readily absorbed carbohydrate such as fruit juice; when the patient cannot take anything by mouth, glucagon is the answer, given intramuscularly or by the newer intranasal preparations. Once the patient is awake, a complex carbohydrate follows and the glucose is rechecked more often.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a hematoma, and which two technique errors cause it?
opciones: Blood pooled under the skin; a needle pushed beyond the vein lumen, or too little pressure during and after the draw
Pinpoint bleeding into the dermis; leaving the tourniquet on too long, or using a needle that is too small
Pooling of blood under the skin; shaking the tube after filling, or drawing the tubes out of sequence
Bleeding into the skin larger than 2 mm; drawing from the basilic vein, or using povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma is the pooling of blood under the skin, and two errors are linked to it: deep insertion of the needle beyond the lumen of the vein, and failure to apply adequate pressure during and after the draw. The WHO adds a third, letting the patient bend the arm. Pinpoint dermal bleeding is petechiae, and spots larger than 2 mm are purpura in the petechiae chapter.

preguntas.pregunta: When is a mattress stitch chosen?
opciones: For a deeper wound, since the deeper bite minimizes tension and holds the edges together
For a shallow wound, since the shallow bite keeps the suture line off the dermal vessels
For a contaminated wound, since the wide bite lets exudate escape between the stitches
For a facial wound, since it is the technique that leaves the least visible scar of any
preguntas.explicacion: The mattress stitch, vertical or horizontal, goes deeper into the skin layers, which minimizes tension and closes the edges better, so it suits deeper wounds. It can be thrown in temporarily and taken out once tension is spread across the wound, or left in place when tension persists, since that lowers the risk of dehiscence.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Closure Techniques", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: What is the commonest reason for a falsely high sweat chloride result?
opciones: Evaporation of the sample during collection or handling
Collection from a stimulated area smaller than 2 inches square
Storage of the collected gauze at 4 degrees for up to 72 hours
Analysis of the sample on the day after it has been collected
preguntas.explicacion: Evaporation is the leading cause of a falsely elevated sweat chloride, so the procedure is followed carefully to prevent it and to avoid contamination. Samples are ideally analyzed the same day; gauze that must wait is reweighed at once and may be kept in a tightly closed container at 4 degrees Celsius for up to 72 hours. Sweat is never collected from two sites in one test, because chloride depends on the sweating rate.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sweat Testing", Interfering Factors and Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: What does integrative health mean?
opciones: Bringing conventional and complementary approaches together, coordinated
Replacing conventional treatment with a non-mainstream approach entirely instead
Limiting practice to herbs, vitamins, minerals and probiotic products
Treating one organ system at a time with the most specific therapy
preguntas.explicacion: Integrative health puts conventional and complementary approaches together in one coordinated plan. It stresses multimodal interventions, two or more used together such as medication, physical rehabilitation or psychotherapy alongside acupuncture, yoga or probiotics, and it aims at treating the whole person rather than one organ system, with care coordinated among providers.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinician needs to raise alcohol use with an older patient who seems reluctant. Which opening is recommended?
opciones: Framing it as something many people in her situation face
Asking a direct yes-or-no question early in the interview
Handing her a brochure instead of raising it out loud
Asking the companion about it while she is out of the room
preguntas.explicacion: The technique offered for broaching sensitive subjects is a universal, nonthreatening approach that presents the topic as a common concern among older patients, with openings such as many people experience this. Informative brochures left in the exam room are the fallback for patients who still avoid the subject, not the opening move.

preguntas.pregunta: Burnout among health care professionals is described as which three-part response?
opciones: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, low accomplishment
Emotional exhaustion, anxiety, and impaired concentration
Irritability, absenteeism, and reduced clinical competence
Fatigue, compassion for patients, and a heavier workload
preguntas.explicacion: Burnout is a job-related stress syndrome made of emotional exhaustion, depersonalization and reduced personal accomplishment, arising as a prolonged response to chronic occupational stressors. National surveys have repeatedly put prevalence near or above 50 percent, which frames it as a system problem.

opciones: The patient's own anxiety
Sitting at the patient's level
Use of open-ended questions
Introducing yourself by name
preguntas.explicacion: The barriers reported in studies are: the patient's anxiety, under-recognition of cultural differences, colloquial language differences, overworked providers, shortages of time or staff, fear of abuse or litigation, and unrealistic patient expectations. preguntas.pregunta: Two medical assistants are giving CPR to a 4-year-old child. Which compression-to-ventilation ratio do they use?
opciones: 15 compressions to 2 breaths, because two rescuers are working
30 compressions to 2 breaths, the ratio for a single rescuer
5 compressions to 1 breath, trading places after every cycle
10 compressions to 2 breaths, with 1 breath every 6 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: A child or infant worked by one rescuer gets 2 breaths after every 30 compressions; when two rescuers are present that changes to 2 breaths after every 15 compressions. The rate stays at 100 to 120 per minute either way. One breath every 6 seconds is the rate for rescue breathing in a patient who still has a pulse, not a compression ratio.

preguntas.pregunta: Who may qualify for CHAMPVA?
opciones: The spouse or child of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from service
The veteran who is rated permanently and totally disabled from a service condition
The spouse or child of a service member who is currently on active-duty status
The parent of a veteran who died while serving in the uniformed services abroad
preguntas.explicacion: CHAMPVA covers the spouse or dependent child of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability, and the surviving spouse or child of a veteran who died from such a disability or who was so rated at death. preguntas.pregunta: What is strongly recommended before prostate cancer screening is started or stopped?
opciones: Shared decision-making between the patient and the healthcare provider
An empiric course of antibiotics to remove prostatitis as a confounder
A confirmatory second sample drawn eight weeks after the first result
A biopsy of the prostate to establish the patient's baseline condition
preguntas.explicacion: Because the marker is sensitive but not specific, most men with a raised value do not have cancer and a normal value does not rule it out, the decision to screen at all is made jointly with the patient. preguntas.pregunta: The flow into the tube is slow during a child's draw. Which measure does the WHO offer for the parent to do?
opciones: Rhythmically tighten and release the child's wrist to help the flow
Lower the child's arm below the level of the table for a minute
Press firmly above the elbow until the vein stands out clearly
Rub the puncture site briskly with dry gauze between the tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where venipuncture proves difficult, the parent may be asked to tighten and release the child's wrist rhythmically so there is adequate blood flow, the child may be kept warm, warm cloths may be laid over the puncture area to dilate the vessels, and a transilluminator or pocket pen light may be used to show the dorsal hand veins and those of the antecubital fossa.

preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory notifies a phlebotomist that a specimen was rejected for a critically ill patient. Why must the recollection be arranged without delay?
opciones: Rejection forces a new sample request, prolongs turnaround and can delay diagnosis and treatment
Rejected specimens are discarded after 30 minutes, after which the original order is cancelled
The laboratory cannot issue any report for the patient until the replacement sample is received
A second rejection from the same unit automatically triggers an accreditation incident report
preguntas.explicacion: Sample rejection stops the analysis and generates a new request, which lengthens turnaround time and delays diagnosis and treatment of critical patients, with adverse outcomes described in the literature; that is the reason the task of contacting the patient or unit for recollection matters. Rejected tubes are actually kept 24 hours at 4 °C, other reports are not blocked, and accreditation bodies ask for monitoring, not automatic incidents.

opciones: Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, loss of vascular integrity
Low platelets, high haematocrit, iron deficiency, loss of vascular integrity
High platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, raised blood pressure
Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, dehydration, prolonged tourniquet pressure

preguntas.pregunta: How many culpability categories does the civil money penalty scheme for HIPAA violations use?
opciones: Four, running from not knowing up to willful neglect that was never corrected
Three, running from an honest mistake up to a deliberate sale of patient records
Two, one for covered entities and a separate one for their business associates
Six, one for each of the circumstances in which records may go to law enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: The HITECH Act set four categories of violation reflecting rising culpability, with four matching tiers of penalty amounts. In order they are: the entity did not know and would not have known with reasonable diligence; the violation was due to reasonable cause and not willful neglect; it was due to willful neglect but was corrected within 30 days; and it was due to willful neglect and was not corrected.

preguntas.pregunta: The R waves on a strip are spaced unevenly, so the square method will not work. What is done instead?
opciones: Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 6
Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 4
Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 10
Count the small squares between two R waves and use 300
preguntas.explicacion: The square methods assume the beats are evenly spaced. When they are not, the count is taken over the whole ten-second strip and multiplied by six to reach a rate per minute. Dividing 300 by small squares mixes up the two grids and gives a figure far off the real rate.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does laying a patient flat bring them round after a faint?
opciones: Blood returns from the legs and the heart no longer pumps uphill
Blood leaves the legs and pools where the tourniquet had been
The vagus nerve is compressed and the heart rate rises at once
Cooling of the skin restores the vascular tone that had been lost
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient falls or is laid supine, circulating volume returns from the lower limbs and the heart no longer has to deliver blood against gravity, so consciousness comes back quickly. That is also why the person is asked to sit or lie down promptly as soon as the warning symptoms appear.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with sore fingertips asks about testing somewhere else. What can be said?
opciones: The earlobe, heel, forearm and palm are alternatives, if the meter allows it
The earlobe, heel, forearm and palm are alternatives, in any meter on sale
Only the heel may be used instead, and only in patients under one year old
Alternative sites are read as interstitial glucose and need a separate scale

opciones: Cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria entering the blood directly
The inflamed skin blanches under pressure, which hides the vein from view
The swelling dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid, just as squeezing a finger does
Alcohol cannot be used on inflamed skin, so the site cannot be disinfected
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions such as cellulitis or an abscess can increase the risk of bacteria infiltrating the blood directly, so another site is chosen. preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to start monitoring extra-analytical quality but can only afford two indicators. Which two areas do accreditation criteria and the literature put first?

Reagent inventory control, and calibration of the chemistry analyzers
Phlebotomist productivity, and the number of tubes drawn per patient
Duplicate test requests, and the utility of interpretative comments on reports

preguntas.pregunta: Which serous membrane surrounds the heart, and which surrounds the lungs?
opciones: The pericardium surrounds the heart; the pleura surrounds the lungs
The pleura surrounds the heart; the pericardium surrounds the lungs
The peritoneum surrounds the heart; the pleura surrounds the lungs
The pericardium surrounds the heart; the meninges surround the lungs
preguntas.explicacion: There are three serous cavities with their own membranes: the pericardium around the heart, the pleura around the lungs and the peritoneum around several abdominopelvic organs. preguntas.pregunta: A clinic uses event-related shelf life for its sterile packs. What does that mean in practice?
opciones: A pack stays sterile until something compromises it, such as a tear, wetness or a broken seal
A pack stays sterile for thirty days from the cycle date, after which it is reprocessed
A pack stays sterile until the next biological indicator is run, regardless of its cycle date
A pack stays sterile only while it sits in a closed cabinet, and is reprocessed once moved
preguntas.explicacion: Event-related practice recognizes that contamination is caused by an event, not by the calendar: a tear in the packaging, packaging that gets wet, a broken seal. The son may sign, because adult children are the default decision-makers for parents
A clinic staff member signs on the patient's behalf as a neutral third party
The draw is deferred until a court appoints a guardian for the patient

Recording the refrigerator temperature at the moment of removal
Checking that the kit lot matches the lot of the control material
Writing the date of opening on the outside of the reagent vial

preguntas.pregunta: Under Contact Precautions, what does the CDC recommend for a blood pressure cuff and similar patient-care equipment?
opciones: Disposable or dedicated equipment; if sharing is unavoidable, clean and disinfect it before the next patient
Shared equipment may be used freely, since the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient, not with objects
Wrap shared equipment in a protective cover that is changed at the end of the shift
Autoclave the equipment after each use, since disinfection does not reach contact pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's Contact Precautions recommendations name blood pressure cuffs as the example: use disposable or dedicated patient-care equipment, and when common use for several patients cannot be avoided, clean and disinfect it before use on another patient. The reason is that contact transmission includes the patient's environment and objects, not only skin. The same page asks that rooms of these patients be cleaned and disinfected frequently, at least daily or before another patient uses the space in outpatient settings, with attention to high-touch surfaces.

preguntas.pregunta: How should the puncture stroke itself be made in capillary sampling?
opciones: One quick, continuous and deliberate stroke, to get good flow and avoid repeating the puncture
Two short strokes in the same track, so that the second opens the capillary bed fully
A slow, controlled stroke that stops as soon as the first drop of blood appears
A rocking stroke across the fingerprint lines, which widens the opening without going deeper
preguntas.explicacion: The skin is punctured with one quick, continuous and deliberate stroke, to achieve a good flow of blood and to prevent the need to repeat the puncture. A second puncture would mean either reusing the lancet or the site, both of which are prohibited because of bacterial contamination and infection. Depth is controlled by lancet length, not by rocking.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Prepare the skin

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient asks for a sign language interpreter for a long pre-test discussion. May the laboratory tell him to bring a family member instead?
opciones: No, responsibility for effective communication rests on the covered entity itself
Yes, if that family member signs and agrees to interpret for him on the day
Yes, if hiring an interpreter would be an undue burden for the laboratory
No, unless the laboratory offers video remote interpreting as the alternative
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities cannot require a person to bring someone to interpret. An accompanying adult may interpret in only two narrow cases: an emergency with an imminent threat when no qualified interpreter is available, and a non-emergency where the individual asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate. Undue burden does not erase the duty either; it shifts it to another effective aid.

preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient calms down 20 minutes into a 4-hour restraint order. What should happen?
opciones: Remove the restraints immediately; he is no longer a danger to anyone
Keep the restraints on until the 4-hour order expires, as written
Keep the restraints on until the next scheduled face-to-face evaluation
Loosen one limb every 15 minutes until the order runs out
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient is no longer a danger to themselves or others, the restraints are removed at once; the time limit on the order is a maximum, not a prescribed duration. Restraint and seclusion are interventions of last resort, required to be the least restrictive measure, with no evidence that they are therapeutic or reduce aggression, and staff observe the patient regularly throughout.

preguntas.pregunta: How must the hepatitis B vaccination and any post-exposure follow-up be made available to an exposed employee?

Free, but only at the occupational health service the employer has contracted
At the employee's expense, reimbursed once the written opinion has arrived
Free, and only during the first ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) puts four conditions on every medical evaluation and procedure the standard requires, prophylaxis included: no cost to the employee, a reasonable time and place, performance by or under the supervision of a licensed physician or another licensed healthcare professional, and agreement with the Public Health Service recommendations current at that moment. preguntas.pregunta: Which change in practice is credited with markedly reducing needle-stick injuries?
opciones: Dropping recapping and putting the sharp straight into a safety container
Recapping every needle carefully with the cap held in the other hand
Storing used needles on the tray until the end of the drawing session
Rinsing the used needle before it goes into the puncture-resistant bin
preguntas.explicacion: Eliminating needle recapping and disposing of the sharp immediately into a puncture-resistant container is described as markedly reducing these injuries. preguntas.pregunta: A karyotype has been ordered and a buccal specimen is requested. How is it collected?

A swab is put into the mouth and rubbed over the tongue and under it to gather saliva
The patient rinses with sterile saline and spits the rinse into a sterile screw-top tube
A blade scrapes the inner surface of the lower lip and the scraping goes onto a slide

opciones: Coughing hard, straining at stool, standing still too long, passing urine
Eating a light meal, reading in poor light, walking upstairs, yawning
Drinking water, sitting down slowly, wearing loose clothing, resting
Breathing slowly, lying flat for an hour, raising the legs, whistling
preguntas.explicacion: Faints are described as happening during or just after coughing very hard, having a bowel movement with straining, standing in one place too long, or passing urine, especially at night. preguntas.pregunta: At about what age does Piaget's concrete operational period begin and end?
opciones: It begins at 7 years and runs to about 11
It begins at 2 years and runs to about 7
It begins at 11 years and runs into adulthood
It begins at 18 months and runs to about 2 years
preguntas.explicacion: The four periods are sensorimotor from birth through the first 18 to 24 months, pre-operations from about 2 to 7, concrete operations from 7 to about 11, and formal operations from around 11 onward through adolescence. Conservation and class inclusion are what the concrete period brings.
