preguntas.pregunta: An emergency laboratory wants its accessioning staff to apply rejection criteria consistently. What training scheme did the published laboratory use for the secretaries who accept or reject samples?
opciones: One week of specialised training on the rejection criteria, with the programme updated by laboratory specialists every 6 months
One day of orientation on the rejection criteria, with an annual refresher delivered by the nursing education department
Three months of supervised practice on the rejection criteria, after which no further update of the programme was required
Self-study of the rejection criteria table, verified by a written test at the time of hiring and not repeated afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: In that laboratory two specialised secretaries by day and one at night receive the samples and decide to accept or reject them against the laboratory's written criteria; they were trained for one week to specialise in those criteria, and laboratory specialists updated the training programme every six months. preguntas.pregunta: A medical home patient is being discharged from the hospital. Which of the five functions is most in play?
opciones: Coordinated care, which the model calls critical during transitions
Comprehensive care, which makes the practice accountable for most health needs
Accessible services, which shorten waiting times when a need is urgent
Quality and safety, shown by measuring and acting on patient experience
preguntas.explicacion: Coordinated care means the medical home organizes care across the whole health care system: specialty care, hospitals, home health, and the services and supports of the community. The model singles out transitions between sites of care, a hospital discharge for instance, as the moment coordination matters most, and asks for open communication among patient, family and care team.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wearing gloves finishes a draw and removes them. Which CDC moment for hand hygiene applies?
opciones: Immediately after glove removal, before anything else
Only if the gloves were visibly soiled with blood
Before touching the next patient, which covers this case
At the end of the shift, because gloves replace hand hygiene
preguntas.explicacion: Immediately after glove removal is one of the CDC moments for hand hygiene, alongside immediately before touching a patient, before an aseptic task, before moving from a soiled to a clean body site, after touching a patient or the surroundings, and after contact with blood or contaminated surfaces. The same page states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. Waiting for the next patient skips the glove-removal moment, and visible soiling changes only the method, soap and water instead of alcohol rub, not whether hygiene is done.

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker keeps leaving exam rooms cluttered for the next shift. Which reply is assertive rather than aggressive?
opciones: "I feel frustrated tidying rooms each shift. Help me understand."
"Why is your area always such a mess? I dread following you."
"It is fine. I will just clean them myself and keep quiet."
"You never think about the next shift when you leave a room."
preguntas.explicacion: Assertive communication states the facts and the sender's own feelings without disrespecting the receiver, and it leans on "I" messages. "You" messages attack the person instead of the issue and read as aggressive. Absorbing the problem in silence and putting the other person's rights first is the passive style.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a service expected to keep enough laboratory tubes in stock at all times?
opciones: So blood is never decanted from one tube into another to reuse tubes
So the tubes on the tray can be replaced before their expiry each month
So a second tube of every colour is always drawn as a spare specimen
So the same manufacturer supplies the needles and holders in the tray

opciones: Soap and water, dried with single-use towels
Alcohol rub, worked in until the hands are dry
Alcohol rub, followed by a second pair of gloves
Soap and water, dried with a shared cloth towel
preguntas.explicacion: Hand hygiene before a draw can be done two ways: washing with soap and water and drying on single-use towels, or rubbing with alcohol when the hands are not visibly contaminated. preguntas.pregunta: The fasting instruction sheet exists only in English and the patient reads Haitian Creole. What is offered?
opciones: An interpreter trained in sight translation reads the sheet aloud to her
A member of staff with school Creole writes a summary on the sheet
The sheet is handed over as it is, since a copy has to be given anyway
The sheet is dropped, and fasting is left to the appointment reminder
preguntas.explicacion: It should not be assumed that people who use another language will understand notes written in English. Where materials cannot be obtained in the patient's language, interpreters trained in sight translation are enlisted, which means reading a written document aloud in a language other than the one it is written in. Getting by on basic or intermediate skills is ruled out.

preguntas.pregunta: A glucose specimen will not reach the laboratory for two days. What does the additive in the grey top tube provide?
opciones: It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to five days
It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to twelve hours
It activates clotting so the glucose stays with the separated serum
It inactivates thrombin so the glucose stays with the plasma fraction
preguntas.explicacion: The light grey tube holds sodium fluoride with potassium oxalate. The oxalate binds calcium and stops clotting, and the fluoride is the antiglycolytic agent credited with preserving glucose for as much as five days. Clot activation belongs to the red tube and thrombin inactivation to the heparin tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a 'trough level' represent in antiepileptic drug monitoring?
opciones: The lowest drug concentration, typically just before the next dose is due
The highest drug concentration, shortly after the dose has been taken
The unbound, pharmacologically active fraction of the drug in blood
The average concentration across the whole dosing interval
preguntas.explicacion: The trough is the concentration at its lowest point, typically just before the next dose, a measurement that matters most for drugs with short half-lives because it shows the minimum level maintained between doses. Free levels are the unbound active fraction, measured when protein binding may be altered. The peak and the interval average are different quantities.

preguntas.pregunta: A prescriber authorizes extra refills of a Schedule IV drug by telephone. Which limits apply to that authorization?
opciones: The total with the original may not pass five refills or six months from the issue
The total with the original may not pass three refills or twelve months from issue
Telephone authorization is not permitted for a controlled substance in any schedule
The total is unlimited, provided each refill matches the quantity first authorized
preguntas.explicacion: Additional refills of a Schedule III or IV substance may be authorized orally on the original prescription, provided the total authorized including the original does not exceed five refills nor run beyond six months from the date the original was issued. preguntas.pregunta: What makes a POLST or MOLST form different from a living will?
opciones: It records the wishes as medical orders that carry across care settings
It records the wishes as a sworn statement filed with the state registry
It records the wishes of the family rather than those of the patient
It records the wishes only for the hospital where it was first signed
preguntas.explicacion: On a POLST or MOLST the patient's preferences are written as medical orders, and in states that recognize the form those orders travel with the patient across health care settings, including the prehospital one. A surrogate may complete it. In some states the form is void if it contradicts an existing living will; in others it replaces the living will, because it is easier to adjust.

preguntas.pregunta: A group practice and each of its physicians are enrolling. Which NPI entity types apply?
opciones: Type 2 for the organization and Type 1 for each individual provider
Type 1 for the organization and Type 2 for each individual provider
Type 2 for both, since everyone in a group enrolls under the group number
Type 1 for both, since the number always belongs to a licensed human being
preguntas.explicacion: There are two enumeration categories. Entity Type 1 covers individual health care providers, sole proprietors included, and a sole proprietor applies with a Social Security Number rather than an employer identification number even if one exists. preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she cannot follow the eating plan because there is not enough money for food. What is the practice's role?
opciones: Screen for social needs and link her to community resources, then follow up
Repeat the eating plan in simpler language and check with teach-back
Record the refusal in the chart and revisit the plan at the annual visit
Refer her to a dietitian, who is the only role that handles food access
preguntas.explicacion: Unmet social needs damage health, and food, housing and transportation are the common priorities practices screen for. preguntas.pregunta: Why do the veins of the limbs have valves, and roughly what share of the blood volume is in the veins at any moment?
opciones: To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; almost 70 percent
To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; about 10 percent
To produce the pulse felt at the radial artery; almost 70 percent
To regulate flow into the capillary beds; about 5 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are low-pressure vessels, so the larger ones, especially in the limbs, carry valves that keep blood moving toward the heart against the low pressure and the pull of gravity. Thinner, less rigid venous walls let veins hold more blood, almost 70 percent of the total volume, against about 10 percent in the systemic arteries and 5 percent in the systemic capillaries.

Rejection criteria follow the analyser, so they change with the manufacturer
Each laboratory adopts the criteria of the outside laboratory it refers work to

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a ventricular ectopic beat leave a full compensatory pause while an atrial one does not?
opciones: The sinus node keeps its timing, so the next beat is on time
The sinus node is reset, so the next beat arrives early
The AV node is reset, so the next beat arrives late
The sinus node stops firing until the ventricles recover
preguntas.explicacion: A ventricular beat leaves the AV node refractory, so the sinus impulse that follows cannot reach the ventricles, yet the sinus node itself was never disturbed and fires on schedule; the result is an R-R interval exactly double the usual one. An atrial beat usually enters the sinus node and resets it, so the pause is incomplete.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Premature Ventricular Complex", Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: A man with new hypertension asks how much sodium a day the Dietary Guidelines allow for a healthy adult. What do you tell him?
opciones: Under 2,300 mg a day, and less than that for children under 14
Under 1,500 mg a day, and less than that for children under 14
Under 3,400 mg a day, which is what most adults already eat
Under 2,300 mg a day, but only for adults who already have hypertension
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines cap sodium below 2,300 mg a day for the general population and set lower amounts for children under 14. The 1,500 mg figure is the optional lower target of the DASH plan, which drops blood pressure further; 3,400 mg is roughly what people in the United States actually eat, not a goal.

preguntas.pregunta: Which finding is described as apnea?
opciones: Airflow stops completely, with no movement of the respiratory muscles
Airflow falls but continues, leaving the patient hypoxemic and hypercapnic
Airflow rises far beyond what the body needs, dropping the carbon dioxide
Airflow becomes irregular and gasping as the heart stops during an arrest
preguntas.explicacion: Apnea is the complete cessation of breathing, with the respiratory muscles still. It may be central or obstructive in origin and turns up in cardiopulmonary arrest, airway obstruction and drug-induced respiratory depression. Shallow or slow breathing that continues is hypoventilation, and irregular gasping during arrest is agonal breathing.

preguntas.pregunta: Where is the biological indicator test pack placed inside the chamber of a steam sterilizer?
opciones: Flat in the front bottom section near the drain, with the chamber otherwise fully loaded
Flat in the front bottom section near the drain, with the chamber otherwise left empty
Upright in the middle of the top shelf, where the steam reaches the load most quickly
Flat against the back wall of the chamber, furthest from the door and the drain vent
preguntas.explicacion: The pack is deliberately put where sterilization is hardest, which is the front bottom section near the drain, and the chamber around it is otherwise fully loaded so the challenge is realistic. They are mistaken for SC and SL, which stand for under the skin or tongue
They are mistaken for IN and IT, which stand for intranasal and intrathecal
They are mistaken for PO, which stands for the medicine being taken by mouth

A prefix meaning fast plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning artery
A prefix meaning half plus a root meaning muscle
preguntas.explicacion: Brady- means slow and tachy- means fast; cardi- and cardio- name the heart. So bradycardia is a slow heart and tachycardia a fast one. The root for artery is arterio-, and my- or myo- names muscle, which is why a heart attack is a myocardial infarction rather than an arterial one.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits to a history of panic attacks during blood draws. Which two simple measures are described to lower anxiety and prepare for a possible reaction?
opciones: Counting down before the puncture, and having the patient lie down when the history is severe
Drawing without warning so the patient has no time to react, and using a smaller needle
Applying the tourniquet early so the draw is quicker, and keeping the patient standing
Postponing the draw until a family member is present, and skipping the identification questions
preguntas.explicacion: Simple steps such as counting down can significantly reduce anxiety and improve the conditions for the venipuncture, and a patient with a severe history of panic attacks during the procedure may be asked to lie down; identifying patients afraid of blood tests or with a history of vasovagal attacks in advance lets the team prepare for a possible faint. Finish the draw, then wash the glove with soap and water so it can be reused
Cover the tear with tape until the procedure ends, then discard the glove
Replace it only if blood reached the skin; otherwise finish the draw and discard it

Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(B) adds that single-use gloves are not washed or decontaminated for reuse; only utility gloves may be reused, and only while intact, under (d)(3)(ix)(C). preguntas.pregunta: What are the four basic steps of food safety taught for the home kitchen?

Clean, sanitize, cook and freeze
Wash, marinate, cook and reheat
Clean, separate, season and store

preguntas.pregunta: After a stroke a patient follows what is said but answers in short, effortful phrases such as "Bathroom, go." Which pattern is this?

Global aphasia, from damage across the language areas
A stress response that blocks the incoming message
A psychological barrier from the sender's own hurry
preguntas.explicacion: In Broca's aphasia people usually understand speech and know what they want to say, yet produce short phrases with great effort, so they are often aware of the trouble and get frustrated. Medicare pays first and TRICARE pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first for inpatient care and TRICARE for outpatient care
The patient pays first and both programs reimburse him afterward

The prothrombin tube goes third and the thromboplastin tube tenth
Both are citrate tubes, but they follow the serum separator tube
The thromboplastin tube goes second, ahead of the prothrombin tube

preguntas.pregunta: How far should Steri-Strips extend past a staple line, and what is the patient told about them?
opciones: About 1.5 to 2 cm on each side, and to let them fall off on their own over one to three weeks
About 1.5 to 2 cm on each side, and to peel them off gently at the first follow-up visit
About 5 to 6 cm on each side, and to let them fall off on their own over one to three weeks
Only as far as the staple holes, and to soak them off in the bath after three or four days

A doctor of medicine or osteopathy only, with every other degree excluded
Any licensed provider who diagnoses and prescribes, nurse practitioners included
A doctor of medicine, osteopathy or nursing practice, if the state allows it

Standing over the patient, speaking firmly, and blocking the doorway
Leaving without a word and returning with two more staff members
Sitting close and holding eye contact so he feels fully attended to
preguntas.explicacion: Techniques for verbal de-escalation overlap with the therapeutic communication techniques and balance provider safety against patient comfort: keeping a moderate distance without appearing guarded, calm and open body language and tone of voice, standing at a right angle to the person with an awareness of the exits, and letting them leave easily. preguntas.pregunta: Which way of writing a dose appears on The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list?
opciones: 1.0 mg, because a decimal point that is missed makes it look like 10 mg
0.5 mg, because the leading zero in front of it makes it look like 5 mg
0.5 mg, because a zero in front of the point is used for whole numbers
1 mg, because a whole number needs a trailing zero after a decimal point
preguntas.explicacion: Two dose designations sit on that list, and they are opposites. A trailing zero after a decimal point, as in 1.0 mg, is read as 10 mg when the point is missed, so whole numbers are written without one. A dose smaller than one measurement unit needs a leading zero, so 0.5 mg is written that way and never as .5 mg, which is read as 5 mg. Both misreadings shift the dose ten-fold.

preguntas.pregunta: A QRS complex on a strip measures two small squares. Which range is the normal one?
opciones: Under 120 ms, and usually between 60 and 100 ms
Under 200 ms, and usually between 120 and 160 ms
Under 80 ms, and usually between 40 and 60 ms
Under 440 ms, and usually between 300 and 400 ms
preguntas.explicacion: The QRS complex is ventricular depolarization and normally takes less than three small squares, that is under 120 ms, most often 60 to 100 ms. A wide complex points to a bundle branch block, to high potassium, or to a beat that started in the ventricles instead of above them.

8 hours, the same minimum as for a fasting plasma glucose

The skin is pinched instead of stabilized, and the needle enters at 45 degrees
The skin is held taut and flat, and the needle enters at 5 to 15 degrees
The skin is stabilized instead of pinched, and the needle enters at 45 degrees

Powder or deodorant, which stops the leads from sticking
Alcohol or gel, which stops the leads from sticking
Sunscreen or perfume, which stains the adhesive patches

preguntas.pregunta: How many oxygen molecules can a single hemoglobin molecule carry, and what binds them?
opciones: Four, one on the iron ion of each of its four heme groups
Two, one on each alpha-beta pair of globin chains
Four, one bound directly to each of the four globin proteins
About 300 million, one for every hemoglobin in the cell
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin consists of four folded globin chains, two alpha and two beta, each holding a heme group with an iron ion. Oxygen binds to the iron, not to the globin protein, so each hemoglobin carries up to four oxygen molecules. A single red cell holds about 300 million hemoglobin molecules, which is why one cell can carry about 1.2 billion oxygen molecules.

Directly over the wound itself, on top of the soaked dressing
As close as possible to the armpit, no matter where the wound is
Below the wound, between the bleeding point and the fingertips

preguntas.pregunta: Which ethical principle is at work when a limited supply of a treatment is spread fairly across the patients who need it?
opciones: Distributing resources equitably across the patients
Preserving the patient's life and their autonomy
Avoiding acts known to expose a patient to harm
Placing a high value on the dignity of the person

preguntas.pregunta: How does a nasopharyngeal wash differ from a nasopharyngeal aspirate?
opciones: Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril first, and only then is suction applied
Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril afterward, to rinse the suction catheter out
The catheter is passed to a shallower depth, stopping short of the turbinates on either side
The specimen is placed on slides and air dried, rather than into a viral transport medium tube

The privilege applies to written records; confidentiality applies to spoken exchanges
The privilege applies to federal cases; confidentiality applies to state-level cases
The privilege applies while treatment continues; confidentiality applies afterwards

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicaid patient also holds coverage through her husband's employer. Which plan does the practice bill first?
opciones: The employer plan, since Medicaid pays only the portion no third party owes
Medicaid, since a state program always pays ahead of a commercial plan
Whichever plan the patient names, since she may choose the order of payers
Both together, since the two share the bill in proportion to their benefits
preguntas.explicacion: Third party liability means a third party has a legal obligation to pay part or all of the cost of services given to a Medicaid beneficiary, and the examples named are other programs such as Medicare and any other health insurance the person holds. Where such an obligation exists Medicaid pays only its own portion, which is why the other coverage is billed first.

preguntas.pregunta: Which finding rules out ear irrigation for a cerumen impaction?
opciones: A history of tympanic membrane perforation or of previous ear surgery
A history of using cotton-tipped applicators to clean the ear canal
A cerumenolytic such as mineral oil having been instilled beforehand
Aural fullness and decreased hearing on the side to be irrigated
preguntas.explicacion: Otoscopy comes first, to confirm an intact eardrum and no ventilation tubes. Known perforation, tubes, previous surgery such as tympanomastoidectomy, discharge suggesting infection, or prior radiation to the area all rule it out, and those patients go to an otolaryngologist. Cotton swabs are a cause of impaction, and fullness is a reason to treat it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Irrigation", Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: According to HealthCare.gov, who can serve as a patient's primary care provider?
opciones: An M.D. or D.O., a nurse practitioner, a clinical nurse specialist or a physician assistant, where state law allows
Only a physician holding a medical doctor (M.D.) degree, and never a doctor of osteopathic medicine (D.O.)
A physician or nurse practitioner only; physician assistants and clinical nurse specialists are excluded
Any of the four professionals, but only a physician may coordinate the patient's access to other services
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov's definition names four kinds of professional who can be a primary care provider: a physician, whether M.D. or D.O.; a nurse practitioner; a clinical nurse specialist; and a physician assistant, in each case as state law allows. All four share the same role in the definition: to provide, coordinate or help the patient reach a range of health care services. The D.O. is named alongside the M.D., no one of the four is excluded, and coordination is not reserved to the physician.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a latex allergy. Which items on a routine phlebotomy tray are likely to contain latex?

Gloves and alcohol swabs, but not the elastic band
Evacuated tubes and their stoppers, and the labels
Sharps containers and the plastic transport bags
preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up throughout health care, most commonly in gloves, and the medical items listed alongside them include tourniquets and elastic bandages and wraps. A patient with this allergy needs latex-free substitutes for those items, and the whole team has to be told about the allergy.

preguntas.pregunta: A clotted EDTA tube is rejected. Under the CLIA test records standard, what must the laboratory's record system contain about that specimen?
opciones: Its condition and what was done with it, since it did not meet the acceptability criteria
Only the date of receipt, because no test was performed on the specimen
The name and title of the person who collected it and the reason the collection attempt failed
Only its positive identification, because the condition of a rejected specimen is not a record element
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1283(a)(3) requires the record system to include the condition and disposition of specimens that fail the laboratory's acceptability criteria, together with the positive identification of every specimen, the date and time of receipt, and the dates and identity of the personnel who ran each test. The collector's name is not a listed element, and rejected specimens are explicitly covered, not exempt.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospice patient is nearing the end of her second 90-day period and the family asks what comes next. How are the periods arranged?
opciones: Two 90-day periods, then an unlimited number of 60-day periods with recertification
Two 60-day periods, then an unlimited number of 90-day periods with recertification
Three 30-day periods, then one final 90-day period that cannot be renewed again
One single 100-day period, the same ceiling that applies inside a skilled nursing facility
preguntas.explicacion: Hospice runs in benefit periods: two of 90 days, followed by an unlimited number of 60-day periods. Before each new period the team re-evaluates the patient and recertifies a terminal illness with a prognosis under 6 months, and each 60-day period also calls for a face-to-face visit by a hospice physician or nurse practitioner. The patient may change hospice once per period.

preguntas.pregunta: A stage 3 pressure injury drains heavily and needs packing. Which dressing fits, and what must be avoided?
opciones: An alginate, which is highly absorptive and must not be put into a dry wound
A transparent film, which retains moisture and must not be put on fragile skin
A hydrogel, which adds moisture and must not be spread onto the surrounding skin
A dry gauze, which costs the least of these and must not be left in place beyond a day
preguntas.explicacion: Alginates and hydrofibers are nonadherent and highly absorptive, which suits heavily exuding wounds and packing of full-thickness injuries at stage 3 or 4. They are usually changed every 24 to 48 hours depending on how saturated they are, and they are kept out of dry wounds because there they can injure the wound bed.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.5 Wound Dressings

preguntas.pregunta: A child with spina bifida is scheduled for a blood draw. Why is latex a particular concern?
opciones: The prevalence of latex hypersensitivity in spina bifida is 20% to 65%
The prevalence in spina bifida is 1% to 2%, the same as the general population
Spina bifida causes a type IV reaction to the cornstarch in gloves
Children with spina bifida are routinely allergic to bananas and kiwi
preguntas.explicacion: Patients with spina bifida are a recognized high-risk group, with reported prevalence of latex hypersensitivity between 20% and 65%, probably because of repeated corrective surgeries and procedures; patients with repeated catheterization are also at raised risk. One to two percent is the general-population figure, and the fruit link is a separate risk marker, not a rule.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Epidemiology

preguntas.pregunta: An e-mail marked urgent asks a receptionist to open an attachment and confirm her log-in. Which trained response does the guidance describe?
opciones: Hover over the link to read where it goes and check the sender by another route
Open the attachment only if the sender's address matches the practice's domain
Forward it to the whole staff so that everyone recognizes the message on sight
Reply to the same message asking the sender to confirm that it is legitimate
preguntas.explicacion: Malicious attachments and callers asking for log-in details are the usual first step of a ransomware attack. Users are trained to hover first and read the destination address, to weigh the sender, the urgency and the spelling, and, when in doubt, to confirm through a separate channel. Replying in the same thread confirms nothing, since the sender may be the attacker.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.4

preguntas.pregunta: How is waist circumference measured?
opciones: The tape is snug over the side of each hip bone at the mid-axillary line, arms crossed
The tape is snug around the narrowest part of the trunk, arms hanging at the sides
The tape is snug at the level of the navel, with the patient breathing out fully
The tape is snug just under the lowest ribs, with the patient's arms raised overhead
preguntas.explicacion: The patient stands with the arms crossed onto the opposite shoulders, and the tape goes snugly around the lateral aspect of each ilium at the mid-axillary line. The measurement is used in adults and in children because it reads central fat directly, and central fat carries risk of diabetes and heart disease.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A parent is present for their toddler's blood draw. How should the parent be involved?
opciones: Ask whether they would like to help hold the child; give full instructions if yes, or ask another phlebotomist if not
Ask them to wait outside, since the WHO requires two trained phlebotomists for every paediatric draw
Have them hold the child without instruction, since parents know best how to calm their own child
Ask them to hold the child only after the needle is in place, to avoid transmitting anxiety beforehand
preguntas.explicacion: The phlebotomist asks whether the parent would like to help by holding the child. If the parent wishes to help, the phlebotomist gives complete directions on how and where to hold the child; a parent who prefers not to is replaced by another phlebotomist. One phlebotomist is designated the technician and another phlebotomist or a parent the immobilizer. A helper is essential.

preguntas.pregunta: Which position is used for a routine office blood pressure?
opciones: Seated with the back supported, both feet flat on the floor and the legs uncrossed
Seated on the end of the table with the feet hanging and the back left unsupported
Lying supine with the arm at the side, which removes the effect of gravity entirely
Seated with the legs crossed at the ankle, which steadies the patient during inflation
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits with the back against the chair, feet flat and legs uncrossed, and stays that way for at least five minutes before the cuff is inflated. Each departure has a price: an unsupported back and feet add about 6 mm Hg and crossed legs add 2 to 4 mm Hg to the systolic value.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure

preguntas.pregunta: A billing clerk asks a phlebotomist for a patient's full medical history to process a claim. Which HIPAA standard is at stake?
opciones: Minimum necessary: limit the PHI to what the payment purpose requires
Right of access: the clerk may see all records that the patient could see herself
Treatment exception: payment staff are exempt from all limits
De-identification: the clerk must receive only coded data
preguntas.explicacion: Payment is a permitted purpose, but it is not on the list of exceptions to the minimum necessary standard, so the covered entity must make reasonable efforts to limit what the clerk receives to what processing the claim requires. The treatment exception covers providers treating the patient, not billing. De-identified data would not serve payment, and the right of access belongs to the individual, not to workforce members. The same principle appears in guidance that access should match the employee's role, so a laboratory technologist sees laboratory records and not the whole history.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b); StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access

preguntas.pregunta: Why does every billed service have to point to a sign, symptom or complaint in the record?
opciones: Because the documentation is what shows the service was reasonable and necessary
Because the payer needs the symptom to decide which fee schedule amount applies
Because the diagnosis code determines the place of service reported on the claim
Because the coding guidelines require a symptom code on every claim submitted
preguntas.explicacion: Every service billed has to indicate the specific sign, symptom or patient complaint that makes it reasonable and necessary, which is how the record supports coverage under the national or local policy for the service. The fee schedule amount follows the procedure reported, the place of service is a separate two-digit code, and symptom codes are used when no diagnosis is confirmed, not on every claim.

preguntas.pregunta: What is an electronic funds transfer in health care payment?
opciones: The message a plan sends a bank to move the payment into the provider's account
The message a plan sends a provider listing the adjustments made on each claim
The message a provider sends a plan asking for payment for services delivered
The message a clearinghouse sends a provider confirming that claims were accepted
preguntas.explicacion: An electronic funds transfer is the message a health plan uses to order a financial institution to move funds electronically into the provider's account, carrying the amount, the payer and payee identification, the bank accounts, routing numbers and payment date. The explanation of the adjustments is the remittance advice, and the request for payment is the claim itself.

preguntas.pregunta: Which tools are recommended for checking whether a patient really understood the risks, benefits and alternatives?
opciones: The teach-back or test/feedback method
A signed consent form and a staff witness
A formal psychiatric competency evaluation
A reading-level check of the consent form

preguntas.pregunta: A scar is documented as being in the anterior carpal region. Which surface of the wrist does that describe?
opciones: The palm side, because anterior is defined from anatomical position
The back side, because anterior is defined from the resting hand
The thumb side, because anterior is defined from the midline
The little finger side, because anterior follows the ulnar edge
preguntas.explicacion: Every directional term is read as if the body were in anatomical position: standing upright, feet forward, arms out to the sides and palms facing forward. In that position the palm faces front, so an anterior carpal scar is on the palm side, and it keeps that name even when the hand is lying palm down on a table.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient lies tense on the table and the tracing is fuzzy. Besides reassurance, which step is suggested?
opciones: Tuck the hands under the buttocks and raise the knees
Fold the arms across the chest and cross the ankles
Have the patient sit up until the shivering has passed
Hold the arms down against the table during the run
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the hands on the stomach helps, and tucking them under the buttocks usually helps more; a pillow under the knees to raise the legs slightly is part of the same list. Crossing the legs is the opposite of what the position calls for, since the arms rest at the sides and the legs stay uncrossed.

preguntas.pregunta: A sputum culture is scheduled. Which two instructions help the patient produce a usable specimen?
opciones: Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect first thing in the morning
Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect right after the evening meal
Fast completely for 12 hours, and then collect first thing in the morning
Take an over-the-counter cough suppressant, and collect first thing in the morning
preguntas.explicacion: Fluids the night before make the airways produce more phlegm and the sputum easier to raise, and the test is more accurate done first thing in the morning, before eating or drinking. A 12-hour fast is the preparation for bronchoscopy, not for a coughed specimen, and suppressing the cough would defeat the collection. The provider may tap the chest or offer a salty mist to help.

preguntas.pregunta: Who may obtain a copy of an employee's bloodborne pathogens medical record?
opciones: The employee, anyone with the employee's written consent, and OSHA or NIOSH
Any supervisor in the department where the exposure incident took place
The source patient, who is entitled to the results of the exposed worker
The employee's union representative, in the same way as training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iii) keeps these records confidential and forbids disclosing them, inside or outside the workplace, without the employee's express written consent, unless the standard or another law requires it. Employee representatives appear one paragraph earlier, in (h)(3)(ii), and only for training records.

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample from a patient with very high triglycerides is milky. Which analytes did the study by Calmarza and colleagues find clinically affected, and what can remove the interference?
opciones: Phosphorus, creatinine, total protein and calcium; ultracentrifugation of the sample
Potassium, LDH, AST and total bilirubin; dilution of the sample before analysis
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate; refrigeration of the sample at 2 to 8 °C overnight
Glucose, urea and uric acid; filtering the sample through a serum separator gel
preguntas.explicacion: Lipemia from hypertriglyceridaemia produced clinically significant interference for phosphorus, creatinine, total protein and calcium, and those interferences could be reduced or removed by ultracentrifugation; a later study showed that high-speed centrifugation in a micro-centrifuge is a practical, cheaper alternative for several analytes. Potassium, LDH, AST and bilirubin are the hemolysis set, not the lipemia set.

preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act lead to?
opciones: A revision of the bloodborne pathogens standard, with a sharps injury log
A new federal agency dedicated to investigating percutaneous injuries
A requirement that every needlestick be reported to the state health board
A ban on all needle devices that are not fitted with a retracting sheath
preguntas.explicacion: The act became public law on November 6, 2000, and in 2001 the bloodborne pathogens standard was revised in response. preguntas.pregunta: Which three are the augmented unipolar limb leads?
opciones: aVR, aVL and aVF, taken from the four limb electrodes
I, II and III, taken from the four limb electrodes
V1, V2 and V3, taken from the four limb electrodes
II, III and aVF, taken from the four limb electrodes

preguntas.pregunta: How many blood samples does the 3-hour, 100 g gestational glucose tolerance test require, and when are they drawn?
opciones: Four: one before the drink and one every 60 minutes for 3 hours
Three: one before the drink and one every 60 minutes for 2 hours
Five: one before the drink and one every 30 minutes for 2 hours
Two: one before the drink and one at the end of the 3 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is drawn before the 100 g drink and three more times, 60 minutes apart, so the appointment takes at least three hours and yields four values: fasting, 1 hour, 2 hours and 3 hours. preguntas.pregunta: An insurer that should pay before Medicare has sat on a claim for four months. What may happen next?
opciones: The provider may bill Medicare, which can pay conditionally and recover it later
The provider may bill the patient, who then goes after the insurer for the money
The provider may bill Medicare, which pays and closes the matter with the insurer
The provider may bill the insurer again and wait a second 120 days for an answer
preguntas.explicacion: If the insurance company does not pay promptly, which usually means within 120 days, the doctor or other provider may bill Medicare. Medicare can make a conditional payment so the bill is settled and then recover afterwards whatever the primary payer should have paid. For no-fault and workers' compensation claims without ongoing responsibility, prompt payment is measured as 120 days from the day that insurer received the claim.

Cost-, for the ribs
Spondyl-, for a vertebra
Phalang-, for a finger bone

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the ventrogluteal site preferred over the dorsogluteal one for an intramuscular injection?
opciones: The dorsogluteal site risks injuring the sciatic nerve and the superior gluteal artery
The dorsogluteal site holds so little muscle that it cannot take a full millilitre
The ventrogluteal site lies over a very vascular area, so the drug is absorbed faster
The ventrogluteal site is the only one that can be reached with the patient seated
preguntas.explicacion: Intramuscular medication can go into the deltoid, the dorsogluteal, the ventrogluteal, the rectus femoris or the vastus lateralis. The dorsogluteal site, the upper outer quadrant of the buttock, was the traditional choice, but it carries a risk of injury to the superior gluteal artery and the sciatic nerve. The ventrogluteal site targets the gluteus medius and avoids both, which is why it is the recommended one.

preguntas.pregunta: A lesion on the scalp of a patient with years of sun exposure is diagnosed as basal cell carcinoma. Which statement about that diagnosis is right?
opciones: It is the most common cancer in the country and responds best when caught early
It is the rarest of the skin cancers and responds best when caught early
It is the most aggressive skin cancer and rarely responds to any treatment
It is a benign growth of melanocytes that is treated only if it enlarges
preguntas.explicacion: Basal cell carcinoma affects the dividing stem cells of the deepest epidermal layer and is the most common of all cancers in the United States, turning up on the head, neck, arms and back, the areas with the most long-term sun exposure. Like most cancers it responds best to early treatment, whether surgery, cryosurgery or a topical ointment.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for his records and refuses to say what he wants them for. How should the office respond?

Hold the request until he states a purpose the office can record on its own access form

Refer him to the privacy official, who alone may waive the requirement to state a purpose

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the midstream clean-catch technique used instead of simply voiding into a cup?
opciones: To keep germs from the penis or vagina out of the sample, so contaminants and formed particles are minimized
To obtain the most concentrated urine of the day, which shows the kidneys' ability to concentrate
To bypass the urethra entirely, which is the only way to get a sample free of periurethral flora
To capture the first portion of the stream, where epithelial cells and leukocytes are most numerous
preguntas.explicacion: The clean-catch method exists to stop organisms from the penis or vagina from entering the urine. A multicenter comparison found that first-voided samples carried more epithelial cells, red cells and leukocytes than midstream samples, so midstream urine was confirmed as the most appropriate sample. Concentration is the reason for a first-morning specimen, and bypassing the urethra describes suprapubic aspiration, not a voided sample.

preguntas.pregunta: A new patient in her seventies is being roomed for the first time. How should the assistant introduce themselves and address her?

By first name only, addressing the patient by first name
By role only, addressing the patient by the room number
By last name only, addressing the patient as dear or honey

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice protects the assistant's back during a transfer?
opciones: Staying close so the patient's weight rides near the assistant's center of gravity
Lifting with the assistant's own weight so the patient does not have to help at all
Standing at arm's length so that the patient has room to shift the feet freely
Letting the patient link both arms around the assistant's neck for extra security
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules do most of the work: let the patient use their own strength wherever they can, and keep them close so their weight stays near the helper's center of gravity. preguntas.pregunta: When the employer decides which jobs involve occupational exposure, how must protective equipment be treated?
opciones: Ignored: the determination is made as if no protective equipment were worn
Counted: a job is exposed only if PPE cannot fully block the anticipated contact
Counted: the determination lists the PPE provided and excludes tasks it covers
Deferred: PPE is assessed later, in the annual review of safer medical devices
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) states that the exposure determination is made without regard to the use of personal protective equipment. preguntas.pregunta: An uninsured patient and an insured patient need the same limited resource. What does the ethical framework require?

Priority for the insured patient, because the cost is already covered
Priority for the uninsured patient, to correct the existing imbalance
A decision by the business manager, who is accountable for the budget
preguntas.explicacion: The principle of justice tells the practitioner to distribute medical resources fairly and equitably regardless of demographics, insurance status, socioeconomic status or mental disability. preguntas.pregunta: As the needle is advanced, a swelling rises quickly at the site. What has most likely happened?
opciones: The needle went beyond the lumen of the vein and blood is pooling under the skin
The vein has collapsed under the vacuum of the tube and blood is backing up into it
The tourniquet has occluded the artery and the limb is becoming congested
The alcohol was not dry, and the irritated skin is swelling around the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Inserting the needle beyond the lumen of the vein causes a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin. preguntas.pregunta: Where should the search for a diagnosis code always begin?
opciones: In the alphabetic index, before the entry is verified in the tabular list
In the tabular list, before the entry is checked against the alphabetic index
In the payer's coverage policy for the service that was performed that day
In the previous claim for the patient, so the coding stays consistent over time

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the extra rights added to the traditional five rights of medication administration?
opciones: The right of the patient to refuse the medication that has been prescribed
The right of the patient to a generic substitution chosen by the pharmacist
The right of the patient to a second opinion before any injection is given
The right of the patient to a written copy of the prescriber's own signature
preguntas.explicacion: The five traditional rights are patient, drug, dose, route and time. Documentation is usually added as a sixth, and the literature stretches the list as far as ten with right history and assessment, right drug interactions, right to refuse, and right education and information. Under 2 % of samples misidentified
Under 0.01 % of samples misidentified
Under 5 % of samples misidentified

Yes, the plan takes the place of Part B and of the premium that goes with it
Yes, provided the plan she joined also includes prescription drug coverage
No, but the Part B premium is refunded to her each year by the plan itself

The light blue citrate tube
The non-additive tube
The grey fluoride tube

In the order the WHO reproduces from the United States laboratory standards consensus, the blood culture bottle is number 1. A tube with no additive comes second, the citrate tube third, then the clot activator and serum separator tubes, the heparin tubes, EDTA, the ACD tube, and the fluoride/oxalate tube last, in tenth place. preguntas.pregunta: Which finding tells you a burn has reached full thickness?
opciones: The area is leathery and dry and does not blanch or hurt
The area is pink, dry and moderately painful to the touch
The area is red, blisters over, and blanches under pressure
The area is mottled and blanches slowly under firm pressure
preguntas.explicacion: A full-thickness burn takes in the epidermis, the dermis and the tissue underneath, so it looks leathery, stiff and dry, does not blanch because the blood supply is gone, and gives no sensation because the nerves are destroyed. It needs more than 8 weeks and surgery to heal, while a superficial burn heals in 5 to 10 days without scarring.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that appointment calls go to her work number rather than her home. What must the office do?

Refuse, because the number in the demographic record is the only one the office may dial
Require a signed authorization naming the workplace as a permitted disclosure location
Send the reminder by postcard instead, since written notice avoids the problem entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers must let individuals request that communications reach them by an alternative means or at an alternative location. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's palpitations are there all the time, day and night. Which test is enough to catch them?
opciones: A routine 12-lead tracing, taken while the symptom is present
A 24-hour monitor, worn at home while the symptom is present
An implantable recorder, placed under the skin of the chest
A two-week adhesive patch, worn while the symptom is present
preguntas.explicacion: The choice follows how often the symptoms come. Continuous symptoms are caught by an ordinary 12-lead recording, intermittent ones are what the Holter is usually used for, and symptoms that come rarely call for an event recorder or an implantable device.

preguntas.pregunta: How should a practice assess each patient's language needs?
opciones: Ask every patient which language they prefer to speak and to read, and record it
Ask patients how well they speak English, and note the answer in the record
Note the preferred language only for patients who visibly struggle to speak English
Infer the language from the patient's surname or country of birth on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Ask all patients what language they want to speak and read in, to record the preference in the medical record, and to use an 'I Speak' card when a patient cannot answer. It explains why preference is asked rather than proficiency: people lose English when sick or frightened, and may be embarrassed to admit limited proficiency.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dysphagia is prescribed honey-thick liquids. How does that consistency differ from the others?
opciones: It drizzles from a cup and is less pourable than nectar-thick liquid
It holds its own shape and has to be taken with a spoon like pudding
It pours as easily as apricot nectar or a thick cream soup
It is the thinnest of the three and pours the same as plain water
preguntas.explicacion: Thickened liquids are ordered for patients who have trouble swallowing, and three consistencies are used. Nectar-thick pours easily, like apricot nectar or thick cream soup; honey-thick is slightly thicker and drizzles rather than pours; pudding-thick keeps its own shape and needs a spoon. Staff thicken liquids with a commercial product.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the contingency guidance expect of the power arrangements behind the record system?
opciones: An uninterrupted supply for at least ten minutes and a generator with fuel for two days
An uninterrupted supply for at least one hour and a generator with fuel for one day
A generator alone, tested each year, since the record system restarts by itself after a cut
A second electricity contract with another company, switched over by the building's staff
preguntas.explicacion: Two layers are described. A battery or flywheel supply carries the record system instantly for at least ten minutes, and it is tested regularly, optimally monthly. Behind it sits an on-site generator able to keep the functions critical to operations running, with two days of fuel held on site, tested monthly and kept where flooding is unlikely.

preguntas.pregunta: When must bloodborne pathogens training be given to an employee with occupational exposure?
opciones: At initial assignment to exposure tasks and at least once a year afterward
At initial assignment only, with a refresher when an exposure incident occurs
Within 10 working days of hire and again whenever the sharps log is updated
Once every three years, matching the retention period for the training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(ii) requires training at the time of initial assignment to tasks where exposure may occur and at least annually thereafter; (g)(2)(iv) adds that each annual session falls within one year of the previous one. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a training cycle. Ten working days is the vaccine deadline of (f)(2)(i), and three years is how long the training records are kept, not how often the training happens.

preguntas.pregunta: Why can a suprapubic bladder aspiration give false-positive protein, red cell and white cell results?
opciones: Blood from the needle puncture can contaminate the specimen
Periurethral flora enter the specimen as the needle passes the urethra
The antiseptic used on the abdominal skin reacts with the strip pads
The urine has usually been held in the bladder for less than 1 hour
preguntas.explicacion: Suprapubic aspiration is the most invasive and uncomfortable way to obtain urine, and blood introduced by the needle can produce false-positive protein, red cells and white cells. Its advantage is precisely that it bypasses the urethra, so periurethral flora are not a problem. It is reserved for cases where other methods fail or keep producing contaminated samples, which usually means small children.

preguntas.pregunta: Beyond the rate, which characteristics does a complete pulse assessment describe?
opciones: Rhythm, volume, amplitude, rate of rise and symmetry between the two sides
Rhythm, skin colour at the site, capillary refill time and the limb temperature
Rhythm, the pressure needed to obliterate the beat and the width of the vessel
Rhythm, volume and the oxygen saturation read at the same finger during the count
preguntas.explicacion: Counting beats is only part of it. A full assessment covers rhythm, volume, amplitude, how fast the wave rises and whether the two sides match. Symmetry earns its place because unequal pulses can point to major vascular disease such as aortic dissection or coarctation of the aorta.

preguntas.pregunta: The clinician will need to look at a rash on the patient's shoulder by video. Which instruction does the setup guidance give her beforehand?
opciones: To wear loose clothing, so that she can show the part of the body in question
To sit with the window behind her, so that the strongest light falls on the camera
To hold the device in her hand and move it about as the clinician asks her to
To sit far enough back that her whole body stays inside the picture throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The advice on getting set up is to choose a spot with plenty of light and avoid sitting with the back towards a window, since that makes the face harder to see; to keep the camera steady and at eye level with head and shoulders in view; to wear loose clothing where the clinician needs to see skin or a particular part of the body; and to cut background noise and distractions.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient on a diuretic gets dizzy when standing up quickly. What connects the two?
opciones: Blood pressure medicines, diuretics among them, are a common cause of the drop
Diuretics raise the pressure on standing, and the dizziness comes from that rise
Diuretics have no effect on posture, so another cause must explain the dizziness
Diuretics slow the pulse, and it is the slow rate that produces the dizziness
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling dizzy on standing up too quickly is the drop in pressure called orthostatic hypotension, and it is often related to medicines, particularly the drugs used for blood pressure. Diuretics can lower pressure, most often when the patient changes position too fast. Digoxin and beta blockers are the ones that slow the pulse.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's shoulder looks out of position after a fall. What should the assistant not do?
opciones: Move the joint to put the bone back into its socket
Apply a sling to the joint in the position it was found
Press the skin below the joint to check the circulation
Place ice wrapped in a clean cloth over the painful area
preguntas.explicacion: A dislocated joint is splinted or slung in the position in which it was found, and only a bone specialist puts it back. preguntas.pregunta: Which description of the subcutaneous injection sites is correct?
opciones: Outer upper arm, front of the thighs, upper back, upper gluteal area, abdomen
Ventrogluteal area, vastus lateralis and deltoid, chosen by age and body mass
Upper third of the forearm, outer upper arms, and the area between the scapulae
Deltoid alone, located three finger widths below the acromion process of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The subcutaneous sites are the outer lateral aspect of the upper arm, the abdomen from below the costal margin to the iliac crest and more than two inches away from the umbilicus, the front of the upper thighs, the upper back and the upper ventral gluteal area. preguntas.pregunta: When is a competing style the appropriate way to handle a conflict?

When feelings need to cool or the stakes are trivial anyway
When the working relationship matters more than the issue
When two parties of equal power are short of time to decide

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a health savings account can be used for. Which answer is correct?
opciones: Untaxed dollars for qualified medical expenses, but generally not for premiums
Untaxed dollars for premiums, but generally not for deductibles or copayments
Employer dollars that are lost in full if they are not spent by the plan year end
Plan dollars that pay the provider directly once the out-of-pocket limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: A health savings account lets a person set money aside before taxes and spend it on qualified medical costs such as deductibles, copayments and coinsurance; the funds generally may not go toward premiums, and only someone with an HSA-eligible plan may contribute. preguntas.pregunta: A patient's coagulation panel keeps coming back haemolysed. Which two features of the draw are singled out to protect it?

A large tube volume and as long a tourniquet time as the vein allows
A fasting patient and a puncture placed over the basilic vein instead
A second discard tube and a needle finer than twenty-three gauge

An uneven pulse is a normal variant found in roughly a tenth of all people
An uneven pulse only reflects which arm the patient uses for daily work
An uneven pulse appears whenever the rhythm is irregularly irregular

preguntas.pregunta: A 62-year-old patient with permanent kidney failure asks whether she can have Medicare. Who is the program for?
opciones: People age 65 or older, and some under 65 with a disability or kidney failure
People with low income, under the rules that each state writes for itself
Children in families that earn too much to qualify for the state plan
Workers whose employer purchases the coverage as a benefit of the job
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is the government's health insurance program for people age 65 or older. Some people under 65 qualify as well: those with disabilities, permanent kidney failure or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. It helps with the cost of care without covering every medical expense, and it has four parts: A for hospital insurance, B for medical services, C for Advantage plans and D for prescription drugs.

preguntas.pregunta: An electrode will not stay on a patient with a very hairy chest. What is the recommended fix?
opciones: Part the hair before applying it, and tape it down if needed
Shave the whole chest and apply a second electrode on top
Move the electrode one space lower where there is less hair
Use extra gel so that the electrode floats above the hair
preguntas.explicacion: Parting the hair first gives the adhesive a surface to grip, and on extremely hairy chests the electrodes may have to be taped down. Moving an electrode off its landmark is never the answer: even a small displacement of a chest electrode can change the pattern considerably.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the stream of water directed during an ear irrigation?
opciones: Superiorly and posteriorly in the canal, at low pressure, toward the eardrum
Inferiorly and anteriorly in the canal, at low pressure, away from the eardrum
Superiorly and posteriorly in the canal, at high pressure, to break the plug up
Straight along the axis of the canal, at high pressure, until the plug floats out
preguntas.explicacion: The catheter points up and back so the stream runs behind the wax and lifts it off the tympanic membrane, and it is aimed at the membrane rather than into the canal wall. Low pressure is what keeps it safe: force causes trauma, bleeding and pain. Lacerations, perforation and ossicular injury are the complications, rare as they are.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the swollen bruise on the arm can be drained with a needle at home. What is the advice?
opciones: Do not drain it, and rest the bruised part rather than using it
Drain it only with a sterile lancet after cleaning the skin first
Drain it once the colour has turned bluish, but not before that
Do not drain it, but keep exercising the arm to disperse the blood
preguntas.explicacion: The instructions are explicit: a bruise is not drained with a needle, the painful part is rested rather than worked, and pain and swelling are not ignored. preguntas.pregunta: What backup arrangement does the contingency guidance describe for patient data?
opciones: A daily, complete, encrypted copy held off site and restored as a test regularly
A weekly complete copy kept on a second drive inside the same server cabinet
A monthly copy of the day's new entries stored with the software developer
A copy made each time the system is upgraded and kept until the next upgrade
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended arrangement is a daily off-site complete encrypted backup, with the most critical data copied as close to real time as possible. Restoring the whole system and the patient data is tested regularly, optimally monthly, and the media are kept physically apart from the working data, ideally air-gapped so that ransomware cannot reach them.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with cognitive impairment hears you but does not understand the instruction. What should you do?
opciones: Rephrase the statement, without speaking any faster or louder
Repeat it word for word until it finally registers with him
Speak much louder, since hearing is usually the underlying problem
Ask the caregiver to answer so the visit stays on schedule
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient can hear but does not understand, the clinician should try rephrasing rather than repeating, and should not speak too quickly or too loudly. preguntas.pregunta: A wrong medication is caught by the pharmacist before it reaches the patient. What is that called, and what should follow?
opciones: A near miss, and it deserves the same scrutiny as an event that caused harm
A near miss, and no report is needed at all because the patient was not harmed
An adverse event, and the patient must be told before the shift is over
A sentinel event, and the accrediting body must be notified immediately
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error that could have harmed the patient but did not, because someone intervened or because of chance. It is identical to an adverse event except for the outcome, which is exactly why it should get the same scrutiny: it shows the weakness without the cost. An adverse event means the patient was actually injured.

preguntas.pregunta: Which habit is recommended to workers so that a used needle never becomes a hazard in the room?
opciones: Plan how the needle will be handled and discarded before the procedure starts
Recap the needle with one hand until a container can be brought to the room
Set the used needle on the tray until the tubes have been labeled correctly
Carry the needle to the container at the end of the round of draws
preguntas.explicacion: The advice to workers is a short list: avoid needles where a safe alternative exists, help evaluate and then use the safety devices provided, avoid recapping, plan safe handling and disposal before beginning any procedure with needles, dispose of them promptly in the proper container, report every injury promptly, point out hazards, and take part in training and hepatitis B vaccination. preguntas.pregunta: Before asking about drinking, the interviewer remarks that many people drink more under stress. What is that meant to do?

Confirm the diagnosis the interviewer already suspects
Give the patient permission to skip over the question
Meet the duty to say why the information is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Meaningful, positive questions reduce defensiveness during the interview, and one way of doing that is to suggest a behavior commonly associated with the patient's situation, such as people drinking when under stress, before asking whether it applies. preguntas.pregunta: How long does a convulsion have to last before it meets the definition of status epilepticus?
opciones: More than 5 minutes, or repeated seizures without waking in between
More than 15 minutes, the longest a seizure is expected to run
More than 2 minutes, the point at which the airway must be opened
More than 20 minutes, when second-line medicine is started
preguntas.explicacion: A seizure of more than 5 minutes, or seizures that repeat without the patient returning to baseline awareness, is status epilepticus. Symptoms of an ordinary seizure stop after seconds to minutes, and rarely run past 15 minutes. The 20-minute mark is when second-line medicine is added, not when the definition is met.

preguntas.pregunta: Which burn counts as major rather than minor?
opciones: A second-degree burn wider than 2 to 3 inches (5.08 to 7.62 cm)
A second-degree burn narrower than 2 to 3 inches (5.08 to 7.62 cm)
A first-degree burn of the forearm that covers most of the skin there
A first-degree burn on the hand that stings for more than a day
preguntas.explicacion: Minor burns are first-degree burns anywhere on the body and second-degree burns under 2 to 3 inches across. Major burns are all third-degree burns, second-degree burns wider than that, and second-degree burns of the hands, feet, face, groin, buttocks or over a major joint. preguntas.pregunta: A combined nasal and throat swab is being collected for influenza. Which area does the throat swab deliberately miss?
opciones: The tongue, while the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas are swabbed
The tonsillar areas, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are both swabbed
The posterior pharynx, while the tonsillar areas and the tongue are swabbed
The soft palate, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are swabbed
preguntas.explicacion: For the throat half of a combined specimen, a second dry polyester swab goes into the mouth and collects from the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas, and the instruction is to avoid the tongue. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the time of onset of stroke symptoms recorded so carefully?
opciones: Clot-busting medicine has to start within 4½ hours of the first symptom
Clot-busting medicine has to start within 24 hours of the first symptom
Blood thinners cannot be started until 4½ hours have gone by safely
The imaging study cannot be read until 24 hours after the symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: When a clot is the cause, thrombolytic therapy dissolves it, but to work it has to be started within four and a half hours of when the symptoms began, and the sooner it starts the better the outcome. preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes becomes shaky, sweaty and confused while waiting, but can swallow and follow directions. What is offered?
opciones: Juice, a sugary drink or glucose tablets, and then the provider is told
An injection of glucagon into the muscle of the outer part of the thigh
A glass of water and a rest in a cool room until the shaking settles
No food or drink, because the glucose must be measured in the lab first
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who is awake and able to swallow is given fast sugar: juice or another sugary drink, food, or glucose tablets. Glucagon, a medicine that raises blood sugar, is the route when the patient cannot take sugar by mouth. If the signs do not improve after a snack with sugar, the patient goes to the emergency room and does not drive.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient with hearing loss keeps asking you to repeat the fasting question. What should you do?

Raise your voice and use a higher pitch so that the words carry across the room
Turn to the computer and type the questions for her in a large font
Ask her companion to answer the fasting questions on her behalf
preguntas.explicacion: For hearing deficits: check the hearing aid and background noise from equipment, talk clearly in a normal tone because shouting distorts sounds and can sound angry and a high pitch is hard to hear, and face the person directly at eye level so they can lip-read. It was the first survey of experience with private health plans
It is the ambulatory survey about the patient's most recent visit
It is the survey administered only to Medicare beneficiaries

Through a link the clinician reads out over the telephone as the appointment begins

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a personal health record is. Which description fits?
opciones: A record the patient keeps herself, pulling together what several offices hold about her
The legal chart the practice maintains, printed and handed to the patient once a year
The set of records a health plan keeps to adjudicate the claims it has received
The archive a hospital keeps of records for patients who have moved out of the area
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may have charts at several doctors' offices and another at a hospital, on paper or electronically, and those charts are the medical records. preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory uses the patient's electronic chart, rather than a separate form, as the test requisition. When is this acceptable under CLIA?
opciones: When the chart is available to the laboratory at the time of testing and to CMS on request
When the ordering physician signs a paper copy of the chart entry within 30 days of the order
When the chart is used only for waived tests performed at the point of care
When the laboratory also keeps a duplicate paper requisition for every order

That the cheaper drug on the plan's list is beyond what the patient can afford to pay
That the cheaper drug is out of stock at the pharmacy the patient normally uses
That the plan itself covered the costlier drug for this patient in an earlier year

preguntas.pregunta: Tuberculosis is suspected. How does the sputum collection differ from a routine sputum culture?
opciones: A series of 3 early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL is collected on separate days
A single early morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL is collected and sent the same day
A series of 3 specimens is collected 2 hours apart on the same morning and pooled
A series of 3 specimens is collected on separate days and pooled into one container
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each is collected on consecutive days, refrigerated and returned to the laboratory daily; each is examined separately, never pooled. A routine culture takes a single specimen sent in the same day. In an uncooperative patient the organism can also be recovered from gastric contents by stomach aspiration.

The home health aide, the physical therapist and the dietitian who visit the home
The attending clinician, the consultant subspecialist and the pharmacist on call

preguntas.explicacion: The core hospice team is the nurse, the social worker and the chaplain, and those members must be employed by the hospice agency. preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fell and hit their head is unconscious, but breathing and heart rate are normal. What is done?
opciones: Steady the head and neck with both hands and keep them in line with the spine
Turn the head to one side and place a rolled towel under the neck for support
Sit the patient up against a wall and watch the pupils for any change
Shake the patient gently by the shoulder until some response is obtained
preguntas.explicacion: An unconscious patient after a head injury is handled as though the spine were injured: the head is held between both hands, kept in line with the spine, and movement is prevented until help arrives. First and last name and room number, confirmed against the card on the bed
First and last name, read aloud by the phlebotomist for the patient to confirm

preguntas.pregunta: At what angle does the WHO guideline say the needle should enter the vein?
opciones: Swiftly, at 30 degrees or less, then along the vein at the easiest angle
At 30 degrees or more, steepening the angle as the needle advances along the vein
At 90 degrees, straight down, as when piercing a tube stopper directly from above
At 30 degrees or less, with the thumb anchoring the vein just ABOVE the puncture site
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to enter the vein swiftly at an angle of 30 degrees or less and then keep advancing the needle along the vein at whatever angle gives the easiest entry: the angle does not steepen. The step pairs this with anchoring the vein first, holding the patient's arm with a thumb placed BELOW the puncture site, not above it, and asking the patient to make a fist so the veins stand out. preguntas.pregunta: When does a breach of unsecured protected health information also have to be reported to prominent media outlets?

When it affects 500 or more individuals anywhere in the whole country
When it affects more than 500 residents of one hospital's service area
When it affects any number of residents, if the information was unencrypted

preguntas.pregunta: A 5-month-old infant who weighs 6 kg needs a capillary blood sample. Where is the lancet placed?
opciones: On the medial or lateral plantar surface of the heel
On the side of the middle or ring finger, across the print
On the posterior curve of the heel, where the tissue is deepest
On the great toe, which has more tissue over bone than the heel
preguntas.explicacion: The capillary site is chosen by age and weight: heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, finger-prick over 6 months and above 10 kg. On the heel the lancet goes on the medial or lateral plantar surface. In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance is 3.32 mm there, only 2.33 mm at the posterior heel, which is to be avoided, and 2.19 mm at the toe.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's veins are small and hard to see. Which measures can improve the chance of success before the puncture?
opciones: Tapping the skin over the vein and applying a warm compress or briefly soaking the limb in warm water
Applying an ice pack for up to 15 minutes each hour so the vein wall becomes firmer
Keeping the tourniquet in place for two to three minutes so the veins fill completely
Asking the patient to fast for 12 hours and avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Measures that help include ballotting or tapping the skin over the vein, followed by antiseptic preparation, and applying a warm compress or soaking the limb briefly in warm water, along with good positioning and lighting. Ice is first aid for a bruise, a two-to-three-minute tourniquet exceeds both the WHO and StatPearls limits, and the fasting rules concern the tests, not vein visibility.

Usually after 24 hours, and baths are preferred because the warm water loosens the tape
Usually after 7 days, and showers are preferred because soaking can reopen the wound

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's oral temperature is 36.4 °C at 7 am and 37.1 °C at 5 pm on the same day. What accounts for the difference?
opciones: Normal daily variation: the value is lowest early in the morning and peaks late in the afternoon
A change of site: an axillary reading runs about one full degree above an oral one in the same patient
The second half of the menstrual cycle, which lowers the recorded value by about one degree
An early low-grade fever, which is graded from a reading of 37.3 °C upward at any hour
preguntas.explicacion: Body temperature swings by roughly half a degree Celsius over 24 hours: lowest in the early morning, highest late in the day. Both readings sit inside the 36.5 to 37.5 °C band, so neither is a fever. preguntas.pregunta: In a resting adult, what are the end diastolic volume of a ventricle and the stroke volume?
opciones: EDV about 130 mL; stroke volume 70 to 80 mL
EDV about 70 to 80 mL; stroke volume 130 mL
EDV about 130 mL; stroke volume 50 to 60 mL
EDV about 5 liters; stroke volume 130 mL
preguntas.explicacion: Just before ventricular contraction a resting adult's ventricle holds about 130 mL, the end diastolic volume or preload; each ventricle then ejects 70 to 80 mL, the stroke volume, leaving 50 to 60 mL behind as the end systolic volume. preguntas.pregunta: For an infection to be classified as healthcare-associated (nosocomial), which condition must be met?
opciones: The patient was admitted for a reason other than that infection
The infection was acquired from a healthcare worker rather than from equipment
The infection appeared within 24 hours of admission to the facility
The infection is caused by a multidrug-resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: Healthcare-associated infections are infections acquired in health-care facilities, and the defining condition is that the patient was admitted for some reason other than the infection. They are often linked to surgery or invasive procedures that give pathogens a portal of entry, and to contaminated equipment such as catheters and ventilators; in 2011 more than 720,000 occurred in U.S. hospitals, with surgical sites and pneumonia each about 22 percent. The source may be equipment, staff or the environment, the organism need not be resistant, and there is no 24-hour cutoff in the definition.
