Filling several tubes risks losing the vacuum in the last of them
Filling several tubes risks carrying additive back into the syringe
preguntas.explicacion: Among the drawbacks listed for vacuum systems is that reuse of the needle holder creates a needle-stick risk during disassembly, which happens once the blood is already drawn. Skill in use, mixing components from different makers and higher cost are the other entries on that list.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through the gauze being held on a bleeding wound. What should be done?
opciones: Lay another cloth over the first one and keep up the pressure
Lift the gauze to look at the wound and then press again harder
Replace the soaked gauze with dry gauze and press on the artery
Loosen the pressure for a moment so that a clot can start to form
preguntas.explicacion: A soaked dressing is not taken off: another one is placed on top and pressure continues until bleeding stops, and then the dressing is wrapped firmly in place. Peeking disturbs the wound and makes control harder. Bleeding that keeps seeping through calls for medical attention right away.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes is breathing deeply and rapidly and the breath smells fruity. What does this suggest?
opciones: Ketoacidosis, with acetone on the breath and Kussmaul breathing
Insulin shock, with the low sugar showing on the patient's breath
Hyperventilation from anxiety, which lowers the carbon dioxide level
An asthma attack, in which wheezing may be heard only on breathing out
preguntas.explicacion: Labored, deep and rapid respirations are called Kussmaul breathing, and a fruity smell on the breath comes from acetone; both point to ketoacidosis. The patient may also be passing a lot of urine, be very thirsty, and have nausea, vomiting or abdominal pain, with tachycardia and signs of dehydration on examination.

preguntas.pregunta: Which category of information is expressly excluded from the individual's right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes kept separate from the rest of the patient's medical record
Laboratory results, which the patient obtains from the testing laboratory instead
Billing and payment records, which belong to the revenue cycle rather than the chart
Medical images such as X-rays, because they are not readily producible on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Two categories are excluded outright: psychotherapy notes, meaning a mental health provider's personal notes on a counseling session kept apart from the record, and information compiled in anticipation of or for use in a legal proceeding. The right of access is otherwise broad and expressly reaches billing and payment records, insurance information, laboratory results and medical images such as X-rays.

preguntas.pregunta: A barcode scanner at the accessioning desk misreads a patient identification label. What did the emergency laboratory identify as the cause of such misreads?
opciones: Incompatibility between the barcode print area size or symbology on the wristband or label and the scanner settings
Barcodes printed more than 30 minutes before collection, which fade beyond the reading threshold of the scanner
Labels printed with more than two identifiers, which overload the nine-digit internal code the scanner expects
Heat from the centrifuge, which distorts the code 39 bars so that the digits no longer match the record
preguntas.explicacion: Barcoding is recommended as an evidence-based best practice because it reduces identification errors in specimens and testing, yet the laboratory observed that scanners occasionally misread patient identification barcodes when the print area size or the symbology on the wristband or specimen label did not match the scanner settings. Its internal nine-digit code 39 barcode carries name, sex, age, tube and sample type, print and collection times, collection site, the tests, the ordering doctor and the phlebotomist.

preguntas.pregunta: The practice hires an outside company to process its claims. Under the Privacy Rule, what is that company?
opciones: A business associate, because it performs a function for the practice that uses patient information
A member of the practice workforce, because it handles the same records the front desk handles
A health care clearinghouse, because any outside company that touches claims fits that definition
An ordinary supplier outside the rule, since only entities that treat patients are regulated
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate is a person or organization outside the workforce that carries out functions or provides services for a covered entity involving the use or disclosure of individually identifiable health information. Claims processing, data analysis, utilization review and billing are named as such functions. Someone whose work never touches PHI is not a business associate.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two documents are the predominant health care advance directives?
opciones: The living will and the durable power of attorney for health care
The living will and the hospital's own general consent-to-treat form
The DNR order and the hospital's notice of privacy practices
The DNI order and the surrogate list written into state law
preguntas.explicacion: Several kinds of advance directive overlap, but the two that dominate are the living will, where the person writes down which treatments they want and which they refuse, and the durable power of attorney for health care, which names someone to speak for them. A DNR is a clinician's order, not a directive the patient writes, and the state surrogate list only operates when nobody was named.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has a lot of ground to cover with a patient. When should teach-back be used during the visit?
opciones: In chunks through the visit, checking each segment before the next
Once at the very end, so the whole plan can be repeated together
Once at the start, to find out what the patient already knows
Only when the patient looks confused during the explanation
preguntas.explicacion: The habit is called chunk and check: information is broken into small segments and each one is taught back before the next is started, rather than saving it all for the end. Used consistently it becomes routine and does not make the visit longer.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scores as negative on a suicide screening questionnaire. What does that result mean?
opciones: Screening is not a risk assessment, and the clinical evaluation still goes ahead
Screening has ruled out the risk, so the encounter can move on to other matters
Screening replaces the interview when it is built into the electronic record
Screening should be repeated by a second person before it enters the record
preguntas.explicacion: Questionnaires support screening; they do not stand in for a structured evaluation that pulls together the interview, collateral sources and the record, and weighs static against dynamic risk factors. Treating a screen as the whole assessment creates a false reassurance. Contracting for safety has no evidence behind it either.

preguntas.pregunta: A used needle really has to come off its syringe. How is the one-hand scoop performed?
opciones: Leave the cap on a surface, guide the tip in with one hand, then secure it
Hold the cap in one hand and push the needle into it with the other hand
Pinch the cap between two fingers and twist the syringe until it is covered
Hold the cap with forceps and press the needle down onto a firm surface
preguntas.explicacion: The cap is left resting on a surface, or set against a firm upright surface with its opening facing the worker, and the used tip is guided into it with one hand only. The needle and syringe are then lifted vertically and the other hand fixes the cap once the tip is covered.

preguntas.pregunta: How much blood should one adult blood culture set contain per venipuncture, according to the CDC?
opciones: 20 to 30 mL, which may require more than two bottles
10 to 20 mL, which always fits in exactly two bottles
40 to 60 mL, which requires four bottles in all
5 to 10 mL, which fits in a single aerobic bottle
preguntas.explicacion: An adult set should hold 20 to 30 mL of blood collected by venipuncture, and depending on the culture system and the institution's policy that can take more than two bottles. The 40 to 60 mL range is the total the CDC wants from at least two sets drawn within 24 hours, not the content of one set. Ten millilitres is the target for a single bottle, not for a set.

preguntas.pregunta: A 47-year-old with no risk factors asks whether colorectal screening applies to him yet. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Yes; screening is recommended from age 45, and carries an A grade from 50 to 75
No; screening is recommended only from age 50, and runs through age 75
Yes; screening is recommended from age 40, and carries an A grade from 45 to 75
No; screening starts at 45 only for adults who have a family history
preguntas.explicacion: Colorectal cancer screening is recommended for adults from 45 to 49 with a B grade and for all adults from 50 through 75 with an A grade, so a 47-year-old is inside the window. Grade B means the recommendation rests on somewhat less certainty of benefit than grade A, not that it is optional.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's job ended last month and he kept his employer coverage under COBRA. What changed for him?
opciones: He now pays the full premium, including the employer's old share, plus a small fee
He now pays the same share of the premium he paid while he was still employed
He now pays no premium, and the plan bills the former employer for the coverage
He now pays a premium set by the Marketplace, based on his household income
preguntas.explicacion: COBRA is the federal law that lets a person keep employer coverage for a time after the job ends, after losing dependent status, or after another qualifying event. Whoever elects it pays 100% of the premium, the portion the employer used to cover included, plus a small administrative charge. Nothing shifts the cost back to the employer, and income-based premiums belong to Marketplace coverage instead.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: COBRA

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on omeprazole and a recent course of antibiotics is booked for a urea breath test. What has to happen first?
opciones: Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 2 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 4 full weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 days and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 days
Only the antibiotic has to stop, for 4 weeks; acid suppressants do not interfere
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics and bismuth compounds are stopped at least 4 weeks ahead, and proton pump inhibitors and sucralfate at least 2 weeks ahead, because all of them suppress the urease activity the test measures and produce a false negative. Histamine-2 blockers are ideally held 24 to 48 hours beforehand. Plain antacids are allowed and do not interfere.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urea Breath Test", Procedures (Urea Breath Test)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient pulls a hand away from a hot surface before feeling the pain. Which part of the nervous system handled that?
opciones: The spinal cord, acting as a reflex center without the higher brain
The cerebral cortex, acting as a reflex center without the spinal cord
The cerebellum, acting as a reflex center without the spinal cord
The medulla oblongata, acting as a reflex center without the cord
preguntas.explicacion: Besides carrying impulses up and down on its ascending and descending tracts, the spinal cord serves as a reflex center. The reflex arc is the functional unit: a response to a stimulus that needs no conscious thought, so the hand is withdrawn before the person is aware of the pain. Many reflexes never reach the higher centers at all.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System

preguntas.pregunta: An adult arrives with fast, shallow breathing and no history of anxiety. How is this handled?
opciones: It is treated as an emergency rather than something to be managed at home
It is observed at home for 24 hours, since the pattern often settles on its own
It is managed with an inhaler alone, which settles the breathing once the dose is taken
It is recorded as hyperventilation, which is the term for fast and shallow breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Rapid shallow breathing is generally handled as a medical emergency unless anxiety is the only cause: asthma, a clot in the lung, pneumonia, heart failure and chronic lung disease all present this way. Hyperventilation is the term for breathing that is rapid and deep, which is why the depth is charted along with the rate.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient trying to lose weight asks why fat is watched so closely when some fat is necessary. What is true of dietary fat?
opciones: Gram for gram it carries twice the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries half the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries the same calories as protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries twice the calories that alcohol carries
preguntas.explicacion: Some fat belongs in the diet: it supplies energy, it helps the body absorb certain vitamins, and it shapes cholesterol levels. What makes it easy to overdo is density, since fat holds twice the calories that protein or carbohydrate holds for the same weight, so extra fat puts on weight quickly.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Dietary Fats — Summary

preguntas.pregunta: A patient kept coverage through COBRA and is also a dependent on her spouse's active employer plan. Which plan is primary?
opciones: The spouse's employer plan, with the continuation coverage paying second
The continuation coverage, with the spouse's employer plan paying second
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday in the calendar year
The plan that has covered the patient for the shorter period of time
preguntas.explicacion: When someone holds continuation coverage under COBRA or a state law and is also covered under another plan as an employee, member, subscriber, retiree or their dependent, that other plan is primary and the continuation coverage is secondary. The rule is ignored if the other plan lacks it and the two disagree, and it does not apply when the non-dependent or dependent rule already decides.

preguntas.pregunta: After cleaning the site, a phlebotomist palpates the vein once more with a gloved finger to confirm its position. What does the WHO require now?
opciones: Repeat the disinfection, because the cleaned site was touched
Proceed at once, since the glove was clean and the alcohol has dried
Wipe the fingerprint with dry gauze and proceed without delay
Apply povidone iodine over the alcohol before inserting the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 says not to touch the cleaned site and, in particular, not to place a finger over the vein to guide the exposed needle; if the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. A clean glove does not change the rule. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, which can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three findings define diabetic ketoacidosis?
opciones: Hyperglycemia, acidosis and ketones in the blood
Hypoglycemia, alkalosis and ketones in the urine
Hyperglycemia, dehydration and a low potassium level
Hypoglycemia, tachycardia and a rise in the temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a metabolic emergency defined by high blood glucose, acidosis and ketonemia. It is most often seen in type 1 diabetes but can occur in type 2, and it is set off by new-onset diabetes, infection, poor adherence to therapy, or acute illness, trauma and certain medicines.

preguntas.pregunta: A 42-year-old woman asks when mammography screening should start and how often. What is currently recommended?
opciones: Screening mammography every two years from age 40 through 74
Screening mammography every year from age 40 through 74
Screening mammography every two years from age 50 through 74
Screening mammography every two years from age 45 through 65
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation, updated in April 2024, is biennial screening mammography for women from 40 through 74 years of age, and it carries a B grade. The age of 50 was the older starting point; 45 to 65 is the window for a different screening entirely, the one for cervical cancer, which ends at 65.

preguntas.pregunta: Which tool is named the preferred handoff for patient transitions in care?
opciones: I-PASS, running illness severity through synthesis
SBAR, running situation through the recommendation
DESC, running describe through to consequences
STEP, running status through progress toward a goal
preguntas.explicacion: I-PASS is the handoff tool named for transitions in care. SBAR carries critical information that needs immediate attention, DESC is the constructive script for resolving conflict, and STEP is the situation-monitoring tool covering the status of the patient, team members, environment and progress toward the goal.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a GHS hazard pictogram drawn on a shipped chemical label?
opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: Pictograms on shipped containers consist of a red square frame set on a point with a black hazard symbol on a white background, wide enough to be clearly visible. An empty red frame with no symbol is not a pictogram and is not permitted on the label. The fluorescent orange label with the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are required by the Department of Transportation for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist shakes a filled citrate tube hard to be sure the blood mixes. What is the consequence?
opciones: Frothing or hemolysis that makes the coagulation results inaccurate
Small clots in the tube, the result the review links to under-mixing
A rise in the citrate-to-blood ratio, as happens with a short draw
Loss of the vacuum, so the next tube in the sequence will not fill
preguntas.explicacion: Both the coagulopathies review and the prothrombin time chapter say the citrate tube is inverted gently and never shaken, because vigorous agitation causes frothing or hemolysis and the coagulation results become unreliable. Small clots are the opposite problem, inefficient mixing, in the tube collection review; the citrate ratio changes with underfilling, not with shaking.

preguntas.pregunta: A choking child has an object in the airway that the rescuer cannot see. Should a finger sweep be attempted?
opciones: No: only an object in plain view is removed; a blind sweep pushes it deeper
Yes: a sweep of the back of the throat comes before any back blows or thrusts
Yes, but only once five back blows and five chest thrusts have both failed
No, unless the child has lost consciousness and compressions have started
preguntas.explicacion: A foreign body that can be seen is removed carefully, but blind finger sweeps are avoided at every age because they can drive the object downward toward the larynx. If the child becomes unresponsive, compressions start, and the airway is looked at after each set of 30, again removing only what is visible.

preguntas.pregunta: A lab coat is soaked with blood after a difficult draw. How do the standard's laundry rules apply?
opciones: Bag it where it was used, without sorting or rinsing, in a container that prevents soak-through
Rinse it in the nearest sink first, then bag it, so the laundry service is not exposed
Take it home to wash separately, since the employer is not responsible for laundering
Sort it with other soiled coats at the laundry, where staff wear gloves and gowns
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iv)(A) requires contaminated laundry to be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation, bagged or containerized at the location of use, and never sorted or rinsed there; when it is wet enough to soak through, the bag or container must prevent leakage to the outside. The employer, not the employee, cleans and launders required PPE at no cost under (d)(3)(iv), so taking the coat home is not an option, and the gloves worn by laundry staff under (d)(4)(iv)(B) do not permit sorting at the point of use.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes that she is leaving the practice for a clinician nearer her home. Does the office owe her a termination notice?
opciones: No, though a letter confirming her decision is wise and cuts the risk of a later claim
Yes, and the same thirty days of care and medication refills still have to be offered
Yes, and it has to travel by certified mail with a return receipt like any other notice
No, and no letter should go out either, since the record closes with her last visit
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient is the one who has ended the relationship, the physician is not required to send a termination notice. Sending a letter that confirms her choice in writing is still the wise course, because it removes the ambiguity and reduces the risk of legal liability. The thirty days and the certified mail belong to a termination the practice itself initiates.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two arteries are normally used to palpate a pulse?
opciones: The radial artery at the wrist and the common carotid in the neck
The brachial artery in the upper arm and the femoral in the thigh
The median cubital vein at the elbow and the cephalic along the arm
The dorsalis pedis on the foot and the popliteal behind the knee
preguntas.explicacion: The pulse, the expansion and recoil of an artery, is normally palpated at the radial artery in the wrist or the common carotid artery in the neck, although any superficial artery will do; the temporal, facial, brachial, femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis arteries are other sites. The median cubital and cephalic are veins, and the pulse is a property of arteries.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient is being taught how to make the home safer after a near fall. Which change is advised?
opciones: Take up the loose throw rugs and secure any cords crossing the walking routes
Keep a low stepladder in the kitchen so high shelves stay within easy reach
Choose smooth leather soles, which slide less on carpet than rubber ones do
Move the bedroom upstairs so that the daily climb builds strength in the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Tripping hazards come out first: loose rugs, trailing cords, uneven flooring in doorways. Light the path from the bedroom to the bathroom, put rails by the tub and toilet and a non-slip mat inside. Shoes should be low-heeled with rubber soles, not leather. Standing on chairs or stepladders is out, and daily life is arranged to avoid stairs altogether.

preguntas.pregunta: Life-sustaining treatment is given to a patient whose living will refused it. What claim may follow, and what defeats it?
opciones: Medical battery; the claim fails if the provider did not know of the living will
Medical battery; the claim fails only if a relative asked for the treatment
Negligence; the claim fails if the treatment turned out to help the patient
Breach of contract; the claim fails if the document was signed years earlier
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is an advance directive listing what the person wants if they can no longer give informed consent or refusal, commonly which life-sustaining measures may be used when there is no reasonable expectation of recovery. Administering life-sustaining treatment against it can expose the provider to a medical battery suit, but a provider unaware of the living will will not lose such a claim.

preguntas.pregunta: Which stain does the laboratory add to a sputum smear when tuberculosis is suspected?
opciones: An acid-fast stain, which the mycobacteria keep through an acid wash
A Gram stain, which sorts organisms by the thickness of the cell wall
A methenamine silver stain, which is the standard one for fungal forms
A hematoxylin and eosin stain, which is the standard one in cytology
preguntas.explicacion: Gram staining is the first step on any sputum smear and separates organisms into gram-positive, which hold the crystal violet in their thick peptidoglycan wall, and gram-negative, which take the pink counterstain. When tuberculosis is suspected an acid-fast stain is added, because the rod-shaped mycobacteria retain the color after an acid wash. Silver stain looks for fungi, and hematoxylin and eosin is the cytology workhorse.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Diagnostic Tests
preguntas.subtema: Sputum stains · PBT V.B.3 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.f · RMA III.C.4.b

preguntas.pregunta: A health department reports 43,165 new diagnoses of an infection in one year and 1.2 million people living with it. Which figure is the incidence?
opciones: The 43,165 new diagnoses, because incidence counts new cases in a period
The 1.2 million living with it, because incidence counts everyone affected
Neither figure, because incidence is always given as a percentage of deaths
Both figures added together, because incidence covers new and existing cases
preguntas.explicacion: Incidence is the number or proportion of new cases over a period of time; prevalence is the number or proportion of people who have the illness at a given moment. For a long-lasting disease prevalence runs higher than incidence, because it piles up years of new cases minus those no longer active.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.1 The Language of Epidemiologists, Analyzing Disease in a Population
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: How should the lancet be oriented on the fingertip in a capillary puncture?
opciones: On the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the fingerprint lines
On the centre of the fingertip pad, parallel to the fingerprint lines
On the side of the ball of the finger, parallel to the fingerprint lines
Over the tip of the finger next to the nail, perpendicular to the nail bed
preguntas.explicacion: The finger-prick goes on the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the lines of the fingerprint. Heel-pricks go to the medial or lateral plantar surface. The puncture should be made with one quick, continuous and deliberate stroke so that flow is good and the puncture does not have to be repeated.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1 and Section 7.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches an accountable care organization?
opciones: A group of providers giving coordinated care and chronic disease management
A plan that contracts with a network and limits care to providers inside it
A clinic funded by the federal government to serve an underserved population
A center certified to give surgery to patients who go home the same day
preguntas.explicacion: An accountable care organization is a group of health care providers who deliver coordinated care and chronic disease management, improving the quality of care patients get. Its payment is tied to reaching quality goals and outcomes that produce cost savings. Managed care networks, health centers and surgical centers are different arrangements altogether.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Accountable care organization

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a change in how the office usually does things so that she can be seen. What is the limit on that duty?
opciones: The change is made unless it would fundamentally alter the nature of the service
The change is made unless another patient objects to the way it affects his visit
The change is made unless it costs the practice more than a routine visit is paid
The change is made unless the practice has already made one for her this year
preguntas.explicacion: Providers owe full and equal access, and with it reasonable modifications to policies, practices and procedures whenever they are needed to make the service fully available to a person with a disability. The one boundary written into that duty is a modification that would alter the essential nature of what the practice does.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities

preguntas.pregunta: An Excludes1 note appears under a diagnosis code. What does it tell the coder?
opciones: The excluded code is never reported at the same time as the code above the note
The excluded code may be reported with it whenever the record supports both
The excluded code replaces the one above the note for outpatient encounters
The excluded code is reported first, with the code above it sequenced second
preguntas.explicacion: Excludes1 is a pure excludes note meaning not coded here: the two conditions cannot occur together, as with a congenital and an acquired form of the same problem, so the codes are not reported for the same encounter. The exception is when the two conditions are clearly unrelated, and when that is unclear the provider should be queried. Excludes2 is the note that allows both codes together.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.12.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasting since midnight reports a dull headache. Which mechanisms are proposed for it?
opciones: Low blood sugar, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal
Low blood sugar, high potassium and a raised cortisol
Dehydration, low iron stores and a raised cortisol
Caffeine withdrawal, high potassium and low iron stores
preguntas.explicacion: A tension-type headache is described as a notable effect at the beginning of a fast. Its precise cause has not been identified, and the mechanisms proposed for it are hypoglycaemia, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal. That is one more reason a fasting draw is scheduled early in the morning, so most of the fasting time passes during sleep.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fasting", section Issues of Concern; and MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, How long do I have to fast before the test?

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the heart sit in the body?
opciones: In the mediastinum between the lungs, with the apex pointing to the left
In the mediastinum, with two thirds of its mass to the right of the midline
In the left pleural cavity behind the sternum, with the apex pointing right
In the pericardial cavity below the diaphragm, at the level of the third rib
preguntas.explicacion: The heart lies in the thoracic cavity, medially between the lungs in the mediastinum, inside its own pericardial sac; the base is at the level of the third costal cartilage and the apex lies just left of the sternum between the fourth and fifth ribs, with about two thirds of the mass to the left of the midline. That position matters when placing a stethoscope on the chest.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Location of the Heart; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins on the back of the hand arise from which structure, and where do they drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the dorsal venous arch, into the radial and ulnar deep veins
From the deep palmar arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the median cubital vein, into the dorsal venous arch below it
preguntas.explicacion: On the dorsum of the hand the superficial veins spring from the dorsal venous arch, which empties into the cephalic and the basilic veins, the two main superficial channels of the limb. The palmar arches belong to the deep system and drain into the ulnar and radial veins instead.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is verbally de-escalating an agitated patient in an exam room. What does the guidance say about the room itself?
opciones: Keep an awareness of the exits and let the patient leave easily
Stand between the patient and the door leading to the hallway
Close the door and the curtain to protect the patient's privacy
Sit right beside the patient so the room does not feel isolating
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation techniques overlap with therapeutic communication and add a few of their own: a moderate distance without looking guarded, calm and open body language and tone, standing at a right angle to the person, and keeping an awareness of the exits so the person can walk out. Closing the door is a privacy technique for an ordinary interview.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f

preguntas.pregunta: Which temperature ranges must a vaccine refrigerator and freezer hold?
opciones: Refrigerator 2 to 8 degrees C, freezer -50 to -15 degrees C
Refrigerator 2 to 8 degrees C, freezer -20 to 0 degrees C
Refrigerator 0 to 4 degrees C, freezer -50 to -15 degrees C
Refrigerator 4 to 10 degrees C, freezer -15 to -5 degrees C
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigerators are kept between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius, which is 36 to 46 degrees Fahrenheit, and freezers between -50 and -15 degrees Celsius, which is -58 to +5 degrees Fahrenheit. Thermostats are set to the factory or midpoint setting to make excursions less likely. Thermostat markings show levels of coldness rather than temperatures, so the only way to know is to measure with a monitoring device.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 5: Temperature Ranges
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k74 · CMA I.D.3.a(5)

preguntas.pregunta: How is personal health literacy defined since the 2020 update?
opciones: How far a person can find, understand and use health information and services
How far a person can read and pronounce common medical words correctly
How far a person can obtain and process basic information about a diagnosis
How many years of formal schooling a person has completed before adulthood
preguntas.explicacion: The definition was rewritten in August 2020 with Healthy People 2030. Personal health literacy is the degree to which someone can find, understand and use information and services to make health decisions for themselves and others. The wording deliberately moved from merely understanding information to being able to act on it.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, What Is Health Literacy? Overview

preguntas.pregunta: Beyond first and last name and date of birth, which further identifier is described as accepted for matching a patient to a specimen?
opciones: The social security number or the patient's address
The name of the insurance plan covering the visit
The colour of the identification bracelet in use
The number of the room where the draw took place
preguntas.explicacion: Identification is built on the patient's first and last name and date of birth plus one further general identifier, and the examples given are the social security number or the address. Extra data of that kind lowers the risk of preventable error, which is why more than one item is used.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · D2 2E k41 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14

preguntas.pregunta: When must a provider with a direct treatment relationship give a new patient its notice of privacy practices?
opciones: No later than the first service delivery, with a good-faith effort to obtain acknowledgment
Within 60 days of the first visit, by mail to the patient's home address
Only when the patient asks for it, since posting the notice in the office is sufficient by itself
At the first visit, and the patient must sign it before any care may be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.520(c)(2) requires a covered provider with a direct treatment relationship to give the notice no later than the date of first service delivery, electronic service included, or as soon as practicable after an emergency; to make a good-faith effort to obtain a written acknowledgment of receipt and, if it fails, to document the attempt and the reason; and to have the notice available on site and posted prominently. The acknowledgment is sought, not made a condition of care. Sixty days is the window for a health plan without a website to distribute a materially revised notice.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.520(c)(2), Specific requirements for certain covered health care providers; 164.520(c)(1)(v)(B)
preguntas.subtema: Notice of privacy practices · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: Surgical caps or hoods and shoe covers are required by the standard in which situation?
opciones: When gross contamination can reasonably be anticipated, as in autopsies
When performing any vascular access procedure on an uncooperative patient
When splashes to the eyes, nose or mouth can reasonably be anticipated
When entering the room of a patient placed on Contact Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(xii) reserves caps, hoods, shoe covers and boots for situations where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, and gives autopsies and orthopaedic surgery as the examples. An uncooperative patient is the example the standard uses in (d)(3)(ix)(D)(4)(ii) for when a blood donation center must require gloves; splashes to the face trigger masks and eye protection under (d)(3)(x); and Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves under the CDC recommendations, not for head or shoe covering.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(xii), Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Caps and shoe covers · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why the tubes cannot simply be filled in whatever order is convenient. What reason does the WHO give in Step 8 for a fixed order of draw?
opciones: It prevents the additive in one tube from being carried over into the next tube
It ensures the tubes that need a full draw are filled while the tourniquet is still on
It gives the serum tubes 10 to 15 minutes to clot before the last tube is filled
It minimizes platelet clumping, which is the reason given for the capillary sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 states the purpose in one line: draw the tubes in the correct order to avoid cross-contamination of additives from one tube to the next. The clotting time of 10 to 15 minutes is a processing detail for red tubes, not a reason for the order; and platelet clumping is the reason Chapter 7 gives for the reversed skin-puncture order, not for venipuncture.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8: Draw samples in the correct order

preguntas.pregunta: The same hospital had earlier published rejection figures for its routine core laboratory rather than the emergency one. Which reason topped that list?
opciones: Clotted specimens, followed by inadequate volume
Hemolysed specimens, followed by clotted ones
Misidentified specimens, followed by lipemic ones
Improper containers, followed by delayed transport
preguntas.explicacion: In the core laboratory clotted specimens caused 55.8 % of all rejections and inadequate volume 29.3 %, a pattern the authors describe as similar to the emergency laboratory data. Most of those clotted tubes came from adult inpatient services, 54.3 %, and then from paediatric inpatient services, 26.8 %, which points the training effort at the wards rather than at the laboratory.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency department reports that 15 % of its blood samples are hemolysed. How does that compare with published figures?
opciones: It sits inside the 6 to 30 % range reported for emergency departments, far above the 2 % ASCP benchmark
It is below the 20 % benchmark set by the ASCP for samples drawn during intravenous placement
It is unusually high, since emergency departments typically report hemolysis in fewer than 3 % of samples
It matches the 13 to 14 % rate expected for any sample sent through a pneumatic tube system
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency department blood samples carry a hemolysis rate of 6 to 30 %, much higher than the 2 % benchmark of the American Society for Clinical Pathology; in the pneumatic tube study the ED rate was about 13.5 % against roughly 3 % elsewhere in the hospital, a difference the authors tie to drawing blood during IV placement rather than by straight stick. The 13 to 14 % figure was that hospital's rate, not a rate caused by the tube system.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Introduction and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which federal statute requires that content written for the public be written for its specific audience?
opciones: The Plain Writing Act of 2010
The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016
The HITECH Act of 2009, part of ARRA
The Privacy Rule, published in 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Plain language means content that is clear and easy to understand, and the guidance frames it not only as more efficient and effective but as the law. The Plain Writing Act of 2010 established the requirement that content for the public be written for its specific audience, which is why identifying that audience comes before drafting a letter or a handout.
preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Federal plain language guidelines

preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a lancing device for a fingerstick glucose test, what depth setting is advised?
opciones: No more than 2.0 mm, to minimize the risk of bone injury
No more than 3.0 mm, to minimize the risk of bone injury
At least 2.4 mm, to guarantee a drop large enough for the strip
The deepest setting on the first finger, then shallower on repeats
preguntas.explicacion: For a capillary glucose test the lancing device depth is set to no more than 2.0 mm to minimize the risk of bone injury; newer lancing devices cause less pain than older systems. Modern meters need only 0.3 to 1 microlitre of blood, so a deep puncture is not needed for the strip. The general limit for any finger-prick is 2.4 mm.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: Which strip is described as irregularly irregular?
opciones: One where the spacing between beats follows no pattern
One where the spacing changes in a repeating pattern
One where the spacing is even but the rate is above 100
One where the spacing is even but the QRS is over 120 ms
preguntas.explicacion: Sorting a strip into regular or irregular comes before naming anything. Even spacing is a regular rhythm whatever the rate or the width of the complexes; spacing that repeats a pattern is called regularly irregular, as in flutter; and spacing with no pattern at all is irregularly irregular, as in fibrillation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrial Fibrillation", Differential Diagnosis

preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer keep the medical record it maintains for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus 30 years
For 3 years from the date of the last entry
For 6 years from the date of the last entry
For the duration of employment plus 5 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iv) requires the records of paragraph (h) to be kept at least for the length of employment plus 30 years, following 29 CFR 1910.1020. The record itself holds the employee's name, hepatitis B vaccination status and dates, results of examinations and follow-up, the employer's copy of the written opinion and the information sent to the healthcare professional. Three years is the retention of training records in (h)(2)(ii); six years is the HIPAA documentation period in 45 CFR 164.530(j), a different regulation.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(ii) and (h)(1)(iv), Medical Records

preguntas.pregunta: An excluded provider's period of exclusion has now run its course. What happens to her standing with the federal programs?
opciones: Reinstatement is not automatic; she has to apply for it once the period ends
Reinstatement is automatic on the day the stated period of exclusion runs out
Reinstatement follows as soon as a state Medicaid agency enrols her once more
Reinstatement follows as soon as a practice checks the list and cannot find her
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusions programme states that reinstatement of an excluded individual or entity is not automatic once the specified period ends, and that the person has to apply for it. That is why the list is checked monthly rather than counted forward: an expired period does not by itself put someone back into the federal programs.

preguntas.pregunta: Which non-verbal behaviours signal active listening during the patient interview?
opciones: Eye contact, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient
Standing at a right angle to the patient, near the exit
Sitting at a safe distance and avoiding eye contact
Typing notes while nodding so the patient keeps talking
preguntas.explicacion: The table pairs expression, stance and gestures: eye contact and facial expressions that show interest, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient. Its footnote reserves distance and caution with eye contact for patients with psychosis or paranoia, and standing at a right angle near an exit is a de-escalation technique for agitation. NIA separately warns against talking while typing.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a boxed warning on a prescription drug label mean?
opciones: It is the highest safety warning the FDA assigns, and it is not an absolute ban
It is the highest safety warning the FDA assigns, so the drug may never be used
It is a recall notice, added when a product may cause severe harm or even death
It is a summary of the adverse reactions reported most often after approval
preguntas.explicacion: A boxed warning, once called a black box warning, is the highest safety-related warning the FDA assigns, and it exists to put the drug's major risks in front of whoever reads the label. It usually covers a whole class, because the risk follows the mechanism of action. It is not an absolute contraindication: the prescriber weighs it case by case. More than 400 medicines carry one, and warnings are added, updated or withdrawn.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Box Warning", Definition/Introduction and Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC drawn in EDTA reports a very low platelet count, but the smear shows the platelets stuck together in clumps. What is this called, and what causes it?
opciones: Pseudothrombocytopenia, from in vitro platelet clumping caused by EDTA-dependent agglutinins
True thrombocytopenia, from platelet destruction that had already begun before the blood was drawn
Hemoconcentration, from a tourniquet left in place for more than one minute
Platelet satellitism, from the sodium fluoride in a grey tube drawn before the EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: Platelet clumping can occur when EDTA is the anticoagulant, producing pseudothrombocytopenia, a falsely low count due to in vitro aggregation from EDTA-dependent agglutinins. It is an artifact of the tube, not a disease of the patient. Platelet satellitism is a different smear finding, and hemoconcentration is the tourniquet effect described in the phlebotomy chapter.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation (peripheral smear and pseudothrombocytopenia)
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k57 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: A note sits immediately under a three-character code title and gives examples of what the category holds. What is that note called?
opciones: An Includes note, which further defines the content of that whole category
An inclusion term, a list of the conditions for which that one code is used
An Excludes2 note, saying the condition is not included but may be coded too
A code also note, saying that two codes may be needed with no order given
preguntas.explicacion: An Includes note appears immediately under a three-character code title to define the category further or to illustrate its content. Inclusion terms are a different device: they are the list of conditions for which a particular code is used, they may be synonyms of the title, and they are not necessarily exhaustive, since the Index may add more.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.10 and I.A.11

preguntas.pregunta: A practice bills separately for services that belong in a single comprehensive code. What is that called?
opciones: Unbundling, which the correct coding edits are designed to detect and prevent
Upcoding, which reports a level of complexity higher than the care delivered
Balance billing, which charges the patient the amount above the allowed rate
Downgrading, which reports a level of service lower than the one documented
preguntas.explicacion: Splitting a service into its parts to bill them separately is unbundling, and the procedure-to-procedure edits exist to catch code pairs reported that way. Upcoding is the related abuse of billing a higher level of complexity than was provided or documented. Balance billing is charging the patient the difference between a charge and the allowed amount, which concerns the patient's bill rather than the codes chosen.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244); and CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative

preguntas.pregunta: Why is an interpreter of the same gender as the patient sought when possible?
opciones: To spare embarrassment when the matter discussed is sensitive
Because certification requires it whenever an exam is intimate
Because it is the only way to keep the exchange confidential
So the interpreter may answer for the patient where needed
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance is to obtain a medical interpreter of the same gender as the patient when possible, to prevent potential embarrassment where a sensitive matter is being discussed. It is a preference, not a certification requirement, and an interpreter never answers on the patient's behalf.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
