preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing poorly from a heel-prick in a cold, fussy infant. Which measure improves flow?
opciones: Keep the child warm, swaddled, with only the puncture extremity exposed; warmth can raise flow up to sevenfold
Lower the heel below the level of the heart for two minutes so gravity fills the capillary bed
Squeeze the heel rhythmically at the puncture itself until a steady stream of blood appears
Switch to a 25-gauge butterfly on the dorsal hand, which the WHO prefers when a heel-prick fails
preguntas.explicacion: The child is kept warm by removing as few clothes as possible, swaddling an infant in a blanket and having a caregiver hold the infant with only the sampling extremity exposed; warmth may increase blood flow by as much as sevenfold, with warm cloths on the site. Squeezing causes haemolysis, and 25-gauge or thinner needles are to be avoided.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 6.2.2 and 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 k130 wrapping · NCMA 2C.10

preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient usually positioned for a colonoscopy?
opciones: Left lateral decubitus, though some clinicians prefer supine with knees flexed
Right lateral decubitus, though some clinicians prefer prone with knees flexed
Lithotomy with foot supports, so the scope can be advanced along the sigmoid
High Fowler, so that the abdominal contents drop away from the descending colon
preguntas.explicacion: The standard is lying on the left side, with supine and the knees bent as an alternative some operators prefer, and the position may be adjusted as the scope is advanced. A digital rectal examination with water-soluble lubricant comes before the scope goes in, to rule out anal or perianal disease that would complicate it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Colonoscopy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.c.ii · CCMA 3B3 k64

preguntas.pregunta: A woman with limited English brings her teenage son to interpret for her visit. What should the assistant do?
opciones: Bring in a trained medical interpreter for the encounter
Let the son interpret, since the patient chose him herself
Have the son interpret the history but not the consent
Reschedule the visit until an adult relative can come along
preguntas.explicacion: Organizations are asked to ensure the competence of anyone providing language assistance and to avoid untrained people and minors as interpreters. A relative may edit or soften what is said, and a patient may hold back sensitive details in front of family. Interpreters may be on site, by video or by telephone.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Communication and Language Assistance
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is worried that tissue fluid from a difficult puncture could contaminate a coagulation specimen. What does the WHO table allow in that situation?
opciones: Collecting a non-additive tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the light blue tube first and then a second one for the test
Collecting a purple EDTA tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the citrate tube last, after all the additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 addresses this exact concern: if contamination by tissue fluids or thromboplastins is possible, a tube without additive can be drawn ahead of the additive tube. That keeps the sequence of the table intact, because the plain tube is position 2 and citrate is position 3. EDTA is far down the list at position 8, and citrate never moves to the end.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote d
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A sputum specimen for molecular bacterial testing is too thick to pipette and cannot be run today. Which pair of handling points applies?
opciones: Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to a week
Thin it with sterile saline; hold it at room temperature for up to a week
Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; freeze it at −20 °C the same day
Thin it with buffered glycerol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to three days
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is one of the viscous specimen types that jam automated pipetting, and the additives named for it are N-acetyl l-cysteine and dithiothreitol; homogenisation with inert beads in sterile buffer is the physical alternative. For storage the general guideline is 4 to 8 °C for up to seven days, with below −70 °C reserved for keeping it as long as twelve months.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2 and section 5
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: While palpating for a venipuncture site you feel a vessel that pulses. Which set of features identifies an artery rather than a vein?
opciones: Thick wall, small rounded lumen, high pressure, no valves
Thin wall, large flattened lumen, low pressure, valves in the limbs
Thin wall, large lumen, high pressure, valves present in the limbs
Thick wall, small lumen, low pressure, valves present in the limbs
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries have thick walls, a rounded appearance, high pressure and no valves; veins have thin walls, irregular often collapsed lumens, low pressure and valves, mostly in the limbs and below the heart. The pulse itself is the expansion and recoil of an artery as blood is ejected from the heart, so a pulsing vessel is an artery.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Table 20.2 Comparison of Arteries and Veins; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 k7 (applied D3 k61 palpation, k62) · PBT I.A.2 I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: How does a self-blunting phlebotomy needle protect the person drawing the blood?
opciones: A blunt cannula inside it is pushed past the tip before the needle leaves the vein
A spring pulls the needle back into the tube holder once the vein has been entered
A hinged shield snaps over the tip as the tube is pushed onto the holder
A blunt cap is screwed onto the tip once the needle has left the vein
preguntas.explicacion: In a self-blunting phlebotomy or winged-steel needle, a blunt cannula sits inside the needle and is advanced beyond the needle tip before the needle is withdrawn from the vein, so what comes out of the patient is no longer sharp. Retracting needles and hinged or sliding shields are separate designs on the same list, and each works at a different moment; the blunting one is the only one that acts while the needle is still in the vein.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Examples of Safety Device Designs
preguntas.subtema: Self-blunting needles · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: The firewall blocks a log-in attempt from outside the practice that never reached any record. Does the Security Rule count that as a security incident?
opciones: Yes, the definition takes in attempted as well as successful unauthorized access
No, an incident starts only once information has actually been reached or altered
No, unless the attempt is later shown to have exposed unsecured information
Yes, but only where the attempt interferes with how the information system runs
preguntas.explicacion: The definition is deliberately wide: attempted or successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification or destruction of information, and also interference with system operations. Interference is one branch of it, not the only one, and the practice has to identify, respond to, mitigate and document these events.
preguntas.subtema: Security incident · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1.b · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the practice never to tell her employer's health plan about one particular visit. What is the practice's position?
opciones: It need not agree to the restriction, but once it agrees it is bound by what it accepted
It must agree to any restriction a patient requests about treatment, payment or operations
It may agree only if the patient pays the visit in full at the time of the appointment
It may not agree, because restrictions would conflict with the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals have the right to ask a covered entity to restrict uses and disclosures for treatment, payment or health care operations, and disclosures to people involved in their care or to notify family. The entity is under no obligation to agree. If it does agree it must comply with what it accepted, with one exception written into the rule: when it must treat her in a medical emergency.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Restriction Request
preguntas.subtema: Restriction requests · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to sign for a procedure while already medicated in the holding area. Why is that criticised?
opciones: Consent should be a two-way talk with time to ask questions and reflect
Consent signed outside a clinic has to be witnessed by a second nurse
Consent is not valid unless the same clinician performs the procedure
Consent in writing takes the place of discussing risks and benefits
preguntas.explicacion: The improper methods singled out are discussing the procedure shortly before it happens, taking consent in the preoperative holding area, and taking it while the patient is medicated or on the point of falling asleep. What is called for instead is a structured two-way dialogue in a clinic or office, leaving the patient time to ask questions and reflect.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Time Pressures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: Under ISO 15189, at what point does the preanalytical phase end?
opciones: When the analytical examination begins
When the laboratory receives the specimen
When the specimen has been centrifuged
When the request is entered into the LIS
preguntas.explicacion: The ISO 15189 definition runs the preanalytical phase in chronological order from the clinician's request through preparation and identification of the patient, collection of the primary sample and transport to and within the laboratory, and ends it when the analytical examination begins. Receipt, centrifugation and order entry all happen inside that span, not at its end.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has greeted the patient and is about to clean the skin for the puncture. Which moment for hand hygiene is that?
opciones: Before a clean or aseptic procedure
After contact with the patient nearby
After exposure to any body fluid
After leaving the patient's own room
preguntas.explicacion: The five moments are before touching a patient, before a clean or aseptic procedure, after exposure to body fluids or after removing gloves, after contact with the patient, and after contact with the patient's immediate surroundings. Preparing the skin for a puncture is the aseptic procedure itself, so the hand hygiene belongs before it, not only at the start of the encounter. The three moments that begin with after come later and are counted separately.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications: Five Moments for Hand Hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Moments for hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: How many National CLAS Standards are there, and how are they arranged?
opciones: Fifteen: one principal standard and three themed groups
Fifteen: five on governance, five on language, five on data
Fourteen: two principal standards and four themed groups
Twelve: one principal standard and two themed groups
preguntas.explicacion: The National CLAS Standards are 15 action steps. One is the principal standard, on effective, understandable and respectful care. The rest fall into Governance, Leadership and Workforce; Communication and Language Assistance; and Engagement, Continuous Improvement and Accountability.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2C k17

preguntas.pregunta: Which organization created the first patient bill of rights, in 1973?
opciones: The American Hospital Association (AHA)
The American Medical Association (AMA)
The American Cancer Society (ACS)
The Joint Commission (TJC)
preguntas.explicacion: The American Hospital Association produced the first patient bill of rights in 1973, a document about relationships between patients, professionals and organizations that carried little enforceability. The American Cancer Society also produced one in the same decade, and the AMA did not publish a list of patient rights until 2017. Such bills remain non-enforceable.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", sections Introduction and History (1973)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA E.1.d (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: Why would a 12-lead Holter be chosen over the usual two or three leads?
opciones: To establish where premature beats or a tachycardia are starting
To keep the recording running for a longer stretch of days
To let the patient shower while the device is still in place
To cut down the number of electrodes stuck on the chest wall
preguntas.explicacion: Two or three leads are enough when the goal is only to follow rate and rhythm. When the question is where premature beats, a dysrhythmia or a tachycardia originate, the 12-lead version is preferred, and it can name a long list of rhythms immediately.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A technologist telephones a critical potassium result to a nurse. According to the Joint Commission International communication goal, what must the receiver do?
opciones: Write down the result, read it back, and confirm that what was written is accurate
Repeat the result aloud once and hang up so the physician can be notified as quickly as possible
Enter the result in the chart and ask the laboratory to send a written copy later
Ask a second nurse to listen in on the call as a witness to the reported value
preguntas.explicacion: The second international patient safety goal requires a procedure for verbal and telephone orders and for critical results: the receiver writes down or enters the complete result, reads it back, and both parties confirm that the written value and the read-back are accurate. A single repetition, a later written copy or a second listener do not complete the write-down / read-back / confirm sequence that surveyors look for.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.1, IPSG 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5G · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13

preguntas.pregunta: A collection agency contacts a patient about a medical debt. What must it send within five days of that first contact?
opciones: A written notice with the amount, the creditor, and the right to dispute
A written notice with the itemized services and the dates of each visit
A copy of the remittance advice showing what the health plan paid on it
A payment plan proposal that spreads the balance over the coming months
preguntas.explicacion: Within five days of the initial communication the debt collector must send written notice of the amount of the debt, the name of the creditor, and a statement that the debt will be assumed valid unless the consumer disputes it within 30 days, along with what happens if the consumer does dispute it or asks who the original creditor was. Itemized bills, remittance advices and payment plans are not part of that notice.
preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 809
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187 · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027)

preguntas.pregunta: Chest wall moving inward during inspiration is charted for a patient with rib injuries. Which term names it?
opciones: Paradoxical ventilation, seen in chest wall trauma and muscle fatigue
Orthopnea, seen when the patient is lying flat and eased by sitting up
Biot respiration, seen when the pons is damaged by stroke or trauma
Bradypnea, seen when the drive to breathe is depressed by medication
preguntas.explicacion: When the chest wall pulls in rather than out as the patient breathes in, the term is paradoxical ventilation, and it turns up with diaphragmatic paralysis, respiratory muscle fatigue and chest wall trauma. It is a finding of pattern, not of rate, so a chart that carries only a number would lose it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Respiratory Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · RMA III.E.3 Respiration c

preguntas.pregunta: A provider moves the practice to another state and changes her married name. What happens to her National Provider Identifier?
opciones: It stays the same, since the number never changes once it is assigned
It is reissued, since the number reflects the state where she practices
It is reissued, since the enrollment record has to match the legal name
It is suspended until the payer confirms the new address on the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Once assigned, the identifier remains the same even when the provider changes name, address or other information, because it carries no geographic or specialty meaning. Every HIPAA-covered provider, whether an individual or an organization, obtains one and uses it in all standard transactions, and a health plan may not require a provider who already has one to obtain an additional number.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Provider Identifiers Standard, Administrative Simplification
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing requirements · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185

preguntas.pregunta: When is a person falsely imprisoned?
opciones: When they are confined in an area bounded in every direction, without consent
When they are asked to remain in a room until the paperwork has been finished
When they are told they may face a lawsuit if they leave the building early
When they are kept waiting far longer than the appointment time they were given
preguntas.explicacion: False imprisonment is intentionally restraining someone inside a bounded area without their consent or legal authority, and an area counts as bounded only if movement is blocked in every direction; a reasonable and safe way out means it is not. Restraint can come from a locked door, force, failure to release or misuse of authority. A threat of future legal trouble is not enough.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: false imprisonment
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports extreme pressure and severe pain in a large bruised area of the forearm. Why does that need urgent care?
opciones: It may be compartment syndrome, which can threaten the limb and life
It may be a periosteal bruise, which heals only after several months
It may be thrombophlebitis, which resolves once the arm is elevated
It may be simple swelling, which settles with ice applied every hour
preguntas.explicacion: A feeling of extreme pressure in a bruised part, especially when the area is large or very painful, can mean compartment syndrome, in which rising pressure cuts the blood and oxygen supply to the tissues. It is described as life-threatening and needing emergency care, sometimes surgery.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.5 · RMA XV · NCMA 2C.12

preguntas.pregunta: Having measured an overall specimen rejection rate of 6 %, a laboratory sets itself a target below 2 %. Which two measures did it adopt to get there?
opciones: Monthly documentation of rejected samples and training where rejection is worst
Automatic acceptance of borderline samples and a monthly report to the medical director
A separate set of rejection criteria for the night shift and longer storage of rejects
Weekly rotation of the accessioning secretaries and a stricter barcode reading policy
preguntas.explicacion: The plan to bring 6 % down below 2 % rested on two things: enhanced documentation of every rejected sample, reviewed monthly, and periodic training organised for the departments with the highest rejection rates. Identifying and documenting the problem is described as the first step in improving quality; loosening the criteria would only move the error further down the line.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: What does an external loop recorder do that a plain event recorder does not?
opciones: It records all the time, holding 30 days in a loop memory
It records all the time, holding 24 hours in a loop memory
It is implanted under the skin of the chest wall
It transmits every event to the office as it happens
preguntas.explicacion: The loop recorder monitors continuously and keeps a rolling 30 days in memory, so when the patient activates it the device stores a fixed stretch from before and after the press. It suits infrequent symptoms that do not involve fainting, since an unconscious patient cannot activate anything.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ambulatory Electrocardiogram Monitoring", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii

preguntas.pregunta: The plan approved the preauthorization for a scheduled procedure. What has the office actually obtained?
opciones: A decision that the service is medically necessary, with payment still not promised
A decision that the service is medically necessary, and a guarantee it will be paid
A decision that the patient has met the deductible for the plan year in question
A decision that the provider may bill the patient if the plan denies the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the plan's finding that a service, treatment plan, drug or item of durable medical equipment is medically necessary. The glossary is explicit that it is not a promise that the plan will cover the cost, since eligibility, benefits and coding still apply when the claim is adjudicated. It says nothing about the deductible, and shifting liability to the patient is what an advance written notice of non-coverage does in Medicare.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67, 6E · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9

preguntas.pregunta: A lumbar puncture yields three numbered sterile tubes. Which tube is routinely designated for microbiological culture and sensitivity?
opciones: Tube 2, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 3, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 2 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to cytology and tube 3 to chemistry and serology
preguntas.explicacion: Cerebrospinal fluid collected under strict asepsis, usually between L3-L4 or L4-L5, is distributed into three sterile tubes: the first for chemistry and serology, the second for culture and sensitivity, and the third for cytological examination. Processing has to be immediate, because delay degrades the cells and shifts the biochemical values, glucose in particular, so a mis-sent tube costs time the specimen does not have.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant records a rapid strep result in the log as '+'. What does the record-keeping guidance say?
opciones: Qualitative results are recorded in words or abbreviations, such as 'Positive' or 'Pos', not as symbols
A '+' is acceptable as long as the cover page of the log has a key that explains what each symbol means
Symbols are preferred for qualitative results because they save space and they cannot be misspelled
Only the final result is recorded; a first result that was invalid is omitted so that the log stays clean
preguntas.explicacion: Results are recorded accurately and kept as a permanent record with enough detail to be retrieved. Quantitative results carry the units of measurement given in the manufacturer's instructions, and qualitative results are written as words or abbreviations rather than symbols: 'Positive' or 'Pos', 'Negative' or 'Neg', 'Reactive' or 'R', 'Non-reactive' or 'NR'. Invalid or unacceptable results are recorded too; the test is repeated and only the final acceptable result is reported.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Recording Results
preguntas.subtema: Recording qualitative results · CPT D5 k94 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D3 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss does not catch the instructions before the draw. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Face her at eye level and speak clearly in a normal tone, without raising the voice
Raise the voice and lift the pitch so the words carry over the background noise
Repeat the same sentence faster, since a shorter run of speech is easier to follow
Ask the relative who came with her to interpret, rather than saying it again herself
preguntas.explicacion: Shouting distorts the sounds of speech and can read as anger, and a high-pitched voice is harder to hear, so the advice is a clear normal tone with the face visible at eye level for lip reading and visual cues. Background noise should be reduced, and a notepad kept handy for the words that matter, such as the test being drawn.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods · CMA II.F.1.c(2) hearing impaired

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who is overbreathing from anxiety is coached to breathe out slowly through pursed lips. What is the point?
opciones: To raise the carbon dioxide level in the blood, which ends the symptoms
To raise the oxygen level in the blood, which slows the pulse rate down
To lower the carbon dioxide level, which is what causes the tingling
To lower the oxygen demand of the muscles used in breathing hard
preguntas.explicacion: Overbreathing blows off carbon dioxide, and the low blood level of it produces most of the symptoms; the goal of treatment is therefore to raise that level again. Pursed-lip breathing, puckering the lips as if blowing out a candle and breathing out slowly, does it, and calm reassurance from someone nearby helps as much.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Hyperventilation", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.q · 2027 I.B.8.q · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures of the inner ear are responsible for hearing and which for balance?
opciones: The cochlea for hearing and the vestibule for equilibrium
The vestibule for hearing and the cochlea for equilibrium
The ossicles for hearing and the tympanic membrane for equilibrium
The ear canal for hearing and the Eustachian tube for equilibrium
preguntas.explicacion: The external ear holds the auricle, the ear canal and the tympanic membrane; the middle ear holds the ossicles and connects to the pharynx through the Eustachian tube; the inner ear holds the cochlea, for audition, and the vestibule, for equilibrium. Head position is read by the utricle and saccule, and head movement by the semicircular canals.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Audition and Equilibrium
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes a physician specialist from a non-physician specialist?
opciones: The non-physician specialist is a provider with more training in one area
The non-physician specialist works only under the direct order of a physician
The non-physician specialist may not be seen without a referral from the plan
The non-physician specialist treats only patients enrolled in managed care
preguntas.explicacion: A physician specialist focuses on a specific area of medicine or a group of patients, in order to diagnose, manage, prevent or treat certain symptoms and conditions. A non-physician specialist is a provider who has more training in one specific area of health care. Nurse practitioners and physician assistants may also give care alongside most types of specialist.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Specialist; and MedlinePlus, Types of health care providers
preguntas.subtema: General vs specialty care · CCMA 1A k7

preguntas.pregunta: A new patient walks in while the record system is down. What does the contingency guidance expect the practice to have arranged?
opciones: Temporary record numbers to assign now and reconcile once the system returns
A paper chart opened under the patient's name and filed as a permanent record
A wait until the system returns, since a record cannot be opened without it
Registration in the read-only backup system, which accepts new patients too
preguntas.explicacion: Patient identification is one of the required practices for downtimes. There has to be a way to register a new patient while the system is unavailable, including assigning unique temporary record numbers, plus a process for reconciling those identifiers once the record system comes back. A read-only system, by definition, cannot take a new registration.

At least every 2 years, jointly by CDC with USDA

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how soon a urine culture will tell which organism is growing. What is the usual answer?

In 2 to 4 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 48 to 72 hours, the incubation time the plates need before any organism can be identified
In about a week, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified

Payment of the provider's billed charges once the claim has been adjudicated
Payment of a fixed amount per enrolled member for each month of coverage
Payment of a bonus when quality measures for the reporting year are met

Because a stronger dilution kills spores, while the ready-to-use dilution never touches them
Because it is a sterilant on metal items and a high-level disinfectant on plastic ones
Because it is a sterilant when heated in a reprocessor and inert at ordinary room temperature

With both hands, so the shield is seated squarely over the used needle
After the needle is in the container, where the tip can hurt no one
By the coworker who receives the device, before the tube is removed

opciones: The Mini-Cog, one of the quickest of the screens in common use
The MoCA, the most widely used and validated of the screens today
The MMSE, which has been studied since it appeared back in 1975
The SLUMS, first developed for use in the veteran population

No: the doctrine covers only acts committed inside the employer's premises
Yes: the doctrine covers every clinician the practice pays to see patients
Yes: the doctrine covers any clinician working under the practice's name

It is recommended only when the ordinary 2-hour test comes back normal
It is recommended only in pregnancy, once the 3-hour test is abnormal
preguntas.explicacion: Reactive, or postprandial, hypoglycemia is a fall in blood glucose 2 to 5 hours after a high-carbohydrate meal, early between 2 and 3 hours and late between 3 and 5. Chart it once the patient has answered the teach-back questions correctly
Chart it, since any licensed staff member is allowed to record it
Ask the unit nurse to perform the assessment and to chart it instead
preguntas.explicacion: Because of licensure, determining capacity is not a job for nurses, nursing assistants, technicians or other support staff; a licensed physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner performs it and documents it. A critical access hospital, which keeps a small number of inpatient beds in a rural county
An inpatient rehabilitation facility, which gives intensive therapy under physician supervision

preguntas.pregunta: A blood count report uses the word leukopenia. What does the ending of that term indicate?
opciones: A deficiency or lack of the cells named by the root
A blood condition involving the cells named by the root
An enlargement of the structure named by the root
An abnormal softening of the tissue named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -penia means a deficiency or lack, so leukopenia is too few white cells. The endings around it name other things: -emia is a blood condition, -megaly an enlargement, and -malacia a softening. Leukocytosis, with -osis for an abnormal condition, points the other way.

preguntas.pregunta: One hour after lunch, a patient's fingerstick meter reads 205 mg/dL while a venous sample drawn at the same time gives 186 mg/dL in the laboratory. What does this pattern reflect?
opciones: Capillary values run slightly higher than venous ones after meals; discrepant results are confirmed by the laboratory venous test
The meter is out of calibration and must be taken out of service until two levels of liquid control material have been run and passed
The venous sample was falsely low because it was drawn from an arm that was receiving an intravenous glucose infusion at the time
Capillary values run lower than venous ones after meals, so the laboratory value should be reported instead of the meter
preguntas.explicacion: A clinically relevant difference exists between capillary blood glucose and venous or arterial plasma values: capillary readings tend to be slightly higher in the postprandial state. Results from point-of-care capillary testing should not be casually combined with laboratory venous values, and discrepant capillary results are confirmed with laboratory venous testing, particularly in hospital. preguntas.pregunta: A CBC report lists white cells at 7,000 per microliter. How do leukocytes differ from the other formed elements?
opciones: They are complete cells with a nucleus, some 5,000 to 10,000 per µL
They are anucleate biconcave discs, numbering about 5 million per µL
They are cell fragments, numbering 150,000 to 160,000 per µL
They are complete cells that never leave the vessels, unlike erythrocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Leukocytes are the only formed elements that are complete cells, with a nucleus and organelles, and they are far fewer than red cells, typically 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter, so 7,000 is within range. Unlike erythrocytes, which stay inside the vessels, leukocytes routinely leave the bloodstream to work in the tissues. Anucleate discs are the red cells and fragments are the platelets.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient waiting on a biopsy result says she is frightened, and the assistant answers “I am sure it will be fine.” What is the risk?
opciones: A severe rupture in the relationship if that outcome does not arrive
The patient reads it as a value judgment placed on her situation
The patient hears it as a piece of advice that she never asked for
The subject moves on abruptly and she is left feeling dismissed
preguntas.explicacion: False reassurance is listed among the pitfalls precisely because of what happens when the promised outcome does not come: the relationship can be severely and significantly damaged. preguntas.pregunta: Which five components make up the Apgar score?

Color, heart rate, reflexes, muscle tone and temperature
Color, blood pressure, reflexes, muscle tone and respiration
Color, heart rate, weight, muscle tone and respiratory effort
preguntas.explicacion: Each of the five is scored 0, 1 or 2 and the five are weighted evenly, so the total runs from 0 to 10. preguntas.pregunta: An enzymatic detergent has been used on a set of instruments. What has to happen next, and why?
opciones: The enzymes must be rinsed off, because residue left behind can provoke adverse reactions
The enzymes must be left to dry on, because their action continues while the item waits
The enzymes must be neutralized with a germicide, which finishes off any protein they missed
The enzymes must be reused on the next set, since the proteases stay active between loads
preguntas.explicacion: Enzymatic cleaners are not disinfectants. The proteases in them attack the protein that makes up much of common soil such as blood and pus, but like any chemical they have to be rinsed from the equipment or reactions such as fever and proteinaceous residue can follow. Care outside the network is never paid, no matter the reason for the visit
The plan pays more inside the network and part of the cost outside of it

preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is the most abundant and contributes most to the osmotic pressure of blood?

Fibrinogen, about 7 percent of plasma protein
Gamma globulin, the antibody fraction
Alpha globulin, which carries iron and lipids
preguntas.explicacion: There are three groups of plasma proteins. Albumin, made by the liver, is the largest share at about 54 percent (3.5 to 5.0 g/dL); it binds fatty acids and steroid hormones and is the main protein holding water inside the vessels, which helps keep blood volume and pressure. Globulins are second at about 38 percent, and the gamma fraction is the antibodies. Fibrinogen is about 7 percent and is needed for clotting.

preguntas.explicacion: The guidance recommends designating an appropriately trained person, who understands the impact of switching test systems, to discuss new products with sales representatives, because uninformed staff may use a promotional kit on patients without realizing the consequences of substitution. preguntas.pregunta: A patient says angrily that the office lost her paperwork. Why should the reply not be defensive?

It keeps the exchange from moving to another subject too abruptly
It stops her from reading approval or disapproval into the answer
It avoids handing her a piece of advice that she has not asked for
preguntas.explicacion: Responding defensively is named as a pitfall and is admitted to be a hard one to avoid. The abnormal cells have reached one nearby lymph node only
The abnormal cells have already settled in a second organ
The abnormal cells are not cancer and will not spread at all
preguntas.explicacion: In situ means in its original place, so in a carcinoma in situ the abnormal cells are found only where they first formed and have not spread. preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old with paper-thin skin bruises after a routine draw. What age changes explain this?
opciones: Thinner, paler, less elastic outer skin and more fragile blood vessels, so older adults bruise more easily
The skin thickens with keratin and the veins sink deeper, so the needle tears more tissue on the way in and out
The skin loses its sweat and oil glands, so the alcohol cannot dry and irritates the puncture site
The platelet count falls sharply after 80, so every puncture bleeds under the skin
preguntas.explicacion: With aging the outer layer of the skin gets thinner, paler and less stretchy, and that because blood vessels get more fragile with age, older adults tend to bruise more easily and bruises take longer to heal. Three years after the training it documents, with the trainer's name removed

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic receives far more appointment requests every single day than its clinicians could ever see. What can open access do for it?

Solve it, once the backlog has been worked down over six to eight weeks of longer days

preguntas.explicacion: The model rests on the supposition that the problem is usually an imbalance between supply and demand rather than a shortage of capacity, and it can absorb excess demand on a given day. A confidential paper file of doses given, held by each individual provider
A national registry of adverse events reported after a vaccine was given
A federal list of the vaccines each state requires before a child enrolls

preguntas.pregunta: What proportion of blood plasma is water?
opciones: About 92 percent
About 55 percent
About 45 percent
About 7 percent

It is read as qhr, every hour, when the letters are run together
It is read as OD, right eye, when the periods are left out of it

30 to 60 percent in the work areas, and not above 45 percent in sterile storage
50 to 75 percent in the work areas, and not above 60 percent in sterile storage
20 to 40 percent in the work areas, and not above 70 percent in sterile storage

That it be checked only when a reading looks wrong to the operator
That it be calibrated once, on the day it is first put into service

Grief, the person's own emotional response to loss
Bereavement, the period of grief following a death
Yearning, one of the emotional signs of a loss
preguntas.explicacion: Grief is the emotional response to a loss, mourning is how that response is expressed outwardly through cultural and religious custom, and bereavement is the stretch of time in which grief and mourning happen. preguntas.pregunta: What is sinus arrhythmia?
opciones: Variation in rate, with the R-R interval changing over 0.12 s
Variation in rate, with the R-R interval changing under 0.04 s
A run of early beats from a focus outside the sinus node
A rate that climbs above 100 and then falls back below 60
preguntas.explicacion: It is a variation of ordinary sinus rhythm: the spacing between beats shifts by more than 0.12 seconds while the P waves keep one shape and the pattern of activation from the sinus node. preguntas.pregunta: A chlorine solution is not made up fresh each day. How long may it be kept, and what happens to it?
opciones: Up to 30 days in a capped opaque bottle, losing about half its chlorine over that month
Up to 30 days in a capped clear bottle, losing about a tenth of its chlorine over that month
Up to 7 days in a capped opaque bottle, after which the free chlorine is entirely gone
Up to 90 days at room temperature, because the hypochlorite ion is stable once diluted
preguntas.explicacion: Diluted chlorine can be held at room temperature for as long as 30 days in a capped, opaque plastic bottle, but the concentration falls by about half over that time: a solution at roughly 1,000 ppm on day zero is down near 500 ppm by day 30. Only when the patient or parent asks for the benefits and risks in writing

preguntas.pregunta: What do the letters H, I and L stand for in the serum indices that conventional laboratory analyzers measure, and how are the same problems detected at the point of care?
opciones: Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care only by visual inspection of a centrifuged aliquot
Heparin, infusion and light; at the point of care by a built-in spectrophotometric check on every strip
Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care by an automatic index reported with each result
Hematocrit, ionic strength and lactate; at the point of care by running a control before each sample
preguntas.explicacion: Conventional laboratories add a step that measures the serum index for hemoglobin (H), icterus (I) and lipemia (L), usually spectrophotometrically, because all three can make results inaccurate or incalculable, potassium being especially vulnerable. Point-of-care devices have no such index, so hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can be recognised there only by looking at a centrifuged aliquot; dilution may fix excess bilirubin and ultracentrifugation excess lipids.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors (HIL indices)

preguntas.pregunta: What separates hyperpnea from hyperventilation?
opciones: In hyperpnea the breathing matches metabolic demand and the blood gases stay normal
In hyperpnea the breathing is slower than normal while each breath grows much deeper
In hyperpnea the rise happens only during sleep, while hyperventilation happens awake
In hyperpnea the depth falls while the rate rises, which is what lowers carbon dioxide
preguntas.explicacion: Hyperpnea is breathing that has grown deeper and faster in step with what the body needs, during exercise or with a fever, and the blood gases stay where they should be. Hyperventilation goes beyond the metabolic requirement, so carbon dioxide falls and respiratory alkalosis follows; anxiety, pain, fever and panic can trigger it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: A strip shows a PR interval under 120 ms with a sharp upward slope running into the QRS complex. What does that describe?
opciones: A tract that bypasses the node, as in Wolff-Parkinson-White
A delay inside the node itself, as in a first-degree block
A block below the node, as in a Mobitz type II block
A failed impulse at the sinus node, as in a sinoatrial block
preguntas.explicacion: A PR shorter than 120 ms says the signal reached the ventricles too quickly, classically through an accessory tract that goes around the atrioventricular node. The sharp slope rising out of the PR baseline into the complex is the delta wave that goes with it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "P wave", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: Between the fasting and 2-hour samples of an OGTT, the patient asks to step outside for a cigarette. What is the correct response?
opciones: No; the patient must stay seated and must not smoke during the test
Yes, as long as the patient is back within 5 minutes of the draw
Yes, but the walk must be recorded because exercise lowers glucose
Yes, but only after the 1-hour sample has been collected
preguntas.explicacion: During the OGTT the patient remains seated and smoking is avoided; those are stated conditions of the test, alongside the fast, the morning start and the three-day diet. Vigorous exercise is something to avoid in the days before, not something to log and allow. The five minutes in one option is the time over which the glucose drink is swallowed, not a grace period for leaving the chair.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old is on the ward with his father. How does the WHO guidance say the child should be identified before a draw?
opciones: Ask the father for the child's first and last names, then match the form
Ask the child to state his own first and last names, then match the form
Read the name off the band tied to the cot rail, then match the form
Ask the nurse who admitted the child, then match her answer to the form
preguntas.explicacion: For paediatric patients a band counts only when it is on the child, never one fixed to the bed or cot, and where a parent or legal guardian is there, that adult is asked for the child's first and last names. The name, date of birth and hospital or file number on the laboratory form are then matched against the patient.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.1

preguntas.pregunta: A vegetarian patient is afraid she cannot get all her amino acids without meat. What should she be told?
opciones: Plant sources such as soy, beans and quinoa can supply what she needs
Only animal sources such as meat, milk and eggs supply amino acids
Essential amino acids have to be eaten together at every single meal
The body makes the essential amino acids out of the nonessential ones
preguntas.explicacion: Amino acids come from animal foods and also from plant foods such as soy, beans, legumes, nut butters and grains like quinoa and wheat germ, so animal products are not required. Essential amino acids are the ones the body cannot build and food has to supply, but the balance across the whole day is what counts, not each meal.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Protein in diet — Function

preguntas.pregunta: Name the three layers of meninges from the outside in.
opciones: Dura mater, arachnoid, pia mater
Pia mater, arachnoid, dura mater
Arachnoid, dura mater, pia mater
Dura mater, pia mater, arachnoid
preguntas.explicacion: The dura mater is the outer layer, tough white fibrous connective tissue. The arachnoid lies in the middle and looks like a cobweb; the space beneath it holds cerebrospinal fluid and blood vessels. The pia mater is innermost, thin and delicate, and bound so tightly to the brain and cord that it cannot be lifted without damage.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes a live, attenuated vaccine from an inactivated one?
opciones: The live one has to replicate in the recipient to produce an immune response
The live one cannot replicate, which is why one dose is usually enough for it
The live one is unaffected by circulating antibody, so its timing is free
The live one is stable in heat and light, so the cold chain matters less to it
preguntas.explicacion: A live, attenuated vaccine is a weakened wild virus or bacterium that must replicate in the vaccinated person to produce a response, so a small dose grows into enough organism to stimulate immunity, and one dose usually protects. Circulating antibody from any source can block that replication and cause vaccine failure. These vaccines are fragile and can be destroyed by heat and light. Inactivated vaccines cannot replicate.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 1: Classification of Vaccines
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(1)

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of items has to be documented as part of an informed consent discussion?
opciones: The nature of the procedure, its risks and benefits, and the alternatives with their own
The nature of the procedure, its cost, the patient's coverage and the billing code used
The nature of the procedure, the clinician's credentials and the facility's current licence
The nature of the procedure and its risks, with a signature witnessed by two employees
preguntas.explicacion: Documented informed consent has five parts: the nature of the procedure, its risks and benefits, the reasonable alternatives, the risks and benefits of those alternatives, and an assessment that the patient understood all of it. The emphasis has moved away from the signature and toward the conversation, and a competent patient must be free to decide without feeling pushed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Function

preguntas.pregunta: How are a child's height and weight recorded so that they can be interpreted?
opciones: As points plotted on the growth chart, which places them as percentiles
As raw figures alone, since the chart is drawn only when a problem appears
As a percentage of the average value for children of that age and sex
As a single combined score, which the chart converts into an age equivalent
preguntas.explicacion: An isolated anthropometric figure is of little use: the value has to be set against the reference for that age and sex, and the charts do that by percentile curves. Each measurement taken at a well-child visit goes onto the chart, and the same chart follows the child from year to year.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Growth chart

preguntas.pregunta: Which duty does the code of ethics for NHA-certified professionals state?
opciones: To protect and respect the dignity, privacy and safety of every patient
To report any colleague suspected of an error to the state licensing board
To accept any assignment the employer gives while the shift is under way
To keep patient information from the patient's own family in every case
preguntas.explicacion: The code lists six duties a certified professional takes on, and one of them is guarding the dignity, privacy and safety of all patients. The others cover working for the betterment of society and the profession, professionalism and honesty, continued learning, taking part in activities that improve health and the allied health field, and acting in the public's best interest.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics

preguntas.pregunta: You are teaching a patient to inject insulin at home. Which statement about the route and the equipment is correct?
opciones: Under the skin, with a disposable syringe marked in units and a fine short needle
Into the muscle, using a longer needle whenever the ordered dose is a large one
Into a vein at home, since regular insulin can also be given by that same route
Under the skin, with a tuberculin syringe marked in milliliters and a long needle
preguntas.explicacion: Insulin is given subcutaneously in almost every case, with a plastic disposable syringe that holds 30, 50 or 100 units and carries a fine needle, as thin as 31 gauge, from about 3/16 of an inch for infants to half an inch or more for adults. Pens and pumps are the other options. Muscle and vein are used only under close supervision in a hospital or similar setting, never as home teaching.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Human Insulin", Administration

preguntas.pregunta: During the HIV follow-up period after an exposure, what does the CDC advise the worker to avoid?
opciones: Donating blood, semen or organs and unprotected sex, mostly in the first 6 to 12 weeks
Patient care duties of any kind until the 6-month antibody test comes back negative
Close contact with household members until the 12-week antibody test is negative
Any other medication, since it would interfere with the antiretroviral regimen
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC brochure asks exposed workers, especially during the first 6 to 12 weeks when most infected persons show signs of infection, to follow HIV prevention recommendations: no donation of blood, semen or organs, no sexual intercourse or consistent condom use, and consideration of not breastfeeding. WHO's annex adds no blood or organ donation for up to 6 months. Neither source restricts patient care or household contact, and the CDC asks workers to tell the treating provider about other medications, not to stop them.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Precautions during follow-up: HIV; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Follow-up

preguntas.pregunta: Which benefit does ONC attribute to electronic health records?
opciones: Less duplicate testing, and legible documentation that supports accurate coding and billing
An automatic release of records to any provider who asks, without further authorization
A guarantee that no unauthorized person will ever reach the information they contain
An exemption from the Security Rule, since certified systems already meet its standards
preguntas.explicacion: The advantages ONC lists include accurate, up-to-date and complete information at the point of care, quicker access for more coordinated care, secure sharing with patients and clinicians, fewer medical errors, safer prescribing, legible and complete documentation with streamlined coding and billing, better privacy and security of patient data, and lower costs through less paperwork and less duplicated testing.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What are the advantages of electronic health records?

preguntas.pregunta: Besides reading the number, what does the daily temperature routine ask staff to look at on the thermometer itself?
opciones: Whether the column is separated, or there are gas bubbles or cracks
Whether the probe still sits in the middle shelf of the compartment
Whether the calibration sticker is still inside its expiry period
Whether the minimum and maximum display has been reset since the last read
preguntas.explicacion: The recording instructions add a physical check to the daily reading: each time the thermometer is read, look for a separated column, for gas bubbles and for cracks, where those apply. Resetting the minimum and maximum display belongs to the optional data logger used over weekends and closures, and it is done after the reading rather than instead of the inspection.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who hurried in and is visibly anxious has a regular strip at 108 with upright P waves in I and II. Which reading fits?
opciones: A sinus rhythm sped up by stress, one of the physiologic triggers
A rhythm from the AV node, since any rate past 100 starts there
An artifact of movement, which doubles the complexes counted
A recording error, since the paper ran at 50 mm per second
preguntas.explicacion: Sinus tachycardia is the same tracing as normal sinus rhythm with a rate above 100, and its physiologic causes are catecholamine-driven: exercise, stress, pain and anxiety. Those cases usually need no cardiac treatment, but the strip still goes to the provider to read.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Tachycardia", Etiology

preguntas.pregunta: For whom is osteoporosis screening recommended to prevent fractures?
opciones: Women 65 and older, and younger postmenopausal women at increased risk
Women 50 and older, and younger postmenopausal women at increased risk
Women 65 and older only, with no recommendation below that age
All adults 65 and older, regardless of sex or of risk factors
preguntas.explicacion: Two separate recommendations exist. One covers women 65 years or older; the other covers postmenopausal women younger than 65 whose risk of an osteoporotic fracture is raised, judged with a clinical risk assessment. Neither one extends the recommendation to men on the same terms.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: A and B Recommendations — Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: Screening

preguntas.pregunta: How many sections does a GHS-format Safety Data Sheet have, and which of them does OSHA not enforce?
opciones: 16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 12 through 15
16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 9 through 11 and 16
12 sections; OSHA does not enforce the last two, transport and regulatory
8 sections, one per required pictogram; all are enforced by OSHA
preguntas.explicacion: A safety data sheet under the Hazard Communication standard has 16 numbered sections in a fixed order. Sections 12 through 15, ecological information, disposal, transport and regulatory information, must be present to match the GHS, but OSHA does not enforce their content because other agencies handle those matters. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold technical data such as physical properties, reactivity, toxicology and the date of preparation, and they are enforced. Eight is the number of pictograms OSHA requires, not of SDS sections.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the National CLAS Standards, what is owed to a patient with limited English proficiency?
opciones: Language assistance at no cost, announced in writing and out loud
Language assistance at cost, once the patient asks for it in writing
A translated consent form only, since the rest is spoken anyway
A bilingual staff member who has had no interpreter training
preguntas.explicacion: One standard tells organizations to offer language assistance at no cost to the person, so care is not delayed. Another tells them to inform everyone, in writing and orally, that the service exists. A third requires competent interpreters, which rules out grabbing whoever happens to be bilingual.

preguntas.pregunta: What has to be true for consent to be valid?
opciones: Enough mental capacity, and no coercion, fraud or mistake behind it
A signature on the practice's own form, witnessed by a staff member
A relative present at the time the person agrees to the procedure
A note in the record showing the person was told the likely outcome
preguntas.explicacion: Consent means the person voluntarily and willingly agrees to what is proposed. The person consenting must have sufficient mental capacity, and the agreement must be free of coercion, fraud or error. It divides into express consent, given directly in speech or writing, and implied consent, inferred from actions, signs, facts or even silence.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: consent

preguntas.pregunta: An epinephrine autoinjector has to be used. How is the device handled?
opciones: Grasp the middle, pull the cap, press the tip to the outer thigh, hold 5 seconds
Grasp the top, pull the cap, press the tip to the outer thigh, hold 30 seconds
Grasp the middle, pull the cap, press the tip to the deltoid, hold for 5 seconds
Grasp the bottom, pull the cap, press the tip to the abdomen, hold for 5 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The device is grasped firmly around its middle, with the hands away from the top and the bottom, because covering either end can fire it into the user. The activation cap comes off the top, and the tip that holds the needle is pressed perpendicular to the outer middle of the thigh of either leg until a click is heard, then held in place at least 5 seconds. The needle is covered by the tip on removal.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Safe and Effective Administration of Vaccines and Epinephrine Autoinjection", Anaphylaxis and Epinephrine Autoinjector
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.2.c(1)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with influenza symptoms asks whether it matters how soon the swab is taken. What is the answer?
opciones: Yes: shedding in the upper airway falls off about 3 to 4 days after onset, so earlier is better
No: the amount of virus in the upper airway stays steady for about two weeks after onset
Yes: the virus is undetectable in the first 3 to 4 days, so waiting improves the yield
No: a negative rapid test rules out influenza whenever the swab happens to be taken
preguntas.explicacion: Influenza shedding in the upper respiratory tract drops substantially around 3 to 4 days after illness begins, so specimens are collected as close to onset as possible, ideally within four days. Infants and immunosuppressed patients may shed longer. A negative rapid antigen test never rules the infection out and should not stop further testing by molecular assay or empiric treatment.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Information on Collection of Respiratory Specimens for Influenza Virus Testing, Outpatients; and CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Considerations

preguntas.pregunta: Why should an explanation given to a six-year-old stay away from abstract ideas?
opciones: Logic at that age is applied to concrete, tangible things
Symbolic play and make-believe are beyond that age group
Language is not yet used to recall events already past
Object permanence has not been established at that age
preguntas.explicacion: In the concrete operational period a child applies logical rules to concrete or tangible objects and can mentally transform what is seen and heard; abstraction waits for formal operations around 11. Symbolic play, drawing and the verbal recall of past events all arrive earlier, in the preoperational period.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Piaget", Issues of Concern; and Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · CMA F.1.c(7)(b) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(a) · CMAA 2D k17

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is listed as a specific care coordination activity rather than a broad approach?
opciones: Settling who is accountable and who takes responsibility
Using health information technology in the practice
Operating the practice as a patient-centered medical home
Running a care management program in the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Coordinated care is reached two ways. Broad approaches are the general levers: teamwork, care management, medication management, health information technology and the patient-centered medical home. Specific activities are the concrete steps: settling accountability, sharing knowledge, helping with transitions, assessing needs and goals, and building a proactive care plan.

preguntas.pregunta: The label of a lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide tablet carries a boxed warning. What does that warning cover?
opciones: Fetal toxicity: the drug is stopped as soon as a pregnancy is detected
Lactic acidosis: reported cases have ended in death, hypothermia, bradycardia
Severe cutaneous reactions: the drug is stopped if the rash keeps spreading
Head and neck angioedema: reported more often in Black patients on this class
preguntas.explicacion: The box on this label is short and single-minded: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system injure and can kill the developing fetus, so treatment stops as soon as pregnancy is known. Lactic acidosis is the boxed warning of metformin and severe cutaneous reactions belong to the amoxicillin label. The angioedema sentence is in this same label, but under Indications and Warnings, not inside the box.

preguntas.pregunta: What are essential health benefits?
opciones: Ten categories of service that plans must cover under the health care law
Ten categories of service that plans may add to lower the monthly premium
The list of covered prescription drugs that each plan updates every year
The preventive screenings that plans must provide without any cost sharing
preguntas.explicacion: Essential health benefits are the ten categories of service the health care law requires plans to cover, among them doctors' services, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, prescription drugs, pregnancy and childbirth, and mental health care. Dental coverage must be offered for children; for adults it is optional. The covered drug list is the formulary, and free preventive care is one protection among several, not the whole set of categories.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Essential health benefits

preguntas.pregunta: A patient cannot say back what he has to do before a glucose tolerance test. What comes next?
opciones: Explain it another way and ask again, until he can describe the plan in his own words
Hand him the printed instruction sheet and ask him to read the relevant lines out loud
Document that the teaching was offered and refused, and tell the ordering provider later
Repeat the same explanation word for word but more slowly, and move on once he nods
preguntas.explicacion: When teach-back uncovers a misunderstanding, the cycle repeats: explain it using a different approach, ask for the teach-back again, and keep going until the patient describes the information correctly in his own words. Words repeated back verbatim are a warning sign rather than a pass, and a nod proves nothing at all.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method

preguntas.pregunta: A patient breathes in clusters of deep, even breaths separated by pauses, with no build-up or fading within each cluster. Which pattern is charted?
opciones: Biot respiration, clusters of deep breaths broken by spells of apnea
Cheyne-Stokes respiration, breaths that swell and fade before a pause
Kussmaul respiration, deep and rapid breathing that never pauses at all
Paradoxical ventilation, the chest wall drawing in during inspiration
preguntas.explicacion: The pause is shared by two patterns, and the shape of the breaths between pauses tells them apart: Cheyne-Stokes grows and fades in a crescendo, while Biot keeps the same depth from breath to breath. Biot respiration follows damage to the pons from stroke, trauma or herniation, and also appears with opioid toxicity.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the lobby coughs forcefully after swallowing a piece of food and can still speak. What is the correct response?
opciones: Stay with the patient and let the coughing go on, watching it weaken
Deliver five firm back blows between the shoulder blades without waiting
Begin cycles of five abdominal thrusts before the airway closes completely
Sweep a finger through the mouth to hook out the piece of food lodged there
preguntas.explicacion: First aid for choking is not started while the person is coughing forcefully and able to speak: a strong cough often expels the object by itself. The rescuer stays ready to act if the cough weakens or speech is lost. A blind finger sweep can push the object further down toward the larynx and is avoided in every age group.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about discrimination in health care is correct?
opciones: It can rest on perceived group membership, and no harm needs to have occurred
It requires proof that the patient was harmed by the action or omission
It requires that the patient actually belong to the group in question
It is limited to the overt acts that Title VII and the ADA prohibit
preguntas.explicacion: Discrimination in health care is negative actions or lack of consideration based on preconceived notions about identity, adding that it can occur on perceived membership, that a person need not belong to the group, and that harm does not have to occur. Title VII and the ADA reduced overt racism, after which awareness shifted to the subtler microaggressions.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", sections Introduction and Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e

preguntas.pregunta: When explaining fasting instructions, which approach follows the health-literacy principles for communicating clearly?
opciones: Give one to three need-to-know points in plain words, and repeat them
Cover every instruction once, quickly, so that none of them is left out
Use the precise medical terms so the patient learns them for next time
Hand over the printed sheet and skip the spoken explanation entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Limit content to one to three need-to-know or need-to-do points and to emphasize them more than once, to slow down, and to use plain non-medical language, because jargon excludes patients. Kessels found that up to 80% of what patients are told is forgotten at once, and nearly half of what they keep is wrong, which rules out a fast, exhaustive or paper-only approach.

Services or supplies listed in the plan's contract as covered benefits for the year

preguntas.pregunta: A trough level is ordered for a patient on an antiepileptic drug. When is the sample drawn?

At the highest point of the dosing interval, just after the next dose
Halfway between two doses, when the concentration is most stable
At the same hour each morning, independently of the dose times

preguntas.pregunta: A biller is uneasy because a Medicare claim has still not paid twenty-two days after it was sent. What do the benchmarks for time to payment say?

preguntas.pregunta: Which foods are patients told to avoid before a guaiac-based fecal occult blood test?

Beets, blackberries, rhubarb, carrots and other strongly colored foods
Onions, garlic and asparagus, which change the odor of the specimen
Cranberry juice and a high-protein diet, which acidify the specimen

One episode of vomiting in a child who is alert and behaving normally
Tenderness at the site of the blow with slight swelling under the skin

Up to three months, under the skin of the chest wall

The tympanic membrane, which is convenient but not advised as a primary site

After the light blue tube, before the lavender
Last, after the grey tube
Right after a non-additive discard tube

preguntas.pregunta: A patient takes 1,000 mg of vitamin C daily and is about to do a guaiac stool test. What effect should be expected if she continues?
opciones: A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid blocks the guaiac color reaction
A false-positive result, because ascorbic acid has peroxidase activity
An unchanged result, because only vitamin C above 2,000 mg a day interferes
A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid stops intestinal bleeding for 3 days

At the wrist, listening over the radial artery
At the neck, listening over the common carotid artery

preguntas.pregunta: A wound culture is being taken. From where in the wound is the swab taken?

From the thickest pocket of pus, where the organisms are present in the largest numbers
From the eschar at the edge, where the oldest tissue holds the longest-standing organisms
From the skin just outside the margin, where exudate collects and dries against the dressing

Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; smooth is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; skeletal is striated and involuntary
Striated, spindle and rectangular; spindle is striated and involuntary
preguntas.explicacion: Skeletal muscle attaches to bone, is striated and is under voluntary control. Superficial, the depth once called a first-degree burn
Full thickness, the depth once called a third-degree burn
Superficial with inhalation injury, since blisters mean smoke
preguntas.explicacion: Blisters mark the partial-thickness level, which reaches the outer layer and the layer beneath it and is painful, red and swollen. preguntas.pregunta: A patient sues after an injury during a draw. Which four elements must the plaintiff prove for a medical malpractice claim to succeed?
opciones: A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and damages
A duty to the patient, a written complaint, an apology refused, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, an intent to harm, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and a policy in force
preguntas.explicacion: A mistake alone is not malpractice. The plaintiff has to establish that the clinician owed a duty to this patient, that the duty was breached against the standard of care, that the act or omission caused the poor outcome rather than the underlying disease, and that damages followed. preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the three steps of hemostasis occur after a vessel is punctured?
opciones: Vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation
Platelet plug, vascular spasm, coagulation
Coagulation, fibrinolysis, platelet plug
Vascular spasm, coagulation, fibrinolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a ruptured vessel, in three steps: first the smooth muscle of the vessel wall contracts (vascular spasm), then platelets stick to the exposed collagen and to each other (platelet plug), and finally a fibrin clot forms (coagulation). Fibrinolysis is not one of the three; it is the later breakdown of the clot as the vessel heals. Failure of any step leads to hemorrhage.

Over the lateral antecubital fossa, where the radial artery begins its course
Over the middle of the cuff, so the sound reaches it through the inflated bladder
Over the wrist at the radial artery, where the pulse was palpated before inflating

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room starts a nosebleed. How is it managed?

Sitting up and tilting the head back, pinching the bridge for 5 minutes
Lying down flat with a cold pack on the neck and the nostrils packed
Sitting up and blowing the nose gently every minute to clear the clots
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits, leans forward so blood is not swallowed, breathes through the mouth, and squeezes the soft part of the nose shut between thumb and finger for a full 10 minutes without checking early. preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation?

Irregularly irregular wide complexes with clear P waves
Regular narrow complexes with a P wave before each of them

preguntas.pregunta: What is the basic difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
opciones: Medicare is federal and age or disability based; Medicaid is federal-state and income based
Medicare is federal and income based; Medicaid is federal-state and age or disability based

Medicare pays first and the group health plan pays second during that period

preguntas.pregunta: The rapid HIV test on the source patient will not be back for hours. What do the WHO and CDC guidance say about starting PEP?
opciones: Start it without waiting for results; stop it later if the source proves negative
Wait for the result, since PEP is only prescribed once the source is confirmed positive

preguntas.explicacion: Health workers should not wait for test results before taking or administering PEP, and prophylaxis can be stopped if the source turns out to be negative. The CDC says the same for the exposed person's own rapid test: if results are unavailable and PEP is indicated, give the first dose immediately and stop later if the person has HIV or the source is found not to. preguntas.pregunta: A product insert states the kit is "FDA-cleared." What can the testing site conclude from that alone?
opciones: Only that it is substantially equivalent to a marketed test, not its CLIA category
That it is waived, because FDA clearance is one of the three routes to a waiver
That it is moderate complexity until the manufacturer applies for a waiver
That it may be used under a Certificate of Waiver at any point-of-care site
preguntas.explicacion: FDA-cleared means the agency reviewed the test and judged it substantially equivalent to one already legally marketed for the same use. That review can end in a waived, moderate or high categorization, so clearance by itself does not tell the site which certificate it needs. The waiver or complexity status is usually printed in the package insert or found in the FDA CLIA database.

preguntas.pregunta: Why may a level be drawn while a patient on an antiepileptic is entirely seizure-free?
opciones: It sets a benchmark to compare against if control or symptoms change
It confirms the diagnosis of epilepsy without an electroencephalogram
It takes the place of the clinical assessment of how the drug is working
It is required before any brand may be exchanged for a generic
preguntas.explicacion: A single level can reasonably be taken while the patient is seizure-free, and it then serves as a benchmark for future reference should seizure control deteriorate or symptoms of toxicity appear. Assessment of efficacy should itself be clinical, with level monitoring used as a complementary tool; epilepsy is assessed clinically with electroencephalograms and imaging.
