preguntas.pregunta: Within the metric system, which way does the decimal point move when a larger unit is converted into a smaller one?
opciones: To the right, because the unit is getting smaller
To the left, because the unit is getting smaller
It stays put, since only the unit's name changes
It moves both ways, depending on the drug ordered
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is organized in units of ten, so a conversion inside it only moves the decimal point: to the right when going to a smaller unit, and to the left when going to a larger one. Grams to milligrams is a move to the right by three places; milligrams to grams is the same move to the left. The prefixes run kilo, hecto, deca, the base unit, deci, centi and milli.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4: Metric Equivalencies
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(1) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7

preguntas.pregunta: A man is having a urethral discharge culture collected. Which instruction protects the result?
opciones: Do not urinate for 1 hour before the test, and ideally wait 2 hours after voiding
Urinate right before the test, so the urethra is clear of any residual urine
Do not urinate for 8 hours before the test, and take no fluids at all during that time
Urinate a small amount into the toilet first, then hold the rest for the swab
preguntas.explicacion: Voiding washes away the very organisms the swab is meant to pick up, so the patient is asked not to urinate for an hour before the test and the swab is best taken at least 2 hours after the last void. The tip of the penis is cleaned with sterile cotton or gauze, and the swab goes about three-fourths of an inch, roughly 2 cm, into the urethra and is turned.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urethral discharge culture (003750), How the Test is Performed and How to Prepare for the Test

preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the boxed warning of an extended-release metformin product describe?
opciones: Lactic acidosis, with malaise, myalgia, breathing trouble, drowsiness and belly pain
Hypoglycemia deep enough to bring on seizures, coma and death if a meal is missed
Fetal toxicity, so that the drug has to stop as soon as a pregnancy is detected
Anaphylactic reactions, occasionally fatal, of the kind seen with beta-lactam drugs
preguntas.explicacion: The box on this label describes metformin-associated lactic acidosis reported after marketing, which has ended in death, hypothermia, hypotension and resistant bradyarrhythmias. It lists the risk factors, among them kidney impairment, age 65 or over, contrast studies, surgery and heavy alcohol use, and it directs that the drug be stopped and hemodialysis started promptly when acidosis is suspected.
preguntas.fuente: DailyMed, GLUMETZA (metformin hydrochloride) extended-release tablets, Boxed Warning

preguntas.pregunta: What can cause alternating-current interference on a tracing?
opciones: Loops in the lead wires, or poor electrode contact
A cold patient, or a nerve disorder of the arms and legs
A pillow under the head, or crossed legs on the table
Scaly skin, or an electrode placed over breast tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Interference from the current in the walls is common in clinics and hospitals, and it traces back either to poor contact at an electrode or to equipment near the room. Wires are pulled straight when they are attached because a loop in a lead wire also invites it.

preguntas.pregunta: What happens when the accommodating style is used too often?
opciones: It breeds resentment and comes across as weakness
It lets disagreements fester into team dysfunction
It damages psychological safety and stifles speaking up
It costs more effort than any of the other four styles
preguntas.explicacion: Accommodating means yielding to keep the relationship or because the issue matters more to the other side; it is useful when relational capital counts or when you were wrong, but overuse breeds resentment and signals weakness. Festering disagreement belongs to habitual avoiding, harm to psychological safety to competing, and high effort to collaborating.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is on the table for a 12-lead. How is the examination gown handled?
opciones: A man's gown top comes off; a woman's stays draped over her chest
A woman's gown top comes off; a man's stays draped over his chest
Both gowns come off, and a sheet is drawn up over the shoulders
Both gowns stay closed, and the electrodes go on top of them
preguntas.explicacion: A male patient takes the top of the gown off so the chest is exposed. A female patient slips her arms out but keeps the gown over her chest, and after the chest electrodes are on, the gown is carefully re-draped over her while the tracing is recorded.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's adult daughter is helping with his care and asks about the medication list. What does the Privacy Rule permit?
opciones: Sharing what is directly relevant to her involvement in his care, on his informal permission
Sharing the entire record with her, since a relative helping with care stands in for the patient
Withholding the list unless she is appointed as his personal representative by a court
Sharing only after she signs an authorization form on the patient's behalf at the front desk
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may rely on informal permission to give family, relatives, friends or others the patient identifies the information directly relevant to that person's involvement in the care or payment for care. That is narrower than a personal representative, who stands in the patient's shoes for all purposes. The same provision lets a pharmacist hand filled prescriptions to someone acting for the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: A primary care clinician sends a focused question to a specialist and receives the answer two days later. Which telehealth service is that?
opciones: An electronic consultation, which is one of the asynchronous arrangements
A facilitated virtual visit, where an assistant gathers the objective data
A teletriage visit, used to sort symptoms quickly in an urgent setting
A remote critical care consultation, which guides a team at the bedside
preguntas.explicacion: Asynchronous telemedicine, the store-and-forward method, gathers history, images and diagnostic data and sends them to a specialist to interpret later. Electronic consultations, where a primary care clinician asks a specialist a focused question, belong here, along with portal messaging, teledermatology, remote reading of images and digital intake questionnaires.

preguntas.pregunta: In a finger-prick on a small child, what can the parent be asked to do with the child's wrist to help blood flow?
opciones: Rhythmically tighten and release the wrist
Hold the wrist tightly throughout, as a tourniquet
Shake the hand downward between drops
Press the wrist flat, palm up, on the chair arm
preguntas.explicacion: For a paediatric finger-prick the parent can rhythmically tighten and release the child's wrist to ensure sufficient flow. In the lap position for immobilization the parent holds the wrist palm down; the palm-up grip belongs to the table position for venepuncture, where a firm grasp on the wrist gives the phlebotomist a kind of tourniquet. Massaging or squeezing the finger is to be avoided.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Paediatric and neonatal patients

preguntas.pregunta: A basic metabolic panel was drawn after the skin was prepared with povidone iodine. Which results does the WHO warn may be falsely raised?
opciones: Potassium, phosphorus and uric acid
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate
Glucose, BUN and creatinine
Albumin, bilirubin and total protein
preguntas.explicacion: The note to Step 5 explains why alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine: blood contaminated with iodine may show falsely increased potassium, phosphorus or uric acid. The other groups are real components of the metabolic panels (electrolytes, kidney waste products, liver proteins), but the WHO does not link them to iodine contamination.

preguntas.pregunta: An instrument is dropped during a minor procedure and is needed at once. Which use of flash sterilization does the guideline accept?
opciones: This one, because the item will be used immediately and cannot be packaged and stored first
This one, but only if the tray it came from is recalled and reprocessed as a whole set
None, because a dropped item has touched the floor and must go through a full wrapped cycle
None, unless the office has no second set, which is the only accepted reason for the short cycle
preguntas.explicacion: Reprocessing an inadvertently dropped instrument is one of the situations the guideline names for flash sterilization, along with cleaned items that cannot be packaged, sterilized and stored before use. What it forbids is running the short cycle for convenience, to save time, or instead of buying a second instrument set.

preguntas.pregunta: What standard limits Medicare coverage of an item or service?
opciones: It must be reasonable and necessary for diagnosis or treatment, within a benefit category
It must be ordered by a specialist and delivered in a hospital outpatient department
It must be listed in the fee schedule with a payment amount for the current year
It must be approved in advance by the contractor for each individual patient
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare coverage reaches items and services that are reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of an illness or injury and that fall within a benefit category and are not excluded. National coverage determinations settle this nationally through an evidence-based process, and where there is no national policy the contractors may issue local coverage determinations. Being on a fee schedule or ordered by a specialist decides nothing by itself.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006976

preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms does the WHO describe in some vacuum-tube systems for dealing with the used needle?
opciones: One retracts the needle into the barrel and snaps shut; another releases it into the sharps container
One shears the needle from the hub with a small blade; another bends it so it cannot be used a second time
One recaps the needle automatically; another sterilizes it in place for reuse on the same patient
One dissolves the needle in disinfectant; another seals it inside the last tube that was filled
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says some systems have a mechanism that, once the needle has been used, retracts it into the barrel and snaps it shut, while others have a quick-release mechanism that dislodges the used needle straight into the sharps container. Shearing or breaking contaminated needles is prohibited by OSHA, and no source describes automatic recapping, dissolving or sealing a needle in a tube.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems

preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what changes once a patient enrolls in hospice. Which service does Medicare stop covering?
opciones: Treatment intended to cure the terminal illness, and drugs meant to cure it
Nursing visits and the medical equipment that the hospice plan of care calls for
Short-term inpatient care the hospice team arranges when symptoms get out of hand
Care for a health problem that is unrelated to the terminal illness itself
preguntas.explicacion: Once the benefit starts, Medicare no longer pays for treatment aimed at curing the terminal illness or its related conditions, nor for prescription drugs meant to cure rather than to control symptoms or relieve pain. It also stops paying for care from a hospice the team did not set up, and for room and board. Original Medicare still covers unrelated health problems.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Costs
preguntas.subtema: What the hospice benefit changes · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Which sutures are taken out first when an incision line is being cleared?
opciones: Every second one, with the wound reassessed before any of the rest come out
Every one at once, since leaving some in place delays the closure of the skin
The two at the ends first, since they carry the most tension along the line
The ones nearest any redness first, since those are the ones most likely to infect
preguntas.explicacion: Alternate sutures are removed first, then the wound is judged again: if the edges are well approximated the rest can follow, and if there is doubt the remainder wait several days. Removing them all too early risks dehiscence. Steri-Strips may be applied before removal to lower that risk, and the line is watched for separation throughout.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.10 Checklist for Intermittent Suture Removal

preguntas.pregunta: From what age is body mass index calculated in children, and how often?
opciones: From the age of 2, and once a year as part of the growth assessment
From the age of 5, and once a year as part of the growth assessment
From birth, and at every well-child visit alongside length and weight
From the age of 2, but only when the weight has crossed a percentile line
preguntas.explicacion: The index can be worked out from the age of 2, once height and weight are both being measured in the usual way, and an annual assessment using the growth charts is recommended from that age. Tracking it over time is what makes it useful, for monitoring growth and development and for dosing medicines.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Body Mass Index (BMI)

preguntas.pregunta: A staff member e-mails a lab result to the wrong patient. How does the Breach Notification Rule treat that event at the outset?
opciones: As a breach, unless a risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised
As a breach only after the Office for Civil Rights investigates and reaches that conclusion
As an incidental disclosure, since a misdirected message cannot reasonably be prevented
As a security incident rather than a breach, because e-mail systems are technical safeguards
preguntas.explicacion: An impermissible use or disclosure under the Privacy Rule is presumed to be a breach. The presumption falls only if the covered entity or business associate demonstrates a low probability that the PHI was compromised, using a risk assessment. Entities may also skip the assessment altogether and simply notify.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a bluing agent placed in the toilet before a federal drug test collection?
opciones: To keep toilet water from being used to dilute the specimen
To preserve the drug metabolites until the specimen reaches the laboratory
To disinfect the bowl between one donor and the next donor
To mark the temperature strip so the reading can be seen clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Preparing the collection area means putting a bluing agent in the toilet and, where none is available or an automatic flush is fitted, turning off the water and flushing to empty the bowl. Water sources inside the restroom are turned off or secured, soap and disinfectant are removed as potential adulterants, and places where something could be hidden are inspected. The donor is also told not to flush.

preguntas.pregunta: Every complex in lead I comes out inverted. What is checked first?
opciones: The arm electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The leg electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The chest electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The clip connectors, which are almost certainly loose
preguntas.explicacion: Inverted complexes throughout lead I point to the two arm wires having been swapped, a common error that the technician does not always catch. Reversed leads can even produce something that looks like electrical interference, so the hook-up is verified before blaming the room or the machine.

preguntas.pregunta: Which pre-test instruction reduces false results with a guaiac-based fecal occult blood test?
opciones: Avoid red meat for three days, since heme has peroxidase activity of its own
Avoid red meat for three days, since dietary iron binds the guaiac on the card
Take extra vitamin C for three days, since it sharpens the color change
Avoid raw fruit for seven days, since gastric acid cannot break down plant fiber
preguntas.explicacion: The guaiac reaction reads peroxidase activity, so anything else with that activity fools it. Red meat is avoided for about three days for that reason, and raw vegetables rich in plant peroxidases are discouraged. Vitamin C works the other way: a gram or two a day can produce a false negative. Aspirin, warfarin and other blood thinners are stopped seven days ahead.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: What does that code say about a certified professional's knowledge over time?
opciones: That learning continues and that the person keeps up with current research
That the original training is sufficient until the credential is renewed
That new techniques are learned only through the employer's own program
That research is followed only when the employer pays for the coursework
preguntas.explicacion: One of the six duties is to keep learning, applying and advancing scientific and practical knowledge and skills, and to stay current with the latest research and how it is used in practice. Nothing ties that duty to who pays or who provides the course, and the very purpose of renewing the credential is to show that the holder stays current.

preguntas.pregunta: A smoker says he knows he should quit but is not ready to pick a date. Which stage of change is that?
opciones: Contemplation, weighing change but still holding back
Precontemplation, with no interest in changing at all
Preparation, lining up the tools and a plan to start
Maintenance, guarding a change already carried through
preguntas.explicacion: The transtheoretical model runs precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action and maintenance. Someone considering change but still clinging to fears and reluctance is contemplating. Preparation is the point where tools and strategies are actively being lined up, sometimes with help planning.

preguntas.pregunta: By what mechanism does the EDTA in a purple top tube keep the blood from clotting?
opciones: It binds the calcium in the sample so the coagulation cascade cannot proceed
It inhibits the formation of thrombin, as the heparin in a green tube does
It activates clotting on contact so the cells can be spun away from the serum
It blocks the breakdown of glucose, which also keeps the cells from clumping
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA works by chelating the calcium ions in the blood, and the WHO table describes the same action as forming calcium salts to remove calcium. Because the blood never clots, the liquid left after spinning is plasma. Thrombin inhibition is how heparin works, contact activation is the plain red tube, and blocking glycolysis is the sodium fluoride of the grey tube.

preguntas.pregunta: The practice's billing vendor suffers a breach of unsecured PHI. What does the vendor owe the practice?
opciones: Notice without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovering the breach
Notice within 30 days, together with the individual notices already mailed on its own
No more than its yearly report to the Secretary, which the practice can look up
Notice only once the practice asks, since the duty to notify patients rests with the practice
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate that suffers a breach must notify the covered entity without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days from discovery, and should identify each affected individual and supply what the entity needs for its own notices. The covered entity remains ultimately responsible for notifying the individuals, although it may delegate that task to the business associate when that makes more sense.

Straighten the lead wires so that no loops are left in them
Ask the patient to hold a breath while the strip is recorded
Switch the machine off and on so the self test runs again

Unsolicited advice
Changing the subject abruptly
Responding defensively

preguntas.pregunta: While a practice works down its backlog it is told to apply max packing. What does that mean in the appointment book?
opciones: Handling any upcoming preventive or screening need at whatever visit brings the patient in
Booking the patient's next preventive and screening visits before she leaves the office
Replacing one-to-one visits for a chronic condition with a single group visit
Using the telephone and e-mail for concerns that do not really need a visit at all

preguntas.pregunta: Which dose, concentration and route of epinephrine are used for anaphylaxis in an adult?
opciones: 0.3 to 0.5 mL of 1:1,000 intramuscularly, the thigh being preferred
0.3 to 0.5 mL of 1:10,000 intramuscularly, the deltoid being preferred
0.3 to 0.5 mL of 1:1,000 subcutaneously, the upper arm being preferred
0.01 mg per kg of 1:1,000 intramuscularly, for adults as well as children
preguntas.explicacion: Epinephrine is given intramuscularly at 0.3 to 0.5 mL of the 1:1,000 concentration, and the thigh is preferred to the deltoid when possible; the intramuscular route works faster and gives better outcomes than subcutaneous or intravascular. The 1:10,000 concentration is the one used if epinephrine has to go intravenously. Pediatric dosing is 0.01 mg per kilogram, or 0.15 mg by autoinjector.

preguntas.pregunta: A chemical splashes into a patient's eye at the front desk. What is done?

Cover both eyes with a dry pad and send the patient to the hospital
Rinse the eye for 30 seconds and then check the vision with a chart
Hold the eyelid open and wipe the chemical away with sterile gauze
preguntas.explicacion: A chemical in the eye is flushed with water immediately and the irrigation keeps going for at least 15 minutes under running water, and medical help is sought right away. Household remedies, ointments and salves are not put on a chemical burn, and a blister or dead skin is left alone.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her video appointments freeze constantly. Which barrier does HHS name as the biggest one for telehealth?

Lack of a telephone line at the address where the patient normally lives
Lack of a signed consent form covering the use of video technology
Lack of a printer at home for the visit summary the clinician sends
preguntas.explicacion: The single biggest barrier named is a lack of access to internet service with enough bandwidth for video. The suggestions offered are that the patient may qualify for federal support through the Lifeline program, that many fast food restaurants have free Wi-Fi reaching the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often private rooms.

preguntas.pregunta: After a tuberculin skin test is placed, the expected wheal does not appear. What is done?
opciones: Repeat the test at once on another site, at least five centimetres from the first
Repeat the test in seven days on the other arm, and read that one at 48 hours
Read the first site anyway at 48 to 72 hours and measure the induration
Massage the site so the solution spreads, then read it at 48 to 72 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Delivering the solution into the dermis raises a wheal six to ten millimetres across, and that wheal is the sign the technique worked. When it does not form, the test is repeated immediately on another site at least five centimetres away from the first. The patient is told not to touch the area and to keep it uncovered and clean, and the site, date and time, tester, lot number and manufacturer are documented.

The abnormal findings and your own read of the situation
The patient's name and location and the recent vital signs
What you want the provider to order, change or reassess
preguntas.explicacion: Background carries the pertinent history: admitting medical diagnoses, code status, recent relevant laboratory or diagnostic results and allergies. The abnormal findings and your evaluation go in Assessment, the name, location and vital signs go in Situation, and what you want done goes in Request or Recommendation.

preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker, the CDC puts the risk of HBV infection from a single needlestick with HBV-positive blood at which figure?
opciones: 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source's HBeAg status
0.3 percent, the same figure the CDC gives for HIV
About 1.8 percent, the same as for hepatitis C
Under 0.1 percent, since most workers are vaccinated
preguntas.explicacion: A susceptible person stuck or cut with HBV-infected blood faces a 6 to 30 percent chance of infection, and where in that range depends on the source's hepatitis B e antigen status: HBsAg-positive individuals who are also HBeAg-positive carry more virus and transmit more readily. Workers who were vaccinated and developed immunity are at virtually no risk, which is why the question specifies a susceptible worker. There is no known risk from intact skin. The 0.3 and 1.8 percent figures are for HIV and HCV.

preguntas.pregunta: A lavender EDTA tube for a CBC arrives with a visible red-cell clot. Which handling error is the most likely cause according to the rejection study?
opciones: Poor mixing after collection and leaving the tube lying horizontally instead of upright
Centrifuging the tube too soon, before the anticoagulant had time to dissolve
Transporting the tube in a padded holder, which stops the additive from circulating
Filling the tube above its nominal volume so that the EDTA was diluted by excess blood
preguntas.explicacion: Visible clots in anticoagulated tubes, whether red-cell clots in whole blood or fibrin in plasma, are attributed mainly to poor mixing after the draw and to tubes left horizontal rather than vertical; manufacturers and CLSI ask for gentle inversion several times to bring blood and additive into contact. Anticoagulated tubes are not centrifuged for a CBC, and racks or padded holders are the recommended way to carry tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: A non-blanching spot at the puncture site measures about four millimetres. What is it called?
opciones: Purpura, because it is larger than two millimetres
Petechia, because it is smaller than ten millimetres
Erythema, because it sits over an inflamed puncture
Ecchymosis, because it is smaller than ten millimetres
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is two millimetres: a non-blanching spot below that size is a petechia and one above it is purpura. A very large bruised area of bleeding under the skin is called an ecchymosis, and redness that fades under pressure is erythema, not bleeding at all.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the recommended daily allowance of vitamin D for adults, and how does it change with age?
opciones: 15 mcg (600 IU) through age 70, rising to 20 mcg (800 IU) at 71
15 mcg (600 IU) through age 50, rising to 20 mcg (800 IU) at 51
10 mcg (400 IU) through age 70, rising to 15 mcg (600 IU) at 71
20 mcg (800 IU) at every adult age, with no change after 70
preguntas.explicacion: Adults from 19 through 70 are set at 15 micrograms, which the label shows as 600 international units, and the figure moves up to 20 micrograms, or 800 IU, from age 71. The 10 microgram amount belongs to infants. Too little vitamin D causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in teens and adults.

preguntas.pregunta: Over four hours a patient's pulse and respiratory rate climb steadily, though every value is still inside the usual range. How is that read?
opciones: As possible early deterioration, since the trend carries more than one value
As normal, since a value inside the reference range is by definition normal
As measurement error, since real change would cross the range boundaries
As anxiety, the usual reason for a rise while the readings stay in range
preguntas.explicacion: Vital signs are compared with the patient's own earlier values, not only with a reference range. Trends over time carry more meaning than isolated measurements in evolving infection, bleeding, respiratory failure or shock, and even modest progressive change can be early physiologic deterioration while every reading still sits inside the traditional range.

preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of a hazardous disinfectant arrives at a laboratory with a label but no safety data sheet. What must the employer do?
opciones: Obtain one from the manufacturer or importer as soon as possible
Return the shipment unopened, since the sheet travels with the label
Write one from the label, which carries the same hazard information
Wait for the next shipment, which must include the updated sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers and importers have to provide a safety data sheet with the first shipment and with the first shipment after the sheet is updated, either with the containers or beforehand. When a shipment labeled as a hazardous chemical arrives without one, the duty falls on the distributor or employer to obtain it from the manufacturer or importer as soon as possible, and they must also supply one on request. A label alone is not a substitute: it carries a fraction of what the sheet holds.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist collects three patients' tubes and labels them all at the desk afterwards. When and where should tubes be labeled?
opciones: Tube identification and labeling are done in the presence of the patient to avoid misidentification
Labeling at the desk is acceptable if the tubes were kept in separate racks per patient
Labels are applied before the draw, at the desk, so that the tubes are ready when the patient arrives
Labeling may wait until the laboratory receives the tubes with the matching requisitions
preguntas.explicacion: Both tube identification and tube labeling should be carried out in the presence of the patient to minimize the risk of tube misidentification, and identification data and labeling are double-checked before the blood is withdrawn. preguntas.pregunta: A clinic offers a mammogram to a woman with no symptoms. Which level of prevention is that?
opciones: Secondary prevention, which looks for disease before it declares itself
Primary prevention, which acts on risk factors while the person is healthy
Tertiary prevention, which limits the damage once disease is established
Primordial prevention, which acts on the socioeconomic and environmental risks
preguntas.explicacion: The levels follow the natural history of disease. Primary prevention works on modifiable risk factors in someone still healthy: diet, exercise, avoiding tobacco, keeping weight in range. Screening catches disease that has begun but is still silent, which is secondary. Tertiary prevention limits complications and disability once the disease is there.

preguntas.pregunta: Tissue typing, a paternity study and a DNA study are requested on the same patient. How many different tube types does the table assign?

Two, because paternity work is listed against the purple EDTA tube
Three, because each of the three studies has its own tube and colour
Two, because DNA studies are listed against the red clot activator tube
preguntas.explicacion: The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube carries all three uses in one row: HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies. preguntas.pregunta: How is therapeutic communication defined, following van Servellen (1997)?
opciones: A verbal and non-verbal exchange meant to help the patient overcome emotional distress
A verbal exchange meant to obtain a complete and accurate medical history quickly
A written and verbal exchange meant to document that informed consent was given
A non-verbal exchange used mainly with patients who are unable to speak
preguntas.explicacion: Van Servellen's now generally accepted definition reads: an exchange between patient and provider using verbal and non-verbal methods, whose ultimate goal is to help the patient get past some form of emotional or psychological distress. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the resting tracing studied closely before the exercise part of a stress test starts?
opciones: Some baseline changes make ischemia impossible to judge afterwards
Some baseline changes decide the speed of the very first stage
Some baseline changes set the target heart rate for the patient
Some baseline changes are copied onto the final report only
preguntas.explicacion: ST shifts of a millimeter or more, a bundle branch block, a paced rhythm, ventricular hypertrophy, pre-excitation or T-wave inversions all obscure what the test is looking for, and when one is present imaging is added. The resting strip is taken lying and standing.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic in a low-resource setting cannot afford safety-engineered devices. What does the guidance accept?
opciones: Skilled use of a needle and syringe is acceptable in that situation
Draws should be postponed until safety devices can be purchased
Needles may be reused between patients if they are sterilized first
Only capillary sampling should be offered until devices arrive
preguntas.explicacion: Cost drives what a low-resource service can buy, and where safety-engineered devices are not available, skilled use of a needle and syringe is accepted. preguntas.pregunta: An ESR rack sits on a shelf that leans a few degrees away from vertical. How much can that change the result?
opciones: Three degrees off vertical can raise the value by as much as thirty per cent
Three degrees off vertical can lower the value by as much as thirty per cent
Thirty degrees off vertical can raise the value by as much as three per cent
Tilt has no measurable effect once the tube has been standing for an hour
preguntas.explicacion: Tube orientation is one of the technical factors that alters this measurement: tilt and vibration both push the value up, and an angle of three degrees from vertical can raise it by up to thirty per cent. Elevated room temperature and direct sunlight also raise the reading.

preguntas.pregunta: At approximately what serum glucose concentration does glucose usually begin to appear in the urine of a person with normal kidneys?
opciones: About 180 mg/dL
About 126 mg/dL
About 250 mg/dL
About 600 mg/dL
preguntas.explicacion: Glycosuria appears when the filtered load of glucose exceeds the tubular cells' capacity to reabsorb it, which normally happens at a serum glucose near 180 mg/dL. The other figures belong to different rules: 126 mg/dL is the fasting plasma glucose threshold used to diagnose diabetes, acute hyperglycemia symptoms are usually absent below 250 mg/dL, and glucose above 600 mg/dL characterizes the hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state.

A repeat of the same concern in exactly the same words
A note in the chart that the concern was not accepted
A pause until the next shift takes over the patient

opciones: Fewer communication errors and shorter stays in hospital
Longer visits that patients go on to rate as less satisfying
More readmissions, because instructions have to be repeated
Fewer forms, since consent can then be taken out loud

preguntas.pregunta: In which layer of the cubital fossa does the median cubital vein actually lie?
opciones: In the roof, superficial to the tendon sheet that reinforces it
In the floor, deep to the brachialis and supinator muscles below
Beside the brachial artery, between the two heads of pronator teres
Under the biceps tendon, which shields it from the skin above it
preguntas.explicacion: The roof of the fossa is skin and fascia reinforced by the bicipital aponeurosis, and the median cubital vein runs within that roof, which is why it can be reached with a short needle. preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for PT and aPTT arrives filled to about two-thirds of its nominal volume. Applying the acceptance criteria of the emergency laboratory, what is done?
opciones: It is rejected: under-filled citrate tubes below 80 % of target volume fail acceptance because the blood-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong
It is accepted for both tests, because prothrombin time remains reliable at 67 % fill and aPTT is only slightly affected
It is accepted for the prothrombin time only, and the aPTT is cancelled with a note asking for a properly filled tube
It is topped up with blood from the lavender tube of the same patient to restore the nominal volume before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Insufficient volume gives an inadequate blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, and in citrate tubes that lengthens PT, aPTT and thrombin time and lowers fibrinogen; a clinically significant bias appears below 89 % of fill for aPTT and 78 % for fibrinogen, so the laboratory rejects any citrate tube under 80 % of target. Prothrombin time alone stays fairly reliable down to 67 %, but that does not rescue a tube ordered for both tests, and blood is never moved between tubes.

Typed, countersigned, numbered, indexed and filed by the medical record service

Yes, because any positive drug result may later be used in a criminal case
Yes, because immunoassay screens always require confirmation before reporting
Not unless the patient asks for the result to be released to a third party

Everyone aged 18 to 64, regardless of any risk factor they report
Only patients who report a risk factor when they are asked about it
Only patients who ask for the test after receiving pretest counseling

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting morning blood work says she had only black coffee and water since dinner 13 hours ago. Is the fasting acceptable?
opciones: No; water is allowed during the fast, but coffee is not permitted that morning
Yes; black coffee has no calories, and 13 hours exceeds the 12-hour minimum fast
No; the fast must be at least 24 hours, the same interval set for alcohol
Yes, provided she also avoided physical activity for the previous 24 hours

Proceed; five hours is enough because the glucose load resets the baseline
Proceed, but skip the fasting sample and draw only at 2 hours
Proceed with a 100-g load instead, to compensate for the meal

The fasting sample cannot be skipped because the 2-hour value is read against it, and the load for a nonpregnant adult stays at 75 g regardless of what was eaten.

The heel: finger punctures in children under 2 years carry the nerve damage the WHO describes
An ear lobe: the WHO reserves finger-pricks for adults and heel-pricks for neonates and infants

The first is about breathing and the second is about swallowing
The first is about swallowing and the second is about breathing

preguntas.pregunta: Both arteries and veins have three tunics. Which tunic is normally the thickest in an artery, and which in a vein?
opciones: Tunica media in arteries; tunica externa in veins
Tunica externa in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica intima in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica media in both, since both carry blood under pressure
preguntas.explicacion: The layers from inside out are tunica intima, tunica media and tunica externa. The media, rich in smooth muscle and elastic fibers, is normally the thickest layer in arteries, while in veins the media is thinner than the externa, which is the thickest layer there. Veins have less smooth muscle and connective tissue overall, which is why their walls are thinner than those of arteries.

Eosinophil
Neutrophil
Monocyte

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a natural absorbable suture such as catgut provoke more reaction than a synthetic one?
opciones: It breaks down by proteolysis, which inflames more than the hydrolysis of a synthetic
It breaks down by hydrolysis, which inflames more than the proteolysis of a synthetic
It is always braided, and braiding is what raises capillarity and the risk of infection
It is treated with chromium trioxide, and that treatment is itself the irritant in the tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Natural sutures come from purified animal tissue, usually collagen; silk and catgut, made from sheep submucosa, are examples. Absorbable natural material degrades by proteolysis while synthetics degrade by hydrolysis, and hydrolysis provokes the milder reaction. Chromium trioxide is what turns plain catgut into chromic, strengthening it so it lasts longer before absorption.

When the principal is admitted to a hospital for more than one night
When the agent moves out of the state where the document was signed
When the principal signs any later document naming a different agent

preguntas.pregunta: How long does the vascular spasm that follows a vessel injury usually last, and what triggers it?
opciones: Up to 30 minutes, at times hours; triggered by endothelins
A matter of seconds, the time the extrinsic pathway needs
A few minutes, the time the intrinsic pathway needs
About 3 hours, until bradykinin dilates the vessel again

opciones: A falsely elevated hemoglobin, and with it a falsely high MCHC
A falsely low hemoglobin, as is seen with marked hyperbilirubinemia
A falsely high MCV, as is seen with cold red cell agglutination
A falsely low platelet count, as is seen with EDTA-dependent clumping

Writing down only the first letter of each spoken word

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a copy of her lab results. Under HIPAA, how long does the covered entity have to act on the request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receipt, with one possible 30-day extension explained in writing
No later than 60 days after receipt, the same limit as breach notification
No later than 15 days after receipt, the same limit as the OSHA written opinion after exposure
No later than 10 working days, with unlimited extensions if the record is large or on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.524(b)(2) requires action on an access request no later than 30 days after receipt, either granting access or giving a written denial; if the entity cannot act in time it may take one extension of no more than 30 days, provided it tells the individual in writing, within the original period, the reason and the date it will finish. The entity may require requests in writing if it says so. Sixty days is the breach notification limit and 15 days the OSHA written opinion; neither governs access.

preguntas.pregunta: A mobile phlebotomy team works at several sites during one shift. Where may the safety data sheets for its chemicals be kept?

Only in the vehicle, where a paper copy has to travel with the team
At the site being visited, with a copy left behind after each visit
In the state office, which sends the sheet within one working day
preguntas.explicacion: The general rule is that the employer keeps the sheets in the workplace and makes them readily accessible during each work shift while employees are in their work areas; electronic access is fine as long as it puts no barrier in the way. For employees whose work takes them to more than one geographical location during a shift, the sheets may stay at the primary workplace, on the condition that the worker can immediately obtain the information in an emergency.

preguntas.pregunta: An 82-year-old with a urinary infection has a temperature of 37.2 °C (99 °F). Why is that value not reassuring?
opciones: Thermoregulation blunts with age, so a serious infection may raise the value only slightly
Older adults run a higher baseline, so 37.2 °C means the temperature has actually dropped
Urinary infections are the one group of infections that never raise body temperature
The reading is only reassuring once a second value taken an hour later agrees with it
preguntas.explicacion: Baseline core temperature tends to fall with age and the response to infection is blunted, so an older adult may never mount a high fever even when seriously ill. A modest rise above that person's own baseline can be clinically important, which is why the other vital signs and the clinical picture are weighed alongside it.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that laboratory results be mailed to a post office box instead of her home, and never left on the home voicemail. How must the practice respond?
opciones: It must let her ask for an alternative means or location for these communications
It must refuse, because the address of record is the only lawful place to send them
It must obtain a written authorization from her before using any other address at all
It must ask her to explain why the usual address would put her in any kind of danger
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers must permit individuals to request that communications reach them by another means or at another location than the entity normally uses, such as a chosen address or phone number, or a sealed envelope instead of a postcard. A provider may condition compliance on being given a workable alternative and on knowing how payment will be handled. Only health plans face the endangerment test.

preguntas.pregunta: A survey of clinical biochemists asked which quality practices their laboratories actually had in place. Which of these was the weakest area?
opciones: A written critical limits list, held by just over half of them
An electronic handbook, held by just over half of them
Advice on interpreting results, offered by just over half of them
Turnaround time discussions with clinicians, held by half of them
preguntas.explicacion: Among 335 respondents, 84 % had an electronic handbook, 80 % gave help interpreting laboratory data and 75 % discussed turnaround times with clinical staff, but only 58 % kept a written list of critical limits. preguntas.pregunta: How much of the percutaneous injury burden can safety-engineered devices avoid, and what undoes that gain?
opciones: Up to seventy-five per cent; disassembly, recapping, or not activating the feature
Up to twenty-five per cent; disassembly, recapping, or not activating the feature
Up to seventy-five per cent; using them on paediatric rather than adult patients
Up to ninety-nine per cent; storing them in a tray rather than in the packaging
preguntas.explicacion: Replacing conventional devices with engineered ones can avoid as much as seventy-five per cent of percutaneous injuries. The gain is lost when the device is taken apart, when the needle is recapped by hand, or when the safety feature is simply never activated, and exposure to blood then follows.

preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation test (prothrombin time) is ordered. Which tube does it require, and what is the additive?
opciones: A light blue top tube with sodium citrate, always filled completely
A purple top tube with EDTA, which also removes calcium, filled completely
A red top clot activator tube, spun so the serum can be tested
A light grey fluoride/oxalate tube, which also requires a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table lists the light blue coagulation tube for tests such as protime and prothrombin time. Its additive is sodium citrate, which binds calcium as calcium salts and so keeps the blood from clotting, and the table marks it as one of the tubes that needs a full draw. EDTA works the same way on calcium, but the table assigns it to haematology and cross-match, not coagulation; the red top carries a clot activator and gives serum, which a clotting test cannot use; and the grey fluoride/oxalate tube, which also needs a full draw, is the glucose tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a routine urinalysis for a patient coming in tomorrow. Which specimen should the medical assistant ask the patient to bring, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because urine that collected overnight is more concentrated
A random specimen collected two hours after breakfast, because food raises the analyte levels
A 24-hour collection, because a single void cannot be dipped reliably for protein or glucose
A specimen collected after drinking a liter of water, because dilute urine is easier to read
preguntas.explicacion: First-void or morning urine is considered the best specimen for routine testing: the urine that accumulates in the bladder overnight is more concentrated, which reflects the kidneys' ability to concentrate and lets the strip detect trace substances that a dilute sample would miss. Random, postprandial and 24-hour collections exist, but each is ordered for a specific purpose, not for the routine dipstick.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure

preguntas.pregunta: The deaf patient's 11-year-old daughter offers to interpret the pre-draw questions. Under the ADA guidance?
opciones: Not permitted; a minor may interpret only in an imminent-threat emergency
Permitted, provided the patient requests it and the child agrees to help out
Permitted, because the pre-draw questions are short and simple
Permitted, as long as a staff member witnesses the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Using people's children as interpreters has proved particularly problematic. The ADA's two exceptions differ by age: in an emergency involving an imminent threat, an adult or a minor child may be relied on when no qualified interpreter is available; outside an emergency, only an accompanying adult may, and only when the patient asks, the adult agrees and it is appropriate.

preguntas.pregunta: Which costs are included in the term cost sharing?
opciones: Deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for the services a plan covers
Premiums, deductibles and the charges for services a plan does not cover
Premiums and any amount a non-network provider bills above the allowed rate
Only the copayment collected at the desk on the day of the covered service
preguntas.explicacion: Cost sharing is the part of covered costs the patient pays personally, and the glossary names deductibles, coinsurance and copayments as the examples. It leaves out premiums, amounts balance billed by providers outside the network, and services the plan does not cover. Medicaid and CHIP are the exception where premiums are counted as cost sharing. The copayment alone is only one piece of it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which other bedside findings are read alongside a peripheral pulse to judge how well the blood is circulating?
opciones: The color and the temperature of the skin, and capillary refill
The strength of the grip, the turgor of the skin and breath sounds
The oral temperature, the pain score and the pattern of breathing
The last recorded weight, the fluid intake and the urine output
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse is one strand of the circulatory picture. It is read next to the color and temperature of the skin and to capillary refill, which together help tell a local vessel problem from a systemic one such as shock. Read on its own, a single pulse finding says little; read with those signs and the clinical context, it says a great deal.

opciones: Slower flashback, more friction, and harder threading of the line
Faster flashback, less friction, and a lower price for each device

preguntas.pregunta: A chart note lists tonsillitis as the reason for the visit. What does the ending of that term tell you?
opciones: That the structure named by the root is inflamed
That the structure named by the root has been removed
That the structure named by the root has been cut into
That the structure named by the root is drooping down
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -itis means inflammation, so tonsillitis is inflamed tonsils. The endings that get mixed up with it point elsewhere: -ectomy is cutting a part out, -otomy is an incision, and -ptosis is a falling or drooping. Reading the ending first tells you what is happening to whatever the root names.

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency patient is typed AB positive. Which blood types could he theoretically receive, and why?
opciones: Any type, since his plasma carries neither anti-A nor anti-B
Only AB+, since both antigens must match the donor exactly
Only O−, since that is the type of the universal donor
Any Rh− type, since Rh+ cells would sensitize the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The AB positive patient is the universal recipient: with both A and B antigens on his own cells he makes neither anti-A nor anti-B, and as an Rh positive person he can take Rh positive or Rh negative blood. Matched blood is still preferred, because the donor's plasma brings its own antibodies. An Rh positive recipient is not sensitized by Rh positive cells; that risk belongs to Rh negative people.

preguntas.pregunta: Which single fault explains both an unreliable clotting result and the loss of the specimen that produced it?
opciones: A clot in the tube, which uses up the very factors being measured
A tube filled to its line, which leaves the anticoagulant in excess
A tube inverted six times, which shears the fibrin strands apart
A tube kept at room temperature, which activates factor VII early
preguntas.explicacion: When a specimen clots, the clotting factors are consumed inside the tube and whatever the analyser then measures cannot be trusted. Clots follow a traumatic puncture, activation inside the device or poor mixing. Room temperature is the correct storage; it is refrigeration that activates factor VII.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors

Repeat the last sentence twice before beginning the new question
Write out the whole of the new question before speaking any of it
Wait until the patient asks what is going to be discussed next

preguntas.pregunta: What has to be entered on the chain of custody form every time the charge of a specimen changes hands?
opciones: A signature, the date and the time of the transfer
A signature and the reason the transfer was needed
The initials of a witness and the storage temperature
A photograph of the seal and the receiving room number
preguntas.explicacion: Each change of charge requires an entry of signature, date and time, so the paper trail shows who held the specimen at any given moment and can call that person to testify. All social workers, whether their practice is clinical or non-clinical work

Cycles of five back blows and then five chest thrusts, until the object is out

preguntas.pregunta: A patient collected a clean-catch specimen at home at 7 a.m. and cannot bring it to the office until noon. What should she have been told to do with it?

Leave the cup capped on the kitchen counter at room temperature, since refrigeration would alter the cells
Keep the cup in an inside coat pocket so the specimen stays at body temperature during transport
Freeze the specimen at home and let the office thaw it later, since freezing preserves it better than cold
preguntas.explicacion: After collecting, the patient closes the lid tightly without touching the inside of the cup or lid; when the sample is collected at home it goes into a plastic bag in the refrigerator until it can be delivered. Room temperature lets bacteria multiply, freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration in urine preservation, and body-temperature transport in a coat pocket is the instruction for a semen sample, not urine.

Sitting for 15 minutes before the draw
Drinking plain water during the fast
Having the draw done in the morning

preguntas.pregunta: What is patient abandonment?
opciones: Ending the relationship one-sidedly without notice enough to find other care
Ending the relationship after the patient has missed several appointments
Refusing to treat a person who has never been seen at the practice before
Transferring a patient to a specialist without telling the primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment is a breach of duty: the clinician terminates the relationship one-sidedly and without giving the patient adequate notice to arrange substitute medical care. It presupposes that a clinician-patient relationship existed, which starts when the clinician acts on the patient's diagnosis or treatment, or agrees to. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is unsure how urgent her symptom is. Which role does her primary care provider fill?

Deciding which services the health plan will agree to pay for that month
Arranging the hospital admission and writing the discharge summary later
Confirming that the specialist she has picked belongs to the plan network
preguntas.explicacion: The primary care provider is the patient's main provider in non-emergency situations. The role is to give preventive care and teach healthy lifestyle choices, identify and treat common medical conditions, judge how urgent a problem is and direct the patient to the best place for that care, and make referrals to medical or surgical specialists when they are needed.

preguntas.pregunta: What sample does a fingerstick PT/INR meter use?
opciones: A drop of capillary whole blood placed directly on the test strip
Citrated plasma separated from a light-blue-top tube by centrifugation
Serum from a clotted red-top tube after the clot has been removed
Anticoagulated whole blood transferred from a lavender-top tube
preguntas.explicacion: With a fingertip method, in the office or at home, a small needle punctures the finger, a drop of blood is placed on a test strip or special instrument, and the strip goes into a small device that calculates the result. Laboratory coagulation tests, by contrast, are run on citrated plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are consumed when serum forms. Patients on long-term warfarin may be trained to self-test this way.

The provider her plan assigned for a service she has not yet received
The pharmacy her plan asked her to use for a drug it already covers
The appointment time the office offered her for a covered procedure

preguntas.pregunta: At what age does colorectal cancer screening now begin for a patient at average risk?
opciones: 45 years, brought down because early-onset disease has been rising
50 years, the age used before the incidence in younger adults changed
40 years, the age below which the incidence has always been lowest
55 years, the age at which the incidence starts climbing most steeply
preguntas.explicacion: Screening for average-risk adults now starts at 45. The change followed data showing the incidence climbing in adults under 50 at about 2% a year, and it also addresses the higher incidence and mortality among Black patients under 50. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the skin spread taut before an intradermal injection, and which site is used for a tuberculosis test?
opciones: Taut skin eases entry and matters in older adults; the forearm is used at all ages
Taut skin eases entry and matters in older adults; the scapular area at all ages
Taut skin slows absorption in older adults; the outer upper arm is used at all ages
Taut skin raises the wheal in older adults; the anterior thigh is used at all ages
preguntas.explicacion: The non-dominant hand spreads the skin taut so the needle enters easily, and that matters particularly in older adults, whose skin has lost elasticity and whose medication would otherwise not be placed correctly. The forearm is the recommended site for tuberculosis testing at every age; the area between the scapulae is where allergy testing may be done, and the outer upper arms are the third intradermal site.

preguntas.pregunta: Which information does NIOSH say to collect when reporting a needlestick?

The source patient's diagnosis and insurance, and the worker's vaccination card
The lot number of the gloves worn and the brand of disinfectant on the counter
The names of all patients drawn that shift and the time each was seen
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH lists what to gather: the date and time of the exposure, the procedure or action being performed, specific details such as profession, department or unit, shift and whether the injured person was the device user, and the specific type of device with brand and model when known. These details feed the sharps injury log, which records the device type and brand, the work area and how the incident occurred, including depth of injury and whether a safety feature was activated. preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the practice not to share his information with a particular specialist. What does the Privacy Rule require of the practice?
opciones: Only to consider it, since a covered entity is under no obligation to agree to a restriction
It must agree, because a restriction request binds the covered entity once it is written down
It must agree unless the specialist is inside the same organized health care arrangement
It must agree for one year, after which the restriction lapses unless the patient renews it
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals may ask a covered entity to restrict the use or disclosure of their information for treatment, payment or operations, or to people involved in their care. The entity is under no obligation to agree. What it cannot do is agree and then ignore the restriction: once accepted, it binds, with an exception for treating the individual in a medical emergency.

preguntas.pregunta: An eye drop has just been instilled. What is the patient told to do next?
opciones: Close the eye two to three minutes and tip the head down, without blinking hard
Blink several times quickly so that the drop spreads over the surface of the eye
Close the eye ten to fifteen minutes, the time an emergency eye flush station runs
Keep the eye open and look up for five minutes, as is done after an ear instillation
preguntas.explicacion: The lower lid is pulled down to form a pocket, and the drop is released into it with the dropper held close but touching nothing. The eye then stays closed for two to three minutes with the head tipped down as if looking at the floor, without blinking or squeezing; gentle pressure over the tear duct helps, and any excess is wiped away. The fifteen minutes belong to an eye flush and the five minutes to ear drops.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient bleeds about 5 mL onto a countertop. Which hypochlorite dilution does the guideline give for decontaminating that surface?
opciones: 1:100, which delivers roughly 525 to 615 ppm of available chlorine
1:10, which delivers roughly 5,250 to 6,150 ppm of available chlorine
1:50, which delivers roughly 1,000 ppm of available chlorine at day zero
1:5, which delivers the concentration used against Clostridioides difficile spores
preguntas.explicacion: For a small spill of blood or other potentially infectious material, under about 10 mL, a 1:100 dilution of 5.25 to 6.15 percent sodium hypochlorite is used on the nonporous surface, which works out to 525 to 615 ppm of available chlorine. The stronger 1:10 dilution is reserved for large spills and for units with high rates of C. difficile.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the thermal recording paper stored?
opciones: Cool, dry and dark, below 80 °F and 40 to 65% humidity
Cool, dry and dark, below 60 °F and 20 to 30% humidity
Warm, dry and dark, below 80 °F and 40 to 65% humidity
Cool, dry and lit, below 80 °F and 40 to 65% humidity
preguntas.explicacion: The paper is kept in a cool, dry, dark place, under 27.6 °C or 80 °F, with relative humidity between 40 and 65 percent. Bright light and ultraviolet sources such as sunlight or fluorescent lamps yellow the paper and fade the tracings, and cleaning solvents must not touch it.

Fee-for-service reimbursement, which pays for each service furnished
Capitated payment, which pays a fixed amount for each patient served
Value-based purchasing, which links payment to measurable outcomes

Switch to heparin plasma tubes, which contain no clot activator and so cannot form any fibrin at all
Switch to serum separator tubes with gel, which trap the fibrin below the barrier during centrifugation
Switch to citrate tubes filled completely, which keep the fibrinogen in solution until testing
preguntas.explicacion: To prevent fibrin formation the laboratory planned to use rapid serum tubes, described as tubes that accelerate coagulation, reduce processing time and increase serum quality, a fit for emergency departments and intensive care units. Contact the patient's next of kin to obtain an advance directive on her behalf

preguntas.pregunta: Two weeks after a batch of claims went out, nothing has come back from the payer. What does the guidance on tracking submitted claims advise?

Wait for the remittance advice, which every payer owes within thirty days
Send the whole batch again on paper so the payer cannot say it never arrived
Write the balances off and bill the patients once ninety days have gone by
preguntas.explicacion: Among the remedies for slow payment are gathering demographic data accurately, billing accurately, cross-checking entries before submission, confirming that the claims sent were actually received and processed, and setting reminders to follow up on every claim within twenty-one days of submission. About one inch away from the field
About eighteen inches away from the field
Directly against the surface of the field

Without unreasonable delay and within thirty days, by telephone call to each patient
Within sixty days of the end of the calendar year, in a single written summary
Within ten working days, by a notice posted at the front desk of the practice

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis must be taken to radiology. What does the CDC say about the escort's respiratory protection during transport?
opciones: No respirator is needed in transport if the patient wears a mask and infectious lesions are covered
A fit-tested N95 is always required for the escort, whether or not the patient is masked
A surgical mask on the escort is sufficient, because the patient is out of the isolation room
Transport is prohibited; imaging must be done inside the airborne infection isolation room
preguntas.explicacion: Inside the room, Airborne Precautions require a fit-tested, NIOSH-approved N95 or higher respirator for personnel. For transport, which the CDC limits to medically necessary purposes, the patient wears a surgical mask if possible and observes cough etiquette, and the CDC states that staff transporting such a patient do not need a mask or respirator during the move when the patient is masked and any infectious skin lesions are covered. preguntas.pregunta: Who is generally eligible for Medicare?

People 65 or older, and younger people whose income falls below the poverty level
People 65 or older who worked at least 10 years, and no one under that age
People of any age enrolled in a state program that pays their hospital costs

Identity, the expected results, and the reference ranges for each test ordered
Identity, the tube colours needed, and the order of draw that will be followed
Identity, the diagnosis code, and the physician's working differential diagnosis

preguntas.pregunta: A patient cannot produce a semen sample by masturbation and asks about collecting it during intercourse. What must he be told?
opciones: A nontoxic collection condom supplied by the provider is used; ordinary latex condoms are not acceptable
An ordinary latex condom is acceptable as long as it is rinsed with sterile saline before it is used
Collection during intercourse is never acceptable, because the first fraction is always lost that way
A nontoxic collection condom is used, and the specimen is then frozen until it reaches the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: When masturbation into a clean, wide-mouthed container is not possible, semen may be collected in a special condom given by the provider. preguntas.pregunta: How should staff treat what they know about a patient's cultural group?

As the plan, since group practice predicts the person
As a script, applied the same way to every member
As a warning, since some beliefs will delay the care

preguntas.pregunta: A processor holds a separated serum tube up to the light and records it as clear. Below roughly what free haemoglobin concentration will hemolysis escape the naked eye?
opciones: About 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, below which separated serum still looks normal
About 0.5 to 0.6 g/L, the level taken as significant interference at the bench
About 1.0 to 1.5 g/L, the level at which potassium begins to climb
About 0.05 to 0.1 g/L, roughly the detection limit of the analyser
preguntas.explicacion: Once the serum has been separated, hemolysis becomes visible at a free haemoglobin of about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the concentration accepted as clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. opciones: Updated evidence suggests it may not be needed for every patient
It stands as a firm requirement of 150 g daily for three days
It was replaced by a 24-hour fast in place of the eight-hour one
It applies now only to patients who are already taking insulin

Only when the manufacturer's insert makes external controls mandatory for that kit
Each day patient samples are tested, with two levels of control, as for all waived tests

A copy filed with the risk management office that day

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between an antiseptic and a disinfectant?
opciones: Antiseptics are applied to living tissue and skin, disinfectants only to inanimate objects
Antiseptics kill bacterial spores outright, disinfectants leave those spores alive behind
Antiseptics are the germicides meant for surfaces, disinfectants the ones cleared for skin
Antiseptics lift the visible soil first, disinfectants act only once that soil is gone
preguntas.explicacion: Both are germicides; what splits them is where they go. Antiseptics are used on skin and living tissue, disinfectants on inanimate objects only, and the two are not swapped: disinfectants can injure skin and tissue. Killing spores is what marks a chemical sterilant, and lifting visible soil is cleaning, which is a different step altogether.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking metformin alone asks whether the tablets can drop the blood sugar too low. What is correct?
opciones: They do not, because metformin does not make the pancreas secrete extra insulin
They do, because metformin shuts the potassium channels of the pancreatic beta cells
They do, because metformin drives glucose and potassium into the cells like insulin
They do, but only once the daily dose passes 2000 mg taken in divided doses
preguntas.explicacion: Metformin works on the liver and the muscle: it activates hepatic AMP-activated protein kinase, damps gluconeogenesis and lipogenesis, and improves the uptake of glucose driven by insulin. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being taught to monitor blood pressure at home. Which instruction is given?
opciones: Take at least two readings 1 or 2 minutes apart, at the same time each day
Take one reading a day, at the hour the patient happens to be free that day
Take at least two readings 10 minutes apart, at a different hour each day
Take a reading only on days the patient feels unwell, and log those values
preguntas.explicacion: Self-measured monitoring works best with a routine: the same hour every day, at least two readings a minute or two apart, and every value written in a log. One common plan is a reading before breakfast and before dinner for five days, which gives the provider at least ten values to work from.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Measuring Your Blood Pressure: How to measure your blood pressure at home
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B14 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.21

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia signed a consent form last month. What does that tell the team about today's decision?
opciones: Nothing by itself; capacity is judged for the decision at hand, on the day
It stands until a court holds a hearing and rules the patient incapacitated
It stands as long as the same clinician is the one obtaining consent today
It stands, because a dementia diagnosis makes the finding permanent anyway
preguntas.explicacion: A capacity assessment is valid only for the time, place and situation in which it was made: it is a snapshot, not a status. The same patient may be lucid and deciding well one day and disoriented two weeks later, and an intoxicated patient may decide soundly once sober. The court hearing settles competence, which is the separate legal question.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Clinical Significance: When To Assess Capacity
preguntas.subtema: Capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A problem list records a TIA two years before the CVA the patient was admitted with. What separates those two entries?
opciones: A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is the stroke itself
A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is a clot in a deep vein
A TIA is a heart attack, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
A TIA is a brief seizure, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
preguntas.explicacion: TIA stands for transient ischemic attack, listed as a small stroke, while CVA is a cerebrovascular accident, the stroke or brain attack itself. The abbreviations that get swapped in belong to other organs: AMI and MI are the heart attack, and DVT is the clot in a deep vein.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's blood pressure is recorded as 120/80. What does each number represent?
opciones: 120 is systolic, during ventricular contraction; 80 is diastolic, during relaxation
120 is diastolic, during ventricular relaxation; 80 is systolic, during contraction
120 is the pulse pressure in the aorta; 80 is the mean arterial pressure in the arteries
120 is the pressure inside the aorta; 80 is the pressure inside the venae cavae
preguntas.explicacion: A blood pressure of 120/80 is a normal adult value written as systolic over diastolic: the higher number, around 120 mm Hg, is the arterial pressure produced by ventricular contraction, and the lower, about 80 mm Hg, is the pressure during ventricular relaxation. Pulse pressure is their difference (40 mm Hg here) and mean arterial pressure is a separate calculated value.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Systolic and Diastolic Pressures; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of Circulation, Pulse and Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A caregiver reports a child's temperature as 38 °C. Which Fahrenheit value is recorded, and what does it mean by the rectal route?
opciones: 100.4 °F, which is exactly the rectal threshold for fever in a child
101.4 °F, which is above the rectal threshold for fever in a child
99.5 °F, which is the oral rather than the rectal threshold in a child
98.6 °F, which is the average adult value and not a fever at any site
preguntas.explicacion: The two scales are recorded as a pair in clinical sources: 38 °C is 100.4 °F, and that is the exact point at which a rectal reading counts as fever in a child. The oral threshold is 99.5 °F (37.5 °C) and the average adult value is 98.6 °F (37 °C), which is why the route is always written beside the number.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A5 k56 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: How does the action of the endocrine system differ from that of the nervous system?
opciones: It is slower and more generalized, working through hormones in the blood
It is faster and more localized, working through hormones in the blood
It is slower and more localized, working through impulses along nerves
It is faster and more generalized, working through impulses along nerves
preguntas.explicacion: Both systems regulate the body, but on different clocks. The nervous system uses electrical impulses and neurotransmitters, and its effects are local and last seconds. The endocrine system uses hormones carried in the blood, and its effects are measured in minutes, hours or weeks and reach far more of the body at once.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Endocrine System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(9) (2027 I.C.6.f(9)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which tube in the WHO order of draw is filled immediately before the purple EDTA tube when a full set is collected?
opciones: The light green PST with lithium heparin and gel
The dark green sodium heparin tube
The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The red-grey tiger top or gold serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA is position 8 in Table 2.3, and position 7 is the light green plasma separator tube with lithium heparin and a gel separator. The dark green sodium heparin tube is position 6, the serum separator tube position 5, and the pale yellow ACD tube comes after EDTA at position 9. Reading the table by neighbours is the surest way to reconstruct the whole sequence.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: Blood from a syringe has to go into a sample tube that has no rubber stopper. How is it transferred?
opciones: Injected extremely slowly, keeping pressure and speed to a minimum
Injected as briskly as possible so the tube fills before it can clot
Poured down the inner wall of the tube after the needle is removed
Injected only after the needle has been recapped for the transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Where there is no rubber stopper to pierce, the blood is injected extremely slowly, because keeping the pressure and the velocity of the transfer low is what limits haemolysis. The instruction that closes that step is not to recap and remove the needle afterwards.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7

preguntas.pregunta: After a blood culture bottle is filled, how many times should it be mixed?
opciones: 8 to 10 times
3 to 6 times
1 or 2 times
15 to 20 times
preguntas.explicacion: A culture bottle is mixed 8 to 10 times after the blood is added so that the contents combine properly. The 3 to 6 inversions belong to the light blue citrate tube in the coagulopathies review, done immediately after the draw. One or two turns is the kind of under-mixing the review links to small clots, and 15 to 20 is not a figure given for any tube.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Yellow, Pink, and Blue

preguntas.pregunta: Which team member manages oxygen therapy, draws arterial blood gases and runs mechanical ventilators?
opciones: The respiratory therapist, who also gives inhalers and nebulizer medicines
The physical therapist, who also teaches patients to use walkers and canes safely
The occupational therapist, who also assesses the home for safety needs
The clinical laboratory technologist, who also performs blood bank testing
preguntas.explicacion: Respiratory therapists treat respiratory conditions: managing oxygen therapy, drawing arterial blood gases, running mechanical ventilators and CPAP or BiPAP machines, giving inhalers and nebulizer medicines, intubating, assisting with bronchoscopy, performing chest physiotherapy, and taking a central part during cardiac and respiratory arrests.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Interprofessional Team Members (Respiratory Therapists)
