preguntas.pregunta: A referral is addressed to a nephrologist. Which organ does the root of that specialty name?
opciones: The kidney, which is also named by the root ren-
The liver, which is also named by the root hepat-
The bladder, which is also named by the root cyst-
The stomach, which is also named by the root gastr-
preguntas.explicacion: Nephr- and ren- both name the kidney, which is why the same organ gives us nephrology and renal failure. The other roots belong to their own organs: hepat- the liver, cyst- a bladder or sac, gastr- the stomach. Two roots for one organ is common in this vocabulary, one from Greek and one from Latin.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders

preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches a passive communicator?
opciones: One who puts the rights of others first and sounds tentative or apologetic
One who defends their own rights even at the cost of the rights of others
One who respects the rights of others while standing up for their own ideas
One who assumes the message was understood without ever verifying it
preguntas.explicacion: Three styles are described. The passive communicator places everyone else's rights above their own, sounds apologetic or unsure, and stays quiet even when wronged. Defending your own rights at the expense of others is the aggressive style, and balancing both is the assertive one. Assuming understanding without checking describes passive listening, not the passive style.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Communication styles · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a history of a vagal attack during earlier draws sought out before the needle comes out?
opciones: So the team is ready with the means to act should a faint happen
So the draw can be logged as high risk and handed to a nurse
So the tourniquet time can be cut to under thirty seconds
So the patient can be given a sugary drink to break the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Specific attention is to be paid to identifying patients who are afraid of blood testing or who have a positive history of a vasovagal attack during earlier similar procedures, so that every means of acting on a vagal syncope is prepared beforehand. Simple steps such as counting down may greatly reduce anxiety, and a severe history of panic attacks may call for lying down.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D II.I · CCMA 3E1 k126 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: The office accepts assignment for a Medicare patient. What does that oblige it to do about her bill?
opciones: Charge her only the deductible and coinsurance, and file the claim at no charge
Collect the whole charge at the visit and let her seek reimbursement afterwards
Charge up to fifteen percent above the approved amount for each service given
Decide service by service whether the approved amount will be accepted as payment
preguntas.explicacion: Accepting assignment means taking the Medicare-approved amount as payment in full, and it applies to every Part A and Part B service the provider gives. Such a provider agrees to charge only the deductible and coinsurance, usually waits for Medicare to pay its share first, and must send the claim to Medicare without charging the patient for doing so.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: The chemistry analyzer goes down and a stat troponin ordered from the emergency department will not be reported within the laboratory's established time frame. What does CLIA require?
opciones: The laboratory decides, based on the urgency of the test, whether to notify the appropriate person of the delay
The laboratory must notify the ordering person of every delayed result, regardless of the urgency of the test
The laboratory must refer the specimen to another CLIA-certified laboratory within 30 minutes of the failure
The laboratory may wait until the analyzer is repaired, since delays are addressed only by its accreditor
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(h) says that when the laboratory cannot report patient results within its established time frames it must determine, based on the urgency of the tests requested, whether the appropriate individuals need to be told of the delay; a stat cardiac marker is the kind of request where that decision goes toward notification. The rule does not demand notice for every delay, sets no referral deadline, and does not allow the laboratory to stay silent.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(h), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5H · PBT VI.B VI.F · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which parts make up a syringe and its needle?
opciones: Plunger, barrel and needle hub; the needle has hub, shaft and bevel
Plunger, barrel and filter; the needle has hub, shaft and safety shield
Plunger, cylinder and stopper; the needle has hub, bevel and canister
Barrel, spacer and hub; the needle has shaft, bevel and rubber seal
preguntas.explicacion: A disposable syringe consists of a plunger, a barrel and a needle hub, and it comes in sizes from 0.5 mL to 60 mL. The needle itself is made of the hub that fits the syringe tip, the shaft and the bevel, the slanted tip that cuts into the skin, and all three parts stay sterile. A Luer lock syringe has threads in the hub so needles and tubing connect securely, and the barrel carries the readable scale.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Syringes and Needles
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.c

preguntas.pregunta: A scalp wound is bleeding and a skull fracture is suspected. How is the bleeding handled?
opciones: Cover it with sterile gauze without pressing down on the site
Press firmly with a clean cloth until the bleeding has stopped
Wash the wound out first and then press with a sterile dressing
Pull the debris out of the wound and then bandage it tightly
preguntas.explicacion: With a suspected skull fracture, direct pressure is not applied to the bleeding site and debris is not taken out; the wound is covered with sterile gauze. Otherwise bleeding is stopped by pressing a clean cloth firmly, and a soaked cloth gets another on top. A deep or heavily bleeding head wound is not washed.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Head injury - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.s · 2027 I.B.8.s · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a drug given by the rectal route is correct?
opciones: The mucosa is very vascular, and only about half the dose goes straight to the liver
The mucosa is poorly vascular, so it absorbs more slowly than any other enteral route
The whole dose enters the portal vein, so the first-pass effect is at its very greatest
The route counts as parenteral, since the drug never enters the digestive tract at all
preguntas.explicacion: Rectal administration is counted among the enteral routes. Its mucosa carries a rich blood supply, so absorption is rapid and effective, and the drug diffuses passively as it does under the tongue. Only about half of what the rectum absorbs travels directly to the liver, so first-pass metabolism is partly avoided. Parenteral means the injection routes, and an intravenous dose bypasses the liver's first pass entirely.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Enteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(8) · RMA III.G.4.d(ii)

preguntas.pregunta: For printed fasting instructions handed to older patients, what is the recommended minimum type size?
opciones: At least 14-point
At least 12-point
At least 10-point
At least 18-point
preguntas.explicacion: For visual deficits, printed materials should use type large enough, at least 14-point, in a typeface that is easy to read, with adequate lighting and minimal glare, and that patients have their glasses on. The same 14-point minimum is repeated for questionnaires that patients fill out, along with enough space between items.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for visual deficits

preguntas.pregunta: On palpation, a vein feels hard and cord-like from previous punctures. Which contraindication does this represent?
opciones: Venous fibrosis on palpation
A vascular graft in the arm
Cellulitis or abscess
Ipsilateral radical mastectomy
preguntas.explicacion: Venous fibrosis on palpation is one of the local contraindications, alongside previously attempted sites with residual scar tissue. A vascular graft, cellulitis or abscess and a history of radical mastectomy on the same side are separate entries in the same list, each with its own history or appearance rather than a fibrotic feel of the vein itself.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and palpation · CPT D3 k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: How often does the guideline call for biological monitoring of a steam sterilizer?
opciones: At least weekly, and in every load that contains implantable objects
At least monthly, and in every load that contains implantable objects
At least weekly, and in every load, including loads of routine reusable instruments
At least daily, and in the first load after any repair to the machine
preguntas.explicacion: Steam and low-temperature sterilizers are monitored at least weekly with the right commercial spore preparation, and every load holding implantable items gets its own biological indicator, with the items quarantined until the result is negative where that is feasible. Daily testing is an option in busy departments, because it finds a malfunction sooner and shrinks any recall.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations 16: Monitoring of Sterilizers
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA Essential 5

preguntas.pregunta: How is a specimen taken for a wound culture?
opciones: A special swab picks up cells or pus; for a deeper wound a syringe draws fluid or a biopsy is taken
A special swab picks up cells or pus; for a deeper wound the drainage is squeezed onto a glass slide
The wound is irrigated with sterile saline and the runoff is caught in a sterile container
A dry dressing is left on the wound overnight and then sent to the laboratory in a sealed bag
preguntas.explicacion: Wound cultures look for infection in open wounds or burns. A swab collects cells or pus from the surface, and when the wound is deeper a syringe is used to draw out fluid or a piece of tissue is biopsied. Most disease-causing bacteria are ready to read in one to two days, though some need five days or more. A skin or nail culture is collected with a swab or blade instead.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Bacteria Culture Test, Wound Culture; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Skin or nail culture (003762), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Wound culture collection · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(b) · NCMA 2B.20

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement best describes what a patient-centered medical home is?
opciones: A model for organizing primary care that delivers its core functions
A building where several specialties share one waiting room and one chart room
A group of providers whose payment is tied to quality goals and cost savings
A plan that pays a fixed amount per patient no matter what services follow
preguntas.explicacion: The medical home is understood not simply as a place but as a model for organizing primary care so that it delivers the core functions of primary health care. Five functions and attributes define it: comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and a commitment to quality and safety.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: A 'true' latex allergy is which type of reaction?
opciones: Type I, IgE-mediated, with symptoms within minutes of exposure
Type IV, delayed, caused by the chemical antioxidants added in processing
Irritant contact dermatitis from friction or chemical contact
Type IV, delayed, caused by inhaling the cornstarch powder on gloves
preguntas.explicacion: A true latex allergy is a type I hypersensitivity mediated by IgE antibodies bound to the rubber proteins; within minutes the patient may develop hives, wheezing, a runny nose and conjunctivitis, and systemic reactions up to anaphylaxis are possible. The processing chemicals cause a delayed type IV reaction, and irritant dermatitis is a non-immune reaction, neither of them a true allergy.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", sections Introduction, Pathophysiology and History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii

preguntas.pregunta: For which antiepileptic drugs is the trough level said to matter most?
opciones: Those with short half-lives, since the trough marks the between-dose minimum
Those with long half-lives, since the level then reflects long-term usage
Those given intravenously, since the peak arrives with the infusion
Those newly substituted between a brand and a generic preparation
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration at its lowest point, typically just before the next dose falls due, and that is called crucial for antiepileptic drugs with short half-lives, since the trough marks the minimum reached between doses. Phenytoin's long half-life is why its level reflects long-term usage, and monitoring can guide dosing when a substitution is unavoidable.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Other Issues, Trough Versus Free Levels; and section Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: After a routine draw, which used item does the WHO say may go into the general waste (unless local rules differ), and which must go into a puncture-resistant container?
opciones: Gloves that would not release a drop of blood if squeezed may go to general waste; the needle to the sharps container
The gauze pressed on the puncture site may go to general waste; the gloves go to the sharps container
The needle may go to general waste once its safety feature is activated; the gloves go to the sharps container instead
Every item from a blood draw, gloves included, goes to the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 discards the used needle and syringe or sampling device into a puncture-resistant sharps container, and places the other items in their waste category: items that would not release a drop of blood if squeezed, gloves being the example, may be discarded in the general waste unless local regulations say otherwise. An activated safety feature does not turn a needle into general waste.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9: Clean contaminated surfaces and complete patient procedure
preguntas.subtema: Sharps and waste disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: What are the three parts of the Whipple triad?
opciones: Symptoms of hypoglycemia, a low measured glucose, and relief when it is corrected
Symptoms of hyperglycemia, a high measured glucose, and ketones found in urine
Sweating, tremor and confusion appearing together in a patient with diabetes
A low glucose, a high insulin level and a tumor found inside the pancreas
preguntas.explicacion: The triad has been used to describe hypoglycemia since 1938: the clinician recognizes symptoms of hypoglycemia, obtains a low blood glucose measurement, and then sees those symptoms lift immediately once the low glucose is corrected. It is the reason a reading is taken and repeated rather than judging by symptoms alone.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypoglycemia", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.f · 2027 I.B.8.f · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Within what period must an accredited organization finish its analysis and action plan after a sentinel event?
opciones: Within 45 business days of recognizing the event
Within 30 business days of recognizing the event
Within 60 business days of recognizing the event
Within 10 business days of recognizing the event
preguntas.explicacion: Accredited organizations must keep a formal process for identifying sentinel events, running a timely and credible analysis, and putting in a documented risk-reduction and corrective action plan that measures whether the improvements worked. That process has to be complete within 45 business days of recognizing the event.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Incident reports and analysis · CCMA 6M k211 · CMAA 3 k44

preguntas.pregunta: A rectal temperature is being taken with a digital thermometer. What is the described technique?
opciones: A lubricated blunt tip is inserted about 4 to 5 cm at a 20-degree angle, patient prone
A lubricated blunt tip is inserted about 15 cm at a 45-degree angle, patient supine
A bare blunt tip is inserted about 2 to 3 cm at a right angle, patient on the left side
A lubricated blunt tip is inserted about 4 to 5 cm at a 60-degree angle, patient seated
preguntas.explicacion: The described method uses a lubricated blunt-tipped thermometer inserted roughly 4 to 5 cm into the anal canal at about 20 degrees from the horizontal, with the patient prone. The route is reserved for children and for patients who cannot cooperate, and it is the preferred route when hypothermia is suspected.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature b(iii) · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: How far should an isolation gown reach when it is put on correctly?
opciones: From the neck to the knees and to the wrists, wrapped at the back
From the shoulders to the hips, left open behind for ventilation
From the neck to the ankles, with the ties left loose at the neck
From the chest to the knees, over the uniform but under the badge
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the gown goes on first, outside the patient room, and it has to cover the body from neck to knees and the arms to the wrists, and wrap around the back, with the neck and waist ties fastened if the gown has them. Gloves go on last and are pulled over the cuff of the gown, so that no skin or sleeve is left showing between the two. A gown left open at the back is not covering what it was chosen to cover.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Putting on the gown · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks to add a test to a serum sample collected the previous day and kept refrigerated. What decides whether the laboratory can honour the add-on?
opciones: Whether the analyte is documented as stable for that storage time and temperature in that tube type
Whether the request reaches the laboratory within 30 days of the original oral order for the panel
Whether the original requisition already listed the panel to which the new test belongs
Whether the sample can be recentrifuged, since a second spin restores the quality of the serum
preguntas.explicacion: Add-on acceptability rests on stability data: studies such as the one that measured common biochemical analytes in serum separator tubes with and without gel under various storage conditions exist precisely to define the time and temperature within which a stored sample can be retested. The 30-day rule concerns written authorisation of oral orders, the original panel does not fix what may be added, and recentrifugation does not restore an analyte that has already changed.

Skip it, since addressable means the specification is offered to entities as an option
Adopt it anyway, since addressable and required specifications carry identical obligations
Ask OCR for a written waiver before the standard containing it can be treated as met
preguntas.explicacion: Every standard must be met, but the specifications inside them are labelled required or addressable. Addressable does not mean optional: the entity judges whether the specification is reasonable and appropriate for it, and must adopt it where it is. 2 cm proximal, tight enough to abolish the radial pulse for the duration of the draw
15 to 20 cm proximal, loose enough that the veins remain flat until the fist is made
5 to 10 cm distal, tight enough to engorge the veins without obstructing the arterial flow
preguntas.explicacion: For a peripheral line the tourniquet goes roughly 5 to 10 cm proximal to the intended site, tight enough to engorge the veins but not so tight that arterial flow is blocked, since engorgement is what makes the vein easy to identify and cannulate. Retiree coverage, employer group coverage and coverage bought on the Marketplace
Medigap policies, employer supplemental plans and the state Medicaid programs
Liability insurance including self-insurance, Medigap policies and the Marketplace
preguntas.explicacion: A non-group health plan means liability insurance, self-insured entities included, together with no-fault insurers and workers' compensation, and all such claims go to that insurer before they go to Medicare. With a reusable sharps container held open, so the pieces can be swept directly into it

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC describe an HIV exposure as a medical emergency?
opciones: Infection often takes hold within 24 to 36 hours, so PEP works best when begun within hours
Antibodies appear within 24 to 36 hours, so a rapid test must be done before any PEP
PEP is only effective if started before the source patient's viral load is known
The exposed worker becomes infectious to others within 24 to 36 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Infection with HIV takes hold fast, usually 24 to 36 hours after exposure, which is why patients are evaluated rapidly and the first dose is given immediately when rapid test results are unavailable and PEP is indicated. The older CDC brochure makes the same point: treatment should start preferably within hours rather than days, since animal studies suggest less benefit after 24 to 36 hours. Antibody appearance and infectiousness take much longer, which is why follow-up testing runs for months.

The stump is rinsed with sterile saline and wrapped in a bulky dressing
The patient is walked to a chair so the injured limb can be raised
The part is searched for, since reattachment depends on finding it early
preguntas.explicacion: The patient comes before the part: airway, breathing and circulation are checked, rescue breathing, CPR or bleeding control is started if needed, and help is called. Stand up quickly at the first warning sign, drink less fluid, keep the arm raised
Lie down after the test only, restrict salt intake, and avoid all morning draws
Sit upright through the warning signs, drink more fluid, and hold the breath in
preguntas.explicacion: Management of these episodes is conservative: avoid known triggers, take more fluid to improve filling, and change position slowly. Patients are taught the warning signs and told to get themselves supine when one starts, which often stops the faint and prevents a fall.

preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time drawn through an indwelling line comes back markedly prolonged although the patient takes no anticoagulant. What is the likely cause?

Contamination of the sample by the alcohol used to disinfect the skin surface
Excess citrate from a tube that was filled well beyond its stated volume line
Loss of citrate from a tube that was inverted more than six times after filling

Employees may substitute alcohol hand rub at any time, even when sinks are available
A sink is required only in HIV and HBV research laboratories and production facilities
Facilities must be foot- or elbow-operated and located near the exit door of every draw room

Using a mechanical device to remove a contaminated needle when a procedure requires it
Decontaminating utility gloves for reuse when the glove is still intact
Keeping a sharps container upright and replacing it before it overfills

A huddle, called during the session
A debrief, once the session is over
A handoff, as responsibility passes

preguntas.pregunta: Which dressing is occlusive, promotes autolytic debridement, and is avoided on an infected wound?
opciones: A hydrocolloid, usually changed every three to five days
An alginate, usually changed every twenty-four to forty-eight hours
A transparent film, usually left over wounds with no exudate at all
A dry sterile gauze, usually changed at least once every twenty-four hours
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrocolloids act as an occlusive barrier against contaminants, hold a moist environment and bring about autolytic debridement, and the thicker ones take up moderate drainage. Only the outside surface of the folded cuff, held with thumb and index finger
Only the fingertips of the glove, which stay clear of the patient's skin anyway
Only the palm of the glove, which will be covered once the hand slides inside

Pinpoint non-blanching spots smaller than 2 mm
Pooling of blood under the skin with swelling
Lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes a sentinel event from a preventable adverse event?
opciones: The sentinel event is defined by how severe the outcome is; the other is defined by being caused by an error
The preventable adverse event is defined by how severe the outcome is; the other one by being caused by an error
The sentinel event reaches the patient, while the preventable adverse event is stopped before it does
The sentinel event is reported to the state agency, while the preventable adverse event stays internal
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is the defining criterion, not the setting. A preventable adverse event is patient harm traced to an error or to a clinician's inaction, so causation defines it. A sentinel event is defined by outcome severity: death, severe harm or permanent harm reaching a patient. Wrong-site surgery is both; a medication error that causes temporary harm is only the first. An error stopped before it reaches the patient is a near miss.

It is a recognized relaxation technique that slows the heart

preguntas.pregunta: What does wearing two pairs of gloves do for a worker who suffers a sharps injury?

It stops the needle from reaching the skin when the gauge is small
It removes the need to wash hands once the outer pair comes off
It counts as an engineering control under the bloodborne standard

No dairy for 3 days, then a normal breakfast on the morning of the test

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is blood type A. Which antigen is on the red cells and which antibody circulates in the plasma?

A antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
B antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
Neither antigen; both anti-A and anti-B in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: ABO typing looks at two glycoprotein antigens, A and B. Type A cells carry the A antigen, and because people are exposed to A and B antigens in food and microbes early in life, a type A person has naturally formed anti-B antibodies. preguntas.pregunta: A preterm infant on oxygen has a moderately hemolysed serum sample with an LDH ordered for monitoring. What approach did the neonatal laboratory and the surveyed neonatologists favour?
opciones: Report the approximate LDH with a comment that moderate hemolysis affects it, rather than rejecting it outright
Reject the LDH and every other analyte on the sample, since LDH is the analyte most sensitive to hemolysis
Correct the LDH with a formula based on the hemolysis index and report the adjusted value without a comment

The lowest rate seen over 10 minutes, rounded down to the nearest 10 bpm
The highest rate seen over 10 minutes, rounded up to the nearest 10 bpm
preguntas.explicacion: The baseline is the average over a ten-minute window, and that average has to be present for at least two minutes of it, reported in steps of five beats per minute. preguntas.pregunta: What protection does a reporter's identity normally have?
opciones: It is shielded from the alleged perpetrator in most jurisdictions
It is shielded from the investigating agency until a case is opened
It is published with the report once the investigation has closed
It is shielded only when the report turns out to be substantiated
preguntas.explicacion: Every jurisdiction keeps abuse and neglect records confidential, and in 44 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories the reporter's identity is specifically protected from disclosure to the alleged perpetrator, even when other information from the report comes out. Some places release the name in narrow circumstances, such as a finding that the report was knowingly false.

preguntas.pregunta: A primary care office screens for depression with the PHQ-9. What does a score of 12 suggest?
opciones: A possible major depressive disorder, since 10 or more is the threshold
A possible major depressive disorder, since 20 or more is the threshold
A normal result, because the scale runs from 0 to 27 and 12 sits mid-range
A result that cannot be read until a clinician-administered scale is added
preguntas.explicacion: The questionnaire has nine items matching the diagnostic criteria and is filled in by the patient. It scores from 0 to 27, and 10 or above points to possible major depression. It is used to screen, to help diagnose and to follow the response to treatment. Suicidal and homicidal ideation is asked about at every visit, whatever the score comes out.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Major Depressive Disorder", Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: A telehealth appointment has been booked for a nine-year-old. What should the office confirm with the family in advance?
opciones: Who needs to be available, since the minor must be present and the parent may be too
That the child will hold the device alone, so the clinician can assess her unaided
That the parent will complete the visit while the child stays out of the room
That the school nurse will join the call to act as the telehealth facilitator
preguntas.explicacion: Among the topics to discuss with a patient before a first virtual visit, the guidance lists treating the appointment as one would an in-person visit, how the patient will connect, and who needs to be available: for a minor, it says to make clear that the minor needs to be present and whether the parent should or should not also be there. It also covers what to do if the appointment cannot be kept or the connection fails.

preguntas.pregunta: What can VAERS data show, and what can it not show?
opciones: It flags unusual patterns; it cannot establish that a vaccine caused the event
It establishes that a vaccine caused an event, but only for licensed products
It measures how often a reaction happens, since every case has to be reported
It replaces the studies that follow licensure, because the data are national
preguntas.explicacion: VAERS is a passive early warning system: it depends on people sending in reports, so it is useful for spotting new, unusual or rare events, rises in the rate of known reactions, and patient risk factors. It is not designed to establish that a vaccine caused a health problem, and any safety signal it raises has to be confirmed by further studies, such as those run through the Vaccine Safety Datalink.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, VAERS (co-managed with FDA): About VAERS, Background and Public Health Importance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(4)

preguntas.pregunta: Which membrane lines the body cavities that open to the outside, such as the digestive and respiratory tracts?
opciones: Mucous membrane, an epithelium over loose connective tissue
Serous membrane, an epithelium over loose connective tissue
Synovial membrane, a connective tissue without an epithelium
Meningeal membrane, a connective tissue without an epithelium
preguntas.explicacion: Epithelial membranes come in two kinds. Mucous membranes, or mucosae, line the passages that open to the outside world, so the whole digestive tract and the respiratory, excretory and reproductive tracts are lined by them. Serous membranes line the cavities that do not open outward. Synovial membranes and meninges have no epithelium at all.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Cells, Tissues and Membranes: Membranes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through a phlebotomist's gown to the scrubs underneath. When must the gown come off?
opciones: Immediately, or as soon as feasible
Once the procedure has been completed
At the end of the shift, with other coverings
After hands are washed and gloves changed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(vi) says that a garment penetrated by blood or OPIM is removed immediately or as soon as feasible. The standard defines appropriate PPE in (d)(3)(i) as equipment that does not let blood reach work clothes, street clothes, undergarments or skin under normal conditions of use, so a gown that has been soaked through has stopped being appropriate. End of shift is the timing given for surfaces and protective coverings in (d)(4)(ii), not for garments; handwashing follows removal, it does not precede it.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi) and (d)(3)(i), Personal Protective Equipment

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks lost when asked, 'Have you eaten, taken your pills, or had any coffee since midnight?' How should the questioning be reworked?
opciones: Ask one thing at a time, in yes-or-no form, and re-explain who you are
Repeat the whole question more loudly and quickly to hold his attention
Switch to open-ended questions so that he can tell the story in his own words
Put every question to the caregiver, since he cannot answer reliably
preguntas.explicacion: With cognitive impairment: address the patient directly with simple wording, one idea at a time, using yes-or-no or multiple-choice questions; help orient the patient by explaining or re-explaining who you are and what you will do; and avoid speaking too quickly or loudly. Yes-or-no questions also help when the patient struggles with open ones.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment, Tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6)(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(6)(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: What is a debrief for?
opciones: Reviewing how the team performed and drawing out the lessons
Sharing the plan and handing out roles before the work starts
Re-establishing awareness partway through and adjusting the plan
Passing responsibility and accountability on to the next person
preguntas.explicacion: The debrief reviews the team's performance: a structured, intentional but informal and quick exchange meant to improve performance through lessons learned and by reinforcing what went well. Sharing the plan up front is the brief, re-establishing situational awareness in the middle is the huddle, and passing responsibility is a handoff.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Effective Team Event Tools

preguntas.pregunta: An operative report is titled appendectomy. Which ending would have been used instead if the surgeon had only cut into the appendix?
opciones: -otomy, the ending that names an incision
-ostomy, the ending that names an opening
-plasty, the ending for a reconstruction
-pexy, the ending for a surgical fixation
preguntas.explicacion: The four surgical endings are close cousins and each names a different act: -ectomy cuts the part out, -otomy only cuts into it, -ostomy makes an opening, -plasty rebuilds and -pexy anchors a part in place. An appendectomy removes the appendix, so an incision alone would have carried -otomy.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery

preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern of freezing does cryosurgery aim for, and how is a benign lesion margin judged?
opciones: Rapid freezing then slow thawing, with the white halo reaching 1 to 2 mm past the border
Slow freezing then rapid thawing, with the white halo reaching 1 to 2 mm past the border
Rapid freezing then slow thawing, with the white halo reaching 10 mm past the border
Slow freezing then rapid thawing, with the white halo reaching exactly to the border
preguntas.explicacion: Ice crystals form between and then inside the cells, and thawing damages them again as water rushes back in, so the ideal is fast freezing followed by slow thawing. A benign lesion is frozen until the white halo extends 1 to 2 mm beyond its border, usually for five to ten seconds, and thawing is complete when the original color returns and no frost remains.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cryotherapy in Dermatology", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: Where is the line drawn between sustained and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia?
opciones: At thirty seconds, or sooner if the patient becomes unstable
At ten seconds, or sooner if the patient becomes unstable
At three beats in a row, or sooner if the patient is unstable
At two minutes, or sooner if the patient becomes unstable
preguntas.explicacion: A run under 30 seconds is nonsustained; one that lasts longer, or that comes with hemodynamic instability, is sustained. A separate label sorts the same rhythm by shape: monomorphic when the complexes match one another, polymorphic when they vary.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Tachycardia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i

preguntas.pregunta: How should peel packs and trays be positioned when a steam sterilizer is loaded?
opciones: Peel packs on edge in mesh baskets and perforated trays laid parallel to the shelf
Peel packs stacked flat on the shelf and perforated trays stood upright against the wall
Peel packs on edge in solid-bottom pans and nonperforated basins laid flat and nested
Peel packs laid flat under the trays so the heavier metal holds them against the shelf
preguntas.explicacion: Everything is arranged so the sterilant circulates freely and reaches every surface. Perforated trays go parallel to the shelf, nonperforated containers such as basins are stood on edge, small items lie loosely in wire baskets, and peel packs are set on edge in perforated or mesh-bottom racks. Items packed tightly or nested shield one another from the steam.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Loading
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.A.4

preguntas.pregunta: Which vessels are the main site of resistance and of blood pressure regulation, and how wide are they?
opciones: Arterioles, with lumens of about 30 μm or less
Capillaries, with lumens of only 5 to 10 μm
Venules, with lumens of from 8 to 100 μm
Elastic arteries, more than 10 mm in diameter
preguntas.explicacion: Arterioles, with lumens averaging 30 micrometers or less, are called resistance vessels because they slow blood flow and cause the sharpest drop in pressure; their constriction and dilation are the main way blood flow is distributed and pressure is regulated. Capillaries are narrower but far more numerous, and their total cross-sectional area is greater, so they are not the main site of resistance.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Arterioles; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, The Roles of Vessel Diameter and Total Area

preguntas.pregunta: A patient seated in the exam room is about to hear sensitive results. Where should the assistant place themselves?
opciones: At the patient's eye level, seated, facing them and leaning in
Standing beside the chair so both can watch the computer screen
Behind the desk, facing the chart, with the door left open
At a right angle to the patient, with an eye on the exit
preguntas.explicacion: Initial and sensitive exchanges land better when both people are at eye level, and bringing a chair over helps. Facing the patient, leaning slightly forward and making eye contact signal full attention. Standing at a right angle with an awareness of the exits is the posture kept for a patient who may become aggressive.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication

preguntas.pregunta: A workers' compensation carrier denied the bill and the office now wants Medicare to pay it. What has to go with the Medicare claim?
opciones: The reason the compensation insurer gave for denying, taken from its remittance
A letter from the patient's attorney saying the case is still being contested
A copy of the compensation policy showing the condition is excluded from it
A statement that the compensation carrier was billed first and made no payment
preguntas.explicacion: The claim always goes to the primary payer first. When a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation insurer denies on liability grounds, that insurer has to put the reason for the denial on the claim; the provider finds it on the remittance advice it received and sends it on to Medicare. Without that reason Medicare denies the claim. In an electronic remittance the reason lives in the claim adjustment segment.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.3.b(4) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185

preguntas.pregunta: Instruments are being packaged for the autoclave. How should they be prepared?
opciones: Hinged items opened, removable parts taken off, and concave surfaces set so water drains
Hinged items closed, removable parts left on, and concave surfaces set to hold the steam in
Hinged items opened, removable parts left on, and heavy items laid on top of the delicate ones
Hinged items closed, removable parts taken off, and the whole set held to a fixed weight limit
preguntas.explicacion: Once items are cleaned, dried and inspected, they go into trays arranged so the sterilant reaches everything: hinges opened, removable parts disassembled unless the manufacturer says otherwise, concave surfaces positioned to let water drain, and heavy pieces placed where they will not crush delicate ones. There is no longer a set weight limit for surgical sets.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Packaging

preguntas.pregunta: What is a non-preferred provider?
opciones: A provider with no contract with the plan, whom the patient pays more to see
A provider with a contract with the plan whose discount is smaller than usual
A provider the plan removed from its network after a quality review of the care
A provider the patient may see only when the primary care doctor refers her there
preguntas.explicacion: The non-preferred provider is simply one who has no contract with the insurer or plan, so the patient pays more for that care. A contracted provider whose discount is smaller is described in the glossary as a participating provider inside a tiered network. Removal after a quality review and referral requirements are separate matters; the definition turns on the contract alone.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Non-preferred provider; and Glossary: Preferred provider

preguntas.pregunta: How is a pack-year history worked out?
opciones: Packs smoked per day multiplied by the number of years of smoking
Cigarettes smoked per day multiplied by the number of years smoking
Packs smoked per week multiplied by the number of years of smoking
Packs smoked per day added to the number of years spent smoking
preguntas.explicacion: Packs per day times years smoked gives an estimate of the lifetime consumption. The figure carries weight because it tracks with the presence and severity of smoking-related illness, including coronary artery disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and the smoking-related cancers have all been tied to a higher count.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Nicotine Addiction and Smoking", History and Physical

preguntas.pregunta: Which needle is commonly used for sewing skin, and how is most skin closure curved?
opciones: A reverse cutting needle, with the curve usually three-eighths of a circle
A conventional cutting needle, with the curve usually one-half of a circle
A blunt taper needle, with the curve usually one-quarter of a circle
A sharp taper needle, with the curve usually one-third of a circle
preguntas.explicacion: Cutting needles carry three sharp edges. The conventional kind has the cutting surface on the inside of the curve, the reverse cutting kind on the outside, and it is the reverse cutting needle that is commonly used to sew skin. Most skin closure needles are curved, and the usual curve is three-eighths of a circle, which lets the surgeon keep track of where the tip is.

preguntas.pregunta: How deep should each chest compression go on an adult?
opciones: About 2 inches (5 cm), without using excessive force, with full recoil
About 1½ inches (4 cm), the depth used on the chest of an infant
About 3 inches (7.5 cm), going deeper when the patient is obese
About 1 inch (2.5 cm), just enough to move the sternum downward
preguntas.explicacion: The adult target is roughly 2 inches, or 5 centimeters, pressing hard but avoiding excessive force, and letting the chest recoil completely each time. An inch and a half (4 cm) is the infant figure, not the adult one. Rib fractures occur in up to 70 % of resuscitations, which is a known cost of compressions and not a reason to press less.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told the disease is in complete remission. What does that phrase mean?
opciones: Every sign and symptom has gone, though cancer may still be present
Every sign and symptom has gone, so the cancer is considered cured
Some of the signs and symptoms have gone and the others have not
The signs have gone but the tests still show the disease clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Remission is a decrease in, or the disappearance of, the signs and symptoms of cancer. In partial remission some of them are gone; in complete remission all of them are gone, although cancer may still be in the body. That last clause is why complete remission and cure are not the same word.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, remission

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being placed in lithotomy for a gynecologic procedure. How are the legs handled?
opciones: Abducted 30 to 45 degrees from the midline, knees flexed, raised and lowered together
Abducted 60 to 75 degrees from the midline, knees extended, raised one after the other
Abducted 30 to 45 degrees from the midline, knees extended, raised one at a time
Abducted 15 to 20 degrees from the midline, knees flexed, lowered before the drape
preguntas.explicacion: The legs go out about 30 to 45 degrees from midline with the knees bent and the foot of the bed lowered or removed. Both legs move at the same time, up and down together, because moving one alone twists the spine and strains muscle. Padding under the legs keeps the supports from compressing nerves where they rest.

preguntas.pregunta: Which function of the medical home makes the practice accountable for most of a patient's physical and mental health needs?
opciones: Comprehensive care, which calls for a team of care providers to meet those needs
Coordinated care, which links the practice with hospitals and the community services
Accessible services, which shorten waits and extend hours for urgent problems
Patient-centered care, which treats the family as a core member of the team
preguntas.explicacion: Comprehensive care makes the primary care medical home accountable for the large majority of each patient's physical and mental health needs, prevention and wellness, acute care and chronic care included. Meeting that promise takes a team, which may bring together physicians, advanced practice nurses, physician assistants, nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists, social workers, educators and care coordinators.

preguntas.pregunta: The provider is about to examine the abdomen of a patient with cramping. In what order are the four methods used?
opciones: Inspection, auscultation, percussion and palpation
Inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation
Auscultation, then inspection, palpation and percussion
Inspection, percussion, palpation and auscultation
preguntas.explicacion: The abdomen breaks the usual pattern. Listening comes second, before any hand presses on the wall, because pressing can stir up or quiet the bowel and change what is heard. The chest is the sequence most people memorize instead: inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation. Getting the two mixed up is the classic error.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abdominal Examination", Technique: Auscultation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a · RMA III.F.3.b · CCMA 3B4 · NCMA 2B.10

preguntas.pregunta: Whole blood for a PCR assay cannot be extracted until next week. Which storage plan follows the recommendations?
opciones: Separate the plasma or serum from the red cells and store it at −20 °C or colder
Freeze the whole blood tube at −20 °C or colder until the extraction can be done
Keep the whole blood tube at 2 to 8 °C, where it stays stable indefinitely for DNA
Keep the whole blood tube at room temperature, since cold storage lyses the white cells
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood is not stored below 0 °C: when a frozen sample thaws, heme is released, and heme inhibits the polymerase and quenches the fluorophores used to detect the product. If extraction cannot happen within an acceptable time the erythrocytes are removed and the plasma or serum is frozen at −20 °C or colder. There is no absolute limit for whole blood at room temperature or 2 to 8 °C, but prolonged storage there raises the risk of hemolysis and of nucleic acid degradation from white cell lysis.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)

preguntas.pregunta: Losing half a kilogram of body fat a week calls for what daily energy deficit?
opciones: About 642 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 9,000 kcal
About 642 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 4,500 kcal
About 320 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 4,500 kcal
About 1,280 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 9,000 kcal
preguntas.explicacion: A kilogram of fat stores 9,000 kcal, so half a kilogram means a net deficit of 4,500 kcal over the week, about 642 kcal a day. That deficit is built by eating less and moving more. For someone eating 2,600 kcal it means cutting a quarter of the day's intake if activity does not rise.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dietary Approaches to Obesity Treatment", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 weight control · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports heartburn and regurgitation after meals. Which structure normally prevents that, and what is the diagnosis?
opciones: The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is peptic ulcer disease
The pyloric sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The upper esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: Heartburn, regurgitation and noncardiac chest pain are the usual complaints in gastroesophageal reflux disease, and with those typical symptoms the diagnosis can be made presumptively. What normally holds the contents down is the lower esophageal sphincter, a physiological sphincter three to five centimeters long whose high resting tone keeps stomach contents out of the esophagus.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease", Introduction and Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(6) (2027 I.C.6.g(6)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on plasma. Which tubes will supply it?
opciones: The heparin tubes, the EDTA tube and the citrate tube
The clot activator tube and the serum separator tube alone
The clot activator tube, the citrate tube and the EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma comes from tubes whose additive stops the blood from clotting: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA in the purple tube and citrate in the light blue tube, which is why coagulation testing uses plasma. The red clot activator tube and the gold separator tube are the ones that yield serum.

preguntas.pregunta: Which help falls under home care services rather than under the Medicare home health benefit?
opciones: Housework, cooking or meal delivery, and help keeping the bills paid on time
Wound care for a pressure sore, given by a skilled nurse who visits her at home
Intravenous or nutrition therapy given at home by a skilled visiting nurse
Occupational therapy at home for a patient recovering from a serious stroke
preguntas.explicacion: Home care lets a person with special needs stay at home, whether from aging in place, chronic illness, recovery from surgery or disability. It covers personal care such as bathing or dressing, chores such as cleaning, yard work and laundry, cooking or delivered meals, help with forms and bills, and health care from an aide or through telehealth. Many of these are paid privately.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Home Care Services: Summary

preguntas.pregunta: A practice discovers it was overpaid by Medicare. How soon must the money be reported and returned?
opciones: Within 60 days of identifying the overpayment, to avoid liability
Within 120 days of identifying the overpayment, to avoid liability
Within 12 months, the same deadline that applies to filing a claim
When the contractor requests it after its next scheduled record review
preguntas.explicacion: An overpayment is money paid by Medicare that the recipient is not entitled to, and it must be reported and returned within 60 days of being identified; missing that window can create False Claims Act liability and whistleblower exposure. The 120-day figures belong to the bad debt collection rules, and 12 months is the timely filing limit for claims, so neither governs a refund.

preguntas.pregunta: A bilingual receptionist offers to interpret the pre-draw questions. Why are staff untrained as healthcare interpreters ruled out?
opciones: Research shows untrained people make more clinically significant mistakes
Their interpreting time cannot be reimbursed by any state Medicaid programme
They cannot be listed in the practice directory of bilingual clinicians
They are barred from signing the practice's interpreter ethics statement
preguntas.explicacion: Unacceptable services include clinicians or staff who are not sufficiently proficient in both languages, and those who are not trained or certified as healthcare interpreters, because research shows that people not trained to interpret make more clinically significant mistakes. preguntas.pregunta: A therapist asks the patient to lift the top of the foot toward the leg. Which movement is that, and at which joint?
opciones: Dorsiflexion, at the ankle joint
Plantar flexion, at the ankle joint
Inversion, at the intertarsal joints
Eversion, at the intertarsal joints
preguntas.explicacion: Lifting the front of the foot so the top comes toward the leg is dorsiflexion; lifting the heel and pointing the toes is plantar flexion. opciones: 0.5 to 1 mL in infants and children, and 2 to 5 mL in adults
Up to 1 mL in adults, and up to 0.5 mL in infants and children
0.1 mL at any age, the same volume used for a tuberculin test
Up to 3 mL at any age, at any of the recommended muscle sites
preguntas.explicacion: The volume for an intramuscular injection is 0.5 to 1 mL in infants and children and 2 to 5 mL in adults. Within that range the site still matters: the maximum for one injection at the vastus lateralis in an adult is 3 mL, and the deltoid generally takes about 1 mL. The collector seals the sample and signs the form, and the donor signs on receipt
The laboratory seals the sample on arrival and both parties sign the log at once
The container is sealed by whoever is free, and the form is signed at the end of day
preguntas.explicacion: For drugs-of-abuse testing, the donor identifies the sample and preferably seals the cup themselves, then the chain of custody form is signed by the donor and afterwards by the person who collected it. preguntas.pregunta: Which urine examination is disturbed when the specimen is refrigerated before it is examined?
opciones: Crystal identification, because cold precipitates phosphates and urates in the sediment
Leukocyte esterase, because cold destroys the enzyme within 1 hour of refrigeration
Bacterial culture, because cold stops growth so the colony count becomes falsely low
Specific gravity, because cold urine reads falsely high on the refractometer
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigeration is the preferred way to hold urine, but it makes phosphates and urates precipitate, which can confuse the analysis of those analytes; when crystal differentiation is requested a separate aliquot is kept unrefrigerated. Refrigeration preserves, rather than lowers, the colony count for culture, and the documented false elevations of specific gravity are from dextran, intravenous contrast and proteinuria, not cold.

preguntas.pregunta: A woman reports urinary frequency, urgency, burning on urination and suprapubic discomfort. Which organism most often causes this?

Klebsiella species, responsible for the majority of these infections
Staphylococcus aureus, responsible for the majority of these infections
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, responsible for the majority of these infections
preguntas.explicacion: Frequency, urgency, dysuria and suprapubic discomfort are the typical symptoms of an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, and Escherichia coli causes most of them, with Klebsiella next and Proteus, Enterobacter and Enterococcus behind. preguntas.pregunta: How long should an alcohol hand rub take, and how long should hands be rubbed with soap and water, according to the CDC?
opciones: About 20 seconds for the rub; at least 15 seconds of rubbing for the wash
About 2 to 6 minutes for the rub; at least 20 seconds for the wash
About 10 seconds for the rub; at least 60 seconds for the wash
About 30 seconds for the rub; at least 30 seconds for the wash
preguntas.explicacion: Rubbing sanitizer over all hand surfaces until dry should take around 20 seconds, and with soap and water the hands are rubbed together vigorously for at least 15 seconds; either time is acceptable. StatPearls gives the same figures: 3 to 5 mL of rub for about 20 seconds, and washing for at least 15 to 20 seconds covering palms, backs, wrists, between fingers, thumbs and under the nails. Two to six minutes is the length of a surgical scrub, not routine hand hygiene.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates proximate cause from cause-in-fact in a negligence claim?
opciones: Proximate cause asks whether the harm was a foreseeable consequence
Proximate cause asks whether the defendant intended the harm to happen
Proximate cause asks whether the plaintiff suffered any monetary loss
Proximate cause asks whether a statute was broken before the harm began
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence needs both a factual link and a legal one. Proximate cause is the test the law adds on top: it usually turns on foreseeability, so throwing a rock off a balcony without looking is the proximate cause of the injury below because the harm was foreseeable. Conduct by the plaintiff or an intervening third party can break that link.

Six national priority purposes, all of them limited to law enforcement requests
Four national priority purposes, all of them requiring a court order beforehand
Eighteen national priority purposes, one for each identifier the rule names

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about restraint or seclusion orders is correct under the CMS patient-rights condition?
opciones: They may never be written as standing or as-needed (PRN) orders
They may be written PRN for patients with a history of falls
They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to ensure the immediate physical safety of the patient, staff or others, never for coercion, discipline, convenience or retaliation, only when less restrictive measures have failed, and under the order of a physician or other licensed practitioner responsible for the patient. Orders must never be written as standing orders or on an as-needed basis. For violent behavior each order is limited to 4 hours for adults, 2 hours for ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, up to 24 hours in total, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, and the intervention ends as soon as possible.

preguntas.pregunta: What is workers' compensation insurance?
opciones: Coverage employers must carry for workers who get sick or hurt on the job
Coverage employers may buy to replace the group health plan for their workers
Coverage the state buys for workers whose employer offers no health plan
Coverage that pays the deductible of the group plan after a workplace injury
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation is insurance employers are required to have to cover employees who become ill or are injured because of their work. preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports that he fainted during his last two blood draws. What is the correct preparation?

Draw quickly while he stands, so that he can walk the dizziness off afterwards
Ask him to watch the needle closely so that he stays alert throughout
Postpone the draw until he returns with a signed consent form

Blood iron peaks around 4 p.m., so the morning gives a trough value
Blood iron is stable in serum for only two hours after waking
Blood iron falls once the 24-hour glycogen stores have been used up

As viral, bacterial or fungal, then by the lobe of the lung involved
As acute or chronic, then by whether the patient has ever smoked
As upper or lower tract disease, then by the age of the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The widely used scheme sorts pneumonia into community-acquired, hospital-acquired and atypical, and then stratifies each by severity. Typical pneumonia is the one caused by organisms such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae and Staphylococcus aureus. preguntas.pregunta: An 80-year-old with a serious infection has a pulse of 76 beats per minute. Why does that not rule out the infection?
opciones: The rise in rate is blunted in older adults, so tachycardia may never appear
The rate in older adults is read against a resting band that starts at 50 per minute
The rate falls rather than rises during infection once a patient passes 75 years
The rate is unreliable at the wrist in older adults and only counts at the carotid
preguntas.explicacion: Older adults often show a blunted rise in heart rate under stress because the response to adrenergic drive is reduced, and drugs such as beta blockers and some calcium channel blockers flatten it further. Tachycardia can therefore be missing in serious infection or blood loss, so a normal-looking rate is not reassurance on its own.

So the patient stays warm and does not shiver
So the wires do not pick up current from the room
So the chest marks are not rubbed off the skin

Giving one before a service that exceeds a frequency limit set by a coverage policy
Giving one before an item that is experimental, investigational or research only
Giving one covering an extended course of treatment listed with its duration

preguntas.pregunta: Blood for serological testing is drawn at a rural clinic in midsummer and sent by car to the laboratory. Which two handling points apply to that specimen?
opciones: Let the blood clot before processing, and protect the sample from extreme temperatures during transport
Centrifuge the tube immediately after the draw, and keep the sample frozen at −20 °C during transport
Mix the tube by five inversions to prevent clotting, and keep the sample at 37 °C during transport
Let the blood clot before processing, and keep the sample on wet ice during the whole transport
preguntas.explicacion: For serological testing the blood is allowed to clot before it is processed, the specimen goes into properly labelled containers, and during transport it is protected from extreme temperatures; serum for prompt serology is then stored at 2 to 8 °C, and only long-term storage or delayed transport calls for freezing at −20 °C or lower. Spinning before the clot has formed is what produces fibrin in the serum, and wet ice is the transport rule for other specimen types.

To the Ryan White notification system for emergency response personnel

In the ordinary office trash, once the label is removed
In the sharps container, together with the used needles

preguntas.pregunta: Tetanus is caught from contact with a skin wound and cannot be passed to another person. Which label fits it?
opciones: A noncommunicable infectious disease, caused by a pathogen but not spread
A noninfectious disease, since it is not caused by any pathogen at all
A contagious disease, since a pathogen is present in the wound and spreads
An inherited disease, since a genetic mutation decides who develops it
preguntas.explicacion: Infectious and communicable are not the same thing. preguntas.pregunta: A patient collects a semen sample at home. What should he be told about getting it to the laboratory?

Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an insulated bag with a cold pack so that it stays chilled
Bring it within 6 hours, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature
Bring it whenever convenient, since the laboratory warms every specimen to 37 degrees anyway
preguntas.explicacion: A home-collected specimen should reach the laboratory inside 30 minutes, kept warm in an inside coat pocket at body temperature, and a specialist has to examine it within 2 hours of collection; the sooner it is read, the more reliable the result. preguntas.pregunta: In the cubital fossa, where does the brachial artery run relative to the biceps tendon, and where is the median nerve?
opciones: The artery just medial to the tendon; the median nerve most medial of all
The artery just lateral to the tendon; the median nerve most lateral of all
The artery deep to the median cubital vein in the roof; the nerve lateral
The artery only at the apex of the fossa; the radial nerve most medial
preguntas.explicacion: The contents of the fossa run from lateral to medial: the radial nerve near the brachioradialis, the biceps tendon, the brachial artery just medial to that tendon, and the median nerve, the most medial structure, usually passing between the two heads of pronator teres. The artery divides into radial and ulnar arteries at the apex. The median cubital vein is not inside the fossa but in its roof.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Structure and Function

preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations does the Privacy Rule REQUIRE a covered entity to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual asking for access or an accounting, and to HHS for a compliance review
To the individual asking for access, and to any provider who requests records for treatment
To HHS for a compliance review, and to the health plan whenever it asks to audit a claim
To a law enforcement official with a badge, and to the patient's closest living relative
preguntas.explicacion: Almost everything in the rule is permissive: the entity may use or disclose PHI in the listed situations but is not obliged to. Only two disclosures are mandatory, namely to individuals or their personal representatives when they request access or an accounting of disclosures, and to HHS when it is conducting an investigation, compliance review or enforcement action.

preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what a nursing home offers that home care cannot. What is the defining feature?
opciones: Nursing aides and skilled nurses on hand 24 hours a day for people not needing a hospital
A private apartment with meals, housekeeping and social activities for independent residents
Surgery on patients who are expected to go home within 24 hours after the procedure
An interdisciplinary team that manages pain for a patient in the last stage of illness
preguntas.explicacion: A nursing home serves people who do not need to be in a hospital but cannot be cared for at home, and most keep nursing aides and skilled nurses available around the clock. Some are set up like a hospital with therapy staff and a nurses' station on each floor; others aim to feel like a neighborhood. Nursing homes are not only for older adults but for anyone needing 24-hour care.

preguntas.pregunta: What decides whether a procedure calls for sterile gloves rather than clean exam gloves?
opciones: Whether contact with a sterile site, tissue or body cavity is expected during it
Whether the patient is on transmission-based precautions during the visit that day
Whether the procedure will last long enough for the practitioner's hands to perspire
Whether any blood or body fluid is likely to reach the practitioner's hands at all
preguntas.explicacion: Clean gloves cover the risk of touching body fluids or contaminated surfaces, as when an intravenous line is started or a catheter bag emptied. Sterile gloves meet FDA sterilization requirements and are used for invasive procedures and whenever a sterile site, tissue or cavity will be touched, so that neither transient nor resident flora is carried in.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a tracing that looks normal not prove the heart is pumping?
opciones: Electrical activity can carry on with no pumping behind it
The tracing follows the atria only, and never the ventricles
The speed of the paper hides the pumping part of each beat
The tracing follows the pumping in the chest leads only
preguntas.explicacion: The recording measures electrical events, and one of its stated limits is that it does not show how well the heart is pumping; electrical activity can appear on the strip with no pumping action to match. Judging the pump takes another test, such as an ultrasound.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an open workers' compensation record is treated for something unrelated, and the contractor denies the claim anyway. What should the office do?
opciones: Appeal with evidence that the care had nothing to do with the injury, and keep treating
Stop treating the patient until the workers' compensation record has been closed
Rebill the compensation carrier, since the open record makes it the primary payer
Write the balance off, since a claim denied on an open record cannot be reopened
preguntas.explicacion: Contractors sometimes deny claims because the diagnosis codes fall within the family of codes attached to a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation record in the patient's eligibility file, even when the care had nothing to do with the accident. Those denials can be appealed with information proving the services were unrelated, and care must go on during the appeal period while the record stays open.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to take her Medicare appeal all the way to federal district court in 2026. What has to be true of the amount in dispute?
opciones: It has to reach $1,960, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $1,960, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
It has to reach $1,000, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $5,000, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
preguntas.explicacion: Judicial review in federal district court is the last of the five levels of Medicare appeal, and it is the only one with a minimum amount in controversy: $1,960 for 2026. Claims may be combined to reach that figure, and the decision letter from the fourth level carries the directions for filing, as every level's letter carries the directions for the next.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her cholesterol figure cannot be set beside the one another laboratory gave her last year. Why not?
opciones: Laboratories use different methods, so their reference ranges differ
Laboratories report in different units, and only the units differ
Laboratories keep results on file for a single calendar year only
Laboratories round the figures differently when they issue reports
preguntas.explicacion: Because laboratories often use different testing methods, they often use different reference ranges to describe normal results. A figure therefore has to be read against the range printed on its own report, and results from two laboratories cannot be set side by side. Anyone looking for a trend over time is told to try to use the same laboratory each time.

opciones: A device to collect and handle blood specimens and separate serum from cellular components; Class II
A device to collect and handle blood specimens and separate serum from cellular components; Class I device
A device with a sharps injury prevention feature that retracts or shields the needle; Class III
A device to transfer blood between tubes without additive carry-over; Class II

preguntas.pregunta: A resting strip is regular at 118 per minute with upright P waves in I and II. What does the assistant do?
opciones: Record it and report the tracing to the provider for reading
Record it and tell the patient it shows sinus tachycardia
Repeat it at half the paper speed to slow the tracing down
Repeat it with the limb electrodes moved up to the thighs
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing is obtained by the technician and interpreted by the clinician, so the finding goes to the provider rather than to the patient. Changing the paper speed would make the recording unreadable against the standard grid, and moving the limb electrodes is a remedy for tremor, not for a fast rate.

preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient do just before coughing a sputum specimen into the container?
opciones: Rinse the mouth with plain water for 10 to 15 seconds and spit the saliva out
Rinse the mouth with an antiseptic mouthwash and spit the rinse out completely
Eat a light breakfast so the cough reflex is stronger and the sputum comes up
Hold the breath for 10 to 15 seconds, which loosens secretions from the airway
preguntas.explicacion: Rinsing with clear water for 10 to 15 seconds clears contaminants from the mouth, and the saliva is expelled before the patient takes three deep breaths and coughs at about two-minute intervals until sputum comes up. A deep-cough sample is best taken early in the morning before eating or drinking. Antiseptic mouthwash is the thing specifically avoided before a throat swab.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure

preguntas.pregunta: Serum for hepatitis serology will not reach the reference laboratory for another six days. How should it be stored in the meantime?
opciones: Frozen at −20 °C or lower, the rule for long-term storage or delayed transport
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C, the rule for serum awaiting prompt serological testing
At room temperature away from extremes, the rule for specimens while in transit
Frozen at −70 °C, the rule for specimens that must keep the virus intact for culture
preguntas.explicacion: Serum meant for prompt serological testing waits at 2 to 8 °C, but when transport is delayed or storage will be long the specimen is frozen at −20 °C or lower. Protection from temperature extremes applies while the sample travels, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture specimens, so each distractor is a real instruction attached to the wrong situation. The blood must also have clotted before the serum is processed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)

preguntas.pregunta: A ward sends a preserved 24-hour urine and asks for a dipstick from the same jug. Which pairing of preservative and false result is correct?
opciones: Thymol reads as albumin; mercury salts read as no leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as glucose; mercury salts read as no urobilinogen present
Thymol reads as no albumin; mercury salts read as leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as nitrite; mercury salts read as no bilirubin present
preguntas.explicacion: Preservatives keep a collection usable but distort the strip. Thymol can produce a false-positive reaction for albumin, and mercury salts a false-negative leukocyte esterase. Formaldehyde gives false positives for leukocyte esterase, the peroxidase reaction, urobilinogen and glucose, hydrochloric acid shifts the pH, and boric acid dulls the leukocyte pad.

preguntas.pregunta: During the resuscitation of an infant, which pulse is evaluated?
opciones: The brachial, felt just above the antecubital fossa on the inner arm
The radial, felt at the wrist just above the base of the infant's thumb
The carotid, felt beside the airway as it is in an adult resuscitation
The dorsalis pedis, felt on the top of the foot beside the tendon there
preguntas.explicacion: In infant resuscitation the brachial artery is the site used, palpated just proximal to the antecubital fossa between the medial epicondyle and the biceps tendon. The carotid is the site preferred during adult resuscitation. The dorsalis pedis is absent in about one person in ten from anatomical variation alone.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomy service is choosing safety-engineered devices for the first time. What is asked of it before the purchase?

Buy whichever device the largest hospital in the region already uses
Buy the cheapest device available, since all are cleared for the task
Trial each device on staff volunteers before any patient is drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices cut exposure to blood and injuries, but not every one of them suits phlebotomy. Users are asked to investigate the devices available thoroughly, looking at appropriate use, compatibility with existing practice and how well they protect staff and patients.
