preguntas.pregunta: Which four tissue types make up every organ in the body?
opciones: Epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue
Epithelial, glandular, cartilage and nervous tissue
Connective, muscle, adipose and vascular tissue
Epithelial, connective, muscle and lymphoid tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Four tissue types cover every job. Epithelium sheets the outer surfaces, lines cavities and passageways and forms glands; connective tissue binds and supports; muscle is excitable and shortens to give movement; nervous tissue is excitable and carries signals. Adipose, cartilage and blood are specialized kinds of connective tissue.

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements of the informed consent discussion have to appear in the record?
opciones: The nature of the procedure, its risks and benefits, the alternatives with theirs, and understanding
The nature of the procedure, its cost, the name of the assistant present, and the patient's signature
The nature of the procedure, its expected duration, the recovery time, and the follow-up date set
The nature of the procedure, the surgeon's experience with it, the anesthetic, and the tetanus status
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation has to carry the nature of the procedure or intervention, its risks and benefits, the reasonable alternatives, the risks and benefits of those alternatives, and an assessment of whether the patient understood all of it. Consent has moved from collecting a signature to a process built on clear communication, with the patient competent and free of coercion.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Function

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's account of when the pain started keeps contradicting itself. Which technique fits?
opciones: Clarifying, with guiding statements that draw out more detail
Reflecting, by repeating the account back almost word for word
Providing rationale, by saying up front why the detail is needed
Using silence, by waiting without interrupting until she stops
preguntas.explicacion: Clarifying is the listed technique for guiding a patient to make a statement clearer and to obtain additional information. Reflecting repeats what was said, sometimes word for word; providing rationale explains why the information or the recommendation is needed; and silence is about attentiveness and not interrupting. All four are techniques, but only one fits a confused account.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: A man doing a testicular self-exam finds a small, hard lump the size of a pea. What is the advice?
opciones: Contact the provider right away, since a hard pea-sized lump is abnormal
Watch it for one full month, since normal blood vessels feel much the same
Ignore it if the other side matches, since the two are normally identical
Ignore it if it is painless, since only tender lumps need to be reported
preguntas.explicacion: A small hard lump, an enlarged testicle, or any change that does not seem normal is reported without waiting. Normal findings are different: each testicle feels firm but not rock hard, and one may sit lower or be a little larger than the other. Vessels and other structures can make the exam confusing, which is another reason to ask rather than wait.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are alcohols not recommended for sterilizing surgical instruments?
opciones: They have no sporicidal action and cannot penetrate material rich in protein
They corrode stainless steel and dissolve the lubricant used on hinged joints
They lose all activity the moment they meet the salts left by tap-water rinsing
They need an exposure of several hours, which no outpatient office can arrange
preguntas.explicacion: Two failures rule them out: they do not kill spores, and they cannot get through protein-rich material. Fatal postoperative Clostridium wound infections have followed attempts to sterilize instruments with alcohol. They also evaporate fast, which makes a long exposure hard to hold unless the item is fully immersed, and they are flammable.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a health care proxy, in the strict sense of the term?
opciones: The agent named in a health care declaration to decide for the principal
The written document itself, listing the treatments the person refuses
The relative the state's law puts first when nobody has been named
The clinician who signs the orders once the person becomes incapacitated
preguntas.explicacion: The proxy is the agent named in a health care declaration to make medical decisions for the person who signed it, once that person cannot decide for themselves. The declaration is the written document setting out how they should be cared for. The proxy's authority usually runs to decisions the declaration never mentioned, to authorizing procedures and to accessing the records.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: health care proxy

preguntas.pregunta: On a rapid pregnancy cassette, what does the built-in control line tell the operator?
opciones: That the device worked and enough sample migrated through the strip; not whether the result is right
That the whole testing process, from sample application to interpretation, was performed correctly
That the result is positive, because a control line only develops in the presence of the analyte
That the kit lot has passed the manufacturer's quality control and is within its expiration date
preguntas.explicacion: Internal, procedural or built-in controls check that the test itself is functioning: the sample volume was adequate, the fluid moved through the strip, and any electronic functions worked. They do not prove the operator handled the whole process correctly; that is what an external control, run like a patient sample, is for. A missing control line means an invalid test, whatever the result window shows.

preguntas.pregunta: On a normal ECG tracing, what does the P wave represent?
opciones: Depolarization of the atria
Depolarization of the ventricles
Repolarization of the ventricles
Repolarization of the atria
preguntas.explicacion: The ECG has three prominent features: the small P wave is atrial depolarization, and the atria start contracting about 25 ms after it begins; the large QRS complex is ventricular depolarization; and the T wave is ventricular repolarization. Atrial repolarization does occur during the QRS complex, which masks it, but that is not what the P wave shows.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Electrocardiogram

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement correctly distinguishes a critical value from a STAT test result?
opciones: A critical value is defined only by how far it lies outside the normal range; a STAT test is designated by the ordering clinician
A critical value is designated by the ordering clinician; a STAT result is any value that falls outside the reference range
A critical value is any result outside the reference range; a STAT result is one that was reported within an hour of collection
A critical value is a result the instrument flags as invalid; a STAT test is one that must be confirmed by a second method
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are results that fall far outside normal ranges and signal potential pathology; they are defined solely by the degree of deviation from the established normal range, regardless of the patient's condition. STAT or urgent tests, by contrast, are designated by the ordering clinician and usually rest on prior knowledge of the patient's status. Both are handled in the post-analytical stage, when findings are communicated to the treatment team.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings; Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Critical value vs STAT · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT IV.C · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare remittance advice shows an adjustment with group code PR. What does that mean for the office?
opciones: The amount is patient responsibility, so the beneficiary may be billed for it
The amount is a provider obligation, so the beneficiary may not be billed for it
The amount is under review, so the office should resubmit the claim as corrected
The amount is a payment for interest owed for a late payment on a clean claim
preguntas.explicacion: Group codes assign responsibility for the unpaid part of the claim balance: CO marks a contractual obligation that belongs to the provider, and PR marks patient responsibility. Beneficiaries may be billed only when the adjustment carries the PR group code. Interest for a late payment on a clean claim appears instead as a provider level adjustment on the remittance.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79, 6D · CCMA 5K k182

preguntas.pregunta: The contents of a delivery do not match the packing list and a temperature excursion is suspected. What happens to those doses?
opciones: They are labelled not for use, kept apart in the storage unit, and the maker is called
They are put into stock and used first, so that no dose is wasted before it expires
They are returned to the carrier at once, since the office never took delivery of them
They are discarded on the spot and the loss is recorded in the inventory account
preguntas.explicacion: A discrepancy or a suspected excursion is reported to the manufacturer immediately. Meanwhile the doses are marked so nobody uses them, and they stay in the proper storage unit but separated from the rest until somebody decides whether they are still viable. Publicly funded stock also means a call to the state or local immunization programme.

preguntas.pregunta: How do providers join the Medicare Shared Savings Program?
opciones: Voluntarily, by coming together as an ACO accountable for quality and cost
Automatically, once the practice bills Medicare for fee-for-service claims
By state assignment, when the state designates a necessary provider region
By accreditation, once an approved organization grants the group deemed status
preguntas.explicacion: The Shared Savings Program is voluntary: it encourages groups of doctors, hospitals and other providers to come together as an ACO and give coordinated care to their Medicare patients. The ACO agrees to be held accountable for the quality, cost and experience of care of an assigned fee-for-service population, and chooses among participation tracks.

preguntas.pregunta: What usually separates a misdemeanor from a felony?
opciones: A misdemeanor is typically punishable by less than 12 months in jail
A misdemeanor is typically punishable by a fine and never by any jail
A misdemeanor is tried in a civil court and a felony in a criminal one
A misdemeanor is charged by the state and a felony only by the federal
preguntas.explicacion: Both are offenses punishable under criminal law. A misdemeanor is typically punishable by less than 12 months in jail, with community service, probation and fines among the usual sentences; the more serious felonies carry stiffer penalties, including jail beyond a year. Many states grade both into lettered classes, while others sentence crime by crime.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: misdemeanor; and Wex: felony

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the date of the last menstrual period recorded at intake for a pregnant patient?
opciones: It dates the pregnancy: 7 days and 9 months are added to give the expected date
It dates the pregnancy: 14 days and 9 months are added to give the expected date
It confirms the pregnancy, since no other method can establish that a patient is pregnant
It sets the dose of prenatal vitamins, which is calculated from the cycle length
preguntas.explicacion: Adding 7 days and then 9 months to the first day of the last period, 280 days in all, gives an estimated date of delivery. The method assumes a regular 28-day cycle with ovulation on day 14, and the patient has to be sure of the date. First-trimester ultrasonography is the most accurate way to confirm or revise it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pregnancy Dating", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: Which sequence describes how the body raises the breathing rate when carbon dioxide builds up?
opciones: Chemoreceptors detect the acid shift and the respiratory centre speeds the rate up
The lungs stretch, and the stretch receptors order the centre to speed the rate up
The heart raises its output first, and breathing follows the rise in cardiac work
The carotid bodies detect the fall in blood pressure and speed the breathing up
preguntas.explicacion: Carbon dioxide crosses into the cerebrospinal fluid and shifts its hydrogen ion concentration; chemoreceptors read that change and the respiratory centre answers with a different rate and volume. The carotid bodies, at the fork of the common carotid, respond to oxygen tension and pH, not to blood pressure.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Respiratory Rate", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k50 · RMA III.E.3 Respiration a

preguntas.pregunta: How long is an exposed worker followed with HIV antibody testing after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Baseline, then periodically for at least 6 months, for example at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
Baseline and one repeat at 7 days, when the 28-day PEP course is one quarter done
Baseline and one repeat at 1 to 2 months, the schedule used after the hepatitis B series
Baseline only, since a negative rapid test rules out infection from that exposure
preguntas.explicacion: HIV antibody is tested as soon as possible after exposure and periodically for at least 6 months, typically at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months; WHO's annex uses baseline, 6 to 12 weeks and 6 months. Workers on PEP also have blood counts and kidney and liver tests before and 2 weeks after starting. The 1-to-2-month test is the anti-HBs check after hepatitis B vaccination, and a baseline test only shows the worker's status at the time of exposure.

A poster stating that visits are conducted in English unless arranged early

preguntas.pregunta: For which of these exposures do the CDC and WHO guidance say HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is NOT indicated?
opciones: A few drops of blood on intact skin
A splash of blood into the eye
A needlestick with a hollow-bore needle
Blood contact with a fresh abrasion on the hand
preguntas.explicacion: Exposure of intact skin to potentially infectious fluids is one of the situations where PEP for HIV and hepatitis B is not indicated, together with fluids not known to transmit HIV such as faeces, saliva, urine or sweat. The CDC adds that a small amount of blood on intact skin probably poses no risk and that no such transmission has been documented, and its PEP guidance lists mucous membranes, non-intact skin and perforated skin as the routes that warrant consideration. Eye splashes, hollow-bore needlesticks and abrasions are all on that list.

preguntas.pregunta: On a normal tracing, how does the R wave change across the chest leads?
opciones: It grows from V1, the smallest, to V5, the largest
It shrinks from V1, the largest, to V5, the smallest
It stays the same height from V1 through to V6
It grows from V6, the smallest, to V1, the largest
preguntas.explicacion: The R wave gets taller as the leads move from the right side of the chest to the left, an orderly pattern called R-wave progression, with the smallest in V1 and the largest in V5. When that build-up is missing, one of the causes to rule out is an electrode placed in the wrong spot.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a living will and a health care power of attorney?
opciones: The living will states the choices; the power of attorney names who decides
The living will names who decides; the power of attorney states the choices
The living will works while the patient can still speak; the power does not
The living will is a medical order; the power of attorney is a legal document
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is a written statement of the person's own wishes, such as whether they want resuscitation or intubation, and it designates nobody. A health care power of attorney grants a named agent the power to make medical decisions on the person's behalf, and that agent may use the living will to guide those decisions. Both are legal documents; neither is a medical order.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are finger-pricks not performed on neonates?
opciones: Puncturing the fingers of neonates can cause nerve damage
Neonatal fingers have no capillary bed close to the surface
The fingerprint lines are not formed, so the lancet cannot be oriented
Neonatal fingers are callused from grasping and flow is poor
preguntas.explicacion: Nerve damage if the fingers of neonates are punctured is a listed complication of capillary sampling. That is consistent with the site table, which assigns the heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and 3 to 10 kg, and the finger-prick only over 6 months and 10 kg. Calluses are the concern for the feet of children who are already walking.

preguntas.pregunta: An order calls for an intramuscular injection, and the same note mentions an intercostal muscle. Which pair of meanings is right?
opciones: Intra- is within and inter- is between
Intra- is between and inter- is within
Intra- is within and inter- is beneath
Intra- is beyond and inter- is between
preguntas.explicacion: Intra- means within, so an intramuscular injection is placed inside the muscle. Inter- means between, so an intercostal muscle lies between the ribs. Two more from the same group are easy to confuse with them: infra- is beneath or below, and ex- and extra- carry the sense of beyond.

Whether she has somewhere quiet and private in which to take the appointment
Whether she is able to raise the camera so that it sits at the level of her eyes
Whether she has the bottles of her current medicines within reach of the screen

opciones: Yes, Medicare covers telehealth from anywhere in the country through December 31, 2027
Yes, but only if she travels to a clinic in a rural area that acts as the originating site
No, Medicare stopped covering telehealth when the public health emergency was declared over
Yes, but only for the brief virtual check-ins that last ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: Through December 31, 2027 Medicare covers telehealth services obtained from anywhere in the United States, the patient's home included. Telehealth there means care from a provider in another location using audio and video technology, or audio only in some cases, and it covers office visits, psychotherapy and consultations. E-visits through a portal and brief virtual check-ins are additional ways to communicate, not the only ones.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient wearing a fentanyl patch asks whether a heating pad may be placed over it for back pain. What is the answer?
opciones: No: heat over a patch speeds the release of the drug and has caused fatal overdoses
Yes: heat brings vasodilation, which is why it is applied over patches of every kind
Yes, as long as the previous patch is left in place while the new one is being applied
No: heat loosens the adhesive, so the patch has to be pressed down for ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Heat is sometimes used with an inunction rubbed into the skin, because vasodilation improves the blood flow and the absorption. Over a patch it is dangerous: heat increases the release of the drug, and with fentanyl or nitroglycerin patches that has caused overdose and death. Manufacturer guidance decides. Pressing for ten seconds and removing the old patch belong to how a new patch is applied.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says 'I hate needles' and begins to tremble. What does WHO step 2 direct?
opciones: Reassure the patient and ask what would make them more comfortable
Tell the patient firmly that it will not hurt at all this time
Proceed as quickly as possible before the anxiety builds further
Ask a colleague to hold the arm firmly while you perform the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says that if the patient is anxious or afraid, the health worker reassures them and asks what would make them more comfortable. Promising that it will not hurt is the false reassurance listed among therapeutic communication pitfalls, rushing ignores the patient, and holding a patient down is a paediatric immobilization technique, not a response to an anxious adult.

preguntas.pregunta: The dominant hand is now gloved. How is the second sterile glove picked up?
opciones: Four fingers together reach under the folded cuff, thumb held out so it touches nothing sterile
Thumb and index finger pinch the inside of the cuff, exactly as the first glove was lifted
The gloved palm presses down on the glove and slides it to the edge of the inner wrapper
The bare hand steadies the glove at the fingertips while the gloved hand pulls the cuff open
preguntas.explicacion: The gloved hand keeps its four fingers together and reaches under the folded cuff, on the outer surface, with the thumb held outstretched so it never brushes the second glove. The bare nondominant hand only steadies the package flap. Its fingers are then held out straight with the thumb tucked into the palm while the glove is pulled on.

preguntas.pregunta: Who may report an adverse event after a vaccination to VAERS?
opciones: Anyone; health professionals must report certain events and makers report all
Only the physician who ordered the vaccine, using the patient's medical record
Only the manufacturer, which collects reports from providers and forwards them
Only a state immunization program, which files on behalf of the practice
preguntas.explicacion: The Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, set up in 1990 and co-managed by the CDC and the FDA, accepts reports from anyone. Healthcare professionals are required to report certain adverse events, and vaccine manufacturers are required to report every event that comes to their attention. Vaccine administration errors are among the things reported, and reports are coded and entered into the database.

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague leaves a needle inserted in a medication vial's septum between doses. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: It opens a direct route for microorganisms into the vial and its contents
It counts as recapping, which the bloodborne pathogens standard prohibits
It exposes the drug to light and reduces its potency within minutes
It is acceptable in a clean medication area away from patient treatment
preguntas.explicacion: A needle is never left inserted in a vial septum for multiple uses, because it creates a direct route for microorganisms to enter the vial and contaminate the fluid; vials whose sterility is compromised or questionable are discarded. The same section asks that medications be drawn up in a designated clean area away from sinks, as close to administration time as possible. Recapping is a sharps rule about the used needle's cap, a different hazard, and the objection has nothing to do with light.

preguntas.pregunta: An order for a child calls for four different specimen types by skin puncture. What is the best approach?
opciones: Consider venipuncture, which may give more accurate results when more than two specimens are needed
Collect all four by skin puncture, starting with blood bank so the largest volume comes first
Collect two by heel-prick and two by finger-prick, so that no single site is over-punctured
Collect all four from one puncture, squeezing gently between specimens to keep the flow going
preguntas.explicacion: If more than two specimens are needed by skin puncture, venepuncture may provide more accurate laboratory results. Capillary blood also suits only a limited number of tests because of skin flora contamination and its small total volume. Squeezing dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid and raises the chance of haemolysis.

preguntas.pregunta: With an antimicrobial scrub agent, how long is the surgical hand antisepsis, and what does going past ten minutes add?
opciones: About 2 to 6 minutes, and going past ten adds no benefit while irritating the skin
About 2 to 6 minutes, and going past ten adds residual activity that lasts the case
About 8 to 12 minutes, and going past ten adds no benefit while irritating the skin
About 30 to 60 seconds, and going past ten adds a measurable drop in resident flora
preguntas.explicacion: Surgical hand antisepsis with an antimicrobial agent runs roughly two to six minutes with a sterile single-use sponge or brush, following the manufacturer and the facility. Scrubbing ten minutes or more brings no extra benefit and raises the risk of skin irritation. Routine handwashing is a different exercise, at 15 to 20 seconds.

The situation, naming what is going on with the patient
The background, giving the clinical context of the case
The recommendation, saying what should be done about it
preguntas.explicacion: SBAR carries critical information that needs attention and action right away. Situation says what is happening with the patient, background gives the clinical context, assessment states what the caller thinks the problem is, and recommendation or request says what should be done to correct it.

preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube is sent to the laboratory for a prothrombin time. Why will it be rejected?
opciones: Coagulation tests need plasma; serum has lost its clotting factors
Coagulation tests need serum; the red tube gives plasma instead
The red tube clots too slowly, beyond the 60 minutes the test allows
The clot activator in the red tube binds the calcium the test measures
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation testing is done on plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are removed when serum forms. The correct specimen is a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate, which chelates calcium and holds the sample in stasis until calcium chloride is added in the laboratory. The clot activator does not bind calcium; it does the opposite, it lets the blood clot.

preguntas.pregunta: A self-sheathing needle is an example of which type of control under the standard?
opciones: An engineering control, which isolates or removes the hazard from the workplace
A work practice control, which changes the way a task is performed
Personal protective equipment, which is used when exposure remains after controls
An administrative control, such as the annual review of the Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in paragraph (b) list self-sheathing needles, sharps disposal containers and sharps with engineered injury protections as engineering controls: devices that isolate or remove the bloodborne pathogens hazard. A work practice control alters how the task is done; the example the standard gives is banning two-handed recapping. PPE is specialized clothing or equipment worn by the employee. NIOSH's hierarchy of controls places elimination and substitution first, then work practices and administrative controls, then engineering controls, and PPE last.

preguntas.pregunta: A pharmacy plans to offer rapid antigen SARS-CoV-2 testing and nothing else. Which CLIA certificate fits?
opciones: A Certificate of Waiver, appropriate when point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 testing is the only testing done
A Certificate of Compliance, because respiratory antigen testing is moderate complexity
A PPM certificate, because the pharmacist reads the result during the visit
No certificate, because negative rapid antigen results no longer have to be reported
preguntas.explicacion: A CLIA certificate is mandatory for point-of-care testing, and a Certificate of Waiver is the appropriate one when SARS-CoV-2 point-of-care testing is the only testing performed. The site completes Form CMS-116, submits it to its state agency, pays the fee, and reports ownership, name, address or director changes within 30 days. Dropping the required reporting of negative antigen results did not remove the certificate.

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old cannot use numbers to rate pain. Which tool fits?
opciones: The Wong-Baker FACES scale, built for children who are nonverbal in acute settings
The numeric rating scale, which most children can manage from the age of four
The McGill Pain Questionnaire, whose 78 descriptors cover sensory and affective terms
The Short Form Health Survey 36, which measures quality of life across many domains
preguntas.explicacion: The FACES scale was designed for children who cannot put pain into words in an acute setting, and it can be adapted for adults with communication difficulties. Numerical scales become usable around adolescence. The questionnaires with dozens of items are self-report instruments for older patients with chronic pain.

preguntas.pregunta: The office plans to follow up with all its patients by text message. What does the toolkit warn about?
opciones: Ask each patient how they want to be contacted; do not rely on electronic means alone
Text everyone, since owning a mobile phone shows the patient accepts texting
Use secure email for everyone instead, since it is part of the patient portal
Use postal mail for everyone instead, since it reaches patients without devices

preguntas.pregunta: A 16-year-old comes to the office alone and asks to be treated without her parents being told. What decides whether she can consent for herself?
opciones: Whether she is emancipated or her state lets minors consent to that service
Whether she is able to pay for the visit herself on the day of the appointment
Whether the clinician judges that she is mature enough during the encounter
Whether a parent can be reached by telephone before the visit starts
preguntas.explicacion: Minors under 18 usually cannot consent, and the parent gives permission instead. The openings are emancipation — marriage, active military duty, or living apart and managing one's own money — and the services a state lets minors seek alone, such as contraception, care for a sexually transmitted infection, or prenatal care. preguntas.pregunta: A PR interval measures four small squares on the strip. How does that compare with normal?
opciones: It is normal: the usual range is three to five small squares
It is long: the usual range is one to three small squares
It is short: the usual range is five to seven small squares
It is long: any value past two small squares is a block
preguntas.explicacion: Each small square is 0.04 seconds, so four of them come to 160 ms. The accepted range runs from 120 to 200 ms, which is three to five small squares, so this interval sits in the middle of normal. A value held above 200 ms with every P wave conducted is what defines a first-degree block.

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient right is guaranteed by federal law, as opposed to a facility's own bill of rights?
opciones: The right to a copy of one's medical records and to keep them private
The right to receive any treatment the patient requests, regardless of medical necessity
The right to free care in any hospital that accepts Medicare
The right to choose which staff member performs each procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Some patient rights are guaranteed by federal law, notably the right to get a copy of one's medical records and to have them kept private and secure; many states add protections, and insurers, medical organizations and facilities publish their own non-enforceable bills of rights. Other common rights are respectful treatment, freedom from discrimination, the right to refuse treatment and informed consent. The CMS condition adds that the right to make informed decisions is not a mechanism to demand treatment that is medically unnecessary.

preguntas.pregunta: What does value-based care describe?
opciones: Care designed around quality, performance and patient experience
Care paid for by the visit, so that volume drives the practice income
Care limited to a network of providers and facilities under contract
Care given only after the plan approves each service in advance
preguntas.explicacion: Value-based care describes health care designed to focus on quality of care, provider performance and the patient experience, the value being what the individual values most. Doctors and other providers work together to manage a person's overall health while weighing personal health goals, coordinating tests and visits so that people can avoid the emergency department and stay out of the hospital.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a wandering baseline is correct?
opciones: It is not caused by the machine but by unstable contact
It is caused by the machine when the paper speed drifts
It is caused by the machine picking up nearby equipment
It is not caused by contact but by the patient breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Drift is the problem technicians meet most often, and the instrument is not to blame for it. The prime suspect is unstable contact between the electrode and the skin, so the fix has to happen before the recording starts: clean skin, fresh electrodes and a firm attachment.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on warfarin comes in for routine monitoring. Which test and tube are expected?
opciones: A PT/INR in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PTT test in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PT/INR in a lavender tube with EDTA
A CBC with differential in a lavender tube with EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: The PT/INR is used most often to check how well warfarin (Coumadin) is preventing clots, with the INR letting providers compare results from different laboratories, and the specimen goes in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate. preguntas.pregunta: A tracing is read against a pressure curve. When does systole begin and end?
opciones: It begins as the mitral valve shuts and ends as the aortic valve shuts
It begins as the aortic valve shuts and ends as the mitral valve shuts
It begins as the mitral valve opens and ends as the aortic valve opens
It begins as the aortic valve opens and ends as the mitral valve opens
preguntas.explicacion: Systole is the contracting and ejecting half of the cycle: it opens with closure of the mitral valve, or the tricuspid on the right, and closes with the aortic, or the pulmonic. Diastole is the mirror image, from that closure to the next, and it is when filling happens.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks orally for an electronic copy of their current hospital records. What is required?
opciones: The records in the form requested, if readily producible, within a reasonable time
A written and notarized request before any copy of the record can be released
A paper copy only, since electronic release is limited to other treating providers
A copy of everything except the current admission, which stays open until discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access covers current records, on an oral or a written request, in the form and format asked for when that is readily producible — including electronic format when the records are kept electronically — and otherwise in readable hard copy or another agreed format, within a reasonable time. The hospital must not frustrate that right.

preguntas.pregunta: The dismissed patient never signed for the certified letter and appears at the desk two months later asking to be booked. What is the guidance?
opciones: Hand her a copy of the letter or say it was mailed, and that care ended on its date
Book her, because a return receipt nobody signed leaves the notice without effect
Start the thirty days again from today, since she has only now learned of the decision
Send a second certified letter and keep seeing her until that new period runs out
preguntas.explicacion: The situation is anticipated: the patient does not sign the return receipt and then contacts the office or turns up after the period in the letter has run. She should be given a copy of the letter, or told by telephone that a letter was sent, and politely told that care ended on the date it named. Nothing in the guidance restarts the clock because the receipt came back unsigned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hands are cold and the oximeter will not settle on a value. Why?
opciones: The device needs pulsating blood, and cold and poor perfusion flatten that signal
The device needs a warm sensor, and the cold skin cools the light emitter itself
The device needs venous blood, and cold shifts the reading toward the arterial side
The device needs a still finger, and the cold makes the patient's hand tremble
preguntas.explicacion: The reading depends on a pulsating vascular bed, so anything that flattens the pulse wave defeats it: severe hypotension, cold extremities, Raynaud disease and excessive movement. Readings are also less accurate at cold temperatures, and a skin temperature near 33 °C (91.4 °F) is given as the level needed for reliable values.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: When can a person apply for Medicaid or CHIP coverage?
opciones: At any time of year, since these programs have no yearly enrollment window
Only from November 1 to January 15, the Marketplace enrollment window
Only within 60 days of a qualifying life event such as a birth or a move
Only during the seven months around the applicant's sixty-fifth birthday
preguntas.explicacion: Applications for Medicaid and CHIP are taken all year, and coverage can begin immediately for those who qualify. The window from November 1 to January 15 is Marketplace open enrollment; the 60-day rule belongs to Special Enrollment Periods for Marketplace plans; and the 7-month period around the 65th birthday is the Initial Enrollment Period for Medicare.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care described when a malpractice claim is judged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician of similar training would give in like cases
The care described in the manufacturer's instructions for the device used
The care the best specialist in the state would have given the same patient
The care the patient expected after reading the practice's own brochures
preguntas.explicacion: The defendant's actions are measured against the standard of care for that diagnosis and situation: the reasonable and ordinary care, skill and diligence that clinicians in good standing, with the same general line of practice, ordinarily exercise in like cases. National boards have flattened much of the old regional variation, though access in rural or underserved areas is the occasional exception.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient loses consciousness during a draw. Which set of findings fits a vasovagal episode while it is happening?
opciones: Slow pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and dry warm skin
Slow pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and a bitten tongue
preguntas.explicacion: During the event the patient is typically bradycardic and hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic, and consciousness returns without help. A bitten tongue points instead towards a seizure, which is why it is looked for afterwards along with any sign of injury from a fall.

preguntas.pregunta: A payer is refusing to accept the adopted electronic claim format. Where can a practice report that?
opciones: To the enforcement and testing tool that takes administrative simplification complaints
To the clearinghouse, which is obliged to report the payer to the standards body
To the code set maintainer, which decides whether the payer's format is acceptable
To the state insurance department, which enforces the electronic transaction rules
preguntas.explicacion: Complaints about possible violations of the transaction standards go through the Administrative Simplification Enforcement and Testing Tool, and the same route takes complaints about the payment, remittance advice and funds transfer standards. The code set maintainers handle requests for new or revised codes rather than enforcement, and the standards themselves are federal rather than a state matter.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two plasma glucose measurements define a standard 75-g OGTT for diagnosing type 2 diabetes?
opciones: Fasting and 2 hours after the load
Fasting and 1 hour after the load
1 hour and 3 hours after the load
30 minutes and 2 hours after the load
preguntas.explicacion: Venous plasma glucose is measured fasting and two hours after the oral load, and the 2-hour value is the one that makes the diagnosis: under 140 mg/dL is normal, 140 to 199 is impaired glucose tolerance and 200 or more is diabetes. Some protocols draw every 30 to 60 minutes for up to three hours, and a 1-hour reference (under 200) exists, but the diagnostic pair is fasting plus 2 hours.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Testing Procedures and Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings; MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), Normal Results

preguntas.pregunta: How many readings are needed before hypertension is diagnosed?
opciones: Three or more measurements taken at separate visits, when that is feasible
Two measurements taken one minute apart during a single office visit
One measurement, provided the cuff was the right size and the arm supported
Three measurements taken during one visit, five minutes apart from each other
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be done, three or more readings at separate visits are used to confirm the diagnosis. Taking two or three at one sitting is good practice for a single visit's value, but it does not settle the diagnosis. White-coat and masked hypertension are common, so home or ambulatory monitoring may be considered too.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: A bedridden patient is repositioned every couple of hours. What is that meant to prevent?
opciones: Pressure injuries, foot drop and contractures, while keeping the body in alignment
Orthostatic hypotension, which appears when a patient stands after lying flat
Aspiration during tube feeding, which is the reason the head of the bed goes up
Compartment syndrome of the leg, which follows long periods in leg supports
preguntas.explicacion: Turning a patient who cannot turn themselves keeps the body in alignment and heads off pressure injuries, foot drop and contractures, with pillows, rolls and blankets used as supports. Care is taken not to leave a patient lying on an arm, which can cause a neurological injury. Raising the head of the bed is what guards against aspiration.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients

preguntas.pregunta: What is the average reading level of adults in the United States?
opciones: About 8th or 9th grade
About 5th or 6th grade
About 11th or 12th grade
About 3rd or 4th grade
preguntas.explicacion: Adults in the United States read on average at an 8th or 9th grade level, and nearly a quarter have low literacy while a third have low numeracy. Health education material is often written well above that average, which leaves half of adults struggling with it.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 11: Assess, Select, and Create Easy-to-Understand Materials

preguntas.pregunta: What separates pharmacokinetics from pharmacodynamics?
opciones: Pharmacokinetics follows absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion of the drug
Pharmacokinetics examines the effect the drug produces on the body and its target organs
Pharmacokinetics weighs the indications and contraindications that decide the prescription
Pharmacokinetics measures how much of a dose survives the first pass through the liver
preguntas.explicacion: Pharmacokinetics studies how the body handles a drug for the whole time it is present, and it is examined through four parameters: absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. Pharmacodynamics is the mirror image, the effect the drug has on the body. Understanding both is what lets a prescriber choose the dose with the greatest benefit and the least risk, and adjust it as a patient's physiology demands.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pharmacokinetics", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k21 · RMA III.G.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: In a published table of critical limits for urgent clinician notification, which adult glucose values require the physician to be notified immediately?
opciones: Below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L) or above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L)
Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or above 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L)
Below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) or above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L)
Below 25 mg/dL (1.3 mmol/L) or above 600 mg/dL (33.3 mmol/L)
preguntas.explicacion: The table of adult and pediatric critical limits sets glucose at below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L), where neuroglycopenic symptoms up to loss of consciousness occur, and above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L), the range of diabetic coma with osmotic diuresis and ketoacidosis; the limits apply after confirmation by repeat measurement in the same sample. The other pairs mix thresholds from elsewhere: 70 and 54 mg/dL mark hypoglycemia levels, 25 mg/dL is the neonatal limit, and 600 mg/dL characterizes the hyperosmolar state.

preguntas.pregunta: The WHO pre-draw interview asks specifically about allergies to which three items?
opciones: Latex, povidone iodine and tape
Latex, alcohol and chlorhexidine
Bananas, avocado and kiwi
Vinyl, silicone and neoprene
preguntas.explicacion: The Annex C interview asks whether the patient is allergic to anything and tells the health worker to ask specifically about latex, povidone iodine and tape. Bananas, avocado and kiwi are the fruits of the latex-fruit syndrome, a reason to probe further rather than the question itself, and vinyl, silicone and neoprene are the latex alternatives used once an allergy is known.

preguntas.pregunta: After a stressful day at work a man lashes out at his family at home. Which defense mechanism is that?
opciones: Displacement, shifting the reaction to another target
Projection, attributing one's own impulses to somebody else
Regression, dropping back to an earlier developmental level
Rationalization, justifying the behavior with a reasoned account
preguntas.explicacion: Displacement transfers an emotional burden or reaction from one target onto another, and the example given is exactly this one. Projection assigns your own maladaptive impulses to another person, regression returns behavior to an earlier stage, and rationalization supplies a reasonable-sounding justification.

preguntas.pregunta: In which situation is a non-fasting lipid profile acceptable?
opciones: Initial risk estimation in an untreated primary-prevention patient
Establishing the diagnosis of hypertriglyceridemia in a patient
Following a patient with a family history of genetic hyperlipidemia
Assessing a patient who is at risk for pancreatitis or has it
preguntas.explicacion: Two situations sit on the non-fasting side: initial risk estimation of an untreated primary-prevention patient, and clarifying the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. The other three options are on the list of cases where fasting is preferred or mandatory, together with residual risk estimation in treated patients. The clinical question decides whether the patient fasts.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the ADA guidance define an 'undue burden' that excuses a particular aid or service?
opciones: Significant difficulty or expense, judged against the entity's resources
Any cost that exceeds the fee the entity charges for the service in question
Any request made with less than 24 hours of advance notice
Any aid the patient did not ask for in writing before the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Undue burden means significant difficulty or expense, weighed against the resources of the entity, and even then another effective aid must be offered if one exists. Reasonable advance notice may be required but not excessive notice, and walk-in requests are honoured to the extent possible; nothing ties the duty to a written request or to the price of the visit.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep the tube holder and pulls the used needle off it with a gloved hand. Which rule does this break?
opciones: Under OSHA, contaminated needles are removed only by a mechanical device or one-handed technique, when no alternative is feasible
Under OSHA, contaminated needles may be removed by hand as long as clean gloves are worn and the tube holder is disinfected afterwards
The WHO allows removal by hand provided the needle is dropped into a sharps container that is within arm's reach
Removal by hand is permitted when the holder is reused on the same patient within two minutes
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) prohibits bending, recapping or removing contaminated needles unless the employer can show no alternative is feasible or a specific medical procedure requires it, and then only with a mechanical device or a one-handed technique; shearing or breaking is always prohibited. WHO Annex E says an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and Chapter 3 prefers discarding barrel and needle together.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)(A)-(B); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex E

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with heart failure breathes in cycles that build up, fade away and then pause before starting again. Which pattern is charted?
opciones: Cheyne-Stokes respiration, a crescendo and decrescendo cycle with apneic gaps
Kussmaul respiration, deep and rapid breaths that keep an even depth throughout
Hyperventilation, rapid deep breathing that carries the carbon dioxide too low
Obstructive sleep apnea, in which snoring and shallow breaths alternate in sleep
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing that swells, fades and then stops for a moment before the next cycle is Cheyne-Stokes respiration. It is seen in heart failure and with raised intracranial pressure, and it carries a poor prognosis. The pattern is described in the chart along with the rate, because the rate alone would miss it.

preguntas.pregunta: After a needle has been re-sheathed with the scoop technique on a work surface, what is the next step?
opciones: Disinfect the surface, so no blood is left behind on it
Rinse the surface with water and dry it with a paper towel
Cover the surface with fresh paper until the session ends
Leave the surface as it is until the end of the working shift
preguntas.explicacion: The manoeuvre is carried out close to a sharps container and the needle is discarded immediately afterwards. Because the cap was resting on the surface, that surface is then cleaned with disinfectant so that no blood is left on it. An exposed used needle is never taken apart by hand.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the technique call for repeating height, length and head circumference twice?
opciones: So two readings agree within 0.2 cm, and the average of the closest two is recorded
So the second reading can replace the first, which is treated as a practice attempt
So the larger of the two readings is charted, since the smaller one loses posture
So each reading can be taken by a different person and compared for agreement
preguntas.explicacion: Each of these measurements is taken twice and the two have to fall within 0.2 cm or 0.25 inches of one another; the average of the two closest values is what goes in the record. Head and waist circumferences vary more than height and weight and are the ones most prone to measurement error.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: What does the light green PST contain, and what kind of sample does it provide?
opciones: Lithium heparin plus a gel separator; plasma for chemistries
Sodium heparin without gel; plasma for lithium and ammonia levels
A clot activator plus a gel separator; serum for chemistries
Potassium oxalate plus sodium fluoride; plasma for glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 describes the PST as a light green tube with lithium heparin anticoagulant and a gel separator, whose gel separates the plasma at the bottom of the tube; its use is chemistries. The dark green tube holds sodium or lithium heparin without gel, the serum separator tube has gel but no anticoagulant and gives serum, and oxalate with fluoride is the grey glucose tube.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a monofilament suture behave compared with a braided multifilament one?
opciones: It has more memory and needs more knots, but passes through tissue with less reaction
It has less memory and needs fewer knots, but passes through tissue with more reaction
It has more memory and needs more knots, and it fractures far more readily under tension
It has less memory and holds knots better, and it carries more surface area for bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: A monofilament is a single strand with less surface area. It carries more memory, meaning it springs back toward its packaged shape and its knots loosen more easily, so it usually needs extra throws; but it slides through tissue more easily, causes less inflammatory reaction and fractures less than a braid. Multifilaments handle better and hold knots, at the cost of friction, capillarity and infection risk.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Staff say there is no time to answer a patient's emotional concerns. What have studies found about that?
opciones: Consultation time changes only marginally when empathy is shown
Consultation time roughly doubles once emotions are addressed
Consultations run long enough to need a second appointment
Consultation time drops because patients then say much less
preguntas.explicacion: The concern about time is not supported. Physicians who gave an empathic response showed only a marginal change in consultation length, and better communication skills were not associated with longer consultations; one observational study put the difference at about 21 seconds. Communication ability is rated by patients as at least as important as technical competence.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: Which goal belongs to the Affordable Care Act as its own text describes it?
opciones: Expanding Medicaid to adults with income below 138% of the poverty level
Expanding Medicare to adults with income below 138% of the poverty level
Replacing employer coverage with a single federal plan for every worker
Setting a national fee schedule that every private insurer has to follow
preguntas.explicacion: The law enacted in March 2010 has three stated goals: make coverage affordable for more people through subsidies for households between 100% and 400% of the poverty level, expand Medicaid to adults with income below 138% of that level, and support delivery methods that lower costs. Not every state took the expansion. Medicare eligibility rests on age and disability, and the law created no single federal plan or universal fee schedule.

preguntas.pregunta: Why might a clinician listen to the heart while palpating a peripheral pulse at the same time?
opciones: To see whether every ventricular contraction produces a beat that can be felt
To confirm that the stethoscope and the palpating fingers agree on the rhythm term
To measure the delay between the heart sound and the wave arriving at the wrist
To decide which of the two sides of the body carries the stronger pulse volume
preguntas.explicacion: Doing both at once answers a specific question: does each contraction of the ventricle reach the periphery as a palpable beat? Contractions that do not produce a felt beat will be missed by counting at the wrist alone, which is why the two are compared when the finding is in doubt.

preguntas.pregunta: During severe hypotension the head of the bed is tilted below the level of the feet. Which position is that?
opciones: Trendelenburg, which is used to promote venous return to the head and heart
Reverse Trendelenburg, which leaves the head as the highest point of the trunk
High Fowler, with the head of the bed raised to between 60 and 90 degrees
Lateral decubitus, with the patient turned onto the side that is not operated
preguntas.explicacion: Trendelenburg is a supine variant with the bed tipped head down so that the pubic symphysis becomes the highest point of the trunk. It is used to increase venous return in emergencies and to improve exposure in abdominal and laparoscopic surgery. Its costs are real: raised intracranial and intraocular pressure, and facial and airway swelling if held too long.

preguntas.pregunta: Staff verify a returning patient online by asking for her date of birth and her mother's maiden name. What does the FTC say about that choice?
opciones: Those details are not reliable authenticators, because they are so easily obtained
Those details are the two identifiers the safety goal asks for before a procedure
Those details satisfy the rule, because they were collected on the intake form
Those details may be used once the patient has signed the privacy acknowledgment
preguntas.explicacion: For existing accounts the program may include reasonable procedures to confirm who it is dealing with, watch transactions and check the validity of address changes, and for online authentication the guidance points to multi-factor techniques with passwords, PINs, smart cards, tokens and biometrics. A Social Security number, date of birth, mother's maiden name or mailing address is not.

preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine was collected at 9:00 a.m., but the office analyzer is down and the specimen cannot be tested until 3:00 p.m. What should be done with it?
opciones: Refrigerate it at 4 °C; a refrigerated specimen can still be tested up to 24 hours after collection
Keep it at room temperature with the lid closed; urine is stable for 8 hours if it is not agitated
Freeze it right away; freezing stops the breakdown of cells and casts until the analyzer is repaired
Discard it and recollect; urine cannot be used for a dipstick more than 2 hours after it is voided
preguntas.explicacion: Urine should ideally be examined within the first hour after collection because cells, casts and crystals are unstable. When that is not possible, the specimen is refrigerated at 4 °C, which slows decomposition, and it remains usable for up to 24 hours; anything older than 24 hours cannot be used for urinalysis. Leaving it at room temperature favors bacterial growth, and freezing is not the described alternative.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO order of draw for plastic vacuum tubes, what position does the light blue coagulation tube occupy?

First, before the blood culture bottle and any other tube
Second, right after the blood culture bottle and before any plain tube
Fourth, after the culture bottle, the plain tube and the red clot activator
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 places the blood culture bottle first, a non-additive tube second and the light blue sodium citrate tube third. The red clot activator tube follows in fourth place. Candidates often remember the citrate tube as the first tube because many draws have no culture and no plain tube, but the table itself puts two positions ahead of it.

preguntas.pregunta: Staples were placed in a patient's scalp laceration. About when are they removed, and why not later?
opciones: About one week, because leaving them longer marks the skin with punctate train-track scars
About three weeks, because scalp wounds carry more tension than any other site on the body
About three days, because the scalp is so vascular that it has already closed by then
About one week, because after that the staple metal begins to corrode against the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Staples suit linear lacerations of the scalp and extremities and go in fast, which helps with brisk bleeding or several wounds at once. On the scalp they come out at roughly a week, since leaving them longer produces the characteristic punctate train-track marks along the line. They approximate edges less precisely than sutures but evert them well.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant's certification lapsed last year but she still signs her name with the initials. What is that?
opciones: Unethical, and a misrepresentation of a credential she no longer holds
Acceptable, as long as she is working toward reinstating the credential
Acceptable, because the exam she passed years ago cannot be undone
Unethical, but permitted while the reinstatement application is pending
preguntas.explicacion: Publicly displaying the certification title, or using the initials after one's name, once the credential has expired is treated as unethical and as a misrepresentation. preguntas.pregunta: Before booking an imaging study, staff contact the insurer for its decision on medical necessity. What limits does that decision carry?
opciones: It is not a promise that the plan will pay the cost of the service
It removes the need for a referral from the patient's primary care doctor
It fixes the amount the patient will owe once the study has been performed
It obliges the imaging center to accept the amount the plan decides to pay
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the insurer's decision that a service, treatment plan, prescription drug or item of durable medical equipment is medically necessary. A plan may require it before certain services, except in an emergency, and it is sometimes called prior authorization, prior approval or precertification. The glossary states plainly that obtaining it is not a promise of payment.

preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's arm carries a fistula with a palpable vibration under the fingertips. What does that vibration mean, and what is avoided on that arm?
opciones: A thrill, meaning the fistula is patent; draws, venous access and cuff readings are avoided
A thrill, meaning the fistula has clotted; draws and cuff readings may go ahead as usual
A pulsation, meaning the fistula is patent; only intravenous fluids are avoided on that arm
A pulsation, meaning steal syndrome has begun; the arm is used only for capillary sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the fingertips lightly over a fistula picks up a thrill, a vibration that means the fistula is open, and a thrill is distinguished from a merely pulsating fistula. To protect veins for dialysis, peripheral access, blood draws and blood pressure readings are kept off that side.

preguntas.pregunta: For a spun microhematocrit, at what speed and for how long is the sealed capillary tube centrifuged?
opciones: 11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes
Roughly 3,000 rpm for 25 to 30 minutes
11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 10 to 15 minutes
1,500 to 2,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: In the microhematocrit method blood is drawn into a capillary tube about 75 mm long and 1 mm in diameter, both ends are sealed with clay or heat, and the tube is spun at 11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes before being read on the holder scale or a card reader. The 3,000 rpm, 30-minute spin belongs to the older macrohematocrit method with a Wintrobe tube, which the capillary method has largely replaced.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: Under section 330 of the Public Health Service Act, which requirement must a center meet to be certified as an FQHC?
opciones: Offer a sliding fee scale to people with incomes below 200% of the poverty guidelines
Keep no more than 25 inpatient beds, counting swing beds, the way a rural hospital does
Sit more than a 35-mile drive on primary roads away from any other hospital or clinic
Report an annual average acute inpatient length of stay of 96 hours or less each year
preguntas.explicacion: Certification asks for comprehensive services with ongoing quality assurance, compliance with health and safety rules, and no approval as a rural health clinic. Section 330 adds three conditions: serving a designated underserved area or population, a sliding fee scale below 200% of the poverty guidelines, and a board most of whose members get care there. Bed and mileage limits belong to critical access hospitals.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006397 Federally Qualified Health Center: Certification

preguntas.pregunta: Which needle is recommended for venipuncture in a paediatric patient, and which gauge is avoided?
opciones: A 23-gauge winged steel needle (butterfly) with extension tubing; avoid 25 gauge or thinner because of haemolysis
A 21-gauge straight multisample needle on a tube holder; avoid 23 gauge because it collapses small veins
A 25-gauge winged steel needle (butterfly), which the WHO prefers because it is the least painful in children
A 23-gauge hypodermic needle on an auto-disable syringe; avoid butterflies because of air in the tubing
preguntas.explicacion: For paediatric venepuncture the needle is a winged steel needle, preferably 23 gauge, with an extension tube; gauges of 25 or more of 25 or more are avoided because they may be associated with an increased risk of haemolysis. The butterfly is used with a syringe or an evacuated tube with an adaptor. Auto-disable syringes are designed for injection and are not appropriate for phlebotomy.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Equipment and supplies for paediatric patients

preguntas.pregunta: How does the viscosity of blood compare with that of water, and what does that viscosity affect?
opciones: Roughly five times that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly twice that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly five times that of water; it lowers resistance to flow
Roughly the same as water, since plasma is 92 percent water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is viscous and sticky, with a viscosity about five times that of water, owing to the plasma proteins and the formed elements. Viscosity is resistance to flow, and it has a dramatic effect on blood pressure and flow: honey resists flow more than water, and blood behaves the same way relative to water. Plasma being mostly water does not make whole blood flow like water.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to give a sputum culture mentions he is on an antibiotic. What is the correct response?
opciones: Record it and tell the provider, since antibiotics can affect bacterial growth in the culture
Tell him to skip today's dose, since antibiotics can affect the bacterial growth in the culture
Ignore it, since antibiotics reach the bloodstream and not the airway secretions
Postpone the collection for 4 weeks, the interval used before a urea breath test
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics can suppress the growth the culture depends on, so the medication is documented and reported; the patient is told not to stop anything unless the provider says so. That is the same rule as in urine culture, where recent antibiotics can produce a false negative. The four-week hold belongs to the urea breath test for Helicobacter pylori.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture (003751), Considerations

preguntas.pregunta: Under a diagnosis-related group payment, what does a hospital receive for two patients with the same diagnosis but different lengths of stay?
opciones: The same payment, since the amount follows the diagnosis rather than the days
A larger payment for the longer stay, since each extra day is billed separately
A payment adjusted daily, since the group sets a rate for each day of care
A payment set after discharge from the charges the hospital actually billed
preguntas.explicacion: The diagnosis-related group pays a single amount for the hospitalization, built from the average cost of treating that condition and adjusted for factors such as teaching hospitals or a large uninsured caseload. Patients with the same diagnosis bring the same payment whether the stay is long or short, which was designed to push efficiency and remove the incentive to over-treat.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pay for Performance and Value-Based Care", Summary
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CMAA 6 k82 · CCMA 1 k6

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of values is read as abnormal on the 3-hour, 100 g glucose tolerance test in pregnancy?
opciones: Fasting 95, 1 hour 180, 2 hours 155, 3 hours 140 mg/dL
Fasting 92, 1 hour 180, 2 hours 153, 3 hours 140 mg/dL
Fasting 95, 1 hour 155, 2 hours 180, 3 hours 140 mg/dL
Fasting 99, 1 hour 200, 2 hours 140, 3 hours 126 mg/dL
preguntas.explicacion: The 100 g test is abnormal at 95 mg/dL or more fasting, 180 or more at one hour, 155 or more at two hours and 140 or more at three hours. The 92 / 180 / 153 trio belongs to the one-step 75 g test, which stops at two hours and has no third value. Fasting 60 to 99, under 200 at one hour and under 140 at two hours are the nonpregnant reference figures, a different scale altogether.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), What Abnormal Results Mean; StatPearls, "Gestational Diabetes", Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: Which instruction protects a patient's fingers after a cast is put on the arm?
opciones: Keep rings off that hand until the provider says it is safe to wear them
Keep rings on that hand so that any swelling can be judged against them
Keep the arm below heart level so that the fingers stay warm and pink
Keep the fingers still inside the cast until the follow-up visit is over
preguntas.explicacion: Swelling works its way down the limb and a ring can become a tourniquet on a finger or toe, so rings come off until the provider says otherwise. The limb is rested and propped above the level of the heart, and ice helps in the first days. Swelling, redness, numbness, a cast that feels too tight or too loose, or a bad smell are all reasons to call.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Closed reduction of a fractured bone - aftercare — Self-care at Home
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.c · CCMA 3B14 k64 · NCMA 2B.13

preguntas.pregunta: A patient under 65 has Medicare because of a disability and works for an employer with 60 employees. Who pays first?
opciones: Medicare pays first, since the employer has fewer than 100 employees
The group health plan pays first, since the employer has 20 or more employees
Medicare pays first, since entitlement based on disability always comes first
The group health plan pays first, since the patient is younger than 65 years
preguntas.explicacion: When Medicare entitlement rests on disability, the group health plan pays first only if the employer has 100 or more employees; below that number Medicare is primary. The 20-employee threshold is the one used for patients 65 or older. Disability by itself does not settle the order, and neither does age: the size of the employer is what decides it in both rules.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1

preguntas.pregunta: Under chain of custody rules, when is a sample considered to be in custody?
opciones: In the authorized custodian's own possession, in a secured place
In a locked laboratory refrigerator, whoever holds the key to it
In the courier's vehicle, once the transport form has been signed
In the collector's work area, as long as the seals stay unbroken
preguntas.explicacion: A sample is deemed to be in custody when it is in the authorized custodian's actual physical possession, in a secured place, without access by unauthorized personnel and with no opportunity for tampering. Both halves matter: an unattended specimen in a room others can enter is not in custody, and neither is one held by somebody who never signed for it on the form.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Custody of the Evidence

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the cardiac impulse pause for about 100 milliseconds at the AV node?
opciones: So the atria complete their contraction before the ventricles begin
So the ventricles finish contracting before the atria start to refill
So the SA node can reset itself before the next sinus rhythm begins
So the Purkinje fibers reach the apex ahead of the two bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The AV node's small cells and less efficient junctions slow the impulse, so it takes about 100 ms to cross the node, and this pause is critical: it lets the atrial muscle finish contracting and pumping blood into the ventricles before the ventricles themselves are stimulated. The cardiac skeleton blocks any other route from atria to ventricles, so the AV node is the only gateway.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Atrioventricular (AV) Node

preguntas.pregunta: Before opening an instrument tray for a procedure, what is checked on the outside of the container?
opciones: The plastic lock and its indicator change, the Julian date and load number, and any moisture
The plastic lock and its indicator change, the expiration date, and the weight of the set
The name of the operator, the load number, and the temperature printout from the cycle
The filter color, the Julian date, and the biological indicator sealed inside the container
preguntas.explicacion: The outside check is threefold: a plastic lock showing an indicator change, a label with the Julian date and load number, and confirmation it is the right set. The container is then looked over for moisture or condensation, and if there is any, that set is put aside and another retrieved. The internal indicator is found later, after gowning and gloving.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has followed a strict low-carbohydrate diet for a week before an OGTT. Why is that a problem?
opciones: The test requires 3 days of unrestricted diet with at least 150 g of carbohydrate a day
The test requires 3 days of fasting so that glycogen stores are emptied first
The test requires a low-carbohydrate diet only on the day before, not for a week
The test requires the same diet the patient will follow after diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: For at least three days before the OGTT the patient must eat an unrestricted diet containing 150 g or more of carbohydrate per day, keep normal activity and avoid unusual or vigorous exercise; a week of carbohydrate restriction invalidates the conditions of the test. The only fast is the 10- to 16-hour one immediately before the morning of the test. MedlinePlus puts it simply: eat normally for several days beforehand.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Testing Procedures and Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: The allowed amount for an office visit is $100 and the plan's coinsurance is 20%. The patient has already met the deductible. What does she owe?
opciones: $20, and the plan pays the rest of the allowed amount for that visit
$80, and the plan pays the rest of the allowed amount for that visit
$100, because coinsurance applies only after the visit has been billed
$120, because the coinsurance is added on top of the allowed amount
preguntas.explicacion: Coinsurance is the patient's percentage of the allowed amount once the deductible is satisfied: 20% of $100 comes to $20, and the plan covers the remainder. The $80 figure inverts the shares. Paying the whole $100 is what happens before the deductible is met, not after. Nothing is added above the allowed amount by a contracted provider, since that ceiling is the negotiated price.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which activity should patients avoid while fasting for a blood test?
opciones: Chewing gum during the fasting hours
Drinking plain water during the fasting hours
Taking a medicine the provider said to continue
Brushing teeth within 30 minutes of the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Besides not eating or drinking anything but plain water, there are three things not to do while fasting: chew gum, smoke, or exercise. Plain water is allowed, and usual medicines are continued unless the provider says to stop. The 30-minute rule about brushing and flossing belongs to the cortisol saliva test, not to a blood draw.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section What is fasting for a blood test
