preguntas.pregunta: A blood sample for potassium and glucose was drawn from the arm carrying a dextrose infusion, through the IV catheter as it was placed. Which two problems does the literature attach to this practice?
opciones: Higher hemolysis from flow through the narrow catheter, and contamination by the infusion fluid
Formation of fibrin clots in the serum, and dilution of the anticoagulant in the tube
Falsely low potassium from the catheter material, and bacterial contamination of the tube
Air bubbles that lower the blood gas values, and loss of vacuum in the evacuated tube
preguntas.explicacion: Draws from indwelling catheters or during IV starts are more prone to hemolysis than venipuncture, which the study links to flow through the narrow tube, and samples contaminated by intravenous infusion were 2.2 % of that laboratory's rejections. The critical-limits paper adds the classic example: a glucose drawn through a catheter used for glucose infusion produces a seemingly critical value that a properly collected sample clears up.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion; PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introductory text
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room falls to the floor with jerking of all four limbs. What should the assistant do first?
opciones: Clear the area of furniture and sharp objects and cushion the head
Hold the arms and legs still so that the patient does not get hurt
Slide a padded tongue blade between the teeth to protect the tongue
Lift the patient onto the exam table where the jerking can be watched
preguntas.explicacion: The whole goal during a convulsion is to keep the patient from being injured: furniture and sharp objects are moved away, the head is cushioned, and tight clothing is loosened, especially at the neck. The patient is not held down, nothing is put between the teeth, and the patient is not moved unless the spot itself is dangerous.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", Home Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: Which activities count as INTERNAL quality assessment at a waived testing site?
opciones: Reviewing QC records, test results and temperature logs, and documenting problems with a plan to fix them
Subscribing to a PT program and exchanging samples with another site using the same method
Undergoing a voluntary inspection by peers or consultants who evaluate practices and records
Receiving the manufacturer's technical bulletin and posting it in the testing area
preguntas.explicacion: Internal assessment is done by the staff who perform and oversee testing: performing and documenting QC, reviewing QC records and results, checking room and refrigerator temperature logs for completeness, and documenting and reviewing problems and injury or incident reports with an improvement plan. External assessment brings in an outside party: voluntary inspections, PT subscriptions and sample exchanges.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Quality Assessment (internal and external)

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the room kept at a comfortable temperature for a recording?
opciones: Shivering alters the tracing, so the patient must be warm
Cold skin holds less gel, so the electrodes come loose
Cold raises the heart rate, so the rate reads too high
Cold slows the paper, so the squares stand for less time
preguntas.explicacion: Any movement changes what is recorded, and shivering counts as movement, so being relaxed and warm is part of the preparation. Keeping the room temperature right is listed alongside removing metal objects and identifying the electrode sites before the patient lies down.

preguntas.pregunta: A manifestation code carries a code first note. How are the two codes sequenced?
opciones: The underlying condition is sequenced first and the manifestation second
The manifestation is sequenced first and the underlying condition second
Either order is acceptable as long as both codes appear on the claim
Only the manifestation is reported, since it names the condition treated
preguntas.explicacion: In the etiology and manifestation convention, the underlying condition is sequenced first and the manifestation follows. The etiology code carries a use additional code note and the manifestation code a code first note; manifestation titles usually end in diseases classified elsewhere, and such codes are never allowed as the first-listed or principal diagnosis, so they cannot stand alone.

preguntas.pregunta: An intradermal injection is about to be given. How is the needle held and inserted?
opciones: Bevel up, almost flat on the skin, entering at an angle of 5 to 15 degrees
Bevel up, held like a dart, entering at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees
Bevel down, almost flat on the skin, entering at 5 to 15 degrees
Bevel down, held like a dart, entering straight in at 90 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe is held between thumb and forefinger with the bevel up and the needle almost flat against the skin, entering at 5 to 15 degrees, and it advances no more than an eighth of an inch, just far enough to cover the bevel. Bevel up lets the needle pierce smoothly and puts the medication into the dermis. The dart grip and the 45 to 90 degree range belong to subcutaneous and intramuscular injections.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.4: Administering Intradermal Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(7) · RMA III.G.2.a(iii) · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: What distance separates direct droplet transmission from airborne transmission in the microbiology definition?
opciones: About one meter: droplets travel a meter or less; airborne goes farther
About three meters: droplets travel three meters or less
About six feet: droplets travel six feet or less; airborne travels farther
There is no distance; the difference is whether a mask was worn
preguntas.explicacion: When a person coughs or sneezes, droplets of mucus that may carry pathogens are ejected; direct droplet transmission covers distances of one meter or less and is treated as a form of contact transmission, while transmission over more than one meter is called airborne and is classed as vehicle transmission through the air. Fine droplets can stay suspended, travel far, and dry into droplet nuclei; tuberculosis is the classic airborne example, needing as few as 10 organisms to infect. The 3 to 6 feet figure is the clinical rule of thumb for Droplet Precautions, a different framework.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Contact Transmission and Vehicle Transmission
preguntas.subtema: Droplet vs airborne · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a federal drug test reads 27°C three minutes after the void. What does the collector do?
opciones: Collect a second specimen under direct observation and send both for testing
Warm the container in the hand and read the temperature again in four minutes
Discard the specimen and start over with the ordinary collection procedure
Accept it and write the reading on the remarks line of the custody form
preguntas.explicacion: A reading outside 32° to 38°C is marked as out of range on the form, and the collector then performs a second collection under direct observation, sending both specimens to an HHS-certified laboratory rather than to an instrumented initial test facility. A comment goes on the remarks line as well, but the comment alone does not make the specimen acceptable, and rewarming it is not an option.
preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection step 14b
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen temperature · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with celiac disease keeps having symptoms even though she buys only gluten-free products. What should be explored first?
opciones: Cross-contact, where gluten reaches her food during storage or preparation
Cross-reaction, where gluten-free grains trigger the same immune response
Tolerance, which builds up so that gluten-free products stop working
Lactase deficiency, which is what actually causes celiac symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Cross-contact happens when foods or products holding gluten touch gluten-free food, which makes that food unsafe for her. It can occur while food is grown, processed, stored, prepared or served, so gluten-free items are kept and cooked apart from the rest of the household's food.
preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for Celiac Disease — Cross-contact
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(e) · CMAA 2G

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist stuck by a used needle agrees to have her blood drawn but refuses HIV testing that day. What does the standard require of the sample?
opciones: Keep it at least 90 days so the employee may still choose to have it tested for HIV
Test it for HIV anyway, since consent to the blood draw covers the serologic testing
Discard it, since HIV testing requires a fresh sample drawn after consent is given
Keep it 30 days, the period in which the written opinion has to be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(iii)(B) separates the two consents. If the employee agrees to baseline collection but not, at that moment, to HIV serology, the sample is preserved for at least 90 days; should she decide within those 90 days to have it tested, the test is run as soon as feasible. Testing without her consent is not allowed, and throwing the sample away would defeat the purpose of the rule. The written opinion has its own deadline, 15 days, and is unrelated to the storage period.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(3)(iii)(A) and (B), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Baseline sample and consent · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient cannot swallow a tablet. Which alternative oral forms of the same drug might be available?
opciones: A suspension or solution, a chewable tablet, or a tablet that dissolves in the mouth
A suppository, a transdermal patch, or an aerosol delivered through a spacer device
An extended-release tablet, a filter needle preparation, or a multi-dose vial product
A sublingual tablet only, since no other form suits a patient who cannot swallow
preguntas.explicacion: One drug is often supplied in several forms for the same route: acetaminophen alone comes as a tablet, a chewable tablet, a capsule, a suspension or solution, an extended-release tablet and an orally disintegrating tablet. Amoxicillin comes as a capsule, a tablet, a chewable tablet and a suspension. The FDA's list of accepted dosage form terms runs from aerosol and elixir through lotion, ointment, patch and suppository.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Acetaminophen and Amoxicillin: How should this medicine be used?; FDA, Dosage Forms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k18 · CCMA 3B k86 · RMA III.G.4.e · NCMA 1.6

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital brings in safety-engineered devices and its injury rate does not fall. Which two problems have been reported in that situation?
opciones: Trouble working the safety mechanism, and needles still discarded improperly
Shortage of sharps containers, and gloves supplied in only one size
Poor lighting at the bedside, and tubes filled in the wrong order
Late reporting of injuries, and no written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices are widely used, but the fall in injuries has not always followed. In one study the rate went from 1.9 to 2.2 per 100 healthcare workers after implementation, and the factors reported most often were difficulty operating the safety mechanism and needles that continued to be disposed of improperly. Both are training and work-practice problems, which is why buying a device is only one part of a prevention program.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Epidemiology: Impact of Safety Devices on Needle Stick Injuries

preguntas.pregunta: In the protocol for the lactose tolerance blood test, what load is given and when are the glucose measurements taken?
opciones: 50 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 60 and 120 minutes
75 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 60 and 120 minutes
50 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 30 and 60 minutes
100 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 120 and 180 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The test uses 50 g of lactose with serial glucose measurements at 0, 60 and 120 minutes, and a rise under 20 mg/dL suggests intolerance; its sensitivity is 75% and its specificity 96%. The 75 g and 100 g loads are glucose, not lactose, and belong to the oral glucose tolerance tests. False negatives happen in diabetes, in small intestinal bacterial overgrowth and with delayed gastric emptying.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Lactose Intolerance", section Evaluation: Diagnostic Tests

preguntas.pregunta: The impulse has arrived at the atrioventricular node. What is the delay before it moves on, and what does a longer one do to the tracing?
opciones: About 100 ms, and a longer delay there widens the PR interval
About 50 ms, and a longer delay there widens the PR interval
About 25 ms, and a longer delay there widens the PR interval
About 225 ms, and a longer delay there widens the PR interval
preguntas.explicacion: The node holds the impulse about 100 ms. The other figures belong to other legs of the trip: roughly 50 ms from the sinoatrial node to the atrioventricular node, about 25 ms down the bundle branches, and about 225 ms in total from the first impulse to ventricular depolarization. The PR interval covers the nodal delay.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Atrioventricular Node

preguntas.pregunta: A muscular 26-year-old athlete has a BMI of 27 and asks whether he is overweight. What is the accurate response?
opciones: BMI ignores muscle mass and body composition, so the provider interprets it
BMI already corrects for muscle mass, so the number stands as measured
BMI is not valid under age 30, so the reading should simply be discarded
BMI is a direct measurement of body fat, so the number settles the question
preguntas.explicacion: Body mass index is built from height and weight alone. It leaves out muscle mass, bone density and body composition, so it is one piece of the picture rather than the whole of it, and the health care provider decides whether a given reading is too high or too low for that person.
preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, BMI Calculator: Calculate Your BMI

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is named by OCR as a reasonable safeguard a health care office can adopt?
opciones: Speaking quietly when discussing a condition with relatives in a public area of the office
Guaranteeing that no visitor can ever overhear or glimpse any patient information at all
Requiring every workforce member to obtain the patient's consent before each chart entry
Sending all internal messages about patients through unencrypted e-mail to speed up care
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule expects appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards, but OCR says outright that they are not expected to guarantee privacy against every possible risk. What counts as reasonable varies with the size and nature of the entity, and the examples given are lowering one's voice in public areas, avoiding names in hallways and elevators, posting reminder signs, and putting passwords on computers.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a mandatory reporter have to have before filing a report?
opciones: The facts and circumstances that raised the suspicion, not proof
A photograph or an X-ray documenting the suspected injury
Proof that abuse or neglect occurred, on the balance of evidence
A second staff member willing to sign the report as a witness
preguntas.explicacion: Reporters are asked for the facts and circumstances that led them to suspect a child has been abused or neglected; the burden of proving that it happened is not theirs. preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks how much blood a commercial citrate tube should receive. What is the answer?
opciones: A line printed on the tube marks the volume of blood to be drawn
The vacuum stops the flow well before the tube can be overfilled
The colour of the stopper sets the volume for every manufacturer
The laboratory calculates it from the patient's haematocrit result
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for these assays is collected into commercially prepared tubes that already hold their trisodium citrate, and each carries a line showing the volume of blood that should go in. Drawing short of that line leaves too much anticoagulant and lengthens the clotting time measured.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant gives postsurgical instructions to a child and then to an adult with the same procedure. What should differ?
opciones: The way the information is delivered, not its substance
The substance of the information, not the way it is given
The person who receives it, and no other element
The record it is charted in, and not the wording used
preguntas.explicacion: The requirements on signs of infection, pain management and the rest may be much the same, but the way the information is provided can be quite different depending on developmental level. Whatever adaptation is made, the sender still has to verify that the patient understood.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the Z-track method for an intramuscular injection involve?
opciones: Pulling the skin about an inch to one side, injecting, and waiting ten seconds
Pulling the skin about an inch to one side, injecting, and withdrawing at once
Pinching the skin into a fold, injecting, and letting go before the needle exits
Holding the skin taut and flat, injecting, and pressing the site for ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The non-dominant hand displaces the skin downward or to one side by about an inch, some two centimetres, and the needle goes in at 90 degrees while that pull is held. Once the medication is in, the needle stays in place ten seconds before coming out in a smooth motion and the skin is released, so the tissue closes over a zigzag path. That keeps the medication in the muscle instead of leaking into subcutaneous tissue.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.6: Z-track Method for IM injections

preguntas.pregunta: A urine drug screen is run on a patient in the emergency department for medical management only. Is a chain of custody required?
opciones: No: a purely clinical result is confidential and cannot be used against the patient
Yes: every drug screen carries the same documentation, regardless of purpose
No: chain of custody applies only to blood specimens, never to urine specimens
Yes: emergency department specimens always travel under a custody form
preguntas.explicacion: The result of medical drug testing is confidential information and cannot be evidence against the individual for disciplinary or penal action, so the chain of custody is not required for it. It becomes essential when the initial positive immunoassay has to be confirmed for use in court, as when the patient was in an accident or the case may go to trial. The matrix is not what decides it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Chain of Custody in Clinical/Medical Drug Testing

preguntas.pregunta: The check-in monitor faces the waiting room and shows the day's schedule with patient names. Which safeguard is at issue?
opciones: Workstation use and security, a physical safeguard covering how workstations are placed and used
Security awareness and training, the administrative standard for teaching staff the policies
Contingency planning, the administrative standard for keeping care going during a system failure
Evaluation, the administrative standard for periodically testing how well the policies work
preguntas.explicacion: The physical safeguards include workstation use and security, which requires policies specifying the proper use of, and physical protections for, workstations that can reach ePHI. The other three options are administrative safeguards: training the workforce, planning for emergencies that damage the systems, and performing periodic technical and non-technical assessments of the policies.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic short of tubes refills used ones by hand with anticoagulant. Why is that listed as a hazard?
opciones: Refilled tubes carry inappropriate amounts of anticoagulant and haemolyse
Refilled tubes carry too little vacuum and stop drawing after a few drops
Refilled tubes carry the wrong stopper colour and confuse the sequence
Refilled tubes carry a broken gel barrier and mix serum back into cells
preguntas.explicacion: Reusing tubes that have been refilled by hand with inappropriate amounts of anticoagulant appears among the causes of haemolysis. It is the practice that stocking enough tubes is meant to prevent, along with decanting blood from one tube into another to make the supply stretch.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.1 and 2.1.4

preguntas.pregunta: A 45-year-old asks how often he needs a tetanus booster after his one Tdap dose. What does the adult schedule call for?
opciones: A Td or Tdap booster every 10 years
A Td or Tdap booster every 5 years
A Td or Tdap booster every 20 years
No further booster once a Tdap dose is on record
preguntas.explicacion: The adult schedule places one dose of Tdap and then a booster of Td or Tdap every ten years thereafter. Separate rules exist for pregnancy, where a Tdap dose is given each time, and for wound management, where a dose of Td or Tdap may be needed regardless of where the ten-year clock stands.

preguntas.pregunta: Section 1557 of the ACA, as enforced by HHS OCR, prohibits discrimination in covered health programs on which grounds?
opciones: Race, color, national origin, age, disability or sex
Race, color, national origin, religion, and creed
Age, disability, insurance status, and income
Sex, age, primary language, and citizenship
preguntas.explicacion: Section 1557 prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, or sex in covered health programs or activities, with sex read to include pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity and sex characteristics, subject to the court stays listed on the page as of January 2025. Religion and insurance status are not in the list.

preguntas.pregunta: A 22-year-old reports bilateral lower abdominal pain, vaginal discharge and pain with intercourse. Which two pathogens most often cause the suspected condition?
opciones: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae
Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae
Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis
preguntas.explicacion: Pelvic inflammatory disease is an infection that climbs from the cervix, and in about 85 percent of cases it is caused by sexually transmitted bacteria or by microbes linked to bacterial vaginosis, with gonorrhea and chlamydia leading. The pain is often bilateral, and some patients have almost no symptoms at all, which does not make the long-term damage any smaller.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pelvic Inflammatory Disease", Etiology and History and Physical

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant wraps the cuff over a thin sweater sleeve to save time. What is the consequence?
opciones: Placing the cuff over clothing can shift the reading by as much as 50 mm Hg
Placing the cuff over clothing can shift the reading by as much as 5 mm Hg
Placing the cuff over clothing is acceptable when the fabric is thin and smooth
Placing the cuff over clothing lowers the reading only, so a normal value is safe
preguntas.explicacion: A cuff over clothing can alter the result by up to 50 mm Hg, the largest of the quantified technique errors. The cuff goes on the bare upper arm with nothing underneath it, and the sleeve is not simply rolled up either, because a rolled sleeve constricts the arm above the cuff.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Complications

preguntas.pregunta: Which findings warn that an abdominal surgical wound may be about to dehisce?
opciones: Redness at the wound margins, increasing drainage, growing pain and a broken suture
Pale flat wound margins, decreasing drainage, easing pain and a suture that has loosened
Blanching margins, clear serous drainage, itching and a suture that has begun to dissolve
Firm raised margins, no drainage, tightness across the line and a suture that has darkened
preguntas.explicacion: Dehiscence is the separation of the edges of a surgical wound, partial or full. The warning signs are redness around the margins, drainage that keeps increasing from the incision and pain that keeps growing; a broken suture can mean minor dehiscence or that it is about to happen. It often occurs suddenly in abdominal wounds while the patient is coughing or straining.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.2 Basic Concepts Related to Wounds

preguntas.pregunta: A week after a venipuncture the small clot at the site has disappeared. Which enzyme broke down its fibrin, and from what precursor was it made?
opciones: Plasmin, from plasminogen
Thrombin, from prothrombin
Fibrin, from fibrinogen
Heparin, from basophils
preguntas.explicacion: The gradual removal of a clot is called fibrinolysis: the inactive plasma protein plasminogen is converted into active plasmin, which slowly breaks down the fibrin, while bradykinin dilates the vessel again. Thrombin is the enzyme that builds fibrin, not the one that removes it; fibrin is the clot material itself; and heparin is an anticoagulant from basophils that opposes prothrombin.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Fibrinolysis; and Plasma Anticoagulants

preguntas.pregunta: A winged (butterfly) set is connected to evacuated tubes and the first tube to be filled is a light blue citrate tube. What does the WHO device table say must happen first?
opciones: A tube without additive is drawn or discarded, because of the air in the tubing
The tubing is flushed with the light blue tube, which is then sent as the specimen
The tourniquet is tightened until the tubing fills, then the citrate tube goes on
A red clot activator tube is drawn first so that the serum tests are not delayed
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 lists, as a disadvantage of winged steel needles used with vacuum tubes, that the air in the tubing means the first tube has to be either a tube with no additive or a discard tube. Sending the citrate tube that was used to fill the tubing would defeat the point, and the table says nothing about tightening the tourniquet or starting with a red tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A bottle of disinfectant concentrate breaks on the processing room floor. Which section of its safety data sheet guides the cleanup?
opciones: Section 6, on containment and cleanup after an accidental release
Section 4, on the first aid to give after contact with the chemical
Section 13, on disposal of the chemical and of its own container
Section 12, on what the chemical does if it reaches the environment
preguntas.explicacion: Section 6 covers the response to spills, leaks and releases: personal precautions such as removing ignition sources or ventilating, the protective equipment that keeps the chemical off skin, eyes and clothing, emergency steps including evacuation and when to call an expert, methods for containment such as covering drains, and the cleanup technique itself. It may distinguish a small spill from a large one. Sections 12 and 13 are among those OSHA does not enforce, and section 4 treats the person, not the floor.

preguntas.pregunta: For a nonwaived quantitative test, what control testing does CLIA require at a minimum each day patient specimens are run?
opciones: Two control materials of different concentrations
One negative and one positive control material
A single control material at the medical decision level
Three controls: low, mid-range and high, every 8 hours
preguntas.explicacion: At least once on each day of patient testing, a quantitative procedure needs two controls of different concentrations, while a qualitative procedure needs a negative and a positive control. Graded or titered procedures and tests with an extraction phase have their own variants. The three-level minimum, mid-point and maximum set belongs to calibration verification, not daily quality control.

preguntas.pregunta: What is seen on the tracing in a third-degree block?
opciones: P waves and QRS complexes at their own separate rates
P waves and QRS complexes at one shared but slow rate
P waves that lengthen the PR until a QRS is dropped
P waves that disappear while the QRS stays regular
preguntas.explicacion: Conduction between the chambers is gone, so the atria and the ventricles beat independently: the P waves march through at their own regular, faster rate while the complexes come at their own regular but slower one, driven by a junctional or ventricular escape rhythm.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrioventricular Block", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8

preguntas.pregunta: An unconscious patient needs an urgent procedure and no surrogate is present. Which doctrine lets the team proceed?
opciones: Implied consent, on the assumption a reasonable person would agree
Expressed consent, obtained afterwards and dated to the time of care
Informed permission, given by the admitting service on arrival
Waived consent, recorded once the patient wakes up and agrees
preguntas.explicacion: Consent may be waived in an emergency when the patient cannot communicate and no surrogate decision-maker is available. For an unaccompanied child the same reasoning is called the emergency exception rule or doctrine of implied consent, on the assumption that a reasonable parent would agree. Permission is what a parent gives for a minor, and consent obtained afterwards is not what authorized the care.

preguntas.pregunta: Four principles dominate the ethics codes: beneficence, nonmaleficence, distributive justice and autonomy. Which one governs sharing one scarce treatment among several patients?
opciones: Distributive justice, used when more than one patient is involved
Beneficence, the one about advocating for the patient's best interests
Nonmaleficence, the one that draws the boundary against causing harm
Autonomy, the one about the patient deciding free of outside control
preguntas.explicacion: In the four-principle heuristic that most code-writing bodies use, distributive justice is the principle that applies equal or equitable treatment when the matter involves more than one patient. Beneficence is advocating for the patient's best interest, nonmaleficence is not harming the patient, and autonomy is preserving the patient's ability to decide independently of outside control.

preguntas.pregunta: Which items does the ordering guidance call essential on every specimen label?
opciones: Name, age, requested test, date and collection site
Name, age, requested test, ward and ordering doctor
Name, sex, requested test, date and storage temperature
Name, age, diagnosis code, date and collection site
preguntas.explicacion: Proper labelling of all specimens with the patient's name, age, requested test, date and collection site is called essential for reliable analysis and traceability. preguntas.pregunta: An emergency laboratory compares specimen rejections by shift over one year. What did the published audit find, and what does it suggest for training?
opciones: Two-thirds of rejections (66 %) came from the night shift, pointing training at the staff who collect at night
Two-thirds of rejections (66 %) came from the day shift, when volume is highest, pointing training at day staff
Rejections were evenly split between shifts, so training was aimed at the units with the most samples instead
Night-shift rejections were higher only for coagulation tubes, so training focused on citrate fill levels
preguntas.explicacion: In the year-long audit the proportion of specimen rejections was 66 % during the night shift against 34 % during the day, even though the night shift runs with fewer laboratory staff. The laboratory's response was enhanced monthly documentation of rejected samples and periodic training for the personnel of the departments with the highest rejection rates, with the goal of bringing the overall rate from 6 % to below 2 %.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on atorvastatin reports diffuse muscle aches with no injury. Which reaction of this class does that fit?
opciones: Myopathy, which is dose dependent and reverses once the statin is discontinued
Rhabdomyolysis, the reaction reported most often in patients taking this class
Necrotizing myopathy, whose weakness clears a day or two after the drug stops
Cognitive dysfunction, the commonest reaction and a reason to change agents
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are generally well tolerated; the reactions seen most are myopathy, hepatotoxicity and new diabetes. Myopathy is dose dependent and shows as diffuse myalgias or otherwise unexplained tenderness or weakness that reverses when the drug is stopped. Rhabdomyolysis is the gravest complication but is rare, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy persists for months, and cognitive change is rare.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Statin Medications", Adverse Effects

preguntas.pregunta: A vegetarian patient asks what counts as one ounce-equivalent in the Protein Foods Group. Which of these does?
opciones: One tablespoon of peanut butter
One tablespoon of sunflower seeds
One cup of cooked beans or lentils
One cup of tofu cut into cubes
preguntas.explicacion: An ounce-equivalent of protein is an ounce of lean meat, poultry or seafood, one egg, a quarter cup of cooked beans, or a tablespoon of peanut butter. Beans, peas and lentils count either here or in the vegetable group. A whole cup of beans is four ounce-equivalents, not one.

preguntas.pregunta: A ward asks why the laboratory presses so hard on hemolysis when redrawing a tube takes two minutes. What consequences does the literature attach to it?
opciones: Delayed decisions, a longer stay in the department, and extra needle sticks
Loss of the quality control run and a forced recalibration of the analyser
A mandatory report of the quality failure to the accrediting organisation
A penalty against the laboratory's proficiency testing performance that year
preguntas.explicacion: A hemolysed sample usually means a repeat specimen has to be drawn and tested. Those repeats delay treatment and clinical decision making, lengthen the patient's stay in the emergency department, and leave the patient dissatisfied after being stuck more than once. The cost lands on the patient, not on the analyser, which is why the collection step gets the attention.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a written grievance about the quality of care. What must the hospital give back?
opciones: Written notice naming the contact person, the steps taken, the result and the date
Written notice that the complaint was received and then forwarded to the state agency
Verbal notice from the department manager once the review has been completed
Written notice of the outcome only if the grievance is found to have merit
preguntas.explicacion: A hospital must run a process for resolving grievances promptly and tell each patient whom to contact to file one. Resolving it means giving the patient written notice of the decision, with the name of the hospital contact person, the steps taken to investigate, the results and the date the process closed. The governing body owns the process.

preguntas.pregunta: The chest electrodes are being placed on a patient. Where does V1 go?
opciones: At the fourth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fourth intercostal space, left of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, in the mid-clavicular line
preguntas.explicacion: V1 sits in the fourth intercostal space just to the right of the sternum, and V2 goes in the same space on the left side. The two spots are found by walking the fingers down from the sternal angle, and they are marked before the skin is cleaned so the location is not lost.

preguntas.pregunta: How does Medicare decide the practice relationship a physician assistant must keep with a physician?
opciones: By the state's own law and scope of practice rules for physician assistants
By a single federal rule requiring the physician to be present in the room
By the collaboration standard written for nurse practitioners in the same part
By the accrediting organization that granted the program its accreditation
preguntas.explicacion: The assistant must perform services in accordance with state law and the state scope of practice rules for physician assistants where the professional services are furnished. Any state rules describing the required practice relationship, explicit supervisory or collaborative requirements included, count as a form of supervision. Where a state has no such rule, a documented working relationship with physicians serves.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures, a prothrombin time and a complete blood count are ordered on one venipuncture. Which specimen is collected third?
opciones: The purple EDTA tube for the complete blood count
The light blue citrate tube for the prothrombin time
The blood culture bottle for the microbiology order
A non-additive tube drawn ahead of the citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Of the three, the culture bottle sits at position 1, the citrate tube at position 3 and EDTA at position 8, so the EDTA tube is the third one filled. A non-additive tube does hold position 2, but the footnote reserves it for when tissue fluid or thromboplastin contamination is a concern.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has been prescribed eardrops. Which set of instructions is correct?
opciones: Warm the bottle in the hand a minute or two, lie with that ear up, stay five minutes
Warm the bottle under hot tap water, lie with that ear down, stay for two minutes
Use the drops cold from the refrigerator, sit upright, and stay still for ten minutes
Warm the bottle in the hand, lie with that ear up, and get up as soon as it is done
preguntas.explicacion: The bottle is held in the hand for one or two minutes to warm the solution, a suspension is shaken, and the ear canal is cleaned and dried with a sterile applicator first. The patient lies with the affected ear uppermost, the ordered number of drops goes in without the dropper touching anything, and that position is kept for five minutes. A cotton wick may be used and is replaced at least every 24 hours.

preguntas.pregunta: Which peripheral pulse is described as the hardest to palpate, especially for a less experienced clinician?
opciones: The posterior tibial, found immediately behind the medial malleolus
The popliteal, found in the popliteal fossa slightly lateral to the midline
The femoral, found just below the inguinal ligament toward the pubic symphysis
The brachial, found between the medial epicondyle and the tendon of the biceps
preguntas.explicacion: The posterior tibial pulse sits just behind the bony bump on the inner ankle and is considered the most difficult of the peripheral pulses to feel. The popliteal is also sought less often, but the one singled out for difficulty is the posterior tibial, which matters when its absence is being used as a finding.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique

preguntas.pregunta: A neuron may hold more than a thousand of one organelle, while a bone cell holds only a couple hundred. Which organelle is it, and why the difference?
opciones: The mitochondrion, because a neuron needs far more ATP than a bone cell
The lysosome, because a neuron digests far more debris than a bone cell
The nucleus, because a neuron stores far more genetic material than a bone cell
The Golgi apparatus, because a neuron exports far more protein than a bone cell
preguntas.explicacion: Mitochondria convert the energy held in nutrients such as glucose into ATP, along an inner membrane folded into cristae. Cells that spend a lot of energy carry a lot of them: muscle cells are packed with them for contraction and neurons need them to run their sodium and potassium pumps, while a bone cell is far less active.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, Organelles for Energy Production

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature must appear on a valid HIPAA authorization form?
opciones: An expiration and a statement of the right to revoke it in writing, all in plain language
A witness signature from a workforce member who watched the patient sign the document
A cost estimate of the copies, since the fee has to be agreed before the release is signed
A clause making treatment conditional on the patient granting the authorization requested
preguntas.explicacion: Authorizations must be written in specific terms and in plain language, and must state the information involved, who discloses it, who receives it, when it expires, and the right to revoke it in writing. A covered entity may not condition treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits on the patient signing one, except in limited circumstances the rule spells out.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization

preguntas.pregunta: Which body mass index range is classified as overweight in adults aged 20 and older?
opciones: 25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 30
25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 35
24 to 28.9, with obesity beginning at 29
27 to 31.9, with obesity beginning at 32
preguntas.explicacion: The adult table runs 18.5 to 24.9 for healthy weight, 25 to 29.9 for overweight, and 30 or higher for obesity, with 40 and above marked as severe obesity. Body mass index estimates overweight and obesity from weight and height together; it is not a direct measurement of body fat.

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an electronic health record from an electronic medical record?
opciones: The EHR is built to be shared with other organizations involved in the patient's care
The EHR is the version the patient keeps at home, while the EMR belongs to the practice
The EHR holds only billing and demographic data, while the EMR holds the clinical notes
The EHR is a scanned copy of the paper chart, while the EMR is entered directly by staff
preguntas.explicacion: An EMR is the digital version of the paper chart in one clinician's office: it tracks data over time, flags who is due for screening and supports quality work inside that practice, but the information does not travel easily beyond it. An EHR is designed to reach past the organization that collected the data, so the record follows the patient to the specialist, the hospital or the next state.

preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine for culture cannot reach the microbiology laboratory for about 6 hours. What keeps the culture result valid?
opciones: Refrigerating it or placing it in a boric acid preservative tube, either of which holds it for up to 24 hours
Keeping it at room temperature, which is acceptable for up to 24 hours as long as the cup stays capped
Freezing it, since freezing stops bacterial growth more completely than refrigeration does
Adding a formaldehyde preservative, the additive that best protects bacteria for later culture
preguntas.explicacion: Urine for culture must be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or placed in a preservative; both boric acid and refrigeration hold the specimen adequately for up to 24 hours. Urine left at room temperature for more than 4 hours shows overgrowth of both pathogens and contaminants. Formaldehyde is used to preserve cells and causes false-positive strip reactions, and freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC4771218 LaRocco et al., Effectiveness of Preanalytic Practices on Urine Cultures (2016), Summary of findings

preguntas.pregunta: A handwritten order reads QD. Which misreading put that abbreviation on the Do Not Use list?
opciones: It is read as QID, four times daily, instead of every day
It is read as QOD, every other day, instead of every day
It is read as QHS, nightly at bedtime, instead of every day
It is read as PRN, only as needed, instead of every day
preguntas.explicacion: QD means every day, but the period after the q, or the tail of a handwritten q, is taken for the letter i, and the order becomes QID, four doses a day. The recommended practice is to write daily. QOD has its own entry on the list, where the poorly written o is the problem.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units

preguntas.pregunta: What does a health plan's "network" consist of?
opciones: The providers, facilities and suppliers under contract with the insurer
The list of prescription drugs the plan covers, also called its drug list
The providers the patient may see without a referral from the primary care doctor
The services that count toward the out-of-pocket limit, including out-of-network care
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the network as the set of facilities, providers and suppliers that have a contract with the insurer or plan to deliver health care services. Being in the network is a matter of contract, not of whether a referral is needed: in many HMOs even in-network specialists require one. The glossary's entry on the out-of-pocket limit shows the other side of the coin: care received out of network does not count toward that limit. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, a separate entry.

preguntas.pregunta: A temperature is charted as 38.2 °C with no other detail. What is missing?
opciones: The route used, since each site carries its own average and its own fever cut-off
The thermometer model, since each manufacturer calibrates its device differently
The room temperature, since a warm room lifts every reading by a fixed amount
The patient's baseline, since a value has no meaning until a baseline is on file
preguntas.explicacion: The same patient reads differently at the armpit, the mouth, the ear and the rectum, and the thresholds for calling a value a fever follow the site. A number without its route cannot be graded or compared with the last one, which is why the route is written beside the value and the hour it was taken.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature e · NCMA 2B.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which natural anticoagulant is released by basophils, opposes prothrombin, and is also given as a drug to surgical patients at risk of clots?
opciones: Heparin
Protein C
Thrombin
Plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: Several plasma anticoagulants keep clotting confined to the injury: the protein C system, TFPI, antithrombin and heparin. Heparin comes from basophils, is short-acting, opposes prothrombin and also sits on the cells lining the vessels; a pharmaceutical form is given, for example, to surgical patients at risk of clots. Thrombin builds fibrin and plasmin dissolves it; neither is an anticoagulant.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Plasma Anticoagulants

preguntas.pregunta: The wheezing of a patient in respiratory distress fades away. How should that be read?
opciones: Not as improvement: breathing and pulse go on being monitored
As improvement, so the emergency call can now be cancelled
As a sign the inhaler worked and that a second dose is not needed
As proof the problem was anxiety rather than a lung problem
preguntas.explicacion: The patient's condition is not assumed to be improving just because abnormal breath sounds such as wheezing can no longer be heard: breathing and pulse are monitored until medical help arrives. Nobody waits to see whether things get better before calling for help, and the patient is not moved after a head, neck, chest or airway injury.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Breathing difficulties - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.p · 2027 I.B.8.p · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: How much authority does an appointed health care proxy have?
opciones: The same authority to request or refuse care the patient would have had
Authority limited to the treatments the living will names one by one
Authority limited to comfort care and to consenting for routine tests
Authority to demand any treatment at all, since the patient cannot speak now
preguntas.explicacion: The proxy or surrogate holds the same power to request or refuse treatment the patient would have held if they could still decide and speak. That authority is not confined to whatever the living will happened to list, and it is not narrowed to comfort measures. What it does not include is demanding care that is not medically indicated: the right to refuse is broader than the right to demand.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advance Directives", Clinical Significance; and Issues of Concern: Living Will

preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient with a known latex allergy is admitted for several days of blood work. Which measure applies?
opciones: Post a sign on the door, note the allergy in the chart, and remove latex items from the room
Use powdered latex gloves, which release fewer allergenic proteins onto the skin
Keep the latex gloves in the room but double-glove with vinyl over them
Notify only the surgical team, since gloves matter most in the operating room
preguntas.explicacion: Hospital patients with latex allergy should ask for a sign on the door and notes in the chart, for latex gloves and other latex items to be removed from the room, and for pharmacy and dietary staff to be told so they do not handle medicines or food with latex gloves. Cornstarch powder on latex gloves is a leading source of inhaled allergen, the opposite of a safeguard.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies - for Hospital Patients, How to Avoid Exposure to Latex in the Hospital
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: How do the terms telehealth and telemedicine relate to each other?
opciones: Telehealth is broader, taking in provider training and administrative work
Telemedicine is broader, taking in provider training and administrative work
They mean the same, since both refer only to a live video visit
Telemedicine covers home monitoring while telehealth covers video visits
preguntas.explicacion: People sometimes use telemedicine to mean the same thing as telehealth, but telehealth is the broader term. It includes telemedicine and adds training for health care providers, administrative meetings, and services furnished by pharmacists and social workers. Remote monitoring, virtual visits and messages through the health record are all telehealth.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Telehealth: What is the difference between telemedicine and telehealth?

preguntas.pregunta: What separates enteral nutrition from parenteral nutrition?
opciones: Enteral goes into the gastrointestinal tract; parenteral goes into a central vein
Enteral goes into a central vein; parenteral goes into the gastrointestinal tract
Enteral is given by mouth in thickened form; parenteral is given by feeding tube
Enteral is used short term only; parenteral is the route for any long-term feeding
preguntas.explicacion: Enteral nutrition is delivered straight into the digestive tract, bypassing chewing and swallowing, through tubes such as nasogastric, orogastric, PEG or PEJ. Parenteral nutrition runs through a central intravenous line for patients who need supplementation but cannot use the enteral route, and it carries glucose, amino acids, minerals, electrolytes and vitamins.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 14: Enteral Nutrition; and Parenteral Nutrition

preguntas.pregunta: An insulin order is written as "4U". Which misreading puts this abbreviation on the error-prone list?
opciones: U is read as a zero or a four, turning 4U into 40 or into 44 units
U is read as IV, which is why international unit is spelled out in full
U is read as mg, which is why the microgram is written out as mcg
U is read as qid, which is why every day is written out in full instead
preguntas.explicacion: U or u for unit is mistaken for a zero or for the number 4, so 4U is seen as 40 and 4u as 44, a ten-fold overdose or worse; it can also be read as cc. The recommended practice is to write unit or units. The other three misreadings are real, but they belong to other rows of the same list: IU read as IV, the microgram symbol read as mg, and QD read as QID.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is placed supine with the arms out on boards. How far may the arms be abducted?
opciones: Less than 90 degrees, which keeps the humerus from pressing on the axilla
Up to 120 degrees, as long as a pad is placed underneath each elbow
As far as the boards reach, provided the palms are turned toward the floor
Exactly 90 degrees, the angle at which the ulnar nerve is under least strain
preguntas.explicacion: Abduction is held under 90 degrees so that the humerus does not press into the axilla and injure the brachial plexus. The forearms rest neutral or supinated, palms toward the body, which keeps pressure off the ulnar nerve; malpositioning of the arm in this position is the commonest source of ulnar injury. A draw sheet tucked under the torso holds an adducted arm.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Structure and Function: Supine Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(7) · RMA III.F.2.b.i · NCMA 2B.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who doubled his fiber in one week complains of gas, bloating and cramps. What should he be told?
opciones: Build fiber up slowly over a few weeks and drink plenty of fluid
Build fiber up slowly over a few weeks and cut back on fluid
Stop the fiber, since these symptoms mean he cannot tolerate it
Switch entirely to fiber supplements, which do not cause symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: A large jump in fiber over a short time brings gas, bloating and abdominal cramps, and the complaint usually settles once the gut bacteria adjust. Adding fiber gradually rather than all at once reduces the gas and diarrhea, and fluid is what carries fiber through the digestive tract, so about eight glasses a day are advised.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fiber — Side Effects; and Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(f) · NCMA B.21

preguntas.pregunta: A seated patient becomes pale and sweaty and says he is about to faint. What should happen right away?
opciones: He should sit or lie down quickly with the legs elevated, and stay horizontal afterwards
He should stand up and walk slowly to a couch, since the movement restores the venous return
He should be given a sugary drink, since hypoglycemia is the most common cause
He should keep still and upright while the last tube finishes filling
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should sit or lie down quickly during an acute episode, with their legs elevated, to help recovery from reflex postural hypotension, and should be kept horizontal afterwards and prevented from standing too soon; any injury from a fall needs immediate attention. Standing up is the opposite of the advice, and hypoglycemia is listed as a mimic of syncope, not its usual cause.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management

preguntas.pregunta: A provider gives a verbal order during a procedure. What does the record have to show afterwards?
opciones: That the order was dated, timed and authenticated promptly by a responsible practitioner
That the order was witnessed by two members of staff before it was carried out
That the order was entered as a standing order approved by the medical staff earlier
That the order was repeated back and then filed in the practice correspondence log
preguntas.explicacion: All orders, verbal ones included, must be dated, timed and authenticated promptly by the ordering practitioner, or by another practitioner responsible for the patient where State scope of practice law, facility policy and medical staff rules allow it. Preprinted and electronic standing orders are a separate mechanism with its own approval and review requirements.

preguntas.pregunta: How do a Medigap insurer and a state Medicaid agency get the Medicare-paid claims data they need to pay their share?
opciones: Through the crossover agreement, a national contract for exchanging that claims data
Through the provider, which rebills each of them once Medicare's payment is posted
Through the patient, who forwards the summary notice Medicare mails to her at home
Through the clearinghouse, which splits the claim between payers before sending it
preguntas.explicacion: The coordination of benefits agreement program sets a national standard contract between the secondary payer contractor and other insurers for sending enrollee eligibility data and Original Medicare paid claims data. Medigap plans, employer supplemental plans, Medicaid and others draw on that national repository, with unique identifiers, to have paid claims crossed over to them. Medicare is usually the primary payer on claims exchanged this way.

preguntas.pregunta: Where along the needle should a needle holder grasp it, and why?
opciones: About a third of the way from the swage toward the tip, so the needle does not bend or break
About a third of the way from the tip toward the swage, so the needle does not bend or break
Right at the swage where the suture attaches, so the thread cannot pull loose while sewing
Right at the point, so the operator can see exactly where the tip will enter the tissue
preguntas.explicacion: The needle sits in the holder roughly one third of the distance from the swage to the tip, which prevents the needle from fracturing, bending or twisting as it is driven through tissue. Holders often lock so the needle stays secure. The swage is where modern sutures are attached to the needle rather than threaded through an eye.

preguntas.pregunta: Which structural feature separates bacteria from the fungi and protozoa?
opciones: Bacteria are prokaryotes, so their genetic material has no true nucleus
Bacteria are eukaryotes, so their genetic material has no true nucleus
Bacteria are acellular, so their genetic material sits outside any cell
Bacteria are multicellular, so their genetic material is shared between cells
preguntas.explicacion: Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes: their DNA is not housed in a true nucleus, and most bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan. Fungi and protozoa belong to the eukaryotes, whose defining feature is that the cell does have a nucleus. Viruses are in neither camp, because they are not made of cells at all.

preguntas.pregunta: When must soap and water be used for hand hygiene rather than an alcohol-based rub?
opciones: When the hands are visibly soiled, and when the patient has Clostridioides difficile
When the hands are visibly soiled, and when the patient is on droplet precautions
When gloves are about to be worn, and when the patient has Clostridioides difficile
When entering a room, and when the previous patient was on contact precautions
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based rub is used until dry for most moments of hand hygiene, but two situations send the practitioner to the sink: hands that are visibly soiled and a patient with C. difficile. Hand hygiene is also one of the infection control measures planned before a procedure, alongside environmental control, the choice of gloves, the aseptic field and sequencing from clean to dirty.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair calls to book a draw and is told to bring someone who can help her transfer. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, the provider must give reasonable assistance so she can be seen on her own
Yes, as long as staff offer to help when the companion cannot manage the transfer
Yes, if the practice can show that lifting would risk injuring its own staff
No, unless she is offered an appointment when the accessible room happens to be free
preguntas.explicacion: A patient with a disability may come to an appointment alone, like anyone else, and the provider has to give the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help undressing, transferring, and being positioned. opciones: A clean paper or towel
A warm compress pack
A rolled cloth tourniquet
A sterile drape with a window

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory rejects a sample as haemolysed. Which collection practices are recognized causes of haemolysis?
opciones: Pressing the syringe plunger, shaking the tube, and a short draw in the grey tube
Leaving the tourniquet on for more than one minute, and drawing the tubes in the wrong sequence
Using a 21 G needle in an adult, and inverting the citrate tube three to six times
Preparing the skin with povidone iodine, and labeling the tubes away from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Pressing the plunger raises the risk of haemolysis, Table 2.3 warns that a short draw in the fluoride tube may cause haemolysis, and vigorous shaking or overmixing of the tube produces haemolysis. A long tourniquet causes hemoconcentration, the wrong sequence causes additive carry-over, iodine raises potassium, and three to six gentle inversions is the correct handling of the citrate tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she had a tetanus booster but has no card. What counts as evidence of vaccination?
opciones: A written, dated record; self-report counts only for a short list of vaccines
A written, dated record only, so vaccination is postponed until one is found
The patient's own account for any vaccine, since records are often incomplete
A written record from the state registry only, never one from another clinic
preguntas.explicacion: Providers should accept only written, dated records as evidence of vaccination, with a short list of exceptions where self-reported doses are acceptable: COVID-19, influenza, pneumococcal polysaccharide and, for people 18 or older, polio. Vaccination should not be postponed because records cannot be found. Histories may come from medical records, personal cards or an immunization information system.

preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, laboratory tests are sorted into how many complexity categories, and which are they?

Two: waived and nonwaived, with no further split
Four: waived, PPM, moderate and high complexity
Three: home use, point-of-care and laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation grades every test system as waived, moderate complexity or high complexity, from the least to the most demanding. Moderate and high together are called nonwaived testing. Provider-performed microscopy is a subcategory inside moderate complexity, not a fourth category, and point-of-care describes where a test is run, not how it is classified.

preguntas.pregunta: What does it mean when the FDA approves a new drug?
opciones: Reviewers judged that the benefits outweigh the known and potential risks
Reviewers judged that the drug carries no known risk for the population
Reviewers confirmed the drug works better than every treatment available
Reviewers accepted the manufacturer's own summary of its clinical trials
preguntas.explicacion: Approval means the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research reviewed the data and concluded the benefits outweigh the known and potential risks for the intended population. preguntas.pregunta: Which three elements must valid informed consent for a research study include?
opciones: Disclosure of information, competency to decide, and a voluntary decision
Disclosure of information, a witness signature, and an approved study budget
Competency to decide, a voluntary decision, and payment for participation
Competency to decide, a signed waiver, and a copy filed with the sponsor
preguntas.explicacion: Valid research consent rests on three major elements: disclosure of information, competency of the patient or surrogate to make a decision, and the voluntary nature of that decision. preguntas.pregunta: For a term newborn who needs several tests, which sampling method is preferred, and why?
opciones: Venipuncture, which is the method of choice for term neonates and causes less pain than heel-pricks
Heel-prick, which is the method of choice for term neonates because it causes less pain than venipuncture
Finger-prick, which the WHO recommends for term neonates because the finger has no bone risk
Arterial puncture, since capillary blood already resembles arterial blood in oxygen content
preguntas.explicacion: Venepuncture is the method of choice for blood sampling in term neonates and causes less pain than heel-pricks, but it requires an experienced and trained phlebotomist; if none is available the physician may need to draw the specimen. Finger-pricks are not used in neonates because of nerve damage, and the heel is reserved for small volumes.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee steadies the vein by pressing a thumb on the skin just ABOVE the intended puncture point. What is the correct anchoring technique?
opciones: Place the thumb below the site and pull the skin down and slightly away, making it taut
Place the thumb above the site but press down harder, so that the vein cannot roll sideways
Use the index finger over the vein itself to guide the shaft of the needle
Skip anchoring; ask the patient to make a fist, which fixes the vein in place
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 of the WHO procedure anchors the vein by holding the arm and placing a thumb below the venipuncture site; the free hand then uses the thumb to pull the skin down and slightly away from the draw site so it is taut. A finger over the vein is what Step 5 explicitly forbids after disinfection, and the fist is an addition that makes the veins prominent, not a replacement for anchoring.

preguntas.pregunta: A caller with no regular provider has a painful ear infection that began last night. Where should the front desk steer her first?
opciones: To an urgent care center, since the problem needs prompt care but is not emergency severe
To the hospital emergency department, where a sudden illness is always evaluated first
To an ambulatory surgical center, the outpatient site that handles same-day procedures
To a skilled nursing facility, where licensed nurses treat and observe a condition daily
preguntas.explicacion: Urgent care is meant for a problem serious enough that a person would want care without delay, yet not so severe that the emergency room is required. Emergency services mean evaluating an emergency condition and treating it so it does not worsen. For someone with no primary care provider, urgent care usually saves time and money over the emergency room.

preguntas.pregunta: A yogurt lists 15 g of total sugars and, indented under it, 7 g of added sugars. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: Seven grams were added in processing and eight occur naturally
Seven grams were added in processing on top of the 15 g listed above
Seven grams are milk sugar and the other eight were added in processing
Seven grams are the share of the sugars the body can actually absorb
preguntas.explicacion: The word "includes" before added sugars means that figure is already inside the total, so the rest of the total is sugar occurring naturally in the milk. Added sugars are the ones put in during processing, plus syrups, honey and concentrated juices. Total sugars carry no Daily Value, because no target has been set.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking a statin has just learned she is pregnant. What does the drug information say about continuing?
opciones: Statins are stopped for most pregnant patients, and are also ruled out in lactation
Statins may run at half the usual dose to the end of the first trimester and stop
Statins are safe throughout pregnancy but are stopped during lactation for the infant
Statins are ruled out in pregnancy but may be resumed as soon as lactation begins
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are discontinued for most patients who become pregnant, and the FDA asks clinicians to weigh the need in the few at very high cardiovascular risk, such as homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or established cardiovascular disease. preguntas.pregunta: Which factor is part of the risk assessment used to decide whether an impermissible disclosure is a breach?
opciones: The identity of the unauthorized person who used or received the information
The number of years the practice has operated without a previous incident
Whether the workforce member involved had completed the yearly privacy training
Whether the patient complained to the practice about the disclosure afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: The assessment must weigh at least four things: the nature and extent of the PHI involved, including the identifiers and the likelihood of re-identification; who the unauthorized person using or receiving it was; whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed; and how far the risk has been mitigated. preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's recordkeeping rule, 29 CFR part 1904, which forms record work-related injuries and illnesses?
opciones: The OSHA 300 log, the 301 incident report and the 300A summary posted each year
The sharps injury log, the training record and the employee medical record
The OSHA 200 log, which the Needlestick Act found sufficient for exposure tracking
The exposure determination, the written opinion and the Appendix A declination
preguntas.explicacion: Covered employers record each recordable injury and illness on the OSHA Form 300 log, prepare a Form 301 incident report with details of each case, and at the end of the year prepare the Form 300A summary and post it in a visible place. The sharps injury log, training records and medical records are kept under the bloodborne pathogens standard; the exposure determination, written opinion and declination are other documents of that same standard. Congress found the old OSHA 200 log insufficient, which is why the sharps log was added.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a read-only backup record system able to do for a practice during an outage?
opciones: Show and print the information already recorded, from a copy refreshed often
Accept new orders and notes that are merged into the record after the outage
Run the scheduling module so that the day's appointments can still be moved
Send the claims already prepared, since billing does not alter clinical data
preguntas.explicacion: A read-only backup is a copy of what is already in the record system, kept up to date as often as possible, optimally hourly, and tested regularly. Users can look things up and print from it, but nothing new goes in, which is why paper forms and temporary record numbers are still needed for what happens during the outage.

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker says a rapid test "must be waived because we run it at the point of care." What is the correct reading of the term point-of-care testing under CLIA?
opciones: It describes where testing is done and says nothing about the test's complexity
It is a synonym for waived testing when the operator is not a laboratorian
It is the category for tests cleared by the FDA for home use
It refers to a laboratory licensed by a state whose rules are stricter than CLIA
preguntas.explicacion: Point-of-care is a location: the bedside or near the site of care. Some point-of-care tests are waived, but faster technology also lets nonwaived tests be run near the patient, so a test cannot be assumed waived just because of where it is performed. Home-use clearance is one route to waived status, and the state-licensed laboratory description is the meaning of CLIA-exempt.

preguntas.pregunta: What does federal regulation require of an electronic prescription for a controlled substance?
opciones: It is created and signed in an application that meets the requirements of part 1311
It is printed out and manually signed before it is transmitted on to the pharmacy
It is followed by a paper copy mailed to the pharmacy within seven days of issue
It is limited to Schedules III, IV and V, because Schedule II still needs paper
preguntas.explicacion: Electronic prescriptions for controlled substances have to be created and signed using an application that meets the requirements of part 1311. preguntas.pregunta: How is care coordination defined?
opciones: Deliberately organizing care activities and sharing information among all participants
Deliberately assigning one clinician to make every decision about a patient's care
Deliberately limiting the number of specialists a patient is allowed to see
Deliberately scheduling all of a patient's appointments on the same calendar day
preguntas.explicacion: Care coordination means organizing a patient's care activities on purpose and sharing information among everyone involved, so care comes out safer and more effective. The patient's needs and preferences are known in advance and reach the right people at the right time, and that information then guides the care delivered.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the typical entry-level education for a medical assistant?
opciones: A postsecondary nondegree award, such as a certificate program
An associate's degree from an accredited community college program
A bachelor's degree, the level typical for clinical laboratory work
A master's degree, the level typical for a physician assistant role
preguntas.explicacion: Medical assistants typically enter with postsecondary education such as a certificate, and some start with a high school diploma and learn on the job. Programs run about one or two years at community colleges, vocational and technical schools and universities, cover medical terminology, anatomy and pharmacology, and usually include supervised experience such as a practicum.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice that stopped sending Medicare claims electronically has lost its access to the eligibility system. What is still open to it?
opciones: Its contractor's secure internet portal, which can still be used to check eligibility
Its clearinghouse's enrollment, which covers eligibility checks for all its providers
A paper eligibility request to the contractor, which has to be answered in 30 days
A telephone request to the contractor, which takes the place of the lost enrollment
preguntas.explicacion: Access to the eligibility system rests on an electronic claims enrollment with a contractor, and a provider that does not follow the enrollment steps or stops submitting electronic Original Medicare claims loses it. preguntas.pregunta: How often does OSHA require an employer's written Exposure Control Plan to be reviewed and updated?
opciones: At least once a year, and whenever the tasks, procedures or positions with occupational exposure change
Within 10 working days of each new hire with occupational exposure, and otherwise every three years
Once a year together with the annual employee training, and at no other time even if tasks change
Every time an exposure incident is reported, and kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iv) sets two triggers: a review at least every year, plus a review whenever new or changed tasks, procedures or job positions alter who is exposed and how. The same review has to take in new technology that cuts exposure and document, each year, which safer medical devices were considered and adopted. The other periods belong to other rules of the same standard: 10 working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine, three years is how long training records are kept, and employment plus 30 years is the retention of medical records. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a rewrite of the plan.

Family history and inherited disease risk
Body mass index and nutrition status
Vaccination record and screening history
preguntas.explicacion: Social determinants are the conditions where people are born, live, learn, work, play, worship and age. The five domains are economic stability; education access and quality; health care access and quality; neighborhood and built environment; and social and community context.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia was found to lack capacity two weeks ago. What does that finding mean today?
opciones: Nothing by itself: the finding held for that time and that situation
It carries over until a judge rules that the patient has recovered
It carries over for the whole admission, once it is in the record
It removes the need to explain the draw, but not to ask permission
preguntas.explicacion: An assessment of capacity is valid only within the time, place and situation in which it took place; it is a snapshot and cannot be carried across to another moment. A history of dementia does not automatically mean the person lacks capacity, and the same patient may be lucid enough today to take part in the discussion. Competence is a court's decision.

preguntas.pregunta: To stretch a kit, a testing site cuts each rapid test strip lengthwise so two patients can be tested per strip. What is the regulatory consequence?
opciones: The test is no longer waived and falls under the nonwaived CLIA requirements
It stays waived as long as the manufacturer's reading time is still respected
The site must run external controls with every patient sample from then on
The test remains waived because only the specimen volume was changed
preguntas.explicacion: Physically altering test components, such as cutting cards or strips to multiply the number of tests, and changing the timing of a test are both modifications. Running more controls does not restore the waiver; only following the insert without modification does.

preguntas.pregunta: Which item on the test requisition allows the laboratory to judge later whether a specimen was transported within an acceptable time?

The date the requisition was printed by the ordering office
The time the specimen was logged into the laboratory information system
The expected turnaround time promised to the ordering provider
