preguntas.pregunta: A stool specimen for a gastrointestinal molecular panel has to travel from a rural clinic. Which transport and storage plan matches the general guidelines?
opciones: Room temperature in stabilising media, or on ice; then 2 to 8 °C for four to seven days
Room temperature without media, or frozen; then 2 to 8 °C for up to twenty-four hours
On ice only, never at room temperature; then at −20 °C from the moment it arrives
Room temperature in stabilising media only; then at room temperature until extraction
preguntas.explicacion: For stool the variables listed are time, transport and storage temperature, stabilisation media and the patient's medications. Transport is either at room temperature when a stabilising medium is used or on ice, and storage runs four to seven days, at 2 to 8 °C or at room temperature if stabilised. preguntas.pregunta: What is an external control for a waived test?
opciones: A liquid or similar material resembling a patient sample, tested to check the entire process
A built-in line or window on the device that confirms the sample moved through the strip
An electronic check the meter runs on itself at start-up to verify its internal functions
A patient sample previously tested by the referral laboratory and retested on site each month
preguntas.explicacion: External controls mimic patient specimens and are run exactly like one, so they monitor the process from sample application to result interpretation and show whether results fall within the ranges printed on the control or in its insert. Symptoms lasting for more than 6 months
Symptoms lasting for more than 2 weeks
Symptoms lasting for more than 12 months

preguntas.pregunta: A patient was discharged from the hospital on Monday and transitional care management has been billed. When must the first contact happen?

Within 2 calendar weeks of discharge, by phone, email or face to face
Within 7 business days of discharge, but only face to face
Within 30 days of discharge, at any point in the service period

preguntas.pregunta: Who should perform quality control testing at a waived site, and how should the control material be handled?

The most experienced operator only, using a shortened version of the patient procedure
The laboratory director personally, at the start of each shift, before staff arrive
A manufacturer's representative, who ships the control results back to the site

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes has a pulse that is very hard to locate in one leg. What may this suggest?

Dehydration, which empties the vessel and flattens the wave that reaches the leg
A bounding circulation, which spreads the wave and makes any single beat harder to feel
An irregular rhythm, in which the beats are too widely spaced for the fingers to catch
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse that is hard to find can mean the artery is blocked, and those blockages are common in people with diabetes or with arteries hardened by high cholesterol. Three to six for the culture bottle and eight to ten for the citrate tube
Eight to ten for both containers, since both hold an anticoagulant
Three to six for both containers, since both are drawn before serum tubes

preguntas.pregunta: A white blood cell engulfs a bacterium. Which organelle then digests it?

The ribosome, whose enzymes break down the material inside it
The mitochondrion, whose enzymes break down the material inside it
The nucleolus, whose enzymes break down the material inside it

Seat the person upright at once and offer a hot drink to raise the blood pressure
Keep the person lying down for at least an hour before allowing any movement

Posterior to the trachea just above the larynx, and the mineral is iodine
Anterior to the trachea just below the larynx, and the mineral is calcium

Bacterial conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Allergic conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Viral conjunctivitis, led by Staphylococcus aureus

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a fasting lipid panel and mentions having chewed sugar-free gum and smoked a cigarette that morning, but eaten nothing. Does the fast hold?
opciones: No: while fasting for a blood test the patient should also not chew gum, smoke or exercise, so the provider is told
Yes: only food and caloric drinks break a fast; sugar-free gum and tobacco are permitted before a lipid panel
Yes, provided the gum and the cigarette were more than two hours before the draw and the patient drank plain water
No: smoking breaks the fast but chewing gum does not, so only the cigarette needs to be reported to the provider
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting for a blood test means nothing to eat or drink except plain water for several hours before the draw, usually 8 to 12 hours, and during the fast the patient is also asked not to chew gum, smoke or exercise. preguntas.pregunta: A patient who moved to a high-altitude city three months ago now has a hematocrit above the sea-level reference range. Which mechanism explains it?
opciones: Kidney cells sensed low oxygen and secreted EPO, raising red cell output
The liver secreted thrombopoietin, raising platelet and red cell output
The spleen released its stored third of the platelets and red cells
Reticulocytes were held in the marrow, so more mature cells circulated
preguntas.explicacion: Interstitial fibroblasts in the kidney secrete erythropoietin when oxygen is low, which steps up erythrocyte production until oxygen delivery is restored; people living at high elevations therefore keep a higher hematocrit than those at sea level, and altitude is a recognized cause of a high hematocrit. Thrombopoietin drives platelets, and the spleen stores platelets, not the answer here.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a throat swab culture collected?
opciones: The head is tilted back, the mouth held wide open, and the swab rubbed at the back of the throat near the tonsils
The head is tilted forward, the tongue depressed, and the swab rolled along the inner surface of both cheeks
The head is tilted back, the mouth held wide open, and the swab rubbed over the tongue and under it
The head is tilted back 70 degrees and the swab passed through a nostril until it reaches the throat
preguntas.explicacion: The patient tilts the head back and opens wide while the sterile swab is rubbed along the back of the throat near the tonsils, and the provider may scrape several times to raise the chance of catching the organism. Gagging is expected and the patient has to resist closing the mouth. The tongue is deliberately avoided, the cheek is where a buccal swab goes, and the nostril route is the nasopharyngeal swab.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a $1,500 deductible and 20% coinsurance has paid nothing yet this year. The office visit is allowed at $125. What does he pay today?

$25, the coinsurance share, because the deductible applies only to hospital care
$100, the plan's share, with the remaining amount billed to him later
$0, because the plan pays first and bills him after the year is closed
preguntas.explicacion: Until the deductible is satisfied, the plan pays nothing toward covered services, so the patient owes the full allowed amount of the visit. The $25 figure is what he would owe on a $125 visit after the deductible, when the 20% coinsurance begins. Deductibles are not limited to hospital services, and the plan's share is what the plan pays, never something the patient is billed for.

100 per minute, from 300 divided by the small squares
20 per minute, from 300 divided by the small squares

Her share of the allowed amount doubles once she has used up the plan's yearly limit
The provider without a contract is paid twice as much by the plan for the same service
The provider without a contract must accept the plan's allowed amount as full payment

preguntas.pregunta: How is the radial pulse located at the wrist?

Two fingers are laid on the underside of the wrist, below the base of the little finger
The thumb is laid over the front of the wrist, in line with the middle finger tendon
Two fingers are laid on the back of the wrist, between the two prominent tendons

A written opinion from the evaluating healthcare professional, kept for 15 days

Flushing it down the toilet, which is safe for every unused medicine

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of vital signs is expected to rise together with a fever?
opciones: Heart rate and respiratory rate, because the febrile state raises oxygen demand
Heart rate and blood pressure, because the vessels constrict to conserve body heat
Respiratory rate and oxygen saturation, because ventilation clears the extra heat
Blood pressure and oxygen saturation, because cardiac output rises with the fever
preguntas.explicacion: Producing a fever is expensive: a rise of one degree Celsius takes 10% to 12.5% more metabolic work. Oxygen demand climbs, and heart rate and respiratory rate climb with it. That is why a fast pulse in a febrile patient is expected rather than surprising, and why a fast pulse may also signal infection or dehydration.

preguntas.pregunta: A blood gas report shows a pH of 7.40. Where does this fall relative to the normal range for blood?
opciones: Right at the average; normal is 7.35 to 7.45
Slightly acidic; normal is 7.45 to 7.55
At the low end; normal runs 7.40 to 7.50
Slightly alkaline; normal is 7.0, like pure water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood pH averages about 7.4, with a healthy range of 7.35 to 7.45, so a reading of 7.40 sits in the middle of normal. Blood is somewhat more alkaline than pure water, whose pH is 7.0, and it carries many buffers that keep the value steady. A range starting at 7.45 or 7.40 would wrongly turn a normal reading into a low one.

preguntas.pregunta: What defines a premature ventricular complex on the tracing?
opciones: An early QRS over 120 ms, usually with no P wave before it
An early QRS under 120 ms, usually with no P wave before it
An early QRS over 120 ms, always with a P wave before it
A late QRS over 120 ms, usually with two P waves before it
preguntas.explicacion: The beat arises in the ventricles, so it comes early, its shape is abnormal and it lasts longer than 120 ms. A large T wave of the opposite polarity typically follows it, and no P wave precedes it, because the impulse did not travel down from the atria.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates an intentional misrepresentation from a negligent one in a fraud claim?
opciones: The speaker knew the statement was false or was reckless about its truth
The speaker put the statement in writing rather than saying it out loud
The speaker gained money from the statement rather than only goodwill
The speaker made the statement to a group rather than to a single person
preguntas.explicacion: For an intentional misrepresentation the speaker must have known the statement was false or been reckless as to its truth, and must have intended the hearer to rely on it; the hearer then has to have relied reasonably and been harmed by relying. 1 hour for adults 18 and older

preguntas.pregunta: Where is an oral thermometer probe placed so that the reading is most reliable?
opciones: In the posterior sublingual pocket, with the lips closed around the instrument
In the buccal space between the cheek and the lower molars, with lips parted
On the middle of the tongue, held down by the patient with gentle pressure
Under the tip of the tongue, kept away from the frenulum and the lower teeth
preguntas.explicacion: The mouth is the most widely used site, but only one spot in it is dependable: the pocket under the back of the tongue, with the lips shut around the probe. preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, when may a laboratory report a patient's result from a nonwaived test system?

As soon as the instrument's internal electronic check has passed for that day's run of specimens
After the result has been confirmed by a second trained operator on the same instrument
Once the result has been compared with the patient's previous value in the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Control results have to meet the laboratory's, and where applicable the manufacturer's, criteria for acceptability before any patient result is reported, and every control procedure performed must be documented. preguntas.pregunta: What is tall man lettering used for on a medication label?

Capitalizing the whole name of any drug that carries a boxed warning
Capitalizing the first three letters of each generic name on the label
Capitalizing the unit of the dose so that mcg is never read as mg

preguntas.pregunta: What makes a laboratory result protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: An identifier linking it to a specific patient, such as a name, phone number or email
Only the patient's Social Security number or medical record number, not the name
Only the result itself, regardless of whether a name is attached
Only electronic storage; a printed result with a name attached is not PHI under the rule
preguntas.explicacion: Protected health information is health information that carries an identifier linking it to a specific patient, such as a name, Social Security number, telephone number, email or street address; the Privacy Rule specifies 18 such elements, and information about a patient's relatives, employers or household members counts too. PHI covers written, spoken, paper and electronic data of any size, inside or outside the facility. A result with all identifiers removed under the de-identification standard is no longer PHI.

preguntas.pregunta: Where is the basic rhythm of breathing generated?
opciones: In a network of neurons in the ventrolateral medulla oblongata
In the stretch receptors of the lung, which set the pace of each breath
In the carotid bodies, at the fork of the common carotid artery
In the diaphragm itself, whose muscle fibres contract rhythmically
preguntas.explicacion: A dense, symmetrical network of neurons in the ventrolateral part of the medulla generates and shapes the breathing rhythm and passes it to the motor neurons that drive the inspiratory and expiratory muscles. The lung receptors and the carotid bodies send feedback that modifies that rhythm; they do not create it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA violation carries a criminal penalty of up to $100,000 and up to 5 years in prison?
opciones: Obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information under false pretenses
Knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information
Selling identifiable health information for commercial advantage or malicious harm
Failing to correct a violation due to willful neglect within the required period
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal provisions have three tiers: knowingly obtaining or disclosing individually identifiable health information, up to $50,000 and 1 year; doing so under false pretenses, up to $100,000 and 5 years; and doing so with intent to sell, transfer or use it for commercial advantage, personal gain or malicious harm, up to $250,000 and 10 years. Criminal cases are handled by the Department of Justice and can reach employees, nurses, secretaries and telephone operators, not only institutions. Uncorrected willful neglect is the top civil tier, not a criminal one.

preguntas.pregunta: A febrile patient in early septic shock has pulses that feel unusually strong and full. How does that fit the picture?
opciones: Distributive shock can give bounding pulses early, from widened vessels
Bounding pulses rule shock out, since every form of shock weakens them
Bounding pulses with fever come from fluid moving out into the tissues
Bounding pulses point to hypovolemia, where vessels clamp down early
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse quality helps separate the kinds of shock. Hypovolemic shock gives weak or absent peripheral pulses, because there is little volume and the vessels constrict to compensate. Distributive shock, of which septic shock is the example, may give bounding pulses early on from peripheral vasodilation, so a full pulse does not rule the diagnosis out.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a possible exposure six weeks ago tests negative for HIV. What is explained?
opciones: A test more than three months after the last exposure is what rules it out
A negative result at six weeks rules out the infection with no further steps
A test more than three weeks after the last exposure is what rules it out
A negative result must be confirmed by a Western blot before it is reported
preguntas.explicacion: The window period is the stretch after transmission during which antigen and antibody are still undetectable. Most people turn positive within three weeks on a fourth-generation assay, but some take up to three months, so repeat testing at one and three months is offered and a test beyond three months is treated as conclusive.

preguntas.pregunta: A purple EDTA tube arrives in the laboratory with several small clots inside. Which collection error is associated with this finding?
opciones: The tube was not mixed enough after it was filled
The tube was inverted too many times in the figure-of-8 pattern
The tube was filled after the grey fluoride tube
The tube was drawn through a butterfly without a discard
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with anticoagulants need adequate mixing, for instance by inverting them in a figure-of-8 pattern, and inefficient mixing can leave small clots. Overmixing is the other extreme and leads to hemolysis, not clots. Drawing out of order risks additive carry-over, and the butterfly discard concerns air in the tubing, not clotting.

preguntas.pregunta: Detergent and water alone are considered adequate for cleaning which surfaces?

Those in exam rooms, once the visible soil has been picked up first
Those in a procedure room, provided no blood was spilled that session
Those that touch broken skin only briefly, such as hydrotherapy tanks
preguntas.explicacion: Detergent and water suffice in nonpatient-care areas such as administrative offices. Hydrotherapy tanks are noncritical surfaces treated with intermediate-level agents.

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient ran a half marathon yesterday and is booked for a draw this morning. Which instruction was missed?

Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity in the hour before
Outpatients should rest lying down for 15 minutes before the first tube
Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity for the whole week
preguntas.explicacion: Patients in the outpatient setting are to be kept from excessive physical activity within 24 hours of blood collection, and exercise is one of the things ruled out during a fast. preguntas.pregunta: A patient lets the cuffed arm hang at the side instead of resting it on the table. What follows?
opciones: The reading runs about 10 mm Hg high, since an unsupported arm raises the value
The reading runs about 10 mm Hg low, since the arm below the heart empties faster
The reading is unaffected as long as the cuff itself is at the level of the heart
The reading runs about 6 mm Hg high, the same amount as an unsupported back
preguntas.explicacion: An arm that is not supported adds roughly 10 mm Hg. The arm rests so that the middle of the cuff sits at the level of the right atrium: below that line the reading comes out higher, above it lower. The unsupported back and feet are a separate error worth about 6 mm Hg.

preguntas.pregunta: An OGTT is ordered for an inpatient who has been on bed rest with pneumonia for a week. What should the phlebotomist recognize?
opciones: The test is not appropriate in hospitalized, acutely ill or inactive patients
The test is appropriate if the load is raised to 100 g to offset the bed rest
The test is appropriate if a fingerstick meter replaces the venous samples
The test is appropriate if only the fasting and 2-hour samples are drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Glucose tolerance is impaired by bed rest, and the OGTT should not be performed in hospitalized, acutely ill or inactive patients, nor in anyone with an infection, traumatic injury or severe illness; the result would not be interpretable, so the provider should be told. Changing the load, the specimen or the number of samples does not fix the problem, and venous plasma at fasting and 2 hours is already the standard protocol.

preguntas.pregunta: Which law made sharing electronic health information the expected norm, and where do its exceptions live?
opciones: The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 171
The HITECH Act of 2009, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C
The Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015, with exceptions in 42 CFR Part 424
The Plain Writing Act of 2010, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 160

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist faxes a patient's lab results to the physician who ordered them. Does HIPAA require the patient's written authorization first?

Yes: any disclosure outside the facility requires a signed authorization
Yes, unless the patient signed the notice of privacy practices acknowledgment
No, but only because fax transmissions are outside the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may use or disclose protected health information for its own treatment, payment or health care operations, and may disclose it for the treatment activities of any health care provider, without an authorization; 45 CFR 164.506 sets that out and 164.502(a)(1)(ii) lists it among the permitted uses. preguntas.pregunta: Which side of the upper limb does each of the two main superficial veins drain?
opciones: The cephalic drains the radial side; the basilic drains the medial side
The cephalic drains the medial side; the basilic drains the radial side
Both drain the radial side, and the median cubital vein drains the medial
The cephalic drains the deep muscles; the basilic drains the skin only
preguntas.explicacion: The cephalic vein takes the radial, or thumb, side of the limb and the basilic takes the medial side; near the elbow the median cubital vein connects the two. When it affects more than 500 individuals nationwide, counted across all States
When it affects any number of individuals and involves an electronic device
When it affects fewer than 500 individuals but the entity cannot reach them by mail

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away after a skin puncture?
opciones: It may be contaminated with tissue fluid or debris such as sloughing skin
It is arterial in oxygen content, and the test needs a venous value
It contains the alcohol that has not yet dried, which hemolyses the sample
It is the drop richest in platelets, which would clump in the microtube
preguntas.explicacion: The first drop is wiped away because it may be contaminated with tissue fluid or debris (sloughing skin). Capillary blood is indeed similar to arterial blood in oxygen content, but that is not the reason here.

preguntas.pregunta: What makes an accidental arterial puncture more painful than a venous one?
opciones: Arteries have thicker walls and more nerves associated with them
Arteries have thinner walls and fewer nerves associated with them
Arteries carry a higher volume of blood at a much lower pressure
Arteries lie deeper and are always covered by the bicipital sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for a draw because they run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and carry more nerves with them, so puncturing one hurts more. The point matters at the elbow, where an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein and make that route the more painful choice.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a 24-hour urine collection at 7 a.m. asks what to do with the urine he passes at 7 a.m. on the first day. What is the correct instruction?
opciones: Void into the toilet and discard it; collect every void after that, including the 7 a.m. void the next morning
Collect it as the first specimen of the period, and stop with the last void before 7 a.m. the next morning
Void into the toilet and discard it, and also discard the 7 a.m. void of the next morning to keep exactly 24 hours
Collect it as a separate first-morning specimen for urinalysis, and start the timed collection with the next void
preguntas.explicacion: The period starts with an empty bladder: the void at the starting time goes into the toilet and is not kept. From then on all urine is saved for 24 hours, and the void at the same clock time the next morning is the last one collected and does go into the container. Keeping the opening void or dropping the closing void both shift the measured period. The container is refrigerated throughout.

In the same wording that went into the clinical note

A recap made by an assistant while the worker holds still

preguntas.pregunta: In the second step of blood typing, called back typing, what is mixed with red cells known to be type A and type B?
opciones: The patient's serum, to look for anti-A and anti-B antibodies
The patient's red cells, to look for the A antigen or B antigen
The patient's plasma with anti-D reagent, to look for Rh factor
The patient's whole blood, to look for clumping of the donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Blood typing has two steps. In ABO typing the sample's cells are mixed with anti-A and anti-B antibodies and watched for clumping. A 9-digit number the payer assigns to each provider it contracts with

preguntas.pregunta: One plan covers a woman because she still works for the employer; another covers her because she retired from a different one. Which is primary?
opciones: The plan covering the person as an active employee is the primary one
The plan covering the person as a retired employee is the primary one
The plan with the earlier effective date is the primary one for the claim
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday is the primary one
preguntas.explicacion: The plan covering a person as an active employee, meaning one who is neither laid off nor retired, is primary, and the plan covering that same person as retired or laid off is secondary; the same holds for a dependent of each. The rule is skipped when the non-dependent or dependent rule already settles the order, and it is ignored when the other plan has no such rule.

preguntas.pregunta: How is sinus bradycardia defined?
opciones: A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 60 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 40 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 80 beats per minute
Any irregular rhythm slower than 60 beats per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The depolarization still starts in the sinus node and the tracing still meets the criteria for sinus rhythm; only the rate is below 60. Most of these patients have no symptoms. There is a growing push to move the cut-off down to 50, since many healthy people rest between 50 and 60, but the accepted figure is still 60.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Pearls and Other Issues

preguntas.pregunta: In what order are these steps done after the payer adjudicates a claim?
opciones: The remittance arrives, payments are posted, adjustments are recorded, balances are billed
Payments are posted, the remittance arrives, balances are billed, adjustments are recorded
Balances are billed, payments are posted, the remittance arrives, adjustments are recorded
Adjustments are recorded, balances are billed, payments are posted, the remittance arrives
preguntas.explicacion: Once the payer approves the claim, an explanation of benefits or an electronic remittance advice is issued listing covered services and the reasons anything went unpaid; payments are then posted, and contractual and noncontractual write-offs are applied. Collecting the patient's portion comes last, in the patient collections step, once the office knows what the plan left unpaid.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a transcription vendor may start receiving electronic protected health information, what must the practice have in place?
opciones: A written business associate agreement obligating the vendor to safeguard the information
A signed authorization from every patient whose dictation the vendor is going to transcribe
A notice of privacy practices addressed to the vendor and acknowledged by its privacy official
An accounting of disclosures listing each record the vendor is expected to receive that year
preguntas.explicacion: Under the Security Rule a covered entity may let a business associate create, receive, maintain or transmit ePHI on its behalf only after obtaining satisfactory assurances through a contract or other written arrangement. preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports palpitations about once a month. Which monitoring gives the better chance of catching them?
opciones: A patch or loop recorder worn for about two weeks
A 24-hour Holter, since it records every single beat
A resting 12-lead tracing repeated at each office visit
An exercise stress test run on the treadmill protocol
preguntas.explicacion: The traditional monitor is the right choice when symptoms come every day. For palpitations that appear now and then, loop recorders and patch monitors have a better yield, and a two-week stretch is the balance usually struck between how much it finds and what it costs.

preguntas.pregunta: A lactose tolerance blood test is abnormal. What test is recommended afterwards, and why?
opciones: A glucose tolerance test, to rule out a problem absorbing glucose itself
A second lactose tolerance test, to confirm the result on another day
A blood culture set, to rule out bacterial overgrowth of the small bowel
A fasting glucose, to rule out the diabetes that flattens the lactose curve
preguntas.explicacion: An abnormal lactose blood test should be followed by a glucose tolerance test, which rules out a problem with the body's ability to absorb glucose: if glucose itself is poorly absorbed, the flat curve after lactose means nothing about lactase. Diabetes and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth are known causes of false negatives on the lactose test, not something a repeat or a culture would settle.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's problem list is blank, but during the medication review he lists several multivitamins and nutritional supplements. Why does that matter?
opciones: Supplement use can uncover a past bariatric surgery the patient did not report as an illness
Supplement use marks an underlying psychiatric condition such as generalized anxiety disorder
Products bought without a prescription are left out of reconciliation because no one ordered them
Nutritional supplements belong under allergies rather than on the list of current medications
preguntas.explicacion: Patients leave out what they do not think of as illness. A stack of vitamins and supplements is a clue to weight-loss surgery and the conditions that came with it, such as hyperlipidemia or sleep apnea. Benzodiazepines are the clue that points elsewhere, to a psychiatric diagnosis. Every product bought over the counter belongs on the medication list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Medical and Surgical History

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that results never be left as a message on his home phone, only mailed to his address. How is that request treated?
opciones: As a right: patients may say how information reaches them
As a courtesy the clinic may grant if its system allows it
As a restriction that needs the privacy officer's approval
As impossible, since results go out the way the system sends
preguntas.explicacion: The list of patient rights includes stating how one's information is to be handled and communicated to others; the example given is a patient who wants any message from the pharmacy or the hospital mailed to his home rather than left on his telephone. It sits beside the right to ask that disclosures be restricted and the right to receive an accounting of the disclosures that were made.

preguntas.pregunta: In lead V6 the ventricular complex shows a deep downstroke instead of the usual tall upright wave. What is suggested?
opciones: Record from a position further to the left, out at V7
Record from a position further to the right, back at V1
Drop V6 one intercostal space and run the tracing again
Raise the standardization and run the tracing again
preguntas.explicacion: V6 is expected to write a tall upward wave. When a deep S appears there instead, the guidance is to move out to the left and take V7, hunting for a pattern whose main deflection points up. Moving an electrode down a space is not part of that advice.

preguntas.pregunta: You are choosing a vein in the antecubital area. Which vein is the most common venipuncture site, and what does it connect?
opciones: The median cubital vein, linking the cephalic and basilic veins
The basilic vein, linking the median antebrachial and axillary veins
The cephalic vein, running superficially along the biceps brachii
The brachial vein, formed where the radial and ulnar veins join
preguntas.explicacion: Venous blood is drawn more often from the median cubital vein than from any other vein; it branches from the basilic vein in the antecubital region and crosses at an angle to join the cephalic vein, forming a V, and it lies very superficially in the roof of the cubital fossa, where it is easy to reach. The brachial vein is deep, formed by the radial and ulnar veins.

preguntas.pregunta: The clerk asks which of the panels she books usually need a fast. Which grouping is named among the common tests that do?
opciones: Blood glucose, a lipid panel and a basic metabolic panel
Blood glucose, a complete blood count and a coagulation panel
A lipid panel, a troponin test and a complete blood count
A basic metabolic panel, a troponin test and a strep screen
preguntas.explicacion: The tests said usually to require fasting are blood glucose tests, cholesterol level tests, that is the lipid panel, and the basic metabolic panel. Liver function tests and a renal function panel may also call for a fast in some cases. A blood count is part of a routine checkup, and troponin is a blood enzyme test used after a suspected heart attack.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What types of blood tests require fasting?; and MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, What are the different types of blood tests?

preguntas.pregunta: Which medication instruction is written the way the toolkit recommends?
opciones: "Take 1 pill in the morning and 1 pill at bedtime"
"Take twice daily", leaving the timing to the patient
"Take 1 pill every 12 hours around the clock as needed"
"Take as directed by the prescribing clinician"
preguntas.explicacion: Precise wording removes the guesswork: naming the standard time periods, morning, noon, evening and bedtime, tells the patient exactly when to take the dose, while "twice daily" invites errors when nobody knows the doses have to be spread out. The label should also carry a plain description of what the medicine is for.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 16: Prevent errors

preguntas.pregunta: Which opening question invites a patient to lay out their own concerns?
opciones: "What is the main reason you are seeking care today?"
"Has this pain been present for more than three days?"
"Would you rather have the lab drawn before the visit?"
"Did the last provider already start you on a medicine?"
preguntas.explicacion: The first question posed is usually open-ended, inviting the patient to share what brought them in and showing that someone is listening without judgment. The other three are focused questions: they gather a specific detail with a yes-or-no answer and belong later in the encounter.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who spends part of the year in another state asks about her telehealth visits. What does Part B cover through the end of 2027?
opciones: Services the patient can get from anywhere in the country, home included
Services the patient can get only from a clinic in a rural shortage area
Services the patient can get only while admitted to a hospital as inpatient
Services the patient can get only through a Medicare Advantage plan network
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth means medical or health services from a provider located somewhere else in the country, using audio and video technology or, in some cases, audio only. Through December 31, 2027, Part B covers telehealth the patient can get from anywhere in the United States, home included. Advance care planning, depression screening and speech therapy are among the examples.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Description and Coverage details

preguntas.pregunta: What is distinctive about how an accountable care organization is paid?
opciones: Payment is tied to quality goals and outcomes that lead to cost savings
Payment is a fixed sum per patient each month regardless of services used
Payment is made for each separate service the providers happen to furnish
Payment is a single lump sum covering one episode of care from start to end
preguntas.explicacion: The organization's payment is tied to reaching health care quality goals and outcomes that result in cost savings. An ACO that both delivers high-quality care and spends more wisely may share in the savings it earns for Medicare, called performance payments. Capitation, fee for service and bundled episode payment are the other arrangements.

preguntas.pregunta: A methotrexate level is being sent to the laboratory. Under which transport condition will the specimen be accepted?
opciones: Carried on ice and protected from light
Carried at room temperature in a gel tube
Carried frozen at –20 °C in an EDTA tube
Carried at 37 °C in a heated transport block
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples for methotrexate measurement are accepted only if they were carried on ice and in the dark; specimens transported otherwise are rejected. The same passage assigns EDTA whole blood to cyclosporine monitoring and bans gel tubes for drug levels, so the distractors combine real rules from neighbouring drugs with conditions the source never gives for methotrexate.

preguntas.pregunta: A pregnant patient is due for group B strep screening. Which specimen is collected, and when?
opciones: A swab of the vagina plus the rectum, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
A cervical swab taken with a speculum, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
A swab of the vagina plus the rectum, usually between 12 and 14 weeks of pregnancy
A clean-catch urine specimen only, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: Group B strep lives in the vagina and rectum, so screening uses a swab of both sites, and the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists puts the timing at 36 to 38 weeks; a patient who goes into labor earlier may be tested then. A urine test is the other option offered, not the only one. A positive result means antibiotics during labor to protect the baby.

preguntas.pregunta: In addition to anchoring the vein, what does the WHO's Step 6 ask the patient to do so the veins stand out?
opciones: Form a fist
Pump the hand
Lower the arm
Hold a breath
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 lists three actions in sequence: anchor the vein with a thumb below the site, ask the patient to make a fist so the veins are more prominent, and enter the vein swiftly at 30 degrees or less. Pumping the hand, dangling the arm and breath-holding are not part of the WHO procedure; the warm compress and tapping are the only other vein-raising measures in the material.

preguntas.pregunta: What do the two ends of the numeric rating scale for pain stand for?
opciones: Zero is no pain at all and ten is the worst pain the patient can imagine
Zero is mild pain and ten is the point at which analgesia becomes mandatory
Zero is no pain at all and five is the worst pain the patient can imagine
One is the least pain measurable and ten is the average pain of childbirth
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs from 0, no pain, to 10, the worst possible pain. It is quick and widely used but crude, and the number is worth more when the patient is asked to explain it: a 1 usually means a bump or a bruise, while a 10 is compared to childbirth or passing a kidney stone. A high number alone does not decide the treatment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: How is lead aVR produced from the limb electrodes?
opciones: The right arm is the positive one and the others a common ground
The left arm is the positive one and the others a common ground
The right leg is the positive one and the others a common ground
The right arm and the left leg are paired against each other
preguntas.explicacion: The augmented leads take one limb as the positive pole and use the remaining limb electrodes together as a common ground: the right arm for aVR, the left arm for aVL and the left leg for aVF. Pairing two electrodes against each other is how leads I to III work.

preguntas.pregunta: Which groups of laboratory parameters can be distorted by venous stasis from a prolonged tourniquet?
opciones: Biochemistry and coagulation factors
Blood cultures and HLA tissue typing
Glucose only, once fluoride is added
Hematology counts only, in the EDTA tube
preguntas.explicacion: In recommending venous illumination devices over prolonged tourniquet use, the chapter says venous stasis from a long application can negatively affect several parameters, naming biochemistry and coagulation factors. The coagulopathies review agrees, asking for minimal tourniquet time to avoid artifacts in clotting tests. Cultures and HLA typing are not among the parameters the chapter lists.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops a rash where the electrode patches were. How is that handled?
opciones: It usually clears when the patches come off and needs no care
It usually clears once an antihistamine cream has been applied
It means the test cannot be repeated on that patient again
It means the gel was left on too long and must be reported
preguntas.explicacion: Skin sensitivity to the adhesive gel is the one complication of a test that is otherwise safe and non-invasive. It settles as soon as the patches are taken off and in most cases needs no treatment at all, although a known allergy to the adhesive is noted as a relative contraindication.

preguntas.pregunta: A retiree's former employer plan pays after Medicare and is paying nothing at all. What does the coordination guidance suggest checking first?
opciones: Whether she signed up for Part B, which a secondary group plan may require of her
Whether she signed up for Part D, which a secondary group plan may require of her
Whether she bought a Medigap policy, which a secondary group plan may require
Whether she met the Part A deductible, which a secondary group plan may require
preguntas.explicacion: Where a group health plan or retiree coverage is the secondary payer, the patient may need to sign up for Medicare Part B before that plan will pay anything. It is the ordinary reason a retiree plan that looks like real coverage pays nothing. Coverage changes should be reported to the doctor and to the provider at the time of care, and questions about who pays first go to the coordination center.

preguntas.pregunta: Interference on a tracing has blurred the P waves in every lead. What follows?
opciones: The strip is run again: the P wave has to be plainly visible
The strip is kept: only the QRS complexes have to be visible
The strip is kept and the interference is noted on the log
The strip is run again only if the QRS is blurred as well
preguntas.explicacion: One of the minimum standards is a complex clearly drawn with the P wave in plain view, with no noise obscuring or wiping it out. Because the tracing is reviewed before the patient leaves, a strip below the standard is repeated rather than filed.

preguntas.pregunta: Before handing a batch of samples to the courier, what final check does the WHO procedure place immediately before dispatch?
opciones: Rechecking the labels on the tubes against the forms
Recentrifuging any tube whose serum looks cloudy
Re-verifying the patient's fasting status by telephone
Recording the tourniquet time for each tube on the form
preguntas.explicacion: After the draw, hand hygiene and waste disposal, the WHO sequence has the phlebotomist recheck the labels on the tubes and the forms before dispatch, then inform the patient that the procedure is over and check the puncture site. Patient-sample matching, that is labelling, and the transportation conditions are two of the factors WHO lists as influencing laboratory results during collection and transport, alongside needle gauge, insertion site and the correct tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter needs a urine culture. From where should the specimen be taken?
opciones: Never from the drainage bag, whose contents are considered contaminated
From the drainage bag, after mixing it so the sample is representative
From the drainage bag, provided it was emptied less than 2 hours earlier
From the drainage bag, after adding boric acid to stop any overgrowth
preguntas.explicacion: When a catheter is already in place, urine that has pooled in the collection bag is regarded as contaminated and is never used for culture, no matter how recently the bag was emptied or what preservative is added afterward. Patients with a permanent catheter often carry bacteria in the urine without true infection, which is called colonization, and bag urine would exaggerate that.

At least seven years, matching the rule for orders and certifications
At least ten years, matching the rule for Medicare Advantage organizations
For the duration of care plus thirty years, matching the OSHA employee rule

preguntas.pregunta: Which pair appears among the contributing factors named for laboratory testing errors?

Delayed billing and missing diagnosis codes on the form
Ordering too few tests for a complex discharge diagnosis
Holding serum at 2 to 8 degrees before serological testing

preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes a disease whose cause is unknown, and which describes one that is present at birth?
opciones: Idiopathic for the unknown cause; congenital for present at birth
Congenital for the unknown cause; idiopathic for present at birth
Hereditary for the unknown cause; idiopathic for present at birth
Acute for the unknown cause; hereditary for present at birth
preguntas.explicacion: Idiopathic describes a disease of unknown cause. Congenital means a condition or trait present at birth, which may be genetic or not. preguntas.pregunta: A menstruating patient asks when in the month to do a breast self-exam.
opciones: About three to five days after her period starts, at the same time each month
About three to five days before her period starts, at the same time each month
On the first day of her period, when the tissue is at its most tender
Halfway between two periods, which is when the tissue is most nodular
preguntas.explicacion: Three to five days after the period begins the breasts are least tender and least lumpy, which makes changes easier to notice; the point is to repeat it on the same schedule every month. After menopause, the same day of each month is used instead. Experts do not agree on whether the practice finds cancers or saves lives.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic decides that stopper colour alone will tell staff in what sequence to fill tubes. What problem remains?
opciones: The sequence still has to be followed; colour by itself does not enforce it
Stopper colours are identical between manufacturers, so the risk is covered
Colour tells the phlebotomist how many inversions each tube will need
Colour identifies the additive, so carry-over between tubes cannot happen
preguntas.explicacion: Colour coding makes the tubes easy to tell apart, but an incorrect collection still follows when the sequence is not respected, which is why training matters. Colour codes can also differ from one laboratory to another, so they should be checked locally rather than assumed.

preguntas.pregunta: How long is the strip captured by a standard resting recording?
opciones: Ten seconds, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Three minutes, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Sixty seconds, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Ten minutes, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
preguntas.explicacion: Everything else in the preparation leads up to a ten-second recording, which is why the patient must be settled before it starts. That same ten seconds is what makes the count-and-multiply method work when the rhythm is too irregular for the square methods.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient spills hot coffee on the hand and the skin is unbroken and red. What is the first aid?
opciones: Cool running water or a cool bath for at least 5 to 30 minutes
An ice water bath for at least 5 minutes, then a snug bandage
A layer of butter or ointment at once, then a dry sterile gauze
A cold pack held on the skin for 20 minutes with firm pressure
preguntas.explicacion: Cool water, not ice water, is run over the burn or the part is soaked for 5 to 30 minutes; a clean, cold, wet towel eases the pain. Afterward the area is covered with a dry sterile bandage and protected from pressure and friction. Butter, oil, ice, creams and household remedies do not go on a burn.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Burns", First Aid: Minor burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: After explaining a 24-hour urine collection, the assistant asks the patient whether he understands. Why does that question not count as teach-back?
opciones: It can be answered yes or no, and patients tend to say yes whether they followed it or not
It tests the patient's memory instead of checking how well the explanation was delivered
It has to be asked at the very end of the visit, once every instruction has been given
It should be put to the caregiver, who is the person actually carrying out the collection
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back asks patients to say in their own words what they need to know or do. Questions that can be closed with a yes, such as asking whether something makes sense, are explicitly not teach-back, because a yes comes just as easily from someone who missed the point. The framing that works puts the burden on the explainer, not on the patient.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k40 · CCMA 6 k199 therapeutic communication · CMA II.F.3.a level of understanding

preguntas.pregunta: 'Do you understand the fasting instructions?' 'Yes.' Why does this exchange fail as teach-back?
opciones: It is a yes-or-no question; patients tend to say yes whether or not they understood
It tests the patient's memory, which is exactly what teach-back is designed to do anyway
It was asked in the middle of the visit rather than at the very end of it
It was asked of the patient instead of the companion who will supervise the fast
preguntas.explicacion: 'Do you understand?' and 'Does that make sense?' are not teach-back questions, because patients are likely to answer yes either way. Teach-back asks the patient to state in their own words what they need to know or do, is not a test of memory, and should be done in chunks during the visit rather than saved for the end.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method, Action
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: Which right does a hospitalized patient have over the plan of care?
opciones: To be informed of their status, take part in planning, and refuse treatment
To be informed of their status and to demand any treatment they have read about
To take part in planning only when a family representative is at the bedside
To refuse treatment only after a second physician has documented agreement
preguntas.explicacion: The patient, or their representative where state law allows one, has the right to make informed decisions: to be told their health status, to be involved in care planning and treatment, and to request or refuse treatment. That right explicitly does not become a way to demand services judged medically unnecessary or inappropriate, and no second signature is needed to refuse.
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · CMA E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant prepares a controlled substance prescription for the prescriber to sign. Who carries the responsibility if it does not meet the regulation?
opciones: The prescribing practitioner, with a corresponding liability resting on the pharmacist
The medical assistant who prepared it, because the preparation was where it went wrong
The pharmacy technician who entered it, because dispensing is the last step in the chain
Nobody, as long as the practitioner signed it the way a legal document would be signed
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation lets a secretary or agent prepare a prescription for the practitioner's signature, but it puts the responsibility on the prescribing practitioner when the prescription does not conform in all essential respects to the law and the regulations, and it places a corresponding liability on the pharmacist who fills one that is not in the form the DEA requires, a central fill pharmacist included.
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are recommended to have a bone density scan on the basis of age alone?
opciones: All women from 65 years upward, repeated no more often than every 1 to 2 years
All women from 50 years upward, repeated no more often than every 1 to 2 years
All women from 65 years upward, repeated once every six months after the first
All adults from 65 years upward, repeated no more often than every 5 to 10 years
preguntas.explicacion: Age by itself triggers the scan for women at 65 and over, and it is not repeated more often than every one to two years. Below 65 it takes a risk factor: a fracture since menopause, a known medical cause of bone loss, low body weight, a parental hip fracture or current tobacco use. A T-score of -2.5 or lower is the density that defines the disease.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Osteoporosis in Females", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k45 · CMA I.A.5.e

preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old comes for a lipid panel with her mother, who agrees to the draw. Which term describes what the mother gives?
opciones: Informed permission
Informed consent
Pediatric assent
Implied consent
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically under 18, cannot give informed consent; parents or legal guardians permit the intervention instead, and that process is called informed permission. Assent is what the child may add, valuable when reasonable. The exception to the rule is the legally emancipated minor, who consents alone.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Children
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: Why is air pushed into a vial before the medication is drawn out of it?
opciones: A vial is a closed system, and the air maintains the pressure gradient inside
The air pushes the rubber seal outward so that the needle pierces it easily
The air is what dissolves a powdered medication before it can be drawn up
The air replaces what was lost from the vial when its plastic cap came off
preguntas.explicacion: A vial is a closed system, so air matching the amount to be withdrawn is injected first to keep the pressure gradient that lets the solution come out. The vial is then turned upside down above the syringe and the plunger drawn to the mark, with the needle tip kept inside the medication and any large bubbles purged. A multi-dose vial is labelled with the date it was opened; a single-use vial is discarded after one use.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Preparing Medications, Vials
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.h(i)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in acute kidney failure has produced no urine at all. Which term names that finding, and how is it built?
opciones: Anuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Dysuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Polyuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Nocturia: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
preguntas.explicacion: The prefix a- or an- means without or lacking, and the ending -uria means in the urine, so anuria is the absence of urine. The distractors reuse the same ending with other prefixes: dys- is difficult or abnormal, and poly- is many or excessive, which is why polyuria is a large output rather than none.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of roots would you expect to see in the terms used by a cardiology practice?
opciones: cardi/o for the heart, angi/o for a vessel, phleb/o for a vein
cardi/o for the heart, aden/o for a vessel, hepat/o for a vein
coron/o for the heart, arthr/o for a vessel, nephr/o for a vein
my/o for the heart, thromb/o for a vessel, splen/o for a vein
preguntas.explicacion: Cardi- and coron- both name the heart, angi- and vasculo- name a blood vessel, and phleb- and ven- name a vein. The roots in the wrong answers belong elsewhere: aden- is a gland, hepat- the liver, arthr- a joint, nephr- the kidney, thromb- a clot and splen- the spleen.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A report describes the femur as a long bone and a carpal as a short bone. What separates the two classes?
opciones: A long bone is longer than it is wide; a short bone is roughly cube shaped
A long bone is thicker than it is wide; a short bone is thin and curved
A long bone has spongy tissue only; a short bone has compact tissue only
A long bone is found in the limbs only; a short bone is found in the skull
preguntas.explicacion: Bones fall into four shapes. Long bones are longer than they are wide, with a shaft and two bulky ends, and make up the thigh, leg, arm and forearm. Short bones are about as tall as they are wide, like the wrist and ankle bones. Flat bones are thin and curved, as in most of the cranium, and the rest are irregular.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Skeletal System: Classification of Bones
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a Mobitz type II block carry more weight than a Mobitz type I?
opciones: It sits below the node and usually calls for a permanent pacemaker
It sits above the node and usually settles without any treatment
It drops every second beat, which the type I block never does
It stretches the PR interval, which the type I block never does
preguntas.explicacion: Type II usually arises below the atrioventricular node, at the level of the His bundle. It marks severe underlying heart disease that can progress to complete block and usually calls for a pacemaker, while most patients with type I have no symptoms at all.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Heart Block
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i

preguntas.pregunta: In an adult finger-prick, why is a 2.2 mm lancet the longest typically used?
opciones: Because the puncture depth should not go beyond 2.4 mm, and pressure makes the puncture deeper than the lancet
Because the puncture depth should not go beyond 2.2 mm, and the lancet must match that limit exactly
Because the skin-to-bone distance on the side of an adult finger averages 2.33 mm
Because lancets longer than 2.2 mm are made only as surgical blades, which the WHO prohibits
preguntas.explicacion: The lancet chosen is slightly shorter than the estimated depth needed, because pressure compresses the skin and the puncture ends up slightly deeper than the lancet length. Since a finger-prick should not go beyond 2.4 mm, a 2.2 mm lancet is the longest typically used. The 2.33 mm figure is the posterior heel of a 3 kg baby, and surgical blades are prohibited for any skin puncture.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2 and 7.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet length · PBT II.J lancets · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.5 equipment

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient is slow to answer the pre-draw questions. What should you do?
opciones: Slow down, give him time to process, and do not interrupt him
Fill each silence by suggesting the answer you think is likely
Ask the questions in rapid succession so he finishes before tiring
Skip the interview and rely on what the requisition already says
preguntas.explicacion: Avoid hurrying older patients: some struggle with rapid-fire questioning or torrents of information, so speak more slowly, give time to process, and do not interrupt, because once interrupted a patient is less likely to reveal all concerns. Supplying answers or skipping the interview loses the allergy, fainting and fasting information the WHO interview exists to collect.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2L k15 k40 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: Breast cancer has spread to the lung. Which cells does the pathologist find in the lung tumor?
opciones: Breast cancer cells, because a metastasis keeps the type of the primary tumor
Lung cancer cells, because a metastasis takes the type of the organ it reaches
A mix of both, because a metastasis blends the primary and the new tissue
Neither, because a metastasis is made of scar tissue rather than tumor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells from the place where they first formed to another part of the body: the cells break away from the primary tumor, travel through the blood or the lymph system and start a new tumor. The new growth is the same type of cancer as the original, so breast cancer in the lung is still breast cancer.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, metastasis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A lead wire on the machine is found with frayed insulation. What is done?
opciones: The unit is left unused and the problem is reported at once
The unit is used and the wire is taped up for the rest of the day
The back of the unit is opened so the wire can be replaced
The unit is used for the limb leads until a repair is arranged
preguntas.explicacion: The unit is grounded, so a shock is highly unlikely, but the rule is firm: if a short happens or frayed wiring turns up, the equipment is not used. The cover and the back are never removed by the technician, and the damage is reported straight away.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 6.1 Equipment Precautions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no health care background looks lost while an assistant explains a procedure. Which barrier fits best?
opciones: Jargon the receiver does not share with the sender
Physiological pain that blocks what the patient recalls
Hallway noise, a loud television and overhead paging
A stress response running in the sender and the receiver
preguntas.explicacion: Medical terminology, complicated words and slang build a barrier the sender creates without noticing; the fix is plain language a person outside health care can follow. Noise, pain and the stress response are barriers too, but none of them is what the scenario describes.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why single-use lancing devices and glucose meters are never shared between patients without cleaning.
opciones: Blood-contaminated devices have been implicated in hepatitis B outbreaks
Shared devices lose their calibration and read the glucose far too low
Shared devices carry latex particles from one patient's skin to the next
Shared devices void the manufacturer's warranty on the meter and lancets
preguntas.explicacion: Reusable finger-prick devices and point-of-care instruments such as glucose meters, once contaminated with blood, have been linked to outbreaks of hepatitis B. The rule that follows is plain: common-use items are visibly clean before they touch a patient, and single-use items are not reused.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Avoidance of contaminated phlebotomy equipment
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality · CPT D3 3B k54 k58 · D1 1K k32 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.B.4 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found unresponsive at the bottom of a staircase and a neck injury is suspected. How is the airway opened?
opciones: By pushing the jaw forward without tilting the head or turning the neck
By tilting the head back and lifting the chin with two fingers
By turning the head to one side so that the tongue falls forward
By placing a folded towel under the shoulders to extend the neck
preguntas.explicacion: When a cervical spine injury cannot be ruled out, the jaw is thrust forward and the head is left alone, and the mouth is not allowed to close. The head tilt-chin lift is the standard maneuver only when no spinal injury is suspected. A patient with a possible spinal injury is moved by two people so head and neck do not twist.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Airway Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether electricity will be passed through the body. What is the answer?
opciones: No: the test is painless and no current is sent through
Yes: a small current goes through and may feel like a tingle
Yes: a current is sent only while the chest leads record
No: but the patches themselves can give a mild shock
preguntas.explicacion: The machine listens rather than stimulates: the test is painless and nothing is sent through the body. The electrodes may feel cold when they are first applied, and in rare cases a rash or irritation appears where the patches were, which is worth saying in advance.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1

preguntas.pregunta: The label on a drum of laboratory reagent is smeared and hard to read. What does the Hazard Communication standard require of the laboratory?
opciones: Labels on incoming containers must not be removed or defaced
Labels may be replaced with the in-house number of the reagent
Labels may be taken off once the sheet is filed in the binder
Labels must be covered with tape until the drum is emptied out
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are covered by the Hazard Communication standard in a reduced way, and the first of those duties is that labels on incoming containers of hazardous chemicals are not removed or defaced. The others are keeping the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments and making them readily accessible during each work shift, and giving employees the information and training of paragraph (h). Filing the sheet does not release the container from carrying its own warning.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(i) and (b)(3)(ii), application to laboratories
preguntas.subtema: Labels on incoming containers · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who needs as much support as possible is being taught to walk on crutches. Which gait pattern gives it?
opciones: The four-point gait: left crutch, right leg, right crutch, then left leg
The two-point gait: left crutch with right leg, then right crutch with left leg
The swing-to gait: both crutches forward, then both legs brought up to them
The three-point gait: both crutches with the injured leg, then the sound leg
preguntas.explicacion: Of the patterns taught, the four-point provides the most support: each crutch and each leg moves on its own, one at a time. The two-point pairs a crutch with the opposite leg, the swing-to sends both crutches out and then both legs, and the three-point — the one used most often — moves both crutches with the injured leg.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b · CCMA 3B4 k65

preguntas.pregunta: How many essential vitamins does the body require, and how are they grouped?
opciones: Thirteen, grouped as fat-soluble and water-soluble
Thirteen, grouped as animal-source and plant-source
Nine, grouped as fat-soluble and water-soluble
Twenty, grouped as essential and conditionally essential
preguntas.explicacion: Thirteen vitamins are essential, meaning the body cannot work properly without them, and they split into two groups by how they dissolve: fat-soluble and water-soluble. Nine is the count of the water-soluble group alone. A few vitamin-like nutrients, choline and carnitine, are also needed but are not counted among the thirteen.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Vitamins
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(e) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA B.21

preguntas.pregunta: What separates sterilization from every other level of processing used on patient-care items?
opciones: It destroys or eliminates every form of microbial life, bacterial spores included
It wipes out many or all pathogens on an object but leaves bacterial spores alive
It takes visible soil off an object with water plus a detergent or enzymatic product
It lowers the count enough that the object is safe to handle, use or throw away
preguntas.explicacion: Sterilization is meant as an absolute: nothing microbial survives it, spores included. Disinfection stops short of that, since it is not sporicidal. Cleaning only lifts the visible soil off, and decontamination is what makes a used item safe for staff to handle. They are consecutive steps, not synonyms, and only one of them is absolute.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Definition of Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k104 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.7

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for culture is collected into a container with boric acid preservative, and the ward also wants a dipstick from the same cup. What should be expected?
opciones: The dipstick leukocyte reagent may be less sensitive and the initial pH altered, though the bacteria are preserved
The dipstick glucose and urobilinogen may read falsely positive, though the bacteria are preserved for culture
The dipstick leukocyte esterase may read falsely negative, and the culture will fail to grow at any concentration
The dipstick albumin may read falsely positive, and the bacteria will be killed within the first hour of storage
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the preservative commonly used to keep bacteria alive in urine, but it can reduce the sensitivity of the leukocyte reagent on the dipstick and change the initial pH, and in excessive concentration it can even prevent bacterial growth in the sample sent for culture. False-positive glucose and urobilinogen are the formaldehyde pattern, a false-negative leukocyte esterase belongs to mercury salts, and thymol gives false-positive albumin.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (Preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.8.c(3)

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a drug taken by inhalation act quickly?
opciones: It crosses the wide surface of the respiratory epithelium into pulmonary circulation
It is swallowed with the saliva and taken up by the very vascular gastric mucosa
It diffuses through the single-layered epithelium of the nasal passage into the veins
It is absorbed by the small intestine, whose surface is the largest one in the body
preguntas.explicacion: An inhaled drug spreads over the large surface of the respiratory tract and passes into the pulmonary circulation, entering the systemic circulation through the pulmonary vein and skipping first-pass metabolism. Particles of roughly 1 to 10 micrometres deliver best, and how much arrives also depends on the patient's tidal volume and inspiratory velocity. The nasal epithelium is a separate route with its own path.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Other Routes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(5) · RMA III.G.4.d(vii)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient needs HLA tissue typing (ACD tube), a CBC and a plasma glucose. Following the WHO table, which tube is filled second?
opciones: The pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing
The purple EDTA haematology tube for the CBC
The light grey sodium fluoride tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 puts EDTA at position 8, the pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies at position 9, and the grey oxalate/fluoride glucose tube at position 10. The purple tube therefore goes first, the ACD tube second and the grey tube last. No heparin tube is ordered here, and it would sit at position 6 in any case.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has just received an opioid analgesic becomes very drowsy and breathes slowly. Which class effect is this?
opciones: Respiratory depression, one of the effects opioid receptors produce everywhere
Serotonin syndrome, which follows any single opioid dose within a few minutes
Hyperalgesia from opioids, which shows up with the first dose in most patients
Anticholinergic toxicity, seen as dry mouth, retention and slowed breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Opioid receptors sit inside and outside the nervous system, so the class produces a wide spread of effects: dysphoria or euphoria, sedation, respiratory depression, constipation, bradycardia, nausea, vomiting, itching and pinpoint pupils. Tolerance and hyperalgesia come from long-term use, not from a first dose, and serotonin syndrome needs a serotonergic opioid combined with another serotonergic drug.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Opioid Analgesics", Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3

preguntas.pregunta: An instruction sheet reads “The form must be returned before the visit.” What does plain language guidance advise?
opciones: Name who acts: “You must return the form before the visit”
Add a heading above it so the section is easier to scan
Move it to the future tense so the deadline reads as clearer
Turn the verb into a noun: “Return of the form is required”
preguntas.explicacion: Active voice makes clear who does what and removes any doubt about who is responsible; passive sentences often hide the actor and are called one of the biggest problems in government writing. Short sections help, but they do not fix the sentence. The future tense and nouns made out of verbs are the two habits the same guidance tells writers to drop.
preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Plain language guides: Writing for understanding, Use the active voice
preguntas.subtema: Written communication · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2C k19 · CMA F.5 / 2027 F.3

preguntas.pregunta: Besides confirming that a vein is suitable, what practical decision does the WHO say locating the vein helps the phlebotomist make?
opciones: The correct size of needle to use
Whether a tourniquet is needed
How many tubes one puncture yields
Which antiseptic to apply
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says that the vein should be visible without the tourniquet and that locating it will help in determining the correct needle size; Chapter 3 repeats that the gauge is chosen to fit comfortably into the most prominent vein. The antiseptic is fixed at 70% alcohol for routine draws, and the WHO does not tie the number of tubes to the vein found.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3; and Section 3.2.2, Choice of gauge

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes microaggressions from macroaggressions?
opciones: Micro: brief everyday slights between individuals; macro: overt and rooted in systems
Micro: always intentional insults; macro: unconscious and unintended snubs
Micro: cause no measurable harm; macro: the only form that causes real harm
Micro: only spoken remarks; macro: only physical acts of exclusion
preguntas.explicacion: Macroaggressions are overt, radical discrimination embedded in a society or system, with internment camps and the Tuskegee study as examples, and microaggressions are short everyday insults or snubs, often unintentional and rooted in unconscious bias, delivered verbally or non-verbally in one-on-one interactions. Repeated microaggressions cause documented harm.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", section Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: Setting prions aside, which organisms sit at the top of the resistance scale to chemical germicides?
opciones: Bacterial spores, above coccidia, mycobacteria, small nonlipid viruses, fungi and vegetative bacteria
Mycobacteria, above bacterial spores, coccidia, fungi, vegetative bacteria and small nonlipid viruses
Lipid viruses, above vegetative bacteria, fungi, mycobacteria, coccidia and the bacterial spores
Vegetative bacteria, above fungi, small nonlipid viruses, mycobacteria, coccidia and lipid viruses
preguntas.explicacion: Bacterial spores hold the highest innate resistance of all, and the ladder descends from them through coccidia, mycobacteria, small nonlipid viruses, fungi, vegetative bacteria and finally lipid or medium-sized viruses such as herpes and HIV. Each group resists for its own reason: the spore coat and cortex act as a barrier, and mycobacteria have a waxy wall.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Innate Resistance of Microorganisms
