preguntas.pregunta: A resting strip on a young competitive athlete is regular at 52 per minute with normal P waves. How does the material read that?
opciones: As sinus bradycardia, common in athletes and during sleep
As sinus arrhythmia, common in athletes and during sleep
As a junctional rhythm, common in athletes while resting
As a first-degree block, common in athletes while resting
preguntas.explicacion: A slow sinus rhythm turns up as an incidental finding in many healthy adults, and it is described as common in athletes and during sleep, where the vagal tone that slows the sinus node is higher. Every criterion of sinus rhythm still holds except the rate.

preguntas.pregunta: Spaulding showed that killing ten spores took 30 minutes while killing 100,000 took 3 hours. What does that demonstrate?
opciones: The larger the microbial load, the longer a germicide needs, which is why cleaning matters
The larger the microbial load, the more concentrated the germicide has to be to work at all
Spores multiply inside a germicide bath, so the exposure has to outrun their growth rate
Exposure time counts more than the germicide chosen, so any product works if left long enough
preguntas.explicacion: With every other condition held constant, more microbes means more time to destroy them. That is the argument for scrupulous cleaning before disinfection or sterilization: cutting the number of organisms that must be inactivated widens the margin of safety and shortens the exposure needed to kill the whole load. Clumped cells are also harder to inactivate than separated ones.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Number and Location of Microorganisms

preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old patient with thin, fragile skin has just finished a recording. How are the electrodes taken off?
opciones: The wires come off first, then each electrode by its tab
The electrodes come off first, then the wires from the tabs
The wires and the electrodes come away together in one pull
The wires stay attached until all the copies have printed
preguntas.explicacion: The lead wires are lifted off the electrodes first, and only then is each electrode removed by pulling gently on its tab; they are thrown away after that single use. The step is done carefully because it can hurt and injure the skin, above all in older patients.

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR is ordered along with a CBC. Which tube is used for the ESR specimen, and can it be shared with other tests?
opciones: It goes in a black-top ESR tube with 3.2% citrate or a lavender EDTA tube, and is not shared with other tests
It goes in the same lavender EDTA tube as the CBC, and the leftover blood is used for the sedimentation
It goes in a light blue citrate tube filled to 90%, and it can be shared with any PT ordered on the same draw
It goes in a plain red tube, and the serum is transferred to the Westergren tube in the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is usually collected in a black-top ESR vacuum tube containing 3.2% sodium citrate; whole blood in a lavender EDTA tube is also acceptable, and the sample must stay in its own ESR-designated tube because of the volume the test needs, so it cannot be shared. The test is run on anticoagulated whole blood, never on serum.

preguntas.pregunta: Which two rhythms are shockable?
opciones: Ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Ventricular fibrillation and asystole after two minutes of CPR
Atrial fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Asystole and pulseless electrical activity with a slow rate
preguntas.explicacion: Once either of those two is recognized, the patient is defibrillated at once, with 120 to 200 joules on a biphasic device or 360 joules on a monophasic one. Speed matters: survival was 39.3% with prompt defibrillation against 22.2% when it was delayed by two minutes or more.

Correction of a diagnosis code after the claim has been paid
Notification that a payer has changed its own fee schedule
Certification that a provider's state license is still current

preguntas.pregunta: Which combination of vital signs makes up Cushing's triad?
opciones: Irregular respirations, high blood pressure and a slow pulse
Irregular respirations, low blood pressure and a fast pulse
Rapid shallow respirations, high blood pressure and a fast pulse
Rapid deep respirations, low blood pressure and a slow pulse
preguntas.explicacion: The triad is irregular breathing, hypertension and bradycardia, and it is the body's answer to rising intracranial pressure. It signals that herniation of the brain is near and calls for immediate action, which is why the three values are read together and not one at a time.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: How quickly must an employer report a work-related fatality, and a work-related inpatient hospitalization, to OSHA?
opciones: A fatality within 8 hours; a hospitalization within 24 hours
A fatality within 24 hours; a hospitalization within 8 hours
Both within 72 hours, by telephone to the area office
Both within 60 days, on the OSHA 300A summary
preguntas.explicacion: Under the recordkeeping rule updated in 2015, as summarized in OSHA's Hospitals eTool, employers report every work-related fatality within 8 hours of learning of it, and every work-related inpatient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours. Reports can be made by phone to the nearest area office, to the 24-hour OSHA hotline at 1-800-321-6742, or through the online serious event form. The 300A summary is an annual posting, not a reporting channel, and 60 days is the HIPAA breach notification limit.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is counted as a fall risk factor in an older adult, defined by a specific number?
opciones: Polypharmacy, which is defined as taking more than four medications
Polypharmacy, which is defined as taking more than two medications
Age, which starts to count as a risk factor from 65 years upward
Body weight, which counts as a risk factor from 30 kilograms upward
preguntas.explicacion: The risk list is headed by a history of falls, impaired balance and reduced muscle strength, and it includes polypharmacy, meaning more than four medications, or the use of psychoactive drugs. Age counts as a risk factor from 80 years upward, not 65. Every added risk factor roughly doubles the one-year risk, from 8% with none to as much as 78% with four.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Falls and Fall Prevention in Older Adults", Etiology

preguntas.pregunta: Which piece of hazard communication information does a laboratory employer NOT have to give its employees?
opciones: Where the written hazard communication program is kept and how to see it
The operations in their work area where hazardous chemicals are present
The measures they can take to protect themselves from those chemicals
The requirements of the Hazard Communication standard itself
preguntas.explicacion: Employees must be informed of the requirements of the standard, of the operations in their work area where hazardous chemicals are present, and of the location and availability of the written program with its chemical list and data sheets. Laboratories get the information and training of paragraph (h) with one item struck out: the location and availability of the written program, because the reduced coverage of laboratories does not require them to have one. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to be moved from the bed onto a stretcher. How is the stretcher set up?
opciones: Brought against the bed slightly lower than it, with its own brakes locked
Brought against the bed slightly higher than it, with its own brakes locked
Set at a 45-degree angle to the bed, with the brakes deliberately released
Left at the foot of the bed until the slider board is under the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The bed is raised or lowered to a safe working height, its brakes go on and the rails come down; the stretcher then comes alongside a little lower than the bed and its brakes are set too, so the patient slides slightly downhill. Three or four people usually do this move. A 45-degree angle is how a wheelchair is placed, not a stretcher.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room stands up clutching the throat with both hands and cannot speak. What does this show?
opciones: The universal sign of a blocked airway, which calls for immediate first aid
The first sign of a heart attack, which calls for rest and for chewed aspirin
A panic attack with hyperventilation, which calls for slow, coached breathing
A seizure that begins with a cry, which calls for protecting the head
preguntas.explicacion: Grabbing the neck with both hands is the universal choking sign. Sudden respiratory distress with coughing, gagging or stridor, an inability to speak or cry, and cyanosis point to a foreign body in the airway and call for action, because severe hypoxia leads to loss of consciousness within minutes.

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient is admitted to hospital in February and again in September. How often may she owe the 2026 Part A deductible?
opciones: Twice, since $1,736 falls due for each benefit period and there is no yearly cap
Once, since $1,736 is a yearly deductible in the way the Part B deductible is
Twice, but at $283 each time, which is the figure the yearly deductible uses
Not at all, since days one to sixty of an inpatient stay carry no charge
preguntas.explicacion: The 2026 Part A deductible is $1,736 for each inpatient benefit period before Original Medicare begins to pay, and there is no limit on how many benefit periods a person may have in one year, so the deductible can fall due more than once. Days one to sixty cost nothing only after that deductible has been paid.

preguntas.pregunta: A housekeeper handles regulated waste bags twice a week, while every phlebotomist is exposed daily. How does the exposure determination list them?
opciones: Phlebotomists as a classification where all are exposed; the housekeeper with the task
Both as classifications where all employees are exposed, with no list of tasks needed
Only the phlebotomists, because the housekeeper wears gloves for that one task
Both by name in the medical record, which is where exposed workers are recorded
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(i) asks for three lists: job classifications in which every employee has occupational exposure, job classifications in which only some do, and the tasks or groups of related tasks that expose the people in that second group. Handling regulated waste is exactly such a task. Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) adds that the determination is made without regard to protective equipment, so gloves never take a job off the list. The medical record of (h)(1) is a separate document kept for each exposed employee, not the determination.

preguntas.pregunta: To which transmissions do the electronic funds transfer standards apply?

Only to those sent between a health plan and a clearinghouse
To every transfer of funds a health plan makes to a provider
To every transfer a provider's own financial institution makes
preguntas.explicacion: The funds transfer standards reach only data sent over the Automated Clearing House network, the processing and delivery system that carries these transfers over nationwide telecommunications networks. The transfer itself is the message a health plan uses to order a financial institution to move money into a provider's account, and it carries the amount, the payer and payee and their identification, the bank accounts, routing numbers and payment date.

One dose a day
Three doses a day
Four doses a day

preguntas.pregunta: A patient had two beers at 11 p.m.; the fasting draw is at 7 a.m. How does that affect the sample?
opciones: Avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw; note it and tell the provider
It is fine, because eight hours have passed and beer counts only as a liquid
It is fine provided he drinks plain water now to dilute the alcohol
It is fine, because alcohol affects only the liver function tests
preguntas.explicacion: Alcoholic drinks should not be taken within 24 hours of the procedure, alongside the 12-hour fast and the ban on coffee and energy drinks that morning. preguntas.pregunta: Which crutch is the most common one, and what is it best suited to?
opciones: The axilla crutch, best for short-term use, sending the load to arms and torso
The forearm crutch, best for short-term use, sending the load to the forearms
The platform crutch, best for short-term use, sending the load to the upper arms
The axilla crutch, best for long-term use in a patient with weak upper body strength
preguntas.explicacion: Axilla crutches are the commonest type and are meant for the short term; their design moves most of the body weight onto the arms and the torso, and most facilities send patients home with them. They are a poor choice where the wrists are troublesome, the upper body is weak or coordination is impaired.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart notes a central venous line. According to the WHO, who may draw specimens from it, and what caveat applies?
opciones: Nursing staff and physicians under protocol; such specimens risk contamination or wrong results
Any phlebotomist trained in vacuum systems; the results are equivalent to those of a peripheral draw
No one; central lines may never be used for laboratory specimens under any protocol
Only laboratory technicians; they must draw a non-additive discard tube first
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says nursing staff and physicians may access central venous lines for specimens following protocols, but that specimens from central lines carry a risk of contamination or erroneous laboratory results. preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube with no anticoagulant has been filled. How long may the specimen need before it is spun?

Usually two to three minutes, and in some specimens up to ten minutes
Usually thirty seconds, the same contact time asked of an alcohol swab
Usually twenty-four hours, the interval allowed for a coagulation test

opciones: Consent forms, discharge instructions and patient rights documents
Handwritten drug orders, preprinted forms and progress notes
Laboratory requisitions, referral letters and imaging reports
Staff schedules, inventory records and equipment logs

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance for email communication with patients?
opciones: Encrypt all emails, keep the patient's name out of the subject line, and send the minimum information
Use a personal commercial email account so the message is not stored on the institution's servers
Put the patient's name in the subject line so the message is easy to locate later
Attach the full record whenever a patient asks a question, to avoid follow-up messages
preguntas.explicacion: Institutions should set email rules: the patient's name is left out of the subject line, the address is verified, only the bare minimum of information is transmitted, a standard disclaimer closes every message, all emails are encrypted, and staff never use personal or commercial accounts for patient communication, only the system the institution provides. Similar rules govern faxes, which sit in a secure area with a cover sheet explaining what to do if the fax is misdirected. preguntas.pregunta: A patient turning 65 asks how many ways there are of taking her Medicare coverage.

Two: Original Medicare, or a Medigap policy bought from a private insurer
Three: Original Medicare, a Medicare Advantage plan, or a Medigap policy
One: Original Medicare, to which every other coverage is only an addition
preguntas.explicacion: There are two main ways of taking the coverage. Original Medicare is Part A and Part B, to which a separate drug plan and supplemental coverage can be added. preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, which disinfectant is applied after the area has been cleaned with water and detergent?
opciones: Sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, a 1:10 bleach dilution prepared daily
Sodium hypochlorite 5.25 percent, used undiluted straight from the bottle
70 percent alcohol, the same solution used to prepare the skin
Sodium hypochlorite 0.05 percent, a 1:100 dilution, kept for a week
preguntas.explicacion: After the glass is removed with tongs, the fluid absorbed with paper towels and the area wiped with water and detergent until visibly clean, the spill area is saturated again with sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, which is 10,000 parts per million of available chlorine, made as a 1:10 dilution of 5.25 percent household bleach and prepared fresh each day. Undiluted bleach is not the instruction, 70 percent alcohol is WHO's skin antiseptic, and a solution kept for a week defeats the daily preparation rule. Gloves come off last, followed by handwashing and an incident record.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a fingerstick glucose, an assistant swabs the fingertip with alcohol and lances it while the skin is still wet. Why does the guidance advise against this?
opciones: Residual alcohol can dilute the drop or cause hemolysis, so the site must dry completely first
Alcohol left on the skin makes the meter read falsely high, because ethanol is measured as glucose
Alcohol is not recommended at all; the guidance calls for washing with cold water and no antiseptic
Wet alcohol stings on puncture, which is the only concern, so the result itself is not affected
preguntas.explicacion: The site is washed and dried thoroughly, using warm water to improve blood flow. Alcohol swabs are not routinely required, but if one is used the skin must be allowed to dry completely before lancing, because residual alcohol can dilute the sample or hemolyze it and affect the reading. Discomfort is not the point; sample integrity is. Cold water is not what the procedure describes.

Two control materials of different concentrations
One control material with graded or titered reactivity
A calibrator from the same lot used to set the cut-off

preguntas.pregunta: Documentation reaches the billing team four or five days after each visit. Against the benchmark for the lag from service to charge entry, where does that practice stand?
opciones: Above the benchmark, which is two days or fewer from the date of service
Below the benchmark, which is seven days or fewer from the date of service
At the benchmark, which is five days or fewer from the date of service
Above the benchmark, which is twenty-one days from the date of service
preguntas.explicacion: The lag from care to charge is benchmarked at two days or less. A longer one usually comes from late dictation and reports, coding queries and co-signatures nobody answered, an overwhelmed or undertrained billing team, or plain clerical delay; the fixes offered are documenting within twenty-four hours, chasing the missing paperwork and finding the bottleneck. Twenty-one days is a different figure in the same material: when to follow up on a claim already submitted.

preguntas.pregunta: Hydrochlorothiazide is prescribed for primary hypertension. Which statement matches the approved use of this class?
opciones: It is approved for primary hypertension, alone or added to other antihypertensives
It is approved for hypertension only once a loop diuretic has failed at a full dose
It is approved for edema only, so any use in hypertension is entirely off-label
It is approved for hypertension only in patients who also have chronic kidney disease
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrochlorothiazide and chlorthalidone are approved for primary hypertension and are used either on their own or alongside other antihypertensives to lift the response in severe cases. The same agents are approved as adjuncts for edema in chronic heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis and corticosteroid or estrogen therapy. Loop diuretics are approved for hypertension too, but they are not the first-line choice.

preguntas.pregunta: Which sequence describes the revenue cycle correctly?

Preregistration, charge capture, data verification, remittance, coding, claim submission
Charge capture, coding, preregistration, data verification, remittance, claim submission
Data verification, remittance, preregistration, charge capture, claim submission, coding
preguntas.explicacion: The cycle starts before the visit with preregistration, where demographic, medical and insurance data are gathered, and with verification of that data. Charge capture begins right after care is delivered, coding follows, claims go out to the payers, and remittance processing posts the payments once the explanation of benefits or electronic remittance advice arrives. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist needs the supplier's emergency telephone number for a cleaning concentrate. Which section of the safety data sheet has it?
opciones: Section 1, which also gives the product identifier and the recommended use
Section 2, which also gives the signal word and the hazard statements
Section 15, which also gives the regulations that apply to the product
Section 16, which also gives the date the sheet was last revised
preguntas.explicacion: Section 1 identifies the product and whoever is responsible for it: the product identifier used on the label along with any synonyms, the name, address and telephone number of the manufacturer, importer or other responsible party, an emergency telephone number, and what the chemical is recommended for, plus any restrictions on its use. Section 15 gathers the regulatory information and section 16 the date of preparation or last revision, neither of which helps in the middle of an incident.

Ophthalmology, which handles eye disorders and eye surgery
Pulmonary medicine, which handles respiratory tract disorders
Neurology, which handles disorders of the nervous system

preguntas.pregunta: A small extra wave follows the T wave on a strip. What is it, and what is it linked to?
opciones: A U wave, commonly associated with low potassium
A J wave, commonly associated with low body temperature
An epsilon wave, commonly associated with low potassium
A delta wave, commonly associated with a slow AV node
preguntas.explicacion: The U wave is a small deflection that comes after the T wave and is attributed to late repolarization of the papillary muscles or the Purkinje fibers; it is commonly seen with low potassium. The J or Osborn wave sits at the junction of the QRS complex and the ST segment in hypothermia.

preguntas.pregunta: A cleaning solution splashes onto a patient's arm and burns the skin. How is the area flushed?
opciones: With cool running water for 15 minutes or more, after dry powder is brushed off
With cool running water for 30 seconds, and then a neutralizing rinse
With warm soapy water for 5 minutes, scrubbing until the pain settles
With a wet compress held in place, so that the chemical is not spread
preguntas.explicacion: Any dry chemical is brushed off first, and clothing and jewelry come off; then the skin is flushed with cool running water for 15 minutes or longer. Dry lime and elemental metals such as sodium or potassium are the exceptions to flushing with water. The rescuer wears eye and skin protection and avoids becoming contaminated.

preguntas.pregunta: How is consent for HIV testing handled in a clinical setting in the United States?
opciones: The patient is told verbally that the test will be run and may decline it
The patient signs a specific written consent form kept with the requisition
The patient signs a written consent, except where state law waives that step
The patient gives consent only after counseling by a trained HIV counselor
preguntas.explicacion: No state requires a signed consent for the test. Patients must be informed verbally that the test is going to be performed and given the chance to say no, which is what the opt-out approach means in practice. Prevention counseling and an evaluation for pre-exposure prophylaxis are offered whichever way the result comes back.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood has leaked onto the outside of a specimen tube. What does the standard require before it is transported?
opciones: Place it in a second container that prevents leakage and is labeled or color-coded
Wipe the tube with disinfectant and transport it in the usual rack with a new label
Discard the specimen as regulated waste and request a new draw from the patient
Place it in a puncture-resistant container, which is required for every leaking tube
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(B) says that when the outside of the primary container is contaminated, it goes inside a second container that prevents leakage during handling, processing, storage, transport or shipping and that is labeled or color-coded per the standard. Puncture resistance is added by (d)(2)(xiii)(C) only when the specimen could puncture the primary container, not for every leak. Nothing in the paragraph calls for discarding the specimen or for cleaning the tube in place of the secondary container.

That it store every recorded visit for six years so the practice can produce it later
That it be certified by the Office for Civil Rights before any visit may be scheduled
That it encrypt the video only when the patient asks for that protection in advance

opciones: It cuts down the risk of mixing up which tube belongs to which patient
It lets the patient read the label and correct the spelling of the name
It shows that the fasting instructions were kept before the first tube
It lets the phlebotomist skip the wristband check on any later visit
preguntas.explicacion: Before the blood is withdrawn the identification data and the tube labelling are double-checked, and both the identification of the tubes and their labelling happen with the patient there, which is what lowers the risk of tube misidentification. preguntas.pregunta: Which content does an electronic health record contain, according to ONC?
opciones: History, diagnoses, medications, immunization dates, allergies, imaging and test results
Only the notes written by the clinician who owns the practice where the record is kept
Only the data elements a health plan needs to adjudicate a claim for the encounter
Only the documents the patient has personally uploaded through the practice portal
preguntas.explicacion: An EHR is described as a digital version of the paper chart that is real-time, patient-centered and available instantly and securely to authorized users. It holds medical history, diagnoses, medications, treatment plans, immunization dates, allergies, radiology images and laboratory and test results, gives access to evidence-based decision tools, and automates and streamlines the clinician's workflow.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a blood culture diversion device reduce contamination?
opciones: It sets aside a small first portion of blood, then collects the culture
It draws the whole set through a closed catheter connector, bypassing the skin
It splits one venipuncture into two sets so a second stick is unnecessary
It adds an antiglycolytic agent that keeps skin organisms from growing
preguntas.explicacion: Commercially available diversion devices first divert a small amount of potentially contaminated blood and then collect the blood for the culture; the CDC lists them as showing promise in further reducing contamination. Drawing through catheters raises contamination, a second set still needs a separate venipuncture, and antiglycolytic additives belong to the glucose tube, not to culture bottles.

preguntas.pregunta: Which tool assesses pain in an infant by watching face, legs, activity, cry and consolability?
opciones: The revised Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability tool for young children
The Behavioral Pain Scale, built for adults who are sedated or unconscious
The Nonverbal Pain Scale, built for intubated adults in intensive care units
The visual analogue scale, on which a mark is placed along a printed line
preguntas.explicacion: Observational tools take the place of self-report in patients who cannot speak for themselves. The one built on face, legs, activity, cry and consolability serves infants and young children, and it is also validated for nonverbal children with neurologic impairment. The other observational scales listed are for adults.

preguntas.pregunta: An order uses cc for volume and the microgram symbol for a dose. What is recommended in their place?
opciones: mL instead of cc, and mcg instead of the microgram symbol
mL instead of cc, and mg instead of the microgram symbol
unit instead of cc, and mcg instead of the microgram symbol
cm instead of cc, and nanogram instead of the microgram symbol
preguntas.explicacion: Cubic centimeters written as cc is mistaken for u, meaning units, so mL is used instead. The microgram symbol is mistaken for mg, which is a thousand-fold difference, so mcg is written. Nanogram appears on the same list because it is read as mg and as nasogastric, and the fix there is to spell the word out. Writing unit fixes neither of the two abbreviations in this order.

preguntas.pregunta: A muscular patient has very prominent, easily visible veins. What is the guidance on tourniquet use in this case?
opciones: Avoiding the tourniquet is recommended when the veins are prominent
The tourniquet is still mandatory, applied about 3 inches above the site
A tighter tourniquet is used, because large veins collapse under vacuum
The tourniquet is applied only after the first tube has been filled
preguntas.explicacion: Controversy remains about tourniquets in blood sampling, and avoiding them, especially in patients with prominent veins, is recommended; otherwise a disposable tourniquet goes about 3 inches above the site. preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands in a sputum cup holding a few milliliters of clear, watery fluid from the mouth. What should the medical assistant do?
opciones: Ask for a new specimen coughed up deeply, because thin, clear material is rejected
Send it as it is, because any material from the mouth still carries airway organisms
Add sterile saline to the cup and send it, because the volume is what was too small
Refrigerate it and send it the next morning, when a fresh specimen can be added to it
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is what comes up from the air passages on a deep cough, not spit. The thicker the material, the more likely it truly represents lower respiratory secretions and shows the organism causing the infection, and many laboratories will not accept a clear, runny sample for microscopy or culture. Volume and quality are both assessed, and collection may be repeated until 10 to 20 mL is obtained.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair is sent for a tracing. What decides whether it goes ahead?
opciones: Whether the patient can move onto the table alone or with help
Whether the patient can stand unaided all through the recording
Whether a provider signs off on the extra assistance beforehand
Whether the tracing can be recorded with the patient still seated
preguntas.explicacion: Nobody is automatically excluded from the test. For a patient in a wheelchair the question is only the transfer: it goes ahead if the person can get onto the examination table alone or with help from whoever usually lifts them.

preguntas.pregunta: A dose is ordered per kilogram and the patient's weight is recorded in pounds. Which equivalence is used?
opciones: 1 kilogram equals 2.2 pounds
1 kilogram equals 1.2 pounds
1 kilogram equals 16 pounds
1 kilogram equals 10 pounds
preguntas.explicacion: One kilogram is 2.2 pounds, and it is also 1000 grams. Weight-based doses are calculated on the metric weight, in kilograms for children and adults and in grams for newborns, which is why the weight belongs on the order whenever the dose depends on it. The 16 in the household table is the number of ounces in a pound, not a conversion between pounds and kilograms.

preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old was at the 75th percentile for weight, moved to the 25th at 9 months and lower at 12 months. Why does that worry the provider?
opciones: The measurements are no longer tracking one curve, which matters more than any single value
The 25th percentile is below the normal range, so a single value there is the concern
Weight percentiles are expected to climb steadily, so any fall at all is abnormal
The child has crossed into the band that defines undernutrition on the charts
preguntas.explicacion: What raises concern on a chart is a measurement that stops following its own line, or one that stays below the 10th or above the 90th percentile for the age. A single value at the 25th percentile is not itself abnormal; a toddler can lose weight after a bout of diarrhoea and regain it. Abnormal growth is a sign, not a diagnosis.

preguntas.pregunta: After explaining a condition in everyday words, what three things should be checked with the patient?
opciones: The health issue, what to do about it, and why acting matters
The diagnosis, the dose of each drug, and the next appointment
The health issue, the cost of the visit, and whom to call later
The diagnosis, the address of the referral, and pharmacy hours
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told not to assume patients know medical terminology, to use simple common language, to ask whether anything needs clarifying, and then to check that the patient has understood the health issue, what they need to do and why it matters to act. Doses, costs and addresses may all be discussed, but they are not that three-part check.

preguntas.pregunta: A bystander with no duty to act stops to help at a roadside crash. What does the Good Samaritan rule say about that?
opciones: Taking charge assumes a duty to use reasonable care from then on
Taking charge carries no duty at all, since the help was voluntary
Taking charge creates liability only if payment was later accepted
Taking charge is barred unless the helper is licensed in that state
preguntas.explicacion: Under the rule, someone who provides services for another, whether free or for pay, assumes a duty to use reasonable care, and can be held liable if their negligence injures the person helped or a foreseeable third party. At common law a bystander has no moral or legal duty to help if they did not cause the injury, but once they take charge of a helpless person that duty attaches.

preguntas.pregunta: When must a history and physical examination be completed for a patient scheduled for surgery under anesthesia?
opciones: No more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission, and before the procedure
No more than 7 days before or 48 hours after admission, and before the procedure
No more than 90 days before admission, with no deadline once the patient arrives
At any point during the stay, provided it is filed within 30 days after discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The record must document a history and physical completed and documented no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission or registration, and in any case before surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia. preguntas.pregunta: A physician's office asks the laboratory for the reference interval it uses for a test and for a list of substances that interfere with the assay. What does CLIA say?
opciones: Reference intervals must be available to the ordering person, and information affecting interpretation, like interferences, is given on request
Reference intervals are proprietary to the performing laboratory; only the manufacturer's package insert may be shared with the laboratory's clients

Reference intervals and interference data are provided only when the laboratory holds a certificate of accreditation from CAP

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a flexible spending account is accurate?
opciones: It is an employer arrangement, and the amount put in is not taxed to the employee
It is an employer arrangement, and only the employer may decide the amount put in
It is a bank arrangement open to people enrolled in a high deductible plan
It is a plan arrangement that raises the yearly limit on covered dental services
preguntas.explicacion: A flexible spending account is set up through the employer and lets the worker pay out-of-pocket costs, such as copayments, deductibles and prescription drugs, with money that is not taxed. preguntas.pregunta: Which parts of a practice does the toolkit say have to be covered by language access services?
opciones: Scheduling, signage, front desk, the visit, billing and follow-up messages
Only the clinical visit, where medical information is actually exchanged
Only the front desk and the signage, where written English predominates
Only scheduling and billing, where the written records are generated

preguntas.pregunta: A pregnant patient booked for a glucose challenge test asks whether she must fast. What is the answer?
opciones: No fasting; she drinks the glucose and one sample is drawn an hour later
Fast at least 8 hours; samples are drawn before and 2 hours after the drink
Fast 9 to 12 hours; the test is normally scheduled for the morning
No fasting; a single sample reflects her average glucose over 3 months
preguntas.explicacion: The glucose challenge test used to screen for gestational diabetes needs no fasting: the patient drinks a sugary drink and blood is taken one hour later; a high result leads to an oral glucose tolerance test, which does require fasting and repeated samples. preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes to the office from her own e-mail account asking about her results. What may the office assume?
opciones: That e-mail is acceptable to her, unless she has said otherwise
That she has waived every privacy right she holds over those results
That the message may be forwarded to any provider treating her
That she has consented to receive marketing messages from the practice

preguntas.pregunta: Which four elements must a patient prove to win a medical malpractice suit?
opciones: Duty, breach of duty (negligence), causation and damages
Assault, battery, negligence and abandonment
Intent, foreseeability, restitution and injunction
Duty, consent, documentation and insurance coverage
preguntas.explicacion: A simple mistake is not malpractice by itself. The plaintiff must establish four elements: a duty to the patient, meaning the clinician was responsible for that patient's care; a breach of that duty, the negligence, measured against the standard of care; causation, that the act or omission produced the bad outcome; and damages, the loss for which compensation is sought. The tort pathway states it the same way, duty, breach, proximate cause, damages. Assault, battery and abandonment are separate torts, and restitution and injunctions are remedies.

preguntas.pregunta: Which grains naturally contain the gluten that a patient with celiac disease must avoid?
opciones: Wheat, barley, rye and triticale
Wheat, barley, rye and buckwheat
Wheat, corn, rye and triticale
Wheat, barley, rice and triticale
preguntas.explicacion: Gluten occurs naturally in wheat and its relatives such as durum, semolina and spelt, in barley, in rye, and in triticale, the wheat-rye cross. Barley is why malt, malt vinegar and brewer's yeast matter, and why beer and ale can carry gluten. The diet has to be kept up for life to keep symptoms and intestinal damage away.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage plan asks whether the plan is allowed to cover less than Original Medicare does.
opciones: No, because the plan has to give at least the coverage Original Medicare gives
Yes, because the plan may drop benefits so long as it lowers her premium too
Yes, because the plan may drop the benefits that fall under Part B rather than A
No, because the plan has to give the same coverage and charge the same amounts
preguntas.explicacion: A Medicare Advantage plan or other Medicare plan may have rules of its own, but it has to give at least the same coverage as Original Medicare. Where it does differ is cost: those plans usually have different out-of-pocket amounts, including a yearly limit Original Medicare does not have, and most add benefits Original Medicare leaves out, such as vision, hearing and dental care.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers; and Parts of Medicare

preguntas.pregunta: Which use of an advance written notice of non-coverage is prohibited outright?
opciones: Passing to the patient a cost denied because of a medically unlikely edit
Warning her that a service goes beyond a frequency limit fixed by a coverage policy
Warning her about an item that is always denied as medically unnecessary
Warning her about an experimental item or service before it is provided to her
preguntas.explicacion: The notice may not be used to shift liability for a service denied under a medically unlikely edit, to charge for part of a service already paid through a bundled payment, to transfer liability where the programme otherwise pays, or to compel a patient in a medical emergency or under great duress. Frequency limits, always-denied services and experimental care are the permitted grounds.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Other Prohibitions
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77, 6C k87 · CCMA 5 k186

preguntas.pregunta: How is an eye ointment applied?
opciones: Half an inch into the lower conjunctival sac, running from the inner canthus outward
Half an inch along the upper eyelid margin, running from the outer canthus inward
A thin line over the closed eyelid, which the patient then rubs in with one finger
One drop's worth into the lower sac, with the tube tip resting on the lower eyelid
preguntas.explicacion: Eye ointment follows the same steps as an eye drop, except that half an inch of ointment is laid into the lower conjunctival sac, and the line runs from the inner canthus outward. The patient then closes the lid and moves the eye so the ointment spreads and is absorbed, and should be warned that vision will be blurry for a few minutes. Nothing, dropper or tube, is allowed to touch the eye.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Eye Instillations, Eye Ointment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k70 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii)

preguntas.pregunta: Staff complain that the record system takes half a minute to open a chart, though it has never stopped. How does the contingency guidance classify that?
opciones: As a functional downtime, which is to be identified and addressed proactively
As a security incident, which is documented and reported with its outcome
As an EHR limitation, which is recorded on the worksheet and left to the vendor
As a planned downtime, which is announced to users before the work begins
preguntas.explicacion: Unacceptably slow response time counts as a functional system downtime even though the system is running. It matters because delay invites type-ahead errors, where keystrokes the user has already made land in whatever field opens next, so the guidance asks organizations to measure response times and give users an easy way to report them.
preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.2
preguntas.subtema: Functional downtime · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature separates a hypertensive emergency from a hypertensive urgency?
opciones: Acute organ damage is present in the emergency and absent in the urgency
Acute organ damage is absent in the emergency and present in the urgency
The emergency is defined by a systolic reading above 140 mm Hg
The urgency is defined by a diastolic reading above 120 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: A hypertensive crisis is a severe, sudden rise in blood pressure. It counts as an emergency when acute hypertension-mediated organ damage comes with it, and as an urgency when it does not. Numbers such as 180 over 120 are conventions rather than firm lines, and how fast the pressure rose can matter more than how high it is.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypertensive Crisis", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told that two out of ten people gain weight on a new medicine, rather than that few people have side effects. What principle is that?
opciones: Being specific and concrete instead of using vague, subjective terms
Being reassuring, so the patient is not frightened out of the treatment
Being thorough, so every possible side effect is named at least once
Being brief, so the explanation fits inside a fifteen-minute visit
preguntas.explicacion: Vague words get read differently by different people, so clear communication asks for specific, concrete wording: a number instead of "few". The same set of habits covers plain nonmedical language, using the patient's own words, slowing the pace, drawing pictures, demonstrating, and then checking with teach-back.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods

preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient be taught to do when a cough or a sneeze is coming on?
opciones: Cover the mouth and nose with a tissue or the inside of the elbow
Cover the mouth and nose with the palm of the hand, then wash it
Turn the head to one side and cough without covering the mouth at all
Cover the mouth only, since the nose does not release germs when coughing
preguntas.explicacion: Germs travel from person to person by several routes, and respiratory droplets are one of them. Both mouth and nose are covered, with a tissue or with the inside of the elbow, and hand washing follows any cough, sneeze or nose blowing so nothing is carried onward on the hands.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Germs and Hygiene — How can I protect myself and others from germs?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k169 disease prevention education · CMA I.A.6.c · 2027 I.A.6.c · NCMA D.4

preguntas.pregunta: An Rh negative mother delivered a healthy Rh positive first baby and received no RhoGAM. What is the concern for a second Rh positive pregnancy?
opciones: Her anti-Rh antibodies could cross the placenta and destroy the fetus's red cells
Her anti-A and anti-B antibodies could cross the placenta if the baby is type AB
The first baby's Rh+ cells remain in her blood and agglutinate her own cells
A second Rh+ fetus would sensitize her only if it were also ABO incompatible
preguntas.explicacion: A first pregnancy is usually safe because fetal cells rarely cross the placenta, but at birth the Rh negative parent can be exposed to the baby's Rh positive cells and begin making anti-Rh antibodies. In a later Rh positive pregnancy those antibodies can cross the placenta and hemolyze fetal red cells, causing hemolytic disease of the newborn, which ranges from mild anemia to fetal death.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's spouse comes to the front desk, with other patients waiting behind him, and asks why the patient is here today.
opciones: Ask the patient whether he objects, and talk away from the desk
Answer at the desk, since a spouse needs no written authorization
Refuse any contact until the spouse produces a signed authorization
Send the spouse to the laboratory, which released the result
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules meet here. Information may be shared with a spouse, parent, guardian or other caregiver involved in the person's care without a formal written agreement, but when other people are present the patient is asked first whether there is any objection. And the conversation itself does not belong at a counter or in a hallway: anything specific waits until the patient is in a private room, with only what is relevant said out loud.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: HIPAA and Communication With Patients
preguntas.subtema: At the front desk · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: At which ages does the federal milestone checklist series begin during the first year?
opciones: At 2, 4, 6 and 9 months, and then at one year
At 1, 3, 5 and 7 months, and then at one year
At 3, 6 and 9 months only, and then at two years
At birth and at 6 months only, and then at one year
preguntas.explicacion: The public checklists are organized by age, starting at 2 months and continuing at 4, 6 and 9 months, at one year, at 15 months and onward. Each list gathers what most babies do by that age, which gives a family and a clinician a shared reference point for whether development is on track.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.: Developmental Milestones by Age
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.a and I.C.6.b (2027 I.C.6.a)

preguntas.pregunta: How does the American Diabetes Association define 'fasting' for a fasting plasma glucose?
opciones: No caloric intake at all for at least 8 hours
No food or drink, including water, for 12 hours
No solid food for 8 hours; sweetened drinks allowed
No caloric intake at all for at least 24 hours
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA diagnostic criteria define fasting as no caloric intake for at least 8 hours, with a fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher meeting the threshold for diabetes. Water carries no calories and is allowed; sweetened drinks do carry calories. Twelve hours is the general recommendation for morning sampling, and 24 hours is the alcohol-free window.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Diagnostic Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: What characterizes prospective payment?
opciones: Rates fixed in advance according to average resource consumption
Rates negotiated after the fact from the charges actually billed
Rates set by the share of savings the organization has achieved
Rates paid per member per month, regardless of the care furnished
preguntas.explicacion: Prospective payment methods use fixed rates for health services according to average resource consumption. The aim is financial predictability and cost containment, though the approach can make it hard to predict what resources a case will need and to encourage the appropriate amount of care. It sits among the alternative models beside capitation and global payment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Clinical Resource Management Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care: Prospective payment
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's lips and fingertips look blue and the note reads cyanosis. Which color does that word part name?
opciones: Blue, from the color prefix cyano-
Red, from the color prefix erythro-
White, from the color prefix leuko-
Black, from the color prefix melano-
preguntas.explicacion: The color word parts run through much of the vocabulary: cyano- is blue, erythro- red, leuko- white, melano- black, xantho- yellow and chloro- green. That is why red cells are erythrocytes, white cells leukocytes and the skin pigment melanin, and why blue skin is recorded as cyanosis.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Color
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which content is the notice of privacy practices required to include?
opciones: The individual's rights, how to exercise them, and whom to contact to make a complaint
The fee schedule for copies of records and the practice's policy on missed appointments
A list of every workforce member authorized to open the electronic health record system
The names of the business associates that handle claims and transcription for the practice
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be in plain language and describe how the entity may use and disclose PHI, the individual's rights and how to exercise them including how to complain, the entity's legal duties including its obligation to protect privacy, and whom to contact for more information. It must carry an effective date, and it must be revised and redistributed promptly when privacy practices change materially.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Content of the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Notice content · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital hires per diem and contract phlebotomists for a busy season. How does the bloodborne pathogens standard treat them?
opciones: They are covered, and the plan must describe how the standard is met for them
They are covered after ninety days, the period allowed for a new hire's training
They are covered by the staffing agency's plan alone, never by the host facility
They fall outside the standard, since the exposure determination lists job titles
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan states plainly that part-time, temporary, contract and per diem employees fall under the bloodborne pathogens standard, and that the written plan should say how the requirements will be met for them. Nothing in paragraph (c) sets a waiting period: training comes at the time of initial assignment under (g)(2)(ii)(A), and the hepatitis B vaccine within ten working days of that assignment under (f)(2)(i). The exposure determination is a list of job classifications and tasks, so it does not exclude anyone by employment status.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Employee Exposure Determination (note); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i)
preguntas.subtema: Who the plan covers · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41

preguntas.pregunta: How many characters can an ICD-10-CM code have?
opciones: Three to seven, with all categories being three characters long
Three to five, with the sixth and seventh reserved for inpatient use
Five exactly, in the same way procedure codes carry five digits
Seven exactly, since the seventh character is required on every code
preguntas.explicacion: In the tabular list all categories have three characters; subcategories have four or five, and codes may run to three, four, five, six or seven characters, each level of subdivision adding specificity. A three-character category with no further subdivision is itself a code. The seventh character is required only where the category calls for it, and five digits describe Level I procedure codes instead.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.2
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.b · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: Under the CLAS standards, how are patients told that language assistance exists?
opciones: In writing and out loud, in English and in their own languages
In writing only, in the languages the service area commonly speaks
Orally only, in the languages that serve their linguistic needs
Inside the notice of privacy practices handed out at the visit
preguntas.explicacion: One standard requires informing every individual, in writing and orally, that language assistance services are available, in English and in the other languages their communities speak. A separate standard covers easy-to-understand print and digital materials and signage; neither is folded into the privacy notice.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Communication and Language Assistance
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)

preguntas.pregunta: What is a set point in physiology, and what is the normal range around it?
opciones: The value a parameter is held near, and the healthy band it moves within
The healthy band a parameter moves within, and the value it may not exceed
The highest value a parameter may reach, and the band above that value
The value at which an effector switches off, and the band it then avoids
preguntas.explicacion: Each physiological condition has a set point, the value that its normal range fluctuates around, and a normal range, the restricted band of values that is stable and healthy. Body temperature is the usual illustration, with a set point of about 37 degrees Celsius and readings that drift a little above and below it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Homeostasis", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: What happens to the respiratory rate over the first two years of life?
opciones: It drops from a median near 44 at birth to about 26 during the second year
It drops from a median near 60 at birth to about 40 during the second year
It holds near 30 through the whole period and only falls once the child walks
It climbs from a median near 20 at birth to about 30 during the second year
preguntas.explicacion: Children breathe faster than adults, and the rate falls as they grow: the median goes from around 44 breaths a minute at birth to about 26 in the second year of life. That is why a count that would be alarming in an adult may be ordinary in an infant, and why the value is read against the child's age.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Respiratory Rate", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms cause an ischemic stroke?
opciones: A thrombus forming in the vessel itself, or an embolus arriving from elsewhere
A thrombus forming in the vessel itself, or a rupture bleeding into the brain
An embolus arriving from elsewhere, or a rupture bleeding into the brain
A rupture bleeding into the brain, or a rise in the pressure inside the skull
preguntas.explicacion: Ischemic stroke comes from either a thrombotic or an embolic event that cuts blood flow to a region of the brain. In the thrombotic kind the clot forms inside the affected vessel, usually on atherosclerotic disease; in the embolic kind debris travels there, most often from the heart. Bleeding into the brain defines the other family, hemorrhagic stroke.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Ischemic Stroke", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(3) (2027 I.C.6.g(3)) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse tells the phlebotomist that the patient in bed 12 is the one who needs the draw. Under the Joint Commission International patient identification goal, why is that not enough?
opciones: The room number or location cannot be used as an identifier; at least two identifiers such as name and birth date are needed
Only the bar-coded wristband counts as an identifier, so the nurse's statement must be confirmed by scanning it
The location is acceptable as one identifier, provided a second identifier such as the ordering physician's name is added
Two staff members must independently confirm the bed number before a specimen can be collected
preguntas.explicacion: The first international patient safety goal requires at least two ways of identifying the patient, for example name, identification number, birth date or a bar-coded wristband, and it excludes the room number or location outright. The wristband is one valid option, not the only one; the physician's name identifies the order, not the patient; and a second witness does not turn a location into an identifier.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.1, IPSG 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which range is accepted as the normal body temperature of a resting adult?
opciones: 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F), around an average of 37.0 °C (98.6 °F)
36.0 to 37.0 °C (96.8 to 98.6 °F), around an average of 36.5 °C (97.7 °F)
37.0 to 38.0 °C (98.6 to 100.4 °F), around an average of 37.5 °C (99.5 °F)
35.5 to 36.5 °C (95.9 to 97.7 °F), around an average of 36.0 °C (96.8 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: The figure everyone quotes, 37.0 °C or 98.6 °F, is an average and not a fixed value: the accepted reference band runs from 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F). The hypothalamus holds core temperature inside that narrow band. A single reading at either edge is normal, so it is compared with the patient's own baseline.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes to the collection agency asking it to stop contacting her about the account. What follows under the statute?
opciones: The collector must stop communicating about that debt, subject to narrow exceptions
The collector must stop only once the debt has been validated to her in writing
The collector may carry on for thirty days while the dispute is being investigated
The collector must hand the account back to the practice within five days of that
preguntas.explicacion: Where a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing that she refuses to pay the debt, or that she wants further communication to cease, the collector must not communicate with her about that debt any further, apart from the narrow exceptions the section itself sets out. The thirty days and the five days belong to the validation provision instead.
preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(c)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187

preguntas.pregunta: In which phase of laboratory testing do fasting errors and patient identification errors occur?
opciones: Preanalytical
Analytical
Postanalytical
Interpretive
preguntas.explicacion: Errors can occur in the preanalytical, analytical and postanalytical phases; improper patient preparation and specimen collection errors belong to the preanalytical phase, along with transport delays. Instrument malfunction and reagent instability are analytical, and transcription mistakes and poor communication of critical values are postanalytical.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", sections Continuing Education Activity and Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k46 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: What do front-line staff need for a service recovery program to work?
opciones: Authority to settle complaints without prior approval
A script to read out to every dissatisfied patient
A manager present at each complaint conversation
A written record signed by the patient afterward
preguntas.explicacion: Complaints usually land on front-line staff, who often lack the resources to repair a system problem. What they need is clarity about how far their authority reaches without a manager's approval, defined courses of action for the most frequent complaints, minimal red tape, and named backup for the hard cases.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P Service Recovery Programs
preguntas.subtema: Service recovery · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16 · NCMA EKB 22

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee scrubs for ten minutes before a sterile procedure, believing longer is safer. What is the effect?
opciones: No added benefit, and more risk of irritating the skin
A longer lasting effect on the resident skin flora
The same effect as a rub, which needs no drying time
A shorter effect, since the antiseptic is rinsed away
preguntas.explicacion: The usual scrub with an antimicrobial agent runs about two to six minutes, following the manufacturer and the institution. Scrub times of ten minutes or more add nothing and raise the risk of skin irritation, and irritated skin is harder to keep clean. Some institutions use shorter staged techniques or an alcohol-based formulation instead, applied as the manufacturer directs and left to dry completely before sterile gloves go on.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: Scrub duration · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is switched from a brand-name tablet to its approved generic. What must the generic match?
opciones: The active ingredient, the strength, form and route, and it must be bioequivalent
The active and the inactive ingredients as well, colour and shape of the tablet
The price the brand is sold at, because the FDA sets what a generic may charge
The clinical trials of the brand, which the generic maker has to run over again
preguntas.explicacion: An approved generic works the same way and carries the same benefits and risks as the brand. The applicant has to show that the active ingredient is the same, that strength, dosage form and route of administration match, that manufacturing meets the same standards, that the label is the same apart from certain exceptions, and that the product is bioequivalent. The FDA reviews before approval and inspects the plants.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Generic Drug Facts: Generic medicines work the same as brand-name medicines
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.f · NCMA 1.4

preguntas.pregunta: What is a provisional certification, and how long does it last?
opciones: A placeholder for those not yet eligible, valid for twelve months
A placeholder for those not yet eligible, valid for twenty-four months
A temporary credential for candidates who failed once, valid for a year
A temporary credential granted while a background check is completed
preguntas.explicacion: A provisional certification is a placeholder that lets someone sit the exam close to finishing training even though the eligibility requirements — a high school diploma, a GED or an equivalent — are not met yet. It expires twelve months after the examination date, and if it lapses before the person converts it, the exam has to be taken again. Recertification and reinstatement do not apply to it.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Converting Provisional Certification to Full Certification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: What are the four parameters of steam sterilization that an autoclave has to control?
opciones: Steam, pressure, temperature and time
Steam, humidity, temperature and pressure
Steam, pressure, gas concentration and time
Steam, temperature, pH and exposure time
preguntas.explicacion: The principle is to expose every item to direct contact with steam at the required temperature and pressure for the stated time, which makes four parameters: steam, pressure, temperature and time. Pressure is only the means of reaching the temperature needed. Relative humidity and gas concentration matter for ethylene oxide, not for steam.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA 2027 I.C.5.b(3) · RMA III.A.4

preguntas.pregunta: Which transaction lets an office ask a payer what happened to a claim already submitted?
opciones: The claim status transaction, one of the standard HIPAA electronic transactions
The eligibility transaction, one of the standard HIPAA electronic transactions
The remittance advice, which the payer sends when the claim has been adjudicated
The referrals and authorizations transaction, sent before the service is provided
preguntas.explicacion: Claim status is one of the transactions adopted under HIPAA and is what an office uses to follow an unpaid claim. Eligibility asks whether coverage is active before the visit, referrals and authorizations handle approvals in advance, and the remittance advice is the payer's report once adjudication is finished rather than an inquiry the office can send.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions Overview
preguntas.subtema: Tracking unpaid claims · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M k185

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being fitted with a Holter monitor. How long is it usually worn?
opciones: 24 to 48 hours, recording continuously during normal activity
2 to 4 hours, recording continuously during normal activity
7 to 10 days, recording continuously during normal activity
24 to 48 hours, recording only when the patient presses it
preguntas.explicacion: The monitor is a small recorder carried in a pouch or pocket, wired to electrodes on the chest, and it writes the rhythm without a break for 24 to 48 hours of ordinary life. The patient goes about the usual routine and returns the device afterwards for the provider to review.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Holter monitor (24h)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii III.F.7

preguntas.pregunta: An unexpected outage has kept the record system down for a day and a half. What does the guidance ask the organization to do afterwards?
opciones: Review it in depth with root-cause or failure modes analysis, as a group
Report it to the certifying body that tested the record system's software
Repeat the yearly downtime drill within the month that follows the outage
Rebuild the disaster recovery plan from scratch before the system restarts
preguntas.explicacion: Unexpected downtimes lasting more than 24 hours are treated as learning material. At least a quarter of the grains eaten should be whole grains
Whole grains should replace refined grains completely

preguntas.pregunta: Two isolation gowns carry different fluid barrier levels. What do those levels come from?

The number of layers of fabric the manufacturer sewed together
The quality level that also grades gloves for micro-perforation
The hazardous materials scale that runs from level A down to D

preguntas.pregunta: After filling three tubes at the bedside, a phlebotomist carries them to the nurses' station and labels them there. Which requirement was broken?

NPSG.01.01.01 EP 1: use at least two identifiers when collecting any specimens
NPSG.02.03.01: report critical results within the established time frame
NPSG.07.01.01: follow the current CDC or WHO hand hygiene guidelines
preguntas.explicacion: Goal 1 has two elements of performance. EP 1 is about the identifiers themselves; EP 2 says that containers for blood and other specimens are labelled in the presence of the patient. preguntas.pregunta: Why must the fluid used for ear irrigation be at body temperature?
opciones: Fluid that is too cold or too hot provokes dizziness through the semicircular canal
Fluid that is too cold or too hot hardens the cerumen and blocks the canal further
Fluid at body temperature dissolves keratin, which is what cerumen is made of
Fluid at body temperature keeps the tympanic membrane from becoming translucent
preguntas.explicacion: The lateral semicircular canal lies close to the ear canal, so water off body temperature sets off vertigo and nystagmus. Warm water drives nystagmus toward the same side and cold water toward the opposite side, remembered as cold-opposite, warm-same. Transient vertigo, hearing loss or tinnitus after irrigation usually trace back to the temperature.

About one-half
About one-quarter
About two-thirds
preguntas.explicacion: Age-related hearing loss is common, affecting about one-third of older adults, and the chance of developing it increases with age. Words the sender prefers, matched to the sender's training
Words taken from the record and repeated as documented
Words in plain language, but delivered only in writing
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal communication is more than talking: it is an exchange of information using words the receiver understands, in a way that carries professional caring and respect. preguntas.pregunta: A trainee argues that a mislabelled tube is just paperwork, since the analyser will still give a correct number. Which published figures answer that?
opciones: Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 18 such errors harms
A tenth of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 100 such errors harms
Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, but no such error has harmed
A quarter of transfusion deaths trace to labelling, and 1 in 3 such errors harms
preguntas.explicacion: Of all the steps before the analysis, collection is arguably the most critical, because an identification error sends the right number to the wrong person. preguntas.pregunta: Which materials are acceptable alternatives to natural rubber latex for a patient with latex allergy?

Powder-free natural rubber latex
Natural rubber without antioxidants
Cornstarch-coated latex gloves

No: a directive covers intubation, while a DNR covers only medication
Yes: any written mention of CPR in the chart operates as a DNR order
Yes: once the directive is scanned in, the code status changes to DNR
preguntas.explicacion: Advance directives are legal documents, not medical orders, so a directive that mentions resuscitation is not equivalent to a do-not-resuscitate or do-not-intubate order. The telephone number on file
An assigned identification number
Any other person-specific identifier

preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's point-of-care potassium is critical again today, as it was at the last two visits and is documented in the chart. What does the reporting policy require?
opciones: Treat it as a reportable event and follow the critical value policy for this instance, even though earlier critical values are known
Skip the call, because a critical value that has already been reported for the same patient does not need to be reported again
Report it only if today's value differs from the previous critical result by more than 10 %, and otherwise just record it
Record it in the log and report all of the day's critical values together to the provider at the end of the clinic session
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are treated as reportable events even when previous critical values are already known for that patient, and the critical value reporting policy is followed consistently each time one is obtained. preguntas.pregunta: A multidimensional approach classifies empathy as which three kinds?
opciones: Cognitive, affective and behavioral
Cognitive, affective and vicarious
Affective, behavioral and moral
Cognitive, behavioral and social

preguntas.pregunta: Why are 3 separate stool specimens recommended for an ova and parasite examination?
opciones: Parasites are not shed in the stool every day, so several samples raise the chance of finding them
Each specimen is examined for a different infection: amebiasis, giardiasis or strongyloidiasis
The first specimen is used for culture, the second for the smear and the third for molecular testing
The specimens are pooled to reach the 8 to 10 mL that the microscope smear requires
preguntas.explicacion: Parasites and their eggs may be absent from the stool on a given day, so collecting several specimens over a few days makes the examination more sensitive; three different specimens are the usual recommendation. In the laboratory a small smear of each is placed on a slide and examined under the microscope, and molecular tests may be added. The 8 to 10 mL figure is the volume of each sputum specimen for tuberculosis.

preguntas.pregunta: Tourniquets have been found contaminated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. By which two routes does that happen?

Poor hand hygiene by the patient and storage of the band in a closed tray
Reuse of a contaminated band and application over a sleeve rather than skin
Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and washing the band between patients
preguntas.explicacion: Up to a quarter of tourniquets have been found carrying this organism, and the two causes named are the phlebotomist's lack of hand hygiene and the reuse of bands that are already contaminated. That is why a disposable band is preferred and why gloves go on before the band.

preguntas.pregunta: Which mechanism is described for winged steel needles that carry a safety feature?
opciones: A needle-locking mechanism that also prevents the set being reused
A blunting mechanism that dulls the tip once the last tube is filled
A colour change in the tubing that shows the set has been used once
A hinged shield activated by pressing the wings against each other
preguntas.explicacion: Winged steel needles with a passive or an active safety feature use a needle-locking mechanism that cuts the risk of a stick and stops reuse, and they make the transfer of blood safer when a syringe is used. preguntas.pregunta: A patient fills a preservative-containing urine tube only to one-third of the marked line. What is the problem?
opciones: Too little urine leaves the preservative too concentrated, which can inhibit bacterial growth in the culture
Too little urine leaves the preservative too dilute, so it cannot keep the bacteria from multiplying in transit
The tube should be filled to the line with sterile normal saline so the preservative ratio is restored
Too little urine is acceptable for culture, since only 15 to 30 mL is needed for an accurate analysis
preguntas.explicacion: The preservative-to-specimen ratio matters in both directions. Overfilling past the line dilutes the preservative and weakens its action; underfilling leaves an excess of preservative that can suppress the very bacteria the culture is looking for. Topping up with saline dilutes the specimen and the colony count, and the 15 to 30 mL figure applies to urinalysis in a plain cup, not to a preservative tube with a fill line.

preguntas.pregunta: What share of needlestick injuries did older studies blame on recapping, and what does current hospital surveillance show?
opciones: Between 10% and 25% then; about 5% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 40% and 60% then; about 20% in the surveillance hospitals now
About 5% then; between 10% and 25% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 10% and 25% then; none at all since the standard prohibited it
preguntas.explicacion: Older studies traced ten to twenty-five percent of needlestick injuries to recapping a used needle. Recapping by hand has been discouraged for years and is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard unless no alternative exists, yet it still causes about five percent of the injuries counted in surveillance hospitals. The share fell; it did not disappear, and that is the point of the rule.

preguntas.pregunta: During a child's venipuncture, why does the second adult grasp the child's wrist palm-up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder, and the firm grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the fingers open so the veins of the hand stay visible
It warms the forearm, which lifts the flow of blood sevenfold
It frees the elbow, which the phlebotomist then holds instead
preguntas.explicacion: The immobiliser reaches across the child and grasps the wrist palm-up: reaching across anchors the child's shoulder and stops twisting or rocking, while the firm grasp on the wrist gives the phlebotomist a tourniquet. The immobiliser's other, outstretched hand holds the elbow. Keeping the child warm is a separate measure that may raise the flow.
