preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory ships a hazardous chemical to another employer. How does the Hazard Communication standard treat it then?
opciones: As a manufacturer or distributor: it must label and send the sheet
As a laboratory still: only the incoming label rules apply to it
As a transporter: only the shipping name and number are needed
As an exempt employer, since the chemical is used in patient care
preguntas.explicacion: The reduced set of duties for laboratories has a limit. A laboratory employer that ships hazardous chemicals is considered a chemical manufacturer or a distributor under the rule, so containers leaving the laboratory have to be labeled the way paragraph (f) requires for shipped containers, and a safety data sheet has to be provided to distributors and other employers. Inside the laboratory the short list applies; on the way out, the full labeling rules do.

The recording is allowed to finish and the lead is fixed afterwards

preguntas.pregunta: In which stage of point-of-care testing do most errors and interfering factors arise?
opciones: The pre-analytical stage, when the sample is collected, handled, prepared and loaded
The analytical stage, while the device is actually measuring the loaded sample
The post-analytical stage, when results are transcribed and communicated to the team
The stages contribute equally, since single-use devices remove most handling steps
preguntas.explicacion: POCT has three stages: pre-analytical (collecting, transporting, preparing and loading the sample), analytical (running the test) and post-analytical (communicating and interpreting results, including critical values). The pre-analytical phase is the most critical controllable variable, and most interfering factors occur there, through errors such as misidentification, hemolysis, clotting, under- or overfilling, prolonged tourniquet time, bubbles and microclots. It disrupts the stacking of red cells and raises the value obtained

It raises the value, in the same way that a tilted tube raises it

It is given only when the patient asks, at intervals of four to six hours apart
It is given once and without delay, because of how urgent the circumstances are
It is given at a rate that the nurse raises or lowers according to the response
preguntas.explicacion: An around-the-clock frequency means fixed intervals, for example every six hours, so the concentration of the drug in the patient's bloodstream is kept consistent; that is why pain medication at the end of life is often ordered this way instead of as needed. The machine can erase the record stored inside the device

A report of the patient's employer and insurance details for a workplace injury claim

A report of psychotherapy notes to a family member concerned about the patient

preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a phlebotomist to start an intravenous line for a patient's chemotherapy. How much of the history should the request carry?

The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer
No history at all, since treatment details may not be shared
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are not restricted from talking to one another about treatment, and a patient's care would stall if they were. From the chest muscles, when the patient breathes too deeply
From the arm and leg muscles, when the electrodes have dried
From the heart muscle itself, when the rate climbs above 100

One dose every two years
One dose every five years
Two doses annually for adults

It keeps the agent's authority alive after the person has died
It lets the agent decide about the finances as well as the medical care
It lets the agent be replaced by a backup without a new document

preguntas.pregunta: A red-top tube is left to clot and then centrifuged. What is the fluid above the clot called, and how does it differ from plasma?
opciones: Serum; it is plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed
Plasma; it still contains fibrinogen and the other clotting factors
Buffy coat; the pale layer of leukocytes and platelets above the cells
Whole blood; the formed elements are suspended in the fluid again
preguntas.explicacion: Serum is plasma after the clotting factors have been removed: in a clotted tube it is the fluid squeezed out of the clot as it retracts. Plasma is the fluid part of circulating blood, still carrying fibrinogen and the other factors; serum is what remains liquid after the blood clots in a tube. The buffy coat is the layer of white cells and platelets in a spun, unclotted sample, and whole blood has all the formed elements suspended.

A 20% intravenous lipid emulsion, 1.5 mL/kg over one hour, with no further infusion after

Within 30 days of surgery, and organ or space infections are over half of them

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with obesity has a pulse that cannot be found with light fingertip pressure. What is the next step at the bedside?
opciones: Palpate more deeply or reposition the limb, since a light touch can miss a pulse
Press as hard as possible, because heavy pressure brings a deep pulse to the surface
Record the pulse as absent, because a pulse that light pressure misses is not present
Move to the opposite limb, because a pulse missed on one side is always felt on the other

preguntas.pregunta: Cortisol follows a diurnal rhythm. When is secretion at its peak?
opciones: Near the time of awakening, after rising in the last hours of sleep
Around 4 p.m., after rising steadily through the afternoon
At night, when ACTH release from the pituitary is highest
About two hours after the first meal of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Cortisol secretion follows a diurnal rhythm: levels begin to rise in the final hours of sleep, peak near the time of awakening, decline gradually through the day and reach their lowest concentration at night; healthy adults produce 8 to 30 mg per day. Around 4 p.m. levels are much lower than in the morning, which is why the second sample is drawn then.

preguntas.pregunta: A scheduling error leaves a patient without the coverage her clinician had arranged. How is that treated?

As a breach of unsecured protected health information requiring individual notice
As an information blocking practice, since care was interfered with electronically
As a minimum necessary failure, since the schedule reached the wrong people

15 mL in each bottle, for a target of 30 mL in the set

The history and physical examination updated for any change in condition
The consultation report from the anesthesia service covering the procedure

preguntas.pregunta: How do Transmission-Based Precautions relate to Standard Precautions, according to the CDC?
opciones: A second tier added to Standard Precautions for patients with certain known or suspected infections
A replacement for Standard Precautions once a pathogen has been confirmed by the laboratory
The first tier, applied to every patient until an infection has been ruled out
A set that covers bloodborne pathogens only, while Standard Precautions cover respiratory ones
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission-Based Precautions are the second tier of basic infection control, used in addition to Standard Precautions for patients who may be infected or colonized with agents that need extra measures. They never replace the first tier, and they are triggered by known or suspected infection, not applied to everyone. The three categories are Contact, Droplet and Airborne, chosen by the route of transmission; bloodborne exposure is handled by Standard Precautions and the OSHA standard.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an implanted defibrillator needs electrosurgery on a small lesion. Which precautions apply?
opciones: Bursts under five seconds, lower power, no cutting current, and stay away from the device
Bursts under thirty seconds, higher power, cutting current only, and stay away from the device
Bursts under five seconds, higher power, no coagulation current, and work over the device
Continuous current at low power, no bursts at all, and work as close to the device as possible
preguntas.explicacion: Current can interfere with pacemakers and implantable defibrillators, causing skipped beats, a discharge, bradycardia, asystole or reprogramming. The recommendations are short bursts of under five seconds, lower power settings, avoiding cutting current, and avoiding the area around the device; confining current to a small area with bipolar forceps also lowers the risk.

She is told she has gestational diabetes and is started on a diet
She repeats the same 50 g screening drink at her next prenatal visit
She returns fasting for a 2-hour, 75 g glucose tolerance test

preguntas.pregunta: Where does latex rank among the causes of anaphylaxis in the operating room?
opciones: Second, after muscle relaxants
First, ahead of muscle relaxants
Third, after antibiotics and dyes
Second, after the antiseptic used on skin
preguntas.explicacion: Latex allergy is among the most common causes of anaphylaxis in the operating room, and its prevalence grew with the wider use of latex gloves from the 1980s onward. preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a national coverage determination and a local coverage determination?

The national one binds the whole program; the local one is issued by the state insurance office
The national one applies to hospitals and the local one applies to physician offices
The national one is advisory and the local one decides payment for the claim at hand
preguntas.explicacion: National coverage determinations limit coverage of a service, procedure or technology across the program, and HHS decides them through an evidence-based process that may include an outside technology assessment or the advisory committee. A certificate of compliance
A certificate of accreditation
A certificate for PPM procedures

Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after the breach is discovered

About 3 inches (7.6 cm) above the skin fold at the bend of the elbow

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague suggests puncturing the back (posterior curve) of a newborn's heel. Why is that spot avoided?
opciones: In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is only 2.33 mm, so the lancet may hit bone
In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is 3.32 mm, too deep for a lancet to reach blood
The posterior heel is where the tibial artery runs closest to the skin surface
The posterior heel is the site the WHO reserves for premature neonates with a 0.85 mm lancet
preguntas.explicacion: In a 7 pound (3 kg) baby the distances from skin to bone are: 3.32 mm at the medial and lateral heel, 2.33 mm at the posterior heel and 2.19 mm at the toe. The tibial artery is the risk of the medial aspect of the heel, and the 0.85 mm lancet is simply the size available for premature neonates.

preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine for porphyrins is ordered. Which container feature does this analyte require?

A clear container, so the laboratory can see the color of the pooled urine
A vacuum tube, which draws the sample without opening the container
A sterile container, because porphyrin testing requires a bacteriological culture

Choose the template and the letterhead the practice prefers
Decide which class of mail will carry the finished letter
Check the reading level of the last letter the practice sent

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to use a metered-dose inhaler. Why is a spacer considered best practice?
opciones: It stops particles from settling on the tongue or drifting away into the room air
It warms the medication so that the airway does not spasm as the mist arrives
It lets the patient inhale strongly and quickly, which is what activates a powder
It counts the doses left in the canister so that a refill is ordered on time
preguntas.explicacion: As the patient breathes in from a metered-dose inhaler, small particles get caught on the tongue or aerosolize into the air and never reach the lungs, so a spacer is fitted to get the whole dose in and to waste less. The inhaler is shaken, the spacer attached, the patient exhales and then breathes in normally through it. A strong, quick breath is what a dry powder inhaler needs, not this one.

preguntas.pregunta: V1 is already marked on a patient's chest. Where does V2 go?

One space lower, on the other side of the sternum
One space higher, on the other side of the sternum
At the same space, out in the mid-clavicular line

Wash the area well with soap and water and leave it free of cream
Come without washing, but apply a light moisturizer beforehand
Wash the skin well and keep the eyes covered for the whole visit

The history, the instrument used, the suture material chosen and the dressing applied after
The exact biopsy location, the anesthetic used, the volume injected and the time of injection
The lesion's duration, the antiseptic used, the number of specimens and the container's lot number

preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks about cooling a feverish child with an ice bath or an alcohol rub. What is the instruction?
opciones: Neither is used: both cool the skin and set off shivering, which drives core temperature up
Both are used, but only after an antipyretic, so that the value does not rebound
The ice bath is acceptable; the alcohol rub is avoided because the skin absorbs it
Neither is used, because cooling the skin has no measurable effect on temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Cold baths, ice and alcohol rubs are ruled out: they chill the skin and provoke shivering, and shivering raises the core temperature, so the child ends up worse. A lukewarm bath or sponge bath may help, and it works better after medicine has been given, otherwise the temperature climbs straight back up.

Add a question about reading skills to the intake form and read the answers
Have the clinician judge during the visit which patients seem to struggle

Skip dented cans only, since bulging is caused by normal temperature change
Skip cans past the date only, since packaging damage does not reach the food

Lift each tube out of the rack and hold it steady in the free hand
Keep the tubes in the rack and tilt them so the blood runs down the wall
Lift the rack up to eye level so the coloured stoppers stay in view

preguntas.pregunta: Why do devices with safety features reduce needlestick injuries without eliminating them?
opciones: Some cannot be activated until the needle is out, and some users bypass them
Their shields are made of plastic, which a needle can pierce from inside
They are sold only for hypodermic needles, not for blood collection sets
They must be removed before the tube is filled, leaving the tip exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Several things keep the risk above zero. With some designs the safety feature cannot be engaged until the needle has already left the patient; a needle can be dislodged during the procedure and leave the sharp exposed; some workers do not activate the feature at all; the feature itself can fail; and with some systems users can work around it, as when a needle is used to connect parts of a needleless intravenous system. Training and monitoring after implementation are what close that gap.

preguntas.pregunta: How much alcohol-based hand rub goes on the hands, and how is it worked in?

A single small drop, rubbed into the palms and wiped with a towel
About 15 to 20 mL, poured over the hands and rinsed off with water
Enough to fill a cupped hand, left to evaporate without any rubbing
preguntas.explicacion: When hands are not visibly soiled the alcohol rub is the preferred method, and it is used as the manufacturer directs: roughly three to five millilitres in the palm, rubbed vigorously over all hand surfaces until dry, which takes about twenty seconds. preguntas.pregunta: Tubes of blood go from the draw room to the in-house laboratory in a closed rack, and the facility applies Universal Precautions to all specimens. Is a biohazard label required?
opciones: Not while they stay in the facility and are recognizable as specimens; it is required once they leave
Yes, always: every container of blood must carry the fluorescent orange-red biohazard label
No, never: labeling applies to regulated waste containers, not to specimens of blood
Only if the primary container becomes contaminated on the outside and needs a second container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(A) requires specimen containers for storage, transport or shipping to be labeled or color-coded and closed, but it exempts facilities that handle all specimens under Universal Precautions, provided the containers are recognizable as specimens; the exemption holds only inside the facility, and the label returns the moment specimens leave it. preguntas.pregunta: The bevel is inside the vein and blood has appeared. How is the needle advanced from there?
opciones: Along the vein, at whichever angle of entry proves easiest
Straight down at ninety degrees until the hub meets the skin
Back out a few millimetres and then in again at a steeper angle
Sideways across the vein so the bevel opens against the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The vein is entered swiftly at thirty degrees or less, and the needle then continues along the vein at the easiest angle of entry rather than being pushed deeper. Driving it beyond the lumen of the vein is what produces a haematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin.

preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that her records be mailed to her home. The office tells her to come in person with photo identification. What is wrong with that?

Requiring photo identification is forbidden, since the rule bars verifying who is asking
Requiring mail delivery is forbidden, since mail is not a readily producible means of transfer

Coercion, an overt threat of harm presented to obtain compliance
Incomplete disclosure, because the payment hides a real risk
Injustice, because the burden falls on the people who volunteer
preguntas.explicacion: Belmont separates the two: coercion is an overt threat of harm made to get compliance, while undue influence works through an excessive, unwarranted or improper reward. It adds that an inducement that would ordinarily be acceptable can turn into undue influence when the subject is especially vulnerable. Justice in Belmont is about who gets selected for research.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office for Human Research Protections, The Belmont Report (April 18, 1979), Part C.1: Voluntariness

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a sore throat says she gargled with antiseptic mouthwash on the way to the office. Why does that matter for a throat culture?
opciones: Antiseptic mouthwash is specifically to be avoided before the test, which is otherwise unprepared for
Antiseptic mouthwash is required before the test, so the swab picks up only pharyngeal organisms
Antiseptic mouthwash makes the patient gag more, which prevents the swab from reaching the tonsils
Antiseptic mouthwash stains the pharynx, so the provider cannot see where to place the swab
preguntas.explicacion: The one preparation instruction for a throat swab culture is to skip antiseptic mouthwash beforehand, since it works against the organisms the culture is meant to grow. Everything else about the test needs no preparation. Rinsing the mouth with plain water belongs to sputum collection, where the aim is to wash away oral contaminants rather than to kill anything.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Throat swab culture (003746), How to Prepare for the Test

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a drug level ordered as a trough but says he took this morning's dose an hour ago. What matters?
opciones: Timing relative to the dose changes the result; report it before drawing
The level is stable through the day, so proceed and label the tube as ordered
Draw it now and relabel the sample as a peak level instead of a trough
Wait 30 minutes, which is the standard window for any trough sample
preguntas.explicacion: For TDM the test may need to be scheduled before or after the regular dose depending on the medicine, and the level in the blood varies over time as the body processes the drug. The trough is the point just before the next dose; a sample an hour after dosing is not that. Relabelling it as a peak invents a measurement that was not ordered.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, sections What is TDM, and Will I need to do anything to prepare
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her stomach hurts, and the clinician finds tenderness on palpation. Where does each item belong in a SOAP note?
opciones: The reported pain is subjective and the tenderness found on examination is objective
Both belong under objective, since the clinician wrote them down during the same visit
Both belong under subjective, since abdominal complaints cannot be measured directly
The reported pain is objective and the tenderness found on examination is subjective
preguntas.explicacion: A common documentation mistake is blurring symptoms and signs. Symptoms are what the patient describes and go under subjective; signs are the objective findings related to the reported symptom and go under objective. The article uses this very pair as its illustration: a report of stomach pain against tenderness found on palpation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Objective

preguntas.pregunta: A claim sits unpaid for weeks and the payer finally reports that the member cannot be matched. The patient's surname was mistyped at registration. Which phase of the revenue cycle should have caught it?
opciones: Patient data verification, which checks the name, age, eligibility and billing address
Charge capture, which assembles the documented visit, the services and the facility fees
Claim scrubbing, which searches the outgoing claim for coding and formatting errors
Remittance processing, which posts the payment and sorts the contractual write-offs
preguntas.explicacion: Verification is the phase whose whole job is to keep claims from being rejected, delayed or denied, and the data it checks are the full name, the age, insurance eligibility, the billing address and, above all, preauthorizations. Insurers have been known to let a claim languish over a misspelled name rather than report the failed match. Charge capture, scrubbing and posting all happen later and none of them compares the patient's identity against the plan.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Patient Data Verification

preguntas.pregunta: Two boxes of gloves list different acceptable quality levels. What does a lower number mean?
opciones: A better glove, with fewer pinholes and micro-perforations
A thicker glove, made to be worn as the outer of two pairs
A cheaper glove, meant for handling clean supplies only
A sterile glove, treated so that microbes are eliminated
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptable quality level is a measure of how many defective units a batch may contain, so a lower figure means a higher quality glove with less potential for micro-perforation and fewer pinholes. The recommended minimum is 1.5 for surgical gloves and 2.5 for medical examination gloves. Sterility is a separate property: surgical procedures call for sterile gloves, which have been treated to eliminate microbes, and evidence supports two layers during surgery.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE

preguntas.pregunta: Immediately after washing a needlestick with soap and water, what does NIOSH tell the worker to do?
opciones: Report the incident to the supervisor and seek medical care right away
Wait 72 hours to see whether symptoms appear before reporting
Test the discarded needle for virus before deciding whether to report
Start the hepatitis B vaccine series on their own before reporting
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH's steps are to wash punctures and cuts with soap and water, flush splashes, irrigate eyes, report the incident to the supervisor and immediately seek medical care to determine the risk; it adds that an incident report should be completed where applicable. The 72-hour figure is the outer limit for starting HIV PEP, not a waiting period. WHO's annex specifically says not to test discarded needles or syringes for virus, and any prophylaxis or vaccination is decided during the medical evaluation.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors (Feb. 13, 2025), Treatment and Reporting; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Reporting an exposure · CPT D1 1H k33 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports an allergy to penicillin. What does the record need besides the drug name?
opciones: The reaction it caused, because many patients carry the label without a true allergy
The brand name of the product, because generics do not provoke the same reaction
The date another practice first entered the allergy into the chart being reviewed
Whether an antihistamine was taken, because that clears the entry from the list
preguntas.explicacion: An allergy entry is only useful when the nature of the earlier reaction is recorded with it. That matters most with the beta-lactams, where a great many patients are classified as allergic without being so, and validated tools exist to judge how likely a true drug allergy is. Every allergen asked about, medication or food or latex, gets the same treatment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Allergies and Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k44 · CMA I.A.4.e · RMA III.F.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: What makes an instrument a speculum?
opciones: It goes into a body cavity to help see inside, lit or unlit
It holds the edges of an opening apart to keep tissue exposed
It grips a structure with a hooked point so it can be pulled
It scrapes loose cells off a surface so they can be studied
preguntas.explicacion: A speculum is defined by its purpose: it is inserted into a cavity of the body to aid observation, and it may or may not be illuminated. Holding the edges apart is the retractor's job, gripping and pulling is what the tenaculum does, and scraping cells off the cervix belongs to the cytological spatula.
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · CCMA 3B4 k63

preguntas.pregunta: The prevacuum sterilizer is run each morning with a folded towel pack and a test sheet before the first load. What is being checked?
opciones: Whether air is leaking in or is not being removed, since trapped air blocks steam contact
Whether the resistant spores in the pack survive, which is the direct measure of lethality
Whether the chamber holds pressure long enough for a wrapped load to reach its temperature
Whether the wrap material still lets steam through after repeated laundering and folding
preguntas.explicacion: That is the Bowie-Dick test, and it detects air leaks and incomplete air removal. The sheet goes in the middle of the pack, the pack sits horizontally at the front bottom of an otherwise empty chamber over the drain, and a uniform color change means the vacuum is acceptable; a spot means air kept the steam off the indicator. Spores measure lethality, and that is a different test.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA Essential 5

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee is taught the boundaries of the fossa before palpating it. Which muscles form its lateral and medial borders?
opciones: Brachioradialis on the lateral side and pronator teres on the medial side
Pronator teres on the lateral side and brachioradialis on the medial side
Biceps brachii on the lateral side and brachialis on the medial side
Brachialis on the lateral side and supinator on the medial side of the fossa
preguntas.explicacion: The triangle is bounded laterally by the medial edge of brachioradialis and medially by the lateral edge of pronator teres, with an imaginary line between the epicondyles of the humerus closing it above. Brachialis and supinator lie deeper: they form the floor rather than the sides.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8

preguntas.pregunta: A mother phones about her 2-month-old, whose rectal temperature is 38.1 °C (100.6 °F). What does this call for?
opciones: The provider is contacted right away: 38 °C rectally at 3 months or under is reportable
Fluids and a repeat reading in 24 hours, since the value sits only slightly above the normal band
A repeat reading by the axillary route, because a rectal value is read one degree high
A lukewarm sponge bath first, and a call only if the reading has not come down by then
preguntas.explicacion: Infants of 3 months or younger are the one group where the threshold triggers a call on its own: a rectal reading of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher is reported to the provider immediately, whatever the baby looks like. Waiting a day applies to older children, and no route correction is applied to a rectal value.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures form the central nervous system, and which form the peripheral nervous system?
opciones: Brain and spinal cord centrally; the nerves branching from them peripherally
Brain and cranial nerves centrally; the spinal cord and its nerves peripherally
Spinal cord and ganglia centrally; the brain and its coverings peripherally
Brain and meninges centrally; the spinal cord and the ganglia peripherally
preguntas.explicacion: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord, both inside the dorsal body cavity and both wrapped in bone, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid. The peripheral system is everything that branches out from them, and it forms the communication network between the center and the rest of the body.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives with her adult son, who answers every question for her. How should you handle the visit?
opciones: Ask the patient how she sees her son's role, and keep addressing her directly
Speak mainly to the son, since he manages her medications at home
Ask the son to leave the room before any question is put to her
Record the son as her legal decision-maker for the rest of the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Check with the patient about how they see the companion's role, to protect privacy, and keep the patient involved, sitting so both can be addressed face to face and not directing remarks only to the companion. Asking the companion to step out is an option for sensitive topics, and legal authority to decide exists only for a named health care agent or proxy.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · CCMA 3E1 k127 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2B.2

preguntas.pregunta: A culture is knocked over and spills a large volume in the laboratory. How is the hypochlorite used?
opciones: A 1:10 dilution for the first application before cleaning, then a 1:100 terminal disinfection
A 1:100 dilution for the first application before cleaning, then a 1:10 terminal disinfection
A 1:10 dilution applied once after the visible matter has been cleaned up and discarded
A 1:100 dilution applied twice, with the second application left in place for thirty minutes
preguntas.explicacion: With a large spill, over about 10 mL, or with a laboratory culture spill, the stronger 1:10 dilution goes on first, before cleaning, so that the risk from a sharps injury during the cleanup is already reduced. A terminal disinfection with the 1:100 dilution follows. Visible matter is picked up with disposable absorbent material and discarded in labeled containment.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations 5n: Environmental Surfaces
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.i · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: A Certificate of Waiver site wants to add a moderate complexity analyzer. What must it do before running the first patient sample on it?
opciones: Reapply on Form CMS-116, pay the fee, and receive the appropriate certificate
Notify the state agency within 30 days after the analyzer goes into use
Run two levels of control and document the results for 20 consecutive days
Enroll the new analyte in proficiency testing and pass the first event
preguntas.explicacion: Adding PPM or any nonwaived test to a waived-only menu means reapplying for the appropriate certificate, using the same Form CMS-116 as the original application. Nonwaived testing cannot begin until the fee is paid and the new certificate is received. The 30-day notice covers ownership, name, location and director; quality control and proficiency testing are requirements once nonwaived testing is under way.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): if you perform only waived tests and wish to add PPM or other nonwaived testing

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether to skip his blood-pressure pill before a fasting draw. What is the correct guidance?
opciones: Do not stop a medicine unless the provider said to; ask the provider
Skip every medicine on the morning of the draw, because all pills break a fast
Take it only with a little juice so that the stomach is protected
Take it after the draw with water, never before a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should ask the provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines are fine; for some tests the provider may ask them to stop, but a medicine is never stopped unless the provider says so. Vitamins and supplements should also be reported. Juice is on the list of drinks that break a fast.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section Can I continue taking medicine during a fast
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being evaluated for pulmonary tuberculosis. Which sputum collection and storage instruction is correct?
opciones: Three early-morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each, kept in a refrigerator
One early-morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL, kept at room temperature
Three specimens collected at any time of day, each frozen at −20 °C
Three early-morning specimens of 2 to 3 mL each, kept in a CO2 incubator
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early-morning sputum specimens, 8 to 10 mL each, is collected and stored refrigerated; in patients who cannot cooperate the organism may be recovered from gastric contents obtained by stomach aspiration. Freezing is not part of the instruction, a single specimen is not a series, and the carbon dioxide incubator belongs to cerebrospinal fluid awaiting culture.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Sputum Specimens)

preguntas.pregunta: Where should the sharps container sit while a phlebotomist is drawing blood at the bedside?
opciones: Visible and within arm's reach, and sealed once it is used up
On the cart outside the room, so the patient does not see it
In the utility room, where the used needles are carried after
On the floor by the bed, where it cannot be knocked over easily
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table asks for puncture and leak-proof containers that are sealed after use, kept visible and within arm's reach, and the reason given is that this prevents needlestick injury to patients, health workers and the wider community. The bloodborne pathogens standard says the same in regulatory language: during use the container is easily accessible and as close as feasible to where sharps are used, kept upright, and replaced before it overfills.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Sharps containers; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Where the container goes · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician with similar training and experience would provide
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is judged against the standard of care, defined as what a reasonable physician in the community with similar training and experience would do for that patient; it does not demand perfection, and some states speak of gross negligence. Malpractice itself is the failure to provide the degree of care another clinician in the same position with the same credentials would have provided, resulting in injury. Facility policies and patient expectations may be evidence, but the legal yardstick is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Introduction and Negligence or breach of duty
preguntas.subtema: Standard of care · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.b · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31

preguntas.pregunta: In therapy after shoulder surgery a patient raises the arm while the assistant supplies about half the effort. What is that called?
opciones: Active assist range of motion, with partial help from an outside force
Active range of motion, since the patient starts the movement alone
Passive range of motion, since another person is moving the shoulder
Resisted range of motion, since the arm is working against a force
preguntas.explicacion: Active assist range of motion is joint movement with partial help from an outside force, and the fifty per cent of help given by a physical therapy assistant during shoulder recovery is the example given. Movement by the patient alone is active, and movement supplied entirely from outside is passive.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65

preguntas.pregunta: Why is absorption from a subcutaneous injection slow and sustained?
opciones: The layer beneath the dermis holds few blood vessels, so the drug leaves it gradually
The layer beneath the dermis is richly vascular, so the drug pools there before moving
The drug has to cross the epidermis first, and that barrier slows every molecule down
The drug travels through the portal vein, so the liver removes part of every dose
preguntas.explicacion: A subcutaneous injection is placed in the layer of skin just under the dermis and epidermis. That tissue carries few blood vessels, so what is injected is taken up at a slow, sustained rate. The usual sites are the outer area of the upper arm, the abdomen while staying clear of a two-inch circle around the navel, the front of the thigh, the upper back and the upper buttock behind the hip bone.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Parenteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(2) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the impulse pause at the atrioventricular node before it reaches the ventricles?
opciones: So the atria can finish pumping blood into the ventricles first
So the ventricles can finish filling from the great veins first
So the sinoatrial node can recover before it fires the next time
So the Purkinje fibers can repolarize after the previous beat
preguntas.explicacion: The nodal cells are small and conduct less efficiently than the rest of the system, so the impulse is held up for roughly a tenth of a second. That pause is what lets the atrial muscle complete its contraction and load the ventricles before the ventricular walls are told to squeeze.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Atrioventricular Node
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A processor inspects centrifuged serum tubes and sets aside the ones that look pink. Why do current recommendations favour an automated hemolysis index over this visual check?
opciones: Visual detection is inaccurate: serum looks hemolysed only above about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, whereas the index is reproducible
Visual detection is accurate for serum but not for plasma, so the index is needed only for anticoagulated tubes
Visual detection is reliable above 0.5 g/L, but only the index can detect hemolysis before centrifugation
Visual detection cannot distinguish hemolysis from lipemia, whereas the index reports both as a single value
preguntas.explicacion: Sample quality used to be judged by looking at the tube before and after spinning, but visual detection is inaccurate: after separation, free hemoglobin becomes visible only around 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the cut-off for clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. Chemistry analyzers measure the serum indices, hemolysis included, with high reproducibility, which is why systematic automated measurement is strongly recommended.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a brief real-time exchange with her doctor that lasted under ten minutes. What is that called?
opciones: A virtual check-in
An online e-visit
A monitoring session
A telephone triage call
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare describes several ways to use telehealth. E-visits are non-face-to-face communications that usually run through an online patient portal. Virtual check-ins are brief, real-time communications that usually last ten minutes or less. Both sit alongside the fuller telehealth visits that replace services normally given in person, such as office visits and psychotherapy.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Virtual check-ins · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about high-level, intermediate-level and low-level disinfectants is accurate?
opciones: A high-level agent kills everything except small numbers of spores; a low-level one spares spores entirely
A high-level agent is sporicidal at any contact time; an intermediate one is sporicidal only if left overnight
An intermediate-level agent reliably kills spores; a high-level one is defined by killing mycobacteria alone
A low-level agent kills mycobacteria and most fungi; a high-level one is limited to vegetative bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: The ladder is built on what survives. High-level agents are the same chemicals used as sterilants but for shorter exposure, so they leave only small numbers of spores. Intermediate-level agents may kill mycobacteria, vegetative bacteria and most viruses and fungi but not spores, and low-level ones handle most vegetative bacteria and some fungi and viruses within about ten minutes.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Definition of Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient living in a nursing home elects hospice. What should the family be told about room and board?
opciones: Medicare does not cover it, so the family may still have to pay the facility
Medicare covers it in full once the hospice election statement is signed
Medicare covers it only during the first two 90-day benefit periods of care
Medicare covers it whenever the nursing home also accepts Medicare assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Room and board is not covered when hospice care is given at home, in a nursing home or in a hospice inpatient facility, so a person living in a facility may still owe that cost. If the hospice team decides short-term inpatient or respite care is needed and arranges it, Medicare pays for the stay. A stay the team did not arrange can leave the patient owing the whole bill.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Costs
preguntas.subtema: Hospice in a facility · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30

preguntas.pregunta: Which group of items are the preanalytical quality indicators proposed by the IFCC working group on laboratory errors and patient safety?
opciones: Inappropriate containers, insufficient volume, hemolyzed or clotted samples, improper storage, transport damage
Reagent lot changes, calibration drift, control values out of range, instrument downtime and maintenance
Turnaround time, corrected reports, critical value notification time, legibility and delivery of reports
Repeat test rate, physician satisfaction, cost per test, proficiency testing scores and staff competency
preguntas.explicacion: The IFCC WG-LEPS indicators for the preanalytical phase cover appropriateness of test selection, patient and sample identification, samples collected in inappropriate containers or with insufficient volume, hemolyzed or clotted samples, improperly stored samples and samples damaged in transport. Calibration and controls are analytical measures; turnaround, corrected reports and critical value timing are post-analytical ones.

preguntas.pregunta: Which code set is used to report the patient's diagnosis on a claim?
opciones: ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification used for diagnostic information
ICD-10-PCS, the procedure system used for inpatient facility claims
HCPCS Level II, the system used for supplies, equipment and ambulance
The national drug codes, used for the drugs and biologics dispensed
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic information is coded with ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification maintained on the CDC side. The procedure coding system, ICD-10-PCS, is used for procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A. HCPCS Level II names products, supplies, ambulance services and equipment, and national drug codes identify drugs and biologics, so none of the three carries the diagnosis.

preguntas.pregunta: What target serum trough range is given for vancomycin, varying with the indication?
opciones: 10 to 20 micrograms per millilitre
1 to 2 micrograms per millilitre
30 to 40 micrograms per millilitre
100 to 200 micrograms per millilitre
preguntas.explicacion: Trough concentrations let the team judge whether the dosing regimen is working and how the drug is being cleared. The target serum trough depends on the indication and typically runs from 10 to 20 micrograms per millilitre. It is obtained ideally within the 30 minutes before a dose, once steady-state conditions have been reached.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasted twelve hours before a blood count on his own initiative, though nobody asked him to. What is the concern?
opciones: Fasting when it was not ordered can itself skew some test results
Fasting beyond eight hours voids any test drawn that same morning
Fasting without an order has to be logged as a protocol deviation
Fasting is harmless here, and the sample is unaffected either way
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told plainly not to fast unless the provider asks them to, because fasting for some blood tests may itself affect the results and hand the provider an inaccurate picture of the patient's health. The instruction is to follow the preparation instructions given; no rule voids a sample because the fast ran long.

preguntas.pregunta: An office needs to bill for a wheelchair supplied to a patient at home. Which code set covers that item?
opciones: HCPCS Level II, which names durable medical equipment and similar supplies
HCPCS Level I, which names the professional services physicians perform
ICD-10-PCS, which names procedures reported on inpatient facility claims
The code on dental procedures, which names items dispensed to patients
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS Level II exists precisely because insurers cover services, supplies and equipment that Level I codes do not identify: it names products, supplies, ambulance services and durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies used outside a physician's office. Level I describes medical procedures and professional services, and dental nomenclature covers dental services.

preguntas.pregunta: A transplant patient is scheduled for a tacrolimus level. What timing does the reported reference range assume?

The sample is taken 2 hours after the dose
The sample is taken immediately before the dose
The sample is taken at any hour of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Tacrolimus is reported as 5 to 25 ng/mL with the sample drawn 12 hours after the dose, and the two other drugs used to suppress the immune response against transplanted organs carry the same note: cyclosporine 25 to 525 ng/mL and sirolimus 4 to 14 ng/mL, both at 12 hours. preguntas.pregunta: An unaccompanied 10-year-old with an emergency medical condition needs urgent labs and no parent can be reached. What protects the team that proceeds?
opciones: The emergency exception, also called the doctrine of implied consent
The mature minor doctrine, because the child understands the test
Informed permission, granted on the spot by the hospital administrator
Title X of the Public Health Service Act, covering minors' services
preguntas.explicacion: EMTALA requires a screening exam regardless of consent, and that when an emergency condition is found in an unaccompanied minor, life- or limb-saving care proceeds without waiting for parental consent, protected by the emergency exception rule or doctrine of implied consent, which assumes a reasonable parent would agree. Title X covers reproductive services.

Watches and rings cause it, although glasses do not
Metal objects cause it whenever they touch a lead wire
They cause it only in a room holding several machines
preguntas.explicacion: Jewelry is not the source of electrical interference: watches, glasses, rings and bracelets are named as things that do not cause it, so the hunt goes to the electrode contact and to nearby equipment. Preparation guidance still has metallic objects removed before the recording begins.

opciones: The plan does, through a yearly limit after which it pays all covered services
The plan does not, and neither does Original Medicare without extra coverage
Original Medicare does, through the deductible she pays once each calendar year
Neither does, since a yearly limit belongs to Medigap policies alone
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare sets no yearly limit on what a person pays out of pocket unless she adds supplemental coverage such as a Medigap policy or joins a Medicare Advantage Plan. Advantage plans carry an out-of-pocket limit that varies by plan; once it is reached the plan pays the whole cost of covered services for the rest of the calendar year.

preguntas.pregunta: Where do the coronary arteries arise, and where does most of the blood from the coronary veins drain?
opciones: From the ascending aorta; into the coronary sinus and then the right atrium
From the aortic arch; into the coronary sinus and then the left atrium
From the pulmonary trunk; directly into the superior vena cava
From the ascending aorta; into the four pulmonary veins and left atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The right and left coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta, and they are the only branches of that segment. After passing through the myocardial capillaries most cardiac veins empty into the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium on its posterior wall, just above and medial to the opening of the inferior vena cava.

preguntas.pregunta: A PNAS study examined false beliefs about biological differences between Black and White patients held by medical trainees. What did those beliefs lead to?

Higher rates of hypertension among the trainees who held the beliefs
More referrals of Black patients for kidney transplantation
Overtreatment of pain in Black patients compared with White patients
preguntas.explicacion: Medical students and residents who endorsed beliefs such as thicker skin or less sensitive nerve endings rated Black patients' pain lower and made less accurate treatment recommendations, a legacy visible in the undertreatment of pain. opciones: Higher rates of substance abuse and of suicide
Higher rates of missed appointments and no-shows
Higher rates of insurance denial for routine care
Higher rates of prolonged grief after a bereavement
preguntas.explicacion: Members of this community have faced discrimination and prejudice from providers and have avoided or delayed care because of it, and significant health disparities persist. preguntas.pregunta: Two departments argue over which of them should admit a patient. Which type of conflict is that?
opciones: Intergroup conflict
Intragroup conflict
Interpersonal conflict
Organizational conflict
preguntas.explicacion: Intergroup conflict is disagreement between teams, departments or professional groups, and a dispute between intensive care and surgery over admission criteria is the example used. Intragroup conflict stays inside one unit, interpersonal conflict is between two individuals, and organizational conflict is structural, about policy, pay, staffing or governance.

preguntas.pregunta: Which finding on an arm rules that arm out for a blood pressure cuff altogether, rather than merely calling for caution?
opciones: A dialysis arteriovenous fistula or shunt built into that arm
Swelling from lymphedema that followed surgery on that side
An indwelling venous catheter running in that arm at present
Weakness of that arm left behind by an old cerebrovascular event
preguntas.explicacion: Cuff limitations come in two tiers. A dialysis fistula or shunt, a recent surgical wound and a mastectomy on that side put the limb out of use entirely. Lymphedema, paresis or paralysis, and arterial or venous lines call for caution instead. In either tier the answer is the same: choose the other limb or another site before inflating.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: An insurer asks a substance use disorder treatment program to confirm that a named person is a patient there. What may the program say?
opciones: Nothing that would reveal the person has been diagnosed or treated there
Only the dates of admission and of discharge, with no clinical detail at all
That the regulations bar it from confirming this particular patient
The detail the insurer needs, since payment is a permitted purpose
preguntas.explicacion: An answer that is not permitted has to be given in a way that does not reveal that an identified person has been or is being diagnosed or treated for a substance use disorder. The program may hand the inquirer a copy of the rules and explain that they restrict disclosure in general, but it may not say that they restrict the records of that named patient — which is a confirmation in disguise.

preguntas.pregunta: For which patients can eye contact and sitting close be destabilizing?
opciones: Patients with a psychotic disorder or with paranoia
Patients with hearing loss who are reading your lips
Patients with expressive aphasia after a recent stroke
Patients with low vision who cannot make out the room
preguntas.explicacion: The table of techniques carries a warning: for some people, including those with psychotic disorders and paranoia, eye contact and sitting near can be destabilizing, and where staff safety is uncertain the advice is to sit at a safe distance without leaving the patient feeling isolated. Hearing loss calls for the opposite, facing the patient directly.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques

preguntas.pregunta: When must HIV post-exposure prophylaxis begin, and how long does the course last, according to the CDC?
opciones: As soon as possible and within 72 hours; a 28-day course
As soon as possible and within 7 days; a 14-day course
As soon as possible and within 24 hours; a 7-day course
Within 72 hours; a 6-month course, the length of follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who seek care within 72 hours are evaluated rapidly; PEP is not recommended more than 72 hours after exposure because it is unlikely to work, and the regimen is 28 days of a three-drug antiretroviral combination. WHO's annex gives the same limits: start within 72 hours and take the drugs continuously for 28 days. Six months is the length of antibody follow-up after an exposure, not the length of treatment, and the CDC's occupational page adds that PEP must start within 72 hours.

preguntas.pregunta: A tenaculum is handed to the provider during a gynecological procedure. What does it do?
opciones: It seizes and holds the cervix or the fundus with a hooked point
It reads how deep the uterine cavity runs from the os inward
It exposes the inside of the vagina so the cervix comes into view
It is put into the uterus to lift the organ and move it about
preguntas.explicacion: The tenaculum is hook-shaped and takes hold of the cervix or the fundus so it stays put. Reading the depth of the cavity is the sound's job, exposing the vagina is what the speculum is for, and lifting the uterus from within belongs to the uterine elevator.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist arrives at room 412 to collect a CBC. Which pair of identifiers satisfies The Joint Commission's NPSG.01.01.01 for laboratory services?
opciones: The patient's stated full name plus the assigned identification number
The room number 412 plus the assigned identification number on the band
The patient's stated full name plus the physical location of the bed
The assigned identification number read from the chart, used on its own
preguntas.explicacion: NPSG.01.01.01 asks for at least two identifiers whenever blood or other specimens are collected. The goal's rationale accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another person-specific identifier, and EP 1 states outright that a room number or physical location is not used as one. A single identifier from the chart does not reach two.

preguntas.pregunta: Which group do a blood pressure cuff, a bedpan and a pair of crutches belong to, and why?
opciones: Noncritical, because they meet intact skin, which blocks most microbes on its own
Semicritical, because they can reach mucous membranes if a patient is moved carelessly
Critical, because a cuff is inflated over a limb where the vascular system runs beneath
Noncritical, because they are cleaned in a central area away from where they get used
preguntas.explicacion: Noncritical items touch intact skin and not mucous membranes, and intact skin is itself an effective barrier, so their sterility is not critical. That is why cuffs, bedpans, crutches and computers can be decontaminated right where they are used instead of travelling to central processing, unlike critical and many semicritical items.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Noncritical Items

preguntas.pregunta: Two heel-pricks on an infant have failed to give a satisfactory sample. What is the next step?
opciones: Seek a second opinion on whether to try again or cancel the tests
Make a third attempt on the other heel with a longer lancet
Switch to a finger-prick, which is allowed once the heel has failed twice
Repeat the puncture on the same site, since it is already open
preguntas.explicacion: There is a strict limit on the number of times a paediatric patient may be stuck: if no satisfactory sample has been collected after two attempts, seek a second opinion to decide whether to make a further attempt or cancel the tests. Reusing a puncture site is prohibited, and site choice follows age and weight, not the number of failures.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Unsuccessful attempts in paediatric patients

preguntas.pregunta: Which vessels are the only arteries in the post-natal body that carry relatively deoxygenated blood?
opciones: The pulmonary trunk and its branches
The four pulmonary veins to the left atrium
The coronary arteries off the ascending aorta
The venae cavae entering the right atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The pulmonary trunk and the pulmonary arteries it divides into are the only post-natal arteries carrying relatively deoxygenated blood, from the right ventricle toward the lungs, and the pulmonary veins are the only post-natal veins carrying highly oxygenated blood, into the left atrium. The coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta with oxygenated blood; the venae cavae are veins.

preguntas.pregunta: For which purpose is an arterial sample, rather than a venous one, the indicated specimen?
opciones: Gathering data on arterial blood gases
Gathering data on a complete blood count
Gathering data on coagulation factor levels
Gathering data on a fasting plasma glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Routine draws use veins because they are superficial and the puncture is more comfortable, and arterial sampling is reserved for the case where arterial blood is what the test needs, namely blood gases. preguntas.pregunta: An intake form is marked NKDA. What has the patient reported?
opciones: The patient has no known drug allergies
The patient has no known dietary allergy
The patient has no known kidney disease
The patient has no known cardiac history
preguntas.explicacion: NKDA means no known drug allergies, and it belongs on the intake form before any medication is given. It records the absence of a known allergy, not the absence of any reaction ever, so a new reaction is still possible and the entry has to be checked at every visit.

preguntas.pregunta: An advance written notice was signed, the patient paid, and Medicare later paid the claim after all. What must the provider do?
opciones: Refund the patient within 30 days of receiving the remittance advice for that claim
Refund the patient within 90 days of receiving the remittance advice for that claim
Keep the payment, since the signed notice made the patient liable for the charge
Credit the amount to the patient's account for future services at the practice
preguntas.explicacion: After a properly issued notice the provider may seek payment from the patient, but if Medicare pays all or part of the claim and the patient has also paid, the refund must be timely: within 30 days of getting the remittance advice, or within 15 days of an appeal determination when one was filed. A signed notice does not entitle the provider to keep both payments.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has a long list of instructions to give. How much should be covered in one visit?
opciones: One to three need-to-know or need-to-do points, repeated more than once
One to three need-to-know points, each mentioned exactly one time
Five to seven need-to-know points, prioritized by the assistant beforehand
Everything on the list, since leaving items out risks a safety problem
preguntas.explicacion: Content is limited so the patient is not swamped: what needs discussing is prioritized with the patient, held to one to three need-to-know or need-to-do points, and each of those is emphasized more than once. Repetition is part of the technique, not padding, because most of what is said in a visit is forgotten right away.

preguntas.pregunta: What makes the Korotkoff sounds audible in the first place?
opciones: The cuff compresses the artery, turning smooth flow into turbulent flow
The cuff stops the flow completely, and the silence is broken by the valve
The cuff stretches the vessel wall, and the elastic recoil produces the tapping
The cuff presses the vein against the artery, and the two vessels knock together
preguntas.explicacion: At rest the blood moves through the brachial artery in smooth laminar flow, which makes no sound a stethoscope can pick up. Squeezing the artery with the cuff turns that flow turbulent, and the turbulence is what is heard. When the flow smooths out again below the diastolic pressure the sound disappears.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · RMA III.E.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A child's parents are divorced with no court decree about health care expenses. Which plan does the model rule place first?
opciones: The plan covering the custodial parent, then that parent's spouse
The plan covering the non-custodial parent, then that parent's spouse
The plan of the parent with the earlier birthday within the calendar year
The plan that has covered the child for the longer period of time
preguntas.explicacion: Without a decree allocating responsibility, the order runs through four plans: the one covering the custodial parent, then the one covering that parent's spouse, then the non-custodial parent's plan, and last the plan of the non-custodial parent's spouse. The custodial parent is the one given custody by a court or, absent a decree, the one the child lives with more than half the year.
preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules and Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures and the first dose of an IV antibiotic are ordered together for a patient with suspected sepsis. What is the correct sequence?
opciones: Draw the blood cultures first, then let the antibiotic be started
Start the antibiotic and draw the cultures at any point within 24 hours
Draw one set before the antibiotic and the second set after the first dose
Draw the cultures 12 hours after the dose, when the drug is at its trough
preguntas.explicacion: Blood should be collected for culture before antimicrobial therapy whenever possible; that is step 4 of the CDC procedure and the recommendation for suspected sepsis in its overview. Without a culture taken before antibiotics, the causative organism is more likely to stay unknown and therapy is harder to de-escalate. The 24-hour period defines the septic episode for counting sets, and the 12-hour figure is a drug-level timing, not a culture rule.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, SOP model step 4; and Overview (2022), section 1

preguntas.pregunta: A clearinghouse sends an electronic eligibility request for a provider who has no active enrollment in the Medicare eligibility system. What happens to it?
opciones: It is rejected, because every identifier submitted needs an enrollment on file
It is answered, because the clearinghouse's own enrollment covers its providers
It is held back until the provider's enrollment has been approved by a contractor
It is answered, because enrollment matters only when claims are being submitted
preguntas.explicacion: Since 11 May 2026 an active eligibility enrollment has to be on file for every National Provider Identifier a vendor or clearinghouse submits, and without one the eligibility request is rejected. The vendor's identifier does not stand in for the provider's: each provider has to read and acknowledge the rules of behavior and name its relationship with the vendor, and vendors are told not to enrol providers themselves.

preguntas.pregunta: What falls under spiritual needs at the end of life?
opciones: Finding meaning, ending disagreements, making peace
Relieving pain, easing breathing, treating skin itching
Watering the plants, sorting the mail, paying the bills
Treating depression and anxiety with counseling or drugs
preguntas.explicacion: Spiritual needs can matter as much as physical ones and include finding meaning in one's life, settling disagreements with others and making peace with circumstances. Pain and breathing belong to physical comfort, everyday chores to practical tasks, and depression and anxiety to mental and emotional needs.

preguntas.pregunta: An ankle-brachial index is being taken by the manual method. How wide must the cuff be, and what picks up the pulse?
opciones: At least 40 % of the way around the limb, with a doppler or a stethoscope
At least 20 % of the way around the limb, with a doppler or a stethoscope
At least 40 % of the length of the limb, with a doppler as the detector
At least 80 % of the way around the limb, read off an oscillometer alone
preguntas.explicacion: The manual technique asks for a cuff whose width is at least two fifths of the circumference of the limb, and for a doppler or a stethoscope to detect the pulse. The oscillometer belongs to the automated technique, which takes a regular cuff for a calf under 35 cm and a large one above that.

preguntas.pregunta: A quarter of a practice's receivables are older than ninety days. Which remedies does the guidance name for exactly that problem?
opciones: Tracking at twenty-one days and getting missing documents in within forty-eight hours
Tracking at ninety days and getting missing documents in within thirty days of a denial
Tracking at sixty days and holding every claim until the whole record has been signed
Tracking at thirty days and rebilling each unpaid claim once a month from then on
preguntas.explicacion: Receivables past ninety days come from claim-submission errors, appeals that are slow or never filed, and delayed processing by the insurer; the benchmark is that fewer than fifteen per cent of accounts should be sitting there. The remedies listed are twenty-one-day tracking, identifying missing documents early and submitting them within forty-eight hours, and working denials immediately, including the incomplete material behind them.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a newborn in a hospital cot identified before drawing blood?
opciones: Use a band attached to the baby, ask the parent for the first and last names, and match the form
Use the band attached to the cot and the cot number, since a newborn cannot wear a band safely
Ask the nurse on duty to confirm the cot number and rely on that as the single identifier
Match the mother's wristband to the form, since the baby is registered under her record
preguntas.explicacion: For paediatric and neonatal patients, use a wrist or foot band only if it is attached to the patient, never the bed number or a band attached to the bed or cot; to ask a parent or legal guardian present for the child's first and last names; and to check that name, date of birth and hospital or file number on the laboratory form match the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does systolic pressure tend to rise and diastolic pressure to fall as a patient ages?
opciones: The arteries stiffen progressively, which widens the gap between the two values
The heart contracts more forcefully with age, lifting only the upper of the two
The blood becomes more viscous with age, which raises the peak and lowers the trough
The veins lose their valves with age, so less blood returns between contractions
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries grow stiffer over the years, and the consequence is a higher systolic value, a lower diastolic value and a widened pulse pressure between them. The same stiffness makes auscultatory readings less reliable in older patients, where errors of 30 to 50 mm Hg have been reported.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Variability of Vital Signs in Older Adults

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on an ACE inhibitor has a potassium of 5.6 mEq/L. Which mechanism accounts for the rise?
opciones: Less angiotensin II means less aldosterone, and potassium stops being secreted
More aldosterone is made, sodium and water return, and potassium leaves in urine
The Na-K-2Cl cotransporter is blocked, so potassium cannot return to the lumen
Bradykinin builds up in the lung, which is also what produces the class's cough
preguntas.explicacion: Hyperkalemia here is the mechanism of the drug showing itself. Blocking angiotensin II cuts the aldosterone that follows it; without aldosterone the tubule stops trading sodium reabsorption for the secretion of protons and potassium, so potassium climbs. Kidney disease or potassium-sparing drugs raise the risk further. Bradykinin accumulation explains the cough of this class, not the potassium.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ACE Inhibitors", Adverse Effects: Hyperkalemia

preguntas.pregunta: How should the account of an abusive event be entered in the medical record?
opciones: In the patient's own words, with the evaluation, treatment and referrals
As a summary in clinical terms, since quoted speech is not admissible later
Only after a report has been made, so the two accounts cannot diverge
In the patient's own words, and only if the patient agrees to a referral
preguntas.explicacion: The chart is often the evidence that convicts an abuser, and a thin one can let that person go on to assault again, so the abusive event and the current complaints go down in the patient's own words along with everything done. Reporting to law enforcement, where it is mandated, does not replace that documentation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Domestic Violence", Treatment / Management: Medical Record

preguntas.pregunta: The ward holds two patients named John Ramirez. Beyond the full name and date of birth, what does the accepted practice add before the draw?
opciones: One further general identifier, such as the social security number or address
The bed each of the two men occupies, written by hand on both laboratory forms
The middle initial only, since the ward clerk keeps the two charts well apart
The list of tests ordered, because the two requisitions ask for different work
preguntas.explicacion: Every admitted patient carries an ID bracelet, and the name and date of birth are asked and recorded. The accepted consensus adds one more general identifier, a social security number or an address, because supplementary data lowers the rate of preventable errors. Location never counts: the identification goal rules out the room number or physical place.

preguntas.pregunta: A scan is cut horizontally, dividing the body into an upper and a lower portion. Which plane was used?
opciones: The transverse plane, also called the axial plane
The frontal plane, also called the coronal plane
The sagittal plane, also called the lateral plane
The oblique plane, which meets the body at an angle
preguntas.explicacion: The transverse or axial plane is the horizontal one, and it separates upper from lower; the images it produces are called cross sections. The frontal or coronal plane runs from side to side and separates front from back, the sagittal runs from front to back and separates right from left, and an oblique plane cuts at an angle to all three.

preguntas.pregunta: A dressing change reveals thick, opaque, yellow-green drainage in the wound bed. How is that classified and handled?
opciones: Purulent drainage, which is never normal and is reported to the provider each time it appears
Serous drainage, which is normal during the inflammatory stage and is simply documented
Serosanguineous drainage, which is expected while the capillaries are still fragile and new
Sanguineous drainage, which means fresh bleeding and calls for pressure over the wound bed
preguntas.explicacion: Purulent exudate is thick and opaque and can be tan, yellow, green or brown; it is never considered normal in a wound bed, and any new purulent drainage goes to the provider. Serous drainage is clear, thin, watery plasma and is normal in small amounts during the inflammatory stage; serosanguineous adds a little blood, and sanguineous is fresh bleeding.

preguntas.pregunta: Which pathogens beyond HIV and the hepatitis viruses are named as transmissible through this procedure?
opciones: Viral haemorrhagic fevers and dengue, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Influenza and tuberculosis, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Viral haemorrhagic fevers and measles, with tetanus through the puncture wound
Dengue and influenza, with tetanus and rabies through the puncture wound itself
preguntas.explicacion: Drawing blood can expose workers and patients to bloodborne pathogens, and the list runs beyond HIV and hepatitis B and C to the viruses of Crimean Congo haemorrhagic fever, Ebola, Lassa and Marburg, and to dengue. Malaria and syphilis may also travel in contaminated blood.

preguntas.pregunta: Which number reaches poison control from anywhere in the United States?
opciones: The national toll-free Poison Help line, 1-800-222-1222
The state health department line printed on the label
The manufacturer's hotline printed on the product container
The nearest hospital switchboard, which routes the call on
preguntas.explicacion: One national toll-free line, 1-800-222-1222, reaches the local poison control center from anywhere in the country, free and confidential, 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, and it takes questions that are not emergencies as well. preguntas.pregunta: How many pairs of cranial nerves and how many pairs of spinal nerves does the body have?
opciones: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves and thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves
Thirty-one pairs of cranial nerves and twelve pairs of spinal nerves
Twelve pairs of cranial nerves and twenty-four pairs of spinal nerves
Ten pairs of cranial nerves and thirty-three pairs of spinal nerves
preguntas.explicacion: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves leave the underside of the brain and are named both with words and with Roman numerals. Thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves leave the cord, one pair per segment: eight cervical, twelve thoracic, five lumbar, five sacral and one coccygeal. All of the spinal nerves are mixed, carrying sensory and motor fibers alike.

preguntas.pregunta: Training records under the bloodborne pathogens standard must be kept for how long?
opciones: Three years from the date the training took place
One year after the last entry, like the extinguisher record
Thirty years beyond the end of the worker's employment
Six years from the date the record was last in effect
