preguntas.pregunta: Who is covered by TRICARE?
opciones: Active-duty and retired uniformed services members and their families
Veterans with a service-connected disability rated permanent and total
Civilian employees of the Department of Defense and their dependents
Members of the National Guard only while they are not on active orders
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE is the health care program for active-duty and retired uniformed services members and their families. preguntas.pregunta: Which older adults are at the highest risk of abuse?
opciones: Those with cognitive impairment such as dementia
Those living alone with no relatives in the state
Those with private insurance and several specialists
Those recently discharged after elective surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Prevalence among older adults in the United States is put at 5 to 10 percent, and the abuser is usually someone the person knows: a relative, friend, neighbor, caregiver or facility staff. Older adults with cognitive impairment such as dementia carry the highest risk, with close to five times the rate seen in older adults without it. Only about 5 percent of cases are ever reported.

preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient bites a phlebotomist's forearm and breaks the skin. Under the standard, this contact is best described as which of these?
opciones: A parenteral exposure, since piercing the skin barrier by a human bite is listed as parenteral
Not an exposure incident, because saliva is not OPIM outside dental procedures
An occupational exposure but not an exposure incident, because no needle was involved
A contact exposure that requires Contact Precautions rather than post-exposure follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines parenteral as piercing the mucous membranes or the skin barrier through events such as needlesticks, human bites, cuts and abrasions, and an exposure incident as parenteral or mucous-membrane or non-intact-skin contact with blood or OPIM arising from the employee's duties. A bite that breaks the skin is therefore a parenteral route, and if blood is involved the post-exposure evaluation of (f)(3) applies. Saliva is OPIM only in dental procedures, but the bite itself is the parenteral event; needles are one example of the route, not the only one.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between compensatory and punitive damages?
opciones: Compensatory damages cover the actual loss; punitive ones deter misconduct
Compensatory damages cover the legal fees; punitive ones cover the injury
Compensatory damages are set by statute; punitive ones are set by contract
Compensatory damages are paid by the insurer; punitive ones by the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Damages are what the court awards to make the injured party whole, and in most cases they are compensatory: calculated on the party's real losses, which in a tort case run from medical care, property damage and lost wages to pain and suffering. Where the court wants to deter future misconduct, it can add punitive damages on top.

preguntas.pregunta: A sweat chloride result comes back at 45 mmol/L. How is that read?
opciones: Intermediate: cystic fibrosis is possible and repeat or further testing is needed
Normal: cystic fibrosis is unlikely and no further testing is needed at all
Diagnostic: the value confirms cystic fibrosis without any further testing
Invalid: a value in that range means the sample evaporated during collection
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs in three bands: under 30 mmol/L makes cystic fibrosis unlikely, 30 to 59 mmol/L is intermediate and calls for a repeat test or another approach such as genotyping, and 60 mmol/L or above is diagnostic. An intermediate value may simply mean the patient carries one copy of the gene, and a normal result does not by itself rule the disease out.

preguntas.pregunta: A small practice decides its risk of identity theft is low but agrees that it does hold covered accounts. What does the Rule still require of it?
opciones: A written program, approved by its board or by an appropriate senior employee
A written program, filed with the Commission before the practice may rely on it
A written program, reviewed each year by the insurer that carries its liability cover
No written program, since the Rule reaches only businesses that face a high risk
preguntas.explicacion: The Rule is deliberately flexible: a business facing a high risk of identity theft may need a comprehensive program while one facing a low risk may need only a streamlined one, and where the risk is low the program might focus on how to respond when someone reports that an identity was misused. Even a low-risk business needs a written program approved at that level.

preguntas.pregunta: Sutures were placed on a patient's cheek and on the same patient's forearm. Which removal times apply?
opciones: About 5 to 7 days on the face, and 10 to 14 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 10 to 14 days on the face, and 5 to 7 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 2 to 3 days on the face, and 5 to 7 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 5 to 7 days on the face, and 21 to 28 days on the trunk or an extremity
preguntas.explicacion: Timing follows the site and the tension on the wound. Facial sutures usually come out at five to seven days, while the trunk and extremities are safer at ten to fourteen, depending on how active the patient is and on the quality of the tissue. Nonabsorbable sutures generally sit somewhere in the seven to fourteen day window.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood was drawn with a syringe and must be transferred into evacuated tubes. How does the WHO say the tube should be held and filled to prevent a needle-stick?
opciones: Place the tube in a rack and fill it with one hand, or use a needle shield between needle and hand
Hold the tube firmly in the free hand and pierce the stopper at an angle toward the fingers
Remove the stopper, rest the tube in the palm and inject slowly against the inner wall of the tube
Hold the tube against the patient's arm so the syringe can be steadied on the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says best practice with a syringe or winged set is to put the tube in a rack before filling, and to use one hand to fill it or a needle shield between the needle and the hand holding the tube. The stopper is pierced from directly above with slow, steady pressure and is never removed, because that releases the vacuum. Holding the tube in the hand is exactly the exposure the step is designed to avoid.

preguntas.pregunta: Who decides for a patient who has no advance directive and cannot communicate?
opciones: Whoever the law of that state puts first, often the spouse or an adult child
The first clinician to document that the patient has lost decisional capacity
The hospital's risk manager, who signs on behalf of the absent patient
Nobody: care is limited to comfort measures until a court has appointed one
preguntas.explicacion: Without a directive, the state's law where the person lives determines who may decide, typically the spouse, the parents if available, or adult children. An unmarried partner who was never named can be shut out, and some states let a close friend who knows the person's values step in, or assign a physician to represent their best interests.

Give the patient a state advance directive form already filled out
Give the patient's family a copy of any directive within 90 days
Give the admitting physician a signed directive before care starts
preguntas.explicacion: Providers that take Medicare or Medicaid must hand adult patients written information about their rights under state law to decide about their own care, including the right to accept or refuse treatment and to draw up an advance directive, plus the provider's own written policies on honoring one. preguntas.pregunta: An assistant sits down to take a new patient history. How should open-ended and closed-ended questions be sequenced?
opciones: Open questions first, then closed ones for the details
Closed questions first, then open ones for the feelings
Closed questions only, so the visit stays on schedule
Open questions only, since closed ones feel like a test
preguntas.explicacion: Begin with open-ended questions and let the account flow before moving to closed-ended questioning. Focused yes-or-no questions gather detail efficiently, but a very high number of them makes the person feel interrogated and costs rapport. preguntas.pregunta: Under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens standard, what does the term "Universal Precautions" mean?
opciones: Treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if they carried a bloodborne pathogen
Treating as infectious only the blood of patients whose chart shows HIV or hepatitis B
Reasonably anticipated contact of skin, eyes or mucous membranes with blood in the course of one's duties
Controls that isolate or remove the hazard from the workplace, such as sharps containers and safer needles
preguntas.explicacion: In the standard's definitions, Universal Precautions is one approach to controlling infection: every specimen of human blood, and certain other body fluids, is handled as though it were known to carry HIV, HBV or another bloodborne pathogen. Nothing depends on a chart, a test result or a diagnosis, so the same barriers apply to every patient. The other two definitions sit next to it in paragraph (b): reasonably anticipated contact in the course of one's duties is Occupational Exposure, and devices that isolate or remove the hazard are Engineering Controls.

preguntas.pregunta: A new technician shakes each tube vigorously right after collection to make sure the additive mixes. What does the evidence quoted in the rejection study say about this?
opciones: Tubes should be inverted gently several times; instant vigorous mixing may itself produce hemolysis

Shaking is harmless for whole blood but must be avoided once the tube has been centrifuged
Tubes must be shaken for one full minute, since gentle inversion leaves fibrin filaments in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers' data sheets and CLSI documents recommend gentle inversion of vacuum tubes several times to bring blood and additive together; a study cited found that mixing immediately after collection for a minute with 15 inversions may not even be mandatory and that instant mixing can cause hemolysis, and a later trial saw no fibrin or microclots with five gentle inversions, or even with none. preguntas.pregunta: How are goggles or a face shield handled when the equipment is being taken off?
opciones: By the strap or the earpieces, never by the front surface
By the lower rim, which stays clean during a procedure
By the front, folded inward so the outside faces itself
By the strap, and then wiped dry with the gown's sleeve

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose employer plan pays before Medicare offers to hand over her coinsurance at check-in. What should the office do?

Take it and post it, then refund her share once the primary payer has paid
Take it and leave it unapplied until the primary payer's remittance has arrived
Decline it, because coinsurance is never collected before the visit takes place

preguntas.pregunta: A woman asks how to clean herself before giving a clean-catch urine sample. What should the medical assistant tell her?
opciones: Spread the labia and use two wipes, front to back: one for the inner folds, a second over the urethral opening
Spread the labia and use two wipes, back to front: one for the inner folds, a second over the urethral opening
Clean the urethral opening with one wipe after retracting the surrounding skin, as done for the head of the penis
Rinse the area with warm water and soap, then dry, exactly as done before placing an infant collection bag
preguntas.explicacion: For a clean-catch, a woman sits with her legs apart, separates the labia with two fingers and uses the first sterile wipe on the inner folds and the second on the urethral opening, always wiping from the front toward the back. Retracting the foreskin is the instruction for uncircumcised men, and washing with soap and water is the routine before an infant bag. The labia stay separated while she voids.

Dilution of the sample with tissue fluid, as happens when a finger is squeezed

preguntas.pregunta: How does the enforcement regulation define willful neglect?

preguntas.explicacion: Three defined terms sit next to each other in the enforcement subpart. Willful neglect is a conscious, intentional failure or reckless indifference to the obligation to comply. Reasonable cause covers an act or omission the entity knew about, or would have known about with reasonable diligence, but that was not willful neglect. Reasonable diligence itself is the business care and prudence expected in similar circumstances.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic modifies a waived glucose meter's procedure so it can test patients whose hematocrit is outside the range in the insert. Under CLIA, what happens to that testing?
opciones: It becomes high complexity and needs a Certificate of Compliance or Accreditation
It stays waived as long as the modification is written into the site procedure manual
It becomes moderate complexity and can continue under the same Certificate of Waiver
It becomes a PPM procedure that only the physician or midlevel practitioner may run
preguntas.explicacion: Using a cleared test outside its intended use is off-label use. Any off-label use of a waived test is treated as high-complexity testing, which brings in proficiency testing, verified performance specifications, quality control, quality assessment and personnel qualifications. A site with only a Certificate of Waiver would have to upgrade to a Certificate of Compliance or of Accreditation first.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking large doses of vitamin C has a urine reagent strip run. Which pair of pads can read falsely negative?
opciones: The blood and glucose pads
The protein and bilirubin pads
The nitrite and ketone pads
The urobilinogen and leukocyte pads
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is listed among the causes of a false-negative blood reaction, alongside captopril, a high specific gravity, acid urine and proteinuria, and among the causes of a false-negative glucose, with high specific gravity and uric acid. Bilirubin and ketones read falsely low in stale specimens, urobilinogen after daylight exposure or with formaldehyde, and the leukocyte pad with mercury salts.

preguntas.pregunta: On an over-the-counter Drug Facts label, which heading tells the patient how much to take and how often?
opciones: The Directions section
The Warnings section
The Purpose section
The Uses section
preguntas.explicacion: The Drug Facts panel is fixed: active ingredients with their amount per dosage unit, purpose as the product's action or pharmacologic category, uses as the symptoms or diseases it treats or prevents, warnings covering when not to use it and when to call a doctor, directions with how much, how, how often and how long, inactive ingredients, and other information such as storage. Dietary supplements carry a different panel.

preguntas.pregunta: Which imaging technique combines many cross-sectional X-rays into slices, and what is its main drawback?
opciones: Computed tomography, which delivers a much higher radiation dose
Magnetic resonance imaging, which delivers a much higher radiation dose
Ultrasonography, which delivers a much higher radiation dose than X-ray
Positron emission tomography, which cannot show soft tissue detail
preguntas.explicacion: Tomography means imaging by sections. In a CT study the scanner turns all the way around the patient taking X-ray images, and a computer builds them into slices detailed enough to measure a mass in millimeters. The price is radiation: the dose is many times that of a plain X-ray, which matters most in children and in repeated scans.

preguntas.pregunta: During a surgical hand scrub, how are the hands and forearms held while rinsing, and why?
opciones: Hands above the elbows, so water runs off the least clean part
Hands below the elbows, as in the routine wash at the sink
Hands flat against the sink, so the water reaches the cuticles
Hands at the same height, so the soap is rinsed off evenly
preguntas.explicacion: In routine handwashing the hands stay below the elbows, so water travels from the less contaminated area to the more contaminated one. The surgical scrub reverses that: once scrubbed, the hands are the cleanest part and the forearms and elbows are relatively less clean, so hands are kept elevated and away from the body and the water is allowed to run from the fingertips toward the elbows. Getting the position backwards washes the forearm over the hand.

preguntas.pregunta: Which peripheral pulse is used for the routine adult vital signs, and why?
opciones: The radial, because it is easy to reach and barely disturbs the seated patient
The brachial, because it lies over the artery the cuff will occlude in a moment
The carotid, because its wide vessel gives the clearest beat to count against a watch
The femoral, because a central vessel resists the changes that cool hands produce
preguntas.explicacion: The radial artery is the site used in routine adult examinations: it is accessible at the wrist and asking for a wrist costs the patient almost nothing. Like other distal pulses it also reflects circulatory trouble early. The carotid is the resuscitation site in adults and the femoral is the sensitive one in septic shock.

preguntas.pregunta: An alcohol-based skin prep has just been applied and the surgeon reaches for the cautery. What must happen first?
opciones: Let the prep dry for the time the manufacturer specifies, and be sure none has pooled
Wipe the prep off with a dry sterile sponge, since the antisepsis is complete on contact
Cover the prepped area with a moist drape, which keeps the vapor away from the cautery
Raise the oxygen flow, which dilutes the vapor faster than room air can carry it away
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based preps are fuel. Prevention rests on following the manufacturer's dry time and stopping the fluid from pooling under drapes, along with re-holstering the cautery and keeping currents low. Raising the oxygen does the opposite of helping: a higher oxidizer level lowers the temperature at which a fuel ignites, so the lowest oxygen that maintains saturation is used.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Surgical Fire Safety", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: How should the history be taken when elder abuse is suspected?
opciones: In private, with the caregiver asked to step out of the room
With the caregiver present, so the account can be corroborated
In writing only, so the patient's answers are documented exactly
Through a family member, to avoid embarrassing the patient directly
preguntas.explicacion: The caregiver is asked to leave and the conversation is held in private, because vital information is held back when the patient fears repercussions. Questions are asked without judgment, with time to answer, and something as simple as asking whether the person feels safe at home is a good start. Red flags include unexplained or repeated injuries and delayed care.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides a Medicare Advantage plan, which of these delivers Part A and Part B benefits through a private plan?
opciones: The Program of All-inclusive Care for the Elderly
A Medigap policy sold by a private insurance company
A stand-alone Medicare drug plan approved by Medicare
A state Medicaid program covering dual eligible people
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare health plans deliver Part A and Part B benefits and are generally offered by private companies under contract with Medicare. Besides Medicare Advantage they include Medicare Cost Plans, demonstrations and pilots, and the Program of All-inclusive Care for the Elderly. Medigap helps pay the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than delivering the benefits, a drug plan covers Part D, and Medicaid is a joint federal-state program.

preguntas.pregunta: Which minerals are limited in the eating plan for an adult with chronic kidney disease?
opciones: Sodium, potassium and phosphorus
Sodium, potassium and magnesium
Calcium, iron and phosphorus
Sodium, chloride and calcium
preguntas.explicacion: Damaged kidneys cannot clear these three the way healthy ones do. Phosphorus builds up and weakens bone and blood vessels; potassium can climb high enough to cause heart and muscle trouble; and sodium makes the body hold fluid, raising pressure and swelling. How far each is limited depends on the stage and is set with a dietitian.
preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Eating Right for Chronic Kidney Disease — What aspects of nutrition are important

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reading a label asks which parts of her food count as carbohydrate. Which three forms does food carbohydrate take?
opciones: Sugars, starches, and fiber
Sugars, starches, and glycogen
Sugars, starches, and sugar alcohols
Sugars, fiber, and amino acids
preguntas.explicacion: Carbohydrate reaches the body in three forms, and all three are needed: sugars, starches and fiber. Sugars and most starches are broken down into glucose that circulates in the blood as energy. Fiber is the part that is not broken down at all. Amino acids belong to protein, not to carbohydrate.

preguntas.pregunta: Which combination of findings should be treated as anaphylaxis?
opciones: Hives with wheeze or stridor after a likely exposure, minutes to hours later
Hives alone after a likely exposure, with no other body system involved
Nausea alone after a known exposure, with a normal blood pressure reading
A rash appearing five to eight days after the exposure, with no wheeze
preguntas.explicacion: Anaphylaxis is diagnosed clinically, and involvement of two or more systems within minutes to hours of a likely exposure is enough, even without hypotension. Skin or mucosal signs, respiratory signs such as dyspnea, wheeze, stridor or persistent throat clearing, a systolic pressure under 90 or a fall over 30% from baseline, and persistent cramps or vomiting are the systems counted. Most deaths happen in the first hour.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Evaluation: Clinical Criteria for Anaphylaxis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice would invalidate a sweat chloride collection?
opciones: Wiping the iontophoresis equipment with a bleach-based disinfectant between patients
Wiping the iontophoresis equipment with a bleach-free disinfectant between two patients
Reweighing gauze immediately and storing it in a closed container at 4 degrees
Collecting two samples during the same test to allow for the method's variability
preguntas.explicacion: Everything used for iontophoresis is disinfected between patients, but the product must not contain bleach, which would contaminate the sweat that is about to be measured for chloride. Two samples are the norm, gauze is reweighed at once and may be held closed at 4 degrees Celsius for up to 72 hours, and the sweat itself is not treated as infectious unless it is visibly contaminated with blood.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sweat Testing", Procedures and Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of behaviors is given as psychological workplace violence?
opciones: Sexual harassment, bullying and intimidation of a coworker
Shouting, swearing and threatening language toward staff
Pushing, grabbing and striking a member of the staff
Theft and other criminal acts committed on the premises
preguntas.explicacion: One way of sorting workplace violence is by the nature of the aggression: physical, verbal or psychological. Harassment, bullying and intimidation are the examples given for the psychological form. Shouting and threats fall under verbal abuse, which is the most common form of all; hitting is physical; theft belongs to the criminal type I.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A slide is examined with a 10x ocular lens and the 40x objective in place. What is the total magnification?
preguntas.explicacion: Total magnification on a compound microscope is the ocular magnification multiplied by the objective magnification, so a 10x eyepiece with a 40x objective gives 400x. Oculars are typically 10x and objectives run from 4x to 100x, with the value stamped on the metal casing. The coarse knob is for the 4x and 10x objectives; from 40x upward only the fine knob is used.

preguntas.pregunta: A man raises his voice at the front desk because he has waited an hour. What is the trained response?
opciones: Listen, acknowledge the concern, then guide him to a goal
Tell him the wait is exactly the same for everyone there
Ask him to step outside and return once he has calmed
Recite the office policy on wait times before he says more
preguntas.explicacion: Risk drops when patients are approached calmly and staff make an effort to connect. The trained sequence is to listen to the person, acknowledge their concerns and respectfully guide them toward a goal, repeated as often as it takes. Openings to defuse, such as moving them into an open room sooner, are taken as they appear.

preguntas.pregunta: An interviewer needs to move to a different topic in the middle of a visit. What keeps that from feeling dismissive?
opciones: Asking permission with a transition phrase before the change
Waiting until the patient has run out of things to say first
Summarizing the encounter and ending the interview right there
Providing the rationale for every question asked from then on
preguntas.explicacion: Changing the subject abruptly can be perceived as dismissive; the suggested repair is a transition phrase that asks whether it is all right to move on to another topic. Summarizing does close an interview, and providing rationale explains why information is being gathered, but neither one solves an abrupt turn.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls

preguntas.pregunta: A purple EDTA tube for a complete blood count stops filling at roughly half its volume. What does the order-of-draw table require for this tube?
opciones: A full draw, the same requirement it places on citrate and fluoride tubes
A half draw is acceptable, because EDTA is used in a fixed concentration
A full draw only when a cross-match rather than a blood count is ordered
A full draw only when the tube will be held longer than five days before use
preguntas.explicacion: Three rows of the table carry the note that a full draw is required: the citrate tube, the EDTA tube and the fluoride/oxalate tube. It applies to the EDTA tube whichever of its listed uses is ordered, haematology or cross-match, so a half-filled tube is redrawn.

preguntas.pregunta: The requisition reads 'lipid panel: family history of premature ASCVD'. The patient ate 3 hours ago. What should happen?
opciones: Fasting is mandatory in this case; the draw should be rescheduled
Non-fasting sampling is acceptable for any lipid panel nowadays
Proceed, since fasting matters only when the triglycerides are of interest
Proceed; fasting is required only to diagnose metabolic syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: Routine fasting is no longer mandatory for every lipid profile, but there are conditions in which it is preferred or mandatory: screening and follow-up of patients with a family history of genetic hyperlipidemia or premature ASCVD (fasting mandatory), diagnosing hypertriglyceridemia, residual risk in treated patients, and pancreatitis risk. Metabolic syndrome is a non-fasting indication.

preguntas.pregunta: Which hormone drives megakaryocytes to produce platelets, and where is it made?
opciones: Thrombopoietin, from the liver and kidneys
Erythropoietin, from the kidneys
Colony-stimulating factor, from the marrow
Interleukins, from leukocytes and marrow
preguntas.explicacion: Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the liver and kidneys that triggers the development of megakaryocytes into platelets. Erythropoietin, from the kidney, prompts erythrocyte production instead. Colony-stimulating factors drive myeloblasts toward granular leukocytes or monocytes, and interleukins are cytokine signals from many cell types.

opciones: The tone of voice the sender uses
The actual words the sender speaks
The body language the sender shows
The pace at which the two people talk

preguntas.pregunta: After the tourniquet is tightened, the phlebotomist can no longer feel the patient's radial pulse. What does this indicate?
opciones: It is too tight; it should stop venous flow but leave arterial flow intact
It is correct; the pulse disappears once the veins are fully engorged
It is too loose; a properly placed tourniquet always abolishes the radial pulse
It is correct, provided it is released within two minutes of placement
preguntas.explicacion: The tightness is managed to halt venous flow while maintaining arterial blood flow, and the peripheral line chapter repeats it: tight enough to engorge the veins without obstructing arterial flow. A lost radial pulse means the artery is occluded, so the band is too tight regardless of how quickly it will be released.

preguntas.pregunta: Which abilities belong to the toddler years, from one to three?
opciones: Running and pivoting, walking up and down stairs, pedaling a tricycle
Sitting alone without support, babbling and playing peek-a-boo
Drawing a circle and a square and drawing a stick figure
Reading first written words and beginning to ride a bicycle
preguntas.explicacion: Between one and three a child feeds itself with little spilling, draws a line when shown one, runs, pivots and walks backward, says a first and last name, walks up and down stairs, starts pedaling a tricycle, names common objects and points to body parts. preguntas.pregunta: The vein a patient offers lies under a firm pale mark left by repeated punctures. Why is that site avoided?
opciones: Residual scar tissue at a previously attempted site is a contraindication
Scarred skin cannot be disinfected with alcohol and needs povidone iodine
Scarred skin is where the tourniquet must sit, so the vein cannot be seen
Scarred skin bleeds longer, so a pressure dressing would have to be used
preguntas.explicacion: A site attempted before and left with residual scar tissue is listed as a contraindication in its own right. preguntas.pregunta: Same-day slots are now available and the manager wants to know whether the change is holding. Which measure does the guide name?
opciones: Appointment availability checked daily, such as the third next available appointment
The number of visits each clinician completed daily, compared with the year before
The count of appointments booked in past months, which shows how demand has moved
The share of calls the front desk answers before the telephone rings a third time

preguntas.pregunta: What daily saturated fat limit do the Dietary Guidelines set for people age 2 and older?
opciones: Under 10 percent of the day's calories
Under 10 grams for the whole day
Under 20 percent of the day's calories
Under 30 percent of the day's calories
preguntas.explicacion: Saturated fat gets the same ceiling as added sugars: below a tenth of the calories eaten that day, starting at age 2. The limit is written as a share of calories, not as a fixed weight, so it moves with the person's calorie needs. The label's own Daily Value for saturated fat is 20 grams on a 2,000-calorie diet.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are winged-steel needles and other needles attached to tubing singled out as a disposal hazard?
opciones: The tubing makes them hard to place in a sharps container
The tubing holds enough blood to soak through the container
The tubing keeps the shield from sliding over the used needle
The tubing has to be cut with scissors before it is discarded
preguntas.explicacion: A needle on a length of flexible tubing is awkward to get into a sharps container, and that awkwardness is itself an injury hazard. The related habit of parking the needle somewhere convenient, in a drip chamber, an intravenous port or bag, or even the bedding, leaves an exposed sharp behind. Cutting a contaminated needle is not an option either: shearing or breaking one is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard.

preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine was preserved with formaldehyde, and the laboratory is asked to run a dipstick on an aliquot. Which pattern of false results does formaldehyde produce on reagent strips?
opciones: False positives for leukocyte esterase, peroxidase reaction, urobilinogen and glucose
False negatives for leukocyte esterase, with the remaining reagent pads unaffected
False positives for albumin only, with the pH of the specimen shifted toward acidity
False negatives for glucose and ketones, with the specific gravity reading raised
preguntas.explicacion: Preservatives are used only occasionally because they alter the accuracy of the results: formaldehyde can produce false-positive reactions for leukocyte esterase, the peroxidase reaction, urobilinogen and glucose when strips are used. Mercury salts give a false-negative leukocyte esterase, thymol a false-positive albumin, and hydrochloric acid, used to keep cell structures and for steroid assays, changes the pH.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalized patient is receiving heparin. Which coagulation test is used to monitor that drug, and in which tube is it collected?
opciones: The partial thromboplastin time, in a light blue sodium citrate tube
The prothrombin time with INR, in a light blue sodium citrate tube
The partial thromboplastin time, drawn in a dark green sodium heparin tube
The erythrocyte sedimentation rate, in a black-top citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Monitoring people taking heparin is a use of the PTT (also called aPTT), which measures the seconds the sample takes to clot; the PT/INR is the test tied to warfarin. Like all coagulation studies, the PTT goes in the light blue citrate tube of the WHO table, never in a heparin tube. The ESR measures how fast red cells settle and is a marker of inflammation, not of heparin.

A notice of privacy practices and of patient rights under HIPAA rules
A notice of the two patient identifiers used by the laboratory
A notice of the fee schedule for interpreter services

preguntas.pregunta: Which elements do most state statutes set as the minimum for an informed consent discussion?
opciones: Nature, benefits, risks and alternatives, plus the patient's capacity
Cost, insurance coverage, the referral needed and the appointment date
Diagnosis, prognosis, the physician's credentials and the facility's rating
Names of the staff involved, the equipment used and the disposal method
preguntas.explicacion: The statutory minimum in most American jurisdictions covers the nature of the therapy, its benefits, its risks, its reasonable alternatives, and an assessment of the patient's capacity to decide. The reasoning behind the list is that patients own their bodies and decide what risks to take, but cannot know the risks or the alternatives unless the professional tells them. Consent obtained without these pieces is what tort claims are later built on.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a 24-hour urine protein test had a CT scan with contrast dye two days ago. Why does this matter?
opciones: Contrast dye given within 3 days before the collection can affect the results, so the provider should be told
Contrast dye given within 3 hours before the collection can affect the results, so a short delay is enough
Contrast dye can affect the results only if it was given during the 24-hour collection period itself
Contrast dye lowers the specific gravity reading, so the collection should be extended to 48 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Among the factors that can distort a 24-hour urine result is radiographic contrast given within the 3 days before the test, along with dehydration, emotional stress, strenuous exercise, vaginal fluid in the urine and urinary tract infection. Three hours would be far too short a window. Contrast media falsely raise, not lower, specific gravity, and the fix is to inform the provider, not to lengthen the collection.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant leans in about two feet from a seated patient to check a dressing. Which space zone has been entered?
opciones: The personal zone, the space usually kept for friends and family
The social zone, the one used in social and business exchanges
The public zone, which generally keeps any physical contact out
The zone under eighteen inches, kept for close relationships
preguntas.explicacion: Proxemics puts the personal zone at eighteen inches to four feet, the social zone at four to ten feet, and the public zone beyond ten feet. Staff normally talk with patients in the social zone to hold professional boundaries, but assessing and doing procedures moves them into the personal zone, where the patient may feel psychological discomfort.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Personal Space

preguntas.pregunta: An electronic device reports a very low value in a patient who looks well. How is that handled?
opciones: The value is confirmed manually, since these devices can misread outside the normal band
The value is accepted, since an electronic device removes the human error of listening
The value is repeated on the same device, which is enough to settle the question
The value is charted with a note, and no further reading is taken during that visit
preguntas.explicacion: Automated devices are reliable in the normal range but tend to read hypotensive values too high and hypertensive values too low, and it is exactly the abnormal readings that matter clinically. When a machine gives a suspicious value it is checked by hand. Unexpected findings are repeated with correct technique before decisions are made.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient deep in debt keeps shopping for expensive designer clothes. Which defense mechanism fits?

Avoidance, staying away from the places that stir it
Compensation, achieving in one area to cover another
Intellectualization, over-analyzing to hold emotion off
preguntas.explicacion: Denial dismisses external reality and rests on internal explanations, and the example given is a person who keeps buying expensive clothes despite serious debt. Avoidance dismisses uncomfortable thoughts or steers clear of the people and places tied to them, which is a different move.

preguntas.pregunta: For a finger-prick in an adult, which fingers does WHO Table 7.1 recommend, and which does it say to avoid?

The thumb and index finger; avoid the middle and ring fingers, and also the little finger
The index and middle fingers; avoid the thumb, the ring finger and the little finger
Any finger except the thumb, provided the lancet is placed on the fingerprint lines
preguntas.explicacion: Table 7.1 recommends the second and third fingers, that is the middle and ring finger, with the lancet on the side of the ball of the finger perpendicular to the fingerprint lines. preguntas.pregunta: A physician leaves on a three-month sabbatical without telling patients or arranging emergency coverage. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, since care stopped with no notice and no substitute clinician
As intentional abandonment, since an absence of that length is planned months beforehand
As no abandonment, because nobody was ever told the relationship had come to an end
As an ending chosen by the patients, who were free to find another clinician meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: A clinician need not intend to end the relationship to be liable for abandonment. The example given is exactly this: failing to notify patients or arrange emergency coverage during a prolonged vacation or sabbatical. Being unresponsive to a patient's calls or e-mails, and failing to follow up after surgery or a new medication, are treated the same way.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between sequential and nonsequential double wrapping?
opciones: Sequential wraps one sheet after the other; nonsequential wraps both sheets at the same time
Sequential wraps two sheets at once; nonsequential adds the second sheet after the cycle ends
Sequential uses woven wrap outside and nonwoven inside; nonsequential reverses those layers
Sequential is used for rigid containers; nonsequential is used only for peel-open pouches
preguntas.explicacion: Both make a double barrier. The sequential wrap uses two sheets applied one after the other, so a package ends up inside a package. The nonsequential, or simultaneous, method uses two sheets wrapped together in one pass, which saves time. Either way the wrapping is done so that the package does not tent or gap.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient short of breath sits leaning forward with the elbows resting on the knees. What is this called?
opciones: The tripod position, assumed to enhance lung expansion and air exchange
The lawnchair position, with hips and knees flexed above the level of the heart
The frog-leg position, with hips and knees flexed and rotated outward
The high Fowler position, sitting fully upright at a 90-degree angle
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who cannot get enough air often adopt this posture without being told, leaning forward on their elbows or on a table. It opens the chest and improves air exchange, and it is a visible sign of pulmonary distress during the inspection stage of a chest examination. Lawnchair and frog-leg are variations of supine, used for comfort and for perineal access.

preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches syncope?
opciones: A brief loss of consciousness and postural tone with spontaneous recovery
A loss of consciousness with jerking of the limbs and a slow recovery
A period of confusion and slurred speech with the eyes open throughout
A drop in blood pressure on standing that leaves the patient dizzy only
preguntas.explicacion: Syncope is a transient loss of consciousness and of postural tone from a fall in blood flow to the brain, followed by recovery on its own. It may come without warning or after dizziness, lightheadedness, sweating, nausea and visual disturbance. It accounts for 1 % to 3.5 % of emergency department visits.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory clearing out its storeroom asks whether the analyser printouts filed with old patient results can be thrown away. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Records of patient testing, printouts included, have to be kept
Printouts may go once the result is reported and verified
Printouts are kept only for tests sent to an outside laboratory
Printouts are kept only when the specimen failed acceptability
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond the four items the record system must contain, the same standard adds a plain sentence: records of patient testing, including instrument printouts where they exist, must be retained. There is no carve-out for tests that were already reported, for referred work, or for problem specimens; the retention rule covers the patient testing record as a whole.

preguntas.pregunta: How long must a covered entity retain its HIPAA policies, procedures and other required documentation?
opciones: Six years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later
Three years from creation, matching OSHA training records
Thirty years, matching OSHA employee medical records
Ten years from creation, matching the period for Medicare claims documentation
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(j) requires policies and procedures to be kept in written or electronic form, together with every communication the rule requires in writing and every action, activity or designation it requires to be documented, for six years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later. The same section requires a privacy official, a complaints contact, workforce training, safeguards, a complaint process, sanctions, mitigation and no retaliation. Three and thirty years are OSHA periods, not HIPAA ones.

preguntas.pregunta: A strip comes out with tall, narrow, symmetrical T waves through most of the leads. Which disturbance is that linked with?
opciones: Hyperkalemia, though the height does not track the potassium level
Hypokalemia, though the height does not track the potassium level
Hypothermia, though the height does not track the temperature
Hypercalcemia, though the height does not track the calcium level
preguntas.explicacion: Peaked T waves go with a high potassium, and they run narrower than the broad hyperacute waves of early infarction. How high they stand does not necessarily match how high the potassium is; as it climbs, the P wave flattens, the QRS widens and the PR lengthens.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides the bloodborne pathogens, which vaccination history is reviewed after a puncture wound from a needle?
opciones: Tetanus, since the date of the last dose guides what is given
Influenza, since the season decides whether a dose is due
Measles, since a worker without immunity may be excluded
Hepatitis A, since the wound was contaminated with blood
preguntas.explicacion: A needlestick is a puncture wound, so tetanus risk is assessed along with the bloodborne pathogens, and prophylaxis is decided from the type of wound, the date of the most recent tetanus-containing vaccine and whether the primary series was completed. The hepatitis B vaccination status is reviewed for the same visit, because it decides whether immune globulin is needed. There is no vaccine for hepatitis C, and measles immunity is a work-restriction question, not a wound question.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of bones belongs to the appendicular skeleton?
opciones: Clavicle, scapula, humerus, radius and ulna
Sternum, ribs, vertebrae and the hyoid bone
Parietal, temporal, frontal and occipital bones
Malleus, incus, stapes and the nasal conchae
preguntas.explicacion: The appendicular skeleton is the limbs and the girdles that hang them on the trunk: clavicle and scapula above, the coxal bones below, and the arm, forearm, thigh, leg, hand and foot bones. The thoracic cage, the vertebral column, the skull and the auditory ossicles all belong to the axial skeleton.

preguntas.pregunta: Which 1986 measure made the right to refuse treatment enforceable for patients in facilities using federal insurance programs?

The AHA's 1973 patient bill of rights
Cruzan v. Director, decided by the Supreme Court
The Norwood-Dingell Bill passed by Congress

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the FDA checks a dietary supplement before it reaches the shelf. What is the correct answer?
opciones: No; unlike medicines, supplements need no FDA approval before being sold
Yes; supplements clear the same FDA approval process that medicines clear
No; but each batch must be tested by the FDA before it may be shipped
Yes; but only for supplements that carry a claim about a body function
preguntas.explicacion: Medicines have to be approved by the FDA before they can be sold; supplements do not. preguntas.pregunta: The patient says, 'Last time they stuck me four times and I nearly passed out.' The phlebotomist replies, 'Four sticks, and you nearly passed out.' Which technique is this?
opciones: Reflecting
Summarizing
Clarifying
Validating
preguntas.explicacion: Reflecting is repeating back what the patient said, sometimes word for word, to show active listening. Summarizing restates the patient's account in the provider's own words to build shared understanding; clarifying uses guiding statements to draw out more detail; providing rationale explains upfront why information or a recommendation is needed.

preguntas.pregunta: Which urine collection method is used most often for culture, even though it is not the one least likely to be contaminated?
opciones: Clean-catch midstream, because it is neither invasive nor uncomfortable for the patient
Straight catheterization, because it is quick and needs no cooperation at all from the patient
Suprapubic aspiration, because it is quick and needs no cooperation from the patient
Sterile bag collection, because it is simple and needs no cooperation from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Suprapubic puncture gives the cleanest specimen and single catheterization is the next best, but both are invasive, uncomfortable and labor-intensive, so they are kept for patients who cannot collect their own. The clean-catch midstream is therefore the routine method, and its colony counts agree reasonably well with those two. Bag collection is a pediatric option for children who are not toilet trained.

preguntas.pregunta: Which coverage counts as minimum essential coverage?
opciones: A job-based plan, a Marketplace plan, Medicare, Medicaid or CHIP coverage
A job-based plan or a Marketplace plan, but not a public program coverage
A grandfathered policy bought before March 23, 2010, and no other coverage
Any policy that pays cash benefits toward hospital stays and lost earnings
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is any plan that satisfies the health care law's coverage requirement, and the examples given are Marketplace plans, job-based plans, Medicare, and Medicaid with CHIP; TRICARE and certain other coverage also qualify. Grandfathered policies are individual plans bought on or before March 23, 2010, a separate category, and a cash indemnity policy is not health coverage in this sense.

Buying a second electronic health record from a different vendor as a permanent standby
Printing the whole record of every active patient at the close of each business day
Notifying the Secretary of any system failure that lasts longer than a single work shift

opciones: The worker's name, the facility, and that they are trained to take blood
The worker's name, the tests ordered, and the colours of the tubes needed
The worker's name, the ordering doctor, and when the results are expected
The worker's name, the patient's diagnosis, and the reason for the tests

preguntas.pregunta: At trial, the prosecution cannot show who held a specimen during one stretch of time. What is the likely outcome?
opciones: The chain is deemed broken and the defense may ask to have it annulled
The chain is repaired by having the laboratory re-analyze the specimen
The chain holds, because the tamper-evident seal was never broken
The chain holds, because the analyst can testify to the result obtained
preguntas.explicacion: When inconsistencies persist and the prosecution cannot prove who had the item at a given time, the chain is deemed broken and the defense may ask the court to annul the resulting evidence; evidence without a maintained record can be ruled inadmissible and its legitimacy and integrity questioned. Only until the claim is paid, since the answers live on the claim itself
7 years, but only when the answers show another payer is primary

About 14 days after it receives the appeal, and the result reaches the patient
About 180 days after it receives the appeal, the same time the patient had to file
There is no set time, since the contractor decides appeals in the order received

25 to 27 gauge, three eighths to five eighths of an inch, and 0.1 mL
18 to 25 gauge, half to an inch and a half, and 2 to 5 mL for an adult

opciones: Placing point-of-care blood gas analyzers in the ICUs under laboratory control, and teaching use of the evacuated tube system
Adding heparin to every syringe on arrival in the laboratory, and asking the ICUs to send samples only during the day shift
Accepting clotted gas samples with a cautionary comment, and moving all blood gas testing to the core laboratory
Requiring each ICU to centrifuge gas samples before sending them, and doubling the frequency of the courier rounds

Asking the insurer to move her to another clinician in the network before she is told
Asking the insurer to extend her benefits thirty days so that care is not interrupted
No step at all, since a contract with a plan has no bearing on ending a clinical relationship

The tube already drawn, which has to be discarded and repeated

preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient draped for a pelvic examination?
opciones: Undressed from the waist down and kept under a sheet until she is properly positioned
Positioned first and then draped, so that the foot supports can be adjusted without a sheet
Draped from the shoulders down, with the absorbent pad laid over the abdominal wall instead
Left uncovered from the start, because the external inspection comes before the speculum
preguntas.explicacion: She undresses from the waist down and stays covered by a drape, uncovered only while the examination is actually running and for as short a time as possible. An absorbent pad goes under the buttocks, not over the abdomen. A chaperone, usually the assistant, stays in the room, and consent is obtained before anything begins.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a molecular assay will sit for several hours before extraction. Why is it either processed at once or refrigerated?
opciones: Its low pH and urea denature the nucleic acid at ambient temperature
Its bacteria multiply at ambient temperature and consume the target
Its bilirubin breaks down in the light and quenches the fluorescent dye
Its specific gravity climbs as it evaporates, concentrating inhibitors
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is processed immediately or held at 2 to 8 °C for two reasons. First, the generally low pH of urine and its urea content denature DNA at 25 °C and above. Second, prolonged storage in the cold encourages uric acid, calcium oxalate and phosphorus to precipitate, and those precipitates can themselves inhibit the amplification, so neither extreme is harmless.

preguntas.pregunta: How small a risk must still be disclosed to a patient, according to the federal decision that shaped informed consent?
opciones: A risk of one percent, if it means death or a lasting harm
A risk of ten percent, no matter what harm it would cause
A risk of one percent, but only for elective procedures
A risk of five percent, unless the patient asks for more
preguntas.explicacion: A federal court held that a patient must be told about a risk as low as one percent when the harm in question is death or a life-altering complication such as paralysis. The severity of the outcome, not the size of the probability alone, decides. Because the three branches of government have left the minimum standard vague, these rights are usually enforced after the fact, through tort claims brought by patients.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Informed Consent Prior to Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A group A strep antigen kit's insert describes testing both a throat swab and a colony from a culture plate. Under a Certificate of Waiver, which specimen may the site test?
opciones: Only the throat swab; testing the culture is not a waived use
Either one, because the kit itself is categorized as waived
Only the culture, because the swab requires an extraction step
Neither, because any test with two specimen types is nonwaived
preguntas.explicacion: Waived tests are approved only for direct, unprocessed specimens that need no operator manipulation: whole blood, urine, a throat or nasal swab, stool, saliva. When one insert covers both a processed and an unprocessed specimen, the waiver applies only to the unprocessed one. Group A strep antigen testing is waived on a throat swab and not on a microbiology culture; urine hCG is waived, serum hCG is not.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the maximum overall blood culture contamination rate recommended by the ASM and CLSI, as cited by the CDC?
preguntas.explicacion: The American Society for Microbiology and the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute recommend that the overall contamination rate should not exceed 3%. Many facilities have pushed it below 1%, and the CDC treats 1% as an achievable target when best practices are followed, but 1% is a goal, not the ceiling. Rates as high as 12% have been reported in the literature, which is what the benchmark is meant to correct.

preguntas.pregunta: A commercial plan denies a claim and the patient disagrees with the decision. What right does she have?
opciones: To appeal and have the decision reviewed, including review by a third party
To appeal only if the plan was bought inside the Health Insurance Marketplace
To appeal only after the provider has resubmitted the claim a second time
To have the service repeated at no cost while the plan reviews the decision
preguntas.explicacion: An appeal is a request that the insurer or the Marketplace review a decision denying a benefit or a payment. When a plan refuses to pay a claim or ends coverage, the patient has the right to appeal and to have the decision reviewed by a third party. The right is not limited to Marketplace plans, does not wait on a resubmission, and does not entitle anyone to free repeat care.

preguntas.pregunta: Records are about to be sent to a specialist across an open network. Which technical standard governs that leg of the journey?
opciones: Transmission security, with integrity controls and encryption as its specifications
Integrity, with a mechanism that shows stored information has not been altered
Access control, with unique identifiers and an automatic close of idle sessions
Audit controls, with the mechanisms that record and examine activity in the system
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission security is the standard for information travelling over an electronic communications network. Its two addressable specifications are integrity controls, so that what was sent cannot be modified undetected, and encryption where the practice judges it appropriate. The integrity standard next to it looks at information at rest.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vitamins are the fat-soluble ones, and where does the body keep them?
opciones: A, D, E and K, stored in the liver, fatty tissue and muscle
A, C, D and K, stored in the liver, fatty tissue and muscle
A, D, E and K, stored in the kidneys and cleared daily in urine
B12, D, E and K, stored in the liver, fatty tissue and muscle
preguntas.explicacion: Four vitamins dissolve in fat: A, D, E and K. They are held in the liver, in fatty tissue and in muscle, and the body takes them up more easily when dietary fat is present at the same time. Vitamin C is water-soluble, and B12, although water-soluble, is the one that can sit in the liver for years.

preguntas.pregunta: A primary care office faxes a chart to the specialist it is sending the patient to. What permits that disclosure?
opciones: It is a treatment disclosure, and treatment activities need no authorization from the patient
It is a health care operations disclosure, allowed once both offices sign a shared privacy notice
It is a public interest disclosure, allowed because referrals serve the coordination of care
It is an incidental disclosure, allowed because the fax is a by-product of scheduling the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Treatment is defined as the provision, coordination or management of health care, consultation between providers, and the referral of a patient from one provider to another. A covered entity may disclose PHI for the treatment activities of any provider, and the example given is a primary care provider sending a record to a specialist who needs it. No authorization is required.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis is breathing deeply, rapidly and with visible effort. Which pattern is this?
opciones: Kussmaul respiration, the compensation the body mounts for metabolic acidosis
Cheyne-Stokes respiration, the cycling pattern seen in advanced heart failure
Biot respiration, the clusters of deep breaths broken by periods of apnea
Apneustic breathing, the long gasping inspirations of upper pontine injury
preguntas.explicacion: Deep, rapid, labored breathing in an acidotic patient is Kussmaul respiration: blowing off carbon dioxide is how the body pushes the pH back up. Ketoacidosis, uremia and the ingestion of toxic alcohols or salicylates are the usual causes, and recognizing the pattern early matters for survival.

preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through the morning the team stops to re-establish awareness and check the plan still fits. Which team event is that?
opciones: A huddle, an ad hoc meeting to keep care on track
A brief, held before the start to share the plan
A debrief, held afterward to review performance
A call-out, used to broadcast critical information
preguntas.explicacion: A huddle is the ad hoc meeting held to keep care progressing toward the goal, re-establish or affirm situational awareness, reinforce the plan or judge whether it needs adjusting. A brief comes before the start to share the plan and assign roles; a debrief comes after, to trade lessons learned.

preguntas.pregunta: A weightlifter is told the body mass index falls in the overweight band. What limitation does this show?
opciones: The index cannot separate fat from muscle and bone, all of which add weight
The index is calculated only for people who do not train, so it will not apply
The index needs a waist measurement added before any category can be assigned
The index reads low in muscular people, so the true category is higher still
preguntas.explicacion: The index compares weight with height and cannot tell what the weight is made of, so someone carrying a lot of muscle can land in the overweight or obesity band. It also says nothing about where fat sits on the body. It is read together with the history, the physical findings and the laboratory results.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the second glove removed once the first one is already off?
opciones: Fingers of the bare hand slide under it at the wrist
The bare hand pinches its outer surface at the fingertips
The bare hand pulls it off by the cuff and turns it over
Both gloves are peeled together before the first is dropped
preguntas.explicacion: The first glove is taken off by grasping the palm surface with the other gloved hand and dropping it into the right container. For the second, the fingers of the now bare hand go underneath it at the wrist, so that bare skin never touches the contaminated outside, and it is peeled off over the first. Gloves come off before everything else, and hand hygiene follows immediately, since a glove is not a substitute for washing.

preguntas.pregunta: What counts as genetic information under that law?
opciones: Genetic tests of the person and of relatives, plus family medical history
Genetic tests of the person only, once a result has been reported
Any laboratory result that a physician has flagged as hereditary
Any diagnosis that the person's own parents or siblings are currently carrying
preguntas.explicacion: The definition takes in the person's own genetic tests, the genetic tests of family members, and the manifestation of a disease or disorder in family members — family medical history — because that history is used to judge future risk. preguntas.pregunta: What does the improvement guide say happens to missed appointments once a practice can see patients on the day they call?
opciones: They are likely to fall, so clinical time is used better and less staff time goes on them
They are likely to rise, since a patient who called that morning has less time to plan
They stay where they are, since missed visits follow the reminder system, not the wait
They fall for urgent visits only, since routine ones are still booked several weeks ahead
preguntas.explicacion: Among the benefits listed, practices often see savings in cost and efficiency: because patients no longer face long waits, the number of no-shows is likely to drop, clinical time is used more efficiently, and less staff time goes into managing no-shows and the backlog. The model also treats routine and urgent requests alike, so nothing is left waiting weeks.

preguntas.pregunta: A father says his teething 9-month-old has a temperature of 39 °C (102.2 °F). Why does the provider look for another cause?
opciones: Teething does not push the temperature above 37.8 °C (100 °F), so something else is at work
Teething never changes body temperature at all, so any reading above the normal band is an error
Teething raises the value only in the evening, and the reading was taken at midday
Teething raises the value only after the first tooth erupts through the gum surface
preguntas.explicacion: Teething can nudge a baby's temperature up, but not past 37.8 °C (100 °F). A reading of 39 °C is far above that ceiling, so it is treated as fever from another cause and reported: a child aged 3 to 12 months with 39 °C (102.2 °F) or more is one of the situations where the provider is contacted right away.

preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section repeats the signal word, the hazard statements and the pictograms that appear on the label?
opciones: Section 2, Hazard Identification, with the hazard classification as well
Section 3, Composition, with the ingredients and their concentrations
Section 8, Exposure Controls, with the limits and the protective gear
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with the routes and the symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Section 2 carries the hazard classification of the chemical, the signal word, the hazard statements, the pictograms, which may be drawn or simply named, the precautionary statements, a description of any hazards not otherwise classified, and, for a mixture with ingredients of unknown toxicity, what percentage of it those ingredients make up. It is the section that matches what the reader already saw on the container label.

preguntas.pregunta: When printing instructions and history forms for older patients, what minimum type size is recommended?
opciones: At least 14-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
At least 10-point type, in a typeface that is simple and easy to read
At least 18-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
At least 12-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
preguntas.explicacion: Printed material for older patients should be set at 14 points or larger in a plain typeface, with enough space between items for full answers. Where low vision makes reading hard anyway, the alternatives are spoken instructions, large pictures or diagrams, and pill boxes with raised markings. Adequate lighting with little glare belongs to the same list.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice with three separate office locations runs waived tests at all of them. How many CLIA certificates does it need?
opciones: One for each location, since none of the exceptions applies
One, filed from the main office, covering all fixed sites of the practice
One, provided the total menu stays under 15 waived tests
None, because waived testing at fixed sites is covered by the physician's license
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate is required for each location where testing is performed. The exceptions are narrow: mobile units, health fairs and other temporary sites covered under a designated home base; not-for-profit or government laboratories doing limited public health testing of no more than 15 waived or moderate tests; and hospital laboratories in contiguous buildings on one campus under common direction.

preguntas.pregunta: Which hospice level of care is used during a brief crisis so that the patient can stay at home?
opciones: Continuous home care, which takes 8 hours of skilled care a day, half by a nurse
General inpatient care, used when symptoms cannot be managed in the patient's home
Routine home care, the level given wherever the patient happens to live
Respite care, allowed for no more than five days in a row each occurrence
preguntas.explicacion: Continuous home care is more intense than routine home care and is given during brief periods of crisis, to manage acute symptoms and hold the patient in the home setting. It calls for direct skilled care 8 hours a day, at least half of it delivered by the nurse; intractable pain managed with intravenous medicine is the example given. A nursing home cannot furnish this level.

preguntas.pregunta: Which action is wrong while cooling a patient with heat illness?
opciones: Giving acetaminophen or aspirin to bring the temperature down
Putting cold compresses on the neck, the groin and the armpits
Applying cool wet cloths to the skin and using a fan on the patient
Giving half a cup of a sports drink every 15 minutes while alert
preguntas.explicacion: Fever medicines do not help here and may be harmful. The patient lies down in a cool place with the feet raised about 12 inches (30 cm), cool wet cloths and a fan lower the temperature, and cold compresses go on neck, groin and armpits. Salt tablets, alcohol rubs and drinks with alcohol or caffeine are also out, and nothing by mouth if vomiting.

preguntas.pregunta: On what basis is a substance placed in one of the five schedules of the Controlled Substances Act?
opciones: Accepted medical use, relative abuse potential, and the likelihood of dependence
Accepted medical use, the price of the product, and the route it is given by
The class it belongs to, the strength dispensed, and whether a generic exists
The refills allowed, the storage it needs, and the order form the DEA requires
preguntas.explicacion: Substances controlled under the Act fall into five schedules, and where each one lands depends on three things: whether it has a currently accepted medical use in treatment in the United States, its relative potential for abuse, and how likely it is to cause dependence when abused. The complete list is published every year in 21 CFR 1308.11 through 1308.15. Refill limits and storage follow from the schedule; they do not set it.

preguntas.pregunta: Which electrodes produce lead I?

Lead I comes from the right arm and left leg electrodes
Lead I comes from the left arm and left leg electrodes
Lead I comes from the right and left leg electrodes
preguntas.explicacion: The three standard bipolar leads each pair two limb electrodes: lead I joins the two arms, lead II the right arm and the left leg, and lead III the left arm and the left leg. preguntas.pregunta: How is the machine calibrated in daily use?
opciones: It runs a short self test each time the power is switched on
It is calibrated by the technician before every patient
It runs a self test only when an error code has appeared
It is calibrated once a week against a known signal
preguntas.explicacion: The unit checks itself briefly whenever it is powered up, so no extra calibration step falls to the technician. Deeper checks are periodic and belong to the biomedical engineer, who uses a calibrator that feeds the machine a simulated heartbeat.

preguntas.pregunta: A lactic acid level is ordered. Which tube is used for this test?

The light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the tape go when a child's head circumference is measured?

Around the narrowest part, at the level of the eyebrows and the temples
Around the largest part, below the eyebrows and across the bridge of the nose
From the bridge of the nose over the crown to the base of the skull behind
preguntas.explicacion: The tape circles the head at its widest point, passing above the eyebrows and ears and around the back. preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC say about writing the label on a viral transport tube?
opciones: Use a barcode or a permanent marker, because pencil and pen rub off or smear
Use a pencil, because permanent marker dissolves in the transport medium
Use a pen and cover the writing with clear tape so the ink cannot smear
Label the outer shipping bag instead, so that the tube itself stays easy to read

preguntas.pregunta: How should forensic specimens be packed for transport?
opciones: Sealed in tamper-evident bags or with tamper-evident tape, one form each
Sealed in tamper-evident bags, grouped under one form for the whole case
Double-bagged in biohazard bags, with the form taped to the outer bag
Boxed with absorbent material, with the form kept at the collection site

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the generic name considered the safer one to write on a medication order?
opciones: It lets the pharmacist substitute among brands, and full names are written out
It is shorter than the brand name, so less of it can be misread on the order
It is the only name the pharmacy software will accept when an order is entered

preguntas.pregunta: A caller wants to buy a Marketplace plan in March, outside the yearly enrollment window. When can she enroll?

When she agrees to a higher premium for the months already gone by this year
When her employer confirms in writing that it offers her no coverage at all
When the yearly window reopens on November 1 and closes on December 15

preguntas.pregunta: Which steps are advised when a patient's eyesight makes the pre-draw paperwork hard to read?
opciones: Good lighting with little glare, and a check that glasses were brought
A darkened room, with a torch held close to the page being read
Handwritten notes in a small neat script on unlined white paper
A relative reading the paperwork aloud in place of the patient
preguntas.explicacion: For visual deficits the advice is to ensure adequate lighting, including light on your own face, and to keep glare down; to check the patient has brought and is wearing glasses or contact lenses; and to make handwritten instructions clear and printed type large enough. Where low vision blocks reading, audio instructions or large pictures and diagrams are offered.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse auscultating a patient hears the 'lub' and then the 'dub'. What produces the second heart sound, S2?
opciones: Closing of the semilunar valves during ventricular diastole
Closing of the atrioventricular valves during ventricular systole
Opening of the semilunar valves during the ventricular ejection phase
Contraction of the atria pushing blood into a stiff, hypertrophic ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: A healthy heart has two audible sounds: S1, the lub, comes from the atrioventricular valves closing as the ventricles contract, and S2, the dub, from the semilunar valves closing as the ventricles relax. Heart sounds are vibrations caused by valve closure, and abnormal sounds are called murmurs. An atrial push into a stiff ventricle is S4, rarely heard and a sign of left ventricular failure.

preguntas.pregunta: When is routine gestational diabetes screening performed in an uncomplicated pregnancy?
opciones: Between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation
Between 12 and 16 weeks of gestation
Between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation
At the first prenatal visit, in every patient
preguntas.explicacion: Screening is done between 24 and 28 weeks; ACOG and the USPSTF recommend that window for all pregnant patients, although the method and the cutoffs vary between experts. Testing is moved earlier when urine glucose runs high at prenatal visits or when the patient is at high risk: a 75 g or 50 g test at the first visit is suggested for a BMI of 30 or more plus another risk factor. That is targeted, not routine.

preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section states whether a chemical is stable in storage and which conditions could set off a hazardous reaction?

Section 3, which also names the ingredients and their percentages
Section 5, which also names the extinguishing agents to be used
Section 12, which also names the effects on fish and other species

preguntas.pregunta: Why are skin hooks preferred over toothed forceps for handling wound edges in a cosmetically sensitive area?
opciones: They hold the edge with less crush injury to the tissue that has to heal
They grip a wider span of skin, which spreads the tension along the incision
They are supplied sterile as single-use items, so they never carry contamination
They can be held in the nondominant hand while the scalpel stays in the dominant one
preguntas.explicacion: Atraumatic handling is one of the principles of a good closure, along with distributing tension to the deeper layers and everting the margins. Skin hooks are recommended over toothed forceps for that reason: they hold the edge without crushing it, which matters most where the appearance of the final scar counts.

An encryption project covering every workstation, laptop and portable drive it owns
A signed acknowledgment from each patient that electronic records carry some risk
A written designation of the practice as a hybrid entity with health care components
preguntas.explicacion: The administrative safeguards open with the security management process, which requires an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the ePHI the entity holds. preguntas.pregunta: Which findings together point to a localized wound infection?
opciones: Erythema, induration, pain, edema, purulent exudate and odor at the wound
Erythema, pink moist granulation, mild pain and clear serous drainage at the wound
Blanching redness, cool skin, numbness and dry crusting at the edge of the wound
Scant serous drainage, itching, flat pale scar tissue and tightness across the wound
preguntas.explicacion: Localized infection shows as redness, an area of hardened tissue, pain, swelling, yellow or green purulent exudate and odor, and new signs go to the provider with a wound culture expected. preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous line is documented as sitting proximal to the wrist. Where on the arm is it?
opciones: Nearer the trunk than the wrist, up toward the elbow
Farther from the trunk than the wrist, out toward the fingers
On the palm side of the wrist rather than the back of it
On the thumb side of the wrist rather than the other side
preguntas.explicacion: Proximal describes a position in a limb nearer to the point of attachment or to the trunk, and distal one farther from it: the upper arm is proximal to the forearm, and the part of the leg below the knee is distal to the thigh. Front and back are anterior and posterior, and the two side terms are medial and lateral.

preguntas.pregunta: A nosebleed is charted as rhinorrhagia and a runny nose as rhinorrhea. Which contrast between the two endings is correct?
opciones: -rrhage is bleeding, while -rrhea is a flow or discharge
-rrhage is a suture, while -rrhea is a surgical binding
-rrhage is a bursting, while -rrhea is a narrowing or block
-rrhage is a swelling, while -rrhea is a falling or dropping
preguntas.explicacion: Both endings start the same way and are easy to swap. The pair -rrhage and -rrhagic means bleeding, while -rrhea means a flow or discharge of any kind. A third one, -rrhaphy, is a suture. Narrowing is steno-, and drooping is -ptosis, as in the eyelid that will not stay open.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a wound of the abdomen, groin, neck or chest need emergency care even when it looks small?
opciones: Severe internal bleeding may follow, leading to shock and to death
Those areas hold the pressure points that control the limb arteries
Skin there heals more slowly and the scar contracts over the muscle
Tetanus spores survive longer in the tissues found in those regions
preguntas.explicacion: Wounds of the abdomen, pelvis, groin, neck and chest can look minor and still involve severe internal bleeding, which becomes life threatening fast and can end in shock and death. Bleeding into these non-compressible areas cannot be controlled with a tourniquet, so medical care is sought right away.

opciones: The Two-Challenge Rule and CUS
The brief and the debrief session
The call-out and the check-back
STEP and the I'M SAFE checklist
