preguntas.pregunta: A practice reports that 88% of its claims pass all edits without manual work. How does that compare with the benchmark?
opciones: It is below the benchmark of 95% or more, so the causes of the edits need review
It is above the benchmark of 80%, so the current billing workflow needs no change
It matches the benchmark for days in accounts receivable, which is 30 days or less
It matches the benchmark for denial rate, which normally runs between 5% and 10%
preguntas.explicacion: The clean claim rate is the share of claims needing no edits before submission, and the benchmark cited is 95% or higher; lower figures should trigger a look at why claims are being denied or rejected. The 30-day figure is the target for days in receivables outstanding, and the 5% to 10% range describes typical denial rates, so neither describes a percentage of clean claims.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's annual bloodborne pathogens training is a video played at the workstation, with nobody available afterwards. What is missing?

A written test at the end, which the standard says is kept for three years
A copy of the hepatitis B declination form for each attendee to sign
A separate session for each job title named in the exposure determination
preguntas.explicacion: The training program has a minimum content list in paragraph (g)(2)(vii), and its last item is an opportunity for interactive questions and answers with the person giving the session; (g)(2)(viii) adds that this person has to know the subject as it applies to that workplace. A video with nobody to answer fails both. The standard never asks for a written test, the declination form belongs to the vaccine under (f)(2)(iv), and one session may cover several job classifications.

preguntas.pregunta: Charts routinely take two days to reach the clinicians who ask for them. Which requirement of the medical record condition of participation is at stake?

Keeping every record in its original or legally reproduced form for five years
Using an author identification system that protects the security of the entries
Releasing information from a record only to individuals authorized to have it
preguntas.explicacion: The condition opens with organization and staffing: the medical record service must be sized to the scope and complexity of the work, and the hospital must employ adequate personnel so that records are completed, filed and retrieved promptly. preguntas.pregunta: Two phlebotomists discuss a named patient's HIV result in a crowded elevator. Under HIPAA this conversation is which of these?
opciones: A violation: oral disclosure of identifiable health information is PHI
Permitted, since both are workforce members of the same covered entity
Permitted, since spoken information is not covered, only written or electronic
A violation only if a patient's relative happens to be in the elevator
preguntas.explicacion: PHI covers written, paper, spoken and electronic information, and the elevator conversation about an identifiable patient is the very example used to illustrate an oral violation; discussions of patient information do not belong in public places, hallways, cafeterias or shared phone lines. Being workforce members does not help, because the disclosure reaches people not involved in the patient's care and exceeds the minimum necessary. State law may add stricter rules for HIV results, and the violation does not depend on who happens to overhear.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the Affordable Care Act did about pre-existing conditions.
opciones: Insurers may not refuse to cover the condition or charge the patient more for it
Insurers may cover the condition after a waiting period set by each state law
Insurers may charge more for the condition only inside the Marketplace plans
Insurers must cover the condition when the patient buys a supplemental policy
preguntas.explicacion: A pre-existing condition is a health problem, such as asthma, diabetes or cancer, that the person had before the new coverage started. Under the health care law, insurance companies can neither refuse to cover treatment for it nor charge extra because of it. There is no waiting period left to serve, the protection is not limited to Marketplace plans, and it does not depend on buying anything additional.

preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan pays for only thirty tablets a month and the prescriber wants a larger dose. What is that rule, and what is the way round it?
opciones: A quantity limit, and the prescriber may ask the plan for an exception on medical grounds
Step therapy, and the patient must first try the cheaper drug that sits on the plan's list
Prior authorization, and the plan has to approve the drug before it will be covered at all
A transition fill, and the plan covers one thirty-day supply while the matter is settled
preguntas.explicacion: Plans may cap how much of a drug they cover over a period, for safety and for cost, and the example given is thirty tablets a month. The patient or the prescriber may contact the plan for an exception where the prescriber believes the limit is not medically appropriate for her condition, for instance because she needs a higher dose.

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice makes a medical office a creditor for purposes of the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Regularly reporting delinquent patient balances to a credit reporting company
Regularly deferring payment for services or billing patients afterwards
Regularly accepting payment cards at the front desk for the balance due
Regularly submitting claims to a health plan on the patient's behalf
preguntas.explicacion: The test has two steps, and only the second one decides. Billing patients afterwards answers the first step yes, but the guidance answers the professional who bills at the end of the month plainly: deferring payment on its own is not enough. The second step asks whether the office regularly uses consumer reports in a credit transaction, gives information to credit reporting companies, or advances funds to be repaid; reporting delinquent balances is that second kind, so it is what makes the office a creditor. Taking payment cards does not make anyone a creditor either, and billing a health plan is not credit extended to the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: When must a provider give a Medicare fee-for-service patient an Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage?
opciones: When a payment denial is expected and the financial liability would pass to the patient
When a payment denial is expected and the service is one Medicare never covers at all
When the patient asks for a written estimate of the charges before a scheduled service
When the patient is enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan with a network restriction
preguntas.explicacion: The ABN, form CMS-R-131, is issued by fee-for-service providers and suppliers when they expect Medicare to deny payment and want the liability to move to the patient, typically because the item or service is not reasonable and necessary or is custodial care. For services Medicare never covers, notice is not required, though a voluntary one may be given as a courtesy. It is not used for Part C or Part D care.

Facility security plan, which protects the building and its equipment from intrusion
Contingency operations, which open the facility so lost information can be restored

preguntas.pregunta: What do the hand hygiene guidelines say about the fingernails of staff with direct patient contact?
opciones: Keep them short, clean and free of artificial nails and polish, under about 0.5 cm
Keep them short and clean; polish is acceptable as long as it is fresh and unchipped
Keep them short and clean; artificial nails are acceptable if gloves are always worn
Keep them under about 2 cm, which is short enough to be reached by a nail cleaner
preguntas.explicacion: Nails are kept short, clean and free of artificial nails and polish, with current guidance putting the length under half a centimeter. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the otoscope held like a pen with a free finger resting on the patient's cheek?
opciones: So a sudden movement cannot drive the speculum into the canal or eardrum
So the magnifying lens stays aligned with the axis of the ear canal
So the instrument warms to skin temperature before it is introduced
So the light beam is angled away from the pars flaccida of the eardrum
preguntas.explicacion: Gripping the instrument between the first and second fingers and bracing another finger against the cheek means the otoscope travels with the patient's head if it moves, which is what protects the canal and the tympanic membrane from injury. preguntas.pregunta: Which claim belongs under invasion of privacy?
opciones: Public disclosure of private facts about the person concerned
Publication of a written falsehood that damages a reputation
Repetition of a spoken falsehood in front of other employees
Retention of a record for longer than the policy allows for
preguntas.explicacion: Invasion of privacy covers a family of claims: intrusion on seclusion, public disclosure of private facts, false light and appropriation. preguntas.pregunta: How long must a covered entity keep its privacy policies, its privacy notices and the record of how complaints were resolved?
opciones: Six years from creation or from the last date the document was in effect, whichever is later
Two years from creation or from the last date the document was in effect, whichever is later
Ten years from creation or from the last date the document was in effect, whichever is later
Six years from creation, with no account taken of when the document stopped being in effect
preguntas.explicacion: The documentation clock runs six years, counted from the later of the date a document was created or the last date it was in effect, and it covers privacy policies and procedures, the privacy practices notices, the disposition of complaints, and the other actions and designations the rule requires to be documented. preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an endocrine gland from an exocrine gland?
opciones: An endocrine gland has no duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has no duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
preguntas.explicacion: Exocrine glands have ducts that carry their product to a surface, which is how sweat, sebaceous and mammary glands and the digestive enzyme glands work. Endocrine glands are ductless: their hormones go straight into the blood and travel everywhere, but they act only on the cells that carry a receptor for them.

preguntas.pregunta: After a report has gone to the ordering physician, the laboratory discovers a transcription error in one result. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Promptly notify the ordering person, issue a corrected report promptly, and keep duplicates of the original and the corrected report
Issue a corrected report within 30 days and destroy the original so that only the corrected version remains on file
Correct the value in the LIS and rely on the next routine report to carry the corrected result to the physician
Notify the ordering person by telephone with read-back, which replaces the need for a corrected written report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(k) has three parts when a reported result is found to be wrong: the laboratory promptly notifies the authorized person who ordered the test, and whoever uses the result, of the reporting error; it issues a corrected report promptly; and it maintains duplicates of both the original and the corrected report. The original is never discarded, a silent LIS edit notifies nobody, and the read-back procedure belongs to critical results, not to corrections.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient who improves after epinephrine still sent to the hospital?
opciones: A second wave of symptoms can return hours after the first has settled
The autoinjector dose is only half of what the reaction really needs
Epinephrine wears off within 5 minutes and cannot be repeated at all
Skin testing for the allergen has to be done in the first hour
preguntas.explicacion: Anaphylaxis can be biphasic in up to 20 % of cases, with symptoms coming back and peaking 8 to 11 hours after the first reaction, so the patient is observed. preguntas.pregunta: Naegele's rule is applied to a last menstrual period of March 10. How is the date worked out?
opciones: Add 7 days and subtract 3 months, then add a year: December 17
Add 7 days and add 3 months, then add a year: June 17 of next year
Subtract 7 days and add 3 months, then add a year: June 3 next year
Add 10 days and subtract 3 months, then add a year: December 20
preguntas.explicacion: Starting from the first day of the last period, seven days are added, three months are taken off and a year is added, which comes to the same as adding seven days and nine months, or 280 days in all. The rule assumes a regular 28-day cycle with ovulation on day 14, and it needs the patient to be sure of that first day.

preguntas.pregunta: What compression rate is kept during adult CPR?
opciones: 100 to 120 per minute, letting the chest rise fully between compressions
80 to 100 per minute, starting the next push before the chest rises
60 to 80 per minute, matched to the normal resting adult pulse rate
140 to 160 per minute, matched to the resting pulse rate of an infant
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are fast and hard, in the band of 100 to 120 per minute, and the chest is allowed to come all the way back up after each one. Full recoil between compressions is what maintains coronary artery perfusion pressure, so leaning on the chest defeats the compression that follows. The counted set of 30 is done without pausing.

preguntas.pregunta: From the moment the donor hands over the specimen until the bottles are sealed, who has to keep it in sight?
opciones: Both the donor and the collector keep visual contact with the specimen
The collector alone, because the donor is no longer part of the process
The donor alone, so that the collector cannot be accused of tampering
A second collector acting as a witness for the whole of the procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Both the collector and the donor must keep the specimen in view from the moment it changes hands until the bottles have been sealed for shipment to the laboratory or the testing facility. preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO classification of safety-engineered devices, how are retractable lancets categorized, and what is their listed advantage?
opciones: Passive devices; they retract and prevent needle-stick injuries
Active devices; the user must slide a sleeve forward over the blade
Passive devices; they prevent reuse but do not reduce needle-sticks
Active devices; the mechanism can trigger during probing and require a new puncture
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 places lancets under passive safety-engineered devices with the advantage that they are retractable and prevent needle-stick injuries. The sleeve that slides forward describes the active self re-sheathing needles, and the two remaining descriptions belong to auto-disable syringes, the other passive device, which prevents reuse but offers no needle-stick protection and can trigger while probing.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Safety-engineered devices

preguntas.pregunta: Which vascular injury is associated with puncturing the medial aspect of a newborn's heel?
opciones: Laceration of the tibial artery, with collapse of veins
Rupture of the plantar vein, with a spreading haematoma
Thrombosis of the calcaneal branch, with local necrosis
Puncture of the tibial nerve, with loss of the venous branch used
preguntas.explicacion: The first listed complication of capillary sampling is collapse of veins if the tibial artery is lacerated from puncturing the medial aspect of the heel. The same list includes osteomyelitis of the calcaneus, nerve damage when the fingers of neonates are punctured, haematoma with loss of the venous branch, scarring, and localized or generalized necrosis as a long-term effect.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.4 Complications

preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the office that unencrypted e-mail is unacceptable to her. What should the office do?
opciones: Offer another channel, such as a more secure electronic method, mail or telephone
Explain that e-mail is the only channel the Privacy Rule permits for results
Continue using e-mail but omit her name from the subject line of each message
Close her portal account, since electronic access would raise the same problem
preguntas.explicacion: An individual may ask a covered provider to communicate by alternative means or at alternative locations where that is reasonable. The example given is accommodating a request for appointment reminders by e-mail rather than on a postcard. The same principle runs the other way: where unencrypted e-mail is unacceptable to a patient asking for confidential communications, other means such as more secure electronic methods, mail or telephone should be offered.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: Alternative means · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 4H k62 · NCMA 3.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which rhythms are the ones a defibrillator can correct with a shock?
opciones: Ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Asystole and pulseless electrical activity, treated with epinephrine
Sinus bradycardia and sinus tachycardia in a patient with a pulse
Atrial fibrillation and supraventricular tachycardia with a pulse
preguntas.explicacion: Pulseless rhythms split into shockable and nonshockable. The shockable pair is ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia, where early defibrillation converts the rhythm into one that perfuses. Asystole and pulseless electrical activity are not shocked: they are managed with compressions, epinephrine and the search for a cause.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Shockable and nonshockable rhythms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic in a state that does not license radiologic technologists is hiring. What will applicants still likely be asked for?
opciones: Certification, which employers typically require or prefer regardless
A doctoral degree, since imaging is interpreted by the technologist
A hospital diploma program, the only route the states have accepted
State licensure anyway, because an employer cannot waive state law
preguntas.explicacion: Most states require radiologic technologists to be licensed or certified, and few require licensure for MRI technologists. Licensure usually means graduating from an accredited program and either passing a state certification exam or obtaining certification from a credentialing organization. Employers typically require or prefer certification even where the state does not.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Radiologic and MRI Technologists — Licenses, Certifications, and Registrations
preguntas.subtema: Licensure vs certification · CCMA 1A k3

preguntas.pregunta: Who can serve as the attorney in fact under a power of attorney?
opciones: A person or an organization; being a lawyer is not required
A licensed attorney at law admitted in the principal's state
A relative of the principal, once the court has approved them
A person named in the principal's will as the estate executor
preguntas.explicacion: A power of attorney is an agreement between a principal and an attorney in fact, and the attorney in fact does not have to be a lawyer. It gives that agent the right to act in the principal's place, and the agent is a fiduciary of the principal. Powers may be general, limited or special, and are usually written, though some jurisdictions allow oral ones.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: power of attorney
preguntas.subtema: Power of attorney · CCMA k218 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.2

preguntas.pregunta: Besides pain and fluid loss, which threat makes a large burn dangerous?
opciones: Infection, because burned skin no longer keeps pathogens out
Anemia, because burned skin no longer produces red blood cells
Hypertension, because burned skin no longer widens its vessels
Jaundice, because burned skin no longer clears bile pigments
preguntas.explicacion: Burns kill skin cells, and the fluid loss that follows can lead to dehydration, electrolyte imbalance and renal and circulatory failure, so patients are given intravenous fluids and nutrients. The other serious threat is infection: with the intact layers gone, burned skin is extremely susceptible to bacteria and other pathogens.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.4 Diseases, Disorders and Injuries of the Integumentary System, Burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(1) (2027 I.C.6.g(1)) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital chaplain asks for the names of admitted patients of his denomination. What does the privacy rule allow?
opciones: Telling him, provided the patient was informed and did not object
Telling him, since clergy are workforce members of the hospital
Refusing, unless each patient signed a written authorization first
Refusing, because religious affiliation is never disclosed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Clergy and religious figures may be told which patients belong to their denomination, on the condition that the patient was informed first and raised no objection. That is why these preferences, along with who may visit and who should be notified, are asked at admission and put in writing. Disclosure can still happen in an emergency or when an incapacitated patient could not consent, if it is consistent with that person's best interest and the reasoning is documented.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Clergy and Other Religious Figures
preguntas.subtema: Clergy and the patient list · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: Which parts of the eye is an ophthalmoscope built to examine?
opciones: The cornea, aqueous, lens and vitreous, and the retina behind them
The pressure inside the globe, by indenting or flattening the cornea
The refractive error of the eye, with lenses of several dioptric powers
The front segment alone, lit by a thin bright beam through a diaphragm
preguntas.explicacion: The ophthalmoscope carries its own illumination and viewing optics, and it looks through the media of the eye — cornea, aqueous, lens and vitreous — as far as the retina. Reading the pressure is the tonometer's job, measuring refractive error belongs to the manual refractor, and the narrow slit of light is the slit lamp.
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · CCMA 3B4 k62

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient with low vision cannot make out the video remote interpreting screen. Under the ADA guidance?
opciones: VRI is not effective for him; an on-site interpreter may be required
VRI is sufficient as long as it meets the four performance standards
Written notes replace the interpreter, since VRI was properly offered
The patient must now bring his own interpreter, because VRI failed
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA allows VRI where it would be effective, but VRI is not effective in every case, for example for a person who has difficulty seeing the screen because of vision loss or positioning; then an on-site interpreter may be required. Meeting the technical standards does not cure that, and the entity may never shift the duty to the patient.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services (VRI)

preguntas.pregunta: Which confusion does the device table warn about when winged steel needles are stocked?
opciones: Winged sets for evacuated tubes look like winged infusion sets
Winged sets for evacuated tubes look like retractable lancet devices
Winged sets with a safety feature look like auto-disable syringes
Winged sets for paediatric use look like adult hypodermic needles
preguntas.explicacion: The disadvantages listed against winged steel needles include the difference between those made for evacuated system tubes and winged infusion sets, which can create confusion at the tray. The other two entries are the air in the tubing and the higher cost of the device.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A 3B k54 k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: How does the federal Health Center Program require a health center to be led in part by the people it serves?
opciones: A majority of the governing board's members must be patients of the health center
A majority of the clinical staff must live inside the area the health center serves
A majority of the board must be licensed providers who practice at the health center
A majority of the patients must have incomes under the federal poverty guidelines
preguntas.explicacion: Health centers are community based and led in part by their own patients. Program rules say the center must have a governing board where most members are patients, must focus on the needs of the people and areas it serves, must build systems of care centered on the patient, and must see everyone, even a person who cannot pay. About 90% of its patients have incomes under 200% of the poverty level.
preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Bureau of Primary Health Care: What is a Health Center? (What must health centers do?)
preguntas.subtema: Health center governance · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose left side is weak is being helped from the bed into a wheelchair. Where does the chair go?
opciones: On his stronger right side, at a 45-degree angle to the bed and with the brakes on
On his weaker left side, at a 45-degree angle to the bed and with the brakes on
Squarely facing the bed at the patient's feet, with the brakes left off for now
On his stronger right side, parallel to the bed, with the footplates left down
preguntas.explicacion: The chair is set at about 45 degrees to the bed with the brakes applied, and when one side is weaker it goes on the healthier side so the patient pivots toward strength. Shoes go on first, the patient sits with feet flat on the floor, and a gait belt is applied if it is needed. Coming back, the footplates are raised and the leg rests swung out of the way.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Care Transfer Techniques", Clinical Significance: Bed to Wheelchair
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2A.5 · CCMA 3B4 k65 · RMA III.H.3.a.ii

preguntas.pregunta: Which credential does a respiratory therapist need?
opciones: An associate's degree, and a license in every state except Alaska
An associate's degree, and a license in every state without exception
A bachelor's degree, and a national certification instead of a license
A master's degree, and supervised clinical experience after graduation
preguntas.explicacion: Respiratory therapists care for patients who have trouble breathing, for example because of a chronic condition such as asthma. They typically need an associate's degree in respiratory therapy, and some employers prefer a bachelor's degree. They must be licensed in every state except Alaska, and the requirements vary from one state to another.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Respiratory Therapists — How to Become One
preguntas.subtema: Allied health roles · CCMA 1A k2

preguntas.pregunta: Which instruction belongs in the teaching for a breast self-exam?
opciones: Lie down with one hand behind the head, then examine the armpit as well
Stand throughout, because lying down flattens tissue and hides the lumps
Press only over the nipple, where discharge would first become visible
Look in the mirror only with the arms raised over the head, not lowered
preguntas.explicacion: Lying down spreads the tissue and makes the whole breast easier to cover, with one hand behind the head and the flat of the middle fingers of the other hand pressing in small circles. Breast tissue runs into the armpit, so that is felt too, sitting or standing. The mirror check is done both with arms at the sides and with arms raised.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Breast self-exam — Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21

preguntas.pregunta: Two conditions are linked by the word with in the Alphabetic Index, and the note never says one caused the other. How are they coded?
opciones: As related, since the classification presumes a causal link between the two
As unrelated, unless the provider has explicitly documented a link between them
As related only where the two conditions sit inside the same chapter of the book
As related, but with the order of the two codes on the claim reversed for it
preguntas.explicacion: The words with and in are read as associated with or due to wherever they appear in a code title, in the Index or in an instructional note, and the classification presumes a causal relationship between the conditions they link. They are coded as related even without documentation saying so, unless the record states they are unrelated or a guideline demands an explicit link.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.15
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8

preguntas.pregunta: Where does lymph come from, and what happens if it is not returned to the blood?
opciones: From interstitial fluid; without return there is edema and a falling blood volume
From arterial blood; without return there is edema and a rising blood volume
From the bone marrow; without return there is anemia and a falling blood volume
From the digestive tract; without return there is edema and a rising blood volume
preguntas.explicacion: Lymph is close in composition to blood plasma and comes from the fluid that leaves the capillaries into the tissues. Once that interstitial fluid enters a lymph capillary it is called lymph, and returning it to the blood is what keeps edema away and holds blood volume and pressure where they belong.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Lymphatic System: Components of the Lymphatic System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027 I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with metallic implants that contain iron is scheduled for an imaging study. Which one must be reconsidered, and why?
opciones: MRI, because its powerful electromagnets can dislodge such implants
CT, because its rotating scanner can dislodge such implants
Ultrasound, because its sound waves can heat such implants
X-ray, because its short wavelength can magnetize such implants
preguntas.explicacion: An MRI scanner surrounds the patient with magnets strong enough that the room itself has to be shielded, so patients carrying iron-containing implants, from internal sutures to some prosthetic devices, cannot be scanned. The trade-off elsewhere is favorable: MRI uses no radiation at all and is unmatched for finding tumors.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging, Magnetic Resonance Imaging
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen preserved with formaldehyde is run on a reagent strip. What should the laboratory expect?
opciones: False-positive leukocyte esterase, urobilinogen and glucose readings on the strip
False-negative leukocyte esterase, urobilinogen and glucose readings on that strip
False-positive albumin readings on the strip, the same effect thymol produces
False-negative leukocyte esterase readings, the same effect mercury salts produce
preguntas.explicacion: Formaldehyde preserves cell structure but distorts several pads, giving falsely positive leukocyte esterase, peroxidase, urobilinogen and glucose reactions. Each preservative has its own signature: thymol falsifies albumin upward, mercury salts falsify the leukocyte reaction downward, hydrochloric acid shifts the pH, and boric acid dulls the leukocyte pad and alters the starting pH.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Interfering Factors (Preservatives)

preguntas.pregunta: What must a plaintiff show to rely on res ipsa loquitur?
opciones: That such harm needs negligence, that the thing was controlled, and that they did not contribute
That the defendant admitted the error, that it was documented, and that a witness saw it
That a statute was breached, that the breach was reported, and that the harm was foreseeable
That the injury was severe, that it was permanent, and that another clinician would agree
preguntas.explicacion: The Latin means the thing speaks for itself, and it lets the plaintiff carry the burden with what amounts to circumstantial evidence. Three things must be proved: the incident is of a type that does not generally happen without negligence, it was caused by an instrumentality solely in the defendant's control, and the plaintiff did not contribute to the cause.
preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: res ipsa loquitur
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which design feature does the FDA recommend for every type of sharps injury prevention feature, regardless of mechanism?
opciones: The user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated
The feature should retract the sharp fully within the housing of the device
The feature should activate passively, without any action by the user
The feature should be reversible so that a jammed device can be cleared
preguntas.explicacion: The two recommendations FDA Table 1 applies to all features are that the user can easily tell whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be deactivated and stays protective through disposal. Full retraction is the recommendation for retractable sharps only, passive operation is one of two acceptable mechanisms rather than a requirement, and reversibility contradicts the table.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, All features
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: What characteristics does the WHO ask the phlebotomist to look for when choosing a vein?
opciones: A vein of good size that is visible, straight and clear
The vein closest to the surface, even if it curves or branches
The largest vein, even if it can only be felt with the tourniquet on
A vein on the back of the hand, which the WHO prefers for adults
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 tells the phlebotomist to extend the arm, inspect the antecubital fossa or forearm, and locate a vein of a good size that is visible, straight and clear, adding that it should be visible before the tourniquet goes on. The back of the hand is the preferred site for an IV, and a vein found only under the tourniquet fails the WHO's visibility criterion.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site

preguntas.pregunta: Which growth charts are used for a 14-month-old and which for a 6-year-old?
opciones: WHO standards from birth to 2 years, then CDC charts from 2 years onward
CDC charts from birth to 2 years, then WHO standards from 2 years onward
WHO standards for both, since they cover birth through 19 years of age
CDC charts for both, with the WHO standards kept for children born preterm
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation splits at the second birthday: the World Health Organization standards for infants and children from birth to 2 years, and the national charts for children of 2 and older. A separate extended set of charts exists for children with severe obesity.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Growth Charts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.F.4.a.ii · NCMA 2B.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which rhythm is the one that follows a prolonged QT interval?
opciones: Torsades de pointes, a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Atrial flutter, with sawtooth waves standing in for P waves
A junctional escape rhythm at 40 to 60 beats per minute
A first-degree block with a PR interval longer than 200 ms
preguntas.explicacion: A long QT carries an imminent risk of dangerous ventricular rhythms, and torsades is the polymorphic tachycardia that grows out of a congenital or acquired long QT. The risk factors named are QT-prolonging drugs, low potassium, calcium or magnesium, and ischemia.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: QT Interval
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i

preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act add for covered entities that use electronic health records?
opciones: An audit trail accounting for disclosures, tracking who accesses records and when
A requirement to keep paper copies of every electronic record for 6 years
An exemption from breach notification for encrypted records affecting under 500 patients
A rule allowing shared passwords within a department to speed access
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH promoted adoption and meaningful use of electronic health records and strengthened HIPAA: covered entities with an EHR must provide an audit trail accounting for disclosures, systems track who signs on and off, when, and what data they viewed or downloaded, patients may obtain electronic copies of records held in an EHR, and a patient who pays out of pocket in full may ask that the information not be shared with the health plan. Unique user names and unshared passwords are what make that tracking possible; shared passwords defeat it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Unique User Identification and Electronic Health Records
preguntas.subtema: HITECH · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38

preguntas.pregunta: How common is anaphylaxis after a vaccine, and what has to be on hand because of it?
opciones: Rare, about one per million doses; epinephrine and airway equipment stay ready
Rare, about one per thousand doses; epinephrine and airway equipment stay ready
Common, about one per hundred doses; an antihistamine and oxygen stay ready
Rare, about one per million doses, so no emergency equipment is kept nearby
preguntas.explicacion: Allergic reactions worry vaccine providers, but they are uncommon, and anaphylaxis after vaccination is rare: roughly one per million doses for many vaccines. Epinephrine and the equipment for managing an airway are kept available for immediate use anyway. Reactions can be triggered by the antigen, residual animal protein, antimicrobials, preservatives, stabilizers or other components, all listed in the package insert.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: After the Visit, Allergic reactions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.3.a(1)

preguntas.pregunta: How early in a visit can de-escalation be used?
opciones: As early as triage, before any confrontation has started
Once the patient has raised his voice at a staff member
Once the aggression management team has been called in
Only after chemical and physical restraint were refused
preguntas.explicacion: Triage is named as the point where de-escalation can already start. Management of the workplace turns on prevention and de-escalation, with fight or flight kept as a resort, and physical restraint used as an adjunct to chemical restraint only as a last resort. Waiting for shouting or for a team to arrive throws away the early chances to diffuse tension.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse gets red, irritated hands from her gloves but has no itching and no hives. What does that suggest?
opciones: Irritant contact dermatitis, which is not a true latex allergy
A type I hypersensitivity, the reaction behind a true latex allergy
Allergic contact dermatitis, which adds pruritus and urticaria
Latex-fruit syndrome, in which foods and gloves both provoke it
preguntas.explicacion: Irritant contact dermatitis produces erythema of the skin and comes from friction or contact with chemicals; it is a non-immunologic reaction, so the person does not have a true latex allergy and may need only a protective barrier for the skin. Allergic contact dermatitis is the delayed type IV reaction and brings pruritus and urticaria after exposure.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section History and Physical and section Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: A grey top tube for glucose is drawn short and the laboratory reports the sample as haemolysed. What does the WHO table say about this tube?
opciones: It requires a full draw, because a short draw may cause haemolysis
It requires a half draw, because its additive is concentrated for small volumes
It needs no fill requirement, since fluoride keeps glucose stable for five days
It should be filled last only when a haemolysed sample is expected
preguntas.explicacion: In the uses column for the oxalate/fluoride tube, Table 2.3 states that glucose specimens require a full draw and that a short draw may cause haemolysis. The five-day glucose stability is a separate property of the antiglycolytic agent and does not remove the fill requirement. The grey tube is drawn last (position 10) in every case, not only when haemolysis is suspected.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k59 k51 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: At check-in, why does the office ask a Medicare patient about other insurance at every visit?
opciones: To identify any payer primary to Medicare before the services are provided
To confirm that the patient has kept paying the Part B monthly premium
To decide whether the visit needs an advance written notice of non-coverage
To record which provider referred the patient for the appointment that day
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are told to gather accurate secondary payer data by asking patients or their representatives about other coverage that could be primary to Medicare at each visit, before services are given, and to check eligibility as well; the goal is to prevent incorrect billing and overpayments. Premium payment, advance notices of non-coverage and referral sources are separate matters handled elsewhere.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Your Responsibilities
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMAA 5B k66, 4 k58 · CCMA 5E k182

preguntas.pregunta: Name the four components of the urinary system in the order urine travels through them.
opciones: Kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, urethra
Kidneys, urethra, urinary bladder, ureters
Ureters, kidneys, urethra, urinary bladder
Urinary bladder, kidneys, ureters, urethra
preguntas.explicacion: The kidneys form the urine. The ureters carry it away from them to the urinary bladder, which is a temporary reservoir, and the urethra carries it from the bladder to the outside. Reversing ureter and urethra is the classic slip, and the two words differ by very little in writing.
preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Urinary System: Components of the Urinary System

preguntas.pregunta: A courier leaves a box of specimens on the dashboard of a parked car in direct sunlight for an hour. Beyond the heat, what does prolonged light exposure do to the samples?
opciones: UV irradiation can oxidatively degrade nucleic acids, so samples are covered to shield them from unnecessary light
Visible light fades the bar codes, so samples are relabelled on arrival before they can be accessioned
UV irradiation sterilises the specimen surface, so samples intended for culture are treated as contaminated
Light activates clotting in anticoagulated tubes, so samples are inverted again before they are centrifuged
preguntas.explicacion: Light exposure brings two problems: the temperature swings that come with sitting in the sun, and UV irradiation, which over long exposure leads to oxidative degradation of nucleic acid polymers. The example given for this variable is a sample forgotten in direct sunlight, and the countermeasure is simple: protect specimens from unnecessary light by covering them. Minimising transport time is the surest protection of all.

preguntas.pregunta: A sedimentation rate is set up from a tube that turns out to hold a small clot, and a second one from an icteric patient. What happens to each reading?
opciones: The clotted one reads low; the icteric one is hard to read at the interface
The clotted one reads high; the icteric one is hard to read at the interface
The clotted one reads low; the icteric one reads high from the extra pigment
Both read high, since neither plasma settles at the expected sedimentation rate
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux formation the test depends on, so the value comes out lower than it should. Icteric samples from patients with liver disease give a dark yellow plasma that is visually hard to tell from the settled red cells, and a hemolysed sample turns the plasma red for the same reason, blurring the boundary the reading is taken from.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient phones a week after a draw to say the bruise has turned greenish-yellow. What does that indicate?
opciones: The normal sequence of healing, which ends at the usual skin colour
An infection developing under the skin at the site of the puncture
A deep periosteal bruise that will need a radiograph of the elbow
Fresh bleeding into the same area from the original puncture wound
preguntas.explicacion: A bruise starts pinkish red and tender, turns bluish, then greenish-yellow, and finally returns to the normal skin colour as it heals, over days to months. What would prompt a call to a clinician is streaks of redness, pus or fever, which point to infection, or extreme pressure in the area.

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the WHO's Step 1 say the rack holding the sample tubes should be placed during a draw?
opciones: Close to the health worker but away from the patient, so it is not tipped over
On the patient's lap, so the phlebotomist can reach the tubes without turning
On the far side of the patient, so the sharps container stays nearest the phlebotomist
Inside the sharps container tray, so used and unused items stay together
preguntas.explicacion: Step 1 ends with the instruction to keep the rack with the sample tubes close to the health worker but away from the patient, to avoid its being accidentally knocked over. The same step lists the tray contents, including gauze, labels, forms, leak-proof transport bags and a puncture-resistant sharps container, which Chapter 3 says must be within arm's reach and clearly visible.

preguntas.pregunta: Which electronic transaction does an office use to ask a health plan whether a patient's coverage is active?
opciones: The eligibility transaction, one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA
The claim status transaction, one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA
The remittance advice transaction, which reports the plan's payment decisions
The enrollment transaction, which adds or removes members from a health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Eligibility is one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA, alongside claim status, coordination of benefits, claims and encounter information, enrollment and disenrollment, referrals and authorizations, and payment and remittance advice. Claim status asks what happened to a claim already sent, remittance advice explains how a claim was paid, and enrollment moves members in or out of a plan.

preguntas.pregunta: A point-of-care glucose on a diabetic inpatient is critical for the third time today; the nurse says the team already knows the patient runs high. What does the reporting policy require?
opciones: Treat it as a reportable event and follow the critical value policy each time, even when earlier critical values are known
Skip the report, because a known pattern of critical values exempts later results from the notification policy
Report it only if it is higher than the previous critical value recorded for the patient earlier that day
Report it only after a venous sample confirms it, since a point-of-care glucose is not treated as a critical value
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are treated as reportable events even if earlier critical values are already known for the patient, and the reporting policy is followed consistently for each instance. The only acceptable deviation is an exceptional case backed by sufficient evidence, such as an obvious testing error or a preanalytical error, that justifies setting the value aside. Documentation of the result and of the actions taken accompanies every critical value obtained at the point of care.

preguntas.pregunta: Which working conditions are listed as increasing the chance of a blood exposure?
opciones: Devices without safety features, and sharps containers that are overfilled
Devices with passive safety features, and containers emptied twice a shift
Single-use devices, and containers sealed with a tamper-proof lid on top
Devices used on a single patient, and containers kept within arm's reach
preguntas.explicacion: The factors raising exposure risk include failing to follow standard precautions and safety protocols, doing procedures where blood exposure is expected, using devices that have no safety features, and improper disposal of needles or overfilled sharps containers.

preguntas.pregunta: Packing sticks to the wound bed during a dressing change. What is the correct response?
opciones: Soak it gently with saline or sterile water and lift it off, and remove all of it
Pull it away steadily in one motion, and leave any fragment that will not release
Cut away the exposed part, and leave the adherent portion for the next dressing change
Cover it with a fresh layer of damp gauze, and let the whole packing come out tomorrow
preguntas.explicacion: Adherent packing is soaked with normal saline or sterile water and lifted gently, because pulling it off dry traumatizes the wound bed. Every bit of packing has to come out at each change, and its quantity and type are checked against what the last change recorded. If it will not come free the provider is contacted, and a different packing material is considered.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist packs three tubes and the paper requisition together inside the same plastic transport bag. What does WHO best practice say?
opciones: Use a leak-proof bag with an outside compartment for the request form, so the form is not contaminated
Use a leak-proof bag and fold the form around the tubes, so the two travel together as one unit
Use a leak-proof bag and staple the form to the outside, so the courier can read the destination
Use a leak-proof bag and place the form in a second bag, so it can be discarded on arrival
preguntas.explicacion: Step 10 of the WHO phlebotomy procedure is to pack the samples safely in a plastic leak-proof bag that has an outside compartment for the laboratory request form; keeping the requisition outside is what protects it from contamination. When several tubes travel together they go in a rack or padded holder so they do not break in transit, and the labels on tubes and forms are rechecked before dispatch.

preguntas.pregunta: How does suture numbering work?
opciones: Thick sutures run 0 to 10, with 10 the largest; thin ones run 1-0 to 12-0, with 12-0 the smallest
Thick sutures run 0 to 10, with 0 the largest; thin ones run 1-0 to 12-0, with 1-0 the smallest
All sutures run 1-0 to 12-0, and the more zeroes a suture carries the larger its diameter is
All sutures run 0 to 12, and the number gives the breaking strength in newtons, not the width
preguntas.explicacion: Size is given relative to diameter, and the scale runs in two directions. Thick sutures are numbered 0 through 10, with number 10 the largest; thin ones carry zeroes, from 1-0 down to 12-0, and 12-0 has the least breaking strength of all. Between one size and the next there is roughly 0.01 to 0.05 mm of difference in diameter.

preguntas.pregunta: A resting adult has a pulse of 108 beats per minute. How is that value classified?
opciones: Tachycardia, since anything above 100 beats per minute is above the adult range
Within range, because the adult range reaches 110 beats per minute while seated
Bradycardia is ruled out, but no term applies until the rate passes 120 per minute
Within range for an adult over 65, whose upper limit rises with arterial stiffening
preguntas.explicacion: The resting adult range is 60 to 100 beats per minute. Above 100 the term is tachycardia and below 60 it is bradycardia, and neither limit shifts with age: the same 60 to 100 band covers everyone from 10 years old upward, including seniors. A fast pulse may point to infection or dehydration, so it is reported.

preguntas.pregunta: How close is a pulse oximeter reading to the true arterial oxygen saturation?
opciones: It may run 2% to 4% above or below the true value, so an arterial blood gas can confirm it
It matches the true value exactly, which is why it replaced arterial blood gas testing
It runs about 10% below the true value, and the reading is corrected upward for that
It is exact from 95% upward and unusable below that, where a blood gas is required
preguntas.explicacion: The device gives an estimate: results can be 2% to 4% higher or lower than the real figure, and an arterial blood gas is the test used when an exact value is needed. Oximeters are calibrated over a range of 70% to 100%, so readings below 70% should not be compared with the invasive measurement.

preguntas.pregunta: A woman grieving a pregnancy loss says nobody around her treats it as a real death. Which type of grief is that?
opciones: Disenfranchised grief, over a loss that is not recognized
Complicated grief, whose reactions do not subside at all
Acute grief, which begins right after a death has occurred
Anticipatory grief, which is felt before the loss happens
preguntas.explicacion: Disenfranchised grief covers a loss that is not validated or recognized, so the person does not feel free to acknowledge it openly. The examples given include terminated pregnancies, stillbirth, deaths from stigmatized illnesses, and the end of a relationship that had already been severed.

preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factor is calcium, and why does that matter for citrate and EDTA collection tubes?
opciones: Factor IV; removing calcium from a sample keeps it from clotting
Factor I; it is converted into fibrin at the end of the cascade
Factor III; damaged cells release it to start the extrinsic path
Factor XIII; it stabilizes the fibrin mesh once it has formed
preguntas.explicacion: Calcium ions are factor IV, drawn from diet, platelets and bone, and needed for the entire clotting process. Sodium citrate and EDTA both act by forming calcium salts that remove calcium from the sample, which is how those tubes keep blood from clotting. Fibrinogen is factor I, tissue factor is III, and the fibrin-stabilizing factor is XIII.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a piece of metal embedded in the thigh and bleeding around it. What is done?
opciones: Pad and bandage around the object and tape it where it sits
Pull the object straight out and then press hard on the wound
Rock the object gently loose and pack the opening with gauze
Press directly down on the object to close the vessel beneath it
preguntas.explicacion: An embedded knife, stick or piece of metal is left where it is: pulling it out or probing the wound usually causes more bleeding and more damage. Pads and bandages are built up around the object and it is taped in place. Loose dirt or debris that can be seen is removed, and organs showing through a wound are never pushed back in.

preguntas.pregunta: A subject who reads little English is being enrolled in a study. What does the federal consent rule require?
opciones: Information in language the subject or their representative understands
A translated form filed with the review board ten days after enrollment
A relative of the subject to sign the English-language form as a witness
The review board to waive consent whenever a language barrier is present
preguntas.explicacion: The rule states that whatever is given to the subject or the legally authorized representative has to be in language they understand, and that they must receive the information a reasonable person would want in order to decide, with a chance to discuss it. A board may waive consent only on narrow findings, such as minimal risk, never because translating is inconvenient.

preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act change about the position of business associates?
opciones: It made them directly liable, civilly and criminally, for Security Rule violations
It removed the need for a covered entity to sign an agreement with them at all
It made covered entities solely responsible for the acts of a business associate
It limited their obligations to the Privacy Rule and left the Security Rule aside
preguntas.explicacion: Section 13401 of HITECH applies the administrative, physical and technical safeguards of the Security Rule, along with its policy, procedure and documentation requirements, to business associates just as they apply to covered entities, and makes them civilly and criminally liable for violations. Before that the rule reached them only indirectly, through the agreements covered entities had to sign.

preguntas.pregunta: In the Swiss cheese model applied to laboratory medicine, when does an error reach the patient?
opciones: When the holes in every defensive layer line up and no layer detects and corrects the error
When a single layer fails, since each layer protects a different phase and none of them overlaps
When the analytical layer fails, because the extra-analytical layers cannot stop an analytical error
When more than half of the layers fail, which is the threshold at which the system is declared unsafe
preguntas.explicacion: Reason's model pictures a system as a stack of Swiss cheese slices in which each slice is a defensive layer and the holes are opportunities for an error to pass to the next process; an adverse patient outcome happens when all the holes line up and the system fails to detect and rectify the error. In laboratory medicine the slices are equipment, training, supervision and quality assurance procedures, and management aims to close the gaps and strengthen the defences rather than rely on any single one.

preguntas.pregunta: A rapid strep test on a 30-year-old shows a clear test line and a control line. What does the result mean for further testing?
opciones: Group A streptococcal antigen is present; no confirmatory culture is needed
Group A antigen is present, but a culture must confirm it before antibiotics start
A streptococcus of some group is present, so a culture is needed to identify the group
The patient carries antibodies from a past infection rather than a current infection
preguntas.explicacion: When the rapid test is positive, the patient has strep throat or another group A strep infection and no further testing is needed. The kit detects antigens of group A streptococcus only, not other causes of sore throat and not antibodies. Culture is the backup for negative rapid tests, mainly in children and adolescents. A rapid screen can occasionally be positive without disease, which is called a false positive.

preguntas.pregunta: Which distinction between capacity and competence is correct?
opciones: Capacity is a clinical call for one decision; competence is a legal finding by a judge
Capacity is decided by a judge; competence is assessed by the treating clinician
Both are legal findings that differ only in the standard of evidence required
Capacity is permanent once established; competence is specific to one situation
preguntas.explicacion: Capacity is a functional determination that a person can or cannot make a particular medical decision, relative to their baseline and to the situation and stakes. Competence is the ability to take part in legal proceedings, presumed until disproved at a hearing, and decided by a judge, never by medical providers.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a fingerstick glucose test with cold hands. How is the site prepared?
opciones: Wash and dry the site with warm water; alcohol is optional, and if used the skin must dry fully first
Swab with alcohol and puncture while still damp, since warm water would dilute the sample
Warm the hand with a cloth for 10 minutes, then clean with povidone iodine and let it dry
Rub the fingertip briskly until it reddens, then puncture without any cleaning step
preguntas.explicacion: The testing site is washed and dried thoroughly, using warm water to improve blood flow. Alcohol swabs are not routinely required, but if one is used the skin must dry completely before lancing to avoid diluting the sample or hemolysing it. No temperature or time is specified for warming, and povidone iodine is not used for capillary punctures in children.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says a relative had a heart attack. Which term will appear in the record?

Congestive heart failure, abbreviated CHF
Coronary artery disease, abbreviated CAD
Atrial fibrillation, abbreviated AFIB

preguntas.pregunta: In a hospital where emergency samples hemolyse at 13.5 % and the rest at about 3 %, what did the authors point to as the difference?
opciones: Emergency blood is usually drawn while the catheter is being placed
Emergency blood is usually hand carried instead of going by pneumatic tube
Emergency blood is usually collected into tubes that have no separator gel
Emergency blood is usually drawn by staff who work without a tourniquet
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis in the non-emergency samples of that facility ran near 3 %, against 13.5 % in the emergency department. Transport was ruled out: hand carried and tube-sent samples hemolysed alike.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant wipes the counter with disinfectant and immediately lays out urine reagent strips on the damp surface. Why is that a problem?
opciones: Moisture from a wet or newly cleaned surface can damage the strip and cause incorrect results
The disinfectant neutralizes the color chart, so the pads can no longer be compared to it
Strips exposed to room air for more than 30 seconds lose their nitrite and glucose reactivity
The counter must be dry so that the timer can be started at the exact moment of dipping the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Testing is done in a well-lit, clean and dry area; work surfaces are cleaned and dried before and after testing, and equipment is dried before use. Placing test strips on a moist or freshly cleaned surface may damage the strip and produce wrong results. Reagent strips also stay in their original container, because their shelf life is short and expired or mishandled strips read inaccurately.

preguntas.pregunta: How are patients told that free interpreter services exist at the practice?

A line printed on the appointment reminder card handed at check-out
A notice read aloud by the clinician at the start of every encounter
A leaflet mailed to every household in the languages of the county
preguntas.explicacion: Practices list the languages their qualified bilingual clinicians speak in their directories, and display interpretive services posters in waiting and reception areas so patients learn that free interpreter services are available. preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old is breathing 24 times a minute. How is that read against the range used for older adults?
opciones: Above the adult ceiling but under the 28 per minute used to call an older adult tachypneic
Inside the adult range, because the upper limit rises to 28 per minute after age 65
Below the threshold that matters, since no term applies to an older adult under 35
Above the adult ceiling, and the same 20 per minute threshold applies at every age
preguntas.explicacion: The general adult range stays at 12 to 20, but in the elderly the figure quoted for calling a patient tachypneic is more than 28 breaths a minute. A count of 24 is therefore above the general ceiling without reaching that mark, and it is charted and compared with the patient's own earlier values.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's arm shows no vein crossing the antecubital area, but a prominent vein runs straight up the middle of the forearm into the fossa. Which anatomical variant is this?
opciones: A dominant median antebrachial vein joining the basilic and cephalic
No communication at all between the cephalic and the basilic veins
A median cubital vein present, with the cephalic absent in the upper arm
Venae comitantes, the paired deep veins that travel with the arteries
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein has several recognized variants: the usual pattern, in which it connects the basilic and cephalic veins; a dominant median antebrachial vein of the forearm joining basilic and cephalic in the fossa; a median cubital vein present with the cephalic undeveloped in the upper arm; and no communication at all. Venae comitantes are the paired deep veins that run with the arteries.

preguntas.pregunta: In a rare emergency a phlebotomist judges that stopping to put on a gown would delay care, and draws without it. What does the standard require afterwards?
opciones: The circumstances are investigated and documented, to see whether a change can prevent it
No record is needed, since the judgment of the exposed employee settles the matter
The employee signs the hepatitis B declination form that is kept with the plan
The incident goes in the sharps injury log with the type and brand of the device
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ii) makes the employer ensure protective equipment is used, and allows one narrow exception: the employee temporarily and briefly declined it under rare and extraordinary circumstances, in the professional judgment that using it would have kept care from being delivered or would have increased the danger to someone. Even then the standard does not stop there: the circumstances must be investigated and documented so the employer can see whether something can be changed. The declination form belongs to the hepatitis B vaccine under (f)(2)(iv), and the sharps log records percutaneous injuries.

Sit the person upright at once and offer sips of cold water
Raise both legs higher and keep the person face upwards
Place a rolled towel behind the neck and keep the head back

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about N95 respirators for healthcare workers is correct?

Any worker may use them without fit testing, as with a surgical mask
They protect against droplets only and are replaced by a surgical mask for airborne pathogens
They require fit testing only when used against chemical vapors under Level C
preguntas.explicacion: Loosely woven cloth masks give the least protection and NIOSH-approved respirators the most, that proper fit is a key part of that protection, and that all healthcare workers required to use respirators, N95 included, should be fit tested; where fit testing cannot be completed, a NIOSH-approved powered air-purifying respirator may be considered. preguntas.pregunta: Which formula gives body mass index from measurements in metric units?

Weight in kilograms divided by the height in metres, without squaring
Weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in centimetres
Weight in pounds divided by the square of the height in inches, times 703

preguntas.pregunta: Why are "Do you understand?" and "Does that make sense?" not teach-back questions?
opciones: They can be answered yes, and patients say yes whether they understood or not
They can be answered yes, which the toolkit reserves for the end of the visit
They use medical language that most patients will not recognize at all
They ask about the explanation instead of asking about the patient's plan
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back asks the patient to say in their own words what they need to know or do. preguntas.pregunta: Where should personal protective equipment be put on, and where should it be taken off?

Both inside the patient room, so the corridor stays free of contamination
Put on inside the room and taken off outside, next to the waste container
Put on outside the room and taken off inside, before the door is opened
preguntas.explicacion: Donning takes place outside the patient room, and so does doffing, with one exception spelled out in the sequence: a respirator is not removed until after leaving the room, because the air inside is the hazard it was worn against. The rest of the equipment comes off in order, gloves first, then eye protection, then gown, then mask or respirator, each dropped into the right container. The bloodborne pathogens standard says the same thing in its own words: all protective equipment is removed before leaving the work area.

Results transcribed into the chart late, and duplicate orders entered by two clinicians
Analyser maintenance skipped for a week, and a calibration accepted outside its limits
preguntas.explicacion: Preanalytical errors at the point of care are the same family as in the main laboratory: mistakes in identifying the patient or the specimen, and problems during collection, handling, processing, transport and storage. Cut back on saturated and trans fats and cook with butter or solid shortening
Cut back on unsaturated oils and cook with lard or hydrogenated shortening
Cut back on saturated fat only, since trans fat has no effect on cholesterol

preguntas.pregunta: You need to describe the position of the little toe relative to the middle toe. Which term fits?
opciones: Lateral, because it lies farther from the midline of the body
Medial, because it lies nearer to the midline of the body
Superior, because it lies above the level of the other toes
Proximal, because it lies nearer to the point of attachment
preguntas.explicacion: Medial points toward the midline of the body and lateral away from it. On the foot the big toe is the medial one and the little toe the lateral one, exactly as the thumb is lateral to the other digits of the hand. preguntas.pregunta: Why may a child who is already walking be a harder capillary draw?
opciones: The feet may have developed calluses that hinder adequate blood flow
The heel bone has fused and the skin-to-bone distance drops below 2 mm
Walking children are over 10 kg, so only venipuncture is appropriate
The plantar surface of a walking child carries the tibial artery superficially
preguntas.explicacion: If the child is walking, the feet may have calluses that hinder adequate blood flow, which is one reason the finger-prick takes over above 6 months and 10 kg. Skin-to-bone distances are given only for a 3 kg baby, and the tibial artery risk is tied to the medial aspect of the heel, not to walking.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is wheeled to radiology with the chart on the trolley. What must the transporter be told?
opciones: Not to leave the chart where others could read it
To hand the chart to the first available radiology clerk
To keep the chart closed unless the patient asks to see it
To leave the chart at the desk until the images are done
preguntas.explicacion: Accidental disclosure counts as disclosure. A chart left unattended in a lobby or a procedure suite is the classic example, and when the chart travels with the patient the person pushing the trolley has to know not to leave it anywhere it can be read, on purpose or by accident, by people not involved in that patient's care. Deliberate and accidental disclosure of health information are treated the same way.

Low risk from intact skin exposure and the availability of PEP within 72 hours
Immunity from the hepatitis B vaccine and the low 0.3 percent risk for HIV
The 15-day deadline for the written opinion and the 90-day sample storage

No, First-Class stops at 3.5 ounces for envelopes of every shape
No, a piece above 8 ounces moves to a parcel service priced by weight
Yes, but only once a delivery confirmation service has been added

preguntas.pregunta: Sterile saline is being poured into a basin on the field, and the pour is interrupted halfway. What now?
opciones: Do not restart from that bottle, because its lip is now counted as contaminated
Restart at once from the same bottle, as long as it has not touched the basin rim
Restart from the same bottle after wiping its lip with an alcohol swab and letting it dry
Restart from the same bottle, but pour directly over the field so no splashing occurs
preguntas.explicacion: Once pouring stops it is not resumed, because the edge of the container is then treated as contaminated. Solutions are poured from the side of the field rather than across it, held about six inches above, and only from sealed, sterile, unexpired containers. Apply ice for fifteen minutes each hour until it settles
Raise the arm above the heart and rest it for a further day
Reassure the patient, since bruises last from days to months

Patient refusal and a pacemaker that was fitted recently
An implanted defibrillator and a very hairy chest wall
Recent chest surgery and a known allergy to latex gloves

Hemoconcentration of the specimen from an unevenly worn band
Transmission of hepatitis B, as happens with reusable finger-prick devices
Loss of elasticity that prevents the veins from engorging

Three samples from a single bowel movement, each smeared on a separate card window
One sample from each of 3 bowel movements on 3 different days, sent in a preservative vial
Two samples from one bowel movement, from the first and the last part of the stool
preguntas.explicacion: The home kit asks for 3 different bowel movements; from each one the patient samples two areas of the stool and smears each on one of the two places on that card, then mails the cards to the laboratory. preguntas.pregunta: Blood glucose rises after a meal, insulin is released, and glucose falls back into range. Which kind of feedback is that?
opciones: Negative feedback, because it reverses the deviation from the set point
Positive feedback, because it reverses the deviation from the set point
Negative feedback, because it drives the value further from the set point
Positive feedback, because it drives the value further from the set point
preguntas.explicacion: Negative feedback reverses a deviation and returns the value to its normal range, and glucose control is the standard example: beta cells in the pancreas detect the excess sugar and release insulin, muscle, fat and liver cells take the glucose up, and as the level drops the release of insulin stops.

preguntas.pregunta: In many HMO plans, what must a patient obtain before seeing a specialist if they want the plan to pay?
opciones: A referral, which is a written order from their primary care doctor
A preauthorization, the plan's finding that the visit is necessary
A written order from the specialist, sent back to the primary care doctor
A claim, filed by the primary care doctor before the specialist visit
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a referral as an order, in writing, from the primary care doctor so that the patient can see a specialist or receive certain services. In many HMOs that order is required before getting care from anyone other than the primary care doctor, and without it the plan may refuse to pay. The order runs from the primary care doctor to the specialist, not the other way. A preauthorization is the plan's own decision that a service is medically necessary, a different entry, and a claim is the request for payment that comes after the care, not before it.

A puncture-resistant sharps container, since all regulated waste is handled as sharps
Any lined trash can, provided the bag is closed before it leaves the room
A container marked with the GHS pictogram frame, red square set on a point

Which laboratory they would like to run the ordered tests

Twice a day and three times a day

Twice a day and once a day at night

The laboratory may release it only with the ordering physician's consent

The laboratory may not release it, since results go to authorised persons

preguntas.pregunta: A new patient accepts a service at the office without signing any financial agreement. What kind of contract is that?
opciones: An implied-in-fact contract, inferred from what both parties did
An express contract, since the service was requested out loud
An implied-in-law contract, since no benefit was actually given
No contract at all, since payment terms were never agreed in advance
preguntas.explicacion: An express contract is communicated in speech or writing. An implied-in-fact one is formed when the promises are inferred from the parties' intentional conduct and one side knows, or has reason to know, the other will read that conduct as agreement: accepting a merchant's services means paying their reasonable value. An implied-in-law contract is a remedy against unjust enrichment, not a real agreement.

preguntas.pregunta: During teach-back a patient reads the handout aloud word for word. How should that be handled?

Accept it; reading the handout back proves that she can follow it later
Take the handout away and ask her to recall the instructions from memory
Move on and repeat the whole explanation at the next scheduled visit
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back is not a test of memory, so the patient is welcome to look at the handout while answering. What has to come out in her own words is the content: parroting the text back may mean nothing was understood. When a misunderstanding shows up, the point is explained a different way and teach-back is asked for again.

General and delayed, aimed at the person's own attributes
Private and formal, aimed at the annual evaluation cycle
Immediate and public, aimed at the team's overall workload

preguntas.pregunta: A dermatologist reviews a photograph of a rash uploaded overnight and answers the next morning. Which kind of telehealth is that?

Synchronous, because a clinician and a patient are both involved in the exchange
Remote patient monitoring, because a device captured the image that was reviewed
A facilitated virtual visit, because staff at a clinic gathered the data beforehand
preguntas.explicacion: Asynchronous telemedicine, the store and forward method, gathers history, images and diagnostic data and sends them to a specialist for interpretation and recommendations later.
