preguntas.pregunta: At what rate is sinus bradycardia diagnosed on the current consensus?
opciones: Fewer than 60 beats per minute, with sinus node depolarization otherwise normal
Fewer than 50 beats per minute, with sinus node depolarization otherwise normal
Fewer than 40 beats per minute, with the depolarization starting outside the sinus node
Fewer than 60 beats per minute, but only when the patient reports symptoms too
preguntas.explicacion: The diagnosis rests on a rate below 60 beats per minute with depolarization still starting in the sinus node. preguntas.pregunta: Before asking about alcohol use, the assistant explains why the question is on the form. Which technique is that?
opciones: Providing rationale
Exploring feeling tones
Social pleasantries
Summarizing
preguntas.explicacion: Providing rationale means saying up front why the information or the treatment recommendation is needed. preguntas.pregunta: A strip shows a constant PR interval of 240 ms with every P wave conducted, in a patient with no symptoms. How is that regarded?

As an emergency, with a permanent pacemaker fitted without delay
As an artifact, since a PR that long comes from a lead reversal
As a second-degree block, since a beat is about to be dropped
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing is truly blocked in a first-degree block: the impulse is delayed, each P wave still reaches the ventricles one to one, and the finding is relatively common and has largely been treated as benign. Prompt pacing belongs to the Mobitz type II block.

preguntas.pregunta: What has been found about zero-tolerance policies for workplace violence?

Overall incidence drops, although verbal abuse stays where it was
They lift the duty to treat the patient in the emergency department
They only work where a buddy system has been set up alongside

Inside the room, immediately after the gloves
Inside the room, before the gown so the ties are reachable

preguntas.pregunta: What glucose load is given to a nonpregnant adult for a standard diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test?

50 g of glucose, taken without any prior fasting
100 g of glucose after a fast of 8 to 14 hours
1.75 g of glucose per kilogram of body weight

preguntas.pregunta: How is sinus tachycardia defined?
opciones: A sinus rhythm faster than 100 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm faster than 120 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm faster than 150 beats per minute
Any narrow rhythm faster than 100 beats per minute
preguntas.explicacion: Sinus tachycardia carries the same electrical signature as normal sinus rhythm, with P waves upright in I, II and aVL and negative in aVR, each followed by a QRS complex; the only difference is a rate over 100. Finding and treating the underlying cause is what management rests on.

That the paper requisition be destroyed once the entry is complete
That a pathologist countersign every entry made from a paper form
That the entry be made within 30 days of the specimen's arrival in the lab

The employer may require a prescreening antibody test before agreeing to provide the series
She must wait for the next annual training session, when the vaccine is offered again to staff

Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) keeps every medical procedure under (f), the vaccine included, free of charge and at a reasonable time and place, and (f)(2)(ii) bars the employer from requiring prescreening first. The system design, toward the individual's own training
The near miss, toward the events that reached the patient
The corrective plan, toward the accreditation standard

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being prepared for a transvaginal ultrasound. What is the instruction about the bladder?
opciones: Empty it, because a full bladder pushes the uterus out of the field
Fill it, because a full bladder pushes the uterus into better view
Fill it, because the probe uses the bladder as an acoustic window
Empty it, because a full bladder raises the risk of a urinary infection
preguntas.explicacion: The rule reverses between the two approaches. Transabdominal scanning may see better with a full bladder, while a full bladder displaces the uterus backward and out of reach of the vaginal probe, so that study is done with the bladder empty. preguntas.pregunta: For infants and children who need a urine culture, which noninvasive collection showed the lowest contamination rates?
opciones: Midstream collection with cleansing, compared with bag or diaper collection
Sterile bag collection, compared with midstream or diaper collection
Diaper collection, compared with midstream or sterile bag collection
Midstream collection without cleansing, which equaled cleansing in women
preguntas.explicacion: In children, the evidence pointed to much lower odds of contamination with midstream collection after cleansing than with a sterile bag, a diaper or midstream without cleansing, and that body of evidence was rated high. Catheterization and suprapubic aspiration remain the invasive references.

preguntas.pregunta: A crutch user develops weakness of the hand after leaning on the shoulder rests. What is this?
opciones: Crutch palsy, from pressure on the brachial plexus at the shoulder rest
Crutch palsy, from pressure on the median nerve inside the hand grip
Compartment syndrome, from the arms carrying the whole of the body weight
Peroneal palsy, from the tips of the crutches being set too far from the feet
preguntas.explicacion: Resting body weight on the axillary pad squeezes the brachial plexus and can leave the radial and ulnar nerves palsied. It is repairable with treatment, and it is prevented by teaching that the hands, not the armpits, carry the load. Extra padding helps, though too much of it narrows the gap under the axilla and brings back the problem it was meant to fix.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is on oral vancomycin for colitis and the ward asks for a trough. What does the guidance say?

Oral vancomycin needs a trough within 30 minutes before the dose
Oral vancomycin needs a peak drawn as the capsule is swallowed
Oral vancomycin needs a trough only once steady state is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Unlike the intravenous injection, oral vancomycin typically does not call for serum concentration monitoring, because it is barely absorbed into the circulation: its oral bioavailability is under 10%. The pre-dose trough at steady state and the peak taken at the end of the infusion both belong to the intravenous route.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away before applying blood to a glucose test strip?
opciones: It may contain interstitial or intracellular fluid or be hemolyzed, which can affect the accuracy of the result
It contains alcohol from the skin preparation, which the guidance says lowers the glucose reading by about 10 %
It is arterial rather than capillary blood and therefore reads higher than the venous reference method does
It clots too quickly on the strip, so most meters will display an insufficient-sample error message
preguntas.explicacion: After the lancet fires, the first drop is wiped off with clean gauze because it may hold intracellular or interstitial fluid or be hemolyzed, either of which can distort the result. opciones: Into the radial and ulnar arteries, at the apex of the cubital fossa
Into the radial and ulnar arteries, at the superior border of the fossa
Into the cephalic and basilic branches, at the apex of the cubital fossa
Into the radial and median branches, at the medial epicondyle of the humerus

preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer preserve the medical record of an employee covered by the OSHA access standard?

For thirty years counted from the date of hire
For the duration of employment plus five years
For six years after the employee leaves the job

preguntas.pregunta: Which item comes off first when removing PPE, in the CDC-recommended sequence?

The mask or respirator, released from behind the head
The gown, pulled from the shoulders and turned inside out
Eye protection, lifted by the earpieces or the strap

The Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act of 2000
The Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993

preguntas.pregunta: How does Mobitz type I differ from Mobitz type II?
opciones: In type I the PR lengthens beat by beat until one is dropped
In type I the PR stays constant until one beat is dropped
In type I the PR shortens beat by beat until one is dropped
In type I every other P wave is dropped without any warning
preguntas.explicacion: Both are second-degree blocks, and the PR interval is what tells them apart. In type I it stretches with each beat until a P wave finally goes unconducted; in type II it stays the same and a beat drops out without warning. When every other P wave is blocked the two cannot be told apart, and it is called a 2:1 block.

A copy of every safety data sheet, arranged by section and by supplier
The exposure limits of each chemical and the results of air monitoring
The signed acknowledgment of each employee who attended the training

preguntas.pregunta: Which nerve is most often injured by the leg supports used in the lithotomy position?
opciones: The common peroneal nerve, which wraps around the head of the fibula
The ulnar nerve, which runs along the inner side of the flexed elbow
The brachial plexus, which is stretched when the arm goes past 90 degrees
The sciatic nerve, which is compressed by the pad under the lower back
preguntas.explicacion: The peroneal nerve rounds the fibular head, exactly where the calf rests against the support, so padding between the bony prominence and the support is what protects it. The light blue citrate tube
The lavender EDTA tube
The grey fluoride tube

One value, whichever hour it is
Three or more of the four values
All four of the values must be high

Being treated for a sexually transmitted infection

preguntas.pregunta: A green-top heparin tube arrives for a viral PCR. Why do current guidelines say to reject it, and which tubes are recommended instead?
opciones: Heparin inhibits DNA amplification in a dose-dependent way and is carried through extraction; EDTA or ACD tubes are recommended
Heparin chelates the magnesium the polymerase needs for amplification; citrate or fluoride tubes are recommended instead
Heparin degrades RNA through its own nuclease activity during storage; serum tubes with clot activator are recommended instead
Heparin causes hemolysis during centrifugation and releases heme into the plasma; plain red-top tubes are recommended instead
preguntas.explicacion: Heparin has been shown to inhibit DNA amplification in a dose-dependent fashion, with the degree depending on the polymerase used, and it is recovered during both DNA and RNA extraction, so the consensus is that heparinised plasma is unsuitable for molecular infectious disease testing and current guidelines say heparin-containing specimens should be rejected. preguntas.pregunta: The provider reviews the amendment request and concludes the entry is accurate. What is the patient entitled to?

A second review by a licensed professional who took no part in the original decision
Automatic deletion of the disputed entry, since the record must reflect what she reports
A refund of any copying fee she paid, since the amendment request was not granted
preguntas.explicacion: When a covered entity denies an amendment request it must give the individual a written denial and let her submit a statement of disagreement to be included in the record. The rule sets out the process for requesting and answering these requests. The independent second review by a licensed professional belongs to the access right, not to amendment.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Amendment
preguntas.subtema: Amendment denial · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.5

preguntas.pregunta: The practice has out-of-date addresses for 14 of the patients affected by a breach. What substitute notice is required?
opciones: A notice on its home page for at least 90 days, or in major print or broadcast media
A notice on its home page for at least 30 days, with no toll-free number needed
A single telephone call to each of the 14, which is the alternative for small numbers
A notice to prominent media outlets, the step reserved for a breach of any size
preguntas.explicacion: Where contact information is insufficient or out of date for 10 or more individuals, substitute notice means posting on the home page of the web site for at least 90 days or placing the notice in major print or broadcast media where those people probably live, and including a toll-free number that stays active at least 90 days. For fewer than 10, another written form, a telephone call or another means will do.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Individual Notice
preguntas.subtema: Substitute breach notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1.b · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8

preguntas.pregunta: Who has to use the National Provider Identifier in the transactions adopted under HIPAA?
opciones: Covered providers, health plans and clearinghouses, in place of older identifiers
Covered providers alone, since plans and clearinghouses keep their own numbers
Providers who bill Medicare, since commercial payers assign their own numbers
Providers and patients, since the identifier appears on the insurance card
preguntas.explicacion: Covered health care providers and all health plans and clearinghouses must use the identifier in the administrative and financial transactions adopted under HIPAA, and it takes the place of legacy provider identifiers there. Covered providers must also share their number with other providers, plans, clearinghouses and any entity that needs it for billing, so its use is not limited to Medicare claims.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Provider Identifier Standard (NPI)
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing requirements · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185 · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: A confused older patient keeps apologizing for wrong answers. What should the staff member do?
opciones: Make clear this is a search for information, not a test
Correct each wrong answer so the record stays accurate
Move the remaining questions to the family in the hallway
Stop the interview and chart the history as unreliable
preguntas.explicacion: Support and reassure the patient, acknowledging responses that are correct or understood, and say plainly that the conversation is not a test but a search for information that will help them. A staff member can telephone afterward about the instructions. Real changes in cognition get screening and diagnostic testing.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Confusion and cognitive problems
preguntas.subtema: Cognitive impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient care technician asks the office how to become a licensed practical nurse. How long does the state-approved program typically take?
opciones: About one year, after which the nurse must be licensed to practice
About two years, ending in an associate's degree from a college
About four years, ending in a bachelor of science in nursing
About six weeks of on-the-job training under a registered nurse
preguntas.explicacion: Licensed practical and licensed vocational nurses must complete a state-approved educational program, which typically runs about one year, and they must be licensed. They give basic nursing care, usually under the supervision of a registered nurse, an advanced practice nurse or a physician, and work with stable or chronically ill patients. Associate and bachelor degrees lead to registered nursing instead.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses — How to Become One
preguntas.subtema: Provider titles and credentials · CCMA 1A k2

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being taught to use a glucometer. Which range is quoted as normal blood glucose?
opciones: 70 to 99 mg/dL, which is 3.9 to 5.5 mmol/L in the other unit
70 to 99 mg/dL, which is 7.0 to 9.9 mmol/L in the other unit
80 to 130 mg/dL, which is 4.4 to 7.2 mmol/L in the other unit
60 to 110 mg/dL, which is 3.3 to 6.1 mmol/L in the other unit
preguntas.explicacion: The body holds glucose inside a narrow band, roughly 70 to 99 mg/dL, or 3.9 to 5.5 mmol/L, through the opposing action of insulin and the counter-regulatory hormones. A capillary test needs a lancet, a meter and unexpired strips, and only meters cleared by a regulator and proven accurate should be handed to a patient.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.a · CCMA 3B3 k64

preguntas.pregunta: A daughter insists the hospital must follow her father's directive word for word. What is the honest answer?
opciones: A directive is recognized in law but is not binding in every situation
A directive is legally binding on the team once it is scanned into the record
A directive is legally binding only inside the state where it was written
A directive is only a suggestion, so the team decides what is best for him
preguntas.explicacion: The document is recognized in law without being binding in law. The care team and the proxy will try hard to honor what it says, and there are situations tangled enough that nobody can tell what the person would have chosen. That is why talking things over ahead of time matters as much as the paperwork, and why the form is far more than a suggestion staff may set aside.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Advance Care Planning: Advance Directives for Health Care (are directives legally binding)
preguntas.subtema: Advance directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a (E.7 from 2027) · NCMA 4.2

preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA tube for a hematocrit sat on the counter for eight hours before it was spun. Why is the result questionable?
opciones: After about 6 hours at room temperature the risk of hemolysis rises and red cell shape changes, so results become inaccurate
Whole blood for a hematocrit is acceptable for 24 hours at room temperature, so only the color of the plasma column is affected
The EDTA will have clotted the specimen after that long, which is why hematocrit tubes should contain heparin instead
The packed cell column will read falsely low because the red cells settle and compact before the tube is centrifuged
preguntas.explicacion: Hematocrit testing should be performed right after collection. Prolonged storage at room temperature alters the shape of red cells because of their metabolism, and after roughly 6 hours the risk of hemolysis increases, leading to inaccurate results. The 24-hour allowance applies to prothrombin time specimens, not to hematocrit, and EDTA is the anticoagulant of choice for the macrohematocrit sample, so clotting is not the issue.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Hematocrit specimen age · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.i

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of factors raises the risk of developing osteoarthritis?
opciones: Age, obesity, muscle weakness and previous joint injury
Age, low body weight, declining estrogen and family history
Youth, high activity, low calcium intake and vitamin D lack
Age, tobacco use, high blood pressure and high cholesterol
preguntas.explicacion: The risk factors for osteoarthritis are age, female sex, obesity, anatomical factors, muscle weakness and joint injury from work or sport. The second option lists the risk factors of osteoporosis instead, which is a different disease of the same system: declining estrogen, aging, family history, low body weight and too little calcium or vitamin D.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Osteoarthritis", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(2) (2027 I.C.6.g(2)) · RMA I.A.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which position is adopted most often for an anoscopy?
opciones: Lateral decubitus, with the upper leg flexed at the hip and the knee
Lithotomy, with both legs in supports and the buttocks past the edge
Supine with the knees drawn up, which opens the anal canal widest
Standing and leaning forward over the end of the examination table
preguntas.explicacion: Side-lying with the upper leg bent is the commonest choice, though the knee-shoulder and prone positions also work. A digital rectal examination goes first, to be sure nothing in the canal would be injured by the instrument. The anoscope is introduced with its obturator in place, which is then removed so the canal can be seen as the device is withdrawn.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anoscopy", Preparation: Positioning
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.c.ii · CCMA 3B4 k61

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a sudden change in how many leafy greens a patient eats matter on warfarin?
opciones: Warfarin depletes usable vitamin K, so the vitamin K in the diet shifts the response
Warfarin needs vitamin K to be activated, so more of it in the diet strengthens the drug
Warfarin binds vitamin K inside the stomach, so any food taken with it blocks absorption
Warfarin is a racemic mixture, so food decides which enantiomer the liver handles first
preguntas.explicacion: Warfarin competitively inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, the enzyme that puts vitamin K back into its usable form, so the liver makes less of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X and less protein C and S. The response varies widely from patient to patient, and a diet rich in vitamin K is one of the factors weighed when dosing, alongside genetics, other illnesses, interacting drugs and adherence.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Warfarin", Mechanism of Action and Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.8

preguntas.pregunta: Which situation would be expected to raise a patient's recorded body temperature?
opciones: Heavy clothing, a hot and humid room, a recent meal or strong physical activity
A cool examination room, light clothing and ten minutes of quiet sitting first
The early morning hours, when the daily temperature curve reaches its low point
The first half of the menstrual cycle, before the corpus luteum has formed
preguntas.explicacion: Temperature is not fixed: physical activity, strong emotion, eating, heavy clothing, some medicines, a hot room and high humidity all push the value up. The second half of the menstrual cycle adds about one degree Fahrenheit or more, and the daily low point falls in the early morning.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6

preguntas.pregunta: How is a minor cut on a patient's finger cleaned in the office?
opciones: Washed thoroughly with mild soap and water after the hands are washed
Wiped with alcohol and left open to the air so a scab forms faster
Scrubbed with a brush and antiseptic until all the redness is gone
Soaked in hydrogen peroxide for 5 minutes and covered with a dressing
preguntas.explicacion: The person giving first aid washes their hands first, then washes the cut itself with mild soap and water, uses direct pressure to stop the bleeding, and applies an antibacterial ointment and a clean non-stick bandage. A wound is never assumed to be clean because no dirt can be seen, and nobody breathes on an open wound.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Cuts and puncture wounds", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 14

preguntas.pregunta: What marks aggressive communication as opposed to assertive communication?
opciones: It leans on “you” messages and can feel like an attack on the receiver
It leans on “I” messages that name facts and the sender's own feelings
It places the rights of the receiver ahead of the sender's own rights
It repeats the same message until the receiver returns some feedback
preguntas.explicacion: Assertive communication states the facts and the sender's feelings without disrespecting the receiver, and is built on phrases such as “I feel” or “Help me understand.” Aggressive communication uses “you” messages, so the receiver feels attacked instead of hearing the issue. Yielding to others is passive, and repetition is not one of the three styles.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Communication styles · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's red reflex is white in one eye and red in the other. What does that call for?
opciones: Urgent referral to an ophthalmologist, since the finding can be sight-threatening
A repeat check at the two-month well-child visit, since reflexes mature slowly
Reassurance, since a difference in color between the two eyes is a normal variant
A repeat check after the erythromycin ointment has been applied to both eyes
preguntas.explicacion: A normal reflex is red, orange or yellow and looks the same in both eyes in color, intensity and clarity. An abnormal or absent one can mean congenital cataract, retinal disease, retinoblastoma, strabismus or refractive error, and it goes to an ophthalmologist urgently. Debris on the surface can also blacken it, so the patient is asked to blink first.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Red Reflex", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.c · CCMA 3B4 k62 · RMA III.F.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient logging her dairy intake asks how much natural cheese counts as one cup from the Dairy Group. What is the equivalent?
opciones: An ounce and a half of natural cheese
An ounce and a half of processed cheese
Three ounces of any kind of cheese
Half an ounce of natural cheese
preguntas.explicacion: In the Dairy Group a cup-equivalent is a cup of milk, yogurt or soy beverage, or an ounce and a half of natural cheese. Processed cheese takes a larger amount, about two ounces, to reach the same equivalent. Adults are pointed toward three cup-equivalents a day, mostly fat-free or low-fat.
preguntas.fuente: MyPlate, USDA: Dairy — what counts as a cup; and Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 14: Dairy Group
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · NCMA B.21

preguntas.pregunta: The autoclave tape on a load changed color, but the biological indicator from that same load grew. What does the guideline direct?
opciones: Repeat the spore test at once, and recall nothing but implants unless the machine is faulty
Recall and reprocess the entire load at once, since a grown indicator proves a failed cycle
Accept the load, because the chemical indicator is the reading that governs a steam cycle
Quarantine the load until the next weekly spore test comes back negative, then release it
preguntas.explicacion: Single positive spore tests happen sporadically: spore resistance varies slightly, the machine may be misused, the culture may pick up a contaminant. When the mechanical and chemical readings say the cycle ran properly, the test is repeated at once and only implants are recalled. If the repeat stays positive, the machine is pulled until serviced.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's fingers are frostbitten and medical help is far away. How are they rewarmed?
opciones: Soaked in warm water, never hot, for 15 to 30 minutes, without rubbing
Soaked in hot water for 5 minutes and then rubbed briskly to warm them
Held near a radiator until the color returns and the skin feels soft
Massaged gently with a warm dry cloth until sensation comes back
preguntas.explicacion: The affected part is soaked in warm, never hot, water for 15 to 30 minutes, at 104 °F to 108 °F (40 °C to 42.2 °C), keeping the water moving; warming is done when the skin is soft and color and feeling return. The area is not rubbed or massaged, direct dry heat is not used, and blisters are left alone. Refreezing does worse damage than waiting.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Frostbite", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which serious adverse event is described as rare during phlebotomy?
opciones: Loss of consciousness accompanied by tonic clonic seizures
Loss of consciousness lasting under a couple of minutes only
Pain at the puncture site with anxiety about the procedure
Bruising and haematoma at the site of the venepuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Serious adverse events tied to drawing blood are rare, and the example given is loss of consciousness with tonic clonic seizures. Pain at the site, anxiety and fainting are put in the less severe group, and bruising with haematoma is the best documented event of all.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks about the physician assistant who examined her today. What education and credential does that role typically need?
opciones: A master's degree from an accredited program, plus a license in every state
A doctoral degree from an accredited program, plus a license in every state
An associate's degree, plus certification the employer may prefer to require
A postsecondary certificate, plus on-the-job training under a physician
preguntas.explicacion: Physician assistants examine, diagnose and treat patients under the supervision of a physician, and typically enter the occupation with a master's degree from an accredited program. All states require them to be licensed. For Part B coverage the assistant must have graduated from an accredited program or passed the national certification exam, and must be licensed by the state.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Physician Assistants — How to Become One; and 42 CFR 410.74(c)
preguntas.subtema: Provider titles and credentials · CCMA 1A k2

preguntas.pregunta: A blood count drawn in EDTA reports a platelet count far below the patient's usual value, and the smear shows clumps. Which repeat specimen is suggested?
opciones: A repeat count on blood collected into a citrate tube
A repeat count on blood collected into a heparin tube
A repeat count on serum from a clot activator tube
A repeat count on the same EDTA tube after warming it
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets can clump in EDTA because of antibodies that act only in the presence of that anticoagulant, and the analyser then reports a falsely low count. The way round it is to repeat the count on blood taken into a citrate tube instead. Serum has no platelets left to count.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Interfering Factors; and StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: A laryngoscope blade is used on a patient. How is it categorized, and what is the least processing it may receive?
opciones: Semicritical, so at a minimum it needs high-level disinfection after it is cleaned
Critical, so it has to be sterilized because not one bacterial spore may survive on it
Noncritical, so intact skin is barrier enough and a hospital disinfectant will do for it
Semicritical, but an intermediate-level agent is accepted because the contact is so brief
preguntas.explicacion: Blades touch mucous membranes, which puts them in the semicritical group along with respiratory therapy tubing, endoscopes and diaphragm fitting rings. Those items should carry no microorganisms, though small numbers of spores are tolerated, so high-level disinfection is the floor. The brief-contact exception belongs to items like bed rails.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Semicritical Items
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which office task falls within the payment activities a covered entity may carry out without authorization?
opciones: Determining a patient's eligibility for coverage under her plan
Training a new medical assistant on how the practice rooms patients
Evaluating whether a clinician should keep hospital privileges
Preparing a de-identified data set for a population health project
preguntas.explicacion: Payment covers what providers do to be paid and what plans do to collect premiums and provide benefits. The examples the guidance offers include determining eligibility or coverage and adjudicating claims, reviewing services for medical necessity and justification of charges, and limited disclosures to consumer reporting agencies. Training, credentialing and de-identification are health care operations instead.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Payment activities · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient has just given her history to the rooming assistant. What does the guidance ask of the next person?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating it tires her
Take the whole history again, so two versions can be compared
Take the history only from the relative who came with her today
Skip the history, since a form was filled in the waiting room
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is advised in taking the history of an older patient: where possible, have the patient tell their story only once, even if other staff in the office would normally help gather it, because giving the account to one member of staff and then again can be tiring. Preliminary data may instead be requested from records or from forms filled in at home.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k40 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how leukemia and lymphoma differ. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: Leukemia starts in blood-forming tissue, lymphoma in immune system cells
Leukemia starts in immune system cells, lymphoma in blood-forming tissue
Leukemia starts in the lymph nodes, lymphoma in the marrow of the bones
Leukemia starts in bone or soft tissue, lymphoma in the lining of organs
preguntas.explicacion: Leukemia starts in blood-forming tissue such as the bone marrow, and large numbers of abnormal blood cells are produced and enter the bloodstream. Lymphoma starts in cells of the immune system and falls into two families: Hodgkin lymphoma, marked by the Reed-Sternberg cell, and the non-Hodgkin lymphomas, a large and varied group.
preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, leukemia and lymphoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: What does the National Correct Coding Initiative use its procedure-to-procedure edits for?
opciones: To stop payment for pairs of procedures that should not be reported together
To stop payment for services that exceed the units likely for one patient in a day
To set the payment amount for each procedure reported on a professional claim
To assign the diagnosis code that supports the procedure billed on the claim
preguntas.explicacion: The correct coding initiative runs two kinds of edits: procedure-to-procedure edits, which address pairs of codes that should not be billed together, and medically unlikely edits, which cap the units of service a provider would report for one patient on one day. Payment amounts come from the fee schedule, and diagnosis codes are selected from the documentation, not assigned by edits.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative
preguntas.subtema: Bundling and unbundling · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.a(3)

preguntas.pregunta: Incorrect urine collection stayed at 9.2 % in the audited hospital even after staff began speaking to patients. What were patients told about?
opciones: The sampling itself, the type of container, and collecting the midstream portion
Fasting for twelve hours, the type of container, and the time of the first void
The volume required, the transport temperature, and the use of a preservative
The sampling itself, the labelling of the cup, and the delivery time to the bench
preguntas.explicacion: Urine testing is unusually exposed to preanalytical trouble because the patient, not a trained collector, takes the sample. In that laboratory the receiving secretary explained the sampling, the container types, sterile and with or without preservative, and how to catch the midstream portion. Even so, incorrect collection remained at 9.2 % of the urine samples received.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with high cholesterol is being worked up for a secondary cause. Which of these appears on that differential?
opciones: Metabolic syndrome, along with hypothyroidism and chronic renal insufficiency
Metabolic syndrome, plus acute conjunctivitis and otitis media in children
Osteoarthritis, along with hypothyroidism and chronic renal insufficiency
Pelvic inflammatory disease, along with obesity and biliary obstruction
preguntas.explicacion: Before hyperlipidemia is called primary, the secondary processes have to be considered: obstructive liver or biliary disease, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, chronic renal insufficiency, anorexia, obesity, metabolic syndrome and diabetes. A full history and physical with comprehensive labs is what narrows that list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hyperlipidemia", Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.c

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart records a vascular graft in the arm the phlebotomist was about to use. What does that mean for the draw?
opciones: The graft is a listed contraindication, so another site is chosen
The graft is acceptable if the puncture is made well below it
The graft is acceptable once the tourniquet is placed above it
The graft only rules out the arm when dialysis is being given
preguntas.explicacion: Among the contraindications tied to the site are scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or an abscess, a vascular graft, a haematoma, venous fibrosis felt on palpation, a previous radical mastectomy on that side, and any device placed for venous access.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 3F k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8

preguntas.pregunta: The Belmont Report breaks the consent process into which three elements?
opciones: Information, comprehension and voluntariness
Disclosure, documentation and attestation
Capacity, competence and authorization
Risks, benefits and alternative treatments
preguntas.explicacion: Belmont analyzes consent as information, comprehension and voluntariness. Information covers the procedure, its purpose, the risks and expected benefits, the alternatives where therapy is involved, and the chance to ask questions and withdraw. Comprehension depends on how and when the information is delivered. Voluntariness means conditions free of coercion and undue influence.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office for Human Research Protections, The Belmont Report (April 18, 1979), Part C.1
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 (E.6 from 2027) · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: An order is written as MS 4 mg. What is the danger, and what is the correct practice?
opciones: It can mean morphine or magnesium sulfate, so the drug name is spelled out
It can mean morphine or a multiple sclerosis code, so the dose is spelled out
It can mean milligrams or micrograms, so the unit is spelled out in full
It can mean a syrup or a solution, so the dosage form is spelled out in full
preguntas.explicacion: MS and MSO4 stand for morphine sulfate and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate, and the three are swapped for each other in handwriting. Two very different drugs behind one set of letters is why all of them are banned, and the practice is to write the complete drug name every time.
preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Drug Name Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which content belongs in the assessment section of a SOAP note?
opciones: The synthesis of the findings into a diagnosis, with the differential and its reasoning
The chief concern in the patient's own words, followed by the history of present illness
The vital signs and laboratory results gathered during the encounter that day
The tests still needed and the treatment steps planned for each identified problem
preguntas.explicacion: The assessment brings subjective and objective findings together to reach a diagnosis, weighing the problems, their possible interactions and any change in status, and listing problems in order of importance. The differential runs from most to least likely with the reasoning stated, and should include unlikely conditions that could cause harm if missed. Testing and treatment steps belong to the plan.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Assessment
preguntas.subtema: SOAP assessment · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: Which payment model pays the clinician for each separate service furnished?
opciones: Fee-for-service, which ties payment directly to each service delivered
Capitation, which pays a fixed amount per patient over a period of time
Global payment, which offers a lump sum for one whole episode of care
Prospective payment, which fixes rates by average resource consumption
preguntas.explicacion: Fee-for-service pays clinicians for each service provided, creating a direct connection between service delivery and payment; third-party payers reimburse from fee schedules or negotiated rates. The model leaves clinicians and patients room to choose services, but has been criticized for rewarding quantity rather than quality and for lacking cost containment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Clinical Resource Management Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care: Traditional Reimbursement Models
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: What is a concussion?
opciones: A traumatically induced disturbance of brain function that is transient
A bruise of the scalp with bleeding under the skin above the skull
A fracture of the skull that leaves the brain tissue itself untouched
A permanent loss of brain function following a hard blow to the head
preguntas.explicacion: A concussion is a disturbance of brain function caused by trauma, and it passes. It is one of the traumatic brain injuries, which range from mild transient symptoms to long periods of altered consciousness; because the symptoms are usually self-limited, the term mild traumatic brain injury is often used for it. The outlook is generally good.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Concussion", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.s · 2027 I.B.8.s · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: In the table position for infant venipuncture, why does the immobilizer reach across the child to hold the wrist palm up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder against twisting, and the wrist grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the child's face turned away so the needle is never seen by the child
It compresses the brachial artery, which slows the flow and prevents a haematoma
It frees the phlebotomist's second hand to apply a rubber tourniquet above
preguntas.explicacion: Two adults stand on opposite sides of an examination table: the immobilizer lays the child on its back with the head on the outstretched arm, pulls the child close, grasps the elbow, and reaches across with the other arm to hold the wrist palm up. Reaching across anchors the shoulder and prevents twisting or rocking, and a firm grasp on the wrist effectively provides the phlebotomist with a tourniquet.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B k80 assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.B age-specific needs · CCMA 3E1 prepare patient

preguntas.pregunta: Why is there no single free-hemoglobin concentration above which every test result must be rejected?
opciones: The interference is optical, chemical or immunological, so the acceptable limit depends on the test and the method
The interference affects only enzymes, so a single limit applies to LDH and CK and none to other analytes
The interference disappears once the serum is diluted, so any sample can be reported after dilution
The interference is constant across analyzers, but each laboratory is free to pick its own limit
preguntas.explicacion: Free hemoglobin interferes in different ways, optically, chemically, or by interacting with antigen or antibody in immunoassays, so the upper limit of hemoglobin tolerated in serum or plasma is test- and method-dependent; the reagent's method description should state the serum index limitations, and laboratories are advised to load those cut-offs into their analyzers. Even specific proteins such as CRP and haptoglobin can be affected.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: During a treadmill test the patient turns dizzy and unsteady on the feet. What does that call for?
opciones: Stopping the test: growing neurologic symptoms are absolute
Slowing the belt by one stage and going on with the test
Going on until the target heart rate has been reached
Stopping the test only if the tracing changes as well
preguntas.explicacion: Increasing neurologic symptoms such as unsteadiness, dizziness or near-fainting sit on the absolute list, so the test ends there and does not wait for the tracing to change. Mild symptoms in a stable patient with a normal tracing are the ones that do not oblige a stop.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Treadmill Stress Testing", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii

preguntas.pregunta: Which finding turns a mild allergic reaction into one treated as severe?
opciones: Wheezing with difficulty swallowing and swelling of the tongue
A few hives over the neck and the face with mild itching of the skin
Watery red eyes with nasal congestion after mowing a lawn
A rash that appears where a new lotion has been applied
preguntas.explicacion: A mild reaction shows a few hives, itching, a rash, a stuffy nose or watery red eyes. The moderate to severe picture adds wheezing, high-pitched breathing sounds, difficulty swallowing, swelling of the face, eyes or tongue, chest tightness, vomiting, dizziness or unconsciousness, and it is handled as anaphylaxis.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Allergic reactions", Symptoms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a qualifying life event for a Special Enrollment Period?
opciones: Turning 26 and losing the coverage held through a parent's plan
Turning 26 and choosing a plan with a lower monthly premium
Changing doctors within the network the current plan contracts with
Reaching the out-of-pocket limit of the plan before the year ends
preguntas.explicacion: Qualifying life events fall into four groups: losing coverage, changes in the household, changes in residence, and other events such as income changes or leaving incarceration. Turning 26 and dropping off a parent's plan is listed as a loss of coverage. Wanting a cheaper premium, switching doctors inside the network, or hitting the out-of-pocket limit are not events that open enrollment outside the yearly window.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Qualifying life event (QLE)
preguntas.subtema: Coverage enrollment · CMAA 5 k73, 5B k66 · CCMA 5E k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: A parent is told to give one tablespoon of a liquid antibiotic. How much is that in the metric system?
opciones: 15 mL, which is also 3 teaspoons
10 mL, which is also 2 teaspoons
5 mL, which is also 1 teaspoon
30 mL, which is also 6 teaspoons
preguntas.explicacion: In the household system a teaspoon is 5 mL and a tablespoon is 3 teaspoons, which comes to 15 mL. Thirty millilitres is an ounce, not a tablespoon, so mixing the two doubles the dose. Patients are familiar with household measures, which is why the equivalences have to be at hand, but the metric system is the one used for the calculation and for what is written down.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4a: Common Household Conversions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(2) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7

preguntas.pregunta: A bronchoalveolar lavage specimen for molecular detection of Pneumocystis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis is being sent from the bronchoscopy suite. How is it transported and stored?
opciones: Transported on ice; stored at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, or at −20 to −80 °C for the long term
Transported at room temperature; stored at 4 °C for up to 4 hours, then discarded as unsuitable
Transported on wet ice only if RNA is the target; stored at room temperature for up to 7 days
Transported frozen at −70 °C; stored at 4 to 8 °C for up to 7 days with a mucolytic additive
preguntas.explicacion: For bronchoalveolar lavage the general guideline is transport on ice, storage at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, and −20 to −80 °C for long-term keeping; time and temperature are the preanalytical variables listed for it. Wet ice reserved for RNA targets is the CSF entry, 4 to 8 °C for 7 days with N-acetyl-L-cysteine or dithiothreitol is the sputum entry, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A public official states that what he is requesting is the minimum necessary for a purpose the rule permits. May the practice rely on that?
opciones: Yes, where the reliance is reasonable in the circumstances of the request
Yes, and the practice is then barred from making its own determination
No, the practice must always make its own minimum necessary determination
No, unless the official supplies a court order covering the same records
preguntas.explicacion: In certain circumstances the rule lets a covered entity rely on the judgment of the requester about how much information is needed, provided the reliance is reasonable. That is permitted for a public official or agency stating the request is the minimum necessary for a permitted purpose, for a workforce member or business associate professional saying the same, and for a researcher with board documentation. Reliance is never obligatory.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement: Reasonable Reliance
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable reliance · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in cancer treatment is losing weight and asks how her diet should differ from before. What is the guidance?
opciones: She may need extra protein and calories to keep her strength up
She may need fewer calories, since treatment lowers her energy use
She should restrict protein so the tumor has less material to grow
She should keep the same intake, since treatment does not change needs
preguntas.explicacion: Cancer and its treatment can change taste, smell and appetite and cut down how much a person eats or absorbs, which opens the door to malnutrition. Extra protein and calories, from meat, fish, eggs, dairy, fats and plant proteins, help hold strength through the side effects. Unmanaged malnutrition can progress to cancer cachexia.
preguntas.fuente: NCI PDQ, Nutrition in Cancer Care (patient version): eating well during treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 cancer · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(d) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(d)

preguntas.pregunta: Which limb wire is the green one, under the usual color code?
opciones: Left leg, while the right leg wire is black
Right leg, while the left leg wire is black
Left arm, while the right arm wire is black
Right arm, while the left arm wire is black
preguntas.explicacion: The four limb wires are colored so they cannot be swapped: red for the right arm, yellow for the left arm, green for the left leg and black for the right leg. Matching the color to the limb before recording is the quickest guard against a reversal that would distort the tracing.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4

preguntas.pregunta: A healthy young adult's rate rises with inspiration and falls with expiration. What is that?
opciones: Sinus arrhythmia, a normal finding that indicates good health
Sinus tachycardia, a normal finding after any light exercise
Premature atrial beats, a common finding at that age
A second-degree block, which drops the occasional beat
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing changes vagal tone from beat to beat: inspiration lifts the rate and expiration lowers it. This respiratory form is the common one, is seen most in children and young adults, and is taken as a marker of cardiac health; losing it can point to underlying heart disease.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Arrhythmia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a history of latex allergy and the phlebotomist has no elastic band at hand. What must she not do?
opciones: Use a latex glove as a tourniquet on that patient
Ask a colleague to bring a latex-free band to the room
Draw the sample without applying a tourniquet at all
Use a clean band that has been reprocessed since its last use
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table is explicit that a latex glove must not be used as a tourniquet where the patient has a history of latex allergy, since some patients react to latex. The gloves themselves are chosen the same way: a pair of well-fitting, clean, disposable latex or latex-free gloves for each patient or each procedure. An employer also has to keep hypoallergenic gloves or similar alternatives within reach for workers who react to the ones normally supplied.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Tourniquet and Gloves; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(iii)
preguntas.subtema: Latex and the tourniquet · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum returns a haemolysis index around 700 µmol/L and the neonatologist still wants the C-reactive protein. What does the laboratory expect at that level?
opciones: The C-reactive protein would read low, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein would read high, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein can be issued with a note, as is done for LDH
The C-reactive protein is unaffected, since haemoglobin interferes optically
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins withstand hemolysis better than many routine chemistry analytes, but severe in vitro hemolysis still reaches them: above an index of roughly 622 µmol/L this marker is underestimated. In 199 newborn samples it was rejected for that reason, and a repeat draw two to five hours later brought the index down and made every result reportable.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist asks where the reason for each draw is meant to be written down. Where does the WHO expect the indications to be set out?
opciones: In a written protocol, or in documented instructions such as a laboratory form
In the verbal handover the ward nurse gives the phlebotomist each morning
On the tube labels, which carry the tests along with the patient details
In the training record each phlebotomist keeps for supervised sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Provision of clear instructions asks that the indications for blood sampling be clearly defined, either in a written protocol or in documented instructions, and it offers the laboratory form as the example. Tube labels carry names, file number, date of birth and the time of the draw; training and supervision are handled in a separate part of the chapter.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k42 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k124

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO Annex C script, what is the patient told about where the results will go?
opciones: They are returned to the named clinician who ordered the tests
They are mailed to the patient's home address within one week
They are read to the patient by the phlebotomist before leaving
They are posted in the patient portal on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: The script says the tubes will be labelled with the patient's name and details, sent to the laboratory, and that the results will be returned to the doctor whose name the worker mentions, the clinician who ordered the tests. It then asks whether the patient has questions, understood the explanation, and is willing to be tested.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2M · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: An order reads "acetaminophen 500 mg PO every 4-6 hours as needed for pain". What type of order is that?
opciones: A PRN order, given when the patient asks for it or when the symptom appears
A routine order, which is followed until some later order cancels it out
A STAT order, given without any delay because the circumstances are urgent
A standing order, applied to any patient who meets clearly defined criteria
preguntas.explicacion: PRN means as needed: the dose is administered when the patient requests it or when the symptom it treats appears, typically pain, nausea or itching, and this order is written in exactly that form. A routine order such as lisinopril 10 mg PO daily runs until it is cancelled, a STAT order is a single dose given without delay, and a standing order is a protocol applied to any patient in defined circumstances.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Types of Orders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · RMA III.G.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: A minor obtained substance use disorder treatment on her own, as her state allows. Who signs the consent to disclose her records?
opciones: The minor alone, even for billing her parent's insurance
The minor and a parent together, as with any other record
The parent alone, since the parent is the personal representative
The program's director, on the minor's behalf, until she turns 18
preguntas.explicacion: Where state law lets a minor apply for and obtain substance use disorder treatment on her own, only the minor may give written consent for a use or disclosure — and that expressly includes disclosing her identifying information to a parent or guardian in order to get paid. Where state law requires parental consent for the treatment, both the minor and the parent sign.
preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(1) · NCMA 4.3

preguntas.pregunta: A povidone-iodine scrub has been painted on the skin. The clinician wants to begin immediately. What is the problem?
opciones: The product has to dry to be bactericidal, with a preferred minimum of two minutes
The product has to be wiped off first, since dried iodine blocks the scalpel's entry
The product has to be rinsed with saline first, or it will stain the drapes and the skin
The product has to be covered with alcohol first, which is what activates the iodine
preguntas.explicacion: Povidone-iodine scrubs, at 7.5 to 10 percent, are painted onto clean skin and left to dry: drying is what makes them bactericidal, and the preferred minimum drying time is two minutes, though it varies by product. Staining of skin, hair and clothing is a known nuisance of the agent, and its microbicidal activity is lost on contact with blood or sputum.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.d · NCMA 2B.11

preguntas.pregunta: Why are the hands held higher than the elbows while rinsing after a surgical scrub?
opciones: So the water runs from the cleanest area toward the least clean and drips off the elbow
So the water carries the antiseptic down the arm and extends its residual activity there
So the water never touches the forearm, which is scrubbed but is not rinsed at that stage
So the water pressure does not force soap under the nails, where debris was just removed
preguntas.explicacion: After scrubbing, the hands are the cleanest part and the forearms and elbows the least clean, so the arm is passed through the running water in one direction and then raised again to let the water drip off the elbow. Ordinary handwashing runs the other way, hands below the elbows, because there the wrists are the dirtier end.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.D.2.c

preguntas.pregunta: A nonpregnant adult's 2-hour value on a 75-g OGTT is 165 mg/dL. How is it interpreted?
opciones: Impaired glucose tolerance (140 to 199 mg/dL)
Normal glucose tolerance (below 200 mg/dL)
Diabetes, since it exceeds 126 mg/dL
Impaired fasting glucose (100 to 125 mg/dL)
preguntas.explicacion: At two hours, below 140 mg/dL is normal, 140 to 199 mg/dL is impaired glucose tolerance (what a provider may call prediabetes) and 200 mg/dL or higher is diagnostic of diabetes, so 165 is impaired tolerance. The 126 cutoff applies to fasting glucose repeated on two tests, and 100 to 125 defines impaired fasting glucose, another fasting category; below 200 is the 1-hour reference, not the 2-hour one.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), Normal Results and What Abnormal Results Mean; StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: OGTT interpretation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139

preguntas.pregunta: A heavy irregular item has to reach the sterile field. How is it transferred?
opciones: It is opened and held while a second person in sterile gloves lifts it onto the field
It is opened and dropped from a greater height so the wrapper stays clear of the field
It is opened and slid across the drape from the near edge toward the middle of the field
It is opened and set on the one-inch border, then nudged inward with a sterile forceps
preguntas.explicacion: Heavy or irregular items are not tossed. They are opened and held by the person with the packaging, and someone wearing sterile gloves takes them onto the field. Sliding an item across the drape or resting it on the one-inch border defeats the purpose, since that border and the outer wrapper are both counted as unsterile.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which three principles does the Belmont Report set out?
opciones: Respect for persons, beneficence and justice
Autonomy, confidentiality and truthfulness
Beneficence, nonmaleficence and fidelity
Respect for persons, privacy and fairness
preguntas.explicacion: The Belmont Report, published in 1979 by the national commission the National Research Act created, names three basic principles for research with human subjects: respect for persons, beneficence and justice. Respect for persons carries two duties — honoring autonomy and protecting those whose autonomy is diminished. Not harming lives inside beneficence there, as the rule to do no harm.
preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office for Human Research Protections, The Belmont Report (April 18, 1979), Part B
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 (E.6 from 2027) · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic buys needles from one company, tube holders from another and tubes from a third. What is the guidance on mixing components from different manufacturers?
opciones: Needle, holder and tubes should come from the same manufacturer, since mixing brands can cause problems in use
Mixing brands is acceptable as long as every component is within its expiration date and sterile
Only the needle and the holder must match; the tubes are interchangeable across manufacturers
Mixing brands is acceptable for adults but not for paediatric tubes with reduced vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Needle, tube holder and tubes are chosen from the same manufacturer to ensure compatibility; otherwise the volume aspirated, the gel stability and the additives can be affected. The WHO device table lists mixing components from different manufacturers as a disadvantage of vacuum systems that can create a problem during use. Neither text limits the rule to adults or to two of the three parts.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (equipment compatibility); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex C, Table C.1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment selection · CPT D3 3A 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: How should stock be arranged inside a storage unit, and what happens to what has expired?
opciones: The earliest expiration dates go in front, and expired stock is pulled out at once
The newest deliveries go in front, and expired stock is pulled at the next count
The most used items go in front, and expired stock is kept until it is replaced
The earliest expiration dates go behind, and expired stock is marked for return
preguntas.explicacion: Stock is rotated so that whatever expires first is what the hand reaches first, with later dates behind it. Anything already expired is taken out immediately rather than at the next count, because leaving it there is how an invalid dose gets given by mistake.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Stock Rotation and Removal
preguntas.subtema: Stock rotation · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7E k99 · NCMA 4.13

preguntas.pregunta: According to the CDC, when is the source patient tested for hepatitis C after an occupational exposure?
opciones: As soon as possible, preferably within 48 hours, ideally by RNA testing
Within 72 hours, using an antibody test with no reflex to RNA
At 3 to 6 weeks, when HCV RNA becomes detectable in the source
At 4 to 6 months, alongside the exposed worker's final antibody test
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC guidance tests the source patient as soon as possible, preferably within 48 hours, with a nucleic acid test for HCV RNA as the preferred option, or an antibody test with reflex to NAT if positive; the exposed worker is tested at the same time with an antibody test and reflex to RNA. If follow-up is indicated, the worker has an RNA test at 3 to 6 weeks and a final antibody test at 4 to 6 months. Those later dates are the worker's schedule, not the source's, and 72 hours is the HIV PEP window.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guidelines for Health Care Personnel Exposed to Hepatitis C Virus, Test the source patient; Test the HCP; Follow-up testing
preguntas.subtema: HCV testing algorithm · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: What is the first step in managing stress?
opciones: Recognizing it and naming the situations behind it
Removing every source of it from the person's life
Starting a relaxation class as the very first move
Cutting out all caffeine, nicotine and junk food
preguntas.explicacion: The first step is recognizing stress, since everyone shows it differently: anger, irritability, lost sleep, headaches, an upset stomach. The next is identifying the stressors themselves — family, school, work, relationships, money, health — because knowing where it comes from is what makes a plan possible.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Learn to manage stress", Information
preguntas.subtema: Environmental stressors · CCMA 1E k31

preguntas.pregunta: A platelet count comes back under 20,000/µL on a patient with no bleeding at all. Which possibility does the notification list tell the laboratory to rule out first?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia caused by the EDTA in the tube itself
Dilution of the specimen by an intravenous infusion nearby
A clot in the tube that has trapped part of the platelets
Interference from lipemia on the optical platelet channel
preguntas.explicacion: A platelet count below 20,000 per microlitre is listed as needing urgent notification because of the bleeding risk, and the note attached to it is a caution rather than a diagnosis: exclude EDTA-induced thrombocytopenia before the call is made. The upper limit on the same line, above one million, is flagged for the opposite reason, the risk of thrombosis.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E13 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the phlebotomist whether her potassium result means she has kidney disease. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Say that the ordering provider interprets results, and route the question to that provider
Read the reference interval aloud and show her where her own value falls against it
Tell her the value is normal for her age, since age-based intervals are on the report
Refuse to discuss the report at all, because privacy rules bar giving results to patients
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA puts interpretation on the far side of the bench: reference intervals go to the authorized person who ordered the test and to whoever is responsible for using the results, and results themselves are released only to those people. Refusing outright is wrong for a different reason, since a patient may request access to her own completed report.

preguntas.pregunta: What does one small square on the grid stand for on the time axis?

0.02 seconds, and five of them make one large square
0.20 seconds, and five of them make one large square
0.10 seconds, and five of them make one large square
preguntas.explicacion: Each large square is divided into five small ones, so a small square is worth 0.04 seconds. That is the unit used to measure the waves: a PR interval of three to five small squares is normal, and a Q wave wider than a single small square is one of the signs of an old infarct.

Explain the anatomy behind each step in order
Promise the child that it will not hurt at all
Offer the choice of skipping the step for today
preguntas.explicacion: With children, speak calmly and gently, and demonstrating what will be done on a doll or stuffed animal helps; play and drawing build trust. 'Venipuncture' rather than 'blood draw'

A diagnosis made once symptoms pass the one-month mark
A stress reaction that resolves within a few weeks
A reaction seen only in children under eighteen

A brief history of surgery and of iodine contrast allergy
The time of the last meal and of the last cigarette
The results of the last two tracings held on file

Keep the same gloves through the batch to save supplies, but disinfect the counter every hour
Read all cassettes together once the last one has run, so that every result is interpreted at once
Report every negative antigen result to the state health department within 24 hours of testing
preguntas.explicacion: For SARS-CoV-2 testing at the point of care, the guidance calls for new gloves for each person tested, a change of gloves between specimens when processing in batches to avoid cross-contamination, instructions followed in their stated order, results read only within the manufacturer's time frame, and instruments decontaminated after each use. preguntas.pregunta: An automated CBC on an EDTA sample reports a platelet count of 90,000/µL with a platelet-clump flag, in a patient with no bleeding. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: EDTA-induced platelet clumping has produced a spuriously low count (pseudothrombocytopenia)
True thrombocytopenia, which at this level carries a high risk of spontaneous major bleeding
The clumps were counted as red cells, so the RBC count is falsely high and the platelets truly low
The sample was collected in a citrate tube, which dilutes the platelets by about 10 % in every case
preguntas.explicacion: The adult platelet reference interval is 150,000 to 400,000/µL. Platelet counts may appear low because platelets clump in the presence of the EDTA in the collection tube, causing pseudothrombocytopenia, and clumped platelets can be counted as white cells by the analyzer. Major bleeding is unusual unless platelets fall below 50,000/µL, and the risk of spontaneous major bleeding rises sharply below 20,000/µL. Any abnormality is checked against interfering factors, often with a blood smear.

At least 40 percent of the questions asked
At least 50 percent of the questions asked
At least 90 percent of the questions asked

preguntas.pregunta: Which preanalytical problem is the leading cause of test or sample rejection in clinical laboratories, and how large is it?
opciones: In vitro hemolysis, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
Clotted samples, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
In vivo hemolysis, present in about 2 % of routine samples and most rejected specimens
Insufficient volume, up to 22 % of routine samples and the majority of unsuitable specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis was recognised as the most frequent preanalytical error, and in vitro hemolysis is the leading cause of rejection: it can reach 3.3 % of all routine samples and accounts for 40 to 70 % of unsuitable specimens, close to five times more than other causes such as incorrect or clotted samples. Fewer than 2 % of samples with detectable hemolysis are hemolysed in vivo, so the problem is created during collection and transport.

Insulin is prescribed in millilitres, and only an insulin syringe converts them
Insulin syringes carry a filter that keeps particles out of the dose drawn up
Insulin syringes carry a longer needle that reaches the muscle under the fat
preguntas.explicacion: Providers prescribe insulin in units rather than millilitres, and an insulin syringe is calibrated in units, so a syringe marked in millilitres must never be used for it. A filter belongs to the blunt fill needle used with an ampule, and insulin is given into subcutaneous tissue, not into muscle.

Pays the claims that providers submit for the enrolled members
Sets the fee schedule that every insurer in a state has to use
Certifies the providers a health plan may place in its network

Having a second staff member read it aloud and correct the punctuation

Rewriting it at the reading level printed on the practice's own website

Walk the patient slowly to a couch and give a full glass of cold water
Lay the patient flat with the legs raised and start chest compressions
Wait for the provider to see the patient before any call is made out

Bedside reports had lowered satisfaction where they were tried
A handoff had to be in writing before it counted as complete
Handoff tools other than the preferred one were unacceptable

Yes, because sending e-mail to patients is itself an electronic transmission of health information
Yes, because every provider of medical services is a covered entity regardless of how claims go out
No, because only hospitals and health plans are ever treated as covered entities under the rules
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of organization are covered: health plans, clearinghouses, and any provider, of any size, that transmits health information electronically in a transaction for which HHS adopted a standard, such as a claim or an eligibility inquiry. Nocturia alone, which is what the instrument is designed to investigate
Flank pain alone, since the scope reaches the kidney through the ureter

The physician must be present in the office whenever the patient is being seen

The physician must employ the nurse practitioner and bill the services directly

Situational reflex syncope
Carotid sinus syncope

preguntas.pregunta: Which sequence correctly describes the oral glucose tolerance test?
opciones: Fasting sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample at 2 hours
Fasting sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample at 1 hour
Random sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample drawn at 2 hours
Fasting sample, 150 g of carbohydrate, and a sample at 3 hours

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's reading is 134/84 mm Hg on two separate visits. Which category does that fall in?
opciones: Stage 1 high blood pressure: 130 to 139 systolic or 80 to 89 diastolic
Elevated blood pressure: 120 to 129 systolic together with under 80 diastolic
Stage 2 high blood pressure: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
Normal blood pressure, because the diastolic value has stayed under 85 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: The bands are normal under 120 and under 80; elevated at 120 to 129 with a diastolic under 80; stage 1 at 130 to 139 or 80 to 89; stage 2 at 140 or more or 90 or more; and crisis above 180 or above 120. preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA sample for an ESR was collected three hours ago and has just reached the bench. What should the technician expect?
opciones: The ESR may read falsely low, because testing should begin within 2 hours before the red cells lose their biconcave shape
The ESR may read falsely high, because red cells clump into larger rouleaux the longer the sample stands at room temperature
The result is acceptable, because whole blood for an ESR is stable for 24 hours at room temperature or at 4 °C
The result is acceptable only if the sample is transferred to a black-top citrate tube before the test is set up
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for an ESR is collected in a black-top citrate tube or an EDTA lavender tube, and testing should be initiated within 2 hours of collection. Delays cause red cells to lose their biconcave shape, which reduces the sedimentation rate, and clotted blood also lowers it by disrupting rouleaux. The 24-hour window belongs to prothrombin time samples, not the ESR. Reference values are 15 mm/hr or lower for men and 20 or lower for women under 50.
