preguntas.pregunta: OSHA requires that contaminated sharps be discarded into containers with which combination of features?
opciones: Closable, puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom, and labeled or color-coded
Closable, leakproof and labeled or color-coded, with no requirement at all to resist punctures
Fluorescent orange-red with the biohazard symbol, and emptied by hand when it is three-quarters full
Puncture resistant and leakproof on sides and bottom, but left open during use to speed up disposal
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A) lists four features for the container that receives contaminated sharps: it closes, it resists punctures, it does not leak through the sides or the bottom, and it carries the biohazard label or the color code the standard prescribes. While in use it also has to be easy to reach, kept upright, and replaced before it overfills. A container without puncture resistance is the description of a regulated-waste bag in (d)(4)(iii)(B), not a sharps container; reusable sharps containers must never be opened or emptied by hand; and a container left open during use fails the first requirement.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a normal oximeter reading treated with caution in a patient with darker skin?

Devices may underestimate saturation by about 2%, prompting oxygen that is not needed
Devices cannot read at all through darker skin, so a blood gas replaces the test
Devices need a longer sampling time, and a short reading is the one that runs high

preguntas.pregunta: After lancing a fingertip for a glucometer reading, which drop is applied to the test strip?
opciones: The second drop, after the first is wiped away with clean gauze
The first drop, before any tissue fluid has time to mix with it
The third drop, after two drops are wiped to clear the alcohol
Any drop, provided gentle pressure was applied before the puncture
preguntas.explicacion: The operator wipes away the first drop with clean gauze or tissue, because it may contain intracellular or interstitial fluid or be hemolysed, then apply gentle pressure near the site to form a second drop, which is touched to the tip of the strip. Some meters detect an insufficient sample and allow more blood on the same strip. The same first-drop rule applies to all skin punctures.

preguntas.pregunta: Put the levels of organization in order from the simplest to the most complex.
opciones: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
Tissue, cell, organ system, organ, organism
Cell, organ, tissue, organism, organ system
Organ, cell, tissue, organ system, organism
preguntas.explicacion: The cell is the smallest unit that can function on its own. A group of similar cells working together makes a tissue; two or more tissue types build an organ; organs that share a job make an organ system; and the systems together make the organism. Below the cell sit the chemical levels of atoms and molecules.

preguntas.pregunta: What does medication reconciliation involve, and how often is it done?
opciones: Comparing the current medication list with the previous one, at every clinic visit and admission
Removing from the list any drug the patient says was stopped more than a year ago
Listing the prescribed drugs only, because the supplements are recorded in another section of the chart
Recording the dose and the route of the drugs that are given during today's visit
preguntas.explicacion: Reconciliation sets the list the patient is taking now against the list already on file, and it is repeated at each hospitalization and each clinic visit. Done consistently it prevents errors, keeps polypharmacy from creeping in and surfaces interactions. Prescriptions, over-the-counter products, vitamins and herbal supplements all belong on the same list.

A key part is broken skin or an insertion point; a key site is a sterile piece of equipment
A key part is the sterile field itself; a key site is the room where the procedure happens
A key part is the practitioner's gloved hand; a key site is the tray holding the supplies
preguntas.explicacion: Key parts are the sterile pieces handled during the procedure, such as needle hubs, syringe tips, needles and dressings. No information may be disclosed without a court order, not even the name
The full record may be disclosed, since law enforcement requests override the Privacy Rule
Only the results of body fluid analyses may be disclosed, not the address

Up to 50%
Up to 20%
Up to 65%

preguntas.pregunta: Feeling behind a patient's medial malleolus you find a firm cord and cannot tell whether it is the artery or a tendon. Which observation separates them?
opciones: A tendon slides under the fingertips, while an artery stays in place
A tendon feels warmer to the finger pad than the artery beside it
A tendon lies deeper, so far heavier pressure is needed to reach it
A tendon crosses the ankle, while the artery runs along its length
preguntas.explicacion: Firm cords sit next to most pulse points, and rolling the structure under the fingertips tells them apart: tendons move, arteries hold still. Two other habits help when a pulse will not come up, warming the limb and letting the patient relax. Too much pressure flattens a weak pulse and too light a touch misses it, so the force is adjusted, not fixed.

Medicaid's, since it is the payer of last resort in every recovery situation
Medicaid's, since state law settles the order in which recoveries are applied
Neither one's; the two divide the recovery in proportion to what each paid out
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare may recover incorrect payments directly from a primary payer, another entity or a third payer, and its right to recover takes priority over any other party's, Medicaid included. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the Physician Self-Referral Law described as a strict liability statute?

Proof of a financial relationship is not required for it to be violated
Penalties are limited to repaying the amount the program overpaid
It applies only when the physician owns the entity outright, not in part
preguntas.explicacion: The Stark law bars a physician from referring designated health services payable by Medicare to an entity with which the physician or an immediate family member has a financial relationship, unless an exception applies, and it forbids the entity from billing for those referrals. It chelates calcium ions, the same mechanism the citrate tube uses
It preserves the viability of microorganisms in a broth mixture
It works as an antiglycolytic agent that keeps glucose stable for days

The risk manager, once the chart has been reviewed for the week

The office manager, who collects the accounts of everyone involved

preguntas.pregunta: Which definition matches an adverse drug reaction?
opciones: A noxious, unintended response at doses normally used for treatment
Any untoward medical occurrence at all during treatment with a product
A predictable effect other than the principal one the drug was used for
A reaction that follows only when more than the prescribed dose is taken
preguntas.explicacion: The definition used by the WHO and the FDA is a response to a drug that is noxious and unintended and that happens at doses normally used for prophylaxis, diagnosis or therapy, or for modifying a physiologic function. An adverse drug event is the broader term: any untoward occurrence during treatment, which need not be caused by the drug. A cotton tip on a wooden shaft, the classic bacterial culture swab
A calcium alginate tip on an aluminum or plastic shaft
A cotton tip on an aluminum shaft, moistened with saline

The median antebrachial vein and the median basilic vein

The accessory cephalic vein and the perforating basilic vein

Passive, active, and weight bearing

About 2 cm above the site, the width of the area the swab must cover
About four to five finger widths below the site, so the vein fills from the hand
Right over the median cubital vein, with the thumb anchoring just below it

preguntas.pregunta: What does psychological safety mean in a clinical team?

The shared picture of the plan that every member carries
The habit of watching the stress levels of other members
The readiness to take over work when a colleague falls behind

Voice the concern openly so the patient has a chance to correct the record
Skip the fasting question, since the answer is already predictable
Document the impression in the chart as a compliance risk factor

About 100 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one
About 75 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one
About 225 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads high in the office every time but normal on a home monitor. What is this called?
opciones: White-coat hypertension, where the clinical setting itself lifts the reading
Masked hypertension, where the office reading hides pressures that are high elsewhere
An auscultatory gap, where the sounds vanish and reappear during deflation
Pseudohypotension, where a stiff artery makes the cuff read below the true value
preguntas.explicacion: A transient rise brought on by being in the clinic is white-coat hypertension, and as many as one in three people with a high office reading are normal outside it. preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial was first punctured on March 1 and the manufacturer gives no date for opened vials. Under USP 797 as cited by the CDC, by when should it be discarded?
opciones: Within 28 days of opening, and never past the manufacturer's expiration date
Within 7 days of opening, the limit for single-dose vials kept for the same patient
Within 72 hours of opening, unless it is kept in a clean medication area
On the manufacturer's expiration date, regardless of when it was opened
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC cites USP General Chapter 797: once a multi-dose vial is opened or needle-punctured it should be dated and discarded within 28 days unless the manufacturer states another date for the opened vial, and the beyond-use date may never exceed the original expiration date. preguntas.pregunta: The heavy utility gloves kept in the draw room for cleaning spills are cracked and peeling. What does the standard say?
opciones: Discard them: utility gloves are reused only while their integrity holds up
Wash and reuse them, since only single-use gloves are barred from reuse
Reuse them for handling contaminated laundry, where no barrier is needed
Keep them until the yearly review of the written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(C) is the only place the standard allows a glove to be decontaminated and used again, and it puts a condition on it: the glove's integrity has to be intact. preguntas.pregunta: What makes an adverse event a negligent adverse event?

The management was unusual enough that the accrediting body reviewed it
The harm lasted long enough to prolong the patient's hospital admission
The harm was avoidable, whether or not the care met the usual standard

Legal negligence is the failure of an average qualified health worker to meet the standard of care reasonably expected for a patient in similar circumstances, so a negligent adverse event is one where the management was substandard enough to meet that legal test and the patient was harmed. Intentional torts, criminal torts and administrative torts
Negligent torts, contractual torts and statutory torts
Negligent torts, punitive torts and constitutional torts

Heel of one hand high on the sternum, between the two collarbones

preguntas.pregunta: Occupational hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers fell sharply after the 1980s. What is that credited to?
opciones: Wide vaccination of workers plus universal precautions and the OSHA standard
The arrival of immune globulin as a treatment for chronic hepatitis B
The switch from glass to plastic tubes in blood collection systems
The end of the use of hollow-bore needles for drawing blood samples
preguntas.explicacion: Surveillance figures put roughly 17,000 new hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers in 1983 and an estimated 800 in 1995, a decline of about 95 percent. Immune globulin is post-exposure prophylaxis, not a treatment for chronic infection, and hollow-bore needles are still in daily use.

preguntas.pregunta: Where do the initials, date and time go when a new medication patch is applied?

Directly on the patch itself, with a fine marker, before it is pressed onto the skin
On the clear plastic backing, which is left attached to one corner of the new patch
On the patient's wristband, beside the two identifiers checked before the dose given
preguntas.explicacion: Writing on a patch can puncture it and make it ineffective, so the initials, date and time go on a strip of tape stuck near it. Physical and sexual abuse, plus self-neglect and guardianship error

Compromising, trading concessions for a middle ground
Accommodating, yielding in order to save the relationship
Competing, pursuing one's position at the other's expense

preguntas.pregunta: A urine culture report reads 100,000 CFU/mL of a single organism. How is that count usually interpreted?
opciones: As significant bacteriuria, the cut-off most laboratories use for urinary tract infection
As a contaminant, since only counts above 1,000,000 CFU/mL are considered significant
As colonization, the term for bacteria in the urine of any patient without a catheter
As catheter-associated infection, which requires at least 1,000 CFU/mL and symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Although not fully standardized, most laboratories set the threshold for a positive culture at 100,000 CFU/mL or more, while accepting that this may miss some real infections. With a request for a referral to a mental health clinic
With a completed screening questionnaire already filled
With a documented family history of a mood disorder

Six, with a seventh and eighth added by students
Five, with the rest carried over from Freud's work

preguntas.pregunta: A patient started an antibiotic yesterday and now gives a urine for culture. What should be documented, and why?

The antibiotic, because it can cause a false-positive culture
The time of the last void, because a culture needs urine held 8 hours
The antibiotic, because it turns the urine alkaline and lyses the cells
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics already on board can suppress growth and give a false-negative urine culture, so the medication is recorded for the laboratory and the provider. About 25 ms, travelling along the internodal pathways
About 225 ms, travelling along the internodal pathways

Acute otitis media, a sudden focal neurological deficit
A transient rise in blood pressure with no neurological deficit
A migraine headache, which produces no focal neurological deficit

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who takes warfarin has a point-of-care INR of 1.5. What does this value indicate?
opciones: It is below the usual therapeutic target of 2.0 to 3.0, so the patient may be at risk of forming a clot
It is above the usual therapeutic target of 0.8 to 1.1, so the patient may be at risk of serious bleeding
It is within the usual therapeutic target of 1.0 to 2.0, so no change in the warfarin dose is expected
It is a normal value for someone who is not on anticoagulants, so the warfarin can be discontinued
preguntas.explicacion: For a person not taking anticoagulants the PT is about 11 to 13.5 seconds and the INR 0.8 to 1.1. For most patients on warfarin the provider aims to keep the INR between 2.0 and 3.0: results above 3.0 carry a higher bleeding risk, while results below 2.0 may leave the patient at risk of developing a blood clot. At initial assignment and at least annually thereafter, within one year of the last session
Once, at hire, with a written test kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years

preguntas.pregunta: After centrifugation, the serum in a red-top tube shows fibrin strands floating above the gel. What is the most probable cause?
opciones: The tube was centrifuged before the blood had finished clotting
The tube was left at room temperature for too long before being spun
The tube was drawn through an intravenous catheter during an IV start
The tube was inverted too many times right after it was collected
preguntas.explicacion: Blood must be allowed to clot before serum is processed; the high rate of fibrin-containing samples in the emergency laboratory was linked to the short interval between collection and centrifugation, on average about 10 minutes. A, for alleviating and aggravating factors that change it

Section 2, Hazard Identification and signal word
Section 8, Exposure Controls and Personal Protection

Applying a second tourniquet below the first to raise the pressure
Drawing with a syringe, which tolerates a longer tourniquet time
Switching to a 16 to 18 gauge needle so the tubes fill faster

Repeat it every six years, when the documentation is renewed

preguntas.pregunta: What happens in the body during the first seconds after a patient stands up?
opciones: Roughly 300 to 800 mL of blood pools in the legs, and sympathetic tone compensates
Roughly 50 to 100 mL of blood pools in the legs, and the heart rate alone compensates
Blood is pushed out of the legs toward the chest, and the vessels there must dilate
Cardiac output rises at once, and the baroreceptors then bring the pressure back down
preguntas.explicacion: Standing lets 300 to 800 mL of blood pool in the lower limbs, so venous return and cardiac output fall. preguntas.pregunta: A patient started on metoprolol reports that the resting pulse is slower than before. Which action of this drug class explains the change?

Blockade of beta-2 receptors, which relaxes the smooth muscle of the airways
Competitive inhibition of the enzyme that turns angiotensin I into angiotensin II
Blockade of the sodium-chloride channel in the distal convoluted tubule

preguntas.explicacion: The hypodermic needle and syringe is listed as widely available, the least expensive option, supplied in a wide range of lengths and gauges, and usable without special training. What it does not avoid is the transfer of blood into tubes, which is where its needle-stick risk comes from.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices

preguntas.pregunta: How does capillary blood compare with venous blood, and what limits its use?
opciones: Similar to arterial blood in oxygen content; limited by skin flora contamination and small volume
Similar to venous blood in every analyte; limited only by the pain of the puncture
Similar to arterial blood in oxygen content; limited by its high platelet count
Poorer in oxygen than venous blood; limited by dilution with tissue fluid in every sample
preguntas.explicacion: Blood from a capillary specimen is similar to an arterial specimen in oxygen content and is suitable for only a limited number of tests because of its higher likelihood of contamination with skin flora and its smaller total volume. Dilution with tissue fluid is a consequence of squeezing, not as a property of every capillary sample.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.1.1 Choice of procedure and site

preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops hives and wheezing minutes after a vaccination and an epinephrine autoinjector is used. How is the device handled?
opciones: Held around the middle, pressed against the outer thigh, kept there 5 seconds
Held by both ends, pressed against the upper arm, kept there for 30 seconds
Held around the middle, pressed against the abdomen, kept there for 1 minute
Held by the orange tip, pressed against the outer thigh, kept there 10 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The device is grasped around its middle, never over the ends, because a hand over the tip can fire the needle into the rescuer. The blue cap comes off, the orange tip is pressed firmly against the mid outer thigh until a click is heard, and it is held there at least 5 seconds; afterward the needle is covered by that tip and the unit is discarded.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Safe and Effective Administration of Vaccines and Epinephrine Autoinjection", Complications

preguntas.pregunta: An out-of-network provider charges $200 and the plan's allowed amount is $110. Beyond her cost sharing, what may he bill the patient?
opciones: Ninety dollars, the gap between what he charged and what the plan allows
A hundred and ten dollars, since the plan pays that sum straight to him
Twenty-two dollars, being twenty percent of the amount the plan allowed
Two hundred dollars, the whole charge, since no contract binds him to the plan
preguntas.explicacion: Balance billing is when a provider bills the patient for the balance the plan does not cover, meaning the difference between the amount actually billed and the allowed amount. The uniform glossary uses these figures as its example. It happens most often with out-of-network providers; a network provider may not balance bill for covered services.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Balance Billing

preguntas.pregunta: A very icteric sample and a very lipemic one both give unusable point-of-care readings. Which remedies are described for each?
opciones: Dilution for the excess bilirubin, and ultracentrifugation for the excess lipid
Ultracentrifugation for the excess bilirubin, and dilution for the excess lipid
Warming for the excess bilirubin, and a longer spin for the excess lipid
Dilution for both, since neither pigment nor lipid can be spun out of a sample
preguntas.explicacion: How such errors are handled depends on the device and the manufacturer's instructions, but two routes are named: dilution can resolve sample errors caused by excess bilirubin, and ultracentrifugation can clear those caused by excess lipid. At the point of care these three interferences can only be spotted by looking at a centrifuged aliquot, not measured as an index.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: An agitated patient is taken to a safe assessment room. What has been reported about those rooms?
opciones: Most patients settle down there within about twenty minutes
Most patients there need physical restraint within the hour
They cut down verbal abuse but not physical aggression
They only help once an aggression team is already present
preguntas.explicacion: Safe assessment rooms improve the management of acutely agitated patients, and most of those patients calm down inside about twenty minutes. Taking a patient to an available room early is listed as an opportunity to diffuse tension that should be seized. Restraint is a last resort, not the expected outcome of the room.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is choosing a needle for a routine draw. On what basis is the gauge decided?
opciones: The one that fits the most prominent vein with little discomfort
The widest one the tray holds, so the tubes fill more quickly
The finest one the tray holds, so the puncture hurts far less
The one that matches the colour of the stopper being filled
preguntas.explicacion: The gauge chosen is the one that fits comfortably into the most prominent vein while causing little discomfort. Going too wide tears the vein and bleeds into the tissue; going too fine damages the blood cells, which invalidates tests that need whole cells or free haemoglobin.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 3.1.1 and 3.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count reports a hemoglobin below the reference value for the patient. Which term names that finding?
opciones: Anemia, a reduction in the circulating red blood cell mass
Leukemia, a reduction in the circulating red blood cell mass
Polycythemia, a reduction in the circulating red blood cell mass
Hemophilia, a reduction in the circulating red blood cell mass
preguntas.explicacion: Anemia is a fall in circulating red cell mass, seen as a lower hemoglobin, hematocrit or red cell count. It is a finding rather than a diagnosis, and the causes range widely: nutritional deficiency, inflammation, chronic kidney disease, hemolysis, blood loss, marrow failure, pregnancy and inherited hemoglobin disorders.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anemia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10

preguntas.pregunta: A patient had a radical mastectomy on the left side two years ago. Where should the blood be drawn?
opciones: From the right arm; a history of ipsilateral radical mastectomy contraindicates the left
From the left arm, provided the tourniquet stays on for less than one minute
From either arm, since the contraindication applies only during the first six months after surgery
From the left hand only, below the level of the surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Among the site-specific contraindications, the phlebotomy chapter lists a history of radical mastectomy on the same side, alongside scar tissue, cellulitis or abscess, a vascular graft, a hematoma, venous fibrosis on palpation and any venous access device. The chapter sets no time limit after which the arm becomes acceptable and no exception for the hand or for a short tourniquet time.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: Which picture on the tracing goes with dextrocardia?
opciones: Right axis deviation with all complexes inverted in lead I
Left axis deviation with all complexes inverted in lead I
Right axis deviation with all complexes inverted in lead II
Right axis deviation with the R wave growing from V1 to V6
preguntas.explicacion: A heart sitting on the right side of the chest shows right axis deviation, inversion of every complex in lead I, an upright P wave in the augmented left lead, and an R wave that never builds up across the anterior chest leads.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dextrocardia", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k151 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.2

preguntas.pregunta: How are contaminated sterile gloves removed at the end of a procedure?
opciones: Grasp the outside of one cuff, peel it off inside out, then use a bare finger inside the other cuff
Grasp the inside of one cuff, peel it off inside out, then use a gloved thumb under the other cuff
Grasp both cuffs at once and pull the gloves off together so no skin contacts either outer surface
Grasp the fingertips of one glove, pull it halfway off, then push the second glove off against it
preguntas.explicacion: The first glove is taken by its outside cuff with the other gloved hand, avoiding skin, and pulled off inside out into the palm of the hand still gloved. The bare index finger then tucks inside the remaining cuff and peels that glove off inside out and over the first. Waste is discarded appropriately and hand hygiene follows.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.8 Checklist for Applying and Removing Sterile Gloves

preguntas.pregunta: An FDA-cleared label for high-level disinfection with more than 2% glutaraldehyde at 25 °C sets what range of exposure?
opciones: 20 to 90 minutes, depending on the product
5 to 12 minutes, depending on the product
3 to 10 hours, depending on the product
90 to 180 minutes, depending on the product
preguntas.explicacion: Federal rules require the FDA-cleared label claim to be followed, and for glutaraldehyde above 2 percent at 25 °C those claims run from 20 to 90 minutes. Some other products carry shorter claims, such as 12 minutes for a 0.55 percent ortho-phthalaldehyde at 20 °C. The hours-long exposures belong to the chemical sterilants, where spores are the target.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations 10o: High-Level Disinfection
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k103 · CMA 2027 I.C.5.b(3) · RMA III.A.4

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the wide variation in the superficial veins of the elbow a practical concern?
opciones: Mispuncture has caused bruising, haematoma, altered sensation
Mispuncture makes the tourniquet slip below the level of the vein
Variation changes which tubes may be filled from a single puncture
Variation means the median cubital vein is absent in most patients
preguntas.explicacion: Because the pattern differs so much from patient to patient, adverse effects from puncturing the wrong vessel have been reported across health systems: bruising, haematoma and sensory changes. That variation is the argument put forward for using an illuminator to see the vein first.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8

preguntas.pregunta: What is a taper needle for?
opciones: Soft delicate tissue and tendon repair, where it spreads tissue instead of cutting it
Tough dermal tissue and scalp repair, where a rounded tip resists bending under force
Skin closure in cosmetic areas, where three sharp edges leave the finest entry point
Ligament repair and fascia, where the three cutting edges pierce the densest structures
preguntas.explicacion: Taper needles are rounded rather than edged, and can be sharp or blunt. They pierce tissue by spreading it apart as they pass rather than cutting it, which makes them suitable for soft, delicate tissue and for tendon repair. The needles with three sharp cutting edges are the cutting and reverse cutting types, which are what skin usually gets.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k75 · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches primary care?
opciones: A range of prevention, wellness and treatment for common illnesses
Care focused on one area of medicine or on one group of patients
Care for an injury serious enough that a person seeks it at once
Care given after admission to a hospital or a nursing facility
preguntas.explicacion: Primary care covers a range of prevention, wellness and treatment for common illnesses. Primary care providers include doctors, nurses, nurse practitioners and physician assistants. They often keep a long-term relationship with the patient, advise and treat on many health issues, and may coordinate the patient's care with specialists.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Primary care
preguntas.subtema: General vs specialty care · CCMA 1A k7

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen sat uncovered on a sunlit counter for three hours before testing. Which two analytes are most likely to have broken down?
opciones: Bilirubin and urobilinogen
Glucose and ketone bodies
Protein and nitrite
Leukocyte esterase and blood
preguntas.explicacion: Bilirubin and urobilinogen are unstable in light and warmth and decompose when a specimen is left exposed, which is why light-sensitive analytes travel in amber containers. Prolonged daylight is also listed among the causes of a false-negative urobilinogen. Room temperature adds a second problem, since it favors the growth of bacteria, which can falsify the blood reaction and shift the pH of the sample.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Interfering Factors; and PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Which sampling container is preferable?
preguntas.subtema: Light exposure · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · NCMA 2C.15

preguntas.pregunta: At the end of a 24-hour urine collection, what does the laboratory do before analysis?
opciones: Records the total volume and submits a representative sample of the pooled urine
Discards the first and last voids and analyzes the pooled urine in between
Divides the urine into three numbered tubes for chemistry, culture and cytology
Records the collection time and refrigerates the whole volume for 24 hours before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Once the full period is over, the total volume is measured and written down, and a representative portion of the mixed urine is sent for analysis; the daily excretion is calculated from that volume. The first void of day one is the only one discarded, and the closing void is kept. Three numbered tubes are the cerebrospinal fluid routine. If a full day is not feasible, a shorter timed collection can be used provided the exact time is recorded.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "24-Hour Urine Collection", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: 24-hour volume and aliquot · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.i

preguntas.pregunta: What is the Medication Administration Record used for?
opciones: It is the chart record the dose is matched against and documented on
It is the pharmacy's own file of what was dispensed to the department
It is the list of every drug the facility keeps in stock, by strength
It is the form on which an error is reported to the safety committee
preguntas.explicacion: The Medication Administration Record, or the electronic version, is a specific kind of documentation inside the patient's chart. Checking the right drug means confirming that what is about to be given matches the order or the record and that no allergy to it is documented. Documentation is itself the sixth right, and administering a medication is not finished until it is recorded.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Right Drug and Rights of Medication Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B7 k71 · CMA I.D.2.e(1)

preguntas.pregunta: Which hematocrit value falls within the usual reference range for an adult woman?
preguntas.explicacion: Common adult reference values are about 37 to 48 % for men and 34 to 43 % for women, so 38 % sits inside the female range. A value of 30 % is below it and would fit anemia, 52 % exceeds even the male range, and 45 to 61 % is the range quoted for newborns, whose hematocrit is high and falls during the neonatal period. Ranges vary slightly between laboratories.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Hematocrit (003646), Normal Results; StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: Which form of workplace violence is reported most often in health care?
opciones: Verbal abuse, more common than physical assault
Physical abuse, reported by nearly all the staff
Sexual harassment, the most reported form overall
Property damage, which precedes the other forms
preguntas.explicacion: Violence is divided by the nature of the aggression into physical, verbal and psychological, and psychological forms include sexual harassment, bullying and intimidation. In the professional environment verbal abuse is the most common form. Nearly twenty percent of health care workers have met with physical abuse.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction; and Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16

preguntas.pregunta: The requisition reads 'Maria Lopez, DOB 03/14/1961'; the wristband reads 03/14/1967. The patient confirms her name. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Defer the blood sampling until the discrepancy has been resolved
Proceed, since the name matched and the date of birth is secondary
Draw the sample now and have the wristband corrected afterwards
Ask the patient which date is right and correct the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Before any blood is withdrawn, the identification data and the tube labelling are double-checked, and if any discrepancy appears among those data the sampling is deferred until the issue is resolved. A matching name does not cancel a mismatched date of birth, and the phlebotomist does not settle the conflict by editing the paperwork on the spot.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2E k41 · PBT II.A II.C · CCMA 3E2 k124 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: What does a valproate level mainly reflect, given the short half-life of that drug?
opciones: Short-term compliance, which makes the measurement low-yield
Long-term usage across the preceding weeks of treatment
The unbound fraction, untouched by any change in protein binding
The risk of a breakthrough seizure over the coming month
preguntas.explicacion: Valproate has a short half-life, which makes measuring it low-yield and primarily a reflection of short-term compliance. Phenytoin, with its long half-life, gives a level that reflects long-term usage instead. Free levels, not total levels, are what show the unbound and pharmacologically active fraction when protein binding has been altered.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Issues of Concern, Variability in Antiseizure Medication Levels; and section Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these therapists enters the occupation with a doctoral degree?
opciones: The physical therapist, who needs a Doctor of Physical Therapy degree
The occupational therapist, who needs a doctorate in occupational therapy
The speech-language pathologist, who needs a doctorate in the specialty
The respiratory therapist, who needs a doctorate in respiratory therapy
preguntas.explicacion: Physical therapists entering the occupation need a Doctor of Physical Therapy degree, and all states require them to be licensed. Occupational therapists typically need a master's degree and are also licensed in all states. Speech-language pathologists are licensed everywhere and typically need at least a master's plus supervised clinical experience and an exam.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Physical Therapists, Occupational Therapists and Speech-Language Pathologists — How to Become One
preguntas.subtema: Allied health roles · CCMA 1A k2

preguntas.pregunta: In the counted brush stroke surgical scrub, how many strokes does each finger receive?
opciones: Forty, since each finger is treated as four sides at ten strokes apiece
Thirty, since each finger is treated as three sides at ten strokes apiece
Twenty, since each finger is treated as two sides at ten strokes apiece
Sixty, since each finger is treated as four sides at fifteen strokes apiece
preguntas.explicacion: Each finger is divided into four sides and each side gets ten strokes, which totals forty per finger. The nails and cuticles come first, thirty strokes in a circular motion across the top of the nails; the palm then takes thirty and the back of the hand thirty. Only after both hands and arms are done does the rinsing start.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.A.3.b(i) y III.D.2.c

preguntas.pregunta: Dried blood spot cards and dry buccal swabs are left in an outdoor specimen lock box for pickup, and the courier is delayed on a humid day. What is the concern?
opciones: High humidity compromises dried specimens kept at ambient conditions, degrading nucleic acids and inviting microbial growth
High humidity rehydrates the dried specimens, so the volume recovered falls below the minimum the assay requires
High humidity matters only for the buccal swabs; dried blood spots stay stable under any ambient conditions
High humidity fixes the dried specimens in place, so they must be soaked in transport medium before extraction
preguntas.explicacion: Dry oral and buccal swabs and dried blood spots kept under ambient conditions are the sample types that high humidity compromises: viral and microbial nucleic acids degrade during prolonged storage, water contributes to reactive oxygen species that break down DNA, and humid conditions make the specimens prone to fungal and bacterial contamination. The scenario given for this variable is a delayed pickup from an uninsulated lock box; when storage cannot be controlled, those sample types are avoided or validated first.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 1 and section 4.2 Humidity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E14 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which record is exempt from the long retention period of the OSHA access standard?
opciones: A one-time treatment of a minor cut, if it is kept apart from the medical program
A record of exposure monitoring, once the substance is no longer used in the office
A record belonging to an employee who has left, once the final pay has been issued
A safety data sheet, once the product it describes has been taken off the shelves
preguntas.explicacion: The employee medical record is preserved for the length of employment plus thirty years, with narrow exceptions: health insurance claim files kept separately, first aid records of one-time treatment of minor injuries made on site by a non-physician and kept separately, and the records of employees who worked under a year if handed to them on leaving.
preguntas.subtema: Retention exceptions · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4

preguntas.pregunta: A 17-year-old on active military duty arrives alone for a drug level. Who consents to the draw?
opciones: The minor himself, since active-duty status makes him an emancipated minor
A parent reached by telephone, because he is still younger than eighteen years
The ordering clinician, invoking the emergency exception under EMTALA
A parent, because emancipation applies only to minors who are married
preguntas.explicacion: Minors who are married, on active military duty, or living apart from their parents and managing their own finances are generally considered emancipated, and emancipated minors can consent to or refuse care without parental permission or notification. EMTALA's emergency exception is a different route, for emergency conditions, not for a routine level.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must appear on every prescription for a controlled substance?
opciones: Full name and address of the patient, drug, strength, form, quantity and directions
Full name and insurance plan of the patient, drug, strength and treating diagnosis
Full name and date of birth of the patient, drug, and the number of refills allowed
Full name and address of the patient, drug, and the pharmacy chosen to dispense it
preguntas.explicacion: A prescription for a controlled substance is dated as of and signed on the day it is issued, and it carries the patient's full name and address, the drug name, the strength, the dosage form, the quantity prescribed and the directions for use, along with the name, address and registration number of the practitioner. The regulation says nothing about the payer or a diagnosis, and refills are governed separately by schedule.
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why she has to eat vitamin C foods every few days but not vitamin A. What explains the difference?
opciones: Water-soluble vitamins are not stored and leave in the urine
Water-soluble vitamins are stored in muscle and used up faster
Water-soluble vitamins are destroyed by stomach acid within hours
Water-soluble vitamins are absorbed only when dietary fat is present
preguntas.explicacion: The nine water-soluble vitamins, vitamin C and the whole B complex, are not kept in the body; whatever is left over leaves in the urine, so they have to be eaten regularly to avoid a shortage. Vitamin B12 is the exception that can be held in the liver for years. Fat is what helps the fat-soluble group get absorbed.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Vitamins
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(e) · NCMA B.21

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks unsure who you are as you set out the tray. What does the guidance advise?
opciones: Explain again who you are and what you will be doing during the visit
Ask the caregiver to introduce you, then begin without further delay
Begin the draw quickly, since explanations add to the confusion
Postpone the draw until a family member is able to attend in person
preguntas.explicacion: Among the tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment: address the patient directly with simple wording and one idea at a time, and help orient them by explaining, or re-explaining, who you are and what you will be doing during the visit. The patient is also reassured that their answers are not being judged.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment, Tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6) · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: A policy states which programs may be run at the front desk computer, how they are to be used and how the desk is laid out. Which standard is that?
opciones: Workstation use, which sets the functions, the manner of use and the surroundings
Workstation security, the physical guard that limits a machine to authorized users
Access control, the technical limit on who may open which record in the system
Facility access controls, which limit physical entry to where the systems are kept
preguntas.explicacion: Two standards sit side by side. Workstation use asks for policies on the proper functions, the manner in which they are performed and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a workstation or class of workstation. Workstation security is narrower: the physical measures that keep an unauthorized person away from the machine.
preguntas.subtema: Workstation use · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient had to be moved from lying to sitting just before the draw. What should the phlebotomist do about it?
opciones: Record the change of position so the results can be interpreted
Cancel the draw and reschedule it for the following morning
Wait 2 minutes, then draw; no note is needed for a brief change
Return the patient to the supine position and draw at once
preguntas.explicacion: Position is meant to be maintained for at least 10 to 15 minutes before venipuncture; when a change cannot be avoided, it is documented so the laboratory results can be read in that light. The draw is not cancelled for that reason, two minutes is the WHO's tourniquet limit rather than a stabilization period, and drawing immediately after repositioning defeats the purpose.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a nasal spray administered?
opciones: The patient blows the nose, tilts the head back, and one nostril is held closed
The patient blows the nose, leans forward, and both nostrils are sprayed at once
The patient tilts the head back and the tip is pushed in until it meets the septum
The patient lies on one side and the spray goes into the upper nostril only
preguntas.explicacion: Nasal medication is used mostly for allergies, sinus infections and congestion, and clean technique is enough. Tissues are offered and the patient blows the nose, then sits or lies with the head tilted back, looking upward. The tip of the spray bottle or the dropper goes into one nostril while the other is occluded, and the spray is released as the patient breathes in. Gloves and the medication rights apply as always.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Nasal Instillation

preguntas.pregunta: How many bones are in the axial skeleton and how many in the appendicular skeleton?
opciones: 80 axial and 126 appendicular
126 axial and 80 appendicular
106 axial and 100 appendicular
60 axial and 146 appendicular
preguntas.explicacion: The skeleton splits in two. The axial part, with 80 bones, is the skull, hyoid, vertebral column and thoracic cage. The appendicular part, with 126, is the limbs plus the pectoral and pelvic girdles that anchor them. The two together give the adult total of 206.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice is shredding charts that state law no longer requires it to keep. Does the Privacy Rule have anything to say about that moment?
opciones: Yes, its safeguards run for as long as the information is held, disposal included
No, its safeguards end on the day the state retention period runs out for a chart
Yes, but only if the practice is destroying more than 500 records at one time
No, because destroying a record is a health care operation and needs no safeguard
preguntas.explicacion: HIPAA sets no retention period for the clinical record itself; state law does. What the Privacy Rule does require is appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards for whatever period the information is kept by the covered entity, and it names disposal as part of that period.

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the upper respiratory tract and which the lower?
opciones: Nose, pharynx and larynx above; trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, pharynx and trachea above; larynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose and pharynx above; larynx, trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, larynx and trachea above; pharynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting passages split into an upper tract of nose, pharynx and larynx and a lower tract of trachea, bronchial tree and lungs. Both open to the outside and are lined with mucous membrane, with hairs in some regions to filter the air and cilia in others to move mucus along.

preguntas.pregunta: An intensive care manager asks why the laboratory's improvement plan targets the medical units and not the surgical ones. What did the rejection audit show?
opciones: Non-surgical intensive care rejected about four times as many specimens as surgical
Surgical intensive care units rejected about four times as many specimens as medical ones
Neurology intensive care showed the lowest rejection ratio of all the intensive care units
Rejection ratios in intensive care matched those of the adult emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: Inside intensive care the split was wide: 40 % of the rejections came from non-surgical units and 10 % from surgical ones. Neurology intensive care was the worst single unit at 14 %, twice the internal medicine unit at 7 % and three times the surgical units at 4.5 %. That is why the training effort was pointed at the medical units rather than spread evenly.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood splashes into a phlebotomist's eye while she uncaps a tube. What is the first thing to do?
opciones: Irrigate the eye with clean water, saline or a sterile irrigant, then report the exposure
Apply an antiseptic eye drop, then complete the incident report before seeking care
Squeeze the eyelids shut and wait for the occupational health nurse to examine it
Flush with a dilute bleach solution, which inactivates bloodborne viruses on contact
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC and NIOSH give the same immediate steps: wash needlesticks and cuts with soap and water, flush splashes to the nose, mouth or skin with water, and irrigate eyes with clean water, saline or sterile irrigants; then report the exposure to the department that manages exposures and seek medical care right away. OSHA's laboratory guidance suggests irrigating eyes and mucous membranes for 15 minutes. The CDC adds that there is no evidence that antiseptics or squeezing reduce transmission and that caustic agents such as bleach are not recommended.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads her record and says one entry is wrong. What right does she have?
opciones: To ask for a correction, which the provider may accept or deny
To have the entry deleted within thirty days of the request
To have the entry rewritten by the clinician who made it
To bill the provider for the time spent finding the mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the rights the privacy rule gives are the right to a notice of privacy practices, to ask that disclosures be restricted, to say how information should be handled and communicated, to inspect and review one's own information and request a change to anything that looks wrong, to obtain a copy, to receive an accounting of disclosures, and to complain to the Office for Civil Rights. The request for a change is a request: the provider may accept or deny it, and a documented diagnosis a patient dislikes is not erased for that reason.

preguntas.pregunta: A newer machine shows muscle tremor that an older one never wrote. How is that read?
opciones: As an advantage: it also writes small P and Q waves
As a fault: the unit needs the biomedical engineer
As a fault: the standardization has drifted upward
As an advantage: it filters the tremor out by itself
preguntas.explicacion: Picking up the tremor is not a defect. A machine able to reproduce those small signals is also able to write the small P and Q waves that less accurate units have missed, so the answer is to settle the patient rather than to blame or replace the equipment.

preguntas.pregunta: Where is the mitral valve heard loudest during auscultation of the heart?
opciones: The 5th intercostal space on the left, at the midclavicular line
The 2nd right intercostal space beside the sternal border
The 2nd left intercostal space beside the sternal border
The 4th left intercostal space beside the sternal border
preguntas.explicacion: The four valve areas run in order: aortic in the 2nd right space, pulmonic in the 2nd left, tricuspid in the 4th left, and mitral in the 5th left at the midclavicular line. The first heart sound is the mitral and tricuspid valves closing in systole; the second is the aortic and pulmonic valves closing in diastole.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Heart Sounds", Related Testing

preguntas.pregunta: Which burn injuries are on the list of criteria for transfer to a burn center?
opciones: Burns of the face, hands, feet, genitalia or perineum, and any chemical burn
Burns of the trunk only, and any burn with blisters over a joint surface
Burns of the forearm and calf, and any burn that has not healed in 3 weeks
Burns of the scalp only, and any burn a patient cannot dress unaided
preguntas.explicacion: The burn association sets 10 transfer criteria, which take in burns of the face, hands, feet, genitalia and perineum, any full-thickness area, chemical and electrical burns, inhalation injury, and a total body surface area above 10 %. That surface can be figured with the rule of nines, the Lund-Browder chart or the rule of palms.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides the tests listed in the regulation itself, by which two routes does a test become waived?
opciones: FDA clearance for home use, or a manufacturer's waiver application with supporting data
State agency approval, or two years of acceptable proficiency testing at the site
A CMS inspection of the site, or accreditation by a CMS-approved organization
A Certificate of Registration, or categorization as PPM by the physician
preguntas.explicacion: Three doors lead to waived status: the tests named in 42 CFR 493.15(c), tests cleared or approved by the FDA for home use, and tests a manufacturer submits to the FDA with scientific data showing the waiver criteria are met (a CLIA Waiver by Application, for a test first categorized as moderate). Inspections, accreditation and site-level proficiency testing concern the laboratory, not the test.

preguntas.pregunta: A safety concern has been taken up the chain of command. What does the rule still require?
opciones: Telling the whole team that further input has been sought
Repeating the same concern a third time to the same person
Letting the colleague who was challenged answer it first
Holding any further action until the supervisor arrives
preguntas.explicacion: Turning to the supervisor is meant to overcome the natural tendency to assume the team leader must know what they are doing even when the plan departs from guidelines. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist washes her hands between patients. How long should that last, and which parts are easy to miss?
opciones: At least thirty seconds, covering the wrists and between the fingers
At least ten seconds, covering the palms and the backs of the hands
At least two minutes, covering the forearms as far as the elbows
At least thirty seconds, covering the fingertips and the nails only
preguntas.explicacion: The infection control table asks for hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub, washing carefully for at least thirty seconds and including the wrists and the spaces between the fingers. The pairing instruction on the other side of the table is simply not to forget to clean the hands.

preguntas.pregunta: In the one-year audit of an emergency laboratory, what was the single most frequent reason for rejecting biochemistry specimens?
opciones: Fibrin clots, found in 28 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Hemolysis, found in 28 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Insufficient volume, found in 35 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Lipemia, found in 22 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
preguntas.explicacion: For biochemistry the leading cause was fibrin clots at 28 %, followed by inadequate volume at 9 %; for coagulation, blood gases and CBC the leaders were clotted samples at 35 % and inadequate volume at 13 %. Hemolysis accounted for about 2 % of samples in that laboratory and lipemia for 0.1 %, so the percentages in the distractors are borrowed from other rows of the same study.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist sustains a needlestick from a used needle. According to the WHO's infection prevention table, what is the time limit after which post-exposure prophylaxis is no longer effective?
opciones: 72 hours
24 hours
48 hours
7 days
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.2 of the WHO guideline pairs each practice with its opposite. On the Do side: report any needle or sharps injury at once, seek help, and start post-exposure prophylaxis as soon as possible following the local protocol. On the Do-not side: do not put off PEP after contact with potentially contaminated material, because past 72 hours it no longer works. The lesson for the exam is twofold: report at once, and the window is three days, not one day and not a week.

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR rack was bumped and the Westergren tube stood tilted about 3° off vertical during the hour. What effect does this have?
opciones: Tilting raises the ESR; an angle of 3° can increase the value by as much as 30 %
Tilting lowers the ESR, because the red cells slide along the glass and settle more slowly
Tilting has no measurable effect as long as the reading is taken at exactly 60 minutes
Tilting affects only the Wintrobe method, whose shorter tube is more sensitive to inclination
preguntas.explicacion: The Westergren ESR is the distance red cells settle in a vertical tube after one hour, reported in millimeters per hour. Tube tilt and vibration falsely elevate the result, and an inclination of 3° from vertical can raise the ESR by up to 30 %. Elevated room temperature and direct sunlight also increase it, and air bubbles from an underfilled tube add to the error. Delay in setting up the test has the opposite effect and lowers the value.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Testing Procedures; Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about the CLIA quality standards for moderate and high complexity testing is accurate?
opciones: They differ only in the personnel requirements
They differ only in proficiency testing rules
High complexity sites are inspected; moderate sites are not
Moderate sites follow the insert only, like waived sites
preguntas.explicacion: Both nonwaived categories must hold a certificate, be inspected, and meet the quality system standards for proficiency testing, quality control, quality assessment and personnel. The single point where the two sets of standards diverge is personnel: who may direct, supervise and perform the testing. Following the insert alone satisfies CLIA only for waived tests.

preguntas.pregunta: When is a testicular self-exam most easily performed?
opciones: Standing, during or just after a shower, when the scrotal skin is relaxed
Lying down, first thing in the morning, before the scrotal skin has warmed
Standing, before a shower, so that the skin stays dry and easier to grip
Sitting, at the end of the day, when the scrotum hangs at its lowest point
preguntas.explicacion: Warm, relaxed scrotal skin is what makes the testicle easy to feel, so during or after a shower, standing up, is the moment to teach. One hand steadies the testicle while the fingers and thumb of the other cover the whole surface firmly but gently, and then the other side is checked the same way.

preguntas.pregunta: What can follow from repeatedly giving Medicare inaccurate information about a patient's other health coverage?
opciones: A fine, where the inaccurate information is given knowingly, willfully and repeatedly
A fine, wherever the inaccurate information leads Medicare to pay as the primary payer
Exclusion from the program, where the inaccurate information is given more than once
Recovery of the payment alone, since the responsibility rests with the primary payer
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law lets Medicare recover what it paid incorrectly as primary payer, and the provider has to return it. Beyond that, a provider can be fined for knowingly, willfully and repeatedly giving inaccurate information about a patient's other health insurance coverage. Recovery may also be pursued straight from a primary payer, another entity or a third payer.

preguntas.pregunta: An older adult asks why the provider chose cetirizine instead of diphenhydramine for allergic rhinitis. What is the reason?
opciones: Second-generation agents barely enter the brain, so they sedate less and go first
First-generation agents barely enter the brain, so they suit a driver on therapy
Second-generation agents block H2 receptors, so they settle the stomach as well
First-generation agents are the guideline choice once drowsiness has worn off
preguntas.explicacion: First-generation H1 antagonists are lipophilic and cross into the brain, so they bring sedation, slowed reaction times and anticholinergic trouble: dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, blurred vision. Second-generation agents stay peripheral, and guidelines put them first for allergic rhinitis and urticaria. In older adults the risk of falls and of cognitive decline has narrowed the use of diphenhydramine.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antihistamines", Indications and Adverse Effects

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist pours a bleach solution from a labeled jug into a basin she will use and empty during her own shift. Must she label the basin?
opciones: No: a portable container for her own immediate use is exempt
No: containers under one liter are exempt from workplace labels
Yes: every container in the work area needs the full label
Yes: unless the jug's own label is carried alongside the basin
preguntas.explicacion: The standard does not require labeling a portable container into which a hazardous chemical is transferred from a labeled container when it is intended only for the immediate use of the employee who performs the transfer. The exemption is narrow: it turns on immediate use by that same person, not on the size of the container, so a bottle filled for the next shift or for someone else falls back under the workplace labeling rule. Drugs a pharmacy dispenses for direct administration are exempt too.

preguntas.pregunta: What causes the symptoms of lactose intolerance?
opciones: Too little of the enzyme lactase to digest the sugar in milk
An immune reaction to the protein in cow's milk and dairy foods
Too little stomach acid to break down the fat in dairy products
Damage to the small intestine caused by the gluten in malted milk
preguntas.explicacion: Lactose is the sugar of milk and dairy foods, and the enzyme lactase is what digests it. Infants make lactase for breast milk; production may fall off later, which is why the problem is common in adults. An illness or surgery involving the small intestine can also lower how much lactase is made.

preguntas.pregunta: An office gets no answer back when it checks Medicare eligibility electronically. Which detail must be on file for the HETS system?
opciones: A HETS enrollment for the provider's National Provider Identifier
A HETS enrollment for the patient's own Medicare Beneficiary Identifier
A signed release of information from the patient for every eligibility check
A paper claim already on file with the Medicare Administrative Contractor
preguntas.explicacion: Providers, suppliers, vendors and clearinghouses enroll in the electronic data interchange for the eligibility system, and enrollment must be on file for every National Provider Identifier submitted for an eligibility check. Patients are not enrolled, no release is required for the check, and no prior claim is needed.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and heads to the cafeteria still wearing her gloves and lab coat. What does the standard require?
opciones: All PPE must be removed before leaving the work area and placed in a designated container
Gloves must be removed, but the lab coat may be worn out if it is not visibly soiled
PPE may be worn out if hands are washed first with soap and running water
PPE may be worn out if it is penetrated by blood, so long as it is changed within the shift
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(vii) requires all personal protective equipment to be removed before the employee leaves the work area, and (d)(3)(viii) says removed PPE goes into a designated area or container for storage, washing, decontamination or disposal. The rule covers every item, coat included, and does not depend on visible soiling. Handwashing after glove removal, in (d)(2)(v), is an additional duty, not a permit to keep PPE on, and a garment penetrated by blood comes off immediately under (d)(3)(vi).

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, fatigue and weight gain. Which laboratory pattern would confirm the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: A high TSH with a low free T4
A low TSH with a high free T4
A high TSH with a high free T4
A low TSH with a low free T4
preguntas.explicacion: Those complaints point to hypothyroidism, and the serum TSH is the first test. In primary hypothyroidism the gland cannot keep up, so free T4 falls and the pituitary pushes TSH up. When TSH is raised but free T4 is still normal, the picture is subclinical. Symptoms are mild and nonspecific often enough that the labs, not the story, settle it.

preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes in the order of draw share the same mode of action on calcium. Which are they?
opciones: The light blue citrate tube and the purple EDTA tube
The light blue citrate tube and the grey fluoride tube
The purple EDTA tube and the dark green heparin tube
The grey fluoride tube and the light green PST tube
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate at position 3 and EDTA at position 8 are both described as forming calcium salts to take calcium out of play, which is why both tubes stop the blood clotting. Heparin works instead by inactivating thrombin and thromboplastin, and the grey tube pairs oxalate with an antiglycolytic agent.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a claim denial expensive beyond the unpaid service itself?
opciones: Staff time to rework and appeal it adds administrative cost and delays the cash
The payer charges the practice a fee for each claim it has to deny in a year
The patient's coinsurance must be refunded whenever a claim ends up denied
The practice must return the contractual adjustment already posted to the account
preguntas.explicacion: Well-run revenue cycle management is described as reducing denials, shortening the gap between submission and payment, and cutting the administrative cost of billing and denial processing, which is where the extra cost of a denial sits. Payers do not bill practices for denying claims, the patient's share is not automatically refunded, and a contractual adjustment is a write-off recorded at posting.

preguntas.pregunta: A tracing shows inverted complexes in lead I but a normal chest lead pattern. What does that point to?

A heart on the right side rather than reversed arm electrodes
Reversed leg electrodes rather than reversed arm electrodes
A normal variant that calls for no check of the electrodes

preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient has an IV catheter running in the right forearm. Why does the WHO say NOT to take blood from that existing peripheral access?
opciones: Results may be false: haemolysis, contamination and IV fluid or medication alter them
The catheter lumen is too narrow, so the tubes fill slowly and the sample clots inside
The nursing staff alone may access it, and only for blood cultures
The results are valid only if a non-additive tube is drawn first and discarded
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says that in hospitalized patients blood should not be taken from an existing peripheral venous access site because this may give false results, naming haemolysis, contamination and the presence of intravenous fluid and medication as the causes. The contraindication list likewise includes any venous access device, including an IV catheter, as a contraindication. The WHO mentions no discard-tube workaround.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC ask occupational health services to establish for reporting infectious exposures?
opciones: A timely, confidential, non-punitive mechanism available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
A written form reviewed by the supervisor and filed within 60 calendar days
A monthly review meeting where exposures of the previous month are discussed
A punitive policy, so that workers who fail to follow precautions are held accountable
preguntas.explicacion: Recommendation 7.b.2 asks for a timely, confidential and non-punitive mechanism for personnel to report potentially infectious exposures and reach exposure management services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with access to expert clinicians and prompt laboratory testing on the same footing. The background explains why: exposures are significantly underreported because of time constraints, fear of reprimand, not knowing how to report and worries about cost coverage. A punitive policy would deepen exactly that problem, and 60 days is a HIPAA breach figure.

preguntas.pregunta: While verifying a date of birth with a hard-of-hearing patient, which technique applies?
opciones: Say the digits one at a time, 'six, one', rather than 'sixty-one'
Say the year louder, because numbers are especially hard to lip-read
Show the date on the wristband and ask him to confirm it with a nod
Skip the date of birth and use the room number as the second identifier
preguntas.explicacion: Give context when a patient has trouble hearing the difference between certain letters and numbers, for example 'm as in Mary' or 'five, six' instead of 'fifty-six'. Shouting distorts language sounds, the WHO wants the patient to state identifiers rather than nod at them, and The Joint Commission excludes the room number as an identifier.

preguntas.pregunta: Which task can some patient portals let a patient perform, beyond viewing information?

Correcting a diagnosis in the chart directly, without asking the practice
Opening the records of a family member who uses the same practice
Cancelling a claim the practice has already submitted to the health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Some portals go past viewing and let the patient message the doctor securely, request prescription refills, schedule non-urgent appointments, check benefits and coverage, update contact information, make payments, download and complete forms, and view educational materials. ONC frames the portal as a way to save time and support care between visits.

preguntas.pregunta: Does shifting the limb electrodes onto the upper arms and thighs change the reading?
opciones: No, the accuracy of the tracing is not affected
Yes, the limb leads then read the chest instead
Yes, the tracing has to be marked as non-standard
No, but the standardization has to be halved first
preguntas.explicacion: The move is offered precisely because it costs nothing: placing the limb electrodes higher up eliminates tremor from the arms and legs and in no way affects the accuracy of the electrocardiogram. It is a useful option in a patient who cannot keep the limbs still.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is filling an evacuated tube from a syringe. In what position is the tube held, and with what pressure?
opciones: Upright, pierced from directly above, with slow and steady pressure
Upright, pierced from directly above, with one firm push on the plunger
Tilted, pierced through the side of the stopper, with steady pressure
Upright, with the stopper taken off first and the blood run down the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The stopper is pierced with the needle directly above the tube, using slow and steady pressure, and the plunger is not pressed because the extra pressure raises the risk of haemolysis. The stopper is never removed either, since taking it off releases the vacuum inside.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7

preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old infant is choking, cannot cry, and is turning blue. Which sequence is used?
opciones: Up to five back blows face down, then up to five chest thrusts face up
Up to five abdominal thrusts with the infant held along the forearm
Thirty chest compressions and two breaths, repeated in cycles of five
Five back blows alone, repeated until the object leaves the airway
preguntas.explicacion: The infant is laid face down along the forearm with the head lower than the body and given up to 5 blows between the shoulder blades with the palm; if the object stays, the infant is turned face up for up to 5 chest thrusts. Those cycles repeat until the object comes out or the infant stops responding, and then CPR begins.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Choking - infant under 1 year", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in mild respiratory distress is sat up in Fowler's position. What does that change?
opciones: Chest expansion is maximized and abdominal muscular tension drops, so oxygenation rises
Venous return to the head and to the heart increases, which is useful in severe hypotension
Abdominal contents shift up against the diaphragm, so higher airway pressures are needed
Ventilation is favored in the nondependent lung as the mediastinum shifts to one side
preguntas.explicacion: Sitting the patient up lets the chest expand, relieves the pull of the abdominal muscles and takes gravity off the chest wall, which is why it helps in mild to moderate respiratory distress. Raising venous return by tipping the head down is Trendelenburg, and shifting ventilation toward the upper lung is what the lateral decubitus position does.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Structure and Function: Fowler Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(2) · RMA III.F.2.a.i

preguntas.pregunta: One chest electrode is left to place on a patient. Where does V6 go?
opciones: Fifth intercostal space, in the mid-axillary line
Fifth intercostal space, in the mid-clavicular line
Fourth intercostal space, in the mid-axillary line
Sixth intercostal space, in the mid-axillary line
preguntas.explicacion: V6 marks the left end of the chest row: fifth intercostal space, mid-axillary line. The mid-clavicular line at that same level belongs to V4, and the fourth space is where V1 and V2 sit, so the two coordinates have to be read together rather than one at a time.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: The P, QRS and T are almost invisible in one standard limb lead. What is the likely cause?
opciones: Two of the electrodes for that lead are on the legs
Two of the electrodes for that lead are on the arms
The chest electrodes were attached in reverse order
The gel on those electrodes had dried out completely
preguntas.explicacion: When all three main components go nearly flat in one of the standard limb leads, the probable reason is that both electrodes feeding that lead ended up on the two legs, so there is almost no voltage difference between them. The hook-up is checked before the tracing is repeated.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5

preguntas.pregunta: How is the length of a menstrual cycle counted?
opciones: From the first day of one period to the first day of the next one
From the last day of one period to the first day of the next one
From the first day of one period to the last day of that same period
From the estimated day of ovulation to the first day of the next period
preguntas.explicacion: The count starts on the first day of bleeding and ends the day before the next period starts; the day of heavy flow is day 1. Most cycles run about 28 days, and normal frequency is described as a cycle every 24 to 38 days, so shorter or longer cycles can still be normal.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Menstruation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k54 · RMA III.E.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: What does the T wave represent?
opciones: Repolarization of the ventricles, after their contraction
Depolarization of the ventricles, before they contract
Repolarization of the atria, after their contraction
Depolarization of the septum, before the ventricles fire
preguntas.explicacion: The T wave is ventricular repolarization: the muscle cells returning to their resting charge before the next impulse arrives, which roughly matches ventricular diastole. Its shape is easily changed by hormones, electrolytes and drugs, so it is one of the most variable parts of the tracing.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiography T Wave", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: After a post-exposure evaluation, how soon must the employer give the employee a copy of the healthcare professional's written opinion?
opciones: Within 15 days of completing the evaluation
Within 10 working days of the exposure incident
Within 30 days of the exposure incident
Within 90 days, once the baseline sample is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5) obliges the employer to obtain the evaluating professional's written opinion and hand the employee a copy within 15 days of the completion of the evaluation. The other periods belong elsewhere in the standard: 10 working days is the window for offering the hepatitis B vaccine after initial assignment, and 90 days is how long a baseline blood sample is preserved when the employee consents to the draw but not yet to HIV testing. Thirty days is not a deadline in this standard.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(5), Healthcare Professional's Written Opinion
