preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls to say her period started the day the stool cards were due. What is the advice?
opciones: Wait, because collecting during menstruation can give a false positive
Collect anyway, and note the menstruation on the card for the laboratory
Collect anyway, because menstrual blood does not react with the guaiac
Wait, because menstruation makes the card produce a false negative result
preguntas.explicacion: Samples are not collected when blood may be present in stool or urine from another source: menstruation, active hemorrhoids or a urinary tract infection all set off a false positive. Povidone-iodine antiseptic does the same by oxidizing the guaiac, so it is kept away from the perianal area before this test.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.c.i · CCMA 3B3 k64 · NCMA 2B.21

preguntas.pregunta: What separates suppression from repression?
opciones: Suppression is a conscious choice to block the thought
Suppression is a subconscious block of the same thought
Suppression swaps the impulse for its exact opposite
Suppression channels the anxiety into a useful pursuit
preguntas.explicacion: Suppression is consciously choosing to block undesirable ideas or impulses, which is what sets it apart from repression, a subconscious process. Reaction formation replaces an initial impulse with the opposite one, and sublimation redirects the feeling into a pursuit that societal norms treat as useful.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Defense Mechanisms", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Defense mechanisms · CCMA 1E k33 · CMA F.1.b / 2027 F.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the OIG guidance say the compliance officer should sit in an entity's reporting structure?
opciones: Reporting to the chief executive with independent access to the board, or to the board
Reporting to the billing manager, who sees every claim before it leaves the office
Reporting to the entity's outside counsel, who then directs any investigation there is
Reporting to the human resources director, who imposes the consequences on staff
preguntas.explicacion: Compliance leadership and oversight is the second element, and every entity should designate a compliance officer with the authority, stature, access and resources the role needs. That officer should report either to the chief executive with direct and independent access to the board, or straight to the board, and should stand as an equal among the other senior leaders.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 2: Compliance Leadership and Oversight

preguntas.pregunta: Two phlebotomists discuss a named patient's positive result in a crowded elevator. Is that a HIPAA problem?
opciones: Yes, because protected health information covers spoken communications, not only written records
No, because the rule reaches only electronic records and the papers printed out from them
No, because both of them work for the same covered entity and are part of its workforce
Yes, but only if a patient or a visitor from outside the organization actually overheard them
preguntas.explicacion: Protected health information is protected in any form or medium: electronic, paper or oral. A conversation naming a patient in a public space is a disclosure like any other, which is why the surgeon discussing a case in a full elevator is the standard example of a violation. Belonging to the same workforce permits access for a job reason, not conversation in public.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Definition of PHI
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7E k220 · RMA I.C.1.b disclosure laws · NCMA Law and Ethics 3

preguntas.pregunta: Along which vein does the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve travel, and at what level does it reach the surface?
opciones: With the basilic vein, about ten centimetres above the medial epicondyle
With the cephalic vein, about ten centimetres above the lateral epicondyle
With the median cubital vein, at the apex of the cubital fossa itself
With the basilic vein, about two centimetres below the medial epicondyle
preguntas.explicacion: This sensory nerve runs down the arm inside the brachial fascia together with the basilic vein and leaves that fascia roughly ten centimetres above the medial epicondyle, dividing into an anterior and a posterior branch. Its closeness to the basilic vein is what puts it at risk during a draw.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Nerve injury · CPT D3 3F 3L k62 k68 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12

preguntas.pregunta: Which safeguard applies when faxing protected health information?
opciones: Keep the fax machine in a secure area and use a cover page saying what to do if misdirected
Place the fax machine at the reception desk so that staff can retrieve incoming pages quickly
Send faxes overnight so that they arrive before the office opens and are not seen
Confirm receipt by mailing a paper duplicate of every fax to the recipient on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Fax machines are kept in a secure area away from the public, patients and most staff; the first page is a disclaimer telling the recipient what to do if the fax reached the wrong number; faxes are sent during working hours except in emergencies, so that they are picked up rather than left in the tray; and the sender contacts the other party to confirm the fax was collected. A machine at reception and overnight transmissions both leave PHI exposed, and mailing duplicates adds a second disclosure instead of a confirmation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Faxes
preguntas.subtema: Fax safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient who has just hurried up three flights of stairs sits down in the drawing chair. According to the phlebotomy guidance on position, what should happen before the draw?
opciones: The patient stays seated for at least 15 minutes before the draw, and any unavoidable change of position is recorded
The patient lies down for 2 minutes and the draw proceeds, because lying down offsets the effect of the exertion
The draw proceeds at once, because position affects only patients who are drawn lying down in the hospital
The patient stands for 5 minutes to let the blood volume redistribute, then sits and is drawn immediately
preguntas.explicacion: Changing position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is maintained for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the procedure; in an office setting the patient should sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand, and when a change of position is unavoidable it is recorded so the results can be interpreted accordingly. Outpatients are also told to avoid excessive physical activity in the 24 hours before collection.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position and fasting)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)

preguntas.pregunta: What does a dietitian typically need besides a degree?
opciones: Supervised training through an internship, and in many states a license
A doctoral degree in nutrition, and a license in every one of the states
A postsecondary certificate, and certification preferred by employers
A residency of several years, and board certification in a specialty
preguntas.explicacion: Dietitians and nutritionists run food service or nutrition programs so that people can live healthier lives. They typically need a bachelor's or master's degree and are typically required to have supervised training through an internship. Many states require them to be licensed. They work in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, cafeterias and for governments.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Dietitians and Nutritionists — How to Become One

preguntas.pregunta: The tubes are filled and the needle is discarded. Which closing steps does the WHO list before the patient leaves?
opciones: Check labels and forms, perform hand hygiene, ask how the patient feels and check the site for bleeding
Invert every tube 8 to 10 times, remove the gloves and send the patient out while the tubes clot in the rack
Apply ice to the site for 15 minutes, then recheck the labels once the patient has gone
Ask the patient to bend the arm over the gauze and hold it for five minutes before standing
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 runs through the closing routine: discard the sharp into the sharps container, check the label and forms for accuracy, discard the other items in the right waste category, perform hand hygiene again, recheck the labels before dispatch, tell the patient the procedure is over, ask how they feel, verify the site is not bleeding, and say something reassuring. Bending the arm is what Step 6 forbids.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9: Clean contaminated surfaces and complete patient procedure
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care · CPT D3 3Q 3R k74 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E9 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old has a pulse of 118 beats per minute at a well-child visit. What does that value represent?
opciones: A normal rate: children of 3 to 4 years rest between 80 and 120 beats per minute
Tachycardia: the 60 to 100 adult band is applied from the age of 3 years onward
A normal rate, but only for children under 2 years, whose band reaches 130 per minute
A rate that needs a recount, since a value above 100 in a child is not reported as such
preguntas.explicacion: Resting rates fall as children grow: 80 to 130 at 1 to 2 years, 80 to 120 at 3 to 4, 75 to 115 at 5 to 6, 70 to 110 at 7 to 9, and 60 to 100 from 10 years and through adulthood. A rate of 118 in a 4-year-old sits inside the band for that age, so the adult ceiling of 100 does not apply.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7

preguntas.pregunta: How does underfilling a tube contribute to haemolysis?
opciones: The ratio of anticoagulant to blood ends up greater than one to nine
The ratio of anticoagulant to blood ends up smaller than one to nine
The vacuum left in the tube pulls the red cells against the stopper
The additive settles at the bottom and never reaches the red cells
preguntas.explicacion: Among the recognized causes of haemolysis is underfilling a tube so that the proportion of anticoagulant to blood rises above one to nine. It is the same arithmetic that lengthens clotting times in a short-drawn citrate tube, where the plasma is outnumbered by the anticoagulant.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A certification expired eight months ago. What does getting it back require?
opciones: Fifteen continuing education credits, plus recertification and reinstatement fees
Ten continuing education credits, plus the recertification fee for that cycle
Re-registering, retaking the examination and paying the full examination price
Twenty continuing education credits, plus a written appeal to the certifying body
preguntas.explicacion: Reinstatement is allowed within one year of the expiration date, and it takes evidence of fifteen continuing education credits — twenty hours for pharmacy technicians — together with the recertification fees and the reinstatement fees. Once more than a year has passed, reinstatement is off the table and the person must re-register, sit the exam again and pay full price.
preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Reinstatement
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47

preguntas.pregunta: A team member is given feedback after missing a step. Which feature does formative feedback require?
opciones: It stays on the behavior instead of the person's attributes
It is saved for the annual review so that it carries weight
It lists everything that went wrong over the whole shift
It comes from the team leader only and never from a peer
preguntas.explicacion: Formative feedback is shared to improve performance and should be appreciative, timely, respectful, specific, aimed at improvement, considerate and focused on the patient. Respectful is defined as keeping to behaviors rather than personal attributes, and timely means soon after the behavior, which rules out saving it for a yearly review.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Formative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: Coaching and feedback · CCMA 6L k203 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient cutting sodium asks what the front-of-package claim "low sodium" guarantees. What does it mean?
opciones: One serving of the food holds 140 milligrams of sodium or less
One serving of the food holds 35 milligrams of sodium or less
The food carries at least 25% less sodium than the regular one
The food carries at least 50% less sodium than the regular one
preguntas.explicacion: Sodium claims are defined per serving: salt-free means under 5 mg, very low sodium means 35 mg or less, and low sodium means 140 mg or less. The comparison claims are different animals: reduced sodium is at least a quarter less than the regular product and light in sodium is at least half less.

preguntas.pregunta: Two records appear to belong to the same woman, one under her maiden name. Which process is meant to resolve that?
opciones: Patient matching, which links a person's data by comparing several demographic fields
Accounting of disclosures, which lists everyone the practice has sent her records to
Terminal digit filing, which places the record by the last pair of digits of its number
De-identification, which strips the identifiers so the two files can be compared safely
preguntas.explicacion: ONC defines patient matching as identifying and linking one patient's data within and across health systems so that a full view of the record can be obtained. At a minimum it works by linking several demographic fields, and the ones named are name, birth date, telephone number and address. ONC treats it as a critical component of interoperability and of the national health IT infrastructure.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient told to avoid immediately before a resting tracing?
opciones: Exercise or cold water, since either can falsify the result
Eating or smoking for the three hours before the recording
Taking any regular medicine on the morning of the test
Speaking or moving for the ten minutes before the test
preguntas.explicacion: Exercising or drinking cold water just beforehand may produce false results. Medicines are not stopped on the patient's own decision; the provider is told what is being taken, because some drugs interfere with the reading. The fasting rules belong to the exercise test.

preguntas.pregunta: What do surveillance data say about how often needlestick injuries are actually reported?
opciones: About half go unreported, and a typical hospital sees some 30 per 100 beds a year
Nearly all are reported, since the sharps injury log is reviewed every month
About one in ten goes unreported, mostly among housekeeping employees
Half go unreported, and a typical hospital sees about 300 per 100 beds a year
preguntas.explicacion: Estimates put 600,000 to 800,000 needlestick and other percutaneous injuries a year in the United States, and about half of them are never reported. Surveillance data suggest an average hospital sees roughly 30 needlestick injuries per 100 beds per year. Under-reporting matters twice over: the worker misses post-exposure management, and the institution loses the record it needs to see where the hazard is. That is why employers are told to establish procedures that encourage reporting.

preguntas.pregunta: A family earns too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance for their children. Which program is meant for them?
opciones: CHIP, which covers children in that income range and is run by each state
COBRA, which continues children's coverage in that income range for a time
Medigap, which supplements children's coverage while the parents apply
Medicare Part C, which enrolls children whose parents lack job-based coverage
preguntas.explicacion: The Children's Health Insurance Program covers children whose families earn too much to qualify for Medicaid but not enough to buy private coverage; states run it under federal requirements and fund it with the federal government, and in some states it also covers pregnant women. Applications are accepted at any time of year. COBRA continues employer coverage, Medigap supplements Original Medicare, and Medicare Advantage is Medicare coverage.

preguntas.pregunta: An athlete who sweats heavily asks whether plain water replaces what he loses. What is accurate about electrolytes?
opciones: They are lost in sweat and plain water holds no meaningful amount of them
They are lost in sweat and plain water replaces them as fast as they are lost
They are lost only in urine, so sweating does not change the body's supply
They are lost in sweat, but only the sodium and the chloride are affected
preguntas.explicacion: Electrolytes are the charged minerals of blood and body fluid: calcium, chloride, magnesium, phosphorus, potassium and sodium. They govern body water, blood pH, and nerve and muscle function. Sweat carries them out, and since plain water holds almost none, they have to come back in fluids that contain them.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Electrolytes

preguntas.pregunta: A contract cleaning crew works nights in a laboratory that stores hazardous chemicals. What must the laboratory's program provide for?
opciones: On-site access to the sheets, the precautions to take, and the labeling system
A copy of the crew's own written program, kept in the laboratory office
Training of the crew by the laboratory, repeated once every three years
A separate storage room for the chemicals while the crew is on site
preguntas.explicacion: Where an employer produces, uses or stores hazardous chemicals in a way that can expose another employer's workers, the written program has to add three things: how the other employer will be given on-site access to a safety data sheet for each chemical their people may meet, how they will be told what precautions are needed under normal operating conditions and in a foreseeable emergency, and how they will be told which labeling system the workplace uses. Each employer still trains its own staff.

preguntas.pregunta: Apart from raising the risk of contamination, what else follows from puncturing before the antiseptic has dried?
opciones: It appears on the list of factors that cause haemolysis
It appears on the list of factors that cause clotted tubes
It appears on the list of factors that cause nerve injury
It appears on the list of factors that cause a lost vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Failing to let the alcohol or disinfectant dry is named among the factors that increase the risk of haemolysis, as well as leaving the site poorly disinfected. That is why the swab is followed by thirty seconds of drying rather than an immediate puncture through a wet surface.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses an insulin pump covered under the Part B equipment benefit. What is the most she pays for a month's supply of that insulin?
opciones: Thirty-five dollars, and the yearly Part B deductible is not applied to it
Thirty-five dollars, but only once she has met the yearly Part B deductible
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as for other equipment and supplies
One hundred and five dollars, the ceiling set for one month's covered supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where insulin is covered through the Part B durable medical equipment benefit for a pump, or through a Medicare Advantage Plan, the cost of a month's supply cannot exceed thirty-five dollars and the Part B deductible does not apply. A three-month supply is capped at thirty-five dollars for each month, so generally no more than a hundred and five dollars in all.

preguntas.pregunta: The surgeon changed the procedure on the day of surgery and the authorization still names the old one. What is the warning about fixing that afterwards?
opciones: Some payers will change an authorization only up to fourteen days after the service
Some payers will change an authorization only up to sixty days after the service
No payer will change an authorization once the service has already been provided
Every payer has to reopen the authorization when the record justifies the change
preguntas.explicacion: When the procedure billed differs from the procedure authorized, the advice is to update the information before the claim goes out, or to justify the discrepancy with solid reasons. If the code changed and authorization was required, it has to be addressed at once: some payers will not touch an authorization more than fourteen days past the date of service, and after that the denial is likely to be permanent.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what Part B is for in the broadest terms. Which two categories of service does it cover?
opciones: Medically necessary services and preventive services
Medically necessary services and long-term custodial care
Preventive services and inpatient hospital admissions
Preventive services and skilled nursing facility stays
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers two kinds of thing. Medically necessary services or supplies are those meeting accepted standards of medical practice for diagnosing or treating the patient's condition. Preventive services are the care meant to head off illness or catch it early, when treatment is likeliest to work, and most of them cost the patient nothing when the provider accepts assignment. Inpatient hospital and skilled nursing stays belong to Part A.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to record intake in millilitres and reports drinking one cup of water. What is recorded?
opciones: 240 mL, since a cup is 8 ounces and an ounce is 30 mL
180 mL, since a cup is 6 ounces and an ounce is 30 mL
480 mL, since a cup is 8 ounces and an ounce is 60 mL
120 mL, since a cup is 8 ounces and an ounce is 15 mL
preguntas.explicacion: One ounce is 30 mL and one cup is 8 ounces, so a cup comes to 240 mL. The rest of the household ladder follows from there: a pound is 16 ounces, a pint is 2 cups, a quart is 4 cups and a gallon is 4 quarts. Intake and output conversions are one of the routine calculations, and they are recorded in metric units even when the patient reports them in household ones.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4a: Common Household Conversions

preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a malpractice claim against the practice. May the practice drop him at once?
opciones: No: the suit does not release the clinician from giving due notice
No: the suit freezes the relationship until the case has been decided
Yes: filing suit is treated as the patient ending the relationship
Yes: a conflict of interest requires the practice to dismiss him now
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who sues does not thereby end the therapeutic relationship, and a court has expressly rejected the idea that suing absolves the clinician of the duty to give due notice of withdrawal and ample opportunity to secure other care. Dropping such a patient without the usual process is precisely what exposes the clinician to an abandonment claim.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Issues of Concern: Patient Abandonment

preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the assistant to send a pamphlet and book a follow-up; the assistant restates the task and the provider confirms. Which strategy is that?
opciones: A check-back, which closes the loop on the message
A call-out, which informs the whole team at once
A teach-back, which confirms a patient understood
A handoff, which transfers responsibility for care
preguntas.explicacion: A check-back is the closed-loop strategy for making sure what the sender conveyed is what the receiver understood: the receiver repeats it and the sender confirms. A call-out broadcasts to everyone at once, a teach-back checks a patient or family member, and a handoff moves responsibility between caregivers.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Closed-Loop Communication

preguntas.pregunta: Two R waves on a regular strip sit five large squares apart. What does that give?
opciones: 60 per minute, sitting at the lower edge of the normal band
75 per minute, sitting in the middle of the normal band
50 per minute, sitting just under the lower edge of normal
100 per minute, sitting at the upper edge of the normal band
preguntas.explicacion: With an even rhythm the rate is 300 divided by the large squares between two R waves, so five of them give 60 per minute. That is the bottom of the 60 to 100 band: one square more would put the tracing under 60, which is what bradycardia means.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on warfarin comes in for the scheduled blood test. Which result guides the dose of this drug?
opciones: The international normalized ratio, which standardizes the prothrombin time
The prothrombin time in seconds, preferred because it is not standardized
The hemoglobin and hematocrit, which are drawn every six months on therapy
The potassium and the creatinine, drawn before starting and then once a year
preguntas.explicacion: Warfarin is followed with the INR, which puts the prothrombin time on one scale whatever reagent the laboratory uses; someone not anticoagulated sits near 1.0. Hospitalized patients are checked daily and maintenance patients roughly every four weeks, plus whenever an interacting drug starts or stops. Hemoglobin and hematocrit are baseline and six-month checks, not the dosing guide.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Warfarin", Monitoring

preguntas.pregunta: A professional submits the continuing education documents three weeks after the expiration date. What is the position?
opciones: Still inside the one-month grace period the certifying body allows
Outside the deadline, so reinstatement fees are now due as well
Outside the deadline, so the credential is nullified permanently
Still valid, because documents are accepted for a year afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation of the ten credits and the fees can be submitted annually or all at once before the certification expires, and a one-month grace period is allowed. Failing to meet the requirement before the expiration date nullifies the credential, but reinstatement stays open for a year, with fifteen credits plus recertification and reinstatement fees.

preguntas.pregunta: A 25-year-old woman asks how often she needs cervical cancer screening. What is recommended for her age band?
opciones: Cytology alone every 3 years from 21 through 29
Cytology alone every 5 years from 21 through 29
Cytology with HPV cotesting every 3 years from 21 through 29
Cytology alone every year from 21 through 29
preguntas.explicacion: Screening for cervical cancer covers women from 21 through 65. Between 21 and 29 it is cervical cytology alone every three years. From 30 through 65 there are three acceptable strategies: cytology alone every three years, high-risk HPV testing alone every five, or the two together every five. The recommendation carries an A grade.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's stat chemistry goes into a green top tube. Which heparin salts may it hold, and what is tested?
opciones: Sodium, lithium or ammonium heparin; the sample tested is plasma
Sodium or potassium heparin; the sample tested is serum after a spin
Lithium heparin only; the sample tested is serum after a longer spin
Sodium or lithium citrate; the sample tested is plasma after a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: Green tubes hold heparin in the form of the sodium, lithium or ammonium salt, and the heparin stops thrombin from forming. Because the blood does not clot, what the laboratory tests is plasma, not serum; these tubes are often chosen when chemistry results are wanted immediately.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of elements makes up a comprehensive history intake at a wellness visit?
opciones: Past medical and surgical history, allergies and medications, plus family and social history
Vital signs, height and weight, and all of the findings of the head-to-toe physical examination
The chief concern alone, expanded with the onset, location and severity of the symptom
Laboratory results, imaging reports and the discharge summaries of earlier admissions
preguntas.explicacion: A full intake gathers what the patient has lived through: conditions already diagnosed, operations already done, illnesses that run in the family, the social picture, allergies with the reaction each one caused, and every current medication. Vital signs, examination findings, laboratory values and imaging are objective data and are recorded apart.

preguntas.pregunta: How soon after restraint or seclusion begins does CMS require a face-to-face evaluation of the patient?
opciones: Within 1 hour
Within 4 hours
Within 30 minutes
Within 24 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Within 1 hour of initiating seclusion or restraint the patient must be evaluated face to face by a clinician or licensed independent practitioner, or by a registered nurse or physician assistant with the required training; state law may be stricter. Four hours is the length of an adult restraint order, and 30 minutes and 24 hours are figures from drug-level timing and alcohol avoidance.

opciones: Plain or gel tubes, and last the tubes holding additives
Tubes holding additives, and last the plain or gel tubes
Capillary microtubes, and last the tubes holding additives
Plain or gel tubes, and last a second sterile culture bottle

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that a copy of her records be sent directly to another physician. What does HIPAA require of that request?
opciones: That it be written, signed, and clearly name the recipient and where to send it
That the receiving physician sign a business associate agreement before records are sent
That the patient collect the records in person and deliver them herself
That the request be approved by the privacy official within 15 days
preguntas.explicacion: Under 164.524(c)(3)(ii), when an access request directs the covered entity to transmit the copy to another person designated by the individual, the entity must send it to that person; the request must be in writing, signed by the individual, and clearly identify the designated recipient and where to send the copy. A business associate agreement covers entities working on the covered entity's behalf, not a physician chosen by the patient to receive her own records.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient needs a serum lithium level and an ammonia level. Which heparin tube is required for each?
opciones: Sodium heparin for the lithium level; either heparin salt for the ammonia level
Lithium heparin for the lithium level; sodium heparin only for the ammonia level
Either heparin salt for the lithium level; sodium heparin only for the ammonia
Sodium heparin for both, because lithium heparin is limited to chemistry panels
preguntas.explicacion: The dark green heparin tube may carry sodium heparin or lithium heparin. For a lithium level the sodium salt is the one specified, while an ammonia level accepts either salt. The light green PST is the tube that carries lithium heparin with a gel separator, and its listed use is chemistries.

preguntas.pregunta: Why has a needle and vacuum tube assembly been singled out as carrying a higher injury risk?
opciones: It has to be taken apart or handled after use, which has raised injury rates
It holds a larger volume of blood than a syringe of the very same gauge
Its needle is longer, so it reaches deeper into the vein of the patient
It cannot be fitted with a shield, so no safer version of it is made
preguntas.explicacion: Devices that must be taken apart or manipulated once the draw is over, such as prefilled cartridge syringes and phlebotomy needle and vacuum tube assemblies, are an obvious hazard and have been linked to higher injury rates. Safer versions do exist: hinged or sliding shields for phlebotomy and winged-steel needles, sliding shields on vacuum tube holders, and needles that retract into the holder. Length and blood volume are not what the injury data point to.

opciones: Room temperature, humidity and how much light the specimen receives
Room temperature only, since humidity and light reach sealed tubes
Barometric pressure and the height of the chair the patient sits in
The colour of the tray and how far the rack sits from the patient

preguntas.pregunta: How often should a person revisit an advance directive already on file?
opciones: At least once a year, and after a major life event
Only when the named agent asks for it to be changed
Only when a new diagnosis is added to the problem list
Every five years, which is when the form legally lapses
preguntas.explicacion: Advance directives are meant to be living documents: reviewed at least once each year and updated after a major life event such as retirement, a move to another state or a significant change in health. When a form is replaced, the older version is kept and dated. No annual or five-year expiry makes the document lapse on its own.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory sends a specimen to a reference laboratory. When the result comes back, what may and may not the referring laboratory do with it?
opciones: It may let the testing laboratory report directly to the ordering person, but must not revise the result and must keep an exact duplicate
It may reformat and revise the result to match its own reference intervals, provided it keeps a copy of the original report
It must always reissue the result under its own name and address, because the ordering person deals only with the referring laboratory
It may discard the testing laboratory's report once the value has been transcribed accurately into its own report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(i) sets three rules for referred testing: the referring laboratory must not revise results or interpretive information supplied by the testing laboratory; it may permit the testing laboratory to send the result straight to the person who ordered it, but must retain or be able to produce an exact duplicate of that report; and it must notify the ordering person of the name and address of every location that performed the testing.

preguntas.pregunta: A laptop holding unencrypted patient results is stolen from a laboratory courier's car. How soon must the affected individuals be notified?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days after the breach is discovered
Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 30 days after the breach is discovered
Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 90 days after the breach is discovered
Within 60 days of the end of the calendar year in which the breach came to light
preguntas.explicacion: Individual notice goes out without unreasonable delay and never later than 60 days after discovery, in writing by first-class mail or by email if the person agreed to that. It must describe the breach, the types of information involved, what people should do to protect themselves, and what the entity is doing about it. The year-end deadline applies to reporting small breaches to the Secretary.

preguntas.pregunta: For a blood pressure of 120/80, what are the pulse pressure and the approximate mean arterial pressure (MAP)?
opciones: Pulse pressure 40 mm Hg; MAP about 93 mm Hg
Pulse pressure 40 mm Hg; MAP about 100 mm Hg
Pulse pressure 200 mm Hg; MAP about 100 mm Hg
Pulse pressure 30 mm Hg; MAP about 80 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic, so 120 minus 80 gives 40 mm Hg, and it should be at least 25 percent of the systolic value. MAP is approximated as diastolic plus one third of the pulse pressure: 80 plus 40/3, about 93 mm Hg, within the normal 70 to 110 range. A MAP under 60 mm Hg for long leaves tissues without enough flow.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse Pressure; Mean Arterial Pressure

preguntas.pregunta: Which term names the belief that one's own culture is better than another's?
opciones: Ethnocentrism, rating one's own culture above others
Stereotyping, assigning group traits to an individual
Prejudice, a preconceived and unfavorable judgment
Discrimination, unfair treatment that denies rights
preguntas.explicacion: Ethnocentrism is holding one's own culture, race, ethnicity or country to be preferable to another's. Stereotyping assumes a person carries the attributes and values of a group because they belong to it, prejudice is prejudging, and discrimination is the unfair treatment that denies people rights and opportunities.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a chemical splash in one eye. How long does irrigation continue?
opciones: At least 30 minutes, and until the surface pH reads 7.0 to 7.4 on litmus
At least 5 minutes, and until the patient reports the pain has settled down
At least 30 minutes, and until the visual acuity returns to its usual level
Until the ophthalmologist arrives, since irrigation may wash away the evidence
preguntas.explicacion: Copious irrigation is the single most important step and it often matters more to the final vision than which chemical was involved. It runs for a minimum of half an hour, longer in severe injuries, until the ocular surface reads neutral on litmus paper. Alkali burns need more volume and more time, because they keep penetrating after the exposure ends.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ocular Burns", Treatment / Management

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fainted during a draw remains unresponsive for more than five minutes, with jerking movements and loss of bladder control. What does this episode indicate?
opciones: It is not simple syncope but more likely a seizure, which needs urgent evaluation
It is a prolonged vasovagal episode; keep the legs raised and wait calmly for recovery
It is typical syncope, since jerking and incontinence are common during a faint
It is near syncope, because the patient never fully lost postural tone
preguntas.explicacion: Any episode lasting more than a few minutes is not syncope but more likely an acute neurologic process such as a seizure, and, unlike seizure patients, people with syncope keep sphincter control, rarely show tonic-clonic activity and are not confused on waking. Emergency services are called if the person does not become alert within a couple of minutes.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", sections Etiology and Pathophysiology; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting

preguntas.pregunta: A light blue tube reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. Which collection faults are recognized causes?
opciones: A traumatic venipuncture, clotting inside the device, or poor mixing with the additive
A tourniquet released too early, a needle angle below fifteen degrees, or a warm room
An expired needle, a second puncture in the same arm, or a bandage applied too tightly
A tube filled from a syringe, a tube stored upright, or a label written after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting in a citrate specimen is traced to a traumatic venipuncture, activation of coagulation inside the collection device, or the anticoagulant not being properly mixed with the blood. A clot consumes clotting factors, so the testing that follows is unreliable and the specimen is repeated.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: In one laboratory 8.28 % of newborn specimens carried an identification error, ten times the rate of other patients. What explanation was offered?
opciones: The small newborn tubes leave no room for two identifiers on the label
Newborns are often still unnamed, so the wristband carries only a case number
Newborn samples are collected by nurses who work outside the barcode system
Newborn labels are printed at the station and applied after the heel stick
preguntas.explicacion: In 93.4 % of those newborn cases the problem was the same one that dominates in adults: fewer than two identifiers on the label. The reason given is physical rather than procedural, since the special small tubes used for newborn blood simply do not have room to write two identifiers. The overall figure for the laboratory was 0.81 % of samples with some identification error.

Fewer than ten per cent of all of them
Almost exactly fifty per cent of them all

Staff don gown and gloves; the patient's room is disinfected at least daily

preguntas.pregunta: Which organs form the digestive tract itself, and which are the major accessory organs?
opciones: Mouth to large intestine form the tract; salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas assist
Mouth to large intestine form the tract; kidneys, spleen, thymus and appendix assist
Liver, gallbladder and pancreas form the tract; mouth, stomach and intestines assist
Stomach and intestines alone form the tract; mouth, pharynx and esophagus assist
preguntas.explicacion: The digestive tract, also called the alimentary canal, is one continuous tube from mouth to anus: mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. preguntas.pregunta: Under fee-for-service payment, how is a provider paid?

A single payment covers the whole episode, regardless of the tests or visits it needs
A fixed amount per enrolled patient per month covers all the services they use
A payment is earned only when the quality measures for the year are met in full
preguntas.explicacion: Fee for service pays doctors and other providers for each service delivered, office visits and tests among them, so the payment follows the volume of work. preguntas.pregunta: What is the practical advantage of chlorhexidine over povidone-iodine as a surgical skin prep?
opciones: Excellent sustained residual activity, which persists after it is wiped off the field
Excellent sporicidal activity, which is what povidone-iodine has never been shown to have
Excellent activity in the presence of blood, which inactivates chlorhexidine far less
Excellent tolerance around the eye and the ear, where iodine solutions must be avoided

A stimulus, a set point and a normal range
A receptor, a hormone and a target organ
A sensor, a normal range and a stimulus

preguntas.pregunta: What total blood volume does the CDC consider optimal for diagnosing bacteremia in an adult, and over what period is it collected?

10 to 20 mL from at least two sets within a 5-minute period
80 to 100 mL from four sets within a 48-hour period
preguntas.explicacion: The optimal volume is 40 to 60 mL, reached by collecting at least two sets, by peripheral venipuncture, within a 24-hour period and before antibiotics whenever possible; the standard of practice is two to four sets per septic episode. preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old has an axillary reading of 37.3 °F converted in error; the correct axillary value is 37.3 °C. Does this meet the definition of fever in a child?
opciones: Yes: an axillary reading of 37.2 °C (99 °F) or above is a fever in a child
No: an axillary reading only counts as fever from 38 °C (100.4 °F) upward

Whether the patient has any days left in the current skilled nursing benefit period

preguntas.explicacion: When the provider decides a patient needs home health, the patient receives a list of agencies serving her area, and the provider must say whether the organization holds a financial interest in any agency on it. preguntas.pregunta: When does a practitioner registered with the DEA take an inventory of the controlled substances on hand?

An actual physical count on registering, and a new inventory at the end of every year
A physical count every six months, matching the life of a Schedule IV prescription
A physical count only when the DEA inspects, using records kept for two years before
preguntas.explicacion: When the Certificate of Registration is issued the practitioner takes an initial inventory, an actual physical count of every controlled substance in their possession; if there is none on hand, that fact itself is recorded as the initial inventory. It usually pays more inside the network but still pays part of outside care
It lets her choose between the two arrangements each time she needs care
It pays each provider a fixed amount per patient enrolled with the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Managed care plans contract with providers and facilities to furnish care to members at reduced cost, and those providers make up the plan's network. Neutrophils
Eosinophils
Monocytes
preguntas.explicacion: The hematopoietic stem cell gives rise to two lines: lymphoid stem cells, which produce only the lymphocytes (T cells, B cells and natural killer cells), and myeloid stem cells, which produce everything else, including erythrocytes, the megakaryocytes that shed platelets, monocytes and the three granular leukocytes. preguntas.pregunta: What makes a test "waived" under CLIA?
opciones: It is a simple procedure with an insignificant risk of an erroneous result
It is performed at the bedside or in an exam room rather than in a laboratory
It has been cleared by the FDA as substantially equivalent to a marketed test
It is a moderately complex procedure done by a physician during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: The regulatory criteria are simplicity and low risk: the test is cleared for home use, or its method is so simple and accurate that user error is negligible, or a wrong result would pose no reasonable risk of harm. Location does not qualify a test; FDA clearance applies to waived, moderate and high tests alike; and a moderate microscopy test done by the physician is PPM, a different category.

preguntas.pregunta: A technician using the same technique all day still gets a mix of clean and poor tracings. Why?
opciones: Skin chemistry varies, so some skin needs extra care
The machine loses its calibration as the day goes on
The room current varies through the day and interferes
The alcohol evaporates, so later sites get less of it
preguntas.explicacion: Skin resistance is not the same from one patient to the next: some skin is sweatier and some scalier, and each condition calls for a different level of care when the electrode goes on. Good technique compensates even for the most difficult skin, which is why the preparation step is never rushed.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient enrolled in an HMO asks whether her plan will pay for a specialist in another state who does not belong to the plan. What is the correct answer?
opciones: It generally pays nothing for that visit, because the care is outside the network
It pays a smaller share of that visit, because the specialist is outside the network
It pays the visit in full once her primary care doctor signs a written referral
It pays the visit in full once she has met the yearly deductible of her plan
preguntas.explicacion: An HMO usually restricts coverage to physicians employed by the plan or under contract with it, and it will not pay for care outside that group except in an emergency. A supervisor pulls a record to check that the collection procedure was followed
A billing clerk asks the laboratory for the diagnosis codes attached to a claim

Take as many extensions as the retrieval needs, so long as each one is documented internally
Take one extension of up to 60 more days, the period the rule gives for amendment requests
Deny the request outright, since information that is not readily accessible falls outside access

preguntas.pregunta: Under which doctrine is a supervising physician or employer held liable for the acts of an employee working within the scope of employment?
opciones: Respondeat superior, a form of vicarious liability
Strict liability, applied to inherently dangerous activities
Proportional liability, apportioned by degree of fault
Sovereign immunity, which limits awards against governments
preguntas.explicacion: Vicarious liability holds an employer responsible for the torts of employees acting within the scope of their employment, on the policy view that the employer is better placed to absorb the loss; when a midlevel provider working under a physician's license is sued, the plaintiff focuses on the supervising physician under the doctrine of respondeat superior. Proportional liability reduces an award by the claimant's own share of fault, strict liability applies to dangerous activities and defective drugs or devices, and sovereign immunity caps damages against governmental entities.

Testing must be repeated to confirm the status before any prophylaxis is offered
Testing must be repeated within 72 hours and recorded in the sharps injury log
Testing is replaced by a second baseline sample from the exposed employee

preguntas.pregunta: The 2009 H1N1 influenza strain was classified as a pandemic. Which feature of that strain made the classification possible?
opciones: It had acquired efficient person-to-person transmission after reassortment
It had acquired resistance to every antiviral drug then in use
It was carried in pork products eaten in many countries at once
It was confined to close contact between people and infected pigs
preguntas.explicacion: Swine influenza viruses only set off a pandemic once reassortment gives them efficient spread from person to person, which is what happened in 1918 and again in 2009. The widespread belief that the infection came from eating bacon or ham was wrong: the virus stays in the respiratory system, and food-borne transmission is unlikely.

preguntas.pregunta: Anticoagulated specimens from a neonatal unit clot at 6.67 %, against 0.36 % elsewhere in the same hospital. Which explanation fits the published data?
opciones: Drawn-out, difficult venipuncture and failure to mix the tube afterwards
Excess anticoagulant in the microtubes chosen for very small blood volumes
Transport of the microtubes upright in a rack instead of a padded holder
The longer wait before newborn serum is separated from the cells
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting inside a tube that contains an anticoagulant is attributed to two things: a challenging or prolonged venipuncture, and a tube that was not mixed properly once filled. Newborn draws are hard, which is why their clotting ratio ran roughly eighteen times the hospital average. Published median figures for clotted samples elsewhere sit between 0.05 % and 0.21 %.

Leave them standing upright until the additive has dissolved on its own
Invert them only if the local laboratory has not already specified otherwise
Shake them firmly for a few seconds so the additive reaches all the blood

preguntas.pregunta: An instructor compares the analytical phase of the laboratory with the rest of health care using the sigma scale. Which comparison is the one drawn in the literature?

Health care sits at 4 sigma, roughly level with airline baggage handling
Health care sits at 5 sigma, matching the analytical phase of the laboratory
Health care sits at 3 sigma, ahead of airline baggage handling at about 2
preguntas.explicacion: Measured on the sigma scale, health care as a whole performs at 1 to 2 sigma, which compares poorly with an industry such as airline baggage handling at roughly 4 sigma, and the overall defect rate in United States health care has been put at 31 to 69 %. A blunt cannula, and a mushroom-shaped needle guard
A magnetic tray, and a slotted needle removal rack

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory is writing its specimen identification policy. Under CLIA, over what span must positive identification and integrity of a patient's specimen be assured?

From the moment the specimen is accessioned until the analyzer finishes the run
From collection until the specimen is centrifuged and the aliquots are labeled
From receipt in the laboratory until the specimen is discarded at the end of its retention period

preguntas.pregunta: What is stored in the threads of chromatin inside the nucleus, and what does the nucleolus produce?

Chromatin holds RNA; the nucleolus makes the DNA for chromosomes
Chromatin holds enzymes; the nucleolus makes the lipids for membranes
Chromatin holds histones; the nucleolus makes the ATP for the cell
preguntas.explicacion: The nucleus is the control center, and the chromatin inside it is DNA wound around histone proteins. When the cell divides, that chromatin condenses into chromosomes. The nucleolus is a dense region within the nucleus that turns out the ribosomal RNA, and the new ribosome subunits leave through the nuclear pores.

It should be red, so the used device is visible in the sharps bin
It should differ between hospitals, so devices are not mixed up
It should change once the safety feature has been activated once

preguntas.pregunta: How long after a patient's death does HIPAA continue to protect their health information?

For 6 years after death
For 30 years after death
Indefinitely, with no time limit

preguntas.pregunta: What separates a sprain from a strain?
opciones: A sprain injures a ligament at a joint; a strain tears a stretched muscle
A sprain injures a muscle belly; a strain injures the joint capsule itself
A sprain is a partial break of bone; a strain is a bruise over that bone
A sprain follows a direct blow; a strain follows a twist of the same joint
preguntas.explicacion: A sprain is damage to the ligaments around a joint, the fibers that hold bone to bone, and it happens when the joint is forced into an unnatural position, as in a twisted ankle. A strain, also called a pulled muscle, is a muscle stretched too far so that part of it tears, from an accident, overuse or using the muscle the wrong way.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is epinephrine added to a local anesthetic for a laceration repair, and where must it not be injected?
opciones: It constricts vessels and prolongs the block; it is kept away from the ears, nose tip and digits
It dilates vessels and prolongs the block; it is kept away from the ears, nose tip and digits
It constricts vessels and shortens the block; it is kept away from the scalp, cheek and lips
It buffers the solution and reduces the sting; it is kept away from the scalp, cheek and lips
preguntas.explicacion: Epinephrine causes vasoconstriction, which limits blood loss, and it lengthens the anesthetic effect by delaying absorption of the agent. It is not injected around the ears, the tip of the nose, the penis or the distal phalanges, because tissue necrosis can follow. Local anesthetics are otherwise vasodilators, cocaine excepted.

To the ordering provider and to any physician or relative who states that they are involved in the patient's care

preguntas.pregunta: The CDC states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. Which rule in the OSHA standard expresses the same principle?

Gloves are worn whenever hand contact with blood can reasonably be anticipated
Disposable gloves are replaced as soon as feasible when torn or punctured
Utility gloves may be decontaminated and reused while they remain intact

preguntas.pregunta: On the one-step 2-hour 75 g test used in pregnancy, which fasting value counts as abnormal?
opciones: 92 mg/dL or higher
95 mg/dL or higher
100 mg/dL or higher
126 mg/dL or higher
preguntas.explicacion: The one-step test is abnormal at 92 mg/dL fasting, 180 at one hour and 153 at two hours. Outside pregnancy, 100 to 125 mg/dL is impaired fasting glucose and 126 on two tests diagnoses diabetes.
