The chemical formula of each product and its molecular weight
The purchase price of each product and the budget for replacing it
preguntas.explicacion: Training has to include at least four things: the methods and observations that can reveal the presence or release of a hazardous chemical in the area, such as monitoring by the employer, continuous monitoring devices, or the appearance or smell of the chemical when it escapes; the physical and health hazards, including asphyxiation, combustible dust, pyrophoric gas and hazards not otherwise classified; the measures employees can take to protect themselves; and the details of the program, the labels and the data sheet, including the order of its information.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(h)(3)(i) to (h)(3)(iv), Employee information and training
preguntas.subtema: What the training covers · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b · RMA II.B.7.d.iii III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: How long does the whole trip take, from the impulse being born in the sinoatrial node to depolarization of the ventricles?
opciones: About 225 ms, counting every leg of the journey
About 100 ms, counting every leg of the journey
About 75 ms, counting every leg of the journey
About 400 ms, counting every leg of the journey
preguntas.explicacion: The legs add up: some 50 ms between the two nodes, about 100 ms held inside the atrioventricular node, roughly 25 ms down the bundle and its branches to the apex, and about 75 ms for the Purkinje fibers to reach every ventricular muscle cell.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Purkinje Fibers
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii

preguntas.pregunta: A man says part of his semen sample spilled outside the container. What should he be told?
opciones: Report the loss to the laboratory, because every fraction of the ejaculate is meant to be collected
Keep it to himself, because the laboratory reports concentration per millilitre and volume does not count
Top the container up with sterile saline to the mark the instructions on the lid show him
Bring a second sample later the same day, since two samples are added together for the count
preguntas.explicacion: Clear instructions are given beforehand precisely so that all fractions of the ejaculate end up in the container, and any loss has to be reported when the sample is handed in. Volume itself is one of the measurements made. Because composition varies from one occasion to another, collecting 2 or 3 separate samples gives more accurate data, but they are analyzed separately, not pooled.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Incomplete semen sample · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · NCMA 2B.18

preguntas.pregunta: Which coagulation pathway is set off by trauma to the tissues around a vessel and is completed within seconds?
opciones: The extrinsic pathway, started by factor III
The intrinsic pathway, started by factor XII
The common pathway, started by factor X
The fibrinolytic pathway, started by plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: The extrinsic (tissue factor) pathway is the quicker and more direct one: damaged cells outside the bloodstream release factor III, thromboplastin, which with calcium and factor VII activates factor X, and the whole sequence takes seconds. The intrinsic pathway begins inside the blood when factor XII meets a damaged wall or a foreign surface and takes minutes. Both feed the common pathway.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Clotting Factors Involved in Coagulation; Extrinsic Pathway
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A tube reaches the laboratory with no label on it, and the courier says he knows which patient it came from. What does the CLIA specimen identification standard require?
opciones: Reject it, because positive identification has to hold from collection through to reporting
Accept it and label it from the requisition, since the courier can confirm where it came from
Accept it and note the discrepancy on the report as an unacceptable specimen condition found
Accept it when the order is stat, and label it once the ordering provider confirms the source
preguntas.explicacion: The written policies must ensure positive identification and optimum integrity of the patient's specimen from the moment it is collected or received until testing and reporting are finished, so a tube nobody can tie to a patient breaks the chain at its first link. A third party's recollection is not identification. Noting specimen condition on the report belongs to specimens the laboratory did accept.
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F.2 Specimen collection · CPT D1 1B k25 operational standards · NCMA Law and Ethics 12 · CCMA 7A k214

preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking an ACE inhibitor arrives with swelling of the lips and face. Why is this reaction treated as an emergency?
opciones: The swelling can reach the upper airway, and intubation may be needed to secure it
The swelling is the first stage of the dry cough that most treated patients develop
The swelling means potassium has risen, which is the commonest reaction to the class
The swelling marks the sulfonamide allergy shared with the thiazide in the tablet
preguntas.explicacion: Angioedema is rare with ACE inhibitors but can kill: the face, lips and upper airway swell in episodes, and the airway may have to be secured with an endotracheal tube. Treatment starts with stopping the drug, and the class is avoided in anyone with hereditary angioedema or a previous episode. Hyperkalemia is a separate reaction, reported in 2% to 6%, and it does not swell the face.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ACE Inhibitors", Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3

preguntas.pregunta: After a break-in the practice replaces the back door and its lock. Which addressable specification asks for that work to be documented?
opciones: Maintenance records, for repairs and changes to the parts of the building tied to security
Facility security plan, for keeping the premises and the equipment safe from tampering
Contingency operations, for reaching the building when information has to be restored
Access control and validation, for checking entry by role and for controlling visitors
preguntas.explicacion: Facility access controls carry four addressable specifications. Three of them plan access; the fourth, maintenance records, is about paperwork: policies to document repairs and modifications to physical components related to security, such as hardware, walls, doors and locks.
preguntas.subtema: Maintenance records · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.E.1.e · RMA II.B.5.b · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to publish counts of abnormal results for a quality project. What does the Privacy Rule say about de-identified health information?
opciones: There are no restrictions on its use or disclosure once it is genuinely de-identified
It may be used inside the organization but never released outside it in any form
It still requires a signed authorization from each patient whose result is counted
It may be released only under a business associate agreement with the recipient
preguntas.explicacion: Information that neither identifies a person nor gives a reasonable basis to identify one falls outside the Privacy Rule's restrictions altogether. There are two accepted routes to get there: a formal determination by a qualified statistician, or removing the specified identifiers of the individual, their relatives, household members and employers, provided the entity has no actual knowledge that what remains could still identify anyone.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, De-Identified Health Information
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CMAA 3C k36 · CCMA 7E k220

preguntas.pregunta: What is the Health Insurance Marketplace?
opciones: A service where people compare and enroll in plans, run federally or by a state
A service where insurers submit bids to the state to run managed care programs
A federal agency that reviews and approves the premiums insurers may charge
A network of clinics that treat patients whose income is below the poverty level
preguntas.explicacion: The Marketplace, also called the exchange, helps people shop for and enroll in coverage; the federal government runs it for most states and some states run their own. Applicants learn there whether they qualify for premium tax credits or for Medicaid and CHIP, and small employers use the SHOP Marketplace. Insurer bidding belongs to state managed care contracting, and the Marketplace is a service, not a rate-approving agency or a clinic system.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Health Insurance Marketplace
preguntas.subtema: Insurance fundamentals · CCMA 5 k181, k182 · RMA II.A.1

preguntas.pregunta: The patient cannot come in, so the advance written notice is read to her over the telephone. What has to follow?
opciones: A written copy at once, with the contact documented while the signed copy is awaited
No more than that, provided the office documents the telephone call in her record
A witness signature on her behalf, after which the original is filed as issued
A postponement of the service until she can attend and sign the notice in person
preguntas.explicacion: Where the notice cannot be issued in person it may go by telephone, e-mail, mail or fax under HIPAA policy, and the patient should not dispute the contact. A telephone contact has to be followed immediately by a hand-delivered, mailed, e-mailed or faxed notice; the contact is documented and the unsigned copy kept on file while the signed one is awaited.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Completing the notice
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186

preguntas.pregunta: A new tube brand asks for ten inversions on its insert while the poster on the wall says eight. What settles the number?
opciones: The number the local laboratory specifies for the tubes it has in use
The larger of the two numbers, since extra mixing carries no penalty
The smaller of the two numbers, since extra mixing produces haemolysis
The number printed on the poster, which follows the published sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Before tubes are sent, those holding an additive are inverted the number of times the local laboratory specifies, which is what the guidance points to when brands disagree. Neither extreme is safe on its own: overmixing can haemolyse the sample and too little mixing leaves small clots.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: What has to accompany a wound culture specimen when it goes to the laboratory?
opciones: A label made at the bedside and a request form noting any current antibiotic therapy
A label made at the nurses' station and a request form noting the last dressing change
A label made at the bedside and a request form noting the wound's measured dimensions
A label made in the laboratory and a request form noting the patient's temperature trend
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen is labeled in the presence of the patient, with details such as name, date, time, wound location and the site and source, precisely so it cannot be mislabeled. Current or recent antibiotic therapy is noted on the request form because it can alter the result, and where possible the culture is taken before antimicrobials are started. It travels in a biohazard transport bag.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.9 Checklist for Wound Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.i · NCMA 2B.20

preguntas.pregunta: Who must certify that a patient is terminally ill before the Medicare hospice benefit can begin?
opciones: The hospice doctor together with the patient's regular doctor, if there is one
The hospice medical director alone, after a face-to-face meeting with the family
Any two physicians enrolled in Medicare who have examined the patient that month
The attending clinician alone, since that clinician is the one who knows her best
preguntas.explicacion: To elect the benefit the patient needs Part A and must meet three conditions: the hospice doctor and the regular doctor, if the patient has one, certify a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 6 months or less; the patient accepts comfort care instead of care aimed at a cure; and the patient signs a statement choosing hospice. Only those doctors may certify.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Who's eligible and Provider requirements
preguntas.subtema: Hospice eligibility · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient raises a fist at the front-desk staff but does not strike. In tort terms this may be which of the following?
opciones: Assault: an intentional act creating apprehension of imminent harmful contact
Battery: harmful or offensive contact that actually occurs
Negligence: an unintentional failure to act as a reasonable person would
Strict liability: harm during a known dangerous activity, regardless of fault
preguntas.explicacion: Common law defines assault as an intentional act that creates a reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful or offensive contact; if the strike lands, battery is added to the assault. The example of a patient threatening front-desk staff and raising a fist is the one used to illustrate it, with the note that reasonableness matters, since a person several meters away would not yet cause apprehension. Negligence is unintentional, and strict liability attaches to inherently dangerous activities or defective products without regard to fault.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Assault vs battery · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31

preguntas.pregunta: How does the CDC sequence describe removing a mask at the end of doffing?
opciones: By the ties or straps behind the head, never by the front
By the front panel, pulling it down under the chin first
By the nose bridge, lifting it up and over the head
By the ear loops after untying the gown, keeping gloves on
preguntas.explicacion: The front or mouth area of the mask or respirator is never touched; it is removed by releasing the ties or straps around the back of the head, bottom ties first and then the top, lifting it away from the face, and discarded in the proper container. The front is considered contaminated, which is also why eye protection is lifted from behind the head. Gloves are the first item off, so they are already gone by the time the mask is removed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Removing PPE
preguntas.subtema: Mask removal · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: Under the OIG's seven elements, who has to receive compliance training and how often?
opciones: Board members, officers, employees, contractors and medical staff, at least each year
Only the employees who handle claims and coding, at least once every three years
Only the compliance officer and the compliance committee, at least twice each year
Everyone in the entity, but only after an audit or an investigation has found a fault
preguntas.explicacion: Training and education is the third element. All board members, officers, employees, contractors and medical staff should be trained at least annually on the entity's compliance program and its compliance risks, and the training reviews the applicable fraud and abuse laws. The compliance officer builds an annual plan that takes in whatever audits and investigations turned up.
preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 3: Training and Education
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k189 · NCMA 4.6

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the proposed additional vital signs is supported by evidence strong enough for routine use?
opciones: Pulse oximetry, whose value in detecting hypoxemia early is well established
Pain intensity, whose use as a fifth vital sign has been broadly maintained
Smoking status, which is treated as a physiologic measurement in its own right
Skin temperature from a wearable sensor, now recommended for every patient
preguntas.explicacion: The four traditional vital signs are temperature, pulse, blood pressure and respiratory rate. Of the parameters proposed as additions, only pulse oximetry and smoking status show a real effect on outcomes, and only oximetry counts as a physiologic measurement; smoking is better treated as a health risk factor. Pain as the fifth vital sign has largely been abandoned in the United States.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: What must the provider record about an adult patient's advance directive?
opciones: Whether or not one exists, in a prominent part of the current record
Whether or not one exists, in the billing file kept with the claim
The full text of the directive, scanned into the record within 90 days
The name of the agent, sent to the state survey and certification agency
preguntas.explicacion: The rule is that the provider documents in a prominent part of the patient's current medical record whether or not that individual has executed an advance directive. The state survey and certification agency is where complaints about these requirements are filed, not where agents are registered, and the 90-day clock belongs to updating information after a change in state law.
preguntas.subtema: PSDA · CCMA 7D k217, k219 · CMA E.8.d (E.7.c from 2027) · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: Integrated behavioral health care is also known by which other name?
opciones: Collaborative care, or primary care behavioral health
Accountable care, or the shared savings arrangement of Medicare
Managed care, or the point-of-service arrangement
Custodial care, or long-term services and support
preguntas.explicacion: Integrated behavioral health care blends into one setting the treatment of medical conditions and of the behavioral health factors that affect health. It is sometimes called behavioral health integration, integrated care, collaborative care or primary care behavioral health. Behavioral health itself covers mental health and substance use conditions, life stressors and crises, stress-related physical symptoms and health behaviors.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Academy for Integrating Behavioral Health and Primary Care: What is Integrated Behavioral Health?
preguntas.subtema: Collaborative care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1

preguntas.pregunta: Which scissors are described for dissection and tissue cutting, and which for cutting tissue and sutures?
opciones: Curved McIndoe scissors for dissection; Mayo scissors, curved or straight, for tissue and sutures
Mayo scissors, curved or straight, for dissection; curved McIndoe scissors for tissue and sutures
Curved McIndoe scissors for both, with Mayo scissors reserved for cutting oxidized cellulose
Mayo scissors for both, with curved McIndoe scissors reserved for trimming a mucoperiosteal flap
preguntas.explicacion: Scissors come in various shapes and sizes for cutting soft tissue, sutures, oxidized resorbable cellulose and dissected tissue, and different ones have different jobs: curved McIndoe scissors are preferred for dissection and cutting tissue, while Mayo scissors, with either curved or straight blades, are often used for cutting tissues and sutures.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Oral Surgery Instruments", Scissors
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.B.2.a

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and, out of habit, starts to push the cap back onto the used needle with both hands. Which OSHA rule does this break?
opciones: Contaminated needles are not recapped, bent or removed unless no alternative is feasible or a procedure requires it
Contaminated needles may be recapped with a one-handed technique whenever the phlebotomist finds it convenient
Contaminated needles may be sheared or broken with a mechanical device, but they may never be bent by hand
Recapping is permitted whenever the employer documents that it is faster than reaching the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(vii) forbids recapping, bending or removing a contaminated needle, and forbids shearing or breaking one outright, mechanical device or not. The only way around it is for the employer to show that there is no feasible alternative or that a specific medical or dental procedure demands it, and even then the job has to be done with a mechanical device or with one hand. Convenience and speed are not exceptions, and the one-handed technique is the method for the exception, not a general permission. The standard's own definition of a work practice control gives this very example: banning two-handed recapping.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) and (b), Definitions: Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Sharps safety and needlestick prevention · CPT D1 k30 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: Why do accreditation bodies treat a mislabeled blood specimen as one of the most dangerous laboratory errors?
opciones: Mislabeling can lead to a hemolytic transfusion reaction from incompatible blood
Mislabeling always causes hemolysis of the specimen during centrifugation
Mislabeling invalidates the CLIA certificate of the laboratory that reports the result
Mislabeling is the most common reason a specimen clots before it is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Identification errors can lead to inappropriate treatment, and a mislabeled blood specimen may end in a hemolytic transfusion reaction from incompatible blood; up to half of transfusion-related deaths trace back to identification error, and as many as 1 in 18 identification errors produce an adverse outcome. The error is about the patient, not about the specimen clotting or hemolyzing, and it does not by itself void a certificate.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.1, IPSG 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: What is a call-out meant to accomplish during a critical situation?
opciones: Inform every team member at once and name who acts
Confirm the receiver understood by repeating it back
Confirm the patient can restate the instructions given
Transfer responsibility and accountability to a team
preguntas.explicacion: A call-out communicates important or critical information: it reaches all team members at the same moment, helps them anticipate the next steps, and directs responsibility by name to the person who will carry the task out. Repeating back is the check-back, and moving responsibility is the handoff.
preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Call-Out
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · CMAA 2E k23

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the medical assistant's part in electrocardiography end?
opciones: At obtaining the tracing: the clinician reads and diagnoses
At reading the rate and rhythm: the clinician reads the rest
At flagging an abnormal wave for the patient to ask about
At writing a preliminary reading beneath the machine's own
preguntas.explicacion: In clinics and hospitals the recording is usually made by trained technicians and interpreted by clinicians, often confirmed by a cardiologist. Technicians are not expected to interpret, but they are expected to watch the tracing come out with a trained eye so lead problems are caught and fixed.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Personnel
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 3F4 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9

preguntas.pregunta: Among the preanalytical quality indicators tracked by that emergency laboratory, which one affected the largest share of samples?
opciones: An inadequate blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, near 35 %
The presence of a fibrin clot inside the tube, near 28 %
An insufficient volume of specimen, near 22 %
Visible or measured hemolysis of the serum, near 2 %
preguntas.explicacion: Ranked against the indicator set of the IFCC working group on laboratory errors, the sample-to-anticoagulant ratio was the worst at 34.9 %, followed by fibrin clots at 27.9 % and insufficient volume at 22 %. Hemolysis and contamination from an intravenous infusion sat at 2.2 % each and lipemia at 0.1 %. Under-filling is what drives the first three together.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: What does a nursing assistant usually have to do before working under that title?
opciones: Finish a state-approved education program and pass a state competency exam
Finish a one-year state-approved program and pass a licensing examination
Earn an associate's degree and register with the state board of nursing
Complete short on-the-job training only, since no state regulates the title
preguntas.explicacion: Nursing assistants often need to complete a state-approved education program and pass the state's competency exam to become licensed or certified, while orderlies typically have at least a high school diploma. Certification of unlicensed assistive personnel varies between jurisdictions. Assistants work mostly in hospitals and long-term care facilities.
preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Nursing Assistants and Orderlies — How to Become One
preguntas.subtema: Allied health roles · CCMA 1A k2

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen was left out overnight and the strip now reads a pH of 8.5. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: The specimen is stale and bacteria have split its urea, releasing ammonia
The specimen is stale and bacteria have consumed all the glucose it contained
The patient has been drinking cranberry juice, which pushes the pH upward
The patient is on a high-protein diet, which pushes the pH upward as well
preguntas.explicacion: Urine pH normally falls between 4.5 and 8, usually 5.5 to 6.5, and it is slightly acidic because of metabolic activity. The commonest reason for an alkaline reading is an old specimen in which bacteria have grown and broken urea down into ammonia. Bacteria metabolizing glucose push the pH down, not up, and cranberry juice and a high-protein diet are both listed among the causes of acid urine.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (pH)
preguntas.subtema: Alkaline stale urine · CPT D4 4G · PBT V.D.2 / V.A · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b · NCMA 2B.19

preguntas.pregunta: Where does V5 go?
opciones: Directly between V4 and V6, in line with both
Directly between V3 and V6, in line with both
Directly between V2 and V4, in line with both
In the mid-axillary line, one space lower down
preguntas.explicacion: V5 is placed straight between V4 and V6, and the three should be linear. The mid-axillary line belongs to V6, and the gap between V2 and V4 is where V3 goes, so mixing the two rules up shifts several electrodes at once and changes the pattern the provider sees.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4

preguntas.pregunta: A code in a category that has an applicable seventh character is reported with only six characters. What is wrong?
opciones: The code is invalid, since a code missing its applicable seventh character cannot be used
The code is valid, since the seventh character is added only when the payer asks for it
The code is valid, but the payer will pay it at a lower level of specificity than usual
The code is invalid, since every diagnosis code has to reach seven characters to be used
preguntas.explicacion: A code that has an applicable seventh character is considered invalid without it, and the character must always sit in the seventh position of the data field. Where the code is shorter than six characters, the placeholder X fills the empty positions so the seventh character lands in place. Codes of three to six characters are perfectly valid when their category calls for no seventh character.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.5
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient pays the full price of a test himself and asks that it not be reported to his health plan. What must the provider do?
opciones: Honor the request, since the care was paid out of pocket in full
Bill the plan anyway, because contracts require every claim
Honor it only if the privacy officer approves the exception
Ask the plan for permission before withholding the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Among the additions that came with the health information technology legislation, covered entities must acknowledge and fulfil a request that information not be shared with a health insurance plan when the individual has paid for that care out of pocket and in full. The same legislation requires an audit trail accounting for disclosures where electronic records are used, and gives patients an electronic copy of what those records hold.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Electronic Health Records
preguntas.subtema: Paying out of pocket · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35

preguntas.pregunta: Closed-loop communication is a three-step process. What happens in the third step?
opciones: The sender verifies the message was received correctly
The receiver passes the message to a second team member
The sender documents the exchange in the patient record
The receiver performs the task and reports back later on
preguntas.explicacion: First the transmitter sends the message to the intended receiver, using their name where possible. Second the receiver acknowledges receiving it out loud, asking for clarification if needed. Third the original transmitter verifies that it was received and interpreted correctly, which is what closes the loop.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Closed Loop Communication Training in Medical Simulation", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: How is a staple extractor used on a surgical staple?
opciones: Slide the lower tip under the staple, close the handle without lifting, then rock it free
Slide the lower tip under the staple, lift as the handle closes, then pull it straight out
Grip the crown of the staple in the jaws, twist the wrist, then draw the staple upward
Grip both ends of the staple with forceps, squeeze them inward, then lift the staple away
preguntas.explicacion: The lower tip goes beneath the staple, and the handle is closed without pulling up and without changing the angle of the wrist or hand. Closing it presses the middle of the staple down so both ends bend outward and lift free of the skin; only when both ends show is the extractor moved away and the staple released onto sterile gauze.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for her first virtual visit asks what telehealth actually means. Which description matches it?
opciones: Using communications technology to give health care from a distance
Using a portal to let a patient read the results of a laboratory test
Using a shared record so that two practices see the same chart notes
Using a telephone line to schedule a visit and confirm the insurance
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth is the use of communications technologies to provide health care from a distance, and those technologies may include computers, cameras, videoconferencing, the internet, and satellite and wireless communications. Examples run from a virtual visit by phone or video, to remote monitoring of a patient at home, to a screening reminder sent by text.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Telehealth: What is telehealth?

preguntas.pregunta: Which specimen counts as other potentially infectious material under the standard even when no blood is visible?
opciones: Cerebrospinal fluid from a lumbar puncture
Urine from a routine clean-catch collection
Sweat wiped from a feverish patient's brow
Tears from a patient with conjunctivitis
preguntas.explicacion: The definition of other potentially infectious materials in paragraph (b) names semen, vaginal secretions, cerebrospinal, synovial, pleural, pericardial, peritoneal and amniotic fluids, saliva in dental procedures, any fluid visibly contaminated with blood, and all fluids where types cannot be told apart, plus unfixed tissue and HIV or HBV cultures. StatPearls notes that universal precautions do not extend to sputum, feces, sweat, vomit, tears, urine or nasal secretions unless blood is visible in them, so those three become OPIM only when bloody.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's plan has a $2,000 deductible. What does that number mean for the patient?
opciones: The patient pays the first $2,000 of covered services before the plan starts to pay anything
The plan pays the first $2,000 of covered services and the patient pays the coinsurance on the rest
The patient's monthly premium for the coverage is $2,000, whether or not any services are used
The most the patient will pay in the plan year for covered services, after which the plan pays 100%
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the deductible as what the patient pays for covered care before the plan begins paying, and uses this very figure as its example: with a $2,000 deductible, the first $2,000 of covered services comes out of the patient's pocket, not the plan's. Once it is met, the patient usually still owes a copayment or coinsurance. The monthly payment owed whether or not care is used is the premium, and the yearly ceiling after which the plan pays 100% is the out-of-pocket maximum: two other glossary entries, two different numbers.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Deductible

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's income is above her state's Medicaid limit, but her medical bills are enormous. Which route may her state offer her?
opciones: A medically needy program, where the expenses she incurs spend her income down
A premium tax credit, which lowers what she pays for a plan on the Marketplace
A sliding fee discount, which lowers what a health center charges her directly
The Medicare Savings Programs, which pay premiums and cost sharing for her
preguntas.explicacion: States may set up a medically needy program for people with significant health needs whose income is too high for the other eligibility groups. Such a person becomes eligible by spending down: she incurs expenses for medical and remedial care she has no insurance for, and once those exceed the gap between her income and the state's standard, Medicaid picks up what is above it.

preguntas.pregunta: A choking adult loses consciousness while back blows and abdominal thrusts are being given. What comes next?
opciones: Lower the patient to the floor, start CPR, and look in the mouth first
Keep giving abdominal thrusts, now with the patient lying flat on the back
Raise the legs about 12 inches (30 cm) and wait for the ambulance to arrive
Give two rescue breaths and then check the pulse for up to 10 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Abdominal thrusts are for the conscious victim; the moment consciousness is lost, chest compressions take over. The patient goes onto a firm flat surface, CPR is started, and the mouth is inspected for the object before each set of breaths, taking out only what can be seen.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid

preguntas.pregunta: In a vacuum extraction system, what is the role of the barrel, also called the tube holder?
opciones: It holds the tube in place and shields the phlebotomist from direct contact with blood
It creates the vacuum that pulls the blood into the tube once the needle is in the vein
It retracts the used needle automatically in every model once the last tube is filled
It mixes the additive with the blood by rotating the tube as it fills
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 describes a double-ended needle whose rubber-cuffed end screws into the barrel (the tube holder, also called an evacuated tube needle holder or a bulldog); the barrel holds the sample tube in place and protects the phlebotomist from direct contact with blood. The vacuum is inside the tube itself, retraction into the barrel exists only in some systems, and mixing is done by inverting the tube afterwards.

preguntas.pregunta: A family worries that signing a DNR means their mother will stop being treated. What is accurate?
opciones: Comfort care and pain management continue; the standard of care is not lowered
Only nursing care continues; medications and tests are stopped at that point
Care continues, but the patient must be moved to a hospice unit within a day
Care continues only while the attending physician renews the order each shift
preguntas.explicacion: The idea that a DNR means do not treat is a common misunderstanding. Choosing a DNR or comfort-measures-only status does not reject the rest of medical care, and a DNR order does not lower the standard of care: comfort and pain management go on, and easing suffering is always appropriate. Patients can also name which resuscitative procedures they accept and which they refuse.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Do Not Resuscitate", Function; and StatPearls, "Advance Directives"

preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan denies a medicine because it requires prior authorization. What does the prescriber need to send for an exception?
opciones: A supporting statement explaining why the drug is medically necessary for this patient
A supporting statement listing the other drugs the patient took over the past year
A copy of the plan's drug list with the requested medication marked on the page
A new prescription written for a drug from the lowest cost-sharing tier instead
preguntas.explicacion: An exception is the plan's decision to cover a drug that is off its list or to waive a coverage rule. The patient or the prescriber must request it, and the prescriber has to supply a statement supporting the request: that the drug is medically necessary for this patient despite the rule, that another drug would harm the patient, or that another drug would be less effective. Sending a copy of the list or simply switching drugs is not an exception request.
preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan rules, Prior authorization

preguntas.pregunta: What marks a premature atrial contraction on the tracing?
opciones: An early P wave of odd shape with a normal QRS after it
An early P wave of odd shape with a wide QRS after it
An early wide QRS with no P wave in front of it at all
A missing P wave with the QRS arriving on time as usual
preguntas.explicacion: These beats start in atrial muscle outside the sinus node, so the P wave comes early and its shape and axis differ from the sinus P waves; it may be inverted or biphasic. The QRS is usually normal, and the PR interval can be shorter, longer or the same as in sinus beats.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Premature Atrial Contraction", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8

preguntas.pregunta: A manager reviews the practice's aging receivables. Which figure is the benchmark for claims left unpaid more than 90 days?
opciones: Less than 15% of the accounts receivable should sit beyond 90 days
Less than 50% of the accounts receivable should sit beyond 90 days
Less than 15% of the claims should be denied on their first submission
Less than 5% of the coding workload should wait in a queue at any time
preguntas.explicacion: The benchmark cited is that under 15% of claims should be more than 90 days old in accounts receivable, with submission errors, slow appeals and delayed payer processing behind the older balances. Denials typically run between 5% and 10%, and the target of less than 5% waiting in a queue belongs to coding productivity, so those figures answer different questions.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", AR more than 90 days

preguntas.pregunta: A baby born at 30 weeks of gestation is now 6 months old by the calendar. How are the growth parameters plotted?
opciones: By corrected age, taking off the weeks born early, and so on until age 2
By corrected age, taking off the weeks born early, and so on until age 1
By calendar age, accepting that the first points will sit low on the curve
By calendar age, on a separate chart drawn for babies born before 32 weeks
preguntas.explicacion: Growth parameters are corrected for gestational age by subtracting the number of weeks the baby was born preterm from the age since birth. For a baby born before 32 weeks that correction runs until 2 years of age; for one born between 32 and 36 weeks it runs at least until 12 months. Corrected age is what places the child at the right point on the curve.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Equipment: Growth Chart Correction for Prematurity

preguntas.pregunta: Two vaccines are to be injected into the same limb at one visit. How are the sites arranged?
opciones: Separated by 1 inch or more, so any local reaction can be told apart
Separated by 4 inches or more, so the two products cannot mix at all
Placed at the same spot, one after the other, to spare the patient a site
Placed with the second one below the first, no distance being specified
preguntas.explicacion: Each vaccine goes into a different injection site, and the sites are separated by an inch or more where possible, so that a local reaction can be attributed to the right product. For infants and young children, more than two injections in one limb should go into the thigh, which has more muscle. The most reactive products, such as DTaP and PCV13, go into different limbs where that can be arranged.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 6: Multiple Injections

preguntas.pregunta: What is the certificant entitled to when a disciplinary complaint is opened?
opciones: Written notice of the basis, a chance to submit evidence, and an appeal
Written notice of the basis and a hearing before a panel of three peers
Written notice of the basis and the identity of the person who complained
Written notice of the basis, after which the sanction takes effect at once
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure gives the certificant or applicant written notice of the basis for discipline or for denial of eligibility, an opportunity to submit written evidence about the alleged violations, a decision made by the certification director, and the chance to appeal that decision to an appeals panel established by the certifying board. Cooperating with the investigation is itself required.
preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Procedures for Adjudicating Alleged Violations

preguntas.pregunta: A frail 88-year-old has thin, fragile skin. What does the WHO say about adhesive strips in such patients, and how is the problem avoided?
opciones: Repeated strips can break down the skin in the very young and very old; use enough pressure and observe the site
Adhesive strips are mandatory for the elderly because their bleeding time is longer; apply two overlapping strips
Adhesive strips are avoided only in neonates; in the elderly a strip is applied and left for 24 hours
Adhesive strips are replaced by a pressure bandage wrapped around the arm for at least one hour
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 7, in its list of complications, names skin breakdown from repeated use of adhesive strips, particularly in very young or very elderly patients, and says it can be avoided if sufficient pressure is applied and the puncture site is observed after the procedure. Taped gauze or a bandaid over the gauze is the standard, not a wrapped pressure bandage.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice rewrites its password policy after moving to a hosted record system. What else does the documentation standard ask of it?
opciones: Reviewing the documentation periodically and updating it as operations change
Keeping the version it replaced for ten years counted from the day of the change
Obtaining a written acknowledgment from each patient that the policy has changed
Filing an amended notice of privacy practices with the Secretary within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: Security Rule documentation carries three required specifications: keep it for six years from creation or from the day it was last in effect, make it available to the people who have to carry the procedures out, and review and update it in response to environmental or operational changes. preguntas.pregunta: A staff member asks whether a fixative used in the laboratory is a suspected carcinogen. Which section of its safety data sheet answers that?
opciones: Section 11, which reports the listings and the toxicity figures
Section 8, which reports the exposure limits and the protection
Section 2, which reports the classification and the signal word
Section 15, which reports the regulations that apply to the product
preguntas.explicacion: Section 11 gathers the toxicological and health effects information: the likely routes of exposure, the immediate, delayed and chronic effects of short and long term exposure, numerical measures of toxicity such as the LD50, the symptoms from the mildest exposure to the most severe, and whether the chemical appears in the National Toxicology Program report on carcinogens, in the monographs of the International Agency for Research on Cancer, or has been found to be a potential carcinogen by OSHA.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reports to the state health oversight agency that her employer is reusing single-use devices, and her report includes patient information. How does HIPAA treat this?
opciones: It is protected when made in good faith to a health oversight agency about unlawful conduct
It is a breach of unsecured PHI that the employer must report to HHS within 60 days of discovery
It is permitted only if the patients signed authorizations first
It is permitted only if made to the news media, which is exempt from the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(j)(1) shields whistleblowers: a covered entity is not considered to have violated the rule when a workforce member or business associate, believing in good faith that the entity has acted unlawfully, violated professional standards or endangered patients, workers or the public, discloses PHI to a health oversight agency or public health authority, to an accreditation organization, or to an attorney consulted about the matter. The same section protects a workforce member who is a crime victim reporting limited information about the perpetrator. The media are not among the protected recipients.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient falls in the parking lot and the forearm is deformed and very painful. How is it immobilized?
opciones: With a splint or sling that holds the area above and below the injury
With a splint that presses on the deformity to bring the bone in line
With an elastic wrap around the wrist alone, tight enough to stop movement
With the arm strapped to the chest after the bone is straightened first
preguntas.explicacion: A broken bone is splinted as it lies, and the splint has to hold the area both above and below the injured bone; a rolled newspaper or strips of wood will serve. Nobody without the training lines up a fracture or tries to straighten a bone. Ice packs and elevation reduce pain and swelling while the patient waits.

preguntas.pregunta: Why must urine for culture be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or preserved?
opciones: Bacteria multiply in standing urine, raising colony counts and causing false-positive cultures
Bacteria die in standing urine, lowering colony counts and causing false-negative cultures
Leukocytes lyse in standing urine, so the culture would miss the pyuria that defines infection
The pH of standing urine falls, which inhibits the growth of the causative organism on the plate
preguntas.explicacion: The concern is growth, not death: colony-forming units that do not reflect the patient's true bladder urine rise while the specimen waits, which produces false-positive cultures and overtreatment. Studies found counts about 10 % higher after 4 hours at room temperature and more than 135 % higher after 24 hours. Leukocyte lysis is a urinalysis problem, and standing urine becomes more alkaline, not more acidic.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC4771218 LaRocco et al., Effectiveness of Preanalytic Practices on Urine Cultures (2016), Results (delayed processing)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses to choose an option or sign a properly issued advance written notice of non-coverage. What should the staff do?
opciones: Note the refusal on the original copy and keep it, and consider withholding the service
Sign the notice for the patient and enter the reason for the refusal in the record
Provide the service and bill the patient anyway, since the notice was properly issued
Reissue the notice after the service, dated the day the care was actually delivered
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient or the representative refuses to pick an option or to sign, the notifier annotates the original copy to record the refusal, may list witnesses although that is optional, and should consider not furnishing the item or service unless health, safety or civil liability make that impossible. Staff never sign for the patient, and a notice cannot be backdated to shift liability for care already given.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse asks whether the two blood culture sets must be spaced 30 minutes apart to be valid. What does the CDC identify as the most critical factor?
opciones: The volume of blood collected, more than the timing between sets
The interval between the sets across the 24-hour septic episode
The use of two different anatomic sites for the two sets
The transport time from the bedside to the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's procedure states that the volume of blood collected, not timing, is most critical, and its 2022 overview has the two sets drawn within a few hours of each other by peripheral venipuncture. preguntas.pregunta: Days in accounts receivable have climbed while patient volume stayed flat. What does that suggest?
opciones: Gaps in the billing process, such as submission errors or delayed appeals
A drop in the practice's charges, since fewer services were billed this month
A rise in the contractual adjustments the payers granted the practice
An improvement, since a higher figure means more claims are being filed
preguntas.explicacion: Days in accounts receivable usually stay steady or fall when patient volumes are consistent, so a rise without a matching rise in volume points to gaps in the revenue cycle. The causes named are claim submission errors, delayed appeals on denials, secondary insurance, and delayed workers' compensation settlements. A higher number means money is waiting longer, which is the opposite of an improvement.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient lists three reasons for the visit. How is the chief concern handled?
opciones: In the patient's own words, inviting them to state all of the concerns so the pressing one shows
As the single diagnosis that the assistant believes best explains the symptoms being reported
As the first symptom mentioned, because the opening statement is always the most significant
As a summary written afterward, once the examination confirms which finding is abnormal
preguntas.explicacion: The reason for the visit is recorded the way the patient says it, and it may be a symptom, a condition or a previous diagnosis. The first thing mentioned is not necessarily the most important one, so the patient is encouraged to name every concern while the interviewer watches for the detail that reveals the compelling problem. A diagnosis is not a concern.

preguntas.pregunta: The Korotkoff sounds are very faint in a thin older patient. Which maneuver is described to bring them out?
opciones: Raise the arm overhead for 30 seconds, opening and closing the hand, then inflate
Raise the arm overhead for 5 minutes, keeping the hand relaxed, then inflate
Lower the arm below the heart for 30 seconds so the vessels fill before inflating
Press the stethoscope harder into the antecubital fossa while the cuff deflates
preguntas.explicacion: Holding the arm above the head for about half a minute while the patient opens and closes the hand five to ten times sharpens the systolic sounds without changing the measured pressure; the arm is then brought back down and the reading proceeds normally. Pressing hard on the diaphragm is listed instead as a source of error.

preguntas.pregunta: At what time of day should a diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test begin?
opciones: Between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m., after the overnight fast
Any time of day, as long as the 8-hour fast is complete
Between 12:00 and 2:00 p.m., two hours after lunch
Between 4:00 and 6:00 a.m., before the patient's breakfast
preguntas.explicacion: The OGTT is a morning test that must begin between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m.: the fasting sample is drawn, the 75 g load is taken over about five minutes, and the second sample follows two hours later. The starting time is one of the listed conditions, together with the overnight fast, the three-day unrestricted diet, staying seated and not smoking. A fast alone does not make an afternoon OGTT valid.

preguntas.pregunta: A chart reads: the lesion is distal to the elbow. Where on the arm should you look?
opciones: Farther from the trunk than the elbow, toward the hand
Nearer to the trunk than the elbow, toward the shoulder
On the back of the arm at the level of the elbow itself
Deeper than the elbow joint, under the muscles of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Distal describes a position in a limb farther from the point of attachment or from the trunk, and proximal is its opposite. The hand is distal to the forearm; the upper arm is proximal to the forearm. A lesion distal to the elbow therefore sits somewhere between the elbow and the fingers.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is collecting her own anterior nares swab. Which mistake would spoil the specimen?
opciones: Holding the swab still in one spot of a single nostril for the whole collection
Rotating the swab in sweeping circles for 10 to 15 seconds in each nostril
Using the same swab in the second nostril with the same rotating technique
Sealing the swab in a sterile tube and then in the bag the provider supplied
preguntas.explicacion: For an anterior nares specimen the swab is rotated in four or five sweeping circles for 10 to 15 seconds, then moved to the second nostril and rotated the same way. Swabbing only one nostril, failing to rotate, or keeping the swab in a single spot all risk an inadequate sample. Afterward the swab goes into a sterile tube, which is closed and sealed in the bag provided.

preguntas.pregunta: A biller asks what electronic data interchange means when Medicare uses the term about claims.
opciones: The automated transfer of data in a set format and content between provider and Medicare
The conversion of a paper claim into an image that is stored inside the record
The movement of funds from the payer into the provider's own bank account
The list of code sets that were adopted for use in the standard transactions
preguntas.explicacion: Electronic data interchange is the automated transfer of data in a specific format, following specific rules about content, between a provider and Medicare or between Medicare and another health plan, and that transfer may pass through a clearinghouse or billing service. Both sides process transactions faster and more cheaply through it.

preguntas.pregunta: A swab for viral culture must be shipped to a distant laboratory. At what temperature is it transported to preserve the virus until inoculation or molecular testing?
opciones: Frozen at −70 °C
Frozen at −20 °C
Refrigerated at 4 °C
At room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Viral culture specimens travel frozen at −70 °C so that viral integrity survives until the culture is inoculated or molecular testing is done. The −20 °C figure is the freezer threshold for serum held for delayed serology, 2 to 8 °C is for serum awaiting prompt testing and for tissue sent to microbiology, and room temperature is reserved for CSF and body fluids whose organisms must stay viable for culture.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient stands up and the systolic pressure drops 22 mm Hg within two minutes. What does that meet?
opciones: The definition of orthostatic hypotension: a systolic fall of 20 mm Hg or more
The definition of orthostatic hypotension: a systolic fall of 30 mm Hg or more
No definition, since only a fall in the diastolic value is counted on standing
The definition of a hypertensive response, which is a change of 20 mm Hg either way
preguntas.explicacion: Orthostatic hypotension is a sustained fall of at least 20 mm Hg systolic, or at least 10 mm Hg diastolic, within three minutes of standing after lying down. More than 95% of cases are identified on the systolic figure alone, which is why it is the value most often reported.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Orthostatic Hypotension", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: Before applying a urine collection bag, how should the infant's genital area be cleaned?
opciones: Front to back on a female infant, and from the tip of the penis downward on a male infant
Back to front on a female infant, and from the base of the penis upward on a male infant who is uncircumcised
With an antiseptic solution on both, as is done before passing a catheter
With two sterile wipes on the labia and one on the glans, as in the adult clean-catch
preguntas.explicacion: The area around the urethra is washed thoroughly: from front to back on a girl and from the tip of the penis downward on a boy. Antiseptic cleansing is the preparation for a sterile catheterized sample, which a provider collects when a urinary tract infection has to be ruled out, and the two-wipe routine is the adult instruction. The only common risk of the bag is a mild rash from the adhesive.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses a dry powder inhaler that contains a corticosteroid. What should they do after each dose?
opciones: Hold the breath about ten seconds, then gargle and rinse the mouth with tap water
Hold the breath about ten seconds, then take the next puff with no pause between them
Breathe out into the device at once, then rinse the mouthpiece under hot running water
Wait five minutes without breathing deeply so the powder can settle in the airway
preguntas.explicacion: With a dry powder inhaler the patient exhales, seals the lips around the mouthpiece and inhales strongly and deeply, then holds the breath about ten seconds or as long as is comfortable and breathes out through pursed lips. Puffs are spaced one to five minutes apart. When the powder contains a corticosteroid, gargling and rinsing with tap water lowers the risk of a fungal infection in the mouth.

preguntas.pregunta: What must the record show after a visit conducted by video, according to the telehealth workflow?

That the patient waived her right to an in-person appointment for the same complaint
That the video was retained by the platform for the period the practice specifies
That the clinician held a license in every State where the practice has patients
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation is listed among the steps of the visit itself: the encounter is documented as a telehealth visit, and telehealth-specific billing codes or a modifier to the billing code are used when submitting for reimbursement. opciones: The National Patient Safety Goals
The Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments
The Bloodborne Pathogens standard
The Medication Guide program

preguntas.pregunta: A competent adult refuses a blood draw and the phlebotomist does not proceed. Which ethical principle is being honored?
opciones: Autonomy, respecting the patient's right to decide about their own care
Beneficence, doing what is in the patient's medical best interest
Justice, distributing resources equitably across patients
Nonmaleficence, avoiding actions known to expose the patient to harm
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights rest on a small set of ethical principles: valuing the patient's dignity, acting with goodwill to preserve life and autonomy, avoiding known harm, and distributing resources fairly. Respect for autonomy is the principle at work when a patient with capacity decides against advice; the clinician should still explain the reasons for the recommendation at the level a reasonable person would need, and document capacity, but the decision belongs to the patient. Beneficence is the principle that most often conflicts with it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction and Beneficence (conflicts with respect for patient autonomy)

preguntas.pregunta: A P wave in the inferior leads stands more than 2.5 mm tall. What does that point to?
opciones: Enlargement of the right atrium, known as P pulmonale
Enlargement of the left atrium, known as P mitrale
A first-degree block, from the delay inside the node
Sinus arrhythmia, from the swing in vagal tone
preguntas.explicacion: Amplitude past 2.5 mm in the inferior leads is the sign of right atrial enlargement, tied to chronic obstructive lung disease and to pulmonary hypertension. A left atrial abnormality reads differently: a P wave stretched past 120 ms, often with a notch in it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "P wave", Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: A single biological indicator is positive after an ethylene oxide cycle. How does the response differ from a steam sterilizer?
opciones: Everything since the last negative indicator counts as nonsterile and is retrieved and reprocessed
Everything in that one load counts as nonsterile, and earlier loads are released as usual
No items are retrieved, because low-temperature methods give positives more often than steam
Only the implantable items are recalled, exactly as they would be after a steam cycle
preguntas.explicacion: For methods other than steam the conservative approach applies: any positive is treated as a machine failure, and every item processed from the cycle that last gave a negative indicator up to the next satisfactory one is considered nonsterile, retrieved if possible and reprocessed. No action is needed only where there is strong evidence the indicator itself was defective or its medium contaminated.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations 16: Monitoring of Sterilizers

preguntas.pregunta: How is the child and adolescent immunization schedule meant to be used in the clinic?
opciones: By age first, then catch-up intervals, then medical indication, then the notes
By medical indication first, then by age, and the catch-up table only on request
By reading only the notes, which contain everything the tables would repeat
By reading only the table for the patient's age, since the rest is for programs
preguntas.explicacion: The schedule is worked through in order: Table 1 gives the recommended vaccine by age, Table 2 gives the interval for catch-up vaccination, and Table 3 covers additional vaccines needed for a medical condition or other indication. The notes then cover types, frequencies, intervals and special situations, and the appendix holds contraindications and precautions. The addendum carries new or updated guidance.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule 2025: How to use the schedule

preguntas.pregunta: Of the two main superficial veins of the arm, which one runs along the medial side, where it travels with an artery and a nerve?
opciones: The basilic vein of the arm
The cephalic vein of the arm
The median cubital vein
The brachial vein of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The cephalic vein drains mainly the radial side of the limb and the basilic vein the medial side, and the phlebotomy chapter stresses the need to tell the median cubital vein from the basilic vein, medial along the arm, because the basilic runs with the artery and nerve and a puncture there can be very painful. The WHO's Step 3 says the same of the basilic vein; the brachial vein is a deep vessel, not a superficial one.

preguntas.pregunta: A new patient's card says POS. Before booking him with a cardiologist, what does the office need?
opciones: A referral from his primary care doctor, which this type of plan requires
A written waiver of liability, which this type of plan requires up front
A signed assignment of benefits form, which this type of plan renews each year
A copy of the drug list, since this type of plan ties tiers to specialists
preguntas.explicacion: Point of service plans charge the patient less inside the network and, like an HMO, require the primary care doctor to refer the patient before a specialist visit. A waiver of liability is the Medicare advance notice used when denial is expected, not a scheduling step. Assignment of benefits is an intake form that lets the plan pay the office directly, and the drug list sorts covered medicines into tiers.

preguntas.pregunta: A term in the Alphabetic Index sits inside parentheses. What does the coder take from that?
opciones: It is a nonessential modifier and may be present or absent without changing the code
It is a manifestation code and is always to be sequenced after the etiology code
It is a synonym or alternative wording offered to explain the title of the code
It is an incomplete term needing one of the modifiers that follow it to be assignable
preguntas.explicacion: Parentheses enclose supplementary words that may be present or absent in the statement of a disease without changing the code assigned, and those words are the nonessential modifiers. Brackets do two other jobs: in the Tabular List they hold synonyms and explanatory phrases, and in the Index they mark manifestation codes. A colon follows an incomplete term.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the advantage of simple interrupted sutures over a running suture?
opciones: If one stitch fails or a spot infects, only that stitch has to be dealt with
They can be placed faster, which matters when bleeding has to be controlled quickly
They spread the tension evenly along the whole length of the wound as it is closed
They avoid piercing the skin at all, which gives the most acceptable cosmetic result
preguntas.explicacion: Separate stitches approximate skin and fascia better, give greater tensile strength and risk less injury to cutaneous circulation, and if infection appears the whole line does not have to come out. Running sutures are the fast option that spreads tension, but if the strand ruptures anywhere the entire length unravels. The technique that never pierces the skin is the subcuticular one.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Closure Techniques", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic introduces a new safety-engineered butterfly needle mid-year. The annual training was held four months ago. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Additional training covering the new exposure created, before the annual session comes around
No new training until the next annual session, because training is required only once a year
A full repeat of the annual training program, including the epidemiology of bloodborne diseases
A revision of the Exposure Control Plan in place of training, documented in the sharps injury log
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(v) requires extra training whenever changes such as new or modified tasks or procedures affect the employee's occupational exposure, and it allows that training to be limited to the new exposures. A new device changes how the task is done, so the clinic cannot wait for the next annual date, yet it does not have to repeat the whole program either. The plan review of (c)(1)(iv) is a separate duty that also applies, and the sharps injury log records injuries, not plan revisions.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(v), Information and Training

preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous vancomycin trough is ordered for a patient at steady state. What is the correct collection window?
opciones: Within the 30 minutes before the next dose is given
Within the 30 minutes after the infusion has finished
Within the 2 hours before the next dose is given
Within the 12 hours after the previous dose was given
preguntas.explicacion: Serum trough concentrations should be obtained within 30 minutes before a dose is administered, with the patient at steady state, which is usually reached after the third dose. The target trough varies with the indication and commonly runs from 10 to 20 mcg/mL. Drawing after the infusion gives a peak instead, and the 12-hour rule belongs to lithium and to the transplant drugs.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring

preguntas.pregunta: A patient stepped on a nail this morning. Which detail decides whether a tetanus booster is raised with the provider?
opciones: Whether the last tetanus shot was more than 10 years ago
Whether the wound is more than a quarter inch (0.64 cm) deep
Whether the puncture was rinsed within 5 minutes of the injury
Whether the wound bled freely or barely bled at all afterward
preguntas.explicacion: A puncture wound bleeds little but carries a higher risk of infection, and the provider is contacted if the patient has had no tetanus shot in the last 10 years; the vaccine is generally repeated every 10 years. Depth over a quarter inch, wounds on the face and wounds reaching bone are what raise the question of stitches instead.

preguntas.pregunta: Three injections are due at one visit and one of the vaccines is known to sting. In what order are they given?
opciones: The most painful one last, because pain builds with each injection
The most painful one first, while the patient is still least anxious
The most painful one in the middle, between the two milder products
The order does not matter, since the sites are separated by an inch
preguntas.explicacion: Some vaccines sting on injection, among them measles, mumps and rubella, pneumococcal conjugate and human papillomavirus. Because pain can increase with each injection, giving the most painful one last reduces the overall discomfort of the visit. Up to a quarter of adults fear needles, and most of those fears begin in childhood, so how the visit feels has consequences well beyond the day.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these, held by a medical office, is protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: A patient's e-mail address stored with the record of a visit the office billed last month
The personnel file the office keeps on a receptionist in its role as her employer
A student immunization list held by a school district under the education records law
A journal article on hypertension saved in the practice's shared clinical reference folder
preguntas.explicacion: PHI is individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity in any medium, and demographic data counts when it travels with information about care or payment. Common identifiers named in the rule include name, address, birth date and Social Security number. Employment records held by a covered entity as an employer, and FERPA education records, are expressly carved out.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Protected Health Information

preguntas.pregunta: Extraocular muscle function is being tested. How is it done?
opciones: An object held about 40 cm away is followed with the eyes, the head kept still
An object held about 40 cm away is followed with the eyes and with the head
An object held about 90 cm away is followed with the eyes, the head kept still
A light is shone into one eye and then the other while the pupils are watched
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits or stands with the head up, looking straight ahead, and follows a pen held about 16 inches, or 40 cm, in front of the face as it moves through eight directions, without turning the head. Cover and alternate-cover tests may be added. A little nystagmus at the extremes of gaze to the left or right is normal.

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn is diagnosed with Down syndrome. Which category of noninfectious disease does that example illustrate?
opciones: Congenital, a condition present at or before birth
Inherited, a genetic disease passed from a parent
Degenerative, a progressive irreversible loss of function
Nutritional deficiency, an impairment from a lack of nutrients
preguntas.explicacion: Noninfectious diseases are sorted by mechanism, each with a standard example: inherited with sickle cell anemia, congenital with Down syndrome, degenerative with Parkinson disease, nutritional deficiency with scurvy, endocrine with hypothyroidism, neoplastic with some cancers, and idiopathic where the cause is unknown.

preguntas.pregunta: What separates fever from hyperthermia?
opciones: In fever the hypothalamic set point itself is raised; in hyperthermia it is not
In fever the rise is driven by infection; in hyperthermia it is driven by drugs
In fever the rise is under 41 °C; hyperthermia is any value recorded above that
In fever the patient shivers; in hyperthermia the sweating response is intact
preguntas.explicacion: Fever is a controlled rise: pyrogens move the hypothalamic set point up and the body defends the new level. In hyperthermia the set point stays where it was and heat builds beyond what the body can shed, as in heat stroke or a drug reaction. That difference is why antipyretics work on one and not on the other.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through a draw the patient says, 'I feel hot and dizzy, and everything is going dim.' What do these symptoms represent?
opciones: The prodrome of syncope
The onset of a seizure
A povidone iodine reaction
Tourniquet hemoconcentration
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting may be preceded by dizziness, lightheadedness, diaphoresis, nausea and visual disturbances, and the vasovagal chapter adds warmth, tunnel vision, ringing in the ears and profuse sweating. These warning signs call for the patient to sit or lie down quickly with the legs raised. Hemoconcentration alters laboratory values and produces no symptoms; iodine affects results, not the patient's vision.

preguntas.pregunta: A strip shows narrow complexes with no P waves and gaps between beats that follow no pattern at all. How is the rhythm described?
opciones: Irregularly irregular, the hallmark of atrial fibrillation
Regularly irregular, the hallmark of atrial fibrillation
Irregularly irregular, the hallmark of a first-degree block
Regular but slow, the hallmark of a junctional escape rhythm
preguntas.explicacion: Sorting the spacing comes before naming anything: gaps with no pattern are irregularly irregular. Together with narrow complexes and no discrete P waves, that is what identifies atrial fibrillation, because only some of the atrial impulses get through.

Sixteen to eighteen
Twenty-one only
Twenty-three only

preguntas.pregunta: Of the medication errors traced to abbreviations in a national reporting program, which single abbreviation accounted for the largest share?
opciones: QD, for once daily, at about 43 percent of the errors
MSO4, for morphine sulfate, at about 43 percent of the errors
cc, for milliliter, at about 43 percent of the errors
HS, for at bedtime, at about 43 percent of the errors
preguntas.explicacion: Of roughly 30,000 abbreviation-related errors reported over three years, QD came first at about 43 percent, followed by U for units and cc for milliliters at roughly 13 percent each, then MS or MSO4 near 10 percent and HS around 3 percent. preguntas.pregunta: An assistant leaves a hemostat soaking in a high-level disinfectant with dried blood still packed in its hinge. Why is the result unreliable?
opciones: Organic matter ties up the germicide chemically and also shields microbes as a barrier
Dried blood raises the water hardness of the bath, and divalent cations slow the kill rate
The blood pushes the pH of the bath above the range where a glutaraldehyde stays active
Hinged instruments have to be kept closed while immersed so the outer surfaces get contact
preguntas.explicacion: Serum, blood, pus and lubricant interfere with a germicide in two ways: they react with it, so less active agent is left to attack microbes, and they physically cover the microbes. Hard water is a separate factor and comes from the water, not the soil, a rise in pH actually helps glutaraldehyde, and hinges are meant to be fully opened, not shut.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a biofilm on the inside of a device such a problem for disinfection?
opciones: Bacteria inside one can be up to a thousand times more resistant than the same bacteria loose
Bacteria inside one turn into spores, which is the only form a germicide cannot inactivate
Bacteria inside one keep dividing during the exposure, outrunning the kill rate of the agent
Bacteria inside one are shielded by salt crystals, which no detergent or enzyme can dissolve
preguntas.explicacion: A biofilm is a community of cells stuck tightly to a surface inside a coat of extracellular material, and it cannot simply be wiped away. Bacteria living in one can be up to a thousand times more resistant to antimicrobials than the same bacteria in suspension. Occlusion in salt crystals is a separate mechanism, and it belongs to inorganic soil.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Biofilms
