preguntas.pregunta: A routine urinalysis specimen was collected 30 hours ago and has been refrigerated the whole time. Can it still be tested?
opciones: No: even refrigerated, urine older than 24 hours cannot be used for urinalysis
Yes: refrigeration at 4 °C preserves urine for urinalysis for up to 72 hours
Yes, for the chemical strip only; particles must be examined within 1 hour of voiding
No: refrigerated urine must be tested within 4 hours, the limit for leukocyte assessment
preguntas.explicacion: Urine changes as soon as it is voided, so it should ideally be examined within the first hour; if that is impossible it is refrigerated at 4 °C for at most 24 hours, and a specimen older than that is not acceptable for urinalysis. European guidance sets particle examination at under 1 hour at room temperature or under 4 hours refrigerated, which is where the 4-hour figure comes from, but it does not extend the 24-hour ceiling to 72.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Transport and preservation

preguntas.pregunta: How much blood does an adult male typically have, and what share of adult body weight is blood?
opciones: 5 to 6 liters; about 8 percent of body weight
4 to 5 liters; about 8 percent of body weight
5 to 6 liters; about 5 percent of body weight
8 to 10 liters; about 10 percent of body weight
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is roughly 8 percent of adult body weight; adult men average about 5 to 6 liters and women 4 to 5 liters. The 4 to 5 liter figure is therefore the female value, not the male one. A 10 percent figure does exist in this material, but as the share of the blood volume that sits in the systemic arteries at any moment, not as a share of body weight.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops hives, itching and flushing about ten minutes after an injection. Which reaction type is this?
opciones: A type I hypersensitivity reaction, mediated by IgE and immediate in onset
A type II hypersensitivity reaction, in which IgG binds antigens on cells
A type III hypersensitivity reaction, driven by complexes and complement
A type A reaction, since itching follows from the pharmacology of the drug
preguntas.explicacion: Type I reactions are mediated by immunoglobulin E on mast cells and basophils and come on immediately: the first exposure builds drug-specific IgE, and re-exposure releases vasoactive and proinflammatory mediators, producing urticarial rash, pruritus and flushing, and in severe cases angioedema, hypotension and anaphylaxis. Type II reactions appear 5 to 8 days later and type III can take weeks.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adverse Drug Reactions", Function: Hypersensitivity reactions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.c

preguntas.pregunta: What weight does a bill of rights published by a health care organization carry?
opciones: It is not enforceable on its own, unlike a right written into regulation
It is enforceable once the organization publishes it and posts it publicly
It is enforceable in the states that have adopted it into their own statutes
It replaces the federal patient rights whenever the organization is accredited
preguntas.explicacion: Various American health care organizations wrote their own bills of rights starting in the 1970s, and those documents are not enforceable in themselves. What makes a right enforceable is a body with the authority to enforce it doing so: the rights a hospital must honor come from regulation, such as the federal conditions on notice, decision-making, privacy and grievances.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern; and 42 CFR 482.13

preguntas.pregunta: When can the safety mechanism of a manually retractable syringe NOT be used?
opciones: While the syringe holds blood and during the transfer into tubes
While the needle is still inside the vein and blood is flowing in
While the syringe is empty and before the venepuncture is started
While the device is held in one hand rather than in both hands
preguntas.explicacion: The mechanism draws the needle back into the syringe, which lowers the danger of a stick and stops the device being reused, but it cannot be activated while the syringe is full of blood or during the transfer of that blood. Self re-sheathing devices carry the same limitation.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Manually retractable syringes

preguntas.pregunta: Who is a hospital expected to reach with the electronic notifications it sends when a patient arrives at or leaves its emergency department?
opciones: The patient's established primary care practitioner or the practice he names
Every provider who has treated the patient during the previous twelve months
The patient's health plan, which coordinates the rest of the care from there
The state health department, which forwards the message to the care team
preguntas.explicacion: Notifications go out at registration in the emergency department, at admission, and at discharge or transfer, and the hospital must make a reasonable effort to send them to the applicable post-acute care providers and to the patient's established primary care practitioner, practice or whichever clinician the patient names as primarily responsible.

preguntas.pregunta: Hospital surveillance data show that percutaneous injuries cluster in which two moments of the work?
opciones: About 38% happen during use of the device and 42% after use, before disposal
About 62% happen while the container is being replaced by housekeeping
Nearly all happen during disposal, once the device is inside the container
About one quarter happen during use and the rest while recapping needles
preguntas.explicacion: Injuries do not wait for the sharps container. Surveillance in participating hospitals puts roughly 38 percent of percutaneous injuries during the use of the device and 42 percent in the gap between finishing with it and getting rid of it. That is why safe handling has to be planned before the procedure starts. Among hollow-bore needle injuries the largest single cause is manipulating the needle in the patient, at 27 percent, with disposal-related causes at 12 percent and recapping down to 5 percent.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Preventing Needlestick Injuries in Health Care Settings, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries and Figure 2

preguntas.pregunta: Medicare paid a claim as the primary payer and it later turns out an employer group plan should have. Which entity pursues the money?
opciones: The Commercial Repayment Center, which seeks it from the employer and the group plan
The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, which seeks it from the patient herself
The Medicare Administrative Contractor, which seeks it from the billing provider
The Commercial Repayment Center, which seeks it from the patient's own attorney
preguntas.explicacion: When new information shows Medicare made a primary payment by mistake, recovery follows. Where a group health plan turns out to be the proper primary payer, the Commercial Repayment Center goes after the employer and the plan. The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center handles mistaken liability, no-fault and workers' compensation payments, where it is the beneficiary who has to repay Medicare.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, Coordination of Benefits & Recovery Overview
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185

preguntas.pregunta: A drug is described as having an elimination half-life of six hours. What does that number mean?
opciones: In six hours the amount in the body falls to half of what was there at the start
In six hours the whole dose has been cleared from the body through the kidneys
In six hours the drug reaches the highest concentration it will have in the plasma
Six hours is the time the drug needs to be absorbed and reach the circulation
preguntas.explicacion: The elimination half-life is the time a substance needs to drop to half the amount present in the body, and the principle holds for every drug: one half-life removes 50% of what was there. The figure is used to work out excretion rates and steady-state concentrations, and it can be derived from the elimination rate constant or from the volume of distribution and the clearance. Absorption and peak concentration are separate parameters.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Elimination Half-Life", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k21 · RMA III.G.1.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these organizations has to follow the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules as a covered entity?
opciones: A clinic that bills insurers electronically for the laboratory tests it collects
A life insurer that keeps the results of the physicals it required of applicants
An employer that stores the pre-employment drug screens run on its new drivers
A school district that keeps immunization records on file for every student
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities are health plans, health care clearinghouses, and health care providers who transmit health information electronically in connection with a standard transaction such as a claim. Life insurers, employers, workers compensation carriers, most schools and most law enforcement agencies hold health information about people and are simply not covered by these two rules.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Your Rights Under HIPAA, Who Must Follow These Laws
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.5 comply with HIPAA · NCMA Law and Ethics 3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: A patient loses blood pressure minutes after an injection of a new medicine, with hives and wheezing. Which type of shock is this?
opciones: Distributive shock, of the anaphylactic subtype
Hypovolemic shock, of the non-hemorrhagic subtype
Obstructive shock, from impaired filling of the heart
Cardiogenic shock, from an arrhythmia after the drug
preguntas.explicacion: Anaphylactic shock is grouped with the distributive causes, where the vessels dilate at the periphery: an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction produces cardiovascular collapse and respiratory distress from bronchospasm within seconds to minutes of the exposure. Drugs, foods, insect stings and latex are the common triggers.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Shock", Etiology: Distributive Shock
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives underweight and unwashed, with medications that were never refilled. Which category fits, and what follows?
opciones: Neglect, and the case is reported even though it is only suspected
Neglect, and the case is reported once the findings are confirmed
Financial abuse, and the case is referred to the hospital's legal team
Psychological abuse, and the case is handled by the social work team
preguntas.explicacion: Neglect is the caregiver's failure to meet obligations to the older adult: withholding food, water, clothing, medication refills or assistive devices. It shows up as being underweight or dehydrated, poor hygiene, dirty clothing and overgrown nails. Reporting is done even when the abuse is only suspected and not proven, so that Adult Protective Services can investigate.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Elder Abuse", Introduction; and Treatment/Management
preguntas.subtema: Signs of abuse · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c (E.5.b from 2027) · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43

preguntas.pregunta: Which drug is listed as a Schedule II narcotic?
opciones: Hydromorphone
Buprenorphine
Carisoprodol
Alprazolam
preguntas.explicacion: Hydromorphone appears among the Schedule II narcotics, along with methadone, meperidine, oxycodone, fentanyl, morphine, opium, codeine and hydrocodone; amphetamine, methamphetamine and methylphenidate are the Schedule IIN stimulants. Buprenorphine is Schedule III, and alprazolam and carisoprodol are Schedule IV. All four are controlled, so it is the schedule and not the mere fact of control that sets the rules.
preguntas.fuente: DEA Diversion Control Division, Definition of Controlled Substance Schedules: Schedules II-IV

preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses a blood draw. Which list gives the four components used to assess decision-making capacity?
opciones: Understanding, a clear and consistent choice, appreciation, and reasoning
Disclosure of information, competency, voluntariness, and full documentation
Orientation, short-term memory, attention span, and language fluency
Understanding, a signed refusal form, a witness, and a stable diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: The four, in order: the patient shows understanding of the situation and the decision; expresses a clear, consistent choice; shows appreciation, that is, applies the facts to their own case; and reasons, inferring consequences and explaining the refusal. Forms and witnesses are not components, and disclosure and voluntariness are elements of research consent.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's cultural practice does not interfere with the treatment plan. What is the approach?
opciones: Accommodate it, since the plan is not adversely affected
Set it aside until a provider signs off on it in the chart
Document it as a partial refusal of the plan of care
Ask the patient to choose between the practice and care
preguntas.explicacion: Cultural negotiation is a reciprocal, collaborative search for a mutually acceptable way to handle competing interests between the care given, the care prescribed and the patient's cultural needs. When the cultural need does not significantly or adversely affect the treatment plan, it can be accommodated.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, III Glossary; and 3.6 Culturally Sensitive Care

preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation specimen reaches the bench looking cloudy and pink. Which appearances lead the laboratory to ask for another draw?
opciones: Marked haemolysis, lipaemia or icterus in the separated plasma
Marked haemolysis only, since fat and pigment do not interfere
A pale plasma layer, a small gel plug or a warm collection tube
A specimen that reached the bench in under two hours of the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Guidance for clotting assays is to discard specimens showing excess haemolysis, lipaemia or icterus, because all three interfere with clot formation or with the light the analyser reads. Most such errors start before analysis, which is why an abnormal result is repeated on a fresh sample.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: How much may keeping an infant warm raise the rate of blood flow, according to the WHO?
opciones: By as much as sevenfold
By as much as twofold
By about one quarter
By as much as tenfold
preguntas.explicacion: Keeping the child warm may increase the rate of blood flow by as much as seven times, which is why as few clothes as possible are removed, an infant is swaddled in a blanket, and the parent or carer holds the baby with only the limb for the puncture left exposed. Warm cloths over the puncture area help dilate the vessels as well.

preguntas.pregunta: What happens if a subpoena to appear is ignored?
opciones: It may be punished as contempt, unless the material is privileged
It may be punished as a misdemeanor after a second notice is served
It is dismissed, because compliance is voluntary for medical staff
It is referred to the licensing board, which decides on the sanction
preguntas.explicacion: A subpoena is a written order compelling a person to give testimony on a subject at a stated time and place, or to produce documents or other tangible things, whether for a deposition, a trial, a congressional inquiry or another hearing. Failing to comply can be punished as contempt. If the testimony or the documents are privileged, the person is not required to comply.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has cleaned the site and is about to insert the needle. What is expressly forbidden at that moment?
opciones: Laying a finger over the vein to guide the shaft of the needle
Asking the patient to make a fist so the vein stands out more
Anchoring the skin with the thumb placed below the puncture
Waiting for the alcohol to dry before the needle goes in
preguntas.explicacion: After disinfection the site is not touched, and the example spelled out is placing a finger over the vein to steer the exposed needle. If the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. Making a fist and anchoring below the site are both part of the correct technique.

preguntas.pregunta: Which opening question does the WHO interview script use before it asks about fear of needles?
opciones: Have you ever had blood taken before, and how did it feel?
Have you had any food or drink within the last two hours?
Are you allergic to latex, to povidone iodine or to tape?
Have you ever fainted when your blood was being drawn?
preguntas.explicacion: The script seats the patient and then runs through a short set of questions: whether they have had blood taken before and, if so, how it felt and how long ago; whether they are scared of needles; allergies, with latex, povidone iodine and tape named; whether they have ever fainted during a draw; and whether they have eaten or drunk in the past two hours.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long the practice must keep her chart under HIPAA. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: HIPAA sets no retention period for medical records; State law generally governs that
HIPAA sets six years, the same period it applies to its own policies and notices
HIPAA sets seven years from the date of the last service the patient received
HIPAA sets five years, the period Medicare applies to hospital medical records
preguntas.explicacion: OCR answers this directly: the Privacy Rule contains no medical record retention requirement, and State laws generally govern how long records are kept. What the rule does require is that appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards protect the privacy of records for as long as the entity keeps them, disposal included. The six, seven and five year figures come from other rules.

preguntas.pregunta: In what order are the four flaps of a wrapped sterile kit opened?
opciones: The flap away from the body first, then each side flap, then the one nearest the body
The flap nearest the body first, then each side flap, then the one away from the body
Both side flaps first, then the flap away from the body, then the one nearest the body
The flap away from the body first, then the one nearest the body, then both side flaps
preguntas.explicacion: The far flap is opened first, touching only its very edge, then each side flap one at a time using one hand, and the flap closest to the body last. Opening the near flap last keeps the practitioner from leaning across what is already exposed, and already-opened corners are held so they cannot spring back into the sterile area.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b · NCMA 2B.11

preguntas.pregunta: Within the pancreatic islets, which cells make insulin and which make glucagon?
opciones: Beta cells make insulin; alpha cells make glucagon
Alpha cells make insulin; beta cells make glucagon
Delta cells make insulin; beta cells make glucagon
Beta cells make insulin; delta cells make glucagon
preguntas.explicacion: The pancreas is mostly an exocrine gland, but its islets are endocrine. Beta cells, about 75 percent of each islet, release insulin when blood glucose climbs; alpha cells, about 20 percent, release glucagon when it falls. Delta cells make somatostatin, which holds both of the others back.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.9 The Endocrine Pancreas, Cells and Secretions

preguntas.pregunta: A fasting outpatient asks what she should bring to her early appointment. What is suggested?
opciones: A snack, since feeling light-headed after a fasting draw is common
A sugary drink, to be taken half an hour before the first tube
A list of the tests, because the form is not sent to the station
No food at all, because eating waits until the results come back
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may eat as soon as the test is over, and because feeling light-headed after a fasting draw is common they may want to bring something to eat straight away. A sugary drink beforehand would break the fast: only plain water is allowed, and even flavoured carbonated water is ruled out because it may hold sugars or sweeteners.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic adds better lighting, transparent doors, cameras and weapons screening. Which type of violence do those measures reduce?
opciones: Type I, the violence that comes with criminal intent
Type II, the violence from patients and their visitors
Type III, the violence between colleagues and staff
Type IV, the violence tied to a personal relationship
preguntas.explicacion: Environmental measures work by deterrence, and they cut type I incidents and the number of weapons brought in. The pitfall is spelled out: they do not reduce type II violence, which is impulsive and contextual rather than planned, and neither visibility nor physical barriers stop verbal abuse. Types III and IV are not what the doors and cameras address.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Pearls and Other Issues: Environment

preguntas.pregunta: A practice keeps sending patients to a specialist who never sends any information back. What does the toolkit advise?
opciones: Stop referring there; destinations that return nothing should not keep receiving patients
Keep referring there and ask the patient to carry the report back each time
Keep referring there but require the patient to sign a release beforehand
Stop referring there only if patients also report long waits for appointments
preguntas.explicacion: Practices are told to identify, build and keep up relationships with the places they refer to, and to stop referring to clinicians who fail to send information back, who cannot give patients timely appointments, or who consistently draw negative reports from patients. preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 21: Refer patients to clinicians who coordinate care with you

preguntas.pregunta: An oximeter reading does not match the rest of the clinical picture. What quick step is described for checking the device?
opciones: Place the probe on the clinician's own finger to confirm the equipment is working
Restart the device, since the calibration is reset only when the power cycles
Change the probe to the opposite hand, because the reading always differs by side
Cover the whole limb, since ambient light reaching the skin is the usual culprit
preguntas.explicacion: When a value looks wrong, the probe can be put on the clinician's own finger to see whether the device itself is at fault. Ambient light does interfere, and the answer to that is to cover the probe or the site, not the whole limb. Readings should be followed as trends and acted on when they clash with the findings.

preguntas.pregunta: What temperature range is acceptable for a urine specimen in a federal drug test, and how soon must it be read?
opciones: 32° to 38°C (90° to 100°F), read within 4 minutes of the void
35° to 39°C (95° to 102°F), read within 4 minutes of the void
32° to 38°C (90° to 100°F), read within 30 minutes of the void
20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F), read within 15 minutes of the void
preguntas.explicacion: The collector reads the temperature after receiving the specimen and does it within four minutes of the void; the acceptable band is 32° to 38°C, that is 90° to 100°F, and the thermometer must be able to read across that range without touching the urine. Waiting longer lets the specimen cool out of range and forces an observed collection that would not otherwise have been needed.

preguntas.pregunta: Which devices make up the open systems of blood sampling?
opciones: Needles with syringes, and winged steel needles joined to a syringe
Needles with syringes, and winged steel needles joined to vacuum tubes
Vacuum tubes with a holder, and winged steel needles joined to a syringe
Vacuum tubes with a holder, and retractable lancets used on the fingertip
preguntas.explicacion: Open systems are the hypodermic needle with a syringe and the winged steel needle attached to a syringe. Closed systems, which are preferred because they have proved safer, are the ones where the blood goes straight into the tube without being transferred by hand.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a statute of limitations do to a claim?
opciones: It bars the claim once a set period has passed after the injury
It caps the money a court may award once the claim is proven
It moves the claim from a state court to a federal court instead
It suspends the claim while the defendant's licence is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: A statute of limitations is any law that shuts the door on claims after a certain period following an injury, and how long that period runs depends on the jurisdiction and the type of claim. The clock may start on the date of the injury, the date it was discovered, or the date it would have been discovered with reasonable effort. Civil and criminal actions both have them.

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample shows no visible hemolysis, yet its plasma hemoglobin is just under 0.5 g/L. According to the study by Koseoglu and colleagues, which results can already be clinically altered?

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient with no wristband arrives at the draw station. Which pair satisfies the two-identifier requirement?
opciones: The full name the patient states and the telephone number held on file
The full name the patient states and the number of the chair she uses
The assigned identification number, read twice off the requisition form
The full name on the requisition and the tests printed underneath it
preguntas.explicacion: The goal accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another person-specific identifier, and asks for at least two of them whenever specimens are collected for clinical testing. preguntas.pregunta: Staff leave a message on a patient's home answering machine about a lab result. What governs how much may be said?
opciones: The minimum necessary standard and the reasonable safeguards the rule requires
The accounting of disclosures, which must list the message before it is left
The patient's written authorization, needed before any message may be left
The rule on marketing communications, which limits unsolicited contacts
preguntas.explicacion: Messages left where someone else may hear them are the classic incidental disclosure: permitted as a by-product of a use the rule allows, provided the entity has applied reasonable safeguards and the minimum necessary policies to the underlying disclosure. An incidental disclosure resulting from a failure to apply either one is not permitted.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: General Provision
preguntas.subtema: Telephone messages · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.a · CMAA 7F k94 · NCMA 3.2

preguntas.pregunta: What is never permitted when a restraint is ordered?
opciones: Writing it as a standing order or on an as-needed basis
Writing it as a modification to the patient's plan of care
Writing it by a licensed practitioner other than the attending
Writing it after less restrictive measures have been tried
preguntas.explicacion: Orders for restraint or seclusion may never be written as standing orders or PRN. They do go into a written modification of the plan of care, and they may come from a physician or another licensed practitioner responsible for the patient and authorized by hospital policy, with the attending consulted as soon as possible. They are only used after less restrictive interventions have failed.
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights and restraint · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum shows a very high hemolysis index and the CRP is rejected; a repeat heel sample two hours later has a low index and a reportable CRP. What does this pattern indicate?
opciones: The first hemolysis was in vitro, produced during a difficult collection, not by disease in the patient
The newborn has intravascular hemolysis that resolved spontaneously between the two collections
The first sample was contaminated by intravenous fluid, which diluted the C-reactive protein
The analyzer's hemolysis index was miscalibrated on the first run and corrected on the second
preguntas.explicacion: In the newborn series, hemolysis indices were far higher than in patients with documented severe intravascular hemolysis, which pointed to in vitro hemolysis from complicated blood collection; every CRP rejected for severe hemolysis became reliable after a repeat sampling. A true in vivo process would not vanish in two hours, and the index is an automated measurement, not the part that failed.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A cyclosporine level is ordered on a transplant patient. Which specimen does the laboratory accept for that test?
opciones: Whole blood collected in EDTA
Serum from a tube without gel
Heparinized plasma kept on ice
Serum separated and frozen at –20 °C
preguntas.explicacion: For cyclosporine monitoring only whole blood in EDTA is accepted. Serum without gel is what the source recommends for drugs such as phenytoin, ice and darkness are the methotrexate rule, and frozen serum is the storage advice for delayed serological testing, so each distractor is a correct instruction for another specimen. Specimen type is the first acceptability criterion a processor checks.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k129 k139 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)

preguntas.pregunta: Blood drawn into a syringe is being transferred into several tubes. Why does the sequence of tubes still matter?
opciones: Additive left on the needle can be carried into the tube filled next
The vacuum of each tube is spent in the sequence printed on its label
The plunger has to be pressed harder for every tube after the first
Serum tubes clot faster whenever they are filled after additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: One route of contamination described for tube collection is anticoagulant sticking to the needle and passing into the next tube, so a transfer from a syringe is not exempt from the sequence. The order published by the WHO is given for vacuum tubes and for syringe and needle alike.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k54 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.F · CCMA 3E6 k132 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: An injection has just been given. What happens to the needle and syringe?
opciones: The safety shield goes on and the unit goes into a sharps container, uncapped
The cap goes back on with one hand and the unit goes into a sharps container
The needle is snapped off and the syringe goes into the ordinary waste bin
The unit is set on the tray until the visit is over and then carried to disposal
preguntas.explicacion: The needle is not recapped, because recapping is how people puncture themselves. The safety shield attached to the needle is applied instead, and the syringe and needle go into a sharps container. Gloves come off afterwards and hand hygiene follows. Many needles carry these shields precisely to prevent needlestick injuries, and prefilled syringes cut the same risk further back in the process.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5: Description of Procedure, and ch. 18.3: Needles
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.j · NCMA 1.9

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who says she has no immigration papers hesitates at the consent form. What does the guidance note here?
opciones: Fear of deportation can make patients hesitate to sign consent forms
Consent from a patient without papers must be witnessed by two staff
A verbal consent will not stand for a patient who declines to sign
The form is set aside and the draw is recorded in the chart as refused
preguntas.explicacion: Among the cultural differences that complicate consent, the text notes that undocumented immigrants might hesitate to sign consent forms out of fear of deportation. Consent is a communication process rather than a signature, the WHO obtains verbal consent for a routine draw, and hesitating over a form is not the same thing as refusing the test.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Cultural Differences; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A 2F k17 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A first heel-prick yields too little blood. The phlebotomist wants to reuse the same lancet on the same spot. What is the rule?
opciones: Do not puncture more than once with the same lancet or reuse a site: it can cause bacterial contamination and infection
A second puncture with the same lancet is acceptable if the site is cleaned again with alcohol and allowed to dry
The same lancet may be reused once on the other heel, since the blade has touched only that patient's skin
Reusing the site is preferred, because a fresh puncture nearby raises the risk of osteomyelitis of the calcaneus
preguntas.explicacion: There are two prohibitions for the lancet: do not puncture the skin more than once with the same lancet, and do not use a single puncture site more than once, because either can lead to bacterial contamination and infection. A surgical blade is also never used for a skin puncture. Osteomyelitis of the heel bone is listed as a complication of capillary sampling, not as a reason to reuse a site.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 one lancet, one puncture · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)

preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is named as an improper way to obtain consent for a procedure?
opciones: Taking it while the patient is medicated or in the preoperative holding area
Taking it in the office days ahead, with time for the patient to ask questions
Taking it with an interpreter present when the patient's language differs
Taking it with the teach-back method used to check what the patient understood
preguntas.explicacion: Consent obtained shortly before the procedure, in the preoperative holding area, or from a patient who is medicated or nearly asleep is named as improper. The recommended setting is a clinic or office with time to ask questions and process emotions. Interpreters, including sign language interpreters, and the teach-back method are what make the process sound.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA II.E.3 · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old arrives alone for a blood draw her physician ordered. Who normally agrees to the procedure on her behalf?
opciones: A parent or legal guardian, in a process properly called informed permission
The patient herself, since a minor who understands a procedure may agree to it
The ordering physician, who decides for any patient younger than eighteen years
A parent or guardian, unless the phlebotomist judges the patient mature enough
preguntas.explicacion: Children under 18 generally cannot give informed consent; a parent or legal guardian permits the intervention, and that process carries the name informed permission. The exception is the legally emancipated minor, for example one who is married, serving in the military, financially independent, or a mother. Which minors qualify is a matter of state law, not of a bedside judgment about maturity.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Children
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2G · CCMA 7B k216 minors · CMA II.E.3.c exceptions · CMAA 3D k40 consent

preguntas.pregunta: For an adult finger-prick, which fingers are recommended, and which are avoided?
opciones: The middle and ring fingers; the thumb and index have calluses and the little finger has thin tissue
The index and middle fingers; the ring and little fingers are too close to the ulnar nerve branch
The thumb and index finger; the middle and ring fingers have the thinnest tissue over the bone
Any finger except the thumb; the little finger is preferred because it is the least sensitive
preguntas.explicacion: The fingers to puncture are the second and third, meaning the middle and ring fingers, as the ones to puncture. The thumb and index finger are avoided because of calluses, and the little finger because its tissue is thin. The lancet goes on the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the lines of the fingerprint. The finger is the usual capillary site in an adult.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 finger selection · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)

preguntas.pregunta: When is vancomycin usually at steady state, the condition for a valid trough?
opciones: After the third dose
After the first dose
After the fifth dose
After 24 hours of therapy
preguntas.explicacion: Steady state is typically achieved after the third dose of vancomycin, and trough levels are ideally drawn within 30 minutes before a dose under those conditions. The drug's terminal half-life is 4 to 6 hours in adults with normal kidneys and lengthens with renal dysfunction, which is why timing is tied to doses rather than to the clock.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", sections Pharmacokinetics and Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: Which devices should a facility replace first when it plans which safety products to bring in?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles that enter a vein or artery
Solid suture needles used in the operating room
Glass capillary tubes used at the patient's side
Lancets used for finger and heel sticks in clinic
preguntas.explicacion: Priorities are set from data: how injuries are happening in that institution, which devices are used there, and what local and national figures say about injury and disease transmission. The highest priority goes to the devices with the greatest impact on preventing occupational infection, and those are the hollow-bore needles used in veins and arteries, the ones that carry blood. The team that makes these decisions is multidisciplinary and includes the workers who use the devices.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features, step 2
preguntas.subtema: Setting priorities · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory collects blood cultures into evacuated tubes instead of bottles. Does the septum disinfection step still apply?
opciones: Yes: the rubber septum of the evacuated tubes is disinfected the same way
No: evacuated tubes are supplied sterile and their stoppers need no prep
No: the alcohol used on a stopper interferes with the culture broth
Yes, but sterile saline is used on tubes and alcohol only on bottles
preguntas.explicacion: The step covers the rubber septum on the blood culture bottles or on the evacuated tubes alike, disinfected with 70% isopropyl alcohol, and it comes after the venipuncture site is disinfected and before the first set is drawn. Skipping it on tubes leaves the same route for skin organisms that disinfecting a bottle top is meant to close, and contaminated cultures cost the patient unnecessary antibiotics.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, SOP model steps 2 and 3
preguntas.subtema: Bottle preparation · CPT D4 4A k79 blood culture bottle preparation · PBT II.G common tests · CCMA 3E k139

preguntas.pregunta: A requisition asks for a CBC (EDTA), a prothrombin time (citrate) and a basic metabolic panel (serum separator tube). Using the WHO order of draw, in what sequence are the three tubes filled?
opciones: Light blue citrate, then the serum separator tube, then purple EDTA
Purple EDTA first, then the serum separator tube, then light blue citrate
Serum separator tube, then light blue citrate, then purple EDTA
Light blue citrate, then purple EDTA, then the serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 numbers the tubes from 1 to 10. The coagulation tube is number 3, the serum separator tube (red-grey tiger or gold) is number 5, and EDTA is number 8, so citrate comes first, the SST second and EDTA last among these three. Step 8 gives the reason for a fixed sequence: it prevents the additive of one tube from contaminating the next.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: Where do prevention and de-escalation sit in managing a patient who may turn violent?
opciones: First, with restraints held back as a last resort
Last, once a security team has already come in
First, but only after a supervisor authorizes it
Last, and only after chemical restraint is given
preguntas.explicacion: Management centers on prevention and de-escalation, with the fight-or-flight reaction as the last resort. De-escalation may be applied as early as triage, staff should be trained in it, and physical restraints used alongside chemical ones are likewise a last resort rather than a first move.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f

preguntas.pregunta: An office is clearing out old files. How long must a signed advance written notice of non-coverage be kept?
opciones: 5 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
3 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
5 years from the date the claim for that care was finally paid or denied
Until the claim is paid, after which the signed copy may be discarded safely
preguntas.explicacion: Notices are kept for 5 years from the date of care delivery when no other state-law requirement applies, and every record is kept, including cases where the patient declined care, refused an option or refused to sign. The clock runs from the date of service, not from claim payment, and the record is not discarded once the claim closes.
preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Completing the notice
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77, 6 k85 · CCMA 5 k186 · NCMA EKB 23

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement compares the buccal route with the sublingual route correctly?
opciones: Buccal tissue is less permeable, so absorption there is slower than under the tongue
Buccal tissue is more permeable, so absorption there is faster than under the tongue
Buccal drugs pass through the liver first, while sublingual drugs go straight to the heart
Buccal drugs drain into the rectal venous plexus, so half the dose still meets the liver
preguntas.explicacion: Both are enteral routes that skip first-pass metabolism, because the venous blood of the mouth drains into the superior vena cava instead of the hepatic portal vein. The difference is the tissue itself: the mucosa under the tongue is highly permeable and reaches the capillaries beneath it quickly, while the cheek is less permeable and takes the drug up more slowly. The half that meets the liver belongs to the rectal route.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Enteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(v)

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is exercising on a hot day. How does the blood help keep the core temperature from rising?
opciones: More blood is routed to the skin, where heat is lost to the surroundings
Blood is diverted away from the skin so the core keeps its heat
Plasma proteins act as buffers that hold the blood pH near 7.4
The kidneys release erythropoietin so more red cells carry the heat
preguntas.explicacion: Temperature control works as a negative-feedback loop: when the core warms up, more blood is sent to the cooler periphery, heat escapes through the skin vessels and the returning blood is cooler. On a cold day the opposite happens and blood is kept away from the skin to keep the core warm. Buffering pH is a separate homeostatic role of blood, and erythropoietin responds to low oxygen, not to heat.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Maintenance of Homeostasis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · PBT I.B.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient lists what she has paid this year and asks what counts toward her out-of-pocket limit. Which one does?
opciones: The coinsurance the patient paid for covered care given inside the network
The monthly premiums the patient paid to keep the coverage in force this year
The balance billed by a provider who charged above the plan's allowed amount
The cost of a service the plan lists among the benefits it does not cover
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit adds up the patient's share of covered services: deductible, copayments and coinsurance for in-network care. Once it is reached, the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount for the rest of the year. Three things stay outside that tally by definition: premiums, charges balance billed above the allowed amount, and care the plan does not cover at all.
preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25

preguntas.pregunta: A benchtop chemistry analyzer just had its lamp and pump, both critical parts, replaced by the service technician. What does CLIA require before patient testing resumes?
opciones: Control material testing, as after a complete reagent change or major maintenance
A full calibration verification with three levels, regardless of the control results
Enrollment of the affected analytes in a new proficiency testing event
Written approval from the state agency, since a critical part changed the test system
preguntas.explicacion: Control materials must be tested before resuming patient testing whenever a complete change of reagents is introduced, major preventive maintenance is performed, or a critical part that may influence performance is replaced. Calibration verification is a separate requirement, also triggered by major maintenance, but the immediate gate to patient testing is acceptable control results, which must be documented.
preguntas.subtema: QC after maintenance or reagent change · CPT D1 1E / k27 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c

preguntas.pregunta: How do medical asepsis and surgical asepsis differ in what they set out to do?
opciones: Medical asepsis reduces pathogens as a barrier; surgical asepsis attacks every microorganism
Medical asepsis attacks every microorganism; surgical asepsis reduces pathogens as a barrier
Medical asepsis applies in the operating room; surgical asepsis applies at the bedside only
Medical asepsis covers hand hygiene alone; surgical asepsis covers every use of any glove
preguntas.explicacion: Aseptic technique, or medical asepsis, is the deliberate reduction of pathogens so they are not carried from one person or object to another, a protective barrier. Sterile technique, or surgical asepsis, goes further and aims to eliminate every microorganism in and around the field. It is the standard for surgery, invasive wound management and central line care.
preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.7

preguntas.pregunta: A 25-year-old with no risk factors asks how often she needs cervical cancer screening.
opciones: Cytology alone every three years, which is the schedule from 21 to 29
Cytology alone every year, which is the schedule from 21 to 29 years
Cytology with HPV co-testing every five years, starting at age 21
High-risk HPV testing alone every five years, starting at age 21
preguntas.explicacion: From 21 to 29 the recommendation is cervical cytology alone every three years. From 30 to 65 there are three acceptable options: cytology every three years, high-risk HPV testing alone every five years, or the two together every five years. Below 21 there is no screening at all. Under 30 the usual practice is cytology with reflex HPV testing.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pap and HPV Testing", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.5.a · CCMA 3A3 k45 · RMA III.F.4.b.ii

preguntas.pregunta: A new clinic laboratory is writing the manual for everything that happens before testing. Which item needs a written policy under the specimen submission and handling standard?
opciones: Specimen acceptability and rejection criteria
Calibration verification of the analyser
Competency assessment of the testing staff
Enrolment in an approved proficiency testing programme
preguntas.explicacion: That standard lists eight written policies where they apply: patient preparation, specimen collection, labeling, storage and preservation, transport conditions, processing, acceptability and rejection, and referral. Calibration verification belongs to the analytic systems, competency assessment to the general laboratory systems, and proficiency testing to its own separate subpart.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(a), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5D · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c

preguntas.pregunta: How is sweat obtained for a sweat chloride test?
opciones: Pilocarpine is driven into the skin by iontophoresis for 5 minutes, then sweat is collected for no more than 30 minutes
Pilocarpine is driven into the skin by iontophoresis for 30 minutes, and sweat is then collected for no more than 5 minutes
The arm is wrapped in occlusive plastic for 30 minutes and the sweat that forms is blotted onto filter paper
The patient exercises until sweating begins and gauze is then held against the skin for up to 30 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: In the Gibson-Cooke method two electrodes go on the arm or leg, one carrying gauze soaked in pilocarpine and the other deionized water, and a small painless current runs for 5 minutes to make the glands sweat. Collection onto gauze, filter paper or a macroduct coil follows and must not exceed 30 minutes. A trained technician does it at an accredited cystic fibrosis center.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sweat Testing", Specimen Collection and Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Iontophoresis technique · PBT V.C.4 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's father was diagnosed with colon cancer at 52. When should this patient start screening?
opciones: At 42, which is ten years before the age at which the relative was diagnosed
At 45, the same age recommended for everyone who is at an average risk
At 52, matching the age at which the relative received the diagnosis
At 62, which is ten years after the age at which the relative was diagnosed
preguntas.explicacion: A positive family history moves the start date forward: screening begins ten years before the age at which the relative was diagnosed. With a genetic cancer syndrome, testing can begin as early as the teenage years and repeat at short intervals. Risk assessment is what sorts patients into high, average and low risk before any test is chosen.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Colon Cancer Screening", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k45 · CMA I.A.5.a · RMA III.F.4.c.i

preguntas.pregunta: A requisition lists a complete blood count, a lipid panel, a coagulation panel and a troponin. For which of these tests is fasting usually required?
opciones: The lipid panel
The blood count
The clotting panel
The troponin test
preguntas.explicacion: Common tests that usually require fasting are blood glucose tests, cholesterol or lipid panels, and the basic metabolic panel, with liver function tests and the renal function panel sometimes added; a triglycerides test and calcitonin are also listed among tests needing fasting. A CBC, coagulation tests and cardiac enzyme tests such as troponin are described without any preparation, which is why most blood tests need none.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section What types of blood tests require fasting; MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, section What are the different types of blood tests
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)

preguntas.pregunta: How must contaminated reusable sharps be stored while they wait for reprocessing?
opciones: So that no employee has to reach into the container by hand to retrieve them
Immersed in a 1:10 bleach dilution for at least 10 minutes in an open pan
In a red bag closed before removal, like other regulated waste
In a labeled container that is emptied by hand only when three-quarters full
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(E) forbids storing or processing contaminated reusable sharps in any way that requires employees to reach by hand into the container holding them, and (d)(2)(viii) requires that container to be puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom and labeled or color-coded. Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(4) adds that reusable containers are never opened, emptied or cleaned manually. A red bag is for soft regulated waste, and the 1:10 hypochlorite dilution is WHO's spill disinfectant, not a storage method for sharps.
preguntas.subtema: Reusable sharps · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room suddenly has a drooping face on one side, a weak right arm and slurred speech. What is done?
opciones: Call the emergency number at once and note the time symptoms began
Give aspirin and water and drive the patient to the clinic next door
Lay the patient flat with the feet raised and recheck in 15 minutes
Take a full set of vital signs first and then call the provider in
preguntas.explicacion: A stroke is a medical emergency and the single most important action is to call for emergency help right away, at the first signs. Muscle weakness of face, arm or leg on one side, numbness on one side, and trouble speaking or understanding speech are typical and they usually start suddenly and without warning.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Stroke", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.k · 2027 I.B.8.k · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15

preguntas.pregunta: What is the role of the placeholder character X in ICD-10-CM?
opciones: It fills an empty position so the code keeps room for future expansion or a later character
It marks a code the coder could not verify against the medical record documentation
It replaces a character the provider left out of the documentation for the encounter
It flags a code as unspecified when the record gives no further detail about the case
preguntas.explicacion: The X is a placeholder used at certain codes to allow for future expansion, notably in the poisoning, adverse effect and underdosing categories, and it also fills empty positions so that an applicable seventh character sits in the seventh place. Where a placeholder exists it must be used for the code to be valid. It says nothing about missing documentation or about unspecified conditions.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the patient positioned and timed for orthostatic blood pressures?
opciones: Supine for about 5 minutes, then measured again within 1 to 3 minutes of standing
Seated for about 5 minutes, then measured again 10 minutes after standing up
Supine for about 1 minute, then measured again immediately on standing up
Standing for about 5 minutes, then measured again after lying down for 3 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The patient lies down for roughly five minutes and the pressure is taken again within one to three minutes of standing. The measurement is called for in older adults being evaluated for dizziness, fainting, falls or suspected loss of fluid volume, where the reflexes that defend pressure on standing are often impaired.

preguntas.pregunta: A healthy young patient's rate climbs stage after stage on the treadmill. What sets the usual ceiling on it?
opciones: The atrioventricular node passes at most about 220 impulses a minute
The sinoatrial node fires at most about 220 impulses a minute
The Purkinje fibers pass at most about 220 impulses a minute
The bundle branches pass at most about 220 impulses a minute
preguntas.explicacion: Under extreme stimulation from the sinus node above it, the atrioventricular node can still transmit only around 220 impulses a minute, and that is what fixes the typical maximum rate. Damaged or drug-driven hearts can beat faster, but then they pump poorly.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Atrioventricular Node

preguntas.pregunta: A site's two external controls for a rapid test have both failed twice. Which source of error listed in the guidance is worth checking first at the bench?
opciones: Whether the caps of the positive and negative control vials were switched and cross-contaminated them
Whether the operator read the cassette before the minimum time printed in the insert had elapsed
Whether the room temperature log shows a reading above the manufacturer's storage limit last night
Whether the positive control was applied to the sample well or to the result window by mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the actions for unexpected control results, the guidance lists checking that controls and reagents were not cross-contaminated by accidentally switching caps, alongside outdated materials, wrong storage and not following the instructions. Swapped caps contaminate both vials, which fits two controls failing together. Reading time and application errors are real operator faults but are not the cap example.

preguntas.pregunta: Under which two federal laws does HHS OCR say HHS-funded programs must provide language access services free of charge?
opciones: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the ACA
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act together with the ADA
HIPAA and the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act (ADAAA)
EMTALA and Title X of the Public Health Service Act (family planning)
preguntas.explicacion: Two federal laws require language access services at no charge in programs receiving HHS funds: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, each with implementing regulations. Title VII and the ADA are anti-discrimination laws cited elsewhere; EMTALA and Title X govern emergencies and minors.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's husband telephones the laboratory for her results, saying he will pass them along to her. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Release results only to authorized persons and to those responsible for using them
Release results to any adult of the household once his identity has been confirmed
Release results to him if the patient named him in the notice of privacy practices
Release results to him, because a spouse counts as the patient's personal representative
preguntas.explicacion: Test results go only to authorized persons, meaning individuals authorized under state law to order tests or receive results, plus whoever is responsible for using them and the laboratory that requested the test. The one widening is the patient's own access: on request, a laboratory may give the patient or the patient's personal representative the completed reports it can authenticate as hers.

preguntas.pregunta: Are health care workers mandatory reporters of suspected child maltreatment?
opciones: Yes, in every state except the four that instead require everyone to report
Yes, but only in the states that also require training for those reporters
No, unless the child is a patient of that clinician's own practice already
No, the duty falls on the head of the facility, who files on their behalf
preguntas.explicacion: Physicians, nurses and other health care workers are named as mandated reporters in 46 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories. The four missing ones — Indiana, New Jersey, North Carolina and Wyoming — do not list professions at all, because they require every person to report. Training requirements exist in some states and change nothing about who must report.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet asks which vitamin she is most likely to fall short on. Which one, and why?
opciones: Vitamin B12, because only animal foods carry it naturally
Vitamin B12, because plant foods block its absorption in the gut
Folate, because only animal foods carry it naturally
Vitamin C, because cooked plant foods lose almost all of it
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin B12 sits in a wide range of animal foods; plant foods hold none unless they have been fortified, so people who eat little or no animal food may fall short, and so may their infants when they are pregnant or breastfeeding. The adult recommended amount is 2.4 micrograms a day.
preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin B12 — Consumer

preguntas.pregunta: Which conflict belongs to adolescence in Erikson's stages, and which strength comes from it?
opciones: Identity versus identity confusion, yielding fidelity
Intimacy versus isolation, yielding love as its virtue
Industry versus inferiority, yielding competence
Autonomy versus shame and doubt, yielding will
preguntas.explicacion: Each period pairs two opposing tendencies with the virtue gained from navigating them. Adolescence is the fifth stage, identity against identity confusion, and its virtue is fidelity, with repudiation as the malignancy. Intimacy against isolation belongs to young adulthood, industry against inferiority to school age.

preguntas.pregunta: May an employer use a sign or a placard instead of putting a label on a fixed process container?
opciones: Yes, if it names the containers it covers and is available each shift
Yes, if the container is emptied and refilled at least once a week
No, every container of a hazardous chemical must carry its own label
No, unless the safety data sheet is posted beside the container
preguntas.explicacion: For individual stationary process containers the employer may use signs, placards, process sheets, batch tickets, operating procedures or similar written materials instead of affixing a label. Two conditions come with it: the alternative has to identify which containers it applies to and carry the same information a workplace label would, and the written material has to be readily accessible to the employees in their work area throughout each work shift.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(7), Workplace labeling

preguntas.pregunta: Under the federal rule on research consent, what must a subject be told about withdrawing?
opciones: That leaving at any point costs no benefit they were entitled to
That leaving is allowed once the study's enrollment period has closed
That leaving requires the review board to approve the request first
That leaving forfeits any compensation paid for visits already made
preguntas.explicacion: Among the basic elements of research consent is a statement that taking part is voluntary, that refusing carries no penalty or loss of benefits the subject was otherwise entitled to, and that they may stop at any time on the same terms. Nothing in the rule makes withdrawal wait for board approval or tie it to the enrollment calendar.

preguntas.pregunta: A practice manager says the office sends its claims through a clearinghouse. What does a health care clearinghouse do?
opciones: It converts health information between standard and nonstandard formats for others
It reviews the medical necessity of claims and decides whether the payer pays them
It holds the payer's funds until the electronic funds transfer reaches the provider
It assigns the diagnosis and procedure codes for practices that have no coder
preguntas.explicacion: In the HIPAA definition, a health care clearinghouse, billing service or similar entity either turns health information received in a nonstandard format into a standard transaction, or takes a standard transaction and renders it in the nonstandard form the receiver needs. That makes it a covered entity. Deciding medical necessity is the payer's adjudication, banks move the funds, and coding stays with the provider.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 160.103, definition of health care clearinghouse

preguntas.pregunta: A patient treated with liquid nitrogen asks what the treated spot will do over the next days. What is expected?
opciones: Redness, blistering and crusting, with healing over several weeks
Redness and swelling only, with healing complete within about two days
Immediate blanching that fades in an hour, with no visible change afterward
A firm painless nodule that grows for a week and then resolves on its own
preguntas.explicacion: Erythema, blistering and crusting are the expected responses after cryotherapy, and healing usually takes several weeks by secondary intention. The complications worth counseling about are loss of pigment, scarring, nerve injury and recurrence, which is why undertreating a benign lesion is preferred: what persists can be treated at another visit.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cryotherapy in Dermatology", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 2B.11

preguntas.pregunta: Before a venipuncture on a 6-week-old, the tray holds chlorhexidine and alcohol. Which is ruled out at this age?
opciones: Chlorhexidine, which is not to be used on children under 2 months of age
Alcohol, which is not to be used on children under 2 months of age
Both, since the WHO requires povidone iodine for all neonatal skin antisepsis
Neither, since antisepsis is optional in neonates as in glucose testing
preguntas.explicacion: Paediatric venepuncture follows standard skin antisepsis with one addition: chlorhexidine is not used on children under 2 months of age. For capillary punctures in children povidone iodine is ruled out and alcohol is allowed to air dry. The optional alcohol swab applies to glucometer fingersticks, not to neonatal venepuncture.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Drawing blood

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory proposes to keep reporting potassium on hemolysed samples by applying a correction formula based on the hemolysis index. What did the follow-up study on this idea conclude?
opciones: Corrective formulas are unreliable and misleading, because cell contents are not released uniformly
Corrective formulas are reliable for potassium and LDH but not for AST and total bilirubin
Corrective formulas work only when the hemolysis is visually undetectable, below 0.5 g/L
Corrective formulas are acceptable if the corrected result is flagged as an estimate in the report
preguntas.explicacion: Following the study that graded hemolysis, Lippi and colleagues showed that formulas meant to adjust results for the degree of hemolysis are unreliable and potentially misleading, because the mechanical injury of blood cells and the release of their contents into serum or plasma do not happen homogeneously. The answer to a hemolysed potassium is a new sample, not an arithmetic correction, flagged or not.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist keeps a water bottle at the draw station and applies lip balm between patients. Which rule applies?
opciones: Eating, drinking and applying lip balm are all prohibited where exposure is reasonably likely
Drinking is allowed from a closed container, but cosmetics and lip balm are prohibited
Both are allowed if the counter is decontaminated with disinfectant at the end of the shift
Both are allowed as long as the water is not stored in a refrigerator with specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(ix) prohibits eating, drinking, smoking, applying cosmetics or lip balm, and handling contact lenses in work areas where there is a reasonable likelihood of occupational exposure. A closed bottle is not an exception the standard grants. End-of-shift decontamination in (d)(4)(ii)(A) is a housekeeping duty and does not license eating at the bench, and (d)(2)(x), which keeps food and drink out of refrigerators and countertops holding blood, is a second, separate prohibition.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(ix) and (d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls

preguntas.pregunta: Ninety seconds have passed with the tourniquet on and the phlebotomist still cannot find a vein. What should happen next?
opciones: Release the band before two minutes and look again with a vein illuminator
Keep the band on until a vein appears, then draw all the tubes without pause
Tighten the band further until the radial pulse disappears at the wrist
Release the band and draw from the peripheral access line already in place
preguntas.explicacion: One guideline asks for the band to come off within a minute of placement and another sets the ceiling at two minutes, so at ninety seconds it is released. Illumination devices are recommended in place of a long application for veins that are hard to see, especially when two or more tubes are due.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Preparation and Technique or Treatment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6

preguntas.pregunta: A practice asks new patients to sign a consent for use of their information in treatment, payment and operations. What is the status of that form?
opciones: Voluntary, and it does not substitute for an authorization where one is required
Mandatory, since the rule requires written consent before any treatment begins
Mandatory, and it doubles as the acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices
Voluntary, but once signed it permits every disclosure the practice may wish to make
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may choose to obtain consent for treatment, payment and health care operations but is not required to, and one that does has complete discretion over how the process works. A consent document is not valid permission for a purpose that requires an authorization under the rule, nor where the rule sets other conditions on the use or disclosure.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations

preguntas.pregunta: A 30 kg child is scheduled for an oral glucose tolerance test. How much glucose should the child receive?
opciones: 52.5 g, from 1.75 g per kilogram
75 g, the standard adult load
30 g, one gram per kilogram
100 g, the load used in pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: Children receive 1.75 g of glucose per kilogram of body weight, up to a maximum of 75 g; for 30 kg that is 30 × 1.75 = 52.5 g. The cap is the part candidates forget: a 50 kg child would compute to 87.5 g but receives 75 g, which is also the adult load. The 100 g drink belongs to the 3-hour test used after a positive gestational screen, never to a child's OGTT.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory forwards a specialised assay to a distant laboratory and passes the result on to the ordering physician. What else must the referring laboratory tell that physician?
opciones: The name and address of the laboratory that actually performed the test
The reason the assay could not be performed on its own premises
The date on which the specimen was dispatched to the other laboratory
The name of the courier service that carried the specimen there
preguntas.explicacion: When specimens are referred, three rules apply at once: the referring laboratory may not revise the results or their interpretation, it may let the testing laboratory report straight to the ordering person provided it can produce an exact duplicate of that report, and it must tell whoever ordered the test the name and address of every laboratory location where the testing was done.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(i)(3), Standard: Test report

opciones: Thirty days following discharge
Twenty-four hours following discharge
Ninety days following discharge
Five years following discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The content standard closes with the final diagnosis and completion of the medical record within 30 days following discharge. The 24 hour figure belongs to the history and physical, which must be in the record within a day of admission and before anesthesia; five years is the minimum retention period for the record once it is complete.

preguntas.pregunta: When does the serum peak concentration of intravenous vancomycin occur?
opciones: Immediately after the infusion is completed
Within the 30 minutes before the next dose
Four to six hours after the infusion, one half-life later
At steady state, after the third dose has run
preguntas.explicacion: Vancomycin has a rapid onset with a serum peak concentration immediately following completion of the intravenous infusion. The 30-minute window before the next dose is the trough, 4 to 6 hours is the terminal half-life in healthy adults, and the third dose marks steady state; none of these is the peak.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Pharmacokinetics
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: Why are the armrests of the patient's chair adjusted before an outpatient draw?
opciones: So the worker can act quickly if the patient has a vasovagal reaction
So the tourniquet can be anchored on the rest instead of the arm
So the tray of tubes can be balanced within the patient's reach
So the arm stays below heart level throughout the whole procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The chair is expected to be comfortable for both people, with the armrests set to a convenient position that also allows appropriate action if the patient has a vasovagal episode. Preparedness of that kind matters most in the patients who admit to fainting during earlier tests.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
